Academic institutions, esp Cornell, should be guided by a pursuit of truth. Good professors should not only encourage students to share different ideas, but they should also have an open-mind themselves. Someone truly committed to education adapts his/her view when wrong. Joe is the complete opposite of this and believes his view is infallible.

Will not grade and return assignments. I have no clue how I'm doing in this class or what grade I have, and there are no clear guidelines for any of the assignments so it is basically just a bunch of guessing to try and figure out what he wants. Lectures are hard to listen to because of the monotony, and it is difficult for him to stay objective.

I have never met a professor more sanctimonious than Regenstein.  He was really painful to listen to, and he made class mandatory through iClicker questions that added up in points but were intellectually worthless.  He makes everything confusing and more difficult than it needs to be.

Most of the class material is online and the few real assignments are fairly straightforward. His lecturing style often makes interesting material seem incohesive and dull, but the iClicker questions and food he brings should hopefully make attendance worthwhile. The in-class lectures aren't really important for a good grade, though.

If you ask him (or even if you don't) Professor Regenstein will tell you he invented the world and everything in it. He surely thinks quite highly of himself and it gets in the way of his ability to teach. In a class where opinions can and should differ greatly he certainly believes his is the only one that matters.

Regenstein's excessive gesticulation speaks for itself: he is sacrimonious. Joe picks and chooses who he likes and doesn't, and bases his grading on this rubric. I'm not sure where my standing was, but I could certainly recognize this amoung other students. This class is one of great potential, and one Regenstein should not be teaching.

Professor Joseph Conrad was THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD in any class. Throughout the course he was unclear, dishonest, prone to arbitrary grudges, and focused on the 10% of the students who already understood the material. He copies the same lessons from his extremely poorly written book year after year, without adapt to student needs.

Classes with Professor McComas are worth it because she's such a nice woman. They can be boring but once you get to know her she can be fun, and by the end of the semester you realize you actually learned quite a bit.

i took community involvement with katherine.  the class was a little unorganized and the topic was relatively dry but she did a good job explaining the concepts we did cover and making the class as interesting as possible (w/ guest lectures and applied examples).  she was always available to meet outside of class and kind of hot in a mom way.
This Class Sucks!! Mccomas doesnt teach a thing and the group project is soooooo stupid, as a comm major I can say take any class but hers!!
3 prelims - no final, case study, and short paper.  Material isn't hard, just kind of boring.  McComas is a great teacher though
Boring and stupid lectures and assignments, changed my friend's paper grade despite her "no grade changes" policy and then refused to change mine.
She's sorta boring in large lectures and is much better in smaller settings.  I would suggest 376 because you do some practical stuff in the class but at the same time it's not too difficult.

There is too much busy work.  Ridiculously easy but soooo boring.  She tries to tell jokes but just isn't funny.  She pretends to be a hip prof. in class but speaking one on one she's not as frieldly.  Skipable class and still get a good grade.

Kathy was vague with assignments and there was a lot of busy work.  She didn't do much teaching as the entier second half of the semester was class presentation.  Too much busy work not enough instruction and the assignments that mattered were rushed into the mix.  Terrible class

McComas is wonderful. She is intelligent, and concerned with information that can be useful in the real world. She is sweet, a little reserved, but incredible to speak with one on one. Highly Recommended.
I agree with the comment below. She's kinda hot. Needs to losen up a little bit. Overall, very nice but boring... Communication sucks and I got three years left here!!!!
Most exam materials come from lecture, so if you pay attention in the lecture, it will be a easy A class.  The mean score of the class is 85.
Not a bad class. Boring most of the time, but the tests are easy if you either pay attention in class or read the textbook. She is also a really nice professor.
She is one hot piece of acedemic ass. Not only does she give a terrific lecture, there is something sexy sexy sexy about her!
She runs her course in a way where the information you learn is applicable to real life as well as interersting. She gives out a reasonable amount of work and enjoys participation from the class.

Katherine is AWESOME! She is a great masseuse that really understands the stresses of being a Cornell student. She shows you step-by-step the different techniques. This class, Swedish Massage, is a fantastic class to take, it really helps relieve stress, it feels great, and it gives you some new massage techniques to impress your significant other.

I LOVE HER. She is awesome. She is so soft-spoken and cute and knows everything and helps you and will remember your name a year later and will let you come visit and practice even if you're not enrolled. This class is VERY practical and VERY relaxing. TAKE IT!
How can a class like this NOT be good? Katie is a friendly and helpful instructor. Could not have asked for better.
definitely find a partner before you take this class

As a psych major, I can confidently say Kinzler's class has been the best psych course I've taken at Cornell. Her lectures are engaging, build clearly off each other, and if you take notes and pay attention in class you will ace the tests; she isn't out to get you, just testing knowledge. Attendance is taken with clickers, so show up!

Kinzler is a great professor! Her lectures are some of the best psych ones that I've had at Cornell. She is engaging and everyday I wanted to go to class. Also her tests are straightforward and fair. Great professor!

Most of grade based on weekly quizzes, first taken individually then with you group- the grades for the two are combined.  I prefer this to tests because you just have to know the content from the previous lecture and have read the assigned paper vs weeks of content.  She's also a kind prof, seems to really know and care abt the content.

Super nice, personable, accommodating. Non-judgmental. It's clear that she really likes the stuff she's talking about. Explains things clearly and tries to make sure everyone understands fully before moving on. Not hard class but the quiz grade is averaged across 5-question quizzes, so one wrong answer is not minor (so do your readings).
Great FWS and great professor. He was always available to help us with our writing and he did a great job of explaining the lecture concepts.
Super interesting class, one of my favorites! Wish he was a full-time Professor!

Ian is an amazing professor, and I thoroughly enjoyed taking the class. I learned so much about Brazil, and he has inspired me to take more Latin American Studies courses. He is a very fair grader and included helpful and constructive criticism. My writing has definitely improved after taking the course.

Unique FWS subject. Lots of reading and writing-like any history class-but maybe more than other FWSs. Ian has high expectations, but a challenge is better in the long run than an easy grade. I am a more confident writer and researcher because of his class. There are few papers I have been very proud of-my term paper for this class is one of those.

Just the absolute worst of what the FWS program has to offer. Besides making coups and counterrevolutions seem boring this guy is super harsh about attendance grading. Only plus is that he loves hearing himself talk so much that you barely have to participate.

This class was really interesting. The prof went above and beyond to make the class accessible and flexible in the online learning environment. While the lectures were dense, learning goals were clearly identified and the assessments were firmly focused around these. Also assessment was flexible and tailored to each student's preferred method.

Prof. Hewson is clearly very knowledgeable&passionate about his field, but the lectures are very dense and got to be a bit monotonous at the end of the semester Luckily there was no exams on the detailed lecture content, rather theres weekly literature/writing HW, group proj, and final proj. This was nice but made it too easy to tune out lecture
Professor Hewson is a fantastic individual who really knows his stuff! Such a pleasure to have him as a teacher.
This was a great introduction to marine biology. Some of the labs were a little disorganized but at least there were labs!

Dr. Ian's Hewson class is more suited for people with no familiarity with biology than anyone who has even taken intro biology.  It is overall disorganized and presented in a distinctly anthropocentric and unscientific manner

Merwin is awesome. he is so willing to help students, and is very flexible in terms of deadlines and due dates.  He obviously really loves teaching and is very knowledgeable.  I'm sad to be out of classes to take with him!
Merwin's the man.
An awesome teacher and a great human being. I enjoyed his lectures a lot and learn even more than what I expected! he is genuinely a great prof!!
He presents the data clearly.  THe use of the powerpoints and photos makes concepts more tangible.  He gives you print-outs of the slides and brings FOOD to EVERY class.
Great professor, great class! The lectures are interesting and the labs are field trips. Professor Merwin is pretty easygoing. Hort 101 isn't an "easy A" but it's not heinously difficult either.
Loves apples and wines, pomology in general. Great man. Feels the land; down to earth. Loved the class. Easily apporachable and knows what he's talking about, but doesn't seem vain.
Great and easy classes...Nice guy...Definately leftover from the 60's but so incredible awesome and chill. Minimal work for good grades
Merwin is fantastic. One of the most interesting profs I've had at Cornell.
Great guy... leftover from the late sixties, all around cool guy.  Class is great!

Amazing professor, doesn't assign work for the sake of it and is passionate about the topic. Well accomplished (Harvard, Princeton, UCLA), but very humble. If the opportunity to take this class arises, I would 100% sign up.

This was a new course this semester based on a grad course Ian teaches. The class was incredibly interesting, well taught, and had no tests. Grade comprised problem sets, peer grading, and a final group project/presentation. The teaching team was always accessible. I wish they gave A+'s, but otherwise this was my favorite class at Cornell.
Loved the course. Required for the MS degree. Everyone attends.
The weekly lab exercises require you to use Stata to estimate some type of econometric model using data provided. Gives you a great opportunity to learn how to empirically estimate models.
Covers a lot of econometrics but I plan to go to graduate school so that is a plus for me
Tells interesting stories in class.

AEM6080 is a required course for all MS students in the graduate field of applied economics and management. The material covered is essential for upper level courses, especially PhD courses. Professor Tauer does a very good job of teaching the material.
Covers all on the material in the textbook but I appreciated that because I needed to learn the material for my thesis research.

I do not understand the poor ratings given to Professor Tauer. He is a solid instructor. Not an entertainer, like some other faculty in the Dyson School, but he explains material very well in class. Econometrics can be a challenging subject and has a lot of mundane concepts but Prof. Tauer does a very good job.

I took this class fall 2017 and learned econometrics from Professor Tauer. I do not understand the concerns others have expressed about the quality of the lectures, because I thought they were very clear and informative. All I can figure is that in earlier years the lectures were not as well developed and presented.
very boring and not helpful. I regret taking his class.

Dr. Tauer, in the name of efficiency, opted to use textbook slideshows. He was rarely well acquainted with them before class and learning turned to drudgery. A very ineffective educator. A good sense of humor, and has a few good stories... but I am disappointed at how little effort he puts into teaching..
Great guy.  Presentations (in projected Word) are very very dry though, and are not conducive to learning.
Professor Tauer knows his stuff. IF you want to learn production economics, take his class.
No Comments

She was a great lecturer who forced you to participate and read the material. Your grade is dependent somewhat on your participation and 2 pop quizzes, but it's almost solely based on 2 papers in the semester. I left the class with a new perspective and reverence for people. Take it!!!
Very enjoyable class and very interesting readings. I learned a lot.

The class is very enjoyable.  She lets the class discuss/debate issues but always guides it to the points she wants the class come away with.  Its very important to do the readings.  A class is usually 80% student discussion with the discussion centering around a theme that unifies ALL the readings assigned for the class and also past readings.

Figure out if she likes you or not before you drop the course.  If she doesn't like you won't get a good grade no matter what you do.  Also, if you speak up in class and always show up, then she's bound to like you more.  I really enjoy her personal work and liked talking to her, so I enjoyed her classes.

Under-stimulating, terrible with time management, and irritating to sit through most of the time.  If you've thought about any of these issues on your own, then you're probably past what she'll be teaching.  Save your time and money.

nice prof really tries to accomodate class but acts as though it is a high school lecture course. all powerpoint slide class and attendance heavily weighed. takes students too personally and immature in teaching. good lectures but no real intelligent conversation to spark, VERY BAD SPEECH irritating to listen to. easy course but no excuses allowed
She is awesome.

She moved the final exam to online because of students concerns, She actually genuinely cares about students and if you're too swamped in a given week, she's very understanding with pushing back certain assignments. She is simply an amazing person and I really enjoyed taking labor history with her. Gem of a person.

Lots of reading and history can be kind of boring, but she genuinely makes it interesting. Definitely meet with her for feedback while writing your essays, she is very helpful and cares about you doing well.
Super nice professor and very empathetic. Very understanding person. make sure to read
Prof Martinez is a great professor! extremley kind and workload is not too bad. I would highly reccomend to take labor history with her if possible

Professor Martinez is incredibly nice, insightful, and knowledgeable. Her lectures are presented in a way to facilitate conversation and class engagement. This would all have been wonderful if I had found any interest in the course material. There's an unrealistic amount of reading and pretty dull topics. Great teacher but boring course.

One of the kindest, most caring professors. Was extremely lenient with deadlines. Great lectures; I liked how we discussed contemporary issues like police brutality and the disproportional impact of covid on minority groups. A bit reading and writing heavy, but definitely doable and grading was fair.

Somehow takes semi-boring course content and presents it in a way that makes it the most unbearable class I've maybe ever had. Is a nice person and is lenient with due dates but the essay prompts will make you hate your life. Better read everything or know US history well already or else you're screwed

Professor Martinez Matsuda is an excellent professor. She's extremely passionate about the material, and class was extremely interesting and informative. She's also just a really great person that cares for her students deeply.

One of the most caring and friendly professors I have ever had. Made material that would otherwise be somewhat dry very interesting and engaging. I highly recommend any class taught by this professor.

There's a lot of reading and writing in the class: I remember reading (well, skimming) up to 200 pages a week. I didn't think that I was much of a historian, but she makes the material interesting. She is also open to help out if you ever need it! There's also a lot of writing for the class. I had three papers and the final was handwritten essays.

great teacher; aside from the socialistic view that she preaches subtly, she was a great instructor. if your taking us labor history, she is the best teacher to take it with hands down. class is mostly essay based but in total id say its only about 16 pages the entire semester

Prof Martinez-Matsuda is AMAZING. She is super caring and passionate about her students. There is a lot of reading in this course and the discussion sections/pop quizzes are heavily based on these readings- at least skim! She is accommodating and will extend paper deadlines during intense parts of the semester. Take her!

Grade-wise:  It all depends on your TA.  She'll give you extra time if needed for assignments, especially during the heavy part of the semester.  She really loves teaching.  The readings aren't really needed- except there are pop quizzes every once in a while, so make sure to at least skim.  Overall, I'd love to take another class with her again!

For a class that I had no interest in, she is prob the best prof out there. The class (by definition) has a ton of reading and some medium length papers but she is reasonable in expectationsgrading. If in ILR, I would def recommend taking it with her. The TA was nice but a tougher grader than the Prof. There were a couple easy pop reading quizzes

She's super sweet, like literally the sweetest person you'll ever meet. Go to her office hours, and know her on a personal level because she's just that awesome.. Her class is definitely on the difficult side: she assigns a ton of reading and essays throughout the semester. The TA we had graded them on the tougher side, so it was a tough course.
She is absolutely incredible!  She's so energetic and passionate, it would be a mistake not to take a class with her!

i loved this class! She's so energetic and helpful. Also just an incredibly nice person. Classes incorporate video material as well as in-class debates. Very practical and insightful way to learn about immigration and labor.
Some of the information in the class is difficult to understand but Martinez is very good at explaining things and answering questions in office hours.
She's bubbly.
Asis is a great professor. You will learn a lot.

Exam questions are too flexible and he didn't give us enough materials to prepare for the exam (only limited 2-4 in-class exercises can be used to review before exams). Class participation is too strict and meaningless. Accounting class should focus more on helping students understand concepts, instead of penalizing them for not being active.
he would be a great prof if there were 48 hours in a day

He does not teach the material in a way that is productive. No one knows what is going on. The same man that has typos in nearly every assignment is in charge of grading our assessments - this is a problem when he marks a correct answer as incorrect, refusing to release an answer key after the assessment.

This class is probably one of the more difficult class that I've taken at Cornell but I definitely learned the most. Asis is the sweetest man ever. He is so accessible outside of class! You will have to grind (do hw problems over and over again for like 5 times) but if you put in the work, you'll do well. He also curves a lot.

The bad reviews come from ppl who didnt listen. We were to read and do homework before class so we could discuss in lecture. I did so and learned a ton. I participated more than anyone. It irked me that so many of my peers wanted an A handed to them when they failed to do what he asked. Do what the prof wants; they shouldnt bow to entitled hotelies

I really enjoyed taking Asis's class even though I did freak out in the beginning. His teaching style is different from many other professors as he really wants to help students to build up a critical thinking mindset. He has a lot of cool experiences and is willing to help students both academically and professionally.

I really enjoyed having Asis for Managerial Accounting. He is tough, but his class set me up for success in the rest of my classes in the Hotel School. He took the time to get to know everyone . I really appreciated how much he cared for his students, and he was always available for extra help (which really helped me succeed in this hard class).
you can tell he really cares about his students and gives tons of opportunities for OH. he wants his students to succeed past academics.

the hw probs r different from the ones on the test bc the ones on the test require u to apply multiple topics, and many students are used to only being able to do the same types of q. however, he wants u to think like a manager, and u don't always get the same types of q irl. asis is very caring and u can tell he spends sm time on this course:)

I have only taken Asis for higher level classes so that's all I can speak towards, he reasonably expects preparation for class and it creates a great environment where we can go in depth. Mastering Strategy Execution is a small class and discussion based and Asis leading these discussions have been my favorite class taken at the Hotel School

Asis is a nice man, not a great professor. He puts a lot of effort into class and wants his students to understand it (e.g. asking students who are participating further questions to make them think) but this just ends up making student more confused. My best advice is read the textbook, teach it to yourself, and stop listening in class

I love Asis so much as a professor; he always took the time to hold extra office hours if you need it, and you can tell that he truly cares about his students and their future. Have an open mind!! Hes really a gem.

Was the absolute worst ... made me hate accounting so, so much. Get ready for 2 hours of homework before every class. Would try to avoid this prof if possible.

Great Professor. Taking care of students. It was hard at the beginning; however, when understanding his teaching style and the basic logic of the problem sets, the tests are not as terrible as I imagined. Really nice professor and will learn a lot.

Dont take his class,teaching style is such that he really doenst explain much in class. expect us to understand the concepts beforehand and he would just solve a problem based on the concept in class,says that the questions he would put in the paper would have never been seen by us before. Teach yourself the content. Only good is Curve, too many hw

The class concepts aren't too difficult, so as long as you practice the in class assignments and make sure you understand things conceptually, you will be fine for the exams. The workload can be pretty heavy, but he's a nice person and is accessible outside of class to answer questions.

Verbally harasses students and pushed all exams together so we would receive your last exam grade right before the next exam. Impossible to learn and prepare yourself. He refuses to teach, and instead walks through problems while answering them completely different from the questions asks. Broad questions mean missed points and he hates critiques.

Asis does not care to help struggling students and has taken away ALL outside resources. You know he's not a good teacher when the tutors AND the TAs can't even understand what this man is teaching. He does not teach you any fundamental principles so you are completely screwed for the exams so you are left to teach everything by yourself.

His teaching style just isn't suited for this course. He adopts a Socratic style which works for Master's programs and concept-heavy classes, NOT a math-heavy class like man. acc. He fails to teach the material that ACTUALLY matters; leaving students to fend for themselves. Love him as a person, but it's very easy to dislike him as a professor.

Asiss class is a struggle. Hes a very kind and fun-loving person but he is not an effective professor. Most of the material covered in exams are never gone over in class or homework. The exams always have low averages but he curves them so everyone can do decently. The lectures are hard to follow and youll have to teach yourself the material.

Gives insane amounts of hw and has no empathy for struggling students. Assigns an average of 5 assignments/week, and praises himself for giving you a "break" every few weeks and assigning 4 assignments, all WAY longer than normal. Doesn't follow the syllabus at all and won't teach any content in class. Yells at students after cold-calling them.
Don't take the class with him. Run away.
She is so sweet to all students and she knows her stuff so well! I really enjoyed reading literature with her in classes. rewarding experience

I'd only take a class with this guy again if I got hit with a shovel and forgot about the first time, but I learned a ton. By far hardest class I've ever taken and likely ever will take. He's super nice, very easygoing about late submissions, and wants you to succeed. He just really likes math. He may be unaware if everyone is struggling, TELL HIM.
If you can handle it definitely take this course. Very intense but worth it. All tests were long and take home. Most Ive learned in a semester by far. Bettered my math skills significantly.

He is a lecturer that only clicks with certain people. His teaching style was definitely confusing at first, but it got better. One of the hardest classes I've ever taken at Cornell, but also the most rewarding.
exams are too hard
Had him for 4310, textbook was terrible, lectures were hard to understand, and tests were very difficult. One of the worst classes I have ever taken
The lectures were confusing sometimes but he generally did a good job. The most accessible and easy to talk to professor I've had here. Explains things very thoroughly one-on-one.
Avoid at all costs. Worst math professor I've had at Cornell. Handwriting is illegible, prelims are nearly impossible, and does not teach the concepts well at all.
Alright professor
1. incomprehensible handwriting 2. bad pronunciation 3. not good voice 4. exam questions exceedingly difficult 5. low textbook usage. I dont think he is a bad person but he is the worst as a teacher.

Yes, yes, a nightmare of a class. But I feel really really really bad that he's so bad. He is a genius, but not in terms of teaching math. If your smart, i still recommend going to his lectures. Yes, you will have to read the book. Best thing is to go to his office hours, he does the homework for yo
Bright guy, but just can't speak english or teach math. He doesn't understand your questions, and his lectures have no structure or logic.
Very unclear, skips steps in proofs, hard to follow, in general difficult to understand.
nice man but can't teach for crap, speaks Bulgarian with English accent, speaks too fast, can't write, homeworks and exams are way too difficult, the curve is unfair, homeworks are harshly graded.

He's a nice guy, and he tries, but the lectures are very disorganized and hard to follow.  The book isn't much better.  Thankfully the TA was pretty good and managed to explain more of the things that the prof. couldn't. Don't take unless you are really prepared to teach yourself the material.
Clearly cares about the students, knows his stuff. Make sure to take the notes on the slides before lectures because he goes very fast.

Dr. Graef emphasizes active student participation, with transparent grading criteria. Success relies on attentive engagement during lectures, and Dr. Graef fosters a caring atmosphere, contributing to a positive learning environment. Despite challenges, the course offers valuable insights for dedicated students.

I had him for BIOMG 1350. He definitely cares about making sure his students understand the material but he FLIES through the slides. Just soak it in because taking notes is basically impossible. The class is really well organized. Exams definitely require some studying- basically everything is memorization based.

Lectures:  poor, condescending, boring.  Homeworks:  lengthy, tedious, uninformative, nit-picking.  TAs: variable.  HW sneaker-net was demoralizing.  Exams:  races against the clock.  Instructors demeanor:  arrogant, unhelpful.  Chewed out the class because someone's phone rang and he didn't look at his watch.  Lame.  Always late for class.  Awful.

This class is the worst class I have taken at Cornell in 3 years. The lectures are strictly powerpoint, and boring beyond belief. The problem sets are unnecessarily long (8-10 hours/week) and relatively useless. Tests are not fair, objectively. He seems to have no clue how everyone in the class is doing. That being said, he is a very nice person.

The class is nothing like it was supposed to be last year, but is still very manageable as long as you put in the effort.  Schwager's lectures are long and boring and he often goes into depth on really trivial things, but as you go on it gets more interesting.  Tests and homework are very fair and there are plenty of opportunities for redemption.

This class is a nightmare. Lectures are hard to follow and the tests are impossible. Above 75 on the first one got you an A. Homeworks also take everyone 5-10 hours and the average is usually a 30/50. I heard that this class was really easy last year, Schwager really screwed it up. Only plus is he's a very nice, helpful guy but that doesn't cut it.

tests: 2.5 hours, 5 questions; problem sets: 15 hours, 10 questions; grades: horrible; office hours: packed; learning accomplished: zero; EVERYONE HATES THIS CLASS AND PROFESSOR!!!  THEY WILL RUIN YOUR SOCIAL LIFE ENTIRELY!!!

Very helpful.  You can email him with a question at 10 at night and in many cases he will get back to you the same day.  Great office hours as well.  Can tell he really knows what he is talking about.  Homework is helpful in understanding material.

He knows a tremendous amount about his field and is very helpful in office hours because he asks questions that make you get the answer on your own. But he teaches off extremely confusing slide shows using made up variables and talks over an hour straight in his droning voice. Also his homework assignments are hard and often require TA help.

The subject matter was hard, but prof. and his TA were extremely helpful (office hours everyday of the week).  Prof. is an extremely fair  grader, and although material is difficult, you are guarenteed to get at least a B for all your hard work.
Tries to ensure all students perform well in the class. Lectures are well-organized and straight forward as is the textbook.
Reasonably clear for a math teacher and very helpful. Cares very much about how students perform in class.
He's got a great deal of subject content knowledge, but when it comes to teaching pedagogy, he simply just sucks!  Don't waste your time and spare yourself from taking any of his courses!!!

Firstly- we had to write a gigantic paper on calculus.. CALCULUS!!!! The final was the worst thing, homeworks are graded so harshly that NO ONE DOES WELL, and not a thing is clear. I learned nothing from Steve, and if not for my amazing TA, Im 90% sure I would have shaved all my hair off from the stress of this class. NOT WORTH IT!!!! BOOO!!!!!!!
This class is the worst ever, the final was literally impossible and absolute hell on earth and I literally got sick of the stress of this.
Did not help during corona

Steve Bennoun is by far the worst professor I have had at Cornell. On top of not being a great professor to begin with (as reflected by rating before mine), Prof. Bennoun was extremely unaccommodating during the spring COVID-19 semester online. Do not take this class unless you absolutely must as you will dislike it (hence his overall rating of 1).

Worst class ever. Material itself is really not that difficult but somehow the professor makes it the most confusing thing ever. also a harsh grader. a LOT of homework, quiz, test, prelims, clickers and only 3 credits?! seriously, don't take this class if you don't have to.

Lectures feel like a waste of time. Most of the course feels like it needs to be self taught and the textbook is basically math taught through critical reading. There are pre-reading quizzes with confusing wording meant to trick you or "test your critical knowledge". The class also is not curved so you might as well take Math 1110.
No resources available to students to learn outside class. Unclear notes and slides.
This class was extremely disorganized.

Very disorganized lecturer. He teaches two classes that have overlapping material and often confuses the content between the two and you might be tested on material from the class you are not taking. Lectures are very surface level compared to the exams and many times would need to know outside knowledge to be able to answer the questions.

The class started out very strong, with clear lectures, quizzes, and a fair midterm. Later on, his lectures started getting more and more disorganized, his quizzes ridiculously specific (like a fine print under a picture). He was kind of unhelpful when we had logistical questions or even something about information on his slides.
Easy going and understanding

He's a very interesting lecturer that makes interaction during class very easy. He doesn't always have all the answers to questions but he will make an effort to find out the answer and get back to you. All the assessment material is really fair and everything can be found almost word for word on the slides

When I first signed up for his class, I didn't know what to expect. It was my first college experience and I was really nervous. However, once the first class began, Professor Winans blew away any expectations I had! His lectures were very easy to follow and the way he described the contents on his powerpoints instantly captured my attention!

Dr. Winans is a nice, caring guy. I sometimes skip lectures but when I do go, it's just to hear what he has to say. The material is often clear and if you do the work, you should be fine. The class was moved online halfway through the semester but I feel like it is manageable both ways. He is also responsive to students.
Really nice professor who is very knowledgeable. A bit too heavy on the lecturing for my preference but I'm sure it works for some people. Overall a great guy

Professor Winans is one of my favorite professors at Cornell! He is extremely passionate on the subject and is more than willing to help you. The material can be specific, but attending lecture is definitely useful in order to know what to study for quizzes/exams. He also adjusts grading of quizzes/exams to bump up grades. Highly recommend!

Steve was a great professor. His quizzes can be a little tough but he will adjust the curve to make sure the average is an acceptable score. His powerpoint slides are so informative and detailed that I still referred back to them even when I was taking upper level classes. He makes you work for your grade but we're at Cornell so what do you expect?

Unfortunately, Winans has been the worst Professor Ive ever had at Cornell thus far. He single handily ruined Microbiology for me. The main problem for me was how disorganized his portion of the class was. He also directly contradicts his syllabus by putting multiple correct answers MC questions on his prelims/quizzes. Dont take Microbio with him

The course was disorganized and his half of the course was even more so. His lectures never followed the lecture schedule, and his lack of assigned readings made it hard to know what to reference for extra explanation. He wasn't incredibly pleasant when I spoke to him either. He is knowledgeable about his field, but he ruined the subject for me
I really enjoyed his classes. He has a really relaxing voice, so beware of going to class tired.

very enjoyable class because of his great personality. material may be difficult and very detailed but he is willing to explain! weekly partner quizzes (MC) based on homework (MC), prelims based on HWs and quizzes. material is only lecture based and figures can be confusing so attendance is a must!
One of the best professors I have had at Cornell! Made lectures very interesting, and it was very obvious how knowledgable he is. Definitely recommend taking this class.
Great professor!! Loved him!!! Totally recommend this class. Quizzes are sometimes very specific and annoying, and final was kinda hard too.. but overall, it was very fine!

I thought Winans was a nice guy and pretty good professor. His quizzes were pretty straightforward, but his final exam was somewhat difficult (had some short answers in addition to multiple choice). Anyways, you'll enjoy this class if you take it.

He is wryly amusing, yet his work is impeccable, his presentation thorough. Remarkably refreshing, he way he humanizes the sometimes arcane world of microbiology. My interest in science, never above middling warm, grew over the course of the term to a positive snap, crackle and pop. I won't opt into Bio as a major, but Winans is simply awesome.
he is overall very decent - very clear and highly approachable - however, he's sometimes unorganized / goes too slow.

Taught the 2nd half of general microbio. when Ghiorse took a sabbatical leave.  He wasn't quite as clear as G. but went into more depth in lecture, which I appreciated.  He's very passionate about microbio and readily answers student questions in class.  Quizzes got harder w/ him, but studying the material made you appreciate the class more.
Professor Winans was hard but a good lecturer and taught in depth. I actually learned a lot. It was very interesting.

Professor Ichikawa is very funny but some say that she asks more difficult questions during discussion. Format of the class is the same as JAPAN1101 - daily discussion, two lectures a week, and the occasional quiz/test. Frequently you'll have to memorize whole dialogues to act out during class.

Great class with interesting readings and a professor that clearly knows what he is talking about. However he will spend most of lecture discussing things that are only tangentially related to the readings. Grading feels tough during the semester but isn't actually that bad by the end. Would recommend.
Great professor and super nice guy. The readings for this class are heavy and the work is very theoretical. Would take again.

Extraordinarily knowledgeable and gives very passionate lectures. Not afraid to challenge students with difficult, controversial, but phenomenal texts! Go to lectures, and you will be fine. Only downside is that he is so popular, and it's hard to get time during his office hours, especially in a big class.

He's passionate but it doesn't make political theory more interesting. Grading is based on 2 papers worth 25% each, section participation worth 25%, and an essay final worth 25%. Tons of reading - we're averaging a book or so every week. Seems like a great guy and an intellectual. Just not for me.

Take his class!!!! One of the best lecturers you will encounter at Cornell! Jason Frank is absolutely brilliant and the class wasn't that difficult. The median was an A-, so as long as you read the material and listen to the lectures you are fine.

average professor who seems good because of passion and delivery. grading is based 3 papers and discussion. lectures generally have little to do with the actual paper prompts. if ur a good writer and can understand the readings well and incorporate that into ur essays u can get an A
Jason Frank is an Intellectual, listen and learn

He is so far my favorite professor at Cornell. The reading material is quite difficult, but his lectures magically conveys the ideas in those texts in a clear and in-depth way. He is extremely passionate about the topic and he interacts with students in his lectures actively. All these aspects adds to the attractiveness of his personality.
best
BEST and HOTTEST professor ever. Smart. Eloquent. Passionate. Helpful. Great lecturer. Nough said.

Very interesting material and fascinating lectures you won't want to miss. Also, you shouldn't miss them, because you will struggle with the papers if you don't go to lecture. Material is hard, but getting an A is not overly difficult
He is a great professor, and actually peaked my interest in Theory. Don't miss lecture though, because he does have a lot to say.

He was just ok. Very passionate about the subject, but his lectures were wandering and sometimes lacked focus. It was his first time teaching the large lecture course, so perhaps he's better in smaller settings...

Professor Frank is outstanding.  He has the unique ability to direct discussion to bring out the most interesting and thought-provoking elements of American political theory.  Any class with him is highly recommended.  If you work hard, you will do very well.

He expects a lot, stimulates interest, and makes you think critically about American political thought -- and this was a writing seminar.  If you want to learn, and you're willing to do some work, take any class he teaches.
My favorite professor at Cornell! He's very knowledgable and is a great teacher.. He makes class very interesting especially through the discussions. I liked the final project too.
charismatic, easy to follow, makes u wanna go to lecture, super passionate, simplifies complex concepts, explicitly says what he'd ask on a test
Very charismatic lecturer; made me excited to go to class
Amazing, passionate professor. Does a great job at explaining difficult concepts. I learned a lot from him. Also clear about what material will be tested on. Really enjoyed his lectures!!
Very good explanations and teaching
Too hard to get a good grade
Very helpful and engaging. Approachable and nice. Really gets you interested in the material. Love her!
Serious and professional

All you need to know is dont take this guys class if you see his name. He will count off a whole letter grade if you dont show up to class 3 times. Newbie professor who shouldnt be a professor. I put 5 difficulty because if you want to make anything above a B with how he grades it is gonna be borderline impossible. An A+? FORGET ABOUT IT

6 weeks in the class was renamed, which was quite dishonest. Very reading heavy class. Peter does not grade very well, he claims that if you perform "as expected" you can best get a B, but to get an A requires being "all around polished" - whatever that means. He mandates you have cameras on and expects participation even when asking poor prompts.

The worst professor I've ever had. She's horrible at communicating information, often confuses herself with content, and ends up teaching incorrect info. Then she'll quiz you on information she hasn't taught you or taught you incorrectly and stubbornly convinces herself that she didn't. Never seen so many students dislike a professor this much.

Really great professor and lecturer. Lectures were detailed and clear, content roughly correlated with the textbook, and homework was pretty easy if done after reading the book. Lecture slides directly correlated to test questions, and plenty of flexibility with choosing paper topic (there was 1 big paper when I took this class).

Wish I could give a better rating, because he seems like a nice guy who enjoys what he teaches about, but the quality of the class unfortunately doesn't reflect that very well. Hopefully, this class will improve when things return to in-person learning this Fall.

Absolutely horrible lectures that were disorganized and not even close to the material the was on the problems sets, and the tests were even more different than that. The paper had little-no guidance and the expectations were extremely unclear. Worst class I have ever taken by far

I am so disappointed in my experience in this class since it has always gotten good reviews. Professor Lee's lectures are jumbled and disorganized, there is no order to the information. There are three exams plus a 12 page final paper, the tests are impossible. The paper is usually optional but this year we all "have nothing better to do" w COVID.

RUDE and UNCLEAR in grading criteria. The syllabus said that problem sets count towards our final grade but towards the end of class he said they didn't. He showed no understanding towards student technology issues that arose from the switch to virtual learning. His lecture slides are informative but his testing format is extremely confusing.

I am a student who struggles with economic, subjects but is interested in international relations, so I was very worried about this class. However, Prof. Lee's lectures were absolutely fascinating and really made complex subjects crystal clear. He is extremely accessible and really teaches content that is relevant to the real world.

Professor Lee is one of the best professors/lecturers I've had at Cornell. He's really passionate and it comes across in his lectures. Some topics are slow but he's engaging. You definitely have to go to class and listen to do well on the exams, but that's all it really takes. Standard grading structure and hw's are easy and count for a big chunk

DO NOT take this class. Prof seems so overqualified to teach this stuff that he almost seems more bored than the few ppl that still go to class. Terrible at explaining things, unstructured coursework, and uninteresting. A decent effort at studying for the tests result in a good grade, probably because of the massive curve. Still a waste of time

I went in thinking this would be an easy A. Turns out Prof. Lee isn't the best lecturer and his slides could not be more vague or useless. Highly recommend not taking this course, unless you're ready to do heavy reading and learn the slides by heart. In addition to this his prelims means are low (78-80 range) and questions are terribly worded.

Worst professor ever. His class is so boring. He doesn't teach anything. The problem sets don't make any sense because he never does anything with his class. His tests are based off of obscure facts in his horrible powerpoints. WORST TEACHER

He's a nice guy and has an interesting sense of humor. The class isn't too hard, partly because of the content, and also because it's AEM and all AEM classes are easy. As long as you go to lecture you'll be fine. Tests aren't too bad, but do have some specific facts here and there. Sadly no calculations are done on tests.
Very good professor in an interesting class.  Not difficult to get an A if you put the work in, some of the material will be hard if economics and a little finance isn't your thing.
Be prepared to memorize a lot. Lee is a good instructor, but his exams are based on very specific terms from both the book and his lectures. He definitely makes the class harder than it could be.
not a difficult class. never read textbook and did well on all prelims. go to lecture and memorize notes and will be fine

I really liked how the course is structured and given. Prof Lee is a really good lecturer and he gives a thorough picture of what international trade and finance is all about. But if you are not a big fan of memorize stuff, you might wanna think twice before enrollment. In spite of all that, it is a great course. I would recommend it to others.

He's a good lecturer. However, he penalizes students who are good at analytical problems but not rote memorization by making exams almost entirely memorization based. So if you can analyze the effect of a trade policy analytically but don't remember trivial facts like how many jobs have been outsourced - tough luck, you're not going to do well.

Good class. Prof Lee expects a lot for a 2000-level class but is fair. Very organized and easy to follow, but some of the lecture stuff is not easy. Go to class and read the lecture notes and book and you can do well.

Good professor, but hard class if you don't go to lecture. Prof. Lee expects you to be there. Very clear lecturer, nice guy but all business in class. No hard class material but he expects you to work. Don't take this class if you're expecting an easy class with no work.

Course is really good; Prof. Lee is very analytical, sometimes hard, sometimes really easy. He presents economics in an intuitive way. Lots of discussion of current events in trade, international finance. Heavy use of the course texts, but you must go to class if you want to do well.

If you're willing to work and want to learn international economics, this is the course to take. Prof. Lee is mostly all business and isn't there to entertain, which some students don't like. He tries to present material in an intuitive way and tries hard to make sure all students understand. One of the best prof's I've had at Cornell!
Excellent prof. Clear lectures --wants to make sure students understand material. Make economic concepts easy to understand. Has high expectations of students and doesn't patronize.

Take this class only if you're interested in the subject matter. Lee is relatively boring and pretty mean and unhelpful. In order to do well you pretty much have to go to every lecture because tests have a lot of stuff that is found only in class. Don't bother with the reading but go to the optional sections which will help a lot with the hmwk.

Could be a pretty difficult class.  The homeworks are easy and it definitely helps to go to discussion sections.  Some of the material is unclear and rushed.  The exam format sucks.  Lee could be a meanie if you come in late, don't pay attention or talk in class, etc...

Easy class and Prof. Lee is a good professor.  I expected the material to be boring but he managed to present it in an interesting way.  Contrary to what some people have said, the exams were very much based on the homeworks.  Attending the optional sections was helpful and is recommended.
Needs to use powerpoint.

Not that hard a course. Very organized lectures. Clearly taught. Some the material is technical (boring), but Prof Lee tries to make it come home to students. One of the best courses I've had at Cornell.
Excellent course. Hard material but very well organized and understandable lectures. He tries to make economics intuitive to students. One of best courses I've had at Cornell.
Dry material; poor evaluation methods.  Horrible writer of multiple choice exams. Smart guy, though.

Possibly one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Prof. Lee has managed to completely turn me away from economics.His midterms and finals have absolutely nothing to do with the course. You can do great on HW and terribly on the rest.Lectures are boring
Pretty hard class for being 200 level.  The teacher is kind of full of himself, but he's a smart guy.  I learned a lot in it.

A horrible human being. First class on the first day, this guy had the audacity to say that there is a "genocide in Gaza" out of nowhere. This made me and other students who have family in Israel extremely uncomfortable and I hope no one takes him in any classes.

Michael is exceptional. His class is super engaging; from the books he selects for readings to his analysis of them during class, it makes the class so much more interesting and relevant. Most importantly, he really cares about his students, and was the most understanding professor I had this semester when unexpected personal things came up.

I LOVE Professor Lee. In this FWS class, we had homework every class, but it was simply to read short stories. Due to medical reasons, we only had 1 essay which he graded easily. He's a very caring and passionate teacher who genuinely cared for the well-being of the class (he even moved deadlines when we were stressed)! Can't rave about him enough
Absolutely love her.. ILR has some hidden gems and shes one of them.
Best professor at cornell by far. She made a 3 hour night class fun. I do not even realize the time flying while in class. Fabulous class.

Easily the best course I have taken, as a rising senior in ILR, so far in my time at Cornell. I genuinely loved attending class each week. Every single student at Cornell should enroll in this course: super light workload and unbelievably useful skills learned which I have already put into practice.

Prof. Lee is a great professor who makes a 3 hour night class something you don't hate going to. Lectures are packed with great frameworks to approach negotiations and include in person negotiations every time. Taking this course would add a great skillset to your toolbox
difficult class but loved the professor

Professor Lee was great at organizing the class, especially for those with no prior experience with Python (or any coding program, for that matter). The assignments were a little boring but overall they proved essential for learning and practicing the basic tenets of coding. I personally was not a fan of coding in general, but she made it bearable.

I was a repeat cs1110 student this spring (took walker white last fall). Bracy and Lee are a great combo for teaching and I found the assignments more interesting than in the fall, and therefore I was more engaged and completed the course successfully. If possible I would wait until the spring to take this course. I feel more confident in cs now.

Very smart, and extremely responsive outside of class, especially on Ed discussion. Class is terrifically run, and she truly wants everyone to succeed. My only complaint is that the assignments got boring, because a bunch in a row at the end of the year were on the same topic. But overall, a very good professor.

Prof. Lee was the backbone of CS 1110. She is an extremely intelligent woman who knows a lot and makes sure you know that. She makes interesting tests that make you think, but I was annoyed with how the last 3 assignments were all on the same topic: Songs and Mixes. Also, the one lecture she taught was so poorly run and we didn't finish the lesson.

Took this class with little experience in coding and it was great! Assignments were tough at times but going to office hours was helpful even though I only went once. You can tell that she wants her students to succeed. She always tried her best to answer any questions and the practice materials that she gave us were helpful for exams.

Love Prof. Lee as a person and for asking questions outside of class, but they lectured once (Prof. Bracy was out) and it was the most incomprehensible lecture I've ever received. Again, she's so incredibly smart and helpful, until it comes to lectures.

Professor Lee wrote all of the programs throughout this class on assignments and examinations. Class as a whole was very fast moving, and it was hard for a non-Stem major to succeed. Professor Lee ensured that all questions were answered in a quick manner, just class as a whole is a tough class, should only be taken by those who have to take it.

Lee is an incredible professor! She didn't lecture for 1110 (Bracy did) but she crafted all the labs and assignments. The labs were immensely helpful in learning new material and the assignments--though rather difficult--prepared you greatly for exams. She's always willing to help: talking after class, responding on Piazza, or meeting individually.

Lillian is one of the best teachers I have had the privilege to be taught by ever. To start with, she 's so freaking cute and adorable and  so so smart in a dorky way,she'd explain things in a way that she would not only uncomplicate stuff but also make concepts really fun and interesting.  I would never miss any of Lillian's lectures.
Her and prof Merschner do all they can to help.

I took this class with zero computer science background and ended up dropping it. It was with out a doubt the hardest thing I've ever had do at Cornell. Asking questions I always felt like the dumbest person in the room. I'm sure the professor was nice, but the subject she taught was way over my head I guess.
Lillian Lee is the****. She knows a lot and is very passionate about what she is teaching. She's super silly, but a mad genius sort of way.

Lee knows what she's talking about.  Class was interesting, but was also alot of work per problem set.  Still, lee was a great lecturer and kept me awake even as the first class of the day.  Average performance in the class was reasonable too.

I took it the first time it was offered. A lot of people did complain but I thought that she knew her material and the class was well directed. And she definitely is funny in a smarty-pants sort of way,made me laugh several times during the sem. Brilliant

amazing class!  it was really a lot of fun and very interesting (i took it the SECOND time it was offered -- the first time i hear was terrible...) -- lee is a very funny teacher, shes brilliant, knows her material, and lectures well on a hard level
Very interesting and great class. Highly recommend taking this class. It is not terribly difficult and half of the class is participatory discussion. Loved it!

Not a particularly hard class and very interesting material, however, her lectures are monotonous and lack any clear objectives. She does not appear to be interested in teaching the class delivering the material in an uninteresting manner supplemented by poor lecture notes. As such there is almost no point in going to class.

Very enthusiastic lecturer but course content was not at the level of an introductory course. Very little foundational info was given to build a basic understanding of complicated concepts. Grading guidelines for homeworks and exams were unclear, but revisions were allowed for exams for up to 50% of points back.

Dr. Lee was draconian on deadlines and massive points were taken off minor mistakes. Though engaging in his lectures, the course material was not appropriate for an introductory-level course and labs often contributed little to the understanding of the concepts except to provide additional workload.

Prof. Lee is a very smart, funny and caring guy, however he may have not been the best choice for an intro class. His exams are hard and there are few resources to help you prepare for them outside of the in class powerpoints. The TAs for this class were incredibly unhelpful, so it is difficult to seek help unless you go to his few office hours.
Pretty solid choice for an ENGRI. Dr. Lee was a good professor, and the content covered seemed very relevant to current Biomedical Engineering. It wasn't too hard either.

Pretty easy Spanish class if you are confident with your Spanish. Class is almost completely taught in Spanish and students are asked to actively participate (in Spanish only). Not a heavy homework load, and we spend a lot of time going over grammar rules in class, but they aren't taught very well. Watch a lot of videos and listen to songs.

I conducted a project travel initiative with Dr. Flores and she's knowledgeable however she demotivated me as an educator and professional in general with derogatory remarks and belittling commentary. At the end of the day, I obtained my hard-earned A+ in the class  YEARS after I excelled as an educator and administrator.
She used her phone to take notes and remark on presentations; some professors use a notebook; she's techie savvy!  Didn't like size of class for a grad course not good practice!

Oftens texts/checks her email on her phone during class when students are presenting or teaching. Then will send an email that you will "not be a good teacher" if you do the same, following her example.

I've no doubt that Professor Flores is more than sufficiently technically proficient to teach this class; however, Dr. Flores uses her classroom as a venue for addressing issues of a clearly personal (and I suspect traumatic) nature that would be much more appropriately and profitably addressed in a professional  psychotherapeutic environment.
Smart but reply insecure - a dreadful combination  of traits in a teacher.  Radically disaffirming.  Probably has eaten her own young.

She is generally rude to students, especially through email. She thinks she's so culturally aware she can stereotype people--she said extremely insensitive things to many students, in front of the class. (For instance, an Asian girl would blush and act demure when given a compliment!) She also never admits she's not sure, or accepts others' ideas.

Dr. Flores thinks very highly of herself, and very lowly of her students. Her expectations are very unclear to anyone but herself, and she got very frustrated easily. She doesn't even seem to know what she wants, because we would do what she said in the syllabus and then she tore us apart over it because she had said something different in class.
Extremely scholarly and very helpful with help outside the classroom.

Questionable grading practices. She plays favorites and keeps the class late. I tried to meet with her outside of class once and she was completely unreasonable telling me she could speak to me in a few months!!!! BEWARE.
no connection between what she teaches and her projects. very unclear instructions. needs to organize her semester plan keeping her students in mind.
Tough course if you are not in linguistics. But after having only taken lit classes in Spanish, I find that my Spanish isn't that good when it comes to other areas of study
Met her several times in the office and gave me excellent help w/ my project and with questions about the course.

The course is tough since I  only have taken lit courses in the past. The course is related to linguistics so if your Spanish is not good, it is a tough course to follow. The professor used lots of visuals but the discussions were over my head!
It is a hard course and you need to know Spanish to handle the course. It is challenging and difficult. If you don't like to read, don't enroll in the course!

The class itself is not very exciting, but she makes it worse! Can be discouraging and gets into arguments with people when they don't agree with her. Very knowledgable but lacks people skills. Made a girl cry in class!

As long as you are on her good side, you will be okay. Don't argue with her because that will get you on her bad side. Class was relatively easy because the exams were just essay questions that she gave you a week in advance. There was a research project but it was not that hard.

She is the worst professor at Rutgers. She needs to be fired! She has an attitude problem. Her class is hard and boring. She is very negative and discourging. Do NOT take this class with her u will regret it.

She knows her stuff but she's awful. She makes you earn your grade, assigns losts of reading and tests your knowledge of it during class. Attendance and participation in class is mandatory. Her class is boring and pointless to take unless ur a Spanish major. DON'T recommend it to anybody!!!!
No Comments

Lectures are long and she digresses quite a bit; its really tough to maintain attention.  She's very passionate about research and is an incredible source of guidance in this field.  I never had trouble getting in contact with her.  Very sharp with a great (weird) and unexpected sense of humor.

This professor was next to impossible to get into contact with. I tried texting, calling and emailing her. The only time I was successful in catching her was at the end of class. Class was also a long drawn out lecture. Unfortunately, I did not have the best experience in this class.

This professor is extremely passionate about the field and highly motivates us to love literature. She is very helpful and an easy grader. Class can get a little tiring but whenever unsure of something she will clear it up when contacted.

For online Statistics, she is like a moderator. Pre-recorded video lectures are by other professors/experts. Is clear about requirements. Provides helpful online resources. Lots of important reading. Graphing calculator use mandatory. Don't be scared of the calculator. Learn from the tutorials, watch the videos, follow her guides. You'll do great.

Don't expect her to teach you because she doesn't think its her job! Red flags: grading criteria was based on a whim, she expected that we knew the content before we walked in, and the exams had trick questions! My most vivid memory of her is when she embarrassed a classmate for asking a question that she thought was dumb (I had the same question).

Actually took MAC2313 course, she wasn't as bad as the other reviews say, she was respectful and liked participation. Her lectures focus more on how to do the calculus rather than the conceptual aspect which had its pros/cons. Tests were straightforward but hard. No final since it was summer term. Exercises on Webassign help to study.

Not a very responsive professor. Just be ready to teach yourself if online. It is challenging, but doable. There is a couple helpful extra credit reviews available. Module tests can be taken twice(20% of your grade). The midterm and final are worth a total of 60% of your grade. Midterm and final are not based on questions in tests and quizzes.

Awful. Doesn't care to help. Vague emails. Wouldn't be passing if it wasn't for teaching myself and going to Thuc in the tutoring center. Avoid her. I was going to email the academic chair to see if there was anything I could do to get into a different prof's class... SHE IS THE ONE IN CHARGE! *mind blown* Who gave her that job??

Not very caring, will not help struggling students. Possibly a better teacher in person but as far as online goes she will not respond to emails quickly and when she does she says very little back. Again, not a helpful teacher. Had to teach myself calculus which is why I got a D. Also, the final exam was NOTHING like the previous tests she gave.
It was hard to get her to give you feedback on the Homework and quizzes, she had issues following the syllabus and changed the date of our final twice. I was just happy to be done with that class.

The first 2 test in college algebra were really hard but after the 2 the next 2 are easy she does give extra credit she also does tutoring she really does want all her students to pass. You just have to show up to class everyday and ask all the questions you need
Worse Teacher Ever
Failed course, wouldn't take this professor. Good luck trying to pass Calculus. Terrible at grading, non consistent.

DOES NOT RESPOND TO EMAILS WITHIN A 24 HOUR PERIOD AS PER THE SYLLABUS. DOES NOT UPGRADE GRADES DAILY AS PER THE SYLLABUS, DOES NOT CARE TO LET YOU USE NOTES ON THE EXAMS WHICH ARE ALL PROCTORED. COURSE IS EXTREMELY TEST HEAVY, WEIGHTED GRADE SYSTEM 30% EXAMS, 40 % FINAL EXAM 16% QUIZZES AND 14% HOMEWORK. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

One of the worst professors I have ever come up with. You cannot make simple mistakes or forget what she taught you in chap 2 or 3 if you do she gets mad. what for Nydia? we are students, we came here to learn not to be masters of Calculus. There are better ways to teach Calculus, I can guarantee she can't even teach her own kids calculus.
Professor Nelson is exceptional!!! By far my favorite professor I've ever had. She's straight to the point, doesn't require your camera to be on, and she's always available to help.
She doesn't teach. She just gives you videos to watch.

basically everything is on pearson and nothing is really taught or explained. the midterm and final are NOTHING like the practice. I spent hours reviewing the practice and passed every time and then took the test and was shocked at how the review had none for the examples.

Not sure why she has the rating she does. I think she's great. Yes, for an online class all of the work is done in MyMathLab but she doesn't have the exam in there (which makes a huge difference). She also lets you make up any assignments you missed with no penalty. Calculus is hard and having a flexible teacher makes all the difference.
not as much the teacher as much as it is MyMathlab being the worst program ever invented. DO NOT take this class online i was forced to by COVID
Unhelpful and rude consistently, had to continuously fight for grades I got that she graded wrong or refused to put in.

Doesn't care if you're confused and won't re-explain anything. Very mean if you ask a question in or after class. NO study guides for tests. Assigns several lengthy projects that are very difficult if you're not proficient in Excel. I felt like I was being set up to fail the entire semester. My other classes suffered because of it. Horrible.

Worst class i've ever taken, waste of time and money. Wish I never took this class. I did great in hw, quizzes, discussions, c and d on the 2 tests, but bombed the midterm and final which is graded aggressively and harshly. I looked at the statistics of grades and more than half the class failed the midterm and final which means most failed.

Do the HW, because her reviews are nothing like the tests so don't rely solely on reviews. She is a very tough grader, she wants you to write out everything step by step and to always keep the symbols. She's definitely a great professor, very funny, always responds to emails quickly and helps out of class. put in the time and you will pass.

I'm a math major. What's disappointing is this professor does NOT respond to emails. I'm an A student and this is my first C. Lectures aren't even from her. They're recordings from the 90s when StatDisk was a thing. It's 2018 and we're taught to use our TI-84 calculators. I had to Youtube everything. BAD PROFESSOR BEWARE!! Take the class elsewhere.
Communication is terrible. I emailed the professor 4 times during the semester and only got a reply once.

Pretty tough on grading and a bit hard to meet with, but I'd recommend discussing projects with her beforehand to work out any issues, since she's really experienced in her field and will easily identify holes in your projects. Pretty nice to talk with face to face. Will randomly call on students during class. Interesting but disengaging lectures.
Very critical. Not one for constructive criticism just pure criticism. You have to say and reproduce exactly what she wants to hear.
Dr. Nelson is kind of intimidating. She will shut your ideas down if she doesn't agree with them. She also will not hold back on tearing apart your work. She is very hard to please.
This class is easy and interesting! The teaching team is so caring and passionate about the subject. Overall, such a great class.
Nice professor and generally good class, content is kinda dry and one-sided for those really passionate about public health. show up, ready the book and  you'll do well
Passionate and smart professor; great class overall.

Although the class is generally low effort and there are few assignments, so as long as you do well on those you can get a good grade. She barely knows how to use canvas so the site was a mess. All the assignments and exams were CANVAS MULTIPLE CHOICE QUIZZES. There were calculations in the questions but no chance for partial credit

She makes lectures as interesting as possible and always makes sure to answer students' questions throughout class, thoughtfully. She grades with mildly high expectations of what students will submit (specifically final paper draft and other materials). Readings discussion posts twice a week are assigned.

Professor Slayton was amazing. She was engaging as a professor, cared about my success, and kept the lectures and readings interesting. The readings are long and are assigned for each class but are very important for success.

Professor Slayton is great! Her slides are detailed and informative. Her quizzes are very fair and she tells you exactly what she expects, and everything comes from the slides. The readings were a little challenging, but before quizzes, she reviews concepts from them that she wants you to know. Her paper assignments are graded fairly as well.

I don't really write reviews, but Prof Slayton is someone that deserves the recognition for her work and care for her students. Readings can be technical, but she really breaks them down to help you understand. Can get kind of boring, but the concepts are still interesting. Grading is very clear, and she gives A LOT of help and feedback on essays.
Super clear and enthusiastic lectures. Exams are really easy

She is extremely knowledgable in her field and does a great job of sharing her enthusiasm.  She provides excellent feedback and is always willing to help out with writing strategies, assignments, and etc.  The class was extremely enjoyable and interactive.

She pretty much knows everything there is to know about in the Baroque + Classical periods, whether be instrumental, vocal, dance, opera, etc. She will boost your love and appreciation for music to a new height.

Extremely interesting - this prof is super knowledgable and discussion sections were great too. Lots of work for a 3 credit class but definitely worth it. Would recommend to anyone interested in opera!

Way too much work for a 1000-level and 3-credit course. Not an understanding professor and seems to think her class is the only one in existence. Although there are no pre-reqs, the class is taught as if the students all have a pretty high level of understanding of music. Would not recommend.

Funny and caring, and a fantastic lecturer. Her assignments take some effort but are rewarding. Over a year after I took this course I happened to run into her; not only did she remember me but we chatted warmly for ten or fifteen minutes. Highly recommended!

Professor Schneider is wonderful; her class isn't difficult and at all and she genuinely cares about students and wants us to learn the material.  Overall just a really lovely prof and I had a good experience in the class.
Professor Schneider is very passionate and it comes through in her lectures! She is very helpful and the class is interesting.
Rebecca is invested in this subject and her students. Best class I've taken at cornell even though is was a 9:05

Professor Weiner Heinemann is one of the most flexible, understanding, and caring teachers I've ever had. She truly cares about the subject and her engaging teaching style makes students care as well. I've learned so much  in her class, and my writing skills have improved so much.

Professor Weiner Heinemann is the kindest professor I have ever had the pleasure of having. She is understanding of student struggles and helps to find the best solutions for any issues students may have. She is knowledgeable in the subject and is a fantastic lecturer. I would jump on the opportunity to take a class with her again in the future.

Amazing class and professor! There are weekly reflection papers, a take-home exam, and a major group project (Covid-19 breakdown). One of the best professors I have had at Cornell. Really cares about her students and will give more feedback on your papers than you write. Take a class with her!!

Professor Weiner Heinemann was one of the most influential professors I had during college, and I still think about her class and her teaching even though I've already graduated. The class was informative and relevant to current events, and discussions were impactful. I highly recommend taking a class with Professor Weiner Heinemann.
Incredibly caring and helpful professor. One of the best classes I have taken at ILR. I learned so much about disability studies and my writing improved a ton. Definitely take her writing seminar!

Her disability law writing seminar only has two papers. She will provide line by line feedback from your draft on both papers, and you are required to meet with her at least once for each paper. Seems like a tough grader but grades are forgiving in the end.

I can say unequivocally say that Professor Heinemann is the best professor I have ever had. Her lectures are always so interesting and helpful in understanding disability studies. I specifically took her Writing Seminar in Law class about disability studies which was wonderful. She gives a lot of feedback on rough drafts, it's great!

Professor Weiner is absolutely incredible. Her class is hard, but the work is meaningful and useful. She provides extremely helpful feedback - line by line feedback in the writing seminar. There is no textbook, just readings from articles. However, there is still a decent amount of reading. Also learned sm about disability studies. Take her class!

Professor Weiner is an absolute gem of a human. She is so kind and really cares about improving her students writing abilities. She gives really detailed feedback on each draft of your essay. I highly recommend taking a writing seminar with her.

Professor Weiner is by far the best professor I have ever had at Cornell and in ILR. I loved this class and am trying to take another one of her classes again. My writing improved so much because of all of her detailed feedback.

Incredible, tremendously thoughtful and helpful professor. I grew as a writer and a thinker from this class. I have never encountered anyone so invested in the students. I will admit the material was difficult, but she is always willing to help. It was a delight to take a class with Professor Weiner Heinemann and I highly recommend it.
Amazing professor. She truly cares about your growth as a writer and a thinker. Best professor I've had at ILR.

Although the class is long (2.5hrs), the lectures were always interesting. There were 3 reading quizzes (only 2 counted), a midterm & final. Otherwise, u write a quick 5 sentence reflection at the end of each class. Grading is clear cut and class is reasonably easy. There is a lot of readings (go to office hours and she will give you tools to help)

Professor Weiner Heinemann is easily one of the best professors at ILR. While her course is definitely not the easiest way to fulfill the sophomore writing requirement, it is definitely among the ones that will teach you the most. She will challenge you and you will leave her classroom a better writer. Needless to say, her grading is also very fair

This professor is one of the best I have had while in the ILR school at Cornell University! Though her paper assignments are difficult, she is extremely helpful and will go out of her way to assist you. My writing has improved exponentially and I am so glad I took this class.

Hands down one of the best professors that I have had at Cornell. She’s brilliant, funny, approachable, and (genuinely) interested in her students. She is always willing to go above and beyond to make sure that you understand the material.

Professor Weiner is an exceptional instructor. My writing skills improved dramatically from taking her writing seminar. She expects A LOT of work, but is very willing to offer help if you ask for it.I would recommend her class, but am willing to admit that it was not an easy way to fulfill the advanced writing requirement.
