The only thing that took away from his class was the horrible section. However, a good TA would only help improve his class bc the material can be very difficult. I RECOMMEND IT

TAKE THIS CLASS! It's a difficult course (lots of reading, abstract/theoretical concepts) but Katzenstein is a brilliant, engaging lecturer, and actually not that difficult to follow. Absolutely worth the work. Best class I've taken at Cornell by far.

An incredible lecturer.  I looked forward to his lectures, he knows a lot and makes the information interesting and accessible.  That said, it is a very hard class with a lot of reading, but it is all worth it.

He is usually a funny engaging prof. Yet, the amount of reading given was extreme. I have not seen more reading in 300-level government classes here that are even in the same field. He is an expert in IR, unfortunately his brilliance does not shine through in this intro-level course. Try one of his upper-level courses if you really want to take him
Great guy, fun lectures, but often confusing. The reading were good, but there were far too many for a 100 level class.
Take this class! Very hard and lots of reading (all on the exams) but SO worth it. Katzenstein is an amazing intellectual and professor at the top of his field.  He's my hero!

Best class ever- not easy, a lot of reading... but very interesting... almost nothing on the exams are from lecture- but it's worth it to show up, to do the readings, etc. Very relevant. The prof really connects otherwise abstract material to what is going on in the world.
Take this class... it will make you think hard, a lot of reading, but gives a new perspective on the world.  Especially important for this era we're in.
He was ranked by the economist as the most influential scholar in international political economy. His lectures are great, but you have to come prepared. Not an easy class

best class at Cornell. DO the readings. you cheat yourself if you don't. there is a lot to read but unlike other gov classes, this is all great. his lectures are extremely informative. he's also a genius. this is a MUST take. clear your schedule. this class taught me how the world really works.
Interesting, but had trouble staying awake during lecture.  Also, A LOT of reading.

Without a doubt, the best class I have taken at Cornell -- and also the hardest.  Seek out the TA's for help, and be sure to do most of the readings at some point.  In all honesty, this is the type of class makes Cornell a legitimate Ivy League school.  He expects a lot, but you'll learn so much about the world and be forever grateful you took 354.

He's very smart and has a lot of knowledge. Can be arrogant, but overall a nice guy (read lyrics of Sunscreen song on last day of class). A ton of reading, much of which you have to do. Exams are comprehensive and to do well you have to prepare far in advance. Also some basic economics knowledge is helpful for this course, though not necessary.
An amazing professor.  Katzenstein is brilliant and funny.  He's the best professor I've ever had and thanks to him I'm now a government major.  Be prepared to work a lot, but it'll pay off.
Lecture notes are a bit confusing but the man is a genius.

Best class I have ever taken.  Seriously.  Also perhaps the hardest class I've ever taken, but it's well worth it.  Katzenstein is absolutely amazing and now I'm gonna have to take every class he teaches.

If you have come to Cornell to learn how to think clearly and sharpen your mind, then don't waste your time on **** easy courses.  This course is life-changing and it is rare to find such a gem.  I hate to end on a cliche, but nothing really good comes without hard work.
He is one of the most pointless convolluted teachers I've ever had, what a waste of time
almost 2000pages of readings!  readings have no correlation to the lectures, though lectures are interesting.  he is very liberal.

Its a real shame this guy's not teaching this semester. Really smart and ties themes to current events very well. Class is not easy, lots of reading, but you can manage. Sometimes puts very personal, liberal opinions into lectures.
One of the most intelligent people I've ever met. Extremely friendly and helpful. A fantastic teacher.
nice man. bad lecturer.

Professor Katzenstein's grasp on political economy is amazing.  He is intelligent, articulate, and a great lecturer.  He adds current events into the class, making comprehension of the material very simple.  It's not a cakewalk, but not too hard either.

At risk of hyperbole, I'll just say he's the best professor I've had. period. His IR seminar is four hours at a stretch, and the class just never drags. What a fascinating mind, and as available as anyone would ever need outside of class. He is a gift.
Great Prof!  But it's a hard intro class.  He is one of the most brilliant professors you'll find at Cornell.  Make sure your in a good section that will help you handle all the reading.

Interesting course.  Nice teacher who listens to students.  Not always clear how the lectures tie in with the readings.  Never-ending reading. Still, good class.  Learned a lot.  Nice teacher--really knows his stuff--almost intimidating.

Goes well with the course, he knows his stuff. He, however, continuously bashes America too much. We understand he's a citizen now, but that does not mean he should force his negative personal views of America on his students. Overall, though, not bad.

Absolutely brilliant professor. You can't miss a course with him if you have any interest in Politics. The course is hard: lotsa reading. But you'll find him quoted on your readings! He's very knowleadgable.
Accent kinda rocks, even though it makes him harder to understand
Very interesting lectures. Great class

This is def. one of the best courses I've taken. The reading load is close to crazy but they're discussed in section so I wouldn't worry about it. The exams are not difficult and the lecture is very enjoyable!
Great professor... Great Guy... Great Lecturer.. Funny...and Hot as hell   If you do the readings (there is alot), the class is easy

This was probably the best class I ever took at Cornell. He is an amazing lecturer and absolutely brilliant. There's no doubt that it's tough, but you don't have to do absolutely all of the reading (as with any government class).
Lectures and course material are really interesting, but be prepared to read more than you probably will in most 300 and 400 classes.
This was the first government class that I took at Cornell.  He's a great lecturer but the amount of reading for the course was ridiculous.  Make him do the Terminator voice
Far too much reading for a 300 level course.  Interesting topic, however overt liberal bias evident in some lectures.

Great open-ended class where you get to work in a team on a real project that Prof. Jackson actually worked on before. There are no clear guidelines and answers, just like real life, but Prof. Jackson is very helpful and more willing to go the extra mile to get you in the right direction. One of the best classes at Cornell (and ORIE).
This class is very disorganized.  There is virtually no feedback on our proposals/projects.  We only got a grading rubric with three weeks of class left.
Jackson is the best professor I've had so far at Cornell; very helpful and tries to make things interesting. Lectures are quite slowly paced but contents are extremely useful.

I found most of the material in this class uninteresting (just not a good fit with my interests, it fascinates many other people I assure you). Professor Jackson, however, is hands down the nicest, most-approachable professor ever and I think that's what made this class bearable for me. Respect!

the lectures are okay, topics are mostly introduction to industrial systems. the prelims are 90% like the practice ones he posted on course website. a lot of practice prelims to do. i felt like a learned most of the courses through thos exams. I like, he's extremely nice during office hours and debugging for you.
Jackson is the nicest and most approachable engineering professor I've had. He was always very welling to response to questions before and after class.
The course material is very boring, but Jackson is not. He's  incredibly helpful during office hours and very easy to approach. It's a pretty easy class as well.

Jackson is the best prof i have had.lectures are boring power point slides, and often unclear but during office hours after class etc he is very helpful He helps you debug code and helps you figure out what went wrong to prevent it from happening again He takes an interest in getting to know his students and what will help them succeed in his class

I don't know what happened last year, but he literally implies he could give extra credit in return of a good review. I think he needs to focus on the quality of his course rather than finding a way around.

Very funny guy. Gives off the energy of the basketball coach who's forced to teach a class, except he's actually a decent lecturer and not actually a basketball coach. The psets are pretty long and require a solid background in coding. Idk why last years class resented him so much. People generally seemed to like him and the class this year

In most cases, Prof. Diamessis gives you a feeling that he just learnt the material a night before the lecture but not fully understood. Overall, the lack of quality in his class makes you question both his knowledge of the subject and intellectual rigor.

Prof Diamessis is a great guy and is very accommodating towards his students. However, his lectures are very difficult to follow. Psets/ Final project were difficult and TAs were unable to answer many questions in office hours, leaving students even more lost. Exams were doable but grading was extremelyyyyyy harsh on all assignments.

Prof D is a great person, but a terrible professor. He struggles to break down concepts to an understandable level, does not post lecture resources, has difficulties answering student questions, and never works through example problems. Worst of all, his TAs often don't understand the content and thus prelims and finals are graded SUBJECTIVELY.

He chooses his course time for a slot that is honestly waay too early, you'll notice that fewer students show up as a result. Problem set every week but assigned for teams of two, which makes things a little easier. Nice guy, though sometimes a little jumbled. Receives and utilizes student feedback effectively.

Probably the most down-to-earth, friendly professor I've had. Extremely helpful, responsive and pragmatic. Good with posting notes, homework, and practice exams that are relevant so missing class isn't a huge problem. He is the kind of guy you want to sit down and have a beer with.
Cool guy. Know his stuff and helps and cares his students at all times. Lots of coding for homework, but some are very conceptual as well. Exams are hard, but grading is fair.

Cooper's lectures are soaked in Freud (discredited neurologist). Literally tells students that they have p*n1s envy if they are WLW. Showed old movie from the 50s that featured marital r*pe, absolutely no warning, and caused huge panic attack. Tried to report to school, who said he's allowed to teach whatever he wants, even if dangerous/wrong.

Do not take this class period. I am currently enrolled in this class for online due to Coronavirus. He is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He does not know how to use canvas. If you take this class online you have to mail him your essay to his house because he doesnt know how to print from emails. He makes this class so frustrating.

Only 3 essays the whole semester and each one is on an excerpt that is 3 pages long. The professors talks for hours about random stuff and rants about stuff in tangents. You get an A on the essay by copying what he says in class and his opinions. He loves analysis of every little detail. It was an easy A for me but lots of people had a hard time.

Should've been fired a long time ago. Reads through the text and tells a few boring anecdotes that have nothing to do with the assignments. Graded on 3 LONG essays. Gives horrible feedback, very unclear grading criteria. Attendance is required but you can afford to take a few "mental health days" -- you'll need them. Bad lectures. DO NOT TAKE CLASS

Prof. Cooper likes to lecture A LOT and uses a single book for the whole semester, which is nice. If you can stand his rambling lectures and somewhat condescending attitude and you're good at writing LONG essays, then his class is an easy A.

Very tough grader and completely bores the entire class, not entertaining enough for the attention span of 35 college students. Writes on his entire erase board from top to bottom and across with illegible cursive and expects the students to jot it all down.

I rather liked this professor and author and I am surprised to see such bad reviews. I worked hard at his course (mostly because I wanted to--could have had an A with less) but it was interesting because he's somewhat old school and demands a certain coherence and sharp look. Knowledgeable and very nice person with a passion for film analysis..

This is literally the worst professor I've ever had. Avoid him like the plague. There are only three assignments; all of them essays, all of them at least 10 pages (mine averaged around 20). He has NO supplemental assignments. He is unclear as to what he expects from you and treats you like you're stupid for asking questions.

Can't believe he's still teaching after so many years and so many poor reviews. When I took his class, there was little to no access to the films he assigned. He came from LA where you could get these films at 7-11. No joke. I did my best. Got As in most other classes. He gave me an F. PS He was just as bitter in 1989!

I was pretty indifferent towards the ENG205 class. I think hes a bit short with students during lectures. Just make an effort to ask for help after his lectures. He tends to get lost in a train of thought and hates having to interrupt it. Not my favorite course, but an A really is achievable in his course, considering he allows rewrites.

Professor does not want you to think critically at all. He wants you to regurgitate exactly what he says. He is completely repetitive in his lecture and he only assigns 3 essays the entire semester with no clear grading criteria. 80% of the class was talking about a single essay and a film. His feedback is not helpful, just critical.

Honestly I have never even reviewed a professor before no matter how terrible I thought they were. Taking this class is punishing yourself, there is no critical thinking involved you have to use exactly his words, in exactly the way he wants you to or you will not pass. Im going to talk to the head of the English department file a formal complaint.

Worst professor Ive ever had. I never write reviews but everyone should AVOID him. The lectures are super boring, he spent 6 weeks repeating the same thing and then he says not to be repetitive when writing our essays. He gives essays back late and the feedback is very vague. I am an A student and I had to rewrite all my papers 3x to get a B.

Professor Cooper is a very smart professor. He knows his stuff and his accent is not at all difficult to understand. One thing you need to know to pass his class( 3 essays averaged) is that you have to know how to write papers. Pay attention and write good notes and you'll be solid.

I don't typically write reviews, however I felt the need to steer anyone away from this professor for English 205. In his class there are no group discussions, which makes it incredibly hard for many people including myself who tend to work better in an interactive setting. He also tends to repeat himself and make the class setting very awkward.

Omg worst teacher I have ever had. He only gives you a week to complete your essays and doesn't assign page requirements. I thought this was a 205 class not a 47A class. plus he repeats the same information and says write that down. He has us write like 3 essays talking about the same thing. This class was a waste of my time. DON'T TAKE COOPER!!!!

HE IS HORRIBLE! 3 papers total this semester, and he makes you think all is fine b/c  you get to rewrite it as much as you can, but there isn't enough time to and he gives the essays late into the semester. It is now a week before NOV break and we just got 1 essay back. He doesn't correct this essay or give it a grade he just says to rewrite it!!!

If you're on this page you are wondering if you should take his class. The answer is NO. Full - Not a professional teacher. He comes to class ranting about irrelevant things like his personal life. There are only 3 essays. No tests or HW, but he grades  VERY DIFFICULT.  I'm transferring with a 3.70 instead of a 3.78 because of this class. BEWARE.

The class only requires 3 essays, yet unless they are VERY thorough you will not get a good grade.  The trick to this class (and any) is just figuring out how Cooper works.  Expect to get a horrible grade on your 1st paper.  He doesn't make his expectations clear until the whole class  fails the first essay.  HOWEVER, he lets you rewrite all essays

Your grade is based on the 3 papers throughout the semester, he grades them extremely tough. I got my first C on a paper in a long, long time because I interpreted the film differently than he did. He crossed out entire pages of my papers. He will keep you until the very last minute (or past) of class. His lectures are long and boring.

Definitely one of the most boring and tedious classes I had to take. Lectures were long and I dreaded going. Essays were graded extremely harsh with little to no reasoning besides "you don't know what you're talking about" being written across my paper. If given the chance, avoid this professor at all costs necessary.

He honestly loved his class,tho I was a lazy student. Sometimes his voice was monotone, but content was enoughto keep me interested. I loved the film, Modern Times, that he showed in class and I refer to it often in other classes. He taught about the  effects of taylorism and originality in creative works (movies and novels) which he has a point.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Very rude and extremely old fashioned. He doesn't use email or the school site to upload assignments, no technology no nothing. He tells students, including  myself that we are terrible writers. He grades very harshly and won't give you feedback. If he does, you'll be lucky

Strunk and White would be appalled. For the first assignment he will give you a thematic statement to use which is odd to say the least. His writing style is unnecessarily wordy and he liberally uses scare quotes.  If you regurgitate his ideas in your papers you'll be fine, but if you disagree be ready to fail or at least not fare very well.
