Super nice, gives good feedback, tutorial homeworks every week but helps understanding course material. She doesn't take attendance but have clicker questions every lecture and that counts towards participation mark, so think twice before skipping, besides, Liisa's so much fun you won't wanna miss her class anyways.
She's an amazing prof and one of my favourites in the linguistics department. You will learn a lot and enjoy her class.
She knows her materials super well, gives good examples in class, handouts, tutorials, homeworks are all super helpful at aiding understanding of the materials

Liisa is an amazing prof and by far my favorite prof at york. She explains everything clearly, helps you out when you need it, and also does not ask you trick questions. I would recommend going to class since she explains the lecture notes in great detail in class and goes over every problem set. I would recommend taking any course she teaches!

Liisa was a wonderful prof, very knowledgeable on the topics. Incredibly kind and patient when someone doesn't understand and is willing to re-explain if needed. Gives very clear explanations of the assignments, midterm, and the final exam. No surprises. She makes the classes as interesting as she can even though it can be quite lecture-heavy.
Liisa really knows what shes talking about when it comes to phonetics (she's a phonetician after all), however she is a very picky grader and has trouble releasing grades in a timely manner.

She talks really fast because she understands the content and seems to have memorized her slides. She's approachable and engages in open conversation with students. For lectures, i suggest you take notes with a computer AND paper just because of how fast she talks

The best prof I have ever had. She cares about the students and genuinely wants them to do well. She has a variety of office hours so that everyone can come if needed. She is animated in her lectures and you can tell she enjoys the material. She posts her slides which is also super helpful. I would 100% recommend taking this course with this prof!!
I just started her class and I must admit she is really knowledgeable and approachable. I took this course (phonetics) at glendon and I despised it, she made me love it once again.

Liisa is a very good professor. She is super friendly and is there to help you. Phonetics is difficult but she is EXTREMELY fair and doesn't try to trick you in assignments or midterms. Everything asked is straight from her lectures, I didn't use the text and ended with an A+. Keep up with the notes and you will do great if you put in the effort!

Prof. Duncan is an excellent teacher. She genuinely cares about her students and is very approachable. She lectures in a clear and interesting way and gives out very helpful study sheets. Extremely helpful if you have questions and makes class enjoyable.

Prof Duncan is a very clear lecturer, consistently available outside class, and is very knowledgeable about her field. If you ask something she doesn't know the answer to, she will go out of her way to find an answer for you. Her lectures all come with slides & notes online, which don't replace going to class but help SO MUCH. Love this prof.

She is incredibly great. One of the best profs I've got at York. She is very caring and helpful in office hours. She is also very passionate and willing to explain as many times as possible and in the simplest and easiest way if you are confused about the material. Gives good feedback. It was my luck to have her as my Prof for last year courses.

She was probably the other prof that I actually enjoyed learning from. She is SO clear with her explanations, and is so nice to everyone. She genuinely wants everyone to do well, and ALWAYS asks if anyone needs any help, clarification etc.  I am actually lucky enough to get her again this year and I can't wait :)

Liisa Potts is what it means to be a good college professor. She keeps the class engaged with her witty satirical humor. If someone doesn't understand something, she goes out of her way to explain it in a different way. I wish she taught more classes here. And the shoes! Hot, hot, hot!
Took the night class a few quarters ago, she made English pretty fun, always had the assignments back in a timely manner, she was great!

Not really one of my better subjects but I still got an A because I really listened this semester and she seemed to help, maybe this is what it's like to finally be mature.  Very witty comments and her funny style is something I wish my other professors had.
My easiest class ever. Assignments are incredibly easy and are graded easily. She gets papers back quick and tests are almost ridiculous.

To be fair I would say that she(liisa) is funny, interesting,and fair. I didn't learn much. She made insults to many students. Don't expect her to answer any of your e-mails.Overall it was an okay class.

She is young, relatable, and nice. She gave out candy in an 'experiment' once. Youtube clips keep things interesting. Her quizzes are easy if you were paying attention at all. The exams weren't too bad. I would recommend her as well!
Good teacher, uses a lot of videos especially youtube to demonstrate concepts...a little boring at times, but she speeches clear and to the point...I would recommend her.
Rarely covered material on tests in class. Be prepared to read the book. Condescending attitude and did not allow students to ask questions because it took up too much class time.

Ms. Hardaloupas is a fun teacher.  If you just try, you make an A in her class.  She is very scattered brained but the course isn't that difficult.  She doesn't have all the answers but at least it's a class you can do well in.  Take her!!  It's boring but a boring A is better than none!

Very very nice teacher, but she's scatter brained and not very knowledgeable. Easy class if you read every chapter, study voc, and do the mybizlab work. Not a class for someone who doesnt have time to put into the class. There are 3 tests not including the final and a group project. Not my major but I made an A.

Haven't learned a single thing from this professor. 1st test coming up & on the review of what it may cover not a single thing was either assigned for homework OR discussed in class. Very poor knowledge of material & has a hard time answering questions she says "we're all here to learn together" I don't want to learn W/ her I want to learn FROM her
Well respected and esteemed professor. Don't try to cut any corners in his class, he is very good at picking out slackers.

Extremely good teacher, very dry (hilarious) sense of humor. Covers material fast, but you learn to keep up. Very passionate about chemistry. Teaches so you really understand where your electrons go. Hard to get by if you try to memorize without understanding the chemistry. All in all, one of the best professors I've had at Cornell.

A LOT of course material covered in a single lecture. While accurate and clear, his lectures are fast paced. The pace forces you to spend time reading the textbook. He is very helpful in office hours. One of the smartest professors at Cornell dedicated to teaching.

Lewis is one funny man. However, his teaching style is very fast and at times unclear. Fortunately, the book is great and his office hours are very useful too. Difficult tests, tricky, but overall a pleasant experience.
Hilarious in his own way. You'll either love him or hate him, but the textbook is incredible and regardless of what you think of lecture you can learn all the material on your own.
Very enthusiastic about the subject. Good sense of humor, but often assumed we knew things we didn't...

Prof was very knowledgeable and interested in what he is teaching about. Syllabus is clear and Chad is open to listen to and learn from students. Writing assignments helped me practice writing often and class was engaging. I felt lucky to take his class and would again if I could.

Prof. McIntosh was very fun and humorous. He definitely made you work, but he was an easy grader.   I really liked the lectures. He taught the subject very well and made me interested. I would take a class with him again if I could!

Best professor I've had at Cornell. Period. Explains things more clearly than any other instructor - truly interested in your learning the material. I can't say enough good things. Only bad thing is, I learned recently he's retiring from teaching soon. Take his classes while you can. Not sure what the major will look like when he hangs them up.

Well, I just finished my career at Cornell, and the highlight was definitely the classes I took with Evan Cooch. It is so obvious that he is here for us, lowly students, and not for his own career or research. Unfortunately, he is the exception to the usual rule. I just heard he won't be teaching much longer. Take his classes while you can.

Cooch is a model professor. His class was very well organized. It has some difficult content, but it is presented in a way that encourages learning. He has taught this subject for 20+ years and he is still on top of his teaching game.

I took all 3 of Cooch's classes (there are now 4 he teaches). Easily the best classes I took at Cornell. He can take the most complcated idea, and make it cool, and simple. He should probably win every teaching award, but because he doesn't do the Ivy League professor thing (at all...), probably never will. Too bad, because he should.

Best professor I've ever had at Cornell. None of the ivy league bs. Appears to be very tough and intimidates you in the first class, but is actually a very caring and passionate prof. Office hours very helpful. He sends you all the lecture notes, very detailed and thorough.

Thought I'd hate this class (took it to satisfy a quant requirement), but turned out to be the best class I had that term. Evan is amazing. I bombed the mid-term, but with his help (and the army of TA's he has), pulled it up to a decent A-. If you ever want to see someone teach because they want to, not because they have to, take Evan's class.

Cleares, most engaged instructor I've ever had. Had him for several classes a few years back. Takes super-complex ideas and teaches them in a way so by the time you're done, you think its the easiest stuff in the world. He pretty well gave up his big-time research to teach, because he thought that was more important than being a big star.

The best. I took 3100 first, and then about everything else Cooch teaches. Now that I've been in grad school for a while (ok, more than a while) I realize how criticall Cooch's classes were in getting me here. In fact, I still use his notes, which are clearer than the stuff I look at in my 'grad classes'.
I took his 3100 and then 4120, both were well-taught and useful.
Best professor I've had at Cornell. Best class. Evan is a master at explaining things. Has a good sense of humor also.

This guy wants you to succeed and can tell who doesn't show up to class. He can seem very intimidating but he is incredibly understanding and is open to helping you out in office hours. Honestly the best professor I took that semester and I went back to take more classes with him.

Best prof I ever had. Period. Here is a tip, though. Take his 3100 class early - second or third year. That sets you up to take his upper level classes, which are a straight path to grad school . If you take 3100 late, you won't have that option.

wonderful! you will learn so much! he is one of the best professors at Cornell. You will not leave his class without knowing more about ecology, population dynamics, wildlife, etc. TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!
Took a few classes with Cooch. The best. Dedicated to teaching, and to your understanding the material. Can play hard ass, but is actually very forgiving when 'real life' gets in the way.

Great class, great professor. One gripe is that he will not even consider regrading a paper or giving points back. Tough love kind of thing, but amazingly frustrating if you have answered all questions correctly and still did not receive full marks.
Amazingly clear, and the best teacher I experienced at Cornell. Cooch got me into grad school, and this class was one reason.  If Cooch teaches *any* class, take it.

Most unusual prof I've ever had. Amazingly clear, most awesome lecture notes ever (better than a textbook), and absolutely no connection to what I would have imagined for an Ivy League professor. Exams were tough, but fair. TA was a saint. One of the best profs, and best classes, I took at Cornell.

Thought I would hate this class, but turned out to be the best class I've taken in a while. I suspect real 'math geeks' will hate Evan's approach, but for me (hated calc), he was a savior. Still don't know how useful this stuff will be, but it was a fun class.

Hardest class I've ever taken. best class I've ever taken. Scariest prof I've ever had. best prof I've ever had. Now I get the rep of this class. I did really poorly on the mid-term, by Cooch prodded, cajoled, and helped me learn the material, and get an A. He is so anti-typical prof as to be unreal.

Best prof I have ever had at Cornell. Would take more classes with Evan, but they conflict with my schedule. Demanding, funny, very fair. Almost perfect evaluation system (regular assignments that are super helpful), and unlimited time exams.
Ever wonder what it would be like to take a class with someone who doesn't care what anyone thinks, so long as you learn? Evan is that kind of teacher. Cornell must hate him, but thats good for us.

Best prof I ever had. This was not an easy course, but it was so well taught, and I learned so much, it was worth the amount of time (a lot!) I spent on it. Only offered every other year. Take it if you can.
Hard to describe -- great at explaining complex and abstract ideas (really good), but can be a bit abrasive (if you're not into his style of 'humor'). Very fair grading system.

I only took this class because it was required, but I'm so glad I did. Evan is unlike any other prof (in fact, you might have trouble believing he's a professor at a snooty Ivy League school). Does the best job of explaining abstract ideas of any prof I've ever had. And he's pretty damned funny in the process.
Best. Prof. Ever. Took a subject that is abstract and a bit 'dry', and turned it into my favorite class so far at Cornell. He actually likes teaching!

Very nice and entertaining. Class is not very useful - you can just read through his crystal clear lecture notes. Exams can be somewhat challenging because he gives you problems that you've never seen before so you have to really by able to apply what you've learned. BUT gives unlimited time on the exams and is very generous with partial credit.

Co-taught with Tom Gavin when I took it. Cooch is like having a class with Henry Rollins (Gavin was Jimmy Buffet). Awesome. Who knew that matrix models could be cool? If you want to now how high-level consbio works, take this class.

Took both 310 and 410 a few years back - still the best classes I took in NTRES. Evan's lecture notes (more a text than notes) are still what I rely on as a grad student. Wasn't much interested in 'quantitative' things when I took the courses, but Cooch got me hooked (even though he makes fun of fish - my study organism). The best...
Scared me to death at first. Basically flunked the midterm, but he never stopped encouraging me, and helped whenever I asked. Ended up with a B. Evan is great.
Cooch is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. Take any class you can get with him, work hard, and you won't regret it!

I echo the last comment - Cooch is awesome. When I was a student at Cornell, I took all of his classes. He is the person who is basically responsible for getting e into grad school. He has this kack for explaining really complex things in very simple ways. It wasn't until I got to grad school that I realized (i) how much material that normally isn'

Great class - I'm not a 'math person', but Evan is pretty much a master at explaining fairly complex stuff in very accessible language (he should teach a class to the math profs here on how to do it). Even manages to be pretty funny (most of the time), which given the subject is no small feat. About the only class this term I never wanted to miss.
Class is ok. I don't see when in my life I will use anything I learned in this class. Just took it because it is mandatory. Evan is a nice guy once you get to know him and he's a fair grader.
No Comments
Professor Riehl has been my favorite teacher at Cornell and his class has been excellent. Must take for all ILRies, Inequality in higher education. Tough class but very worth it.

The material was presented in an understandable way. Lectures were interesting and group debates were incredibly engaging. He is a fair grader and offers ample feedback to do better next time. He is also incredibly understanding and approachable, so be sure to go to him if you need help. Could not recommend more.
Professor Riehl is a great professor--definitely the best teaching ILRLE 2400. His lectures are generally clear and understandable, and he is very accessible outside of class. Highly recommend!

The best option for labor econ. Super clear lectures; basically all you need to study for his tests is to copy down his notes verbatim and study them later. Lots of availability outside of class, where he is very helpful both with problem sets and with test prep. Problem sets are pretty straightforward for the most part. Tests really aren't bad.

Professor Riehl is super nice and caring. His lectures are great, so I never read the textbook. He basically solves the homework problems for you during his office hours, and practice questions are really good prep for his exams
lectures were good and nicely organized. workload very reasonable. he is not very approachable though, it felt like his fight or flight response activated when I approached him for a regrade.

Not an approachable teacher nor a fair grader. After going to his OH after a bad grade, he didnt offer any advice and just said that I was unlucky and do better on the next test. Also on one homework he agreed my answer was right but since it was not what the key said he gave no points back. He also lacked any empathy or understanding.

Probably one of the best professors in the Econ department, If not THE best. Evan is a great lecturer and class discussions are great too. The problem sets are very interesting and not overly difficult, and the paper assignment is as well. Fair grader. Very engaged/ passionate/ accessible, overall a great guy. Highly recommend this professor.

Professor Riehl is very nice. His lectures are organized and engaging. The workload is very manageable and his tests are easy as long as you can answer the questions on his slides. 100% strongly recommended.

Professor Riehl assigned very interesting readings that you will want to complete. His lectures were also always provocative and engaging. The problem sets were all fun challenges. Bonuses offered for some of the problem sets.
Professor Riehl is super nice!
Great professor, passionate lectures, very project heavy and quizzes directly came from lectures

While her lectures are usually very clear, some of her in-class examples are not totally helpful. Also, there are sometimes mistakes in assignments which lead people to a number of drastically different codes for the same problem.  Otherwise, a good professor.
Best teacher in the department.
Professor Anderson will always help you if you ask for it, especially by email (usually the same day). I definitely recommend her as a professor!
Such a wonderful professor, tries to learn everyone's name in the class. Will set up a private meeting to help you work on your code. Definitely take if you can!
One of the most accommodating professors that I have ever had. She is very helpful, and her lectures are super clear.
She is very friendly, fair, and clear. Nothing bad to say about her.

She's very friendly, and tries to know all student's names. She somewhat picks favorites though, but overall, she is a very nice approachable professor. She is very clear and helpful as well. Somewhat challenging, but overall reasonable.
Lindsay is a rock star. So helpful and so approachable.She is an excellent teacher. Her exams/homeworks are challenging, but fair.
Best Prof ever! She's amazingly nice and a total MILF. She learns everyones name, and is really friendly when approached.

Ms. Anderson was a decent prof.  She really made sure we understood the basics of MatLab.  She was a little spacy and followed directly off her power point slides, but going to lecture helped a lot.  Don't bother buying the book.  If you need reference help, you can get it online, and you can't sell the book back.
Professor Anderson is EXTREMELY helpful. She has a positive attitude and ensures that all of her students learn the course material.
She is a very helpful professor. If you need any help, she will give it. The course is very directed and there a lot of people who will help you. She tries her best and is at every lab section.

As a graduate student, I really love him even though the materials were extremely hard for me. His passion for mechanics and teaching really push you to another level. He makes me realize that I'm far from claiming I'm good at mechanics.

Hui did a great job teaching DiffEq. Always had a clear lecture plan, spoke clearly, great handwriting, and made sure connections between equations were understood before moving on. Exams were mostly re-hashed HW problems (different numbers) up until the final (PDEs). Hard to receive partial credit, but great feedback for missed problems.
He's the kind of professor who likes to screw students up. The average of first prelim was a C+, he thought the mean was too high and decided to make the following prelims a lot harder.

Sure, his lectures may not have been the most interesting, but it's math, I've yet to have a lecturer that makes this stuff super engaging. I actually thought he was pretty funny, which kept me listening. And the prelims were based on homework and lecture material, so if you know all that, you should be completely fine

He's...well, he's not exactly the most interesting professor ever. Pretty much just did other HW in his class and learned everything from the book. The participation grade is really the only reason to go in the first place.

His lectures introduced the material necessary for the homework and exams. They weren't very interesting and he's not the most engaging speaker. His exams were inconsistent in level of difficulty but definitely took a lot of cues from the HW sets.

I didn't really appreciate the lectures very much and the textbook really sucks at teaching you stuff. I don't know why, but I felt the first exam was the hardest (maybe I didn't get it at first). Then, the second prelim and final had A LOT of homework problems on them and weren't too bad. Study the homeworks if you have Hui as your professor.
Great guy, gets right to the material I switched into this class from math 2210 (other lin alg) and this class was so much better compared to 2210
tests were mostly based on hw, but got extremely hard for the final. study the hw!
decent!
pretty decent. fairly clear but sometimes confusing. overall solid teacher

He did not do a good job of conveying the material to me in an apprehensive way however, other students found him very enthralling. Prof. R. Rand taught a second lecture, I was hooked on him the first day I went. Text was crucial for me.
Hui is a really nice guy, gets so excited about the material. His notes are usually pretty clear and straightforward, but I still had to learn from the book a lot.
funny guy, but you'll need to learn from book cause linear algebra makes absolutely no sense in general
Good professor, take this class with him if you can.

Hui is a very good teacher. He conveys a seemingly complex material in a very simple fashion, and prepares you well for his prelims.If you go to class,take good notes,and read the book,you should be able to do very well in his class. Prelims were fairly simple and straightforward,though the final was fairly difficult. Overall though,a great teacher
awesome guy. Tough exams and hw but a very interesting lecturer and funny guy. Clear lectures and knows his stuff. One of the best professors I've had here

Hui is a great teacher.  He is funny and his misuse of english is comical.  However, the guy knows his stuff, rarely messes up on the board, and teaches very well.  Also, he uses some good and relevant examples.
Good lecturer, very willing to help his students, and very knowledge in many subject areas. The only complaint is that he grades kinda harshly.

This guy is insane. He assigns homework problems that he claims "will only take 10 minutes to do" but everyone spends 2 straight days struggling over it. 60% of the class barely passed his take-home exam. And this is a graduate level course and we're all PhD students!
I don't understand why everyone likes him.  He was not a good teacher, and all his examples came straight from the book.  And I CERTAINLY had no problem falling asleep during his lectures...
He taught the material very clearly and made a difficult subject pretty straight-forward and easy to understand. He gave me my first A at Cornell!

went from "i gotta drop this class" (pre-Hui) to "i actually know what i'm doing" (post-Hui). He's awesome, his lectures are damn straightforward, and he does some examples. very neat handwriting...:)
Interesting professor, you'd be hard pressed to fall asleep in his class as he is very enthusiastic about teaching. The actual teaching is rather lacking as it comes straight out of the book.

He's definitely familiar with the materials, but the way he teaches it is not all that clear. If you spend the effort to go to his lectures, do all the homework problems, and read the textbook, you'll do well. Really funny prof, I've never seen anyone getting so worked up just for Linear Algebra!

I dont understand why people would love Hui.  He was an alright teacher, teaching straight out of the book - derivation then equation, etc etc.  the book gets you thru the course, Hui is really nothing special

Hui rules. You must experience the phenomenon before you graduate. There were some hard-to-follow lectures, but for the most part he made the course clear and easy.  Also, by far the funniest prof I've had.

I was trying to learn the materials from the lecture but I eventually realized that wasn't gonna happen with this prof, so I just learnt from the book...  well I understand it's hard to teach linear algebra...
Funny as hell...have to give him that. A pretty bad teacher, but the book was understandable.

The only thing worse than this prof is the book.  Hui needs to learn how to teach.  Every day he'll walk into lecture, start talking and I feel like passing out after 5 mins because of his unclairity and randomness.  LEARN TO TEACH!!
No Comments
Very funny guy, and its not easy to make linear algebra humerous... there was one spontaneous ovation for him one friday morning, no idea how or why, but makes the class worth taking.
An ok teacher.  He's pretty funny, but I still have trouble staying awake through class.
Really funny.  Start a quotes list.

Recommend to any STEM major as alternative to 2214 (if Davis is teaching). His lectures were very thorough and he takes care to explain everything in detail, answering all questions. Throughout the semester you gain a solid understanding of everything from EM waves to fermi statistics and none of it is rushed. One of the best professors I've had.

I found Prof Davis to be a good lecturer.  While he does deeply care for the subject, he does not seem to be as interested in the class itself.  I will say that he went over the material rather quickly, and I would have preferred if he had spent more time on each individual topic.  Still, I think he did a good job with the class as a whole.
Awesome professor. Entertaining and clear lecturer.
One of the best physics professors Cornell has to offer. Great lecturer. Tests are not too hard - material is closely related to the stuff presented in homework sets and in the textbooks.
The exam is a lot harder than everything else covered in the course. It was taught very poorly in the areas that made up  45% of the final( a total of 2 lectures were held for these areas).

This was his first time teaching the course, and most people say he made it extremely hard for an intro class. The lectures were VERY entertaining, but the homeworks and prelims were definitely difficult. he also missed a bunch of lectures and never posted his office hours. Class was fun though. I enjoyed it a lot.
Great lecturer

This class is one of my favorites this semester. Davis is a really great lecturer, and he explains things really well. He is also great about answering questions during lecture. My only criticism is that he misses a lot of lectures, and the TA teaches in his place. The TA is no substitute.
Best professor ever.  Lectures on thermal physics were super interesting, and his commentary on the material added so much to the course.  Only downside is that he was always late.
No Comments

A very good professor. Made quantum mechanics very fun and interesting. It was helpful how he taught QM from a more physical prespective rather than just a mathematical one. Definitly a good teacher to have as your first intro to QM.
Very fun class. Gives students physical insight, instead of just trudging through the mathematics. Also presents special topics such as macroscopic quantum mechanics that relates to his research.

Ridiculously sarcastic and he's the only one that finds his jokes funny. He frequently picks on one student at a time and makes rude jokes towards them to make fun of them. Man comm should be an easy class, but he made it as difficult as possible with his grading scale and unimportant lectures.

Weird guy (has a "loose cannon" personality), grading is harsh and arbitrary; ManCom is useless but he makes it more rigorous for no reason. Would not recommend as all ManCom lectures are curved together regardless of professor. Tyrell does not believe in giving students As. Go with Lennox for ManCom; he's the best and only good ManCom professor.
Tyrell is an amazing professor who is very personal with his students and cares a lot about them. He teachings comm classes which is fitting for him because he is an outstanding speaker.

Overall, definitely do not underestimate the class. In terms of actual course load, it is maybe an average of 2 hrs a week- but grading is tough. He is super open to coaching you to get better and definitely you should go to office hours to work on assignments. If you wait too late to get help- you will probably not be happy with your grade.

Professor Stewart-Harris is definitely a character. He always makes jokes and picks on people, sometimes a little too much. He grades very hard and does not give A's. Expect to be happy with a B-. His rubrics and criteria are very unclear and often contradict each other. Other professors grade much easier and almost always give A's.

Stewart- Harris was hilarious, engaging, and super passionate about what he teaches. Gives good feedback for speeches, but is always kind and fair, and really responsive. Such a fun teacher, but was really straightforward about what was expected in his class which was great!

He does not believe in awarding A's. You can attend his and every TA's office hours, but if your writing is not the best he has ever seen, you will not get an A in the course. Hope that you get a different professor because he will not boost your GPA in any way. He also does not round your grade and does not give out extra credit. Good luck!

Seminar-style class with a lot of readings, but is easy to do well in even if you don't read all the books. I appreciated prof bringing in guest lecturers (Google employee, other profs) to explain technical topics. Sometimes disorganized lectures but if you participate in every 2 lectures, you'll get full credit. Attending OH helped with essays.

She really teaches to teach, not to get students ready for exams, and cares about your learning. 
The course is challenging. I was almost dropped since the history and constitution slavery etc lost me. But the work broadened my perspective. I think it all paid off

She means well, but her lectures are disorganized and poorly planned, with scribbles on the whiteboard and no clear connection between topics. She often goes on tangents about her personal beliefs that don't add much value to the course. Additionally, the assignment instructions are unclear and inconsistent, making it hard to know what to expect.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

Gives out grades without justifications. Let us debate all the time so she can do nothing and just be lazy. Talks randomly and writes down random things on board with no organization. Biased toward immigrants and minorities. Super mean and subjective. Save your time please, don't take her class.

She spends 75% of the class talking about US and Roman history and cold calling about random history facts. The remaining 25% will be cold calling on readings that she assigned. There is no structure to the class. She writes random thoughts on the white board expecting us to understand. AVOID her if you can!

I am sure the 5 rating was written by herself...
Just run, save your time. 
Very subjective, talks about nonsense in class.
I was interested in the topic of AI, but her class just really disappoints me. TAs are mean as well. There is nothing good about her class. Failed politician and worst professor.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. Worst professor I had. 
Came up with the course grading in class, rubric did not exist two weeks into the semester. Grading is very subjective and dependent on whether she likes you or not.
Teach is VERY BAD. She talks about nothing relevant in class. Content is exactly the same as another class.
I LEARNED NOTHING from it.
Great Professor

Prof. Mitrano is the most passionate, caring, and interesting Professor I've had at Cornell. Her teaching combines the history, legislation, and background context surrounding technology which helps tremendously to set the scene of what is going on in our world today. Amazing professor and person.

In one class, we talked about AI, copyright,  the constitution,  American revolution, slavery , Ancient Greece/rome , Slavery , non racebased slavery , Feudalism, Ferdinand and Isabella , Christopher Columbus ,incest,  and nation states. I did not learn anything. Please save your time.

I have never met a worse and distasteful professor in all my time at this school. A FAILED politician who is out of touch with students, class expectations, and reality. Her class is a disorganized mess with no grades in. Assigns 8 books for the semester and cold calls to see if we meet here unreasonable expectations. Shouldn't teach. RUN AWAY!

Professor Angus really knows her stuff, but when it comes time to teach it she is really harsh. She tends to repeat things a lot and she tends to put a lot of pressure on us. I highly recommend the Modern Poetry course with Professor Angus. It is a quite interesting course and her lectures are very interesting. I have learned a lot from this course and it made me fall in love with poetry.

Horrible, horrible teacher. Extremely rude and hot-tempered. She makes rude remarks. Although I am passing her class, I am surprised to see her attitude as of now compared to everyone's comments. DO NOT TAKE HER! --You've been warned.
She is funny, smart and will keep you engaged in her class. The assignments are not difficult. You will very happy with her as a teacher!

I've had professor Angus for a few classes now and I really love her. She's so funny and helpful with all assignments. She does give out a lot of writing assignments, but she isn't a very tough grader. As long as you participate and have fun in the class, she'll love you.
She is very sarcastic but always tries to help if you are not understanding what you are learning. Try her out she is very truthful and gives funny anecdotes that go along with the reading.
Love Dr. Angus cool guy
His lectures are so incredibly boring but his class is so easy to pass. Hes a good guy just very dry.

such a good professor, cares a lot about his work and his students. also kind of a dilf, I said what I said. he was very understanding of any circumstances that students had come up and really loved to see students interact during lectures. such a good prof 100/10

Ryan Angus was a pretty good professor to have. I have no complaints about him. He is very understanding about late work, and his lectures are discussion so READ READ READ. It's an easy class as long as you participate. If you need a pretty easy credit class, take him.

This professor clearly states what is expected and thoroughly enjoys teaching. He wants you to fully grasp concepts before moving forward, cares about your future abilities, and understands different learning styles.

Dr. Angus was great. He was very caring, especially during the pandemic. He was understanding with late work as well and gives you the points if you try and turn it in.

Definitely one of my favorite and most recommended teachers. He is super realistic and likes to put real world events and conversations into lectures. He has a unexpected grading scale, but I turned out loving it and wished more people graded the way he does. 10/10!!

Very simple and straightforward course. He is willing to work with you if you forget to turn in an assignment or whatever the issue may be. The only issue is his lectures tend to be boring, but it's a general English course don't walk in there and expect him to be teaching about something extraordinary.
Also, please for the love of God participate.

Dr. Angus is an amazing prof and is an amazing person, his class is very boring because he tends to lecture a lot, his grading is the best part about him it is clear what he is taking points for and is very clear on due dates, he is also so understanding. I would def take him again, as long as you do the work you will 100% get an A
Super great guy, caring too. Very easy class but super boring like super boring but very enjoyable. Definitely taking again.

Dr. Angus is a wonderful professor. I really enjoyed his class. He explains things well and answers any questions you might have. He is a very understanding and caring person. I would definitely take more classes from him.

I think Dr. Angus is probably one of my favorite professors during my time at Marshall. Tells students to be safe at the end of class, which is nice.

He was very understanding and very nice. I had a lot of issues with Teams and he really worked me. Prof Angus is really awesome about checking his messages and getting back to you in a reasonable amount of time. The lectures are really dry but its a pretty easy class if you pay attention and just show up to class.

Dr. Angus was very nice and graded fairly easily. He gave three major papers including the final and weekly reflections. It was required to read five books that would be discussed in class. I would take him again, and I highly recommend him to anyone.
He is a pretty good professor. He grades pretty easy, but is on a his own weird grading scale. Lectures are a tad boring, but still show up!

Dr. A is amazing. He truly cares about the students and is easily accessible outside of class. Make sure you read because since it's a 400 level class, he expects you to participate in class. For the most part, if you do your work, you'll pass. He's not a hard grader. Take him if you get the chance!

Ryan co-taught this class, and I feel like the other teacher did the majority of the work. He was basically just our comedic side show, and I feel like if he had taught this on his own it wouldn't have been as good. That being said, he is nice and funny, just not the worlds best teacher.

I took his online 201 2nd 8 week course. Being that it's an accelerated course, it does require time management and diligence to get the work done on time. The assignments aren't difficult. There is a weekly question, discussion board, and 3 bigger papers. He is nice and helps when you ask for it. All in all, a solid online class.
This class may be easy, but this dude is dry as can be. Who said he was hot? Lol not the case.
Ryan was definitely the best professor I have had at Marshall. Really down to earth kind of guy. He is super helpful, I highly recommend him.

Really nice guy, very very easy. Can be boring, but you have four absence you get before he says a thing. Very easy paper(s), he will make you write a five page and then you only have to write a page about a project you done! You are guaranteed an A! Awesome professor!
He is good. We had like 2 major paper and 1 creative response to do and that was all. He understood our ideas all the time. I recommend his class!

Nice but so boring.  The only grade we had in the class was a paper.  He talked about the same thing every class. Do not take him in the morning cuz you will fall asleep. I dreaded going to class everyday.

Angus is awesome! He is super cool and tries really hard to make writing fun and enjoyable for everyone. We had like 1 paper and 1 other small project to do and that was all. love love love ryan angus :) i had to miss class a few times this semester for family emergencies, but i went straight to his office and he appreciated me letting him know. he helped me and told me everything i needed to know. not only is he a great teacher, but he's an awesome guy. go to class even though it can be boring :)

Angus is very very easy. he gives u 2 papers one in the middle of the term and the other at the end. his class is so boring i hate to go to this class. as long as u come and do his work A is guaranteed. he doesn't use the book that much. i suggest to take this class as long as u stand coming to class and do nothing !!!!!
Angus is the man.  He is very understanding and very helpful.  The papers aren't hard at all.  Just come to class and you'll be golden.

Ryan Angus is an awesome person! He is a VERY easy teacher. We are three weeks until the school year is over and we have only had 3 EASY EASY EASY assignments. coffee coffee coffee. he likes his coffee. and don't forget THE PANDA SAYS NO!!!
Angus is awesome. Though the class can get a little boring sometimes, he's just..awesome. definelty tke him.

Professor Angus' class was not difficult, but I found the lectures dry, and it took several months before we got grades back for our midterm assignments. Professor Angus was very caring and provided time in class to work on group assignments.
I really enjoyed the field trips to farms and guest speakers in this class.

One of the easiest classes at Cornell if you just show up. Minimal studying is needed if you go to lectures, and pay close attention during labs. Field Trips are engaging and tie back into exams. The class is pretty easy, lots of different assignment styles, which break up the rigidness unlike other Cornell Science classes. Each lecture is pretty boring, and Prof Ryan is not the most well spoken. There are farm field trips instead of traditional labs that are fun and inspiring. Midterm and Final were both straight forward.

Professor Ryan is a great guy and is very accessible. The TA's were very nice and helpful as well. The class is easy as long as you turn things in on time. The only downside was the 3 hour labs outside on farms during freezing rain or snow.
He will literally go out of his way to help you on literally anything. He is super chill. Easy A, and you actually learn valuable skills and subject material.
I took him for my FWS, and he was so kind and sweet throughout the whole semester. I'm so glad I decided to take his class!

My favorite class at Cornell so far. Lectures were very engaging and just a ton of fun. Essay prompts were enjoyable and the research process was straightforward. Ryan is understanding and clearly cares for her students very much. Just show up and try your best, and your efforts will be recognized.

Ryan is so iconic and she genuinely makes her class my favorite part of the day. The essay prompts were enjoyable to write about and they were not very strenuous. The readings were also interesting and were not too long. Attendance is mandatory but the class discussions were always fun so overall I would 100% take a class with her.

Ryan is an absolute icon, and I am incredibly upset that the semester is almost over because I can't imagine how another freshman writing seminar could top this one. Ryan is passionate about the subject matter to the point where she could go on tangents for hours, and genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. This class is so fun. Take it!!

Best professor I've had so far at Cornell. Very patient, encourages questions and makes sure you really understand the content in office hours. Fun guy. Made an effort to go through many example problems in lecture which helped understand so much more than bullet point notes. E&M sounded very scary but this guy made it not that bad

Professor Tapping is one of my favorite professors so far at Cornell. I came into Cornell with a weak Physics background and have struggled at times because of it, but Tapping's excellent lectures and being extremely well-organized overall have made E&M so much more bearable for me.

Professor Tapping always makes sure lecture will be interesting and never comes to class without a demo prepared. Prof. Tapping is wonderful. The class is very well organized, his lectures are clear, his homeworks and exams are all very fair. I cry every night reminiscing about PHYS 2213. I will miss Ryan Tapping so so so much :'(

Ryan Tapping IS THE MAN. Best prof I've had thus far. Lectures and demos are awesome, COOPs are engaging, and I've learnt a ton. Professor Tapping is the best STEM teacher I have ever had. He is so funny and an incredible lecturer. This is coming from someone who made a C in mechanics and is looking like they are going to make an A in this class. Beyond thankful to Ryan who made me feel like I can actually do this again. If you want to learn something, take this class!!!

Dr. Tapping is an amazing professor. He is truly one of a kind. I have so much respect for him. He made phys2213 enjoyable even though it was a hard class. His office hours were very helpful, and he is very patient with students. Thank you for everything Dr. Tapping and to all students taking his class in the future, please be nice to him.

Ryan Tapping is one of the best professors that I have had so far at Cornell. He completely turned around the Phys 2213 program, making a notoriously difficult class into something fun and interesting. His tests were fair and lectures engaging. Tapping is probably the most genuine and considerate professor I've seen.

literally the kindest and most amazing human being! i went to OH after our first prelim and it was completely empty. mans literally came in and talked with me for 3 HOURS; he came back at 11pm to see if i was still there, saying he felt bad for distracting me. he didnt leave till we finished the coop i originally came to OH to do.

Prof. Tapping did an excellent job with 2213, and it was clear from the start how important the class was to him and how much he cared about the students. Lectures and demos were engaging and fun. Though work was intensive, everything was fair.

Fantastic lectures, genuinely caring. His class is involving, and the material is difficult. But unlike others with the same description, he also makes you feel like you are respected, and there is a high level of tolerance.

Tappings is a very caring professor. It is very intentional that he makes 2213 an incredibly chill class. Compared to previous semester, the psets are very relaxed. The prelim is reflective of the psets and coops. Lecture wise, the demos are very cool and aids in conceptual understanding of the concepts. Honestly, no bad comments about 2213.

Dr. Ryan Tapping made sure that students were heard, advocated for, and made active efforts to make PHYS 2213 a better experience. I was originally scared because I heard horror stories about 2213 being tough, but he seriously made lectures enjoyable to attend. I would really recommend his course!

Literally the easiest A+ you could possibly get at Cornell. Honestly, I felt a little bad throughout the course because since it was so beyond easy, nobody took the course seriously. Was an amazing professor. Took this class to lighten up my science heavy semester and boy am I glad that I did. His lectures are interesting and engaging and he gives so much opportunity for extra credit. I highly recommend this class to anyone and everyone.
Fantastic instructor. Never knew there was so much behind the history of the University!

Take his class!!!! One of the best lecturers you will encounter at Cornell! Jason Frank is absolutely brilliant and the class wasn't that difficult. The median was an A-, so as long as you read the material and listen to the lectures you are fine.

average professor who seems good because of passion and delivery. grading is based 3 papers and discussion. lectures generally have little to do with the actual paper prompts. if ur a good writer and can understand the readings well and incorporate that into ur essays u can get an A

best
BEST and HOTTEST professor ever. Smart. Eloquent. Passionate. Helpful. Great lecturer. Nough said.

Very interesting material and fascinating lectures you won't want to miss. Also, you shouldn't miss them, because you will struggle with the papers if you don't go to lecture. Material is hard, but getting an A is not overly difficult
He is a great professor, and actually peaked my interest in Theory. Don't miss lecture though, because he does have a lot to say.

He was just ok. Very passionate about the subject, but his lectures were wandering and sometimes lacked focus. It was his first time teaching the large lecture course, so perhaps he's better in smaller settings...

Professor Frank is outstanding.  He has the unique ability to direct discussion to bring out the most interesting and thought-provoking elements of American political theory.  Any class with him is highly recommended.  If you work hard, you will do very well.

He expects a lot, stimulates interest, and makes you think critically about American political thought -- and this was a writing seminar.  If you want to learn, and you're willing to do some work, take any class he teaches.
My favorite professor at Cornell! He's very knowledgable and is a great teacher.. He makes class very interesting especially through the discussions. I liked the final project too.
Genuinely one of the laziest professors I have had. Every class was exactly the same and he just liked to listen to himself talk. He was often condescending and grading was completely arbitrary.

This class is fascinating, and even students with a Jewish education background will learn a ton. There's a lot of reading and writing involved, which can hit hard in the middle of the semester when it's 10 degrees outside. He is accessible outside of class and encourages students to participate.

Professor Mokhtarian is an incredible professor who cares deeply about seeing his students learn and succeed. Mezey is a fantastic professor. Lectures are well-paced, clear, and he records them to make them accessible. He's accessible outside of class and hosts great OH. Helpful office hours, passionate about teaching, doesn't judge students for not having some prerequisites, and is very clear about what he wants us to learn.
It was a great class. I still refer back to his lectures years after graduating. Solid understanding of statistical concepts and provides a great foundation.

Jason Mezey's class is not easy, but he isn't kidding when he says he'll teach you everything you need to know about GWAS. He's a fine teacher and while I would not choose to take him again he is definitely better than other math professors. His handwriting on the board was a little hard to read but not impossible. Fine professor but there are better.

Jason Manning's calculus: a series of disappointments. Lectures subtract understanding, exams add complexity, and office hours multiply the bewilderment.

Manning's calculus course: where clarity is divided, confusion is multiplied, and understanding is subtracted. Save yourself the headache.

Just an all round gem. Whatta boyyyy

Awesome teacher, relaxed, willing to take the time to really explain things, clearly cares about helping his students really understand math and learn to think mathematically. Has a sense of humor.
So awesome, really relaxed. Often breaks down concepts for the class so they are really easy to understand.
Jeff is a boss, highly recommended TA

Awesome class (comic theatre), super interesting subject and Rusten teaches it exceptionally, very enthusiastic about the subject and very conversational teaching style. GPA saving class but also just an enjoyable part of my week.
Definitely one of the brightest professors at Cornell. He is extremely passionate about the subject matter and cares about his student.

Took this class in Spring 2013 and is still one of my favorite classes at Cornell to date. Dr. Rusten is so passionate and knowledgeable that class was super enjoyable. Since the class was on comic theater, a lot of the hw assignments were  to watch movies or tv shows which was fun.

Rusten is absolutely one of my favorite professors at Cornell. He is such a friendly, easygoing guy who truly cares about the material that he is teaching. My favorite part about this class was watching films from different eras of comedy. I would definitely recommend this class for an easy A.

Lots of research papers to read, but Jeff is pretty chill in this class and gives good hints on what to pay attention to for quizzes, during lectures.
Amazing professor, very helpful always. I highly recommend this class

Jeff was overall a great guy.  I am not at all interested in communications as a whole but Jeff consistently made the class interested.  Attendance wasn't mandatory but I never wanted to skip!  Definitely one of my favorite professors at Cornell
Great professor and an all around nice guy.  Take this class if you can, all essays are peer reviewed

Prof Hancock is a pretty good lecturer, but he can be unclear and vague sometimes, and also focuses a lot of silly, gimmicky-y stuff. Hands down the best Professor I have ever had (or heard of for that matter) at CU. He is extremely witty, intelligent, and extraordinarily helpful. Great person!
honestly can say this class changed the way i'm going to live my life. take it if you can, but more importantly, take a class with prof hancock before you graduate.

awesome.

One of the most interesting classes Ive taken at Cornell. It is essential that you thoroughly do all reading homework because he cold calls students in class. This can be stressful at first but is honestly not a huge deal. I honestly never felt bored, and as long as you show up to every class (attendance is huge) and take good notes you'll do well
Really great professor but not great on Zoom. Be prepared to do a lot of readings and there are cold calls in class as well.
Generally good prof but not great for zoom classes... Lots of cold calls. Lots of reading.
Professor Rachlinski is a very passionate and knowledgable professor. He goes off on tangents sometimes, but they're related and very interesting!
His lectures were really interesting.

Professor Rachlinski is very passionate and well-prepared for every class. He makes materials really interesting. He would pick several students to answer all the questions tho, so just read before classes and enjoy his amazing lectures.

The professor is so good and humorous about the corporate law. You can't stop laughing when he is making a joke accidentally during his dealing with a serious corporate problem. His answer to the course questions and past exams (with suggested answers) are very helpful for preparing my final exam. Highly recommended!
He is the best. no need to say more. If you're looking for an FWS, look no further.
This man is the literal goat. Great class not stressful at all and extremely interesting. Highly recommend taking any class with this professor.

Out of all of the classes I took at Cornell, this class has been the most rewarding and eye-opening. It is a fairly easy 2-credit class, but it has significantly challenged my opinions on pesticides. He's truly HILARIOUS even when he doesn't try to be, so his lectures are always engaging. Very good at explaining concepts and organized. TAKE IT!
Cares about his students, but the class was often very boring.

Professor Avgar cares more deeply for his students than virtually any professor I've had. He takes seriously the responsibility of teaching and is fully committed to teaching undergrads and grad students alike.
Ariel Avgar is an incredibly knowledgeable and engaging Professor. He is very helpful in office hours. Labor Relations can be dry at times but he made the class worth while. Overall great guy.
One of the best professors at Cornell
Best professor ever. Love him to death.
He makes Chemical Engineering really interesting and explains things very clearly. He obviously cares about how you learn and tries to adjust. And he has really cool chalk.

Very good lecturer. Grading is spread evenly between homework, prelims and a final. Workload is fairly light. Lectures follow the textbook, but I would recommend reading the textbook before every lecture. Grading was lenient on exams and class was slightly curved. Would highly recommend this class for an engineering distribution as well.

Generally Duncan is a good professor. Can be blunt in lecture when receiving questions he thinks should be obvious. Group homeworks can be a drag. Tests require very solid conceptual understanding of the content, he will reapply concepts to completely new situations, so do lots of practice. Occasionally funny.

Prof. Duncan's lectures are AMAZING, and he provides every document on his website for easy access. We always knew what was expected of us, and office hours were well-timed throughout the week. Tests were difficult but fair, and homework was done in groups, which I personally loved. Sometimes he can be a bit sarcastic, but he is a great professor.
He was a passive-aggressive professor so it was not a welcoming environment when you wanted to talk to him. Plus, you have to buy his textbook he wrote.

A very respectable and respectful professor who genuinely cares about his students. His care takes the form of wanting the best for the student, which doesn't translate into lax standards in any way. Excellent explanations. Office hours are incredibly valuable.

While homework groups were annoying at times, they weren't terrible. All exams (3 prelims+final) were completely fair and if you took good notes in lecture and really understood homework and section problems, they were straight forward. Don't slack because it seems easier than PChem. Advice, do all problems yourself before exam so YOU actually know
Not the easiest intro course, but probably the most useful. Anyone with the slightest inclination toward pursuing ChemE should take the course.

TMD is the man! He lets you know from the start that it is not a normal intro class in the fact that you must work hard and you learn, but if you stick through it you gain a whole new perspective on your chosen major. It does stink that he wrote the textbook because lectures can seem repetitive, but he is very personable and helpful in office hours

He's an odd teacher - doesn't really teach to the style of the students, despite the fact that he says otherwise. Heavy emphasis on the textbook. Really smart guy though, but didn't seem connected to any of the students but his favorites.

He is best professor I have ever met. He always make everything clear and his class is well organized. Although it is not an easy class to get good grades, you can learn a lot in his class, not only engineering knowledge, but the attitude towards life, critical thinking and communication skills.
Professor Duncan changed my interest from "What is chemical engineering?" to "This is the coolest stuff ever!"
AMAZING

Fantastic course teacher.  Poor advisor.  Condescending if you are not confident or if you do not agree with him.  This is college; kids are supposed to find themselves, not be discouraged. His favorites get more confident while the shy ones get more shy.  This is an unfair and unstable method to students.

In a perfect situation Duncan would be a great teacher. He interacts with the class, seems friendly and is very intelligent.  But the reality is, he takes things personally, a very bad characteristic for someone in a position to educate.  Once he aligns himself against you, consider avoiding him at all costs and not depending on him for help.
He intimidates me ... oh TMD

I had him for multivariable calc and he was a great teacher. He was out of his subject matter and he did an excellent job of teaching the material. He was clear, comprehensive, and loved to interact with the class.
He's definitely someone who picks favorites. But watch out if he doesn't like you. He'll make your life miserable.

This is a very rigorous introduction to chemical engineering. It is not an easy class, but you will learn a lot if you put your earnest effort to it. A lot of skills are honed in this class. For instance, interpreting graphs, guessimating, etc. It is a critical thinking class, and this is how the professor wanted it to be.

Avoid this class at all means possible.  It requires much more work than an intro class and more time consuming than 3 credits should be. If you are thinking of being a chemical engineering, you will really rethink it after this class.

First time a teacher actually knew my name and cares how i was doing. Duncan is by far the best teacher I've had at Cornell (he was named teacher of the year in NY for 2007!) If you take this class, beware, he knows your name and whether or not you care to show up or try hard
Awesome teacher, very willing to help anyone out!!  Teaches great classes.
The best teacher that I have had so far.  He really knows what he is teaching and has a good sense of humor.  Excellent use of chalk and TAs.

He really knows his stuff, but taking notes in class is really hard because of the handouts.  Its impossible to study from the notes in class, and the text isnt much help. Best way to study is do the practice problems on the website. Office hours were overcrowded and the TA's didnt have enough time to be particularly helpful to anyone.
Great Professor in terms of knowing the material and getting it through to the students. Intro to cheme class will give you a good idea of wether chemical engineering is what you want.

The textbook is horrible and convoluted.  you basically buy it for the HW problems inside.  taking notes in class is nearly impossible and pointless since he passes out so many handouts. limited number of practice problems. studying for prelims and final are difficult because of this.
he looks like jack from lost

Helpful; tries to help us learn the material and understand different applications of topics. Lectures are disorganized and somewhat uninteresting, but he manages to teach fairly well anyway. Grades fairly and makes exams so that they really test our knowledge instead of trying to trick us. Helps you do well in the class.

duncan is probably one of the worst teachers i have had at cornell. during pchem i had the impression that he didnt like me.  from the other posts,i can see im not the only one.  he does not act like a teacher.  by this i mean if you annoy or upset him, he takes it very personally and singles you out (ie not offering help, offering it arrogantly)

Lectures are quite disorganized.  Writes all over the board so it's hard to take organized notes without rewriting them after.  His book was the most poorly written book I've ever read (I stopped reading it).  Arrogant and moody.  Best to avoid interaction.
Awesome class and actually a lot of fun, but yes, prepare to work for your grade. I loved his lectures and the text was one of the few that I actually read.
very hard class. Duncan was an alright teacher. Need to get on his good side to do well. He was a bit patronizing.

Overall a bad professor.  His course was well-organized and clear.  But as a person he is: Arrogant, Rude, and Insulting.  If you get on his bad side - watch out; he's going to make your life difficult.  I found the best course to take with him was to avoid him.  In summary he's a decent teacher, but is a vindictive and mean-spirited person.

Quite possibly my favorite professor so far.  He goes far out of of his way to get to know his students really well - he often knows things that you never thought he would care about.  Lectures sound like you're reading from his textbook, which is clear as well.  Knows everything he teaches front and back.

Great teacher!  One of the best at Cornell.
I love Prof. Duncan. He was really helpful during office hours. His lectures were clear, and he really cares about his students progress. He is one in a million.
i <3 T.M.D

Excellent class, very organized and straightforward. Takes time to learn the material well and to do the homework, but it's worth it. I never found him to be unpleasant or rude, nor do I know anyone that's felt that way.
Course is ok. Duncun is not. He can be is a cocky rude mood frequently. But deal-able when he's in non-hostile mode.
Designs very difficult exams, but is a very clear and straightforward teacher, if a bit impersonal.

Duncan was awful. He graded harshly (esp final), expected a lot of work, and was clearly discriminating among students. If you get on his good side, you're lucky. If he hates you, your life in ChemE is gonna be hell. I tried talking to him once, and he's really cocky and rude. God bless Mr. Duncan.

Great professor. He expects you to do a lot of work, but if you're willing to make the effort he really cares about helping you succeed. It was a relief to have a professor who treated teaching an intro class as an important job.
really gud prof...one of the best...xtremely helpful...
Very organized and clear, good professor.
Duncan proves that when you respect your students and treat them like adults, they will respect you back and give their utmost effort.
Professor Duncan is truly inspiring and I've learned more from him in the last few months than I have from any other professors!
The chalk!  the chalk!
Awesome teacher, went out of his way to give students tools for sucess
Wonderful teacher, also teaches math 192
The T. Michael Duncan was the best professor I had in the four years I took classes at Cornell.

Most organized person in the World!

If he can't teach you graphical analysis, your just helpless

Overall, the class was interesting and fairly enjoyable. However, some of the lecturers were boring and lectured beyond our knowledge. Decent class overall, but could be better organized.

She is very clear, organized and knowledgable. Problem sets are fair and tests were an accurate representation of material. There's a lot of readings, but if you understand lectures, then you can do well. I really am enjoying this class, it's one of the first classes I've taken at Cornell that was fair and really sparked my interet.

I WOULD NOT PREFER. I RECEIVING A 50 ON THE FIRST ESSAY, I ASKED FOR GUIDANCE. WE EMAILED BACK AND FORWARDS ABOUT 3TIMES CONCERNING THE 2ND ESSAY.
