Sara is one of the best people to learn from within PMA at Cornell.

She has so much knowledge about the history of the craft its a performance in itself to watch her give a lecture or present to the class.

Her projects are incredibly fun and allow you to be as creative as you want.

If you can take a class with her, do it. You won't regret it.
Show up to lectures, be engaged, and you will do well in this class. She is caring but strict.

The class is all about laughter, should be fun and easy. Attendance is mandatory and you are only allowed to miss one class. Not understanding at all for travel-related absences. Received a whole grade drop for one additional missed class (that should have been excused). Rude handling of the situation and rewards dishonesty over maturity.

Sara is an amazing teacher, and anyone with an interest in any form of social justice should definitely treat themselves to one of her classes. You will read a LOT and have extremely in depth conversations and all of it will be worthwhile. She's charming, dynamic, helpful, and passionate about her subject and her students.
She is incredibly passionate about what she teaches. She is upbeat and optimistic in discussion, fantastic teacher.
Sara is a tremendous professor. Her classes are not easy, but she makes you think as hard as she makes you work. She is dynamic, interesting and compelling - one of Cornell's finest.

She is an extremely engaging and fun lecturer.  You absolutely have to do the work for her class and pay attention, but she is always very helpful and appreciative of those that take the class seriously.  Definitely take any class you can with her.

Great teacher: engaging, funny, fair, and organized. Theatre 240 was my favorite class of the semester, despite the fact that I'm not even a theatre major. You DO need to do the readings and the assignments that Prof. Warner gives you, but if you keep up with them, you'll be fine. Just proofread your papers for grammar/spelling errors before class.

Sara Warner is a rite of passage for any theater major. Lovely human being. But the myths about the tons of reading are true. There will be points where you will have a lot to do. And I'm sorry, but you've got to attend every class and keep up with every reading in order to stay afloat. Do not make that mistake.

have taken 6 courses from this professor to take and loved each and everyone of them. really easy to ask for help in and out of class on difficult topics.  classes are real interactive and lectures are real note-taker pleasers.  Exams are self-explanitory and grading is very very fair.  If you do the work and you listen and show up you will do fine

She KNOWS her stuff.  TONS of notes and reading for the class, but the exams aren't too bad, very memory-based.  And tons of writing involved, but Sara is extremely helpful and very clear about what she expects from you.  Sometimes picky with people's writing styles, but if you do the work, you get the grade.
always encouraging, interesting discussions, projects, and her lectures are easy to take notes from

This class was a lot of work but Dr. Pryor is a really awesome professor! Really good lectures and you can tell she cares a lot about her students. Definitely don't be afraid to ask questions, she's really good at answering them and is very willing to help. Exams were very fair based on the course content and she used a free online textbook.

Lectures were super engaging and clear! Really good at answering and encouraging us to ask questions. Only 4 assignments, 2 exams, and a small project. Assignments took a while to do but she takes a class period to go through them and they're interesting applications of the material. Also she used free textbook pdfs only

Dr. Pryor is a solid choice. Even though the class was all online, the content was easy to follow and well explained in the lecture, plus posted on canvas if I needed to go back. No homework assignments but 5 heavy and intensive bi-weekly lab reports that took a good chunk of time to complete, but reinforced the material well, and one was dropped.

I took this class SP20, and Professor Pritchard was by far the most empathetic instructor that I had when the world tilted. The class can be a lot of reading and is discussion-heavy, but it's very relevant, and I ended up rethinking many of my own assumptions. I definitely recommend this course (and Professor Pritchard as an instructor).

Very monotonous lectures in which she reads off a piece of paper on the same tone of voice. No laptops or screens allowed in class making it all the more boring. She makes jokes that are not at all funny and I come out of lecture feeling as if nothing she said had any meaning, just lots of words but didnt learn anything.

Regardless of your interest in the environment, I recommend everyone to take this class! It is the MOST CHALLENGING class I've taken in terms of its content. As a class cross-listed with philosophy, I was expecting some deep thinking and controversy, but this class makes you question your whole existence. It's a necessary existential crisis.

She can be a bit arrogant and tends to silence voices that aren't in line with her own thought process. Forget about any form of discussion in class. A lot of work is busy work without any substance. I'd recommend you take this class with another teacher.

Favorite class I've taken so far. Discussions were really lively and interesting and Prof Pritchard definitely knew how to keep things moving without controlling the conversations too much. Readings were sometimes long but the discussions made them worth it. I'd recommend this class for sure!
Amazing, interesting class. She is a great professor for small seminars. She is sweet, fun, funny, and interesting. I highly reccommend taking her gender and technology seminar!
Grades too hard for such a BS class!
Professor Warner is quick-minded and can always bring you brilliant ideas. She may be intimidating at first, but you will find out how awesome she is afterward!
In our class, most of us were disappointed because Mildred hides behind City and Regional Planning when in reality she is not a planner and has no interest in this field. Terrible class overall.
Very challenging workshop that requires a lot of effort. Warner is mainly interested in improving her own research rather than teaching.
Mildred is disorganized and does not stick to her syllabus. Then she gives you attitude and expects her students to change their entire schedules for her. Just plain terrible.

While there is a lot of work and her comments on papers can be a bit hard to follow, she is an incredibly intelligent woman who very much wants you to learn and succeed. Even when discussing very difficult realities she always seems to find a morsel of hope to inspire you. One of the best professors I've encountered in CRP.

Readings are long and not always relevant. Mildred really needs to learn how to control her mood swings. Often, she is more interested in arguing for the sake of arguing rather than carrying the class discussion forward.

Prof Warner is absolutely direct, but in no way abusive. She expects as much from her students as she would from her professional colleagues. Fosters excellent classroom discussion and does little lecturing herself. Relevant and provocative syllabus. Always available and helpful outside of class. Fascinating, hard-working classmates.
Abusive professor. I did extremely well in her class and I still can't stand her.
Was much more interested in her precious research and using her students for her research than she ever was in teaching.  The only thing I learned from her is what I did not want to do with my life.
She is an intelligent lady, but purposefully brash.  This abrasiveness can come off as down-right mean.

Warner is among the best lecturers in CEE. He really cares about his students, and all of his lectures are extremely well done. I feel like I learned a lot of valuable stuff. The one TA for this course was spread really thin though. Really needed to go to office hours to do well, but few office hours were available.
The cutest professor in engineering. ;)
A great guy.  Course was a bit scattered, but he definitely wants to get better.

Derek Warner is a great guy and his class is actually really interesting. He was only teaching for the second time when I took his class, so he started out rusty, but got better as a the semester went on. He's SUPER NICE and really enthusiastic about what he is teaching. If you do the practice problems, you'll make good grades on the exams.

Doesn't know how to teach. Doesn't know how to support you in office hours (her positive reviews are obviously written by her if you just read them). Assignment instructions are vague but graded as if you know exactly what she wants. Has a very fragile ego.

Awful professor. Rambles on and on about nonsense then proceeds to penalize your homework responses for not regurgitating what she said in class. Very narrow-minded. Also has a weird fascination with power tripping. Please don't take her class if you want to be respected as a student.

Great experience in her Tang Poetry class. 
She follows a very straightforward and clear syllabus and is understanding of student's situations. 
definitely go to her office hours if you find anything hard to follow in class and she'll sure smoothen things out after class.

A genuine, extremely caring professor who's very personable during office hours. 
She knows her stuff and is capable of delivering the content clearly. 
A fair grader all and all.
Would highly recommend her classes to students who actually want to make an effort and learn something interesting!

Do not take a class with her. Lecture was ok but her grading was insultingly harsh. She pretends like she cares about your mental health then uses grades to punish you for not being a brilliant writer with revolutionary ideas. Honestly one of the worst professors I've ever had at Cornell.

Grades are unnecessarily harsh; feel like she is doing this intentionally to people to get more attention/ trying to get them to work harder. Yet, it is counterintuitive since you lose motivation after constantly getting the same bad grades. The lecture quality is also hilarious; it makes zero sense.

The only class I didn't skip the whole semester, a generally amazing professor. Learned a lot, had a good time in class, gasped out loud a couple times at profound statements. One of the top classes at Cornell.
take this class if you want to have a terrible semester, with a boring teacher
Worst teacher I've had in my life

Very engaging class with a great professor. Professor Warner is very enthusiastic about the material and is very reasonable. She definitely looks out for us and wants us to succeed. An all around positive experience.
Absolutely no text book useage and she even refuse to provide any external reference book. All readings are fragmental and not connected with class material,which is merely her own creation.
Very nice and helpful. Made course material interesting and easy to understand. love her class!

Very helpful and nice. Tests/essays fairly graded, but good note-taking is mandatory to well in the class. Class material was well organized and interesting. She was very clear in explanations and always willing to help! Highly recommended!

Professor Warner is one of the most helpful professors I have ever had. She is always very kind and patient with non-native Chinese speakers - even though the material can be very hard. She gives everyone an equal shot at complex subjects. She knows so much about the material! I love the class I took with her.

I took Chinese Literary Tradition with her few years ago.  As other students point out, she is extremely dogmatic and stubborn. No powerpoint slide/textbook.  She expects you to take very good notes.  Tests were hard,  and she is a tough grader.  Avoid this class if you can.  It is not worthy to take it.
Cannot stick to her own words and explanations from time to time. Refuse to admit her own mistake. Tyrannically put down students suggestions.

Every thing she said was a bunch of foreign words jumbled together. Absolutely incoherent, at times I thought she was talkign to herself. When you ask help for an essay, she goes around in circles and does not help one single bit. Whatever she says goes in one ear and comes out the other. It's not your fault if you do bad, its her bad teaching skil
One of the best instructors I've had the privilege of working with.  She has my highest recommendation.
she is very very nice, willing to help students. I love her!
Material is interesting for the most part, except for the poems :: shudder ::  She speaks in a high-pitched voice, but can be pretty funny.  Just gotta watch out for her data-based quizzes

Very smart prof with a passion for the subject.
He has high standards - I did not reach them, but I learned so much. Psets are darn-near impossible for us mere mortals. Prelims graded very fairly and give so much feedback. You can get sub-30 on a prelim and still get a B.
The mathematica nightmares will go away, but your knowledge won't.
Take 3890.

Solid Prof, good lecturer. Lecture is integral in understanding material, you wont pass if you don't go. Chem 3890 is a conceptually challenging class for most, and Ezra's tests are quite difficult so be ready to study. Also, be prepared to do a lot of math, 3890 is basically a math class. (some diff eq, multi, linear algebra, etc..)

While I do think that Professor Ezra is a kind person, his class was incredibly disorganized and difficult. Homework assignments took forever and were nearly impossible to complete without going to office hours. Exams were difficult and very little partial credit was given. Lectures were disorganized and if you missed a day, you were screwed.
He was not an accommodating professor, and rude when speaking with him 1-on-1.
The course material is hard as it is, and Dr. Ezra has relatively good lectures. The problem is the exams. They are very difficult and you only get 90 minutes..

His longwinded lectures are exclusively given live in a dim room with chalk, his handwriting is small, and he fights tooth-and-nail against accommodating sick students. The PSets are extremely conceptual and usually can only be completed with info from poorly timed OH. Ezra has almost no sympathy for the many students who struggle with PChem.

Makes exams unfathomably hard. Assigns lots of work. Not lenient with grading. Not a great or clear lecturer. He's nice enough, but he's not very helpful. All in all, an extremely difficult professor.
The most articulate professor I ever had at Cornell. Tests are difficult and he might not be that friendly, but he is helpful. Every professor should aspire to lecture like Prof. Ezra.

The best lecturer I have had after 4 semesters. Never missed a word he said, I was utterly captivated. Class was very challenging and I didn't think I would like quantum. I now am considering following it to grad school.

Professor Londe is a great teacher. His lectures were engaging and fun. The grading criteria were as clear as can be, and if there was any confusion, he is attentative to anybody with any questions. Readings were enjoyable, and the amount was reasonable. Take this class if it seems interesting, and you won't be dissapointed.

Took Prof. Londe's FWS ENGL1168 (Comics and Graphic Medicine). Easily the best class of my first semester. He made a flexible syllabus and allowed us to submit activities of our own choice. He was very sweet and caring in and out of class. Highly recommend.

I absolutely loved Professor Londe! He is very passionate about what he does and is very accommodating to his students. Lectures mostly consist of discussions from the reading assigned; it's nothing too crazy and is 100% manageable. Definitely take one of his classes if you have the opportunity!

HE IS THE BEST ENGLISH TEACHER I've EVER HAD!!!!!!
He is an angel, so caring and respectful. He listens to all your perspectives and provides you with inspiring feedback.
Class discussions are extremely interesting. He always brings comic books to share with us (some are very interesting).
Take his class--u won't regret!
ENGL 1168. great professor. easy A class. valuable feedback. lectures centered around reading but you could probably get away without reading a few.
Amazing Professor! Had him for FWS and it is imminent that he cares about students and is flexible with syllabi or course structure.
Took FWS class with him not the course what i put. He is a great caring professor.

Took his math & poetry class. Amazing professor. Lectures are really interesting and it's clear that he knows a lot about the subject he was teaching. He was super accommodating during this COVID semester and I'm very grateful for it.

Greg is a great professor and person. His passion for the subject (taken classes with him on poetry and comics) is infectious and you really start to appreciate the material more after his lectures. Helpful outside class too and always willing to chat about things. Would definitely recommend a class with him.

Absolutely incredible professor who truly loves his subject area (poetry) and does everything to pass that on to his students. He cares for his students deeplyand gave some of the best office hours I've personally ever been to, as well and encourages the students to aid and educate each other. Side note, he always seems to have a great book rec.

He is extremely knowledgable about microeconomics and is genuinely interested in helping students, especially during office hours (which he conducted even over weekends during exam season!) Sections with the TA are really helpful but skipping lectures is not an option. His exams are slightly long but the curve in this course is generous.

absolutely loved this course! challenging content but very doable, and bersharov is very thorough and concise with his lectures. Prelims are exactly like the problem sets, very fair and no surprises, the curve is also pretty generous. would definitely recommend.

Genuinely wants every student to understand the core concepts of Microeconomic-Theory. The content is difficult, but he gives a lot of practice. In terms of workload, he may give some of the most difficult/grueling assignments in the Econ Department, but it really does help you understand the content.

Go to lecture & discussion b/c he doesn't post slides or care about the textbook. HW 3-4 hrs/wk. Tests are hard. Study a lot, & then still expect to get saved by the curve.   Definitely the hardest professor for 3030 but you'll learn a lot more. Not even just learning it more in depth, but like straight up covering topics other profs. don't get to
good professor. challenging  but if you put in the effort its not too bad. very thorough

Besharov's class is very math based, which can make it tricky. He is very willing to help you if you come into his office hours, and the curve is very helpful. Maybe not the easiest intermediate macro professor, but I had a very clear understanding of the subject by the time I left the class. Very helpful guy.

Looks a lot like Sacha Baron Cohen, that aside he knows his stuff and you'll leave the class with a great understanding of intermediate micro. If you aren't comfortable with basic calc and lots of algebra you might want to take the class with someone else.
Never take his class. Not recommended.
Tough but extremely fair professor. Curve was generous if it needed to be.

If you want the easiest classes possible, Besharov is not for you. He is, however, a very clear lecturer who really knows his stuff about a surprisingly wide variety of topics, everything from intermediate micro to Money and Credit, which are pretty much opposites. Tests are hard (time constraints) but reasonable, and he usually curves to B+A-.

I think all the people complaining that Besharov is "too difficult" or goes "too theoretical" are using Masson as the ideal benchmark. But honestly after taking higher level econ courses that required intermediate micro, I feel like I was more prepared for the material based on the rigor of this class. If you genuinely want to learn econ, take his.

Besharov is a good teacher. I had him for Money and Credit and Intermediate Micro and liked both classes. He covers a lot of material, generally follows the book fairly closely if you prefer to learn it that way. His explanations are very clear and he's extremely willing to help struggling students. His one weakness is that his tests can be long
His exams are fair assuming you've kept up with lectures and problem sets. Definitely knows his material, worth taking this class.

I don't understand why he gets so many bad reviews here. As long as you prepare well for lectures and stay on top of the readings, the material is very manageable. The exams were long and stressful but not hard. All the material on the exam was covered in class and in the problem sets. The grading was harsh but the curve was more than generous.

I took 3 of his classes (Public Finance, Financial Economics, International Trade)all of which had the following commonalities: closely follow textbook, often supplement with current articles (article discussions were common), solving actual numeric problems, problem sets every week, understand problem sets and you do great on

Great Professor. Extremely intelligent. Knows exactly what he is talking about. He talks a little bit too fast tho and can be hard to follow at times. He explains the method and underlying philosophy of economics and stimulates you to think. Overall a brilliant professor. His class is hard, but take him if you are truly interested in economics.
terrible class in general. Besharov hardly makes the material worth learning and doesn't care at all about his students.

Class was sometimes way more abstract than the problem sets and ultimately, the exams. Obviously, the people who stopped showing up meant that if you actually went to class and paid attention, the curve boosted your grade.

I took financial economics with him. Not an easy A even if you study.  However, he is very smart, approachable, and interesting to talk to.  From what I heard, this is far better than the other Finance courses at Cornell in terms of gaining an appreciation of the material. If you want an easy A, I suggest the AEM or Hotel versions.

Lectures are too fast to comprehend/take notes. Weekly graded problem sets too difficult to complete even after reading chapter/attending lecture. He posts prob set answers sometimes over a week later but they don't help unless you do the problem again.  Class is too difficult/fast paced/taught poorly to succeed in.
currently sitting in his class bored out of my mind. this is probably the worst and most redundant course I have taken. He cant engage a class and teaches out of the book. Avoid if possible

Terrible lectures. He doesn't know the material very well and doesn't explain things clearly. Problem sets do NOT prepare you for the exams, which are full of tricks, really long, and harshly graded. I feel like even he doesn't really know the answers to his tricky questions, he just makes things up. Unhelpful with answering questions.

Interesting material, but I agree that Besharov makes concepts more confusing than they need be.  He is extremely arrogant, and unwilling to really work with this who are slow to grasp concepts.  If you are not strong in econ but interested in material, consider a different professor.

I love this professor. The class itself was interesting and wasn't too hard. I also felt like I learned a lot! I also liked that the professor made us fill out a midterm review of the course and adapted the rest of the semester based on our opinions. Take this class!! It's not that hard either if you try.

Terrible, just terrible.  Difficult homeworks and tests.  His tests were nearly impossible to prepare for and nothing that I studied showed up for the final exam. Lectures/notes, and even textbook do not prepare well for the exam. On top of that, he is a harsh grader.  Avoid him.

Ouch...one of the best yet worst class I've taken at Cornell. The material is itself interesting, but Besharov somehow makes it horribly dry and confusing. His exams are very long and don't make much sense at first glance, and he DOES NOT give credits for problems that depend on previous answer if your previous answer was wrong.

by far the hardest class I've ever taken at Cornell, hands down. While the material itself is challenging but not difficult to understand with some studying, Besherov is a terrible lecturer and actually does not care about students' and is discouraging rather than encouraging. answers to questions are cryptic and he is quite arrogant.

By far the worst prof I've had at Cornell. He does not understands his own material -can't answer questions aked in class. A nice guy, but the problem sets and lectures DO NOT prepare you for the exams. My guess is that only people with previous background in finance do well. Otherwise, it is impossible to make sense of the tricks he puts on them.

Most encouraging economics professor I had. He explained concepts thoroughly, while others glossed over them. I didn't know what capital and technology really were before I took his class. He's an honest grader, but the problem sets help you become familiar with his material.
OUCH...Poor professor on all fronts.

I took Financial Economics w/ Besharov and found the class to be pretty easy.  With only a moderate amount of time and effort I got an A- out of the class.  Homeworks are grade flotation devices and are graded pretty easily, exams can be tricky if you don't attend class/don't really look at the homework. I'm not sure about the other classes though.

I'm not sure what everyone is talking about on here; Prof. Besharov is a pretty good lecturer and is extremely kind and helpful outside of class.  His tests were challenging, but the class was curved to a B+.  Definitely would recommend, just don't expect to coast through the class.

Had this guy when he was at duke. class lectures are boring and completely useless for exams or prelims, unpublished textbook was awful, prelims and final exams were IMPOSSIBLY hard and made no sense. We got things we had never heard of. He says he curves, but he curved our test average from a D+ to a C+. avoid this man, our average was a C+!

Students who did not attend class were not notified of the fact that one of the final exam questions were revealed during lecture. Do not need to show up to class to get a good grade, but the weekly homeworks are annoying and pointless. Not recommended.
Weak professor. Doesn't help during office hours, doesn't understand his own material. Confused the class often - as a result, attendance was abysmal.
A mediocre prof who compensated for his mediocrity by indiscriminately doling out mediocre grades.
Graded rather than tested to a curve on the first exam, and the final was pretty hard. Weekly homeworks annoying, lectures often boring, but a decent guy.

Not a bad prof.  Sometimes got lost in the middle of lecture, but kept the class very relaxed.  Weekly homeworks were annoying; he stressed the qualitative side of things.  First exam was way too long, but he was generous in grading and the final was just right.  Overall a good class, and not too difficult.  Nice guy.

New professor. The course was not quantitative and exams were ok, time-consuming annoying homework due weekly.He can be adequately described as a novice.sometimes doesn't understand his own lectures, and although i did well his grading system made zero sense and seemed unfair. boring lectures, kind of killed my interest in the class.
Great class. He does a good job at reinforcing which concepts are important while keeping lectures fun and informative.
Take this class if you can, but it's difficult to get in.  Useful, fun, but biweekly quizzes can be tough.
Well-spoken, eloquent, and easy to understand.  Keeps light atmosphere with jokes and stories.  Offers good advice both in and out of class.  Clearly knowledgeable in the area.
Decent, has good stories.
Very interesting prof if you are among those who wish to read fiction about climate change.
Ms. A is a really good teacher. Be sure to take her class if you get the chance.

Kristen is incredibly thoughtful, intelligent, sassy, and well spoken, and makes the effort to relate course content to other topics/ current events. Her passion for feminism and climate change shines through and is truly inspiring. Most importantly, she really cares about her students and doesn't hesitate to go the extra mile for them. Recommend!!

I had Kristen as a reader for my class and she outshone the professor himself, it was a pleasure being in her section and her discussions were truly inspirational and taught me things well beyond the scope of the class. Definitely take a class with her if you get the chance!

Ms. A is very nice and genuinely cares about her students. The course material is actually great and will change your perspective on humanity. She grades kind of hard at first but she gives EC for every assignment so you won't flunk unless you're really really really lazy.

Awesome teacher who really cares about the intersection of literature and climate change.  Varies papers/readings/classtime, never boring, understanding, super relaxed class Makes you question how to live in the Anthropocene...

She is really passionate about her subject which is great! we would receive long and hard readings every other class and she gave us A LOT of papers to write. In this class you will have a reading and 1-2 people in your class will be discussion leaders for the reading, and the next time in class you discuss the reading. we did not have slide tests.

Kristen is clearly very passionate about the subject she is teaching! She has a lovely personality and easy to access outside of class. However, she assigns an exorbitant amount of reading from the textbook as well as supplementary readings. It's a lot. She is a tough grader when it comes to papers so plan to spend a lot of time on them.

Kristen is really passionate about the subject. She is quite willing to help and it is a good idea to go to the officer hours often. The material and assignments were quite difficult, though. Prepare to put in time and effort.

Positives: - Passionate about the material, the class and the students - Knows her stuff - Interesting personality. She grew on me   Negatives: - Long, hard readings. Technically, it fits the guidelines but it's all at grad student level - Confusing prompts. Figuring out what she wanted me to do was sometimes the hardest part of the paper

I enjoy Kristen's personality  and the environment she creates within the classroom. However, the assignments - especially the Final Paper - were a bit stressful to complete at a high level of skill in the time allotted.
Too much effort had to be inputted for a freshman writing seminar, and when you finally get your grade back you realize you got a C on a paper that you spent countless hours working on

For a freshman writing seminar, this class is ridiculously hard. She gives out mostly Cs and Ds on papers and expects grad student level work. The readings are very dense and excessive, and she assumes you already know a ton of history and art. Her prompts are so confusing and complicated, you never really get what she wants.

Kristen is a GREAT TA. Discussions were always interesting and she always incorporated the students in conversations about the writing material. The readings and artwork contained noteworthy background knowledge that I personally think everyone should know. She grades papers very fairly and she is so easy to reach out to get help for anything!
Kristen is such a great TA! She seems to love teaching and shows a genuine interest in helping her students understand the material.

Kristen is extremely helpful, passionate, and interesting.  I thoroughly enjoyed having ARTH2400 Section with her.  Kristen made section fun and very informative! She was very clear and made an effort to help each student in and out of class.  She is a bit of a harsh grader on essays, so she definitely will make you work for your grade.
Really an excellent TA for an excellent class.  Highly recommended.  Very friendly, and very interested in her students and their studies.  Has some strong opinions about art.
LOVED ARTH 2400, Kristen was an amazing TA and made my interest in the subject grow even more.

From Bernini and the Baroque to Leonardo and the Renaissance, Kristen Streahle made ARTH 2400 an exciting, interesting, and engaging. Always willing to help with essays and any questions, the enthusiasm Kristen brought to the subject was unparalleled. There is really nothing bad to say about Kristen. I wish her the best of luck with her PhD.

Kristen is extremely passionate. Even though the subject she teaches is pretty unconventional, she shows up to class everyday excited about the subject and ready to engage each student. Expectations are straightforward. Good class :)
She was very understanding, and helped me to do well in a class I otherwise would not have

Kristen possesses the quality found in all great teachers: passion. She is passionate about her scholarship and students. Dynamic lectures coincide with diverse reading material and writing assignments. Kristen challenges her students to think critically and write purposefully and facilitates these objectives through extensive feedback.
She was nice and did a good job of inspiring me to find an interest in a field I didn't think I had any interest in.  Best of luck in Academia.

Ms. Kristen Streahle is always ready and excited to teach class. Her enthusiasm inspires her students to explore different aspects of the subjects being studied and motivates them to dig deeper, find more information/evidence, and develop a well-rounded understanding of the topic at hand. She is incredibly kind and helpful to her students.

Straightforward class with clear expectations. She was always available for additional help and communicated assignments with individual documents online. Stuck to the syllabus, even though it involved some dense reading, and got a lot out of the class. Overwhelmingly positive FWS experience.

Class material was interesting, and discussions were engaging. The texts can be a little dense, and, especially while interpreting artwork, and require a deal of critical thinking. Streahle herself is awesome, cares about her subject, and wants you to do well. She'll dedicate large amounts of time making sure that her students are oriented.

Kristen gave really clear and useful feedback on papers - a quality that not all FWS teachers have. She utilized some really interesting sources and definitely sparked my interest in the subject matter. Grading was fair and consistent. She's not an easy grader but you get what you put into the paper. Would definitely recommend the class!
This class taught me about monsters that I wouldn't have learned elsewhere. Her teaching style was clear, and I especially liked visuals she brought to class. Enthusiastic, helpful, and fun!

She was clear, fair, approachable, and at times a little stage-fright, but aren't we all. After taking this seminar, I definitely became more interested in art history - a topic far from my major. I had no prior knowledge or interest really. I liked her grading process - you get what you put into your paper. Overall, great experience.

I really liked how Kristen gave good constructive criticism on papers and gave students the opportunity to increase their grade if they revised their papers based on her critiques. It was also awesome how she made sure to spend more time on topics that interested the class and less time on the topics that didn't.

Kristen's class was both enjoyable and challenging. The material was engaging and spanned a multitude of eras and geographic regions. Perhaps she tried to cover a few TOO many topics, but the overall quality of the course was very high. The workload was significant, but I left the class much more intersted in and knowledgable about art history.

Kristen is fun, but often in class we didn't talk about the reading. It made me a little frustrated to do the reading if we didn't discuss it. Otherwise, Kristen is nice and fun and brought up interesting, if someone random  points. She is a hard grader, but after she turns your papers back, she explains what she wants, which is helpful feedback.

Fantastic teacher. Fostered interest about the subject, provided timely and extensive feedback, taught a lot. Liberal towards different perspectives, and compassionate at times of trouble (midterms oh no). Hit the spot with reading assignments as well! Marx, Nietzsche, Freud is definitely a class I'd take again.

Anna was an amazing instructor, she was always prepared and absolutely devoted to teaching. Always down for a conversation, she knew how to keep people interested (exceptionally rare in a philosophy FWS!) and I would most definitely take this class again. Side note, attendance is 'mandatory' but I got away with missing a few days.
Very clear, exercises are really helpful, would take again 10/10! Best at Cornell!
Very confusing
she's a really bad teacher. you'll be better off studying on your own. do hw and pre-class quizzes with care, though she says they're useless. they hurt you later in the semester.
do not go to class. she will confuse you.
Good professor but not very rich class, more as memorization and that's it. Not very inspirational.

Dr. Thalacker-Mercer is a great professor. Sometimes she does read too often from her slides, but everything you need to know for the quizzes, prelims, and final exam come right from the slides. Don't even waste your money on the textbook. Go to class! Some ppl skip and just study the slides on their own but you'll retain so much more if you go!

Anna is a decorated researcher, though falls short as a professor. Lectures consist of linearly reading slides adapted from another prof without context or student interaction. Assignments are very difficult and aren't motivated by lectures. Compared to other inspiring classes at Cornell Tech, this class feels haphazard and unnecessarily difficult.

She didn't write very clearly on the board.  Examples were difficult to follow.  She would sometimes explain how to solve problems during tests so if you were willing to stand the incomprehensible lectures you might get a reasonable grade.

Homeworks got better with some cool applications as the class progressed.  Couldn't have made the exams any easier than what they were.  Always willing to answer questions in office hours and make sure you understand the material.  Lectures could be a little more organized, but overall a good teacher who seems to aspire to do better.

SOOOOOO disorganized. Horrible teaching methods. Long and pointless homework that practically doesn’t count. Zero reference as to any possible application of the theory she teaches. BAD teacher (Nice ass though).
Doesn't speak English well. Bad at explaining things. Writing on the board is very hard to reading. Becomes angry easily. I would say all she's got is her good physical appearance.
worst professor i have had at cornell

Bella Italiana! An amazing professor whose good looks are a bonus to those conscientious enough to go to her classes, which are interesting. This lady will never fall into depression I think, with all the good things going for her (unlike most Cornell students).
No Comments

The class wasn't terrible. She definitely tried to make it understandable for the students and the tests were moooore than fair. And the biggest plus is that she is probably the hottest professor in ECE.

She's a great professor, I don't know what the other reviewers were talking about. She presents the material in a clear way and has a genuine interest in the students' ability to understand the course material.
Yells at students, won't write a letter of rec. Mean and disorganized. Hottest in ECE (that's not saying much). What are you bitter about?
No Comments
Wouldn't round a 99.8% to a 100% for an A+. That's pretty petty. Other than that, she is a good lecturer and the coursework is very managable

I LOVED Professor Haskins! She is one of the most fair and accommodating professors Ive had this semester by far. The course content made me rethink a lot of aspects of my daily life, and was interesting to me as a stem major because its somewhat outside my typical sphere. Definetly reccomend to everyone!

Professor Haskins is one of the best lecturers at Cornell. Her powerpoints are very organized with interesting and applicable content. I learned so much from this class which gave me a much better perspective about the inequalities in America. Everyone should take a class with Professor Haskins before they graduate.

Professor Haskins is organized and lectures very well. Her material is clear and interesting, and even though there are a lot of readings, she summarizes them during class. Her exams are detailed yet fair, and she makes it easy to get a good grade if you put in the effort. The class was eye-opening, definitely recommend!

Professor Haskins is awesome. She is passionate, well-prepared and very clear about what she is talking about. There is a fair amount of reading but you can just skim it thru and she gives clear summary of reading materials during lectures. Her study guide for prelims are well-structured and TAs grade generously. There are also some extra credits.

Loved her, her lecture were extremely helpful so I never did any of the readings. Weekly memos are easy as long as you apply your experience outside of class to the course material. She's extremely approachable and understanding. Overall, really enjoyed her class and will be taking SOC2220 with her this fall!

Lecture felt more like a middle school course than a college course. She read out definitions in class, we mindlessly copied from a powerpoint and regurgitated definitions verbatim on exams. Discussions were useless and "active learning" wasted lecture time. Easy class but I didn't gain much memorizing convoluted definitions I didn't understand.

Mixed feelings about the course. Lectures were pretty straightforward (material got somewhat confusing towards the end). I liked that the prelims were all short answer, however, they were pure memorization. As stated by others, prelim 2 was graded harsh, but I think prelim 1 + 3 were more lax. Generous extra credit! Sections were totally useless.

This class is perfect if you're looking for an easy A, but I personally didn't get much out of it. Haskins simply read out definitions without truly applying them to current events or real world issues. Grading on prelim 2 was harsh and arbitrary; points were deducted for not having a word by word definition of concepts they didn't ask for.

She is a really nice professor, and she really wants us to learn more about critical thinking, while this class per se does not require that much effort to do well. A great relaxation if you have tons of work from other classes. Does not curve. S

At the beginning of the semester, we were told that every test would be purely memorization, and doing so would easily get you an A+. Come the second test, there was very unfair and ambiguous grading over simple word choices. Professor rushes through the material at the beginning of class and tries to hold discussions that don't really help at all.
Incredible professor. Easy class, definitely interesting material. Only 1 homework assignment per week. Don't bother reading the assignments, weekly memos take no effort. Prelims are incredibly easy.

Not a big fan of her class. I knew all the material but somehow didn't do so hot on the prelims. Turns out you have to write exactly what she wants you to write or else it's wrong. Not a big fan of forced memorization over real learning and understanding.

It's an interesting and enjoyable class, but kinda hard. If you don't write what they're looking for on the tests, then you won't do well. Plentyyy of extra credit seminars (and they're interesting!). Overall good class. Discussions were pointless even though they're mandatory. Haskins is super nice and truly does care about the students.

Anna Haskins is my favorite professor at Cornell! SOC2220 was a joy to be in. There are many readings in the course, and I would say that you should do the majority of them for the exams. Prof Haskins is accessible, understanding, and passionate about this class.

Amazing professor. Lectures are very engaging. Offers lots of extra credit opportunities. Material is interesting and relevant. Lots of weekly reading which you have to summarize for a weekly homework response but easy to skim. Highly recommend Haskins, best professor I've had at Cornell!

This class is so much better than DSOC 1101. Haskins is much more interesting to listen to, and the course structure is better (25% each exam/15% sections/10% memos). The readings are so long but they are summarized in lecture, and study guides are provided for exams. The only complaint I have is that the section is useless but attendance is taken.
i love her so much

She is nice, smart, classy, and a great lecturer. But SO MANY READINGS!!! Plus, you have to read the books she assigns you to read or else you will do terrible on the exams. I thought discussion section was a waste of time. Lectures are super interesting though. Tests cover a lot of reading material, so the most important thing to do is read!

Clear, awesome lectures! Open-minded, inspirational, easy grader, amazing teacher and mentor. 11/10 love her!! I took her controversy of inequality class and it was extremely easy. The average on both the prelims were As. But besides that, her lectures are to the point and helpful. She truly cares about her students and the class. TAKE HER CLASS!

Professor Haskins is a great professor who really gets you to focus on the bigger picture. She assigns a good amount of reading but it's all worth it and she goes over it in lecture. Her exams are graded well and she wants to make sure you understand patterns more than numbers. It's a great class and is making me consider a major change!

Haskins is an amazing and the best kind of professor. She made me love the class and I always left class feeling that I really learned something. She cares a lot about students and is a great teacher- take the class! There is a lot of reading but it is interesting and she summarises them in class so you know which parts of the reading to focus on.

Prof Haskins is a great *teacher* who cares that students understand the fundamentals about inequality. She does a good job of not forcing students to be bogged down by minutia in her exams. Understand the basic ideas of readings and the points of her lectures, and you should be fine. Debates were also enjoyablenot stressful. Overall, great class.

She is really passionate about her subject which is great! we would receive long and hard readings every other class and she gave us A LOT of papers to write. In this class you will have a reading and 1-2 people in your class will be discussion leaders for the reading, and the next time in class you discuss the reading. we did not have slide tests.

Kristen is clearly very passionate about the subject she is teaching! She has a lovely personality and easy to access outside of class. However, she assigns an exorbitant amount of reading from the textbook as well as supplementary readings. It's a lot. She is a tough grader when it comes to papers so plan to spend a lot of time on them.

Kristen is really passionate about the subject. She is quite willing to help and it is a good idea to go to the officer hours often. The material and assignments were quite difficult, though. Prepare to put in time and effort.

Positives: - Passionate about the material, the class and the students - Knows her stuff - Interesting personality. She grew on me   Negatives: - Long, hard readings. Technically, it fits the guidelines but it's all at grad student level - Confusing prompts. Figuring out what she wanted me to do was sometimes the hardest part of the paper

I enjoy Kristen's personality  and the environment she creates within the classroom. However, the assignments - especially the Final Paper - were a bit stressful to complete at a high level of skill in the time allotted.
Too much effort had to be inputted for a freshman writing seminar, and when you finally get your grade back you realize you got a C on a paper that you spent countless hours working on

For a freshman writing seminar, this class is ridiculously hard. She gives out mostly Cs and Ds on papers and expects grad student level work. The readings are very dense and excessive, and she assumes you already know a ton of history and art. Her prompts are so confusing and complicated, you never really get what she wants.

Kristen is a GREAT TA. Discussions were always interesting and she always incorporated the students in conversations about the writing material. The readings and artwork contained noteworthy background knowledge that I personally think everyone should know. She grades papers very fairly and she is so easy to reach out to get help for anything!
Kristen is such a great TA! She seems to love teaching and shows a genuine interest in helping her students understand the material.

Kristen is extremely helpful, passionate, and interesting.  I thoroughly enjoyed having ARTH2400 Section with her.  Kristen made section fun and very informative! She was very clear and made an effort to help each student in and out of class.  She is a bit of a harsh grader on essays, so she definitely will make you work for your grade.
Really an excellent TA for an excellent class.  Highly recommended.  Very friendly, and very interested in her students and their studies.  Has some strong opinions about art.
LOVED ARTH 2400, Kristen was an amazing TA and made my interest in the subject grow even more.

From Bernini and the Baroque to Leonardo and the Renaissance, Kristen Streahle made ARTH 2400 an exciting, interesting, and engaging. Always willing to help with essays and any questions, the enthusiasm Kristen brought to the subject was unparalleled. There is really nothing bad to say about Kristen. I wish her the best of luck with her PhD.

Kristen is extremely passionate. Even though the subject she teaches is pretty unconventional, she shows up to class everyday excited about the subject and ready to engage each student. Expectations are straightforward. Good class :)
She was very understanding, and helped me to do well in a class I otherwise would not have

Kristen possesses the quality found in all great teachers: passion. She is passionate about her scholarship and students. Dynamic lectures coincide with diverse reading material and writing assignments. Kristen challenges her students to think critically and write purposefully and facilitates these objectives through extensive feedback.
She was nice and did a good job of inspiring me to find an interest in a field I didn't think I had any interest in.  Best of luck in Academia.

Ms. Kristen Streahle is always ready and excited to teach class. Her enthusiasm inspires her students to explore different aspects of the subjects being studied and motivates them to dig deeper, find more information/evidence, and develop a well-rounded understanding of the topic at hand. She is incredibly kind and helpful to her students.

Straightforward class with clear expectations. She was always available for additional help and communicated assignments with individual documents online. Stuck to the syllabus, even though it involved some dense reading, and got a lot out of the class. Overwhelmingly positive FWS experience.

Class material was interesting, and discussions were engaging. The texts can be a little dense, and, especially while interpreting artwork, and require a deal of critical thinking. Streahle herself is awesome, cares about her subject, and wants you to do well. She'll dedicate large amounts of time making sure that her students are oriented.

Kristen gave really clear and useful feedback on papers - a quality that not all FWS teachers have. She utilized some really interesting sources and definitely sparked my interest in the subject matter. Grading was fair and consistent. She's not an easy grader but you get what you put into the paper. Would definitely recommend the class!
This class taught me about monsters that I wouldn't have learned elsewhere. Her teaching style was clear, and I especially liked visuals she brought to class. Enthusiastic, helpful, and fun!

She was clear, fair, approachable, and at times a little stage-fright, but aren't we all. After taking this seminar, I definitely became more interested in art history - a topic far from my major. I had no prior knowledge or interest really. I liked her grading process - you get what you put into your paper. Overall, great experience.

I really liked how Kristen gave good constructive criticism on papers and gave students the opportunity to increase their grade if they revised their papers based on her critiques. It was also awesome how she made sure to spend more time on topics that interested the class and less time on the topics that didn't.

Kristen's class was both enjoyable and challenging. The material was engaging and spanned a multitude of eras and geographic regions. Perhaps she tried to cover a few TOO many topics, but the overall quality of the course was very high. The workload was significant, but I left the class much more intersted in and knowledgable about art history.

Kristen is fun, but often in class we didn't talk about the reading. It made me a little frustrated to do the reading if we didn't discuss it. Otherwise, Kristen is nice and fun and brought up interesting, if someone random  points. She is a hard grader, but after she turns your papers back, she explains what she wants, which is helpful feedback.
The worst.

Really great prof and person. He discussed a person experience he had which nearly brought me to tears. Textbooks are interesting, assignments are fair and marking is reasonable. Overall, a really great prof and person.

Very basic syllabus and passable course! However, Professor Cheran does not like to actually teach the course. 95% of his lectures have nothing to do with the mid-term exam. You will have to use prior knowledge in different types of social movement like the Woman movement and BLM to pass the course. Very good course to take if you are an BSW major!

He's only hard to understand the first couple classes but then you get used to his accent and understand him better. His lecture slides are terrible, difficult to read unless you go to class. He goes off topic a lot and I feel like 50% of what he says isn't even course material. Papers, exams, tutorials, quizzes, many diff ways to get marks.

I found that if you paid attention in class that you could get past his accent. He was one of the best Professors I have had, as you had to actually read to know what the course was about. I would absolutely take his class again. He was more than helpful, accessible and informative!
No Comments
An engaging and helpful professor!
Nice guy. Realizes you have other classes and a life so he keeps the course load light.
Do yourself a favour and never take this person unless you want to go to class listen to his boring stories and teach nothing about what he is supposed to. And make attendance worth 10%

he is my favourite soc teacher!! i absolutely love him, he is incredibly knowledge and funny, makes great examples and the class work is SOOOOO easy!!!! I have taken 4 courses with him, and I have never received under an 86 as my final grade. I highly recommend him,

One of the most ridiculous professors and class I have ever gotten myself into. His classes are so boring and there are no slides or anything visual that help us study from. He makes the TA mark everything including midterms and finals. Whatever is stated on the syllabus for the exams is also different from what the exams are. 
there is TWO finals.

This class was definitely very interesting and He is a great prof to listen to. He has many stories and is interesting to listen to. I did very well in this class and he was an easy marker for sure. I'd take another class of his again.

Literally would not post slides until someone with a hearing disability said that they needed the lecture slides. He never takes about the lecture only ever about his life experiences. Buy the textbook it will be your best friend as he is not. And wont give extensions also schedules things after the mandatory due date and has them due in finals.

One of the best profs I have ever had at the University of Windsor. I have taken 3 classes with him and expect to take my 4th next semester. There is a lot of work to do and the exams are the longest I have ever taken, however I have always received an A+. Prepare and do what is expected of you and you'll get a great mark and even betterexperience!

Professor Cheran has a very basic syllabus to give the student the opportunity to pass. 1 short-assignment, 1 midterm, 1 group project, 1 take-home exam and participations mark. Great course for Social Work and Sociology majors. There is also a great insight into learning about different movement. Really short classes and not too much lecturing.

Dr. Cheran is an amazing prof who cares about social justice and is not afraid to teah controversial material. If we didn't have him in the department, classes like Genocide, War Crimes, and Ethnic Cleansing probably wouldn't be offered. I've taken several of his classes and he has gone above and beyond to support me. Just go talk to him.

he genuinely seems like a great guy but i pay 9 grand a year so i expect a lot more. He speaks so quietly despite us constantly asking him to raise his voice, his slides are pointless but i cant even take extra notes because i don't understand him,and the midterm is next with and i have absolutely no idea what to expect. terrible class
I hope we do not fail

He is the most difficult prof to understand I've ever had, and I've had tons of profs with language barriers. His lectures aren't good. He cancels class all the time, so now the whole class is going to fail the midterm because no one knows what to study. Very nice guy, I feel bad cuz everyone attacks him in class but we need a new prof.

Someone wrote in the comments that the prof asked for students opinions for the due date of the project then rejected it. ACTUALLY, nobody agreed on anything therefore he decided to set a due date himself. He just wanted to find what was comfortable for us students, but since most people did not agree on a date, he had to set one himself.

Haven't even finished a whole semester yet but thought I'd share my thoughts. I am concerned because I cannot understand him through the thick accent. Also, he was unsure when the course project should be due and asked students their opinion, then decided to reject it. I confronted him in class about it and he made no sense about it. TBC...

If you get through the thick accent, he is an ok prof. For our Globalization class, he would have students teach the class via group presentations, and then he would talk for about 20 minutes after to "fill in the blanks" and leave. Journal and essay were easy, and exams are simple also. Very easy class if you read the textbook and/or attend class.

This Prof is extremely hard to understand if you are not good with accents. His social skills seem to be lacking as he does some strange things in front of the class including sniffling so loud trying to clear his nose and its sounds like wet mucus... He has too many assignments. This is not a simple/easy course. I am taking Globalization.

Really friendly and open prof. People are intimidated/annoyed by the accent, he's actually really easy to talk to and willing to help if you need it. Plus almost all of the exam material is from the textbook.. the accent is no excuse lol. I really enjoyed his class and I hope I have a chance to take another before I graduate!
good

Gay and Lesbian studies. Was his first time teaching this and was honest about it. Strong accent which didn't bother me but others found him difficult to understand. Delivery was unfortunately bad although his heart is in the right place. Even took us for a beer after the last class :)

Its not that this prof is a bad guy, he just has no social skills. Yes, he is approachable but I will never forget that in my first social movements class with this prof, he was actually picking his nose while lecturing. Aside from being a bit odd, hes a fair marker (or his GA is)and very approachable for help.
Just get up and talk to him. class is fine.
cheran is a great prof. hes very laid back though and it sometimes makes him appear to not care. if you go talk to him one on one, he's great.
Great professor, actually lectures without notes, laid back and easy going. Really knows his material and is a fair marker.

He was a good prof...he was approachable and helpful when extra help was inquired about. He may have an accent but if you do required readings before class you are able to understand...overall good experience...
This was the worst prof I have had yet.  Spent all that tuition money trying to understand his thick, crazy accent.  Avoid taking his class at all costs!!!

extremey boring and unintriging prof....theres no way you couldn't fall asleep in his class or wanna kill yourself. Exams were extremely lengthy but he marked okay. Oh yah..you also walk out of that class not having learned a single piece of information. tuition money well spent...again
very easy teacher
The exams were very lengthy, but fair. Overall, he was an easy marker, but his speech was not all that clear and he was definitely  not very helpful.
No Comments
Fairly easy class, difficult to jump from A- to A though

I took Great New Books with Emma in my first semester and it was definitely a fun experience. She's very engaging in managing the discussion and you'll get a lot out of participation. Better yet, she gives amazing feedback on your essays; if you seek her advice you're unlikely to get blindsided by critical grades. She cares about what she does.

Great professor for Intro. to Creative Writing. She relates really well to students and made herself available to meet outside of class. I would definitely take another english class with her and I am far from an english major.

Great teacher! Not too much work, interesting, and kept class fun. Brought us donuts one day! Had her for FWS: Great New Books and it was by far my most fun class, but don't take if you don't want to read, since it goes off the reading a lot.

Perry is great! Took two classes with him, Art of teaching and Youth Organizations. There was reading and writing for both classes but it really was not bad at all. Great guy. Taking another class with him next semester. Make him your BFF if your in the education minor.

It's hard to write an honest review of this class since its basically impossible to not get an A or A+ in the class. The class itself is mostly busy work with in class discussions every week. Your grade is largely dependent on your undergrad TA. There is about 50 points of extra credit you can get added to your final grade at the end.

Professor Perry was amazing! You can tell that he really cares about teaching and his students. He has hilarious stories and fun in-class activities. I was injured during the semester I took his class and he made sure all the assignments were super accessible. All around an amazing professor and person.

Dr. Perry is probably the best prof I've had at Cornell. He is so knowledgable and wants to see everyone do well. His expectations are clear, and if you put in the work it's an easy A. EDUC2410 does require 3 hours of student teaching each week outside of class time, so do not take this class if you have a busy schedule.

There's a certain level of irony in taking and education class where the professor doesn't know how to teach. Literally zero organization. The syllabus, calendar, and modules all have different information, and he doesn't announce any assignments in class so you never know what to do. So much busy work too which he never discusses or announces.

I have never written a review on Rate My Professors before. That being said, this was genuinely one of the most disorganized classes I have taken at Cornell. Readings are outdated, the prof is never there, the TA's were rude, and the class content was boring. Expect to do a lot of busy work.

Pretty solid professor. The fieldwork component of the class is fantastic. The weekly readings are pretty good and generally not too long, but the annotations are kind of annoying. Final presentation rather than a written final or paper which is nice.
Fantastic Professor! Provides good grading rubrics and gives thoughtful feedback. Enjoyed this class and would take it again! Genuinely cares for student success.

Grades papers based on odd personal preferences that aren't listed in the rubrics. Lectures are boring but required. Overall, the class was still easygoing and fun. Only take it if you are interested in teaching.

Perry is a great teacher, even though the TA's do most of the teaching. There are A LOT of assignments but once you get into a routine of doing one or two a week, it's not too bad. If you do all the work, you will do well. The class teaches the material well, and the activities are a lot of fun, but it can drag on because it's a very long class.

Very enjoyable class, great general elective. Prof. Perry is a very understanding professor, who has a passion for education and teaching. The course revolves around dynamic discussions, 10 reflection papers on field work, and reading annotations. Perry is fair and truly cares about student learning. He is a guy you'd want to have beer with.
Good teacher but he is not the main instructor of this class. Usually the graduate TA and other TAs lead the classroom to discuss. He grades fairly and offers effective feedback.
This class is amazing. Grading is great. You have to do about three hours of fieldwork every week but it's so much fun. Classes are long but never boring. There is a lot of discussion.
If you're good at math take Maria Terrell, if not find another professor.
WORST professor I had for Math, ever! Highly opinionated and does not listen.
She was very enthusiastic about the material.  The material was pretty hard but the tests were straightforward.

She's a genius, but VERY disorganized prof. She had us use her unfinished textbook for Multi. That meant it was free, but also devoid of examples and not very helpful. Lectures were also disorganized, and discussions didn't help much. I passed the class thanks to her easy grading, but didn't learn the material. She's nice but I don't recommend.

Don't judge her according to the scores on this site. Professor Terrell is one of the best professors I've ever met at Cornell. She teaches me not only knowledge but also ways to think and how math is related to science. Prelims and finals are OK if you review all homework problems. Yes, she does seem a little weird, but it makes her lecture fun.
She was friendly, helpful, and always willing to give time to explain something. Tests were difficult, but fair. She inspired me to become a math major, and her lectures were incredible.

Dr. Terrell was one of the best profs I've had here so far. She was extremely committed to making sure you understood the material. Office hours were an incredible resource. You can tell she really cares about her students. She was trying out the textbook she was writing, so we got free printouts.
She was trying out a new book that she was writing, which was still a bit rough in some spots. She had a way of making complicated ideas more approachable and had a somewhat eccentric sense of humor.

Both my roommate and I had Maria for Math 1920. The vast majority of lectures are spent on theories that aren't that relevant to the core elements of the course. I would say that only 5% of the lecture topics actually appeared on tests and there is a terrible curve.

Professor Terrell was not helpful to me. One time in office hours, she made me wait 20 minutes so that she could finish writing a review about herself on this site. In the end, I passed the class thanks to the Calc I tutoring sessions done by another professor.
Ineffective lecturer. She struggles to make sense and gets on too many irrelevant tangents. Sometimes she goes over time without any consideration for those of us who have to get to another class.

Dr. Terrell is the best math professor I've had so far at Cornell. She really wants her students to understand the subject and puts a lot of effort into making the concepts more intuitive. She does a lot of examples in lecture that follow clearly to the homework. It's still the Cornell math department though, so tests are hard.

Awful lectures. Maria seems to be more committed to writing fake reviews on this board than to improve her teaching skills. Catch her offguard in office hours and you will see. Tests are somewhat fair. The worst part is the textbook which doesn't provide good examples.
This professor made learning multivariable calculus fun, stress free, and manageable. Her personality animated the lectures and she was a VERY good explainer. Great class. No complaints.

Really eccentric but one of the best lecturers I've had at Cornell. She really makes an effort to explain the math concepts instead of just writing down equations or doing constant proofs and theorems like 1910. Exams were okay except the final which was killer. She's not perfect but as far as 1920 is concerned she's fantastic at teaching it all.

Some complain that the tests are hard but that is not the case at all. I've compared her tests to those set by other professors who've taught the class. Her questions were easy and a straightforward application of the concepts, whereas other professors' required many layers of depth and demanded thorough understanding. Just pay attention in class.

Probably my favorite lecturer thus far. The material is hard but she does a great job coming up with simplified versions that are easy to understand. She is quite entertaining as well. I didn't always take notes in class because, being honest, sometimes I barely made it to 11 am class on Friday but just sitting in class was enough to learn a lot.

Terrell is very quirky but that makes lectures more interesting than they otherwise would be. Emphasizes geometry and thinking about a problem rather than following the same steps for each one. Prelims are reasonable and corrections are very helpful.

I really enjoyed 1920 with Terrell. Her lectures are clear and organized. She make s the class enjoyable with her quirky examples, and she adds some jokes here and there. If you put in some effort  you'll end up with a good grade!
An amazing professor who truly cares about how well her students learn the material and how they do in the class.
Very weird personality, which sometimes got in the way of her lecturing.  Not very helpful office hours.  Tough prelims.  Course is required though so not much you can do.
I don't know why people have negative evaluation on Dr. Terrell. She is one of the best professor I've ever met at Cornell. Extremely nice personality and helpful lecture.

Terrell's lectures were very confusing and unclear. Only about 10% of the lecture was helpful on the prelims. The exams were not too bad... they were fair and the regrading policy definitely helped out the kids that did poorly on the prelims.

Professor Terrell is ultimately an excellent professor. She really cares about teaching, and does a better job explaining than most. She makes sure everyone understands the concepts rather than drilling problems, which is a good thing in the end.

She's nice but not always understanding (in general and with mathematical concepts). Office hours were sometimes helpful, but personally my TA helped me a lot more with this course than Maria's lectures did. After awhile I stopped going to lectures entirely, although the review lectures are helpful and the exams are pretty reasonable.

It is rare to find a professor at Cornell who pours in so much thought as to how to structure the course in the most effective manner. I really admire how Dr. Terrell cares about how we will be applying the concepts in multi to our physics and engineering courses. Her conceptual style was meant to drill useful material that we would encounter often

If you take Calculus with Maria, you will only learn it if you are willing to go to the tutoring sessions taught by a different professor for all the Calc 1 sections. I did it and found it helpful. I earned an A!

Dr. Terrell is easily the best professor I've had at Cornell. She truly cares about teaching kids math, and is an extremely entertaining lecturer. She also goes beyond the basic "this is the equation, here's how to use it" and explains to you the proofs for why the math works. She also is very good at helping you visualize what is going on.

Very enthusiastic about teaching, and a nice person. I had some trouble understanding her lectures at first, but after a while, I got used to them and began to like her lectures more. She was interesting and sometimes would randomly yell about how much she loves flux in the middle of class. Also used a weird barbie doll demonstration.

The first two prelims were rather difficult and required that you really understood the concepts behind all of the major 1920 topics. She does do test corrections which is nice, and that along with a doable final can allow you to get a decent grade. I spent a lot of time learning the material on my own; I didn't benefit too much from her lectures.

Professor Terrell did her best a teaching a very hard subject. Her tests were difficult and I believed them to be unfair at times but that tended to show through grade distributions. She wanted you to learn the material on a deeper conceptual level because multi variable is more than just straight computations unlike most other math courses.

I personally found her lectures tough to follow. Her style didn't really suit me. In her defense though, multi is a tough topic to teach and one that you can really only learn through doing examples over and over. She really does try to help students out.

Dr. Terrell is an extremely dedicated lecturer and goes out of the way to ensure conceptual understanding as opposed to computational ability. Grades should not be the focus of an introduction to vector calculus. In terms of helping students to understand concepts, Dr. Terrell was excellent.

Not a lot of correlation between the material in class/problem sets/textbook examples and the exams... Prof. Terrell is very conceptual, but doesn't explain the concepts well, which makes the class much more difficult than it should be.

She couldn't have been more useless. A german shepherd sitting in front of the lecture would have taught us more. She made this class awful. One of the lowest quality professors ever to grace this university. Does not belong at Cornell, or even at a community college for that matter. Scrambled, incoherent style. Truly a disgrace to her profession.

Condescending, unhelpful in office hours. Occasionally will insult you. Unable to understand student's mistaken logic and merely insults the student's mistake. Lectures have no organization and the professor sometimes makes critical conceptual errors in explanation. Would recommend waiting a semester to take this class with a different professor.

Very poor professor. You will fair much better by skipping lecture and teaching yourself from the textbook. Terrell skips all around the textbook in a random, detrimental fashion. Additionally, her grading style is both elementary and unfair. If at all possible, avoid this professor.
Lectures were useless--she could never really explain things clearly. I suggest self-study (you'll probably do better) if you're stuck with her. The textbook is a better teacher in my honest opinion.
MATH 1920 should have auto-tutorial on its title given that Maria doesn't really teach the material. Cornell should assign a professor, not a lecturer, to this difficult class.

On the first day of class, she says that textbook reading is mandatory. It is. However, the examples and alternative interpretations she provides in lecture are invaluable.
