This teacher is not a real pushover like some of the others.  He tends to get confusing when he discusses sometimes.  He is really easily available for questions.  French became less fun as the year progressed but thats just me.  He always brought culture into the classroom.  Take Ornelas!
He knows french, and has experience in the french culture,but as far as teaching sometimes he gets confused.  But give him a break he's young.  A lot of homework. OK professor

His accent can be hard to understand at times but he is a good professor otherwise. He reads straight from his slides during lectures and exams are very straightforward. There are pop quizzes so just show up, if anything. Not bad, would take him again if I had to.

This professor was the kindest one I have been taught by. However, the tests don't match up to what he usually says to study. Also there are pop quizzes but he seems to forget until the last few weeks, so attendance isn't mandatory up until then.

His lectures were basically read straight from the power points, so it wasn't a big deal to miss class. However, he does have pop quizzes, so it might be important to show up lol. Otherwise the class was fairly easy and felt like a repeat of previous information.
If you take Uriel be prepared to learn about fish and only fish. He is a nice and funny guy, but a terrible professor. I have hardly learned anything outside of fish biology all year.

dr. uriel has a thicker accent, so if you have trouble understanding accents i would pick a different prof. he writes his own tests so the questions are often confusing. he is a very nice, approachable, funny guy but does not check his email often and does not round final grades. comprehensive exams

Hes really helpful and will address any questions you have out of class. If you are having a difficult time with a subject or a grade doesnt make since to you hes always available to talk. His course was super lightweight and he helps to bring your grade up if you ask. This was a great review of biology
Absolutely wonderful definitely recommend him!
Nice and fair. Kind of tough and hard to understand but tests are easier than other profs. He is a funny guy who will round if you ask

He wants you to succeed. He has an accent, so if youre close minded maybe not for you but if youre a normal decent human being you will enjoy yourself. Tests are hard unless you read study guide. If you ask him for anything he will most likely give you it. Minus beer, he says were not allowed to drink that.
Take his class. He is fun and cares about your grade.

Dr. Uriel is a decent professor. Exams are excessively easy even though lecture sometimes is not. No homework assignments and no pop-quizzes. There are scheduled quizzes throughout the semester and a final paper. No comprehensive final.

I think he means well but this class was very difficult due to the Professor Buitrago. His accent is very hard to understand and english is not his first language so there is sometimes grammatical mistakes and other things that make it confusing. I think he's a great person but I didn't learn a single thing in this class. I do not recommend.

Uriel is really nice, however, his accent does make class difficult and and he has a hard time understanding students questions. You could easily do this class without going to class, but he has random pop quizzes so it's hard to skip and they hurt your grade if you miss. The tests are EXACTLY like the study guides he puts up. Easy enough

Hes a great professor you can tell he really cares about his students. Lots of videos in class for animals and he has quizzes that are pop quizzes. His tests are literally word for word from his study guides and if you dont feel ready for the exam you can email him and hell push it. Overall amazing.

Dr. Butriago knows a lot about his subject but there are some times where he slips up in class and doesn't understand student questions. The resources are there to pass but it takes a while to find all the material. He can be decently funny at times and he tries to keep it lively in class but it can fall flat sometimes. Just be ready to study ppts.

As a person, he's a cool dude, but he has a really thick accent which makes lecture very hard to follow. He teaches material needed for the test on the day of the test. The class is extremely hard to pass and the tests are awful. The labs aren't bad and literally made my grade higher in that class. I would NOT recommend.

Test Do NOT line up with lectures. sit near the front, his accent is heavy. Be prepared to read between the lines, he picks questions over topics that are not talked about much in the book or lecture. the "study guides" are not helpful, they list everything in the chapter, so read everything or you won't know it.

I had a hard time understanding what he was trying to teach mostly because of a language barrier but he also seemed lost himself with what he was talking about. He rarely assigns homework and expects us to learn all of the information on our own basically. The information he teaches rarely applies to the style of the tests, get ready to study a lot

He is such a nice man, bad professor. He is hard to understand and teaches material that is on the exam the DAY OF the exam. Slow, lectures are confusing. I wish I would have taken this course with a different professor.
Dr. Buitrago is a very good professor and I would recommend his class to other students. He knows what he is talking about and explains the information in a way that is easy to understand.
Dr. Boitraga is very knowledgeable and enjoyed his class immensely!
I enjoyed Dr. Buitrago class very much! Be prepared to learn!
Buitrago is the GOAT.

Be prepared for everyone to be unprepared for this class, including Dr B. Tests are typo-laden with mislabeled figures and unclear questions. Not available outside of class, though I tried often. Though you'll learn more from the book than going to class, you should still go for random, in-class assignments. Generally unable to convey material.

I do not recommend. Try and switch now if you have him! He had a thick accent that is hard to understand, can be very confusing in his lectures, and was very behind with my class. We would be learning important information the day of a test. The good part is it was not necessary to go to class because he basically reads straight off the power point

Do not take this professor! He is really knowledgeable in his field of study, but he cannot teach! He has a thick accent, and all we did in class was read through slides and watch movies. Would not recommend!
No one should ever take him in the history of Biology. He does not know how to teach at all.

This professor was not clear in lectures often times; he would confuse himself in the midst of explaining a concept to us. He provided way more detail than we needed to know, so it messed with the larger concepts we did need to know.
This teacher messes up a lot in class and the students have to correct him. Contradicts himself quite a bit. Lectures do not really help with exam, usually go into the exams blind.

Buitrago genuinely cares about the success of his students but his lectures/slides were so surface level that it didn't help on the tests. He has a thick Columbian accent that makes it difficult to understand him. I would suggest going to his office hours if you want him to further explain something. Labs and manuscripts are the reason I made a B-.

The biggest hurdle in his class is the lab. Study for the practicals at least every other week and make study guides! Trust me, it is TOO MUCH to study in a few days. The lecture tests are not too bad if you finish the study guides. The pop quizzes are an excellent cushion to your grade. He's a very sweet person! Ask and he will help you!

Lab practicals for vert morph are very tricky... aside from that, the lecture portion with Dr. Buitrago is very doable... most test questions are directly from powerpoints/study guides... going to lecture isnt too helpful except there are pop quizzes so you gotta go.. but he is a great guy and being successful in his tests is definitely manageable

The closer you sit to the front, the easier it is to understand him.  He's willing to help if you go to his office hours.  It's a difficult class, so just be prepared to work.  Do the study guides and memorize the powerpoints.  On the bright side, the lab for this class is an absolute joke.

Dr. Buitrago does have a thick accent, but you will understand what he is saying 90% of the time. He is very kind and nice but truly knows his stuff. Tests are the type where you think you did good but end up not getting as a high a grade as you thought. But if you do the study guides you'll get the majority of it.

Thick accent but super funny guy. His power points are very surface level, but if you go through the intensive study guides prior to the test you will be fine. He is very helpful and if you ask him a question in the right way during a test he will pretty much give you the answer. seems to really care about students. great guy!

I really enjoyed Dr. Butraigo's class. He really knows his stuff and he tells lots of funny stories. His tests are pretty fair, although sometimes the wording is somewhat tricky and confusing because of his accent. Quizzes that are random but he usually reviews before he gives them. Lab practicals are HARD because there's a lot of material covered

Immature teacher that employed alot of childhood camp games, patty cake and the "name" game.  Wish this would've been a more professional course that would've been more structured towards giving presentations and lectures for business purposes.
Fantastic teacher, very enthusiastic! Obviously wants his students to succeed and actually get something out of his class! Definitely recommend!!!

Very juvenile instructor.  He plays a ton of name games and patty cake - not something I would expect in a college course.  He gets very personal with his students - which many young freshmen appreciated.  I would've appreciated professionalism.
I found this class to be really fun... Uri made it interesting, and he likes to play games often, which helps people become acquainted with one another. I would definitely recommend taking his class.

Uri is fantastic. He really makes you want to speak in public, even if it terrifies you. He is very playful in his teaching style, and you will leave his class with a whole new set of friends and a newfound confidence in public speaking.
Very helpful and demonstrates the importance of public speaking

Doug is really funny and nice. He cracks some of the best brilliant jokes. Hes classes are very fun to go to. Materials, though, are very tough. But you dont really have to be able to work out everything. Physically based computer animation requires advanced physics knowledge, but you dont need everything to do well in this class though.
Probably the coolest professor on campus. CS5643 is hard though. I recommend Numerical Anaylsis or some higher-level math background if you want to understand the material.

Although some lectures were not the most cohesive, his friendly demeanor and contagious attitude made the class quite enjoyable. Perhaps not the best lecturer, but if I had to learn from him again, I would be pretty happy.
A good, clear lecturer. He is very knowledgeable and interested in the subject matter. Also, his Canadian sense of humor is great.
A lot of stuff he says goes way over our heads, but he's good at keeping your attention and has that cute nerd thing going on
Terrible!Stay away from him. You will not regret this advice.

Dr. Almy is a FANTASTIC lecturer - you will never regret taking a CHEM course with him.  Very helpful in office hours, clear  and interesting lectures, and VERY COOL demonstrations.  Yes, these intro CHEM lectures were FUN!
Does cool demonstrations.
this guy is the epitome of ****
Really friendly man, very helpful and understanding.
what a little ****.....needs to learn a lot about being a teacher

I didn't read the textbooks, just did my best to memorize the glossary terms from the assigned readings. I took extremely detailed notes of everything he SAYS. Memorize everything you can. His delivery of the lecture was most important. I learned a lot in this class and appreciate Prof Cutting's dedication and passion for these topics :D

Lectures and textbook cover different material with some overlap, and you have to study both for exams. In-class pop "essays" (really just a 2-3 sentence response to a basic question) count for 10%, top two exam scores (out of 2 prelims and the final) each count for 45%. Exams are short answer and require lots of memorization.

His lecture slides by themselves are not too helpful. The real stuff happens in the professor's delivery in class. So attending lecture is key. If you make it, the lectures are fascinating and well-delivered; if you don't, well, good luck trying to infer the content from pictures and random terms. (When I tried that, it didn't go well.)
Knowledgable professor but he cannot communicate information clearly to students. Powerpoint slides are not very helpful. Prelims draw from pure memorization of random definitions.

At the very first lecture, Professor Cutting states that while he knows everyone here are at the top of their game in their respective high school classes, he is here to separate the very best from the best. And he does this by making his notes extremely disorganized and exams ridiculously hard. Knowledgeable professor but horrible teacher.

Yes the tests are really hard, but this class is very fair overall. Best formula to get an A: GO to lecture, write down about half of what he says, learn the bold terms in the book, and study hard for tests. Cutting is a masterful lecturer, very intelligent and knowledgeable. Boring every once in a while but usually fascinating, original material.

An incredibly thorough, clear, and well-organized teacher. Exams were detailed, but very fair. He also let the entire class know outright that lecture material and text readings would be distinct from one another, but that both would be covered on prelims. Hands-down one of the most competent people I've learned something from at Cornell.

The subject matter is interesting, but his exams are really hard - you need to know every little detail, even obscure book definitions that have never been discussed in class! But it's clear he's an expert in what he's talking about, and has many different interests. He's a true intellect, and extremely helpful during office hours. Great guy

Professor Cutting is an absolute genius and his lectures are fascinating. He talks a lot about art and is a very engaging lecturer overall. His exams are difficult, but if you attend lecture, read the book, and study a lot, you CAN get an A. Definitely recommend.
Examinations are a bomb, but if you study you can pass. Very good lecturer and very good prof. overall.Very profesional.

This class is hard. You have to be on top of everything and I mean every litte detail. I recommend taking this class if you have a easy course load. If not don't stress yourself out--Cornell is stressful already.
Very Hard

Prof. Cutting is my advisor. Class was decently hard. The tests were very hard because they involved very detailed memorization of truck-load of material. If you have a very good photographic memory of every page of text and lecture then you are garanteed to get an A or better in class. Last minute cramming will definitely not cut. Highly curved!

Never had a more competent and organized professor. He takes information from a wide range of disciplines and condenses it into these really impressive lectures. It's not easy to get an A, but it's worth it. I learned a lot. Not much reading. Show up, take good notes, and you'll do well. Don't take the optional final!!
HARDEST CLASS EVER!!! Don't subject yourself to it unless you like getting Cs.
Tests are very very hard but material is interesting.  Not good to take as a distribution but good but overall it was a decent course
very enthusiastic, knowledgeable, great use of powerpoint
very clear, knowledgable professor. Difficult exams, but absolutely possible to get good grades if you go to lectures and keep up with the stuff. PSYCH 205 was a really really fun class.
He shines with brilliance and his enthusiasm for the material. Tests are super hard. But I loved the lectures. Seldom have I looked forward so much to going to class.
Really enjoys the subject.  His presentations are very clear, although his tests are really difficult (the curves are generous though).  I would definitely reccommend taking a class with him.

Lectures are very good, but simplistic from my opinion. The course is easilly passable if you just go to lectures, and you can get a good grade if you do anything more. Its an interesting course, and it was great as a low-workload distribution course.
His 205 class was moderately interesting, but his exams were silly exercises in memorization. No real conclusions drawn from the course, but still some exposure to 'fun-to-know' type stuff.
No Comments
No Comments
get him alone if you want to talk about anything, but he's very helpful.
James is very very nice, caring, and is not a tough grader. I love this class because he invites lecturers/ performers from different fields to give presentations in class. They are truly amazing.

You will learn useful, applicable skills in this class if you pay attention and do the work. A lot of people claim that Stapp can be confusing, and while the instruction to assignments can at times be a little confusing, he is more than willing to clarify at anyone's request. If you come into this course wanting to learn, you'll enjoy it.
Lectures are a tad boring and can be awkward at times. Overall, he's just average.

I do not know if Spinazzola taught this class before, but he was very disorganized, and the final project is complete mess. We have gotten so much conflicting information throughout the semester about assignments and dates, and he also tried assigning multiple pieces of work over wellness days.

I think that most of the unhappy reviews are because he taught intro stats (I can see him being difficult to learn from in intro stat). But for an advanced class he was good. Taught the theory in class and gave us examples of how to use R to actually apply the theory in the real world. Met with me 1 on 1 when I was behind and helped me catch up.

Very meh professor. He seemed like he had no desire to teach this class at all as his lectures were very boring with few examples of how to do the statistics for ourselves. Additionally he went awol right before the final and students were panicking because we didn't know what was going to be on the exam and the TAs couldn't help us either.

Kind person, & extremely intelligent. However: He went through slides way too fast, & I ended up teaching myself the whole class & R programming language. Provided very few practice problems you'd see on exam. Concepts were not really explained thoroughly. 8am+kinda boring lecturehalf an auditorium of kids passed out. Would not take again :/

He is very knowledgeable and nice, but he gives his lectures either too fast or too slow, and tbh, kind of boring. Exam mean and median are lower than previous years. Part of the reason is due to his ambiguous lecturing style... Overall I learned a lot from this class, but I won't take his class again.

I LOVE PROFESSOR MCCRAY. 

Cornell needs more people like her here. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed in her course and beyond in a way that is so rare. 

She was always willing to meet to help you improve and also to check in with how you were doing in general. 

My writing definitely improved in her class.

Literally the most perfect professor one could ask for. Very engaging, the content is very relevant to our lives, and gives amazing feedback. If you genuinely care about the course, you will learn and grow so much as a writer with her as your professor. Cares for her students' well-being better than anyone else.

Prof McCray is very caring for her students, and she makes sure we know it. She promotes self-care and is willing to grant extensions on assignments. She is a refreshing change from the rest of the professors. Her grading is pretty lenient, too, and is mostly participation-based.
Theory and Political Anthro are great classes! Thank you, Jaro.

Jaro is a clear, professional, and interesting lecturer. No, he does not use brightly coloured pictures to teach, but he has handfuls of fascinating stories and examples to share. I really enjoyed his class and appreciated his approachability outside of lectures.

Political Anthropology is one of the best classes I have ever taken. Jaro is a very enthusiastic and helpful professor, and a fair marker. He REALLY wants students to do well in exams. Do not miss the video showings: they are very interesting.
Awesome instructor. The class was great, and he always offers help. I had to read a lot, but it was worth the effort!
Very helpful prof, very interesting materials. If you follow his advice, you will do very well. Also, most of the videos he shows in class are fascinating. I definitely recommend him.

Dr. Stacul may appear intimidating, but if you follow what he says in class i.e. read 'x' by 'x' date, and you will be on schedule, and you will do great. He is INCREDIBLY helpful, and he is Very clear in his explanations of the material. Exams show what you learned, not what you did not learn: He is making incredible contributions to learning.

Jaro definitely has a passion for this subject. Brings up interesting topics, etc. Allows for lots of questions during class with awkward pauses. Quite intimidating too. He gives the appearance of helpfulness, but honestly? RUN. RUN RUN RUN. Expectations are ridiculously high, and class is geared toward Anth majors with experience. Sigh.

I dislike that he does not hand back exams, to get the exam back you must have an awkward conversation about it.He says he does it to help students but I found it to be a waste of my time.Do not ask him about the exams in class(freaked out on a girl) or come late(does this rude check watch stare at you thing). He is seriously strange...and boring!
So interesting and super handsome and sweet and offers lots of help!

Found this professor extremely condescending & unapproachable. Often wondered why someone who hates students so much would choose to be a teacher. I think the expectations for the assignments were very high & his criteria for grading was not conveyed thoroughly. I am now paying hundreds of dollars to be in a night class that is NOT taught by him.

I don't understand the negativity towards Jaro. I found him to be highly professional, helpful, and friendly. He basically lays out exactly what you need to know for the exams. Though highly comprehensive, they are not overly difficult. I didn't even read his text and I got a fantastic mark in the class. He's very approachable!

I really like this prof because he is a true professional. He doesn't parade around class telling stupid stories. His lectures are very interesting, but you will have to write a lot of notes. He is highly intelligent so prepare to learn a lot, and make sure you attend his classes!

The Worst. He reminds me of Mr. Bean. I had his class at 8 and his office hours were at 330, which was brutal because i was done at 11 and he absolutely won't make an appointment, had no sympathy for me having to wait 4.5 hours just to see him. maybe I'm whining, hes brutal though, seriously.

He reads off powerpoints and makes you by his book, which was the most expensive one i bought that semester. Assigned readings are mandatory, you'll do terrible if you don't. our class average hovered around a c+, if that's a little low for you avoid him (unless your an anthro major, then you cant avoid him) uh-oh :(

If you go to his class, and read the assigned reading than you will get an A. He does not like student who are there to just "get by", and expects good work. He is HIGHLY intelligent and if you liste, the lextures are very INTERESTING. I thought exams were easy, maybe thats cus i was the only one who did the reading and actually went to class.

Marking methods are HIGHLY subjective: he says that he will be expecting one thing, then he will mark another way and will not provide evidence or reasoning for his marking.  To see our exams we have to go to his office, and he holds the exams, you do not get to look at it. 1st midterm was 14 chapters plus extra readings and movies.  RUN.

Worst prof I have ever had. Incredibly condescending and rude, frequently embarrassed students in front of the class. He would not give us the readings we had to do for our term essay (worth 35%), which were six large journal articles and three movies, until 10 days before it was due. Makes you buy HIS book, very $$. Does not hand ANYTHING back

He wasn't a horrible proff but he wasn't that good either. i found it frustrating that he read off his power points and wouldn't post them on black board. there were a lot of readings aprox 2 chapters a week and they were long chapters. exams were mostly MC which was nice but i could tell he was ESL by some of the questions.

I found him easy to follow, teaching style is poor though, all he does is read from powerpoint slides, of which all the information is basically extracted straight from the textbook. LOTS of videos, at least once a week, always an hour long. Tests arent bad, but you have to study! Oh and poor use of blackboard, doesnt post your grade AT ALL.

OMG this class was insanely not hard but confusing. He assigns articles and movies to for the midterms and finals but you still need to do your textbook readings. He says UM a lot and stops for questions frequently for long periods of time, if we have questions WELL STOP YOU TO ASK, tests are hard. Ick is all i can say, go for any other teacher
I don't like his teaching style, I find him hard to follow and it was difficult in free willingly wanting to attend his class.
The guy is a total ****bag!!! His exams are just whack and your never really sure as to how he marks the damn exams. He say one thing and does the other.

I really think that it is unfair that he has u buy the book he wrote as his thesis, you cannot sell it back and there was so much more that could have been covered.  the first half of the course was great. second half was just grating.  OH and his book was like $96 and you get nothing back.
Imagine Mr. Bean trying to teach you something...STAY AWAY!

Great teacher, very clear and concise notes which are posted on blackboard each weekend. Very approachable and extremely friendly. He is someone who has a passion for teaching and a strong desire to help students do their best.

Most boring class i've ever experienced... he just reads everything off his powerpoint slides and doesn't add anything at all. If you want an interesting course don't take this one. Besides that getting a good grade is ridiculously easy even if you dont attend class. He is a nice guy who will gladly offer extra help if need be though!

He lays out almost exactly what's on the exam and it's just up to the student to go in the text and memorize a few things to get a decent grade. He's always around begging for people to come visit him in his lonely office however there is so much clarity in his class that you will never need to. Really nice awkward guy.

I LOVE DR. BILO SO MUCH. The few exams you do have require studying but they aren't often so it isn't bad. One paper that you have plenty of time to do. He cares about each student and understands if you have things happening in your life. I would recommend this course to anyone and will be trying to take another one of his classes.

I ADORE DR.BILO. He is genuinely so sweet and understanding. Formed a great relationship with him and can tell he wants us all to succeed. All the tests are on stuff he writes on the board and talks about in class so 95% of success in this class is taking notes but it really isn't bad. Wrote one 8-10-page paper but it really wasn't bad. LOVE!
love this class, take it if you can

Dr. Bilo is by far my favorite prof at UD. This is my second class of his, and I'm taking another next semester. Genuinely caring, sweet guy, and extremely knowledgeable, He gives great lectures. class attendance isn't technically mandatory, but he doesn't post his notes online and his exams are entirely class notes, so I almost never skipped.

He's very passionate about what he teaches and the lectures are funny. Make sure to read what he assigns you, and to take good notes in class because what he writes on the board is gone over on the exams.

Dr. B is an awesome prof. His lectures are interesting but have a hard time hearing him sometimes. He is willing to help you if you need it. Don't miss class cause it is all exam material. Overall pretty straight forward class and you can pass it easily
Second go around with Dr. Bilo. He is amazing. Few assignments but a great knowledgeable teacher. Show up and take the notes and you will be fine. Has really good jokes too

Come to class, he is not digital and if you miss lecture you're missing out on exam material. Very few things count for grades, and participation is one so be involved with class. His exams are straight forward and right from his lectures and he also keeps lectures interesting and engaging, so pay attention. I absolutely loved him as a professor.

Dr. Bilo is a great guy, and his class is super engaging. The class can be scary because you are only graded on a few things, but his exams are straightforward and he doesn't grade extremely hard or anything. attendance isn't required I don't think, but his class was super enjoyable (and also notes heavy) so I tried not to skip

Dr. Bilo is a very structured, organized educator. He keeps lectures relevant, enjoyable, & engaging; he welcomes students to chime in with their insights. His grading scheme is a bit tough and can catch you on your heels, but he's not the world's hardest grader. . .not a free A. He's also pretty witty and comedic. I enjoyed the class tons. Take it
Great guy, really understands the topic, but his lectures are long and sometimes boring. You are only graded on a midterm, final, and a term paper. He isn't an easy grader but is fair.

Dr. Bilo is one of the most passionate, caring professors I've ever had. There are only a few assignments in this class so work hard and don't be afraid of asking him for help. He loves when people do the readings and participate in the class lectures. He writes all his notes on the board so if you don't go to class, I hope you have a friend :)
Engaging lectures. Clear expectations, but you have to work for your grade. If you put forth the effort, you'll be rewarded and learn something. No powerpoint notes so go to class

This was my first class with Professor 'Bilo' but I will definitely be taking him again. His notes are word for word the tests, so make sure to take notes. There are very few grades in the class, so make sure to do your best on everything. He is such a nice, caring teacher who wants the students to take something valuable away from the course 10/10
He sucks if you are trying to learn not memorize. its literally a 214 class and treats it like a 400.

Prof. Bilo is one of the most compassionate professors. Took his course as a non-major, but fell in love with political science because of it. The course makes you more aware of US security and is a fascinating study of its progression overtime. NOT at all like a history course tho! Textbooks are not used (just online articles) :) highly recommend!

My class was online so we had note outlines given to us and we would fill in as he was lecturing. Only had 1 term paper and 1 final paper that were graded so not much chance to make points but he gives a lot of time (no class sometimes) to complete them and participation/forums are also graded. He keeps class interesting and entertaining.

Just be ready to take a lot of notes and learn a lot! PLEASE take good notes because this will determine your grade for your midterm & final (30% each of your grade). He RARELY does extra credit, it's only if he sees you actively trying and participating. There is no study guide you must study ALL of your notes for the midterm and final to pass.

not a lot of room for error because points come sparingly. He is not too hard of a grader on papers if you give effort. Class can be boring if you don't love politics. He is insanely passionate and is very knowledgeable. He is a guy you want on your trivia team. His lectures/notes are word for word what u need for the test. STUDYNOTES ARE ESSENTIAL

Dr. Bilo means well but he teaches like its 1997. He has not changed his teaching style with the times and it shows immensely. Alongside having few graded papers and being very specific on tests. He doesnt even run a isidore page.

This is my second class with Bilo, and I'll be taking another of his classes next semester. He loves to make jokes and makes lectures interesting. His exams are easy to study for, just take notes during class and study them! You also have to write a term paper, but he isn't a very hard grader and you get to choose your topic.

I really felt like I learned a lot about the world in general. The class wasn't very hard either as long as you pay attention during lecture. Over all amazing person and really cared about his students. There was one paper (8 pages) we had to write for class, however, you get to chose a topic that interests you which makes it better.

Dr. Bilo might be one of the best professors in the College of Arts and Sciences and in the Political Science department. He really cares about you and 'your grade. Taking notes in class is the only way to do well in his class. You need to go to class in order to do well. But overall, not too hard of a class. I'm for sure taking him again.

Amazing professor!! Would for sure take it again. Take detailed notes of his lectures and you will be fine. Learned so many things about the world and globalization that I would not have otherwise learned. Recommend: 10/10

Dr. Bilo is the best professor I've had at UD. I loved all of his classes, I've taken 3 so far, and wish I could take more. His lectures are very detailed and thorough, so if you take good notes, pay attention, and attend class you should be well prepared for the exams. He really cares about his students, if you take his class you won't regret it!
Dr. Bilo is the man. Far from a breeze but made all lectures interesting and relevant. Great professor would definitely take him again.

Readings aren't totally necessary (no discussion) but they benefit you a lot on the exams and papers. Tests are pretty hard and very specific. Highly recommend.
Good writing seminar in my opinion. He expects a lot from the essays, but grades fairly and has a lot of interest in the subject, which makes the class more enjoyable. Would recommend.
An extremely dedicated professor who really wants to help his students. You WILL improve your writing if you take this class. Be prepared to put in the work, but it's definitely worth it.

I can easily say one of the best professors at Cornell. Very clear, comprehensible, very fair grader, if you put the time into the essays he will give you an A or A-. Very dedicated and approachable and always willing to help. His lectures are never boring. I would very highly recommend this writing seminar. Absolutely amazing guy.

He's a great guy, extremely helpful and knowledgeable, and takes his classes seriously.  He'll do anything for you if you show interest and dedication.  He expects what college professors should of their students.  I would recommend him to anyone

What a nice guy. He may be a tad bit shy/nervous and not the best public speaker but he's knowledgeable about the subject and passionate about it, and if you go to him for help he is always there and very understanding and kind. Only negative is that he expects REALLY good papers and really detailed, hard grader. Good class overall, learned a lot.
This class was not very difficult, and tests were very fair. The readings outside of class were often boring and tedious, but the lectures were pretty good.

If you do your work, the class isn't that hard.  It's just that people think this is an easy A class where you get an A just for showing up.  I didn't do really well, but I definitely got what I put into the course.  Lectures are sometimes boring, but you NEED to go to know what's going on (unless you buy takenote).
Class readings are pretty good, a few dense books though, lecture is interesting, tests are VERY straightforward, you'll know exactly what to study for.
He is very boring to listen too. Of all his lectures I don't think I stayed awake for any of them. He has a monotone voice what tends to put people to sleep.
No Comments

Found it very hard to stay engaged with his bland, text heavy, lectures. Tests were based off of the many readings & were very specific to policy. I felt that even though I read and studied, I was unable to do well. Very disappointed by this class and professor. For a class on education, his teaching style did not work well with my learning style.
Not always the most interesting lectures but he's nice cool & accomplished, very cool dude
Professor Matsudaira is one of the best I've had thus far. He was passionate, helpful, and very intelligent. Really cared and wanted to engage the class. He was also funny!

An excellent class. He uses very interesting material for teaching so it is easy to stay engaged and learn a lot. The group empirical assignments and presentations were not easy, but they were always interesting and I learned a lot from them.

Only about half of what he teaches us is about actual film music. The rest of his class is about discussing the problematic history of hollywood where he goes on tirades about marxism, male gaze, and the evils of whiteness. You're gonna learn a few things about film music, but don't be fooled, he strays away from the actual subject a lot!
Amazing professor and made learning German fun and easy!

Although I would not necessarily call the class easy, I absolutely loved it.  Professor Hull is one of a kind, and the class is one I will never forget.  She has an incredible knowledge of German History, and the class (Post-War German History) is a great one.  If you have the opportunity, take her class!  You will not regret it.

Had I.V. Hull in '81-'83.  Demanding professor who cares about quality.  Best professor I had at Cornell.  Glad to see she is still true to form.  She made me understand that history is a product of interacting groups in society, not just the actions of one leader; not just the program of one ruling party or government.

Hull is probably the best professor at Cornell. She will actually take time and proof your essays before you turn them in (she actually encourages it). She is clear, intelligent, and caring. Idiots beware, she will call you out. Come to class prepared, or get chewed out. If you are prepared to work, definitely take a class with Hull.
Course is a lot of work. Come prepared to sections, go to lecture. Tough grader but not unreasonable; she does have a serious attitude problem, however.

great lecturer- clear concise and a great discussion leader, but her personality leaves something to be desired. If you don't like profanities and hostility directed towards you for no good reason - don't take her.
One of the best profs at Cornell. Take whatever class she is offering--it will be worth it.

Awesome! She is incredible. If you want to become a more critical reader and writer, take her course. Her class is a lot of work but definately worth all the effort. She is the best professor I have ever had!
Really sharp and great discussion leader. Hard grader but completely worthwhile.

This professor graded very harshly and it seemed impossible to do well on an assignment. The class environment made me nervous to participate because I have seen her single students out passive-aggressively. If possible avoid taking a class with this professor as you will put a lot of time and hard work into your assignments for mediocre grades.

SPAN 2095: I always feel comfortable in Spanish classes but this was the first time in my life that a Spanish class made me feel so uncomfortable. She's very passive-aggressive. If you are a native speaker she would grade you harsher. She will literally take off 2 pts in the hw if you forget an accent mark. The material is good, she's not.

she is nice, no busywork which is nice, accessible outside of class, my only issues were the 10 minute quizzes which gave you like 2 minutes to answer each question and how strict grading short response answers was in the class.

Most compassionate professor I've ever had! Assignments have a purpose behind them as the content builds off each other, so there isn't any busy work. Make sure you thoroughly read the readings and pay attention in lectures because there are in-class quizzes. The lectures were pretty engaging, and she really wants you to learn!
amazing professor!
Robin is awesome. His class is interesting and inspiring! Strongly recommend!!!!

Loved the class. 6 quizzes, participation, and one final translation project make up the whole grade. The quizzes are all covered in class. If you studied those well and attended classes regularly, it is an easy A+. Professor McNeal is very understanding and flexible to accommodate students' scenarios. He genuinely cares about the students.

Robin is the best! His lectures are engaging, interesting, and informative. The assignments are well balanced and fun. This guy truly cares about his students and he knows his stuff! I can't recommend this class enough.
Just randomly assign grades to students. Students who work hard and participate actively in class ended up getting lower grades

Doesn't allow for your own interpretation of the theories and readings. It's his way or the highway. Class has a separate clique of people who defend everything he says and therefore succeed in his class.

Had good impression at first, but then realized he gives preferential treatment to a select few and grades are completely based on his opinion. Even if your paper is well-written, if he doesn't agree with you said, expect to get a much lower grade than what you deserve. If you manage to get on his good side, then all is well. Would not take again.

McNeal is my fav prof at Cornell. He's incredibly passionate about his field and is very flexible and considerate. He makes the material interesting and so long as you attend lectures, read most readings, take your time on the essays, and study your notes you'll get a good grade. It was 100% worth getting up early to attend his lectures every week.

Really enthusiastic and knowledgeable of his subject. That being said, he goes off on tangents really easily. Fun to listen to still. As long as you go to lecture, quizzes and papers are really easy. Don't think he gave below an 86 on first paper. Subject material mostly analysis of myth, and only ancient ancient Chinese myth.

He doesn't have a particular format to the quizzes, and grading takes him far longer than it should. He is not that funny, though he tries to be, and some days he doesn't even say anything important to lecture because he goes off on tangents. This course is more literary theory than actual myth but if you want an easy course than this is it.
Lectures are very interesting. Quizes are relatively easy/fair as long as you attend most of the lectures and do some of the readings. I have to say, he is a funny man
He is really great! He is tending and understand the urgent situations. Grading is good too. Really love his course!!!!!
He's a really good teacher and you can tell he loves his subject. He comes in to teach every section for a day. Very easy class, and Wikipedia will be your best friend.
Great guy- funny, realistic expectations. Brought a whole new perspective on China to light. TA's are easy graders; class is really easy to get a good grade in.
Professor McNeal makes learning about Chinese mythology fun and accessible. Awesome teacher, easy class!

take his class ! the best prof in asian dept. very interesting topic and GREAT lectures. like original ideas and discussion. asks questions that make you think. great connection with students! remembers everyone's name and willing to talk to spend time to talk to students. grading is easy too.
Very nice professor and patient. His materials are not too difficult as long as paying attention in class and prepare for quizzes a bit. He explains things well and you know he knows his stuff.
Very good Professor who makes everything he teaches interesting.  Sometimes he oversimplifies more complicated material, but this is an intro class...

This prof has known me for a while. I liked his course a lot. It was an easy course and being Chinese myself I actually learned things. The sections were not that helpful. The essays and quizzes are graded easily, and the homework is almost guaranteed full credit if you just put the effort into them.

An excellent intro to the culture and history of China.  Fun and easy to stomach.  The tests and quizzes aren't hard, and I don't remember reading a lot of the assigned reading (though the reading he assigned was interesting).  The TA can make the class work, like any class here, though, so get in good w/ him/her.
so so easy. SO EASY. he is a good professor. the class is even better if you have a awesome TA like i did.

McNeal is by far the most interesting and helpful teacher out there.  His brilliance is only reiterated by the fact that some of the documents used were translated by him.  He's also incredibly helpful and caring; he will meet with you if you're busy during his office hours.
The prof is HOT, fun, and funny...what else do you want from a class that you're taking to fulfill distribution requirements? Remember gals: eye candy.
Thought 2nd grade multiplication tables were easy? You haven't seen nothing yet. This class will blow your mind. If you don't get an A, you probably should be going to Ithaca College.

Incredibly passionate about ancient Chinese military texts, and can make even a dull reading come to life. Funny, liberal, and an easy grader. That said, not one of the most brilliant minds in the department, and at times you will wonder if the class is worth your time. Great prof if you need distribution requirements; for substance, go elsewhere.
His "Art of War" class is just pure AMAZING...he is a very energetic professor and makes you love the material as much as he does. I absolutely recommend taking the class!!!
I agree that he spends too time on the bronze age.  So he has to rush at the end.   This may because of the reasons why the later part of the course is boring compared to the first half.
Great class, my favorite professor in all my time at Cornell, geniunely interested in the subject, and speaks fluent Mandarin!

Pretty easy class... prof is clear but as he is specialist on bronze age, i think he dwells too much on that period then rushes through the class and then makes the final based on the rushed through portion. That being said, his lectures are clear and he is a nice guy.
Great professor, and very nice guy. Very knowledgable in his field. If you live in Dickson, get to know him, he's your FIR!

Terrible guy. Went to him for help on suggesting academic programs but was replied that my grades suck and thus it would be impossible for me pursue any further study. Is this really what a professor should say? Can't believe such  a man could secure a place at Cornell!!

THE worst lecturer I have ever encountered, which is bad because he tests on them. Slides are unorganized and almost incomprehensible. Uses words and terms unknown to mortal men. TAs even acknowledge that lectures are horrible. Do the reading and go to section and you can get a B. He tests on terms used in lecture, which again, no one understands.

The lectures make almost no sense - even the TAs recognize that. That said, the material is very interesting, and you should be fine if you just do the readings and contribute in sections. You don't really need to understand the lectures that well to do well in the course (although you definitely should try to make sense of them before exams).

Worst teacher I've ever had.I'm not angry about my grade, b/c I did relatively well, but I'm pissed about the class in general--too much reading for a 100 level class, and his lectures are impossible to follow because they are boring and because he has a tendency to ramble and use words and terms that no one understands. DONT TAKE THIS COURSE.
His lectures are incredibly boring, very confusing, and he is completely oblivious to this fact.
Love him! I thought he was a great lecturer and seems to know a lot.

DON'T TAKE unless you have to. awful lectures. He is almost impossible to follow, doesn't know how to use lecture slides. His slides and lectures don't flow at all. He is unorganized, all over the place, and the worst lecturer I've ever had. Readings are interesting though, the subject is interesting, his delivery leaves something to be desired.
Unclear and inserts political bias into every lecture.

DON'T TAKE! Worst prof I've ever had. He tries to act like he's brilliant by making up words. TA's don't speak English. He won't let you choose your TA or switch TA's if you can't understand. He also forces his political views on his students, no opposing ideas or debate. He has no interest in anything that doesn't come from his mouth. PRETENTIOUS
Uses the lecture stage to impose his own beliefs on his students. Books contain no opposing viewpoints.
The dude looks like Santa claus and throws out big words when lecturing- 'nuff said

Don't take don't take. Besides being really pedantic and loving to hear himself talk, Herring doesn't make clear what he's looking for in the exams or on the essay. I went to every lecture, studied, and read and still have no idea what he talked about all semester. Take other intro govt classes instead.
I LOVE THIS MAN!!!!!!!!

Prof. Herring is a pretty chill guy. He likes to use a pretty expansive vocabulary when lecturing and they can sometimes be a bit dry, but if you have any interest in politics and government, you should take this class.Its a lot of reading but thats about it besides one big paper and a midterm&final
Very complex topics but Ron truly wants to see everyone succeed. He always makes an effort to get to know students on a more personal level.

Drugs & the Brain is the hardest and best neuro class I've taken (and I've taken a lot). Between the structure of the course, incredible lectures, and challenging assignments, I learned so so much about neuroscience in this course - more than I have in all my other upper level neuro classes. great lecturer and genuinely cares about his students!
Very engaging lectures and Ron is a super nice guy. Genuinely wants to see all his students succeed and shows everyone tons of respect.

Harder and more involved than bionb 2220 but an excellent introduction to neuropharmacology! The material on the exams comes straight from lecture although they do require a bit of studying. The assignments and final paper are great and provide a deeper understanding of the material. One of the best classes at Cornell, but not nearly the hardest.

The class is fantastic and Dr. Harris-Warrick is an incredible professor. He is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter, well-organized in his lectures, and always willing to help. Would recommend this class to anyone willing to put in the work.

intelligible and amiable prof.  Very approachable and willing to help his students. Heavily tests out of lecture AND text.  READ, KNOW, UNDERSTAND both.  I had to work hard in this class, but I really enjoyed the neuroscience behind it.  You'll work hard to do well, but it was a fulfilling class!  Go to his office hours before the exams.
Awesome professor.  The best professor I will ever have been taught by and the best class that I will probably ever take.  Everything was so well organized, so clear. He's also a genius.

The material was really interesting. Its a team-taught course, so each prof. teaches what interests him. H-W's drugs lectures were fascinating and very organized, which made it easier to study. Exams were still trickyyy. Tested in great detail, considering the large amount of material. Booker was my favorite lecturer. He is the best.
fun course/professor(s) but very bad grading system. would not recommend.

Very bad class to take for those premeds maintaining good GPAs. Course is structured around a few professors who lecture on different topics. Considering this is an Intro Neurobio course, there is just waay too much information presented. The exams are not only tough (a,b,c,a+b,b+c,all of the above) but curved to a B-!!! interesting but not worthit
Talks fast, gives a lot of information in lecture and yes, you need to know every detail, but very interesting. Partly took the class because he was one of my favorites from BioNB222.
The tests are difficult, especially if you don't have a biochem background, but the subject matter is interesting and he's a good lecturer (better than Nowak, who teaches half the course).
Harris-Warrick is amazing as anything! One of the BEST professors at Cornell!!!
No Comments
whoa...celebrity?
Professor Harris-Warrick is really funny, especially in the drugs lecture. His lecture notes are amazingly useful. Very clear and organized. And he definately knows a loooot!
Ronald is a great teacher. Despite the fact the class is pass/fail, he gives students a lot of attention and wants them to both pass and understand the content. He also gives great life advice.
Excellent professor that gives fun and engaging lectures on C++. Very funny, tells great stories, and gives a level of attention to students that is uncommon in an S/U class. "Never say never!"

Fine professor, but I disagree with the way he taught C++ this year. He attempted to teach the 2003 version of the language first, which caused many issues with modern windows computers. His lectures aren't engaging, but the slides are accessible online and helpful for homework. Weekly assignments were unegaging and sometimes frustrating.

I forget I took this class sometimes. He's a nice dude but I think he was filling in for the previous prof who apparently made the class super fun. Dinapoli kind of just read through the slides and I kind of just had to figure out how to do the assignments on my own bc lectures felt pointless to me. Better ways to learn UNIX but nothing against him

He expects you to read his mind on assignments: doesn't give specific instructions and penalizes students heavily for not following implied instructions. He clearly cares more about his other job than he cares about teaching.
Fantastic class. Concisely hits the key features of C++. Gives just enough technical context to appreciate how the language works, without getting inundated by superfluous detail.
Very practical class.  Teaches C++ in a clear, concise fashion. Generally helpful, and a bit eccentric.
An extremely knowledgeable and respected professor

a really incredible person. the tests are very fair and he is always willing to meet with any student. a truly good person to meet at cornell and a person guided by values and compassion for his students. take this class.

Amazing professor who really understands and knows the field. He is very passionate about the subject. Only graded by two exams and a analytical group research paper (usually combining economics and statistics). Read his book-its very helpful and the past exams are usually what he asks on the test.

Professor Ehrenberg was the best professor I have had at Cornell. I am so thankful that I took his class and wish I could take it again before I graduate! He is generally an amazing professor and I recommend that all students have the opportunity to take his class before graduating. He genuinely cares about his students. You're the best RGE!

RGE is a professor you won't appreciate until the very last day of classes. But he truly is an inspiration, a renown economist, and you will learn a ton from his class. He's also very fair - take his paper seriously, use the practice midterm/finals to study from, read Tuition Rising, pay attention in lecture and you'll be fine. He's genuinely nice.
Extremely caring and helpful. Really makes you think about controversial issues and encourages you to form your own opinion. Ehrenberg is the best!
willing to work with students who care

Wonderful professor. Clearly not trying to overburden students with work or destroy any GPAs, just wants us to understand the complexity of university decision making. Attend lecture, pay attention, read Tuition Rising, practice with last years' tests, and go see him in office hours.
Very interesting professor and class. I disagree with commenter who said he is full of himself; while he does boast it is very tongue in cheek.

Ehrenberg is awesome. You have to go well out of your way, more so than with other profs, to get him to notice you... but if you do it's well worth it. He's opinionated, and it's awesome, especially since ILR seems to only hire bleak, boring people who have nothing worth saying anymore. Ehrenberg is the best thing to happen to ILR
Good Class!
I dont know too much about the content, and that stuff... but two words...Stud Muffin.  Every day in this class was like a vacation of my senses.
Good class.

He's a great professor and lectures are very interesting. This class is perfect for economics students who want to listen to fun stories and write essays instead of solving math problems. Attendance is not mandatory, but you won't be bored if you go. Make sure you understand the practice prelim and you'll be fine for the real exam!

Great class. Great professor. He's so funny and amusing. Subject matter is definitely interesting, too. For the economics major, it is definitely a class to be taken if you want a break from all the math and tough grading.
Very interesting guy, good at telling stories, funny and nice but kind of full of himself (in an endearing way though...).  Good class.
No Comments

i had a great time and learned a lot. a very lighthearted but in-depth approach. was nervous about taking a course based on the prof's own book (those can be bad, when the prof just basically reads verbatim -- why go to class!??), but this was well worth it. had a good time with my end-of-term project too.
Very nice and helpful. Exams are a joke and he's very very easygoing. take 240 with him for an easy time

Ehrenberg cares SO MUCH about his students.  He is a very personable, endearing professor who has a passion for what he teaches.  His Econ of the University class is very interesting, great class, and good if you don't want too much work.
No Comments
really interesting, great and easy class (good excuse for a 300-level econ).
coolest prof at cornell... without a doubt
I have never met a man this intelligent or this skilled in his teaching abilities.  A few more like him and this university would be top five.

Not enough space here to describe how horribly unorganized this professor is. Its like they poured researched gathered online and put it on random powerpoint presentations that were full of errors and messy. No clarity or explanations on assignments, very dry course teaching, no interactive experience on such an importance study of a course. Awful

I took a course with Prof. Mize at Oregon State University and the course organization was a disaster from day one, he gave almost no instructions on how to participate in the class discussion board, and then graded rather harshly. A majority of the class had their grades fall in week 3.  Doesn't answer emails on time or at all, do not recommend.

He really knows what he is talking about. Though he is very distractable and goes off on tangents sometimes, he is always entertaining, and will get the class laughing at/with him at least once per class. The reading is heavy, and necessar. You can choose to make this a hard or easy course depending on how much real thought you put into it.

The best teacher I've had at CU. He made lectures interesting and engaging. I couldn't ask for a better lecturer. It's a bit reading intensive (~150pgs/wk) but worth it!!! Take his classes. He's even got a fanclub on facebook!

The class is so easy its embarassing. The prof, though, really shouldn't be at Cornell. I have little problem with a liberal bias but he has no basis for half of his conjectures it's really a disgrace. The textbook is so jaded it's indescribable. And he has no insights at all, just jabs at anything conservative. Class's easier than h. school though

He used statistics, history, & a few specific case studies to describe the communities, but never went deeper than that. No analysis, no insights, almost nothing about culture. Just when I thought it was going somewhere, he would move on to a different ethnic group. Bland, superficial, uninteresting. Not bad, just not good.
Excellent Professor! Great teaching style and definitely knows how to make the material interesting. LOVE HIM!
Very interesting professor.  Topics of discussion were extremely interesting.  He's a fair grader and more than willing to assist any student when in need.  Take his courses.

Covered a broad range of topics concerning an incredibly broad range of racial and ethnic groups. He assigns a lot of readings but it's all really interesting. He really challenges you to introduce new thoughts. Extremely fair grader. AMAZING professor. Take any one of his classes.
Tough grader but not impossible. Attend lectures, go to discussion, you'll be fine. Essays aren't that bad, do the readings

Prof. Kline is very engaged with his material. Although the material itself is not always very exciting, he presents clear arguments about everything he is teaching, and thus makes the content more interesting and applicable.

Prof Kline keeps the potentially boring subject of technological history interesting by focusing upon the use/human-driven perspective of history rather than the much overused technologically driven view of history.  A short writing assignment is due every friday and the majority of your grade consists of 3 papers.
Great

I love prof. Kline- he's a cute old man, esp when his hair is messy. He makes the history very interesting- showing all perspectives, including politics with no bias at all. Very, very interesting readings, and papers were actually sort of enjoyable to write. Grades fairly for sure- do a good job, get your facts straight and you'll get a good grade

Made the subject matter very interesting, surprisingly enough. Is obviously expert in his field and is eager to help anyone who shows interest. Very professional and a real gentleman. This is a great history course for anyone, engineer or not.
Excellent prof, cares very much about his students.  Go to office hours, take advantage of all Prof. Kline has to offer.  You will take a lot away from his class - well worth your efforts.
A genuinely good guy.
Interesting lectures.  Consisted of 3 essays and a final paper.
_Very_ well organized, you know exactly what he's going to be talking about throughout the course of the lecture.  Made an effort to make issues in the History of Technology not boring.

pretty fair grader, people got through the class with B+/A- without doing the readings. really nice man.  tries to crack jokes.  very accessable. says the words "essentially" "striking" and "emphasize" a lot.  a really great teacher
Easily the worst professor I've had at Cornell.
Boring. Hard to listen to.

I don't recommend him or any of his classes. His lectures are very disorganized and unclear. He himself is also very disorganized and unhelpful. He barely knows his material and spends most of the time trying to crack jokes and seem cool. He can be very offending to students at times. Long story short, try your best to avoid this guy!

Professor Booker's teaching style is more annoying than helpful...his tactics to make students pay attention in class ultimately led to distraction. He knows what he's talking about, just doesn't convey it well. The material is pretty straightforward, but the test questions are not very well written.
He stresses what he thinks are important. He words questions so poorly on exams. He shouldn't teach. Pretty much the worst professor I ever had in my life.
He claims that he's a biologist but he doesn't know his material at all. How is he a professor? Students know more about biology than he does. It's a shame that Cornell has a professor like him.
He doesn't even seem to know his material. He's so focused on trying to keep students awake and making jokes that it's distracting. One of the most annoying professors.

Booker made learning fun and entertaining. He was helpful during office hours, and the students who went to OH regularly did better in his class. Just make sure to understand the concepts and review until you do. Ask about stuff you find confusing and you’ll remember it better. Questions will ask indirectly about the material.

He is a great professor who really cares about his students and tries hard to let you LEARN and think. I went to his office hours every week and he makes sure you don't leave his office confused. You do have to put in the effort too, however. He curves the class nicely, and wants people to do well. Tests are fair: work in=work out.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS MAN. Everyone who went to office hours for help left crying. He would attack kids for no reason and was extremely unapproachable and not helpful. He likes to say that he and his daughter worked so much harder than all of us in college. he curved the class to a B-

Cannot keep his focus. He values showing off more than actual teaching. Never gives you a straight answer to without arrogant, useless, and irrelevant sophistry. Took another of his class too, it was the same thing. Arrogance coupled with the inability to keep his mind on a topic consistently for 5 minutes. A peasized brain not suited for the job.

Booker's inability to give a lecture without trying to be "cool" is as irritating as his inability to draft comprehensible exam questions. Prelims are not about understanding material, but about trying to ascertain what he's attempting to ask in his misguided and poorly-worded questions. In office hours he is condescending without needing to be.

Knows his material and is obviously knowledgable, but he seems moronic sometimes (he makes mistakes during lectures and gets confused, gets angry at students who simply do not understand, and makes multiple grading errors). But he DOES care about students, and is very helpful about course advice and the like. Not bad.
Worst professor ever. ruins your gpa. never take his classes.

His subject material is a lot tougher than Seely's for this class but he seems to do a reasonable job of presenting it.  He comes across as a little brusque sometimes but I think it's all in fun.  He's pretty funny sometimes.

Uses a textbook that is designed for upperclassmen and grad students, which is extremely dense. His lectures seem okay, but you have to read the textbook in order to actually understand the material at the depth he wants and do well on his exams. Extremely difficult class that is way more work than an introductory class should be.

He cares more about finishing his lecture than presenting it in an understandable manner. So the material becomes confusing and he's not very approachable for help. Almost as if he doesn't care about the students.
As a lecturer, he's sort of confusing and has SO MANY typos in his powerpoints. He's funny and all, but I had to read the textbook to get clarification. He doesn't really respond to e-mails either.
Not always present, doesn't give useful information always, really only knows his developmental stuff. Doesn't respond to emails.
No Comments

Considering I had Professor Chen for his first time lecturing CHEM 2090, I think he did reasonably well. His lectures got better over the course, and often were relevant for exams so I don't recommend skipping them. Note that because the chem department reuses exams, he doesn't release the answer keys for prelims. Make sure you go to office hours!

This class was alright for the most part. The only reason this class doesn't deserve a 5 is that the professor did not provide any practice material. The content covered on the prelim and final were rather reasonable and can be studied for with just materials you find online.

The exams often go further than what was covered in lecture. There was also a lack of practice exams, meaning that we were completely in the dark as to the format of the questions. The notes were also not posted on canvas.

Honestly not as bad as many people say he is - the lectures are fascinating, and he's very by the book in terms of teaching the content - often following it closely. Unlike previous semesters, he interweaves his research focus, but in a way that is interesting and not heavily focused on(test-wise). Review sessions are a must attend

Lectures seemed pretty irrelevant, Dr. Chen didn't give a lot of information about actual labs. Quizzes were okay but pretty random; office hours were also unhelpful.
