I suggest taking the class because it is Easy to do well but the teacher is such an a-h0le so don't expect to like him. Rude emails and no leniency. 50% of the class should be an automatic 100% though because of the weekly assignments.

Pretty poor teacher. His lectures are a real snore and you often end up just having to self-study in the end. Prelims vary a lot in difficulty. Without AP Stats already under my belt, there is no way I would have gotten the grade I did.

Honestly, the class itself wasn't hard but the lectures are unbearable. He tries to be funny and engage with the class but it honestly isn't that great. I didn't feel like I learned a lot in the lectures but more so in the discussions which attendance is mandatory. but whether the discussion is good or not really depends on your TA so goodluck.

Entner's teaching style sucks. The videos he posts are way better. Lab and exam questions are not clear and sometimes make no sense. No curve at all, I literally had an 89.99% and still didn't get an A-. Learning R is fun if you have a good TA and you can take the lecture quizzes as many times as you need to get a 100% before they close.

Very bad at teaching, give ambiguous exam questions and instructions, is mostly condescending, never reply emails, and seems annoyed when students ask him questions (sometimes judgemental). if not like teaching why become an instructor??? just avoid him

My second semester with Entner and he's sure one of a kind. It's hard to do poorly and isn't too much work and you learn an ok amount, particularly using R and regression, but it's always typos or questions on labs or exams that are very ambiguous. The open notes tests and recorded lectures are what make Entner and the course bearable.

Nice guy but you need to watch the videos in addition to lecture. Course material is extremely bland, but Entner tries his best and  any other professor would get 1/5 reviews. Biggest complaint is zero curve at all.
He is ok. His tests will have things you could never have expected or planned to study for. He will not round your grade at all.

Not the "easy A" class everyone says it is. Concepts are explained poorly/confusingly. Can use a cheat sheet on exams, but only basic calculators allowed despite stat software used in section. Easy to get full section/quiz points, making up 50% of grade. But to do well on other 50% (exams), expect to teach yourself. I barely made the A threshold.

Professor Entner was pretty good in lectures but material was simply enough to be learned outside of class as well. Tests were pretty reasonable as you are allowed a cheat-sheet and other assignments helped boost overall grade. Would highly recommend class, especially for non-stem majors as material is not too complicated.

Good lecturer and a funny guy. Made a very foreign concept interesting/enjoyable through his unconventional sense of humor (he can be out of pocket). Tests are not very hard (cheat sheet allowed). Only work was textbook readings, weekly quizzes (unlimited attempts), and section activities (time limit). Overall, great experience and a good class!
Don't make the same mistake I made.

This guy is the worst. Actually the worst class Ive ever taken at cornell. He teaches NOTHING, seems like he knows nothing either. His tests have the WORST formats, and everything he does is so extra and not helpful. Never replied to ANY emails that are sent to him over the semester. All around USELESS. 0/10.

3010 was an unpleasant experience. Jeremy is not an engaging lecturer, and most people did not attend them. There is no textbook, and the class relies on a notes document Jeremy provides. The tests could be annoying and tricky but were open note, which I appreciated. Late assignments are not accepted and Jeremy would be condescending about it.

He seems like a nice guy,  but he is a TERRIBLE teacher. The discussions are led by other students who don't know what is going on. All the tests are on things barely mentioned in class. He literally is useless, there is no way to contact him, no guide to what is on the exams, and literally no access to any forms of help or practice for this class.
open note tests. that says it all.

Ok so most people dislike him but he's really not that bad. Tests are open note for 3010 and only count for 50% of your grade. Now his test questions are a bit weird but if you pay any amount of attention to the lectures you can figure out how to do them with the notes. This is the major complaint most people have.
He's ok.

His lectures were kind of useless, but I found him to be quite funny. He always wears this backwards camera wherever he goes. I did everything in my dorm (read through the Google slides myself), never went to class etc and still got an A.
skipped the lecture because they were long and boring and didn't want to hear his lame joke. lecture vids posted were lifesavers

Best, easiest college class ever. The material was basic, the tests were exactly like the questions done in discussion section, and the grading scheme emphasized homework, quizzes, and discussions as much as exams. It's totally possible to skip class and still get an A (unfortunately doesn't give A+). He's a quirky guy but I found it entertaining.
Tests are fair if you just listen to the lectures, and he uploads everything online. Multiple attempts allowed for quizzes to get a good grade.

Definitely the least engaging professor I've every had, which explains why 80% of the class didn't attend his lectures. He never replies to emails and his lectures were pretty painful to sit through. I appreciated his leniency with weekly quizzes, but he worded tests so badly that many students without a stats background were destined to fail.

I took his 3010 and 3020. lectures are kind of dry and there are so many trivial details of stat models / R code that you must pay attention to later in 3020. He uploads all lecture videos to Canvas, but his lectures are generally better (at least 60% students never go to lectures). His OH is helpful and he answers individual questions pretty well.

I took STSCI 2100 this semmester and I absolutely hated it. I had taken a previous into to stats college class that I got a 100 average in and while the homework and discussions were easy. He doesn't word the test well. He is never responsive to emails and the ta I had didn't know anything.

Sometimes students can be a little hyperbolic when they say "oh my god, this professor is the worst." Jeremy Entner lives up to the hype. He is easily the worst teacher I have ever had. Like, in my entire academic history from preschool to college. I would choose my daycare teacher from when I was 3 over Jeremy Enter to teach me statistics. Awful.

Professor Entner does his best to make the lectures fun and enjoyable. Despite it being a 4-credit course, the work was lighter than any other course that I've taken. Lectures weren't mandatory, and he recorded videos for the people who didn't want to show up to the lectures. Definitely take Professor Entner's class for intro stats!

Lectures were extremely dry to the point that they made me hate the content that was being covered and really made me not want to become a stats major. There is no extra credit which is terrible because the class isn't curved and the median is low. The workload is fine but there are no practice prelims or a textbook to get help from.

Entner is one of the more down to earth and funny professors I have had. Always cracks jokes and really tries not to overcomplicate lectures and exams. One wrinkle is that the discussion sections mainly use software not available on the exams, leading to exams that students have not been adequately prepared for. Overall kind and willing to help.
Stats prelims are worded oddly. He makes basic concepts (ie graphs/ p value) more difficult by poorly explaining them. You might be better off in Bio stats.
Just cannot understand him for some reason. I have taken stats class with another prof and found it interesting; however, he pushed me away from learning more stats.

The class was super easy, even with no stats or R background. Lectures got pretty boring and some of the exam questions were a little mysterious, but labs, homework, and quizzes were essentially a guaranteed 100 as long as you put in a tiny bit of effort.

This class was not that hard if you have stats experience and the labs on R were very helpful. The only issues with this prof are that some of the questions on his tests are unclear and he is sometimes mean to students in lecture. He does give extra credit and is generally responsive. This class is easy enough that you can get by just with your TA.
Lectures are useless and irrelevant to exams.
Lecture and lecture quizzes pretty much irrelevant to exam.

Stats and R both aren't my thing but Jeremy made them both pretty easy to understand as a non-math person. All content is covered in lecture, and he makes it easy to take good notes. The class overall is pretty light, not a ton of work.

This class is not too conceptually challenging, but it does take up a lot of time. First of all, don't even think about skipping lecture, since everything covered will come up later. Aside from that, the weekly labs have a lot of questions, and are also ambiguously worded to the point that many people need clarification in office hours.

Haha 89.68, what do you want? No curve, no extra credit, you know how much time I have spent on the course? Every weekend, I slept at 3 to finish the lab. Ended up with a B+ but I got A+ on my last stats class.

He is the type of guy who does not round up 89.5 to 90 in the final grade. His exam is also weirdly worded. It was very confusing when you cannot understand what he is trying to test in his exam. Trust me: AVOID him anyway.
Don't get close to statistic here or you will be miserable
very entitled and arrogant person. strange because of how incompetent he is.
Jeremy, why are your tests like this? The wording makes the test more about solving a lexicon puzzle instead of the actual content.

The class is not difficult if you go to lecture and lab. Stats isn't really my thing so I didn't find the material very engaging, but if you keep up with the workload you will get a good grade. The professor gives extra credit if the prelim medians aren't where he wants them to be, and you can tell he wants students to succeed in this class.

Jeremy is, well, goofy. He has this interesting wit that I truly thought was funny. However, his tests were literally out of left field; they were much harder than class material. His explanation of R is a joke. Does give extra credit. ILR stats way less work and easier, take that instead if you can.

The class content was not difficult, however, grading was biased and arbitrary. His exam q's felt like they were testing your understanding of his psyche rather than the material. His behavior in lecture was also immature. He constantly made people uncomfortable by calling students out and mocking them, even for things like going to the bathroom.

Jeremy, oh Jeremy, what a man. While he was a really quirky teacher, and some people didn't like that, he truly knew his stuff when it came to statistics. The class was relatively easy and enjoyable, with little homework, but his tests weren't a good reflection of that we were learning. Notes were helpful, and was always responsive, ready to help!

Lecture feels more like bad stand up than actual class. Not extremely enjoyable and the prof uses strange analogies instead of actually explaining why things work the way they do. Clicker quizzes aren't hard. There is no curve but the grading is somewhat generous.
Very engaging teaching style. Gave extra credit and wanted students to succeed.

Jeremy is one of the rudest, least professional professors I have ever had. Not only is his teaching style odd, distracting and unprofessional, he seems to hate students who bring up anything to do with grades. His tests are also extremely irrelevant to actually using statistics - they are more like decoding double negative T/F questions

Very rude. You learn very little. He doesn't explain most things well. Instead of learning why statistics work, you plug numbers into the equations from your notes that he lets you use on everything. Assumes everyone is lazy. I missed one lecture and went to office hours, and he shamed me about how I would've known the material if I went to lecture
His lectures are awkward, and he is always picking on students. Beware of sitting in the front. He spends more time trying to be an awkward SNL character than a nice prof. He is also super rude.
We read really great things, workload was totally manageable, Professor clearly cared about students + course

Definitely one of the better FWS, IF you enjoyed HS English class. Normally great discussions and essays are very open-ended. Always accessible and very caring, especially during a tumultuous semester. You get what you put in. Recommend for the student willing try and improve; he rewards effort, not content. Not an easy grade, but worth it.

I definitely had to put in the work for this professor but he was amazing! He pushed my abilities as a reader and always expected the best from our class, which was a pretty intelligent group to begin with. This class is definitely more work than those grad taught FWS courses but you will actually learn about writing and reading with Braddock.

The Cold War class wasn't very cohesive, but it was all very interesting and Braddock is a great discussion leader. I always felt like I was learning a lot about the texts and he brought interesting perspectives. He is also clearly very excited about what he teaches, and I found him to be a fair and thorough grader.

Probably one the nicest profs I have ever met. He leads great discussions in class, and you can tell he loves teaching and what he teaches. Kind of all over the place sometimes, but you will really learn a lot about the texts.
He is kind-hearted and helpful. What is wrong with all these reviewers who do not appreciate an intelligent and peaceful approach? Discussion is set up to learn from him, the texts, and each other.

Great discussion leader. He makes smart comments.  As for  racial diversity being odd, it's an American literature class.  Cultural diversity is important in understanding the different perspectives of American life.  The purpose of a class like this is to introduce people to different viewpoints that white ivy leaguers wouldn't normally read.

He comments on what literally each person says in class. So people wouldn't argue with one another they would just talk at him. So our discussions just never really went anywhere. It also seemed like he had tried super hard to include authors from lots of different races. This wasn't a racial studies class, so it seemed odd.
Tends to ramble/stutter, involved the class in discussion way too much for a survey course/big lecture, but in general helpful and made some good points/interesting assignments. easy grader!

The class content, separate from the class, is super interesting. Prof Wallace is an unmistakably kind man who cares about his work/research/field. Yet, lectures tend to be ramble-heavy: there are no clear words on slides so it is hard to take accurate notes that prepare you for exams.  He is also super disorganized with grading.

Fun and kind professor, but 0 text slides means you have to attend lectures and pay attention, other than that it is pretty easy to succeed in the class. Participate and get to know your TA well enough. Fun class and very good education for those who care about climate change.

Really liked him. He's nice and you can tell he cares. A ton of assigned reading but TA will help you figure out what is necessary to know. Lecture attendance not mandatory but I always went and think it helped. Gives terms and example questions ahead of midterm and final. I def got deflated from an A to an A- but recommend, would take again.

I took Prof Wallace for GOVT2294 and he was super down to earth and funny. At times, his lectures were a bit disorganized but thats also because this was his first time teaching that class. He was generous with the assignments and setups of the exams. There were a good amount of readings- a lot were difficult to understand while skimming.
Prof Wallace is relatively new from Ohio or something. Super understanding, very interesting class, nice and funny guy. Would definitely recommend for anyone remotely interested in what he teaches.

Best class I ever took at Cornell. Tests are exactly what you study. The more you study, the higher your grade. No ridiculous amount of studying required, but you'll still need to study. Lectures are full of pictures and cool videos of animal behavior, & are really enjoyable. Jeremy Searle is a super nice and caring British guy. Everybody loves him

Jeremy was great and I loved his shrew jokes and ofc his accent. 1780 is unique with its active learning approach, so there are a lot of in class activities within groups and small grading assignments throughout the year, putting less pressure on prelims. Class was basically memorization. You put in the work and memorize it you get an A.

This course is quite easy for a biology course at Cornell. Prof. Searle is incredibly helpful and nice if you ever go to his office hours. The class has many guest lecturers throughout, which keeps things interesting. The course has iClicker questions for each lecture that affect your grade. Great course, great professor!
By far my favorite professor at Cornell. This class was much easier than domestic but still a challenge. Would recommend him to anyone!!!!

Dr. Allen is awesome! He loves his students and works to see you succeed. Its a very big course with lots of content. Sometimes content is skimmed and prelims can be very difficult, but he makes the class fun

Super funny and great professor, really understanding and loves to get to know his students. This is a super hard class because of how much content there is, but it is doable. Stay on top of studying and go to TA's if you need help with figuring out how to study for this class. I didn't like TA exam grading and how lab was run though.
just take him. Literally my favorite, ever.

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors in the Animal Science department. His classes are difficult but not impossible - you just need to be able to put the work in. He is super personable and really cares for his students. I cannot recommend him enough!

Yes, the course is hard. But Dr. Allen makes it 100x better and much more manageable. If you try your best, he will work with you to help your succeed. He does do random attendance checks, so just beware of that. But overall, this is one of my most favorite classes I have ever taken and most of the reason why is because of Dr. Allen

Avian Management is an easy class compared to 1100 and 2400. He makes the prelims difficult but only because he wants you to study and learn the material instead of brushing the class aside. It was a fun class, and I learned a lot. There's no final but instead a group final project that makes the last month of the semester a little easier on you.

Cornell should pay him triple his salary. His back must hurt from carrying animal science. He's the Michael Jordan of talking about reproduction. If you didn't take BIOAP1100 this class will be really hard, but if you did it will be challenging but easier than domestic. People bring friends not in the class to lecture cause he's that good.

Dr. Allen is a great professor. He is very personable and is always there as someone to talk to if times get tough. Funny guy too; he makes a lot of inappropriate jokes but makes sure to not cross lines and will apologize if he does. Overall, tough course but I learned a lot. He makes sure your education at Cornell is rigorous. Prelims suck though.

Jeremy is the goat. If you disagree you are wrong. He genuinely cares about his students more than any other teacher I've ever had. The class is difficult, but he structures it so that everybody can succeed and offers so much support. He can offer you so much help inside and outside of the class; my Cornell experience is 10x better because of him.

Best professor at Cornell hands down. Hilarious guy, makes you feel so welcome your first year. I suggest any freshman taking Domestic their first semester to get to know him. He helps you so unbelievably much. Get as close as you can to him. Fantastic guy.
Dr.Allen was a top tier professor, I literally take any class I can with him.

It's not a difficult class if you keep up with it, and he's more than fair on every assignment. His exams are extensive, but he will prepare you for every single question. He's funny, but often toes the line. If you put in a little bit of effort to build a rapport with him, you'll find he's very helpful. A mainstay in the animal science department.

Dr. Allen is understanding and caring. You can talk to him about anything. Tests are reasonable for ansc2400 and bioap1100. He is also inspirational and hilarious, incorporating memes into lectures. His lectures are clear and his mode of instruction is among the best professor I've had in cornell. Fantastic professor!

Dr. Allen is a really wonderful professor. He is there to help students who are struggling whether it be with the class itself or with problems outside of class. In both the lecture and the lab he creates an environment conducive to learning and also makes an inclusive space, in and outside of the classroom. Expect to put work into the class.

Dr. Allen is very charismatic and a favorite in the animal science department, evidently. His lectures are engaging and he makes a real effort to foster a comfortable and relaxed classroom environment. His grading is a bit questionable, as he inflates individual assignments but then deflates the class as a whole. Otherwise he is highly recommended.

This man was by far the BEST professor I have ever had. His lighthearted attitude and amazing teaching abilities have allowed me to thrive in his class. He is always SO supportive and such an amazing person to talk to

Dr. Allen is one of the best professors I had in Animal Science. He is compassionate, enthusiastic and extremely reasonable. He wants to make class accessible to everyone and is truly enthusiastic about teaching and the subject matter. He is very open to communication and has a great sense of humor, but that doesn't make his class an easy A.
Dr. Allen is an incredible professor. His classes are engaging and entertaining, and you will learn a lot, however this isn't necessarily an easy class. You have to pay attention and stay engaged.

Absolutely the best professor at Cornell hands down. Cares about his students so much but won't just give you the credit, work hard and you will be rewarded. Most respectable and down to Earth guy you'll find teaching any class. Lectures are interesting and funny. Even people that never had him know of him and think he is amazing.
Hands down my favorite professor. He makes everything fun and engaging and will do his best to make sure that you do yours. The class is not easy, but the content is very clear.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Cornell so far. Besides his evident knowledge and passion for the material he teaches, he has a remarkable sense of humor that makes his class extremely engaging and fun. The nature of the course certainly requires lots of memorization so be ready to grind. On the bright side, Dr. A is extremely helpful

Dr. Allen is one of the nicest professors I have ever met. He truly cares about every one of his students. He makes lectures fun with jokes, memes, and stories. You definitely have to study hard to get a good grade, but he also gives out extra credit. He picks really good TAs that are also extremely helpful. I wish all my professors were like Dr. A

Dr. Allen is genuinely kind and understanding. In lectures, he takes time to thoroughly explain concepts while keeping students' attention during longer and complicated topics. He has a fantastic sense of humor but maintains respect. During office hours, he is receptive to all questions and willing to meet additionally for any reason if needed.
Dr. A is probably one of the nicest profs you'll have the luck to learn under at Cornell. He will listen to you, help whenever he can and honestly, do his darndest to make sure you don't flunk.

He's a nice guy with a great sense of humor, but don't let that fool you into believing that you can get away without studying. Prelims and quizzes require a huge amount of memorization to do well on, so try to avoid this class if you aren't ready to grind.

Dr. Allen is an amazing person who can teach very well, but expect to study very hard for this class -- lots of memorization needed. Really unavoidable as it is an ANSC requirement, if you are having trouble start meeting with him when the semester begins. He lets you retake your lowest test, and the final is usually multiple choice.

Dr. Allen is a great professor. Lectures are always organized and clear, and he is always very transparent about what material you need to know. Gives plenty of extra credit and is flexible with deadlines. He is very understanding of his students and just overall a very genuine person. Best ansci course I've taken at Cornell.
a jocular and knowledgeable professor. Never stop thinking for the students, exams are very fair as long as you study.

Hand down, this was the best class I have taken so far. He is hilarious and makes sure as long you do what you need to do he will help you pass. He cares about his students and offers many resources to make sure you understand the material before the test.

Professor Allen is the best professor I've had at Cornell thus far. He genuinely cares about his students, and it is clear that he truly wants us to learn and understand the material. His tests are never designed to be unfair or unnecessarily fastidious, but rather to fairly judge what we have learned so far. He is enthusiastic and compassionate.

Dr. Allen is by far my favorite professor at Cornell. Absolutely hilarious, makes learning really fun and easy. Course content is very manageable and exams are fair. Plenty of opportunities for extra credit. I'm going to miss this class a lot and wish I could take it again with him.
Dr. Allen is one of the best professors and individuals I've had the pleasure of receiving. He is absolutely hilarious and cares a lot about his students. I wish I could take his class over again!
Wonderful, informative class

Dr. Allen is a great person and professor. He cares about his students and gives engaging lectures. One of the best professors I've had, and repro is not my thing. He doesn't grade on a curve, but he's willing to give extra credit. If you go to class, he makes it pretty clear what kind of stuff will be on the exam, but he's a good lecturer anyway.

Dr. Allen is the best!! If you are a dairy student struggling through the ANSC required classes, don't worry he does a lot of lectures that tie into basic dairy knowledge with regard to repro. It is challenging, but only if you make it that way. Attend lecture, take notes by hand, go to review sessions, and ask questions!

I loved Dr. Allen!! He really cares about his students doing well. While he doesn't believe in curving, he gives many free points and always offers extra credit opportunities. He will always tell you exactly the topics you should study before prelims. He's hilarious and his stories related to the topic he's lecturing about are always so funny! :)
Dr. Allen is truly the best professor I've had at Cornell. The class isn't easy but the lectures are understandable and enjoyable. He's a wonderful person.

This class is very easy, 100% online. If you have good tools and are tech savvy you can easily do the assignments and exams very quickly. The classes consist of 6 short responses of 200-250 words and 6 Exams that are around 40 questions each. It's an easy class, its busy work and boring but its a very easy way to get your GEP 5 requirement.

Class is super doable and is very enjoyable. You have 1 listening journal and an exam every two weeks which are very simple (the study guides help if you do them as well!) He also sends out frequent reminders about the assignments and when they'll be graded by.

Robert Gennaro is a very nice, pleasant instructor who clearly loves music. He is always kind and respectful to us, which I appreciate after having a fair number of less kind and less pleasant instructors at UCF. He will send reminders about upcoming assignments/test but doesnt give extra credit and doesnt accept late work so dont screw around.
Took the class online and it was very doable. 1 assessment and 1 listening journal due every two weeks. Very caring professor, he also sent reminders to students about assignments every week!
I took it online. 1 listening journal and exam due every two weeks. Theres a lot of reading, but the coursework is very doable. Its an easy class if you put the effort!
A fairly easy class. As long as you read the textbook and listen to the music pieces youll be fine.

I liked taking this class. Super Easy A. All material is on Quizlet and it's the best way to study for exams. Every two weeks he has 2 exams and 1 journal. The journals are easy (online 150 words) and the exams are online, open book and open note. He opens and closes modules so you can't work ahead. He emails every week with due dates and reminders

Don't even waste your time contacting him because he's very blunt, but he also makes announcements every week that should answer all questions. Enrolled in this class now for the Fall semester online and its alright. Lots of reading, but overall everything is easy just stay on track. Assignments get opened weekly so no you can't work ahead :(

Simple GenEd class. One 50 ques quiz and one 25 ques quiz due every couple of weekends (not every wk). Just click CTRL and F to look for answers in the modules/ txtbk online, or find them on quizlet. also two paragraphs comparing two music ppl due every couple of wks, just copy and paste info written about them in modules. annoying but easy
MUL2010 online was the best decision of my semester. A great grade booster that also teaches you a lot. I'm a former band kid, but you really don't need a background in music for this class.

Would not recommend taking. Although he is very kind and there to answer your questions, the class is poorly set up. You are forced to teach everything to yourself and it's like learning a new language.

Unhelpful. The tests are really tough and he is not thorough in his emails when you ask a question. He expects that you have read the syllabus and it's supposed to have every answer to every question. If you ask a question, he will probably refer you to the syllabus instead of answering the question.

I was terrified to take this class because it is online and because of the reviews. However, don't be fooled. When it comes to online class professors, this man is as accessible as it gets. He sends emails almost weekly, keeps you updated, and has the most clear instructions possible. Easy stuff, easy to look up, great prof!
Dr. Gennaro was awesome! Wish I could take this class again

I signed up for this class in the hopes that the ratings would be accurate. Unfortunately I don't think Dr. Gennaro is grading his stuff anymore. I have had continuous contact with the TA but to no avail. I forgot to cite ONE sentence in a listening journal and she threatened to send me to student conduct. Not worth it for a 2000 level course.

Dr. Gennaro is a great guy. The thing is, I don't love rock music and I'm not too interested in it. You definitely have to be into rock music to dig this class. Tests were kinda hard, but manageable if you really study. He's a funny guy and likes to involve the class. He's also very informative on when tests and other things are due. Be prepared
The tests are literally the power points, he's easy on the eyes and very funny, your gonna enjoy the class.

If you're not a fan of rock music or old music you probably won't enjoy taking this class if you are however, like I was, you'll love this class. I learned so many cool facts and music I would've never known otherwise. As long as you study and know your stuff you'll be sure to pass.

Memorize the PowerPoints (even the "fun facts" bullet points.) For the listening guide, make sure you know all parts of the songs (esp. instrumental parts), who the song is by, instruments used, and the inspiration for the song. I realized this at the end and saved myself from having an F. Besides that though, I didn't like this professor.

Very nice guy! He's always there for students who need it and tries his best so that any student can pass his class. His lectures were pretty long, but he will crack a joke every now and then to keep us awake. There are 4 exams which make up your grade which are pretty tough. Everything comes from his PowerPoint so just study that and you can pass.

Great professor. I loved him but the class was only interesting towards the end. Majority of the class is spent learning about the music leading up to the rock era which is not very exciting. Don't think this class is an easy A. You will take a ton of notes and his tests aren't super easy either.

Dr. Gennaro is an entertaining lecturer. I had little interest for rock music history, but he made it interesting to me. Book is helpful but not necessary (still worth $30 for used copy if you can get it). He emphasizes important facts in lecture that are likely to be on multiple-choice tests, though somewhat unimportant facts do show up.

This class is an overview of the history of music starting with Gregorian chant and ending at today. He did an amazing job of keeping the lectures entertaining as well as resourceful. Most of the class is spent listening to music or taking notes from a PowerPoint. He expect exact word for word definitions on the test but if you study you will pass.

Really easy class. Took the class online during summer B. You go through 2-3 modules a week and then quizzed on them. 7 quizzes overall but he takes off one which you received the lowest grade on. Tells you to read the textbook but not necessary because all quiz material is on the modules.

YOU DO NOT NEED A TEXTBOOK! I got the textbook and didn't use it once. Survey of Rock is an easy A but it's also a very interesting class. There are 7 quizzes and Dr. Gennaro drops the lowest quiz grade. This is a perfect class to take during summer because it's online so you can still have your summer fun. I highly recommend taking this course.

He's a fun guy who really likes what he teaches and does.  You do not need to textbook, his tests are from the powerpoints and he does reviews before the tests which are really helpful.  Extra credit opportunity with a school concert.  It wasn't hard to receive an A

Don't get the book. The class was pretty boring until the last segment. The class is based on 4 tests and watching an extra credit performance. STUDY THE NOTES. He gives hints on what to study but he doesn't give the Power Points. You must go to class everyday for little info that will be on the test. I wouldn't take it again, but made it with anA

MY FAVORITE PROFESOR. He is hilarious and knows what he is talking about. Easy class and a guaranteed A if you go to class and look over notes before test. We did not get through all of the material and i was very disappointed. Loved the class and definitely recommend him as a teacher.

The class is relatively easy, but she's odd, to say the least. She yelled at the class for not trying hard enough on papers. She's an outspoken liberal (and I took her before Trump took office), so if you're not political or conservative it's not gonna be a fun class. I would avoid if you could.

Easy class if you already know how to write fairly well.  Great feedback and she will work with you to write better. Tells lots of weird stories about herself and how she believes in ghosts which took a lot of time away from class.

Honestly one of the most caring woman I have ever met. I was going through some difficult family circumstances during my time in her class and she was more than understanding. She definitely knows that she's talking about, I totally reccomend.
If you wanna talk about ghosts and crazy stuff, she's the one for you!

Good choice for a VAPA. Not hard, especially if you were in band/choir/orchestra in high school. Most of grade comes from one project with checkpoints and feedback along the way. All quizzes are open note and open book. The class was mostly asynchronous with panopto lectures. Interesting class and good profesor. I really enjoyed it.

Very accommodating when it came to turning in assignments. I emailed her a few times explaining my situation and she was always very receptive and extended my deadline. Tbh kinda a lot of work for a vapa, but was easy and interesting.

Middleton is so kind and understanding towards her students. Class structure was mostly asynchronous with a one hour live lecture (optional & recorded) and a weekly discussion (mandatory). Grades were fair and lenient, but there was a heavy share of busywork, online homework, and writing assignments. Final is in the form of a 6-8 min video project.

Professor Middleton is very lenient with deadlines and grades. She truly cares about her students and is so sweet. The workload and grades you get are somewhat dependent on what TA you get, but you shouldn't get an awful grade either way. Her online courses format is really easy and nice and allows for a lot of flexibility. Highly recommend!
I loved this Dr. Middleton and this class! She's such a caring and sweet professor. The class is very easy - just make sure to go to discussion. Definitely would recommend this for a VAPA!
Professor Middleton was absolutely wonderful - kind, caring about her students, and a fair grader. Very understanding and helpful, and accessible outside of class. Would take again anytime!

Class is basically can you listen to a recording and remember which piece it was from. Lectures just repeat the textbook and she sends the slides out, too. Test is 1/2 textbook info and 1/2 listening to recording, matching it with the piece, and answering some questions (all of the info you need is in textbook). Just memorize for easy A.

The suggested textbooks for this class were perfect for the material covered throughout the semester. She makes the course fun and interesting even though there were minimal field labs due to covid. She looks at things from an instructors perspective, as well as a students so that was a good quality to have while trying to pass the course.

Instructor Redmond is a great lab professor to have. She has most of the difficult problems from the lab write up prepared on the board and does a great job at explaining things for you if you need it. She is very approachable and is a good grader. Definitely remember to include units everywhere though! I would and did definitely take her Lab again

had her for my physics lab instructor and enjoyed it! the class itself is just you and a group working through a lab the entire time so there wasn't much lecture/teaching, but instructor redmond was always willing to answer questions and i felt like she always wanted us to do our best. gives feedback on labs when grading which was helpful as well.

Is very blunt. Try not to take it personal-she is not interested in changing for many who don't take this feedback well. Barely had any time with her, though we were supposed to have 12 hours a week together. Will teach you very little. Not a good model for advocacy.
She gave me a motive to study, literally. She is amazing. She does three times more works than her students do. Every single class was worth it.
charismatic, easy to follow, makes u wanna go to lecture, super passionate, simplifies complex concepts, explicitly says what he'd ask on a test
Very charismatic lecturer; made me excited to go to class
Amazing, passionate professor. Does a great job at explaining difficult concepts. I learned a lot from him. Also clear about what material will be tested on. Really enjoyed his lectures!!
Very good explanations and teaching

He goes through lectures so quickly and doesn't explain what's really important. The lab goes so slowly, and the questions in weekly homework ask for details that aren't intuitive. I basically just had to go to TAs every week to have them explain the answers to me.

Funny guy with a rich history in the field of molecular biology (he discovered the TATA box!). However, very disorganized and lectures can be very boring. At the end of the day, using CRISPR to edit a fly's genome is cool, even though the lectures are boring, which makes this class bearable.

Its been a year since I took the class (Fall 2014?) His lectures are clear but the questions that appear in quizzes and the tests are tough. This class requires 1) a lot of practicing   and 2) very creative approaches.  If you do all the problems, there is a chance that one of them would appear in the quizzes and/or tests.

It's a tough class, but his lectures are very clear and well organized. To succeed make sure you understand how to solve all the hard-looking problems in the back of the chapter. My favorite class at Cornell, and most useful for me :)

His lectures follow the textbook. Lectures are a bit dry but organized and clear. Go to lecture and problem solving sessions. This is a VERY hard and time-consuming class. Be ready for a lot of work for lab as well. Quizes are helpful to prepare for prelims.

This class is the worst class that I've taken thus far. The sad part is that this class actually has the potential to be great. However, the poor structure of the course and an overly difficult professor makes this class impossible to enjoy. Goldberg comes off as arrogant when you go to his office hours which doesn't help a struggling student.

This class is horrible. The work load is insane and almost impossible to keep up with.  The tests questions are convoluted and overly complex.  Worst class I have taken at cornell BY FAR.  It seems as though they want you to do poorly and destroy your confidence.  avoid this class at all costs.

This course is structured poorly and will discourage you, there is a never-ending flow of problem sets and readings, your questions require OH yet the TAs  have so little time fore you that questions go unanswered. Goldberg's exams and quizzes are impossible, and many quiz means are 3/20. He's awful at making fair tests and forgets we're undergrads

Not going to lie, thought this class would be easy b/c it's not 281.  Tests were actually fairly difficult.  You will have to work very hard to break the curve b/c almost everyone gets a B+ and kids who took 281 take 282.  Weekly assignments are annoying b/c you have to go to OH to get anything right.  Prof is sooo boring, but prepares you for mcat

This class was extremely interesting and due to the high level of detail that we are required to know the material, it makes the Genetics questions on the MCAT seem quite simple, which is good! Goldberg wasn't the most interesting lecturer, but he definitely knew his stuff, and while tests were hard, I would not say they were unfair, like orgo!

If 281 isn't required for your major, I would take this one instead: no fruit fly lab and I think the curve is much more forgiving. Tests are trickier than you'd think given how clear everything seems in class, but the curve is very generous. Somewhat dry but very clear lecturer and very helpful and friendly if you go to office hours. Good class!
sack of****
No Comments
Weird dude.
he is an average lecturer. not great, not terrible. pretty hard class

this class is hard work!  tests are challenging and material is much more science-based than discussion-based.  discussion groups are fun, but nero is obviously the one with the teaching skills (it's great when they fight.)
No Comments
by far the worst course i have ever taken.  even the takenotes didnt make sense.

I took his class many years ago and I remember him as the ABSOLUTE WORST Cornell Prof I ever had.  He is pompous, cannot effectively convey any of the concepts, and is entirely demeaning to his students.  The mean on his first exam was 24 (out of 100).

Goldberg, like many others in the Bio department, is conceited, self-centered, and pompous. He has no interest in helping his students succeed, but would rather demean them and discourage them because of his perception that they lack the necessary ability
think ben stein in farris buellers day off. but if you pay attention its useful stuff, though disconnected from the lab, not that anyone in their right mind would want to be connected to the lab
i actually loved this class, but Goldberg was terrible.
this class sucked and was very boring/not as easy as it was supposed to be
Since the class is supposed to be for non-majors, you would think it would be 'easy.'  It's not, and it's a lot more work than its worth.
From a guy who originally thought that Drosophila had 4 wings, he has no business making us suffer through the fly lab!
It's orgo, so of course it's really hard, but he does his best to make it manageable. He's also really available for help, and was really nice during the transition to the pandemic.

Prof. Fors is amazing! His lectures are clear, he's super enthusiastic during them and willing to answer questions, and his practice tests are really similar to the actual prelims. Definitely take him--he has a way of making difficult material seem easier and makes you feel important.

Prof Fors is easily the best prof I've ever had. Remembers your name. Easy if you study. Email him if u ever need anything but he'll randomly not answer to some emails. Extra credit is offered. He has rly good OH and offers 1-on-1 help. Exams are identical to the practice exams. Amazing lecturer and so clear.
Absolutely amazing experience, would take again!

I honestly struggle so much with chemistry and was dreading this class, but Prof. Fors is a gem! His enthusiasm for the material is contagious and honestly makes this class so much better than others. Though this class was probably the hardest chem class I've taken, it's probably the only chem class I'd take again. Bottom line- he's awesome!

You need this man in your life! He cares and loves Organic Chemistry and I am excited to take the class with him. The class is very hard and there are some tricky questions on the prelim that might not be taught in class but in the textbook. He's very understanding during the pandemic. Make sure you keep up with the material because there's a lot.

Professor Fors is AMAZING!!! Such a nice guy and he made CHEM 3580 a little more bearable. Material is challenging, but Professor Fors's exams are pretty fair, and homework grade helps slightly. Definitely need to attend lecture, or at least get good notes. Reading the textbook is helpful too.
Literally one of my fav professors in the chem department by far. He's caring and is always willing to help. The material isn't easy, but he made the class enjoyable.
Fors is a really nice professor, but won't take any bullsh*t. Both CHEM3570 (Ganem) and CHEM3580 are classes that if you miss lecture and don't have a friend's notes, you will fail.
Really nice guy

Professor Fors is a very nice person, and his pros and cons come through being nice. Pro: he is very patient with each question and each student Con: Because he is nice, he is often controlled by the crowd in lectures, problem-solving sessions, office hours, instead of the other way around.
I LOVE BRETT HE'S THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER <3

Although Fors just started teaching, nearly everyone loved him. His tests are fair, and the materials come directly from the notes. As long as you study, you will get what you deserve. However, he goes through a lot in each lecture so prepare to study ahead of time. He is a gem and will make organic chem actually enjoyable.

Professor Fors is AMAZING!! Best chemistry professor I've ever had. He truly cares so much about his students and really makes an effort to ensure we understand. He is very organized, and his lectures are easy to follow

Extremely kind and sympathetic; gets if the whole class is sleep deprived and dying of overwork. Material is really engaging and gives a more rigorous understanding of how to analyze visual media. Fair warning though, it's still incredibly hard to learn and write about for those without much prior study in philosophy, literature, or fine arts.
She is very accommodating, lenient and sweet. Always positive and really interested in her subject and incredibly knowledgeable.
The course is listed as a japanese history and culture course.  It would be nice if she would teach Japanese history and culture not literature analysis.
De Bary is a very sweet prof. with an incredible knowledge of Japanese History. The class is really easy, just make sure you attend lecture - that's where most of her quiz questions come from
Quizzes on almost every lecture. Papers aren't bad. I needed this class for my major and Ann was the only one teaching it. Not good, but not terrible either.
Fascinating topics; terrible professor. Ann has no patience, is often rude, and maintains a "too bad, I don't care" attitude.
Global Cities is not an accurate class title. Professor Forsyth only wanted to cover modern first-world cities and advanced design principles. This wasn't what I signed up for.

Prof. Forsyth is incapable of teaching. She is a great researcher, but sadly that's as far as she goes. In every single class, it seemed as if though she was convinced she was only lecturing to herself. Grades fall under an artificial curve established by her, but the TAs can be very helpful.

Ann would tell us in class that her door was always open. I went to office hours seeking her help and she was very rude. Ended up with a B+ in the class but I made it entirely on my own because she wouldn't be of any help.
Took two classes with her because I had not choice. She only cared about cashing her paycheck. A disgrace to higher education.
Lots of useless terminology and excessively long projects.

I'm a math major and decided to take this class out of pure interest. Mistake! Professor Forsyth would be very rude and confrontational in office hours and I stopped caring at that point. Not that hard to do well, just follow her syllabus and try to overlook her many typos.
Awesome class! Friendly professor. In class discussions and pin-ups are great. Not a class for an easy A but fair.

Intro to physical planning is definitely a good class to take if you want to get a job or internship. It is very skills-oriented. If you want to do one big project you need to do a workshop class but this course gives you skills to succeed in a workshop.
Not an easy class but useful for the major. Good lectures.
Good class. Pinups were really helpful. Classroom could have better furniture.
If you want to learn basic skills this is a good class. She has lots of office hours but doesn't take drop ins. Still, you can email her and she responds quickly.

Pretty hostile to students for the most part. Her grading scale is so weird, an A- is 88% and A+ is 94% but she makes it really hard to get any type of grade within the A range. She is ok but not a top-notch professor.

Ann is a great professor and a very interesting person. She clearly knows what she is talking about. I've taken two classes with her (global cities and intro to physical planning) and enjoyed both of them, particulary physical planning. She expects a lot from her students but gives a lot back in return. Sometimes she can seem a bit intense, but she is very approachable if you go to her office hours. Furthermore, she's a fair grader - she tells you upfront what she expects from each assignment.

Incredibly intelligent professor, who has unlimited experience in CRP. People will write that she is unapproachable and obnoxious, but it is my perception instead that she is simply introverted. Her shyness comes off as aloofness, which is common for reclusive people. Giver her a chance; just be forward and you can learn a lot from her.
Obnoxious! Treats you like you are not worth her time in office hours. She should be doing research in a locked office away from students.

Very knowledgeable about international issues, cares deeply about planning but can be intimidating and unapproachable  at times, opens up a bit in office hours if you talk to her enough. Tough but fair grader.
The type of self-absorbed instructor that has been around for too long. Freshmen: only take this class if you are URS major. Other comments are spot-on.

Awful experience with Prof. Forsythe and her TAs. She says she makes herself available and clearly explains her grading - she doesn't and is not understanding of student needs. Although knowledgeable, she floods the student with information without helping to synthesize it at all. She and the American City professor completely ruined CRP for me.

Has the potential to be a great class, but directions for assignments/projects are cryptic and when asked to clarify, her response is not helpful. TA's are also not very helpful and grading is very, very hard.
Fine professor if you are willing to commit to her class.
Very intimidating professor. Students n TAs are afraid of her for good reasons. Worst class I could have taken as a freshman.

What started as an easy elective quickly turned south. In almost every lecture, a quiz was given and no more than 5 minutes were offered to answer each quiz. Ended up getting a low final grade and Ann refused to talk about it. What bothers me is her mean attitude... she hates students and doesn't belong in a university.

Very knowledgeable in her field and clearly very intelligent. However, the class is very difficult and there is not much help out there. The TAs are useless and Forsythe is moody and very unapproachable; she brags about tons of office hours but she is impossible to interact with. Overall, interesting material, tough, tough, teacher and grading
Interesting and engaging
Probably one of the most intelligent professors out there. However, she is difficult to approach and can be quite moody. Global Cities was a great course.

I was afraid to take a workshop because they tend to be overwhelming in CRP. Ann did an outstanding job organizing this class. All throughout the semester, she gave great suggestions to improve our plan.
Excellent professor always willing to help

She can be a little disorganized at times but over all Ann and CRP 1101 is very focused and interesting. Ann is very interested in what she is teaching and she is very interested in communicating with students. Go to office hours! Great class.

Great Professor, great class, and extremely fair. The work load is extremely reasonable. He doesn't expect you to be an expert of Chinese Film, but he does expect you to watch the films, go to class, and have something intelligent to say. If you pay attention to what he says, you will find him to be extremely witty and intelligent.
Cool professor. His classes are always eye-openning. He is knowledgeable, nice, helpful, with refined manner and sometimes hidden humor. Highly recommended.

Swartz is a good professor in general. The class itself is quite easy; to do well in the class, all you have to do is read a couple textbook sections/do the homework once a week, and you can skip the lectures completely. The lectures themselves are a bit dry. The TA's for this class were fantastic - all knowledgeable grad students.
Great Proffesor!

The workload of this class is light. Prof. Swartz is rude and does not seem to care a for his students. His lectures followed a linear though process, but the writing on the board was small and disorganized. It seems, though, that he is one of the professors that I least interacted with since I would learn more the textbook than from his lectures.

Tests are 80% of grade (each prelim is 25%, final is 30%). Brilliant, funny guy, but writes small/messy on the board and talks quietly, so sometimes difficult to follow. Pretty boring too, hard to focus after 40 min. Exams are pretty difficult but doable with office hours and hw. TA's are really good and know what they're talking about.
Good professor with clear lectures and helpful Office Hours. If you didn't understand a concept he would always explain it multiple ways until you got it. I found his psets difficult though
great teacher

He is a fantastic and interesting lecturer, but his tests present a problem as they often test irrelevant and minute details.  However, it's a fairly easy A if you are willing to pay attention in lectures and read the book thoroughly.  Median grade is like a B.

professor was completley inaccesible and unhelpful. In response to a question regarding the final exam he replied in an email "see class notes where this was discussed four weeks in a row" He could easily have answered my question. Tests are not too difficult but they dont test your knowledge of the subject. Steer clear if its not required
Test should reinforce what is learned - not to see if you can READ THE PROFESSORS MIND! Terrible professor.

STUDY FOR THE EXAMS.  I completely underestimated the difficulty of the prelims, but thankfully he let us drop a prelim so I still did really well (after some serious studying). Read the textbook, take really good notes, and pay attention to guest lectures and you'll do well.  Lectures are fun (movie clips and ads), but the book is boring as hell

This class is a MUST TAKE if u are interested in taking a business course at CU. The lectures are not only clear and easy-to-digest,they are also VERY FUN and INTERESTING!Yes,the exams are DIFFICULT as they require minute details from the textbook+lectures+guest lectures but if u take time to read the text book and attend lectures,all will be fine!

Ed McL is one of the few professors at Cornell who is active in research and talented at teaching.  His tests are tricky and require you to know the material cold, but if you focus in class, read the book, and do the extra credit, you're golden.  Lectures presented lots of information but were fun, thanks to inclusion of funny ads and movie scenes.

McLaughlin is a good guy. He really does make Marketing interesting and fun. The classes are based 50% on lecture and 50% on the text so you have to make sure you read. People only complain that there is a disconnect between his lectures and his tests because they are too lazy to go and actually read the required sections. Recommended Class!

Awful class... If his tests reflected his teaching method, it would be great.  But there's a huge disconnect between the two.  His lectures are easy & fun and span broad topics while his tests focus on details that often have NOTHING to do with the subject matter.  If you can avoid taking this class, do it.
This class sucks.  He teaches a very easy subject that only requires common sense, yet somehow his tests are impossible, requiring minute details.  This class is a waste of time

His lectures are decent and he does explain things in a easy-to-digest fashion. The tests, however, may be unexpected difficult and require you to recall tiny bits of useless information from text/guest lectures. If you want the bonus credits, make your response as cheesy as possible. Just imagine you are trying to entertain your grandfather.

This class is not an easy A. Maybe I was just too lazy but I didn't end up doing very well. You definitely need to do the readings for the tests, and really know them well.  Lecture was fun some times, esp. when he dressed up in a Campbell's soup costume.

Great , lively professor with awesome lectures. Only class where I actually wanted to go to class. :) I really enjoyed the guest speakers, the marketing derby, and the movie clips in class. :)  The exams are a little difficult though, so watch out for that...
Useless class, so-so professor, but very easy.

A good class if you're interested in marketing. Not too much work, just read the textbook and take good notes. Tricky exams but do the extra credits and especially the marketing derby if you want an A. McLaughlin a pretty nice guy, but be careful not to get on his bad side! I've seen this guy pissed off, and lets just say it's not pretty.

Prof. McLaughlin was not very helpful in general, not very insightful, and quite frankly I question his aptitude and the fact that he runs the AEM program. The class was not too hard, sure the prelims were tricky, but with all the extra credit ANYONE should be able to get an A. Read the book, especially the extra articles in the chapters.
my fav class
Take this class! One of the better AEM classes - fun and interesting. The prelims are very tricky, but they're curved up. Very little work.
Very interesting material and an amazing lecturer. But the tests, which make up 90% of your grade are very keen to details. They were much harder than I expected.
Wow...who knew marketing could be so hard.  The degree of difficulty of the lectures does not equal the difficulty of the exams.  Nice guy, but there is soo much to know for tests.
ed mclaughlin is my hero.  he knows his marketing, especially about the food industry.  a brilliant guy who should write more books.

Pretty easy, fun class. If you do the reading and study, and extra credit, you should end up in the A range. No outisde work other than studying for 3 prelims (don't have to take the final if you do well on them).

Interesting subject and pleasant professor but the tests are horrible. He tests on the most insignifacnt details instead of important concepts, discouraging actual learning in lieu of factual memorization. Be sure to go to class and, read several times, and pay attention at guest lectures.

One of the best classes I've ever taken. Great prof - interesting lectures, gotta love the movie clips and ads during lecture. Prelims are much easier than in past years. If you do extra credit and study for prelims, you should get in the A range.
Great guy, great class ... How funny was it when he fell off the stage? I loved it.
Really great lectures.  Tests are difficult, but overall the class is highly recommended.

Be sure to attend all his classes, he might cover some meterials outside the textbook.  Prior to Fall 2004, there are 3 out of 4 essay topic on each prilim.  At Fall 2004, only 1 out of 2 essay topic for each prelim. Pay more attention to the topic that he emphasizes in class repeatedly.
Interesting class, not a lot of work, but prelims are quite hard. Still, a good class that's worth taking

He's a great teacher! I loved the in-class commercials and guest lectures of very prominent business Cornell alum/people. Tests are hard, prepare for them! Out of the 4 exams you take, the lowest one gets dropped. AWESOME! Good amount of EC offered
Interesting lectures, but the prelims are a ****. He tests on the smallest most insignificant details in the text and lectures. If you don't read the text, the highest grade you will get is a C.
Very enjoyable class, but HARD tests.
the class is interesting, and the lectures are engaging, but the tests are horrendously hard. nothing you do will prepare you sufficiently for his nitpicky details....
very interesting class...nice guy, very interested in marketing...tough prelims though...I would reccommend the class

the pro of a good lecture does NOT outweigh the con of good grades..def NOT recommend this class for anyone wanting to do well in a course. appears to be a nice guy but NOT. "easy" lectures, hard prelims, and whats w/ completely random attendenc

great teacher, relaxing lecture class, but be sure to read, because many prelim questions are details in the text and prelims are somewhat difficult...i love how he uncorporates videos in his presentation, brings class to life=)
Nice professor, enjoyable class- many clips, guest speakers, class slides online, generally a fun and relaxing class.  Though, make sure you attend classes...
Not a bad teacher, but definitely an ass. He is the kind to punish you for skipping his class before a break. His tests are completely evil.

Readings were incredibly dense and lengthy. Lectures were genuinely unrelated to the readings. Baptist advertised his own merchandise and book repeatedly. Grading varied wildly across TAs. Grossly incompetent lecturer.

Worst class I've taken at Cornell. Horrible lectures. Boring, disorganized, filled with irrelevant information. Readings were lengthy but interesting. Tests are basically unrelated to much of the readings and lecture. Terrible class

Insane amounts of reading material. No consistency in lectures, and just when it seems he starts talking about something actually important to the core of the class he tangents off on something again losing the attention of his students. He seems like a nice guy who is passionate about what he does, but he is not meant to teach.

Professor Baptist came up with very interesting essay prompts that were virtually all of your grade. It was quite manageable if you paced yourself. Lots of readings but interesting, if you can't do them all it's not a big deal. I got better grades on essays than I expected- don't be afraid to ask him beforehand with questions, he's very helpful.
Professor Baptist is very knowledgeable and kind to his students. Would definitely recommend, however be prepared for tough grading.

Mean guy. Horrible lecturer that will put you to sleep every time. very unreasonable and gives off bad vibes. lecture is all over the place and class has no structure. Not too hard depending on your TA

Mean guy. Unreasonable. Probably unhappy with his life -- I've heard stories about him only justified by extreme unhappiness with his own life. After taking his class, he changed my entire perception of academia and confirmed the suspicion "those who cannot do, teach." Fears face-to-face confrontations.

Baptist is a nice guy and knows a ton but only an OK lecturer. Kind of rambles on and gets off topic easily. Lectures have nothing to do with what the tests are on. Assigned readings are very specific and pretty interesting. Discussion sections were pretty boring. Class was not as interesting as I thought it would be.

Prof. Baptist's Obama and Lincoln course was extremely informative. Some called the course premature but it was probably one of the best courses I've taken at Cornell. Baptist is very helpful during office hours and deeply cares about his students' opinions. Yes, he is a stickler for clear writing but what professor isn't? I highly recommend him!
A bit dry in lecture, but extremely knowledgeable about the subject. Chooses great books. As aren't impossible if you write clearly and ALWAYS check your work for errors.

Seminars w/ Baptist are a good way to get your AMSt diversity/pre-1900 requirements out of the way. Minimal work and Baptist is very knowledgable, passionate about the subject. A little dry, but there are much more boring professors here.

Great professor who is passionate about what he teaches.  Very hard to get A's on his essays...is a stickler for grammer and syntax...make sure to proofread your essays several times over before handing them in.  Good thing is you will be a better writer after taking his class...very nice and helpful too

nice man, but impossible and rather unreasonable grader.  also, in seminar, he can be disrespectful of students, ignoring they're input or in the least shooting them down as though they had no valid point.

Baptist is a fantastic professor.  Very personable and intellectually challenging at the same time. Thought-provoking seminar with interesting readings and discussion.  If you are interested in American history, you should definitely take one of his classes!

He is a great guy and truly loves to teach. Wants you to learn. However, at least in this class, it's really hard to get an A on a paper. He really pushes you to improve your writing. (btw, he's a stickler for grammer and syntax)
Prof Baptist is amazing...even if he tells me to drink more caffeine before class ;)

Baptist is the man. He took the time to review with me all of the essays I wrote for his class. Very intelligent, a great lecturer, and is passionate about both his courses and his students. Highly recommend.

Baptist is very helpful and a great lecturer, knows his material well and makes class interesting, a very fair grader who will go back and take a second look at your work if you ask and reconsider your grade...a great prof

Prof. Baptist is one of the best lecturers I've had, and the material he covers is very interesting. Also, the reading and writing requirements for the course weren't too demanding, and the grading was more than fair.
Prof Baptist is a terrific lecturer!

He's great at explaining things and will get you through the semester, but his grading can be harsh. The work is different from anything I've ever done but interesting. It was a great experience taking the class and he was willing to work with me when there were discrepancies. Highly enjoyed.

Quite possibly the funniest professor I've had for a while.  Really easygoing.  Beware when taking notes for his section...he's not the most organized notegiver.  The lab work gets annoying and the medium's oh-so-fickle, but he teaches you the works to survive a lighting project or two.

She is a really kind, passionate person who cherishes her opportunity to teach us. I really enjoyed her lab section. She makes sure that all students understand the key concepts clearly and works hard to see her students succeed. Very inspiring...

Jennifer is the best lab TA I've ever had. She's so helpful and easy to talk to during class. She never seems condescending even if you ask a dumb question. Lab time is short. She gives you everything you need to pass as long as you're willing to put in the work. She's also available outside lab times - just email her!
She was and still is very awesome at her job. I took Bio 212 Lab and Micro Lab with her. She is so amazing.

This was her first time teaching this lab section, but she always came to class very well prepared for the lesson.  I was really comfortable making comments and asking questions during class, and she never makes class last the full length of time! She's a spectacular teacher! :)
