good humor, great lecture, attendance is 30%, iclicker, midterms are not hard, you dont really need to read the textbook, I love the professor and love the class, definitely recommend people to take her class.

Take her! Not the most interesting but she tries. Mainly focuses on powerpoints so not necessary to attend lectures but good idea to. Not alot of busy work. Weekly hw usually simple & graded on completion. The class is an easy A as long as you know your material & material isn't tough. Discussions are helpful for MT and fun if you have a cool TA!

Dr. Zellou is a great professor. It's obvious that she's very interested in what she's teaching, which interests the class. She is always eager to entertain questions, even if they are very abstract. Attendance is required for lectures and discussions. This is an easy A class and I highly recommend taking it with this professor.

Professor Zellou taught mainly from power point slides, however, when the class got into discussion it was clear she has a lot of knowledge on the field of linguistics. The lectures can be a little dry to sit through and tough to stay awake but it's worth it to go to class because occasionally a couple test questions will relate to class discussion

Sweet prof! The course in general is ridiculously easy, though you still have to go to class to learn the material. Weekly discussion is mandatory but prepares you for midterms. The class is pretty abstract and not super interesting, but coming from a science major it's an easy A (got a 92% on the first midterm without studying). Good 4 unit GE!

All this comments are a lie. I am currently an Econ major and took this.  Grading criteria is purely based on your exam (45% for 2 prelim 45% for final, 10% hw which is completion). DO NOT expect helpful lectures. He skips a lot of fundamental ideas and he is not clear. TA makes the exam so your test depends on the TA, and the TA changed this year.

He posts the lecture notes in advance online so you can have them as supplement while in class. The textbook is rarely used and his lectures are almost exactly what is in the notes. The exams are carbon copies of the HW problems and past prelims.

I was hugely disappointed by Prof. Masson's class. Although my grade turned out fine, I didn't really learn much at all. He teaches from poorly written lecture notes that often deviate from the text, making the textbook (which is really quite good) useless to study from for the exams. I now plan to redo the course material on my own.

Masson's a nice guy and a very approachable professor but he's not a good lecturer. He speaks far too softly and has an annoying habit or circling random words on the blackboard over and over and over again. He leaves a lot in the hands of his T.A. (Pin) who, luckily for us, was simply amazing. Prelims and finals were carbon copies of HW questions.

His lectures are mostly boring and incomprehensible. However, Masson makes great lecture notes that is much better than the textbook. He is a friendly guy and has occasional flashes where he suddenly seems brilliant and his lectures make sense. Prelims were extremely easy and almost a carbon copy of prior year prelims.

He rushes through lectures and draws graphs with sooo many lines it gets so confusing to take notes. He also erases things off the board before you can copy them. He talk to himself. However, as a person he is really nice and friendly. The TA was equally bad. Spoke softly and sometimes couldn't solve hw problem, so just made it up.
Talks to himself drawing many graphs that are disorganized.  He draws so many lines on each graph that he himself cannot figure what they all meant.  Lectures are pointless and the TA was even worse.

Terrible lecturer. Bad handwriting, just talks to  himself drawing dozens of graphs. On the bright side, he doesn't concentrate on the math too much, but he's obsessed with graphs. Just the textbook is enough and does a better job than him.

My class was the first class he had taught in almost 20 years and you could definitely tell. He E-mailed notes that were wrong and incomplete and he wouldn't always catch his mistakes until days later. Class grade based only on midterm/final which could be good or bad depending on the student. Terrible, unorganized teacher. Don't take his class!

Rob was the toughest Honors College instructor that I've had.  He assigned an entire book to read, plus a paper.  Weekly.  He was quite condescending, and was really too obsessed with the term:  Design Principle.  My class should have been titled: Introduction to Design Principles.  Avoid taking his class if you're all about grades.

I think Rob genuinely wants to make a positive change. I think he wants to make his students think outside of the box. His approach however is really painful. Wants to intimidate students. Lectures are pompous and aggressive. Just being in class was stressful. Approached him mid-semester to discuss some issues. Made me feel I was wasting his time.
Prof. Young is articulate, dedicated, and knows his stuff. The class requires a lot of work, but it's worth it. You will not fall asleep during class-- lectures are fascinating. Highly recommended.

If you came to school to have your mind pushed, here's the first place you should look if you have even a slightly "green" heart.  Every move this man makes is outside the box.   Youll learn vary quickly that hes never out of character because he lives what he speaks.  Hes not just trying to teach you,  hes trying to change you.   What doesn't kill us makes us stronger;  I survived Green Cities, so can you.

Prof. Hockett just skips couples of his classes. No PPT, no syllabus, and no homework. His lecture is more like chatting with someone, which is not favored by me. Very open text problems and you cannot miss it.
Prof. is a great teacher who genuinely cares about the material as well as his student's comprehension of it.
Wonderful professor, often no cold calls, makes a very hard subject accessible to students. also takes the time to answer questions right after class is over - the best!

Good professor who cares a lot about his students. He takes things slow, sometimes too slow, in order to make sure that everyone understands everything about the topic. Some might not like that he focuses on theory as well as black letter.
The best!
Prof. Travers is superb! He will change your view of history for the better!

Prof. Travers is an engaging lecturer who seems passionate about teaching and cares about his students. Reading load was reasonable. A variety of graded assignments (papers, exams, discussion participation, etc.). Fair grader.

Great lecturer and ad very good FWS professor too! He divided time between historical lectures, reading Kipling and writing in the class. Lectures were easy to follow and he was very passionate and enthusiastic about the British Empire. Travers also took time to schedule individual meetings for papers and had very open office hours. Great guy!
Travers was great to listen to... He was SO enthusiastic and clearly loves the material (and his British accent always made things interesting).  However, be aware that his readings are VERY long.

Really enjoyable class, lectures can be kind of disorganized, but mainly because he gets excited and goes on tangent. It's clear he's very passionate about what he teaches. It's worth taking any class that he takes.
Prof Travers was so enthusiastic and engaging and it was wonderful to witness in class. Every time I hear the word "Blackpool" I think of the Blackpool Rock song.

Professor Travers is a very engaging lecturer whose passion comes across with every lecture. He is funny and relatable. The only drawbacks are that his lectures are not always easy to take notes on and he demands a lot interms of reading and papers. Expect to work if you take his class but also expect to enjoy him as a professor immensely.

Best professor so far at Cornell! Built engaging lectures based on only a few notes. Covered all the major theories about different aspects of the British Empire, in greater depth than you'd find anywhere else, and tied them together into a coherent presentation. The lectures are worth attending even if you can't take the class.

Travers is a funny guy, at times bordering on hilarious. His lectures, though, were long, somewhat disorganized, and boring. While he was very approachable, very into the material, and very very British, the class was surprisingly intense. Definitely not the easy liberal arts class I was hoping for. If you really want to learn though, it's solid.
Excellent professor. He gives engaging lectures with some good comedy thrown in here and there.  He also makes an effort to get to know his students even in a pretty large class setting.
Professor Travers is wonderfully British, and wonderfully wonderful!
A very engaging speaker, Travers has the unique ability to inspire students and draw them into what he is saying. A fair grader and solid professor

He's an outstanding lecturer. A really nice, down-to-earth, genuinely funny guy. Very passionate about what he does. Interesting class. However, though the lectures were very organized and beautifully presented, the class as a whole was a little unorganized.
Travers is pretty cool, a good lecturer. Class is disorganized but prof is very passionate about subject matter. Western civ might suck, but Travers is a good teacher and funny guy.

Travers is brilliant, engaging, and communicates a tremendous sense of the importance of the material, as well as inculcating a love for history.  Also, he teaches from different historical perspectives and allows students to compare and evaluate them for themselves.  Travers' class is fun and engaging, a rare combination.  And he's funny, too!

just a reminder to anybody looking at this page that the math department professors rate themselves to raise their scores. Strichartz is a failure as a professor and will literally not write notes on the board. Also has bordeline pedophilic tendencies and you should avoid him if possible.

He's an intelligent professor. I like learning from him a lot. He's the best math professor despite all of the negative comments. He seems difficult to approach, but he's very friendly and open to students. The homework is very difficult so make sure to read the book in advance and go to TA's and his office hours and do your work.

The droning lectures were direct copies of the text, only less intelligible and mind-bogglingly dull. His classes became my afternoon naptime and the course was the bane of my existence. The material is alright but the lecture method is deplorable, the homework awful. Don't take his classes lest your mind be imprinted with his loud, nasal voice.
Despite what the haters say, he really cares about the material and knows his stuff.
Unclear lectures but is very lenient and friendly. Does not respond to email. Class is easy

Horrible. absolutely horrible. Math was my favorite subject coming in and now I hate it because of this guy. If you end up with him because of your schedule, SWITCH OUT. It's not worth it. Change your entire schedule to escape this guy. You won't regret it. He's just terrible.

Extremely boring professor. Does not have a clear lecture plan, you end up doing most of your learning from the textbook. Going to class does not help in your understanding whatsoever. NOT RECOMMENDED.

Extremely unclear, very boring lectures.  Kind of helpful when you ask for it.  Very passionate about the subject material, but you will not be prepared for the tests and will be very bored and confused in class.
Attending math 611 class was a total waste of time, because Strichartz made students do the "teaching" instead of doing it himeself
Slightly strange but a very nice guy. I was able to understand him easily and the prelims were pretty straightforward.

If you ask him questions, he walks away. And he doesn't prepare for lecture, just rambles. You don't know how happy it made me to see that it wasn't just me or my relationship with math that made this class bad.

interesting personality, but generally a jolly guy. i don't really learn anything in his lectures though (i learn most of the material at MATH 012) and he gets angry when you ask him questions. you might be better off with a TA for these lectures.

Prof. Strichartz is really smart (after all, he is a Putnam Fellow), but his lectures are very unclear and the class examples are just rehashes of the textbook's examples.  The textbook for the course didn't help either, it's a miserable pile of useless equations without explanations.
Strichartz's lectures are incomprehensible and his command of the material, as evidenced by his joke of an analysis text, is seriously questionable.
No Comments
Rather an odd fellow...stares at the ceiling a lot.  But he's a good lecturer, and obviously an intelligent man.

He embodies everything that makes people think that math is a difficult, undecipherable subject.  There were 40-50 students in the beginning but came down to 17.  The course has been traumatic for me, and I occasionally have nightmares about this course.
Prof. Strichartz is a great lecturer, and just a jolly guy.  He's very approachable and quite funny.

If you wanna actually learn about healthcare and business take US Healthcare Systems, you'll actually learn about it more and with better lectures. Karpman kinda sucks with lectures, the slides are boring and he could be dry. Its 1 credit though so its not that deep, there were only like 3 papers which weren't bad.
lectures were monotonous and weren't very stimulating

Does not know anything about business regulation. Only has knowledge in medicine so tries to reroute every lecture to a conversation about the specifics of biology. When anyone asks him a question on a business regulation, he starts rambling about something else because he doesn't know the answer. Take another class with a more educated prof!

Papers are graded quite harshly, making it hard to engage and appreciate material. Once the prof said to his TA at the end of a lecture recording that "all these premeds care about is grades". Welp, I got a good grade in the class and still am not happy *mic drop*. Class was interesting but sadly frustrating when you have to deal with tough grading

Clearly passionate about business medicine and current health care policies, and always left time for questions. Slightly disorganized and struggles with tech at times, but he does his best. He is very nice and def cares abt students. Grading criteria was unclear, and no rubric provided for writing assignments. Participation and attendance counts.

Karpman is laid back but incredibly knowledgeable. Classes with him can be incredibly useful or incredibly boring depending on whether or not you're willing to put in work. He is not going to force you to participate but you're passing up a big opportunity and a great mentor if you don't.

Professor Karpman lacks a basic understanding of simple topics. He is incompetent, disorganized, and probably the worst professor or teacher I have had in my entire education. Don't take his classes if you want to get any value whatsoever out of the thousands of dollars in tuition you are spending.

Every now and again, Cornell adds a new professor who is phenomenal. Mr. Karpman is not that professor. Though nice and soft spoken, expect to be left confused and bewildered about basic business topics. After you are left even more confused about business topics, expect to be equally perplexed by his grading scheme
Poor lesson plan. Chronically disorganized.
Intelligent professor, but quite organized. The guess lecturers are very interesting but there is no clear cut way grades are calculated.
Interesting material but his presentations and lectures were certainly lacking in details, and tangible examples. As far as Cornell professors go, he easily falls into the mid lower rankings.

Is enthusiastic about conveying the material, but ends up rambling and confuses his points. Mr. Karpman is interesting, however he needs to develop better time management skills. Too often he lectured past class time
Great 1 credit graded class. Easy A and learn some business/medical lessons. Professor Karpman is very clear on what is expected, show up, do the work, and you will be fine.

Great for an introduction to Materials Science, but also a good engri for any major. There were weekly quizzes every Friday which were pretty hard and I hated them. Psets were difficult but not time-consuming and plenty of office hours. For the prelims, we got one page of notes and there was a group project instead of a final exam which was great.

Psets are pretty long and difficult: kind of require attending OH. But, getting a decent grade isn't hard since he  curves the prelim grades and then the overall grade. There are weekly quizzes.Professor van Dover tries to make the lectures engaging by including iClickers(idk if it counts toward attendance) and sometimes jokes.
Overall a very great professor and person. Always reasonable about grading if you ask, just make sure to go to office hours for tough problem set questions.

This class was good, but not the best intro to Material Science eng course that could be provided. Everything is about sustainability/future of materials. I would not suggest taking this course unless you have interest in Materials Science. On the light side though, there is no lab, and instead a group project. The hw definitely takes time...

Chill professor that covers a lot of subjects interestingly. Not too difficult of a class and very conceptual. Some homework questions are randomly difficult that require OH but otherwise fine. OH are also chill with a collaborative atmosphere. Lecture notes aren't too comprehensive but he is always willing to help and chat

Nice professor, cares about his students, tries to make class engaging. Lecture content is often beyond the scope of what most freshman know, but as long as you understand the general concepts its not too bad. Problem sets can be a pain sometimes, but the class is graded very fairly.

Lectures can be very boring- you better like the stuff so you don't doze off. Not really hard stuff, just pay attention in lectures and u don't really have to review anything at home. Problem sets are short just weird so make sure you can make it to office hours to ask for help if u do that you can spend as little as 2h/wk outside for this class.

Great professor. Very approachable. Respect and care about students. Maybe the only thing I don't like that much: he doesn't write much explanation on board or ppt (mostly equations, derivation and pictures. maybe confusing and lost later)
good

Really nice guy. Grading criteria isn't harsh and the class is very comprehensive. Can be a bit hand-wavey at times but a solid introduction. Not the best lecturer but he really tries to answer any questions you have and is very accessible.

Lectures were very boring and I did not get much out of them.  A lot of topics weren't explained that well and he assumed you already knew a good deal about what he was teaching (I didn't). It wasn't toooo hard to get a good grade if you put in the effort, but only take the class if you're genuinely interested in the subject and willing to do so.
Great professor, is amusing when teaching and cares about students more than other professors normally do. Class isn't that hard, but it is fun. It was a memorable class.

Great professor. Very clear that he's interested in teaching and inspiring students, i.e. lectures are not some sort of hassle that gets in the way of his 'real' work. Extremely helpful if you don't understand concepts, friendly and never condescending. Homework isn't bad, labs are usually really quick (eg 15-20 minutes), lab writeups okay. 1010

Very friendly and approachable professor. Extremely helpful if you are having problems on labs, homeworks, or just on general concepts. I personally found his lectures a little boring, but he is very clear and is just a fun professor in the lecture room. For the course, labs are quick and fun. Write ups slightly time consuming but not bad.

I took this Intro to Engineering class because I was interested in the future of energy and wanted to get a general introduction to the material science field. The class was very interesting and most of the lectures were entertaining because Prof. Van Dover is quite an amusing professor. He's very nice and helpful and overall the class was great!
Highly recommend professor Cathles. Climate 102 was such an interesting easy class and you can join class on zoom to get credit.
Great professor, very fun/easy class. A couple group projects and psets, no exams. You are pretty much guaranteed an A if you do the work.

Class is unorganized. There's barely any structure to the materials. He basically teaches whatever comes to his mind. No quiz answers were given and problem set solutions were not followable. The TA does all the work for the class and all he does is show up at lecture. The majority of the final was materials NOT discussed in previous assessments.
boring and unorganized

He is disoriented, disorganized. He takes wrong notes to class several times. He is good at making jokes and telling stories but not giving lectures and explaining things. He gets impatient when you ask silly questions. I would have done better if I started working by my own earlier.

Blume is a poor explainer of the concepts in class and then when the tests arrive they contain material you have never seen before. He neglects to inform the TA of anything that will be on tests so the review sessions are worthless at best. He hands out no syllabus and cites simpsons paradox when talking about grades (look it up).

Definitely the worst professor I've had at Cornell. Lectures were scatterbrained and only covered basic concepts, while problem sets were difficult and exams were impossible to study for. The TA had no idea what was going on half the time. It's honestly worth pushing intermediate micro off for a year to avoid taking a class with Blume.
if you're going to take game theory 3680, you might as well skip lectures and watch these http://www.academicearth.org/courses/game-theory

Lectures are essentially useless - Blume goes over the concepts broadly, but the homeworks and tests go much deeper than what he covers in class. The textbook is close to useless and Blume insists on holding makeup classes when HE misses class. Terrible class, if at all possible, do not take.

"Considering recording lectures for his superiors to see!"  Lol... like Easley?  He is very smart, arrogant, a pain in the ass to deal with, yet broadly interesting; he enjoys and has knowledge of lots of random things. He's not out to get you, he is just extremely disorganized and teaches as if you're having an intellectual chat over coffee.

I have taken two of his classes, and can attest to all the ratings below. Tried many times to find a redeeming quality over the past year, but he is simply an arrogant, pompous buffoon. Lectures are beyond worthless, in that they detract from the time you have to teach yourself the material. Considering recording lectures for his superiors to see!

Completely useless. TA's are the key in learning anything from his courses. Does not teach, no textbook, could care less about how students do or feel about him. The Econ dept. should be ashamed but then again, they dont.

Worst prof ever-- disorganized, a poor lecturer, pompous, arrogant, and a power-tripper. Relies on his own incomplete lecture notes that are filled with typographical, math, and grammar errors. Grading is opaque. You're on your own with this guy.

Bad textbook, mostly useless lectures.  For some reason I went to them though.  There was marginal entertainment value, and occasionally I learned how to do a problem.  Mostly he just talked about the existence of concepts, without actually explaining them, though.
Lecture is useless...be ready to learn everything on your own...
Worst professor ever... he will randomly cancel class and demand to have make-up class at the most inopportune hours.  Wouldn't really matter because his lectures are beyond useless.
don't take it.
Very disorganized, teaching has nothing to do with the book, useless lectures.
I was going to throw my opinion here as well. Luckily, others have already done so. Nice guy. Disorganized. Unclear. A bad teacher.
Disorganized, unclear, unhelpful and condescending.
I would never take a class with this professor again.

Very nice man once you spend some time with him. Extremely smart- engage him in conversation about his work and he responds well. A little fazzled but if you take the time to listen and do the work it comes together.

This guy makes such an interesting course easily the worst class in the Econ dept. He does not teach at all but will go on and on in lectures how smart he is...take the class with Basu if you can. He is incredibly rude, too.
When you get nothing but bad ratings from your students after so many years of teaching, does one need to say more?
Everything I learned about game theory, I learned from the book by Gibbons, not this class. I attended every single lecture and unfortunately I didn't get much out of them.

This professor is perhaps one of the worst that I've ever had in my many years of being a student. He acts very smart but very often he doesn't seem to know the material that well. He also comes in late and doesn't prepare his lectures.

HE DOES NOT SHOW FOR HIS OWN OFICE HOURS!!! and then complains no one comes to them. This guy is very unhelpful. wants to waste your time talking about everything but the course also goes about talking how dumb the students are.
no good
Nice guy, very funny, but very bad instructor. He knows the material but he cant convey it. I wouldn't recommend any course with him.
Smart guy, TERRIBLE course!
Very nice guy. A bit disorganized. Knows material. Have to spend a lot of time going over stuff yourself to get most from class.

This professor is honestly the worst that I've ever had in my many years of being a student.  He acts very smart because he says he is, but he doesn't seem to know the material.  He also comes in late, doesn't prepare his lectures and talks about innaties
Avoid this very rude teacher, thinks he knows everything. Very smart, but probably not as smart as he thinks!
He's a nice guy but the lectures are not organized well.  Problem sets and exams don't reflect lectures enough.
Econ 368 is extremely difficult and his lectures/book choice do not help prepare for the tests. Do not take this class unless you are extremely creative mathematically.
He's actually a nice guy, and his lectures are fun. The problem is that they don't prepare you for the tests and neither did the book.
talks too much, teaches too little!!
terrible lecturer, hard tests, boring class, do not take

Larry seems like a perfectly nice guy, but his teaching style leaves room for improvement. This was my most disorganized class of the semester and although the homework isn't difficult, the textbook assignments are extremely long. Also, as others have said, the quizzes are only based on his hard-to-follow lectures and they can be rough.

You have to put in work to get an A. I found the homework assignments long and tedious and the tests/quizzes are based solely on lectures. If you don't attend lecture, you probably won't do well on the exams because the slides alone aren't helpful. He is also very unorganized when he lectures so its hard to stay focused and grasp concepts.
i love larry

Homeworks were very easy to complete, but the lectures were very hard to follow. A lot of the test questions come from his lectures, rather than the textbook. Overall, it was a low-effort class except for the group project, which was pretty time-consuming.
Cannot follow his lecture. Cumbersome group project. Tough biweekly quizzes. Annoying diary entries. Avoid at all cost

Professor Brown is an intelligent and humorous teacher who cares about his students. Though EAS1220 is known as an "easy science" because he teaches by repetition and offers up a lot of 'gimme' points, his lectures are quite complex/VERY hard to follow and a lot of memorization is required if you're after an A.

I enjoyed going to his lectures. The class is huge so I recommend sitting near the front so you don't miss what he says. It'll help you out during the quizzes. For homework, all you have to do is read chapters from an online textbook and answer questions at the end. Fairly easy. Study the powerpoints for the prelim and final and you should do well.

Pay attention during his boring lectures and focus on vocab --- fairly easy A but don't underestimate it. Most kids do poorly because they think it'll be a "show up and pass" but slight effort really seals the "A".  The in-class quizzes are pretty tough and he pulls most of them for exam questions.

Professor Brown is by far the most considerate teacher I've had. He offers make up quizzes and keeps postponing  deadlines for assignments. Though his lectures can be quite confusing you'll find it easy if you actually read the textbook.

if you are into subtle humor and if you find non-funny things hilarious, you will love this professor as a person. but he speaks way too fast and has trouble communicating a lot of concepts. If you manage to pay attention despite all the loud people in class, memorize the lectures, and memorize key terms you should get an A.

This class was incredibly disorganized. Lectures never started on time, material was unclear, group projects were described very vaguely. This class was almost condescendingly easy considering there was no real work to be done, but skimming the textbook was necessary. Would not recommend at all whatsoever. It was painfully boring and cluttered.

Great guy, wants you to succeed. If you don't do well on the prelim or final, the group project (basically a second prelim) will give a tremendous boost to your grade (it's worth 20%+ of the class). If you read the textbook and listen in class you'll do fine. I didn't really do any work and managed a B+.

Easy class, lectures arent mandatory, and are sometimes boring. Really nice teacher, knows a lot about the material. He curves the course so you're grade goes up a whole letter at the end of the course.Read the textbook and study your quizzes

Extremely disorganized in his lecture style and in his grading. Lectures to an incredible level of detail, then tests on that detail. DO NOT take this thinking it is an easy class to fulfill the science requirement. Still wishing I had dropped this class while I could.
Funny professor... because of takenote did not go to lectures.. did decent. quizzes are same as last years, and the midterm was identical. FInal was hard.

I actually enjoyed lectures (engaging) even tho, as previous reviewers said, Brown is disorganized. This class was easy in part because I ordered the take note service and studied from those for the midterm and the final. Very helpful teacher.  Class will require some reading and work but overall very easy.  Material can be dry at times but the prof. tries to make it fun.  Overall, subject matter is interesting and contemporary.

He is intelligent and knows what he is talking about but he can not, for the life of him, tell us what he knows. Nice, funny guy, though he talks a bit too fast sometimes.  Lectures get boring and meander, and his Powerpoints are disorganized - way too much info. this class was a complete waste of time.  you will take it because it fills a science requirement, but everyone, including the professor, treats it as such a complete joke that you will not be able to take it seriously and will wish that you had taken it pass/fail.  readings, lectures, professors, and TAs are all completely useless in life.

Incredibly boring.  Actually believes his class is worth something.  Tests are way too hard.  Class is a waste.  He left for three weeks and made us sit through awful guest speakers and quizzed us on it.  Books are useless and homework is a joke.
keep up with his quick talk and "uh uh uh's" and you should be fine! comical and genuinely friendly :)
While Larry Brown comes across as comical, he can be quite the devil with the red pen.  Thanks for the C, mate.

Brown is the man.  That is all.

"Earthquake!"  It was pretty cool, in the end I realized I learned a little bit.  Fairly easy material-wise but not grade-wise, which is an interesting mix.  L.B. is the man though, no doubt.  You will laugh your ___ off.
incredible class about financial engineering & hands down the best professor I have had at Cornell.
Lectures are hard to understand but the professor is super caring and does cool side projects. Definitely recommend going to his office hours. Prelims are super similar to the psets.

Def a weed out class. Lectures are hard to follow, took more time trying to figure out his handwriting than the actual content. Exams are very similar to the psets given though, so easy A. Seems like the professor is just too smart to know how to teach.

Varner was my professor for Intro to ChemE. The class was pretty easy although you do need to pay attention and show up since the lectures aren't recorded. The exams are pretty much the same as the review. His handwriting is a bit hard to understand but other than that the class was an easy A.

Very nice and caring professor; however, he's extremely disorganized. It's probably because he's teaching the class that he hated the most when he was an undergrad, but the format of the class is is all over the place. Has a cool personality but do not know how to teach. The lectures are confusing. His handwriting is cool but very hard to read.

Honestly a great professor who is always willing to help his students, the prelims were take home and really easy and there was no hw in the class, however lectures were a little boring but thats because the material is basically a bunch of equations

He has such cool handwriting, but it's sometimes hard to read. The class was very fun and interesting . His lectures were pretty clear. Quizzes and tests clearly correlate to lectures and problem sets.
Awesome professor! Doesn't emphasize grades and wants you to be there so you can learn.
Really really nice guy who cared more about his students than making the class hard. Psets were reasonable but challenging and the class was really fun. Would take it again if I could.

Funny and chill lecturer. Lectures are often easily followable. Problem sets were generally difficult, although there is plenty of help available with office hours and "homework parties". I thought the textbook was often more useful than the lectures except in the case of special relativity.

The class is hard, but his lectures are good and he tries his best to make things as easy to understand as possible. He seems to genuinely enjoy teaching. Problem sets and exams are hard, but the he and the TAs are helpful during office hours and he is very reasonable about extensions, extra help, etc. You just have to ask for help.

I love this professor. Several of us were struggling with the material so he decided to add two weekly two-hour collaborative office hours sessions to his regular office hours. He also periodically shares interesting science-related news with the class, and he makes an effort to connect them to our material. He is always smiling in class too.

The problem sets he gives out are the best. Challenging, yet meant to assist you with the concepts learnt at class. Classes and problem sets are even more enjoyable if you have some prior experience with mechanics with calculus. Tests were hard - especially the take home prelim. Thankfully, the grade is curved.
Jim is the greatest teacher you'll ever have. His class is time-consuming, but you'll be rewarded for your effort. Don't be afraid to talk to him! He has great things to say about physics.

Jim is a fantastic teacher.  His Physics 1116 class is a really good class to take even if you think you know basic mechanics, because of the depth and abstraction he uses.  It's tons of fun, and he sets up "homework parties," which are invariably extremely fun, and somewhat productive.  Take this class.

Prof. Alexander is an outstanding physics professor.  He has explains things very clearly and really cares about the success of his students.  PHYS 1116 is a hard class, but he teaches strategies for problem solving that apply to much more than just physics.  He also has a great sense of humor, and is overall a great intro physics professor.

The class is a huge time commitment and is very difficult.  Alexander is spectacular; he is passionate about the subject, has an interesting back-story and, although knowledgeable, brings analytic physics to a comprehensible level.

This was probably one of the most difficult first-year courses at Cornell. Prof. Alexander did his absolute best to make things lucid and cohesive, though extremely complicated steps in derivations were sometimes omitted as "just algebra." Very personable and understanding with regard to students in dire need. WARNING: THIS CLASS IS HARD!!!

Simply put, this class is very hard. You need to have a very strong intuition for physics to succeed. There is a ton of material in this class and Alexander frequently skips steps when teaching the material. He is very clear in his teaching, but he could have a better sense of which things to focus on in lecture. The TAs were very helpful.

I really appreciate how he made things easy to understand. The professors Ive had at Cornell have made me feel lost bc they yap a whole lot abt nothing during class and then test you on material that ur not prepared for, but Terry has been one of the only professors who made me feel very confident in the material I was learning. Thank you Terry!

Professor Alexander's lectures are him writing all the information on his tablet so it's easy to get lost if you can't read his handwriting or don't like that teaching style. Although attendance isn't mandatory he does pop quizzes to make up for it. Attend his office hours as he is very willing to help his students!
The exams are very vague and difficult.

Terry is absolutely open to suggestions and feedback from students. He is very patient with his students and makes sure that his students fully understand the content. He also makes a lot of funny jokes during class.

I love this man. He is the best. He invites his upper level class over at his house for an end of year party. And I wish he kept doing the brexit course for future students - it was one of my highlights of Cornell.
Favorite professor at Cornell. Very caring and understanding with extension and makeup requests. Just go to class, ask questions, and you will get A easily.

There's no other professor like Terry. He meticulously goes over every concept and will force them into your memory with pithy quips. At the same time, Terry is hilarious during lecture and will go on in-depth tangents about the birth of his son or WWII POW camps. He will also call you out for being on your phone. Easy class, wonderful professor.

Most grades are determined by exams, and he does pop quizzes the majority of classes as a way to "take attendance". While this may seem doable, Terry is an un-engaging professor who stands at the front of the room frantically writing notes on his tablet, with no structure or PowerPoint to keep track of his confusing subject. AVOID

Prof Alexander's class is doable, but A+s are essentially impossible (requires 100%) so don't take him if you're counting on that. His lectures were clear but handwriting was unreadable, exam grading was fair, and pop quizzes were slightly stress inducing but manageable (you need to show up!). Very nice guy though, always helped students out.

Terry is a great guy, and very entertaining, but when it comes to teaching, oh is he bad. He rambles and scribbles illegibly on the board, with no regard for our learning. Everyone I know taught themselves everything before every exam, thankfully the content is not too hard.

Despite what many reviews say, Professor Alexander is not a good professor. He is incredibly disengaging, his notes are impossible to read, and the course is not organized well at all. You are graded on very few things, and the practice problems are hard to find and have no solution. The class isn't that hard, just very boring.

Professor Alexander had great lectures that were very engaging and entertaining due to his occasional side stories and enthusiasm. The finals and prelims were based very heavily on lecture material. Overall, definitely recommend.

Terry is a great teacher. He cares about his students and is willing to help whenever someone needs it. He always listens and will go to lengths to make sure everyone understands the content. People complain about the quizzes but they were easy and my grade went up a lot because of them and they genuinely helped me understand the content.

Terry is one of the kindest and most caring teachers ar Cornell. He makes sure all his students who want to understand macro do. His office hours are so helpful and he makes an effort to know as many students names. There are pop quizzes, but if anything they help your grade, he always reviews the answer BEFORE THE QUIZ.

Terry was a great professor. Initially he didn't post answer keys to exams, but after receiving feedback he released not only the answer key but an entire video explaining the solutions and the point breakdowns. He is a really nice person who cares about his students. He made an effort to remember everyone's names, and it showed.

Amazing lecturer, was always engaged during his lectures. Was also funny, and very accessible through Office Hours and was always willing to discuss material with students. He could seem a little intimidating at first but was very genuine while discussing exams. Exams are representative of lectures.

Handwriting in class is illegible, concepts for exams are very unclear, quizzes almost every day, and practice exams do not have answer keys making the class very difficult to study for. Would prefer having actual PowerPoints in class with clear instructions and step-by-step instructions to do problems. Long tangents on unrelated topics.
Can not teach students at all,

Ignore the bad reviews. He is fun, funny, and a little bit crazy. Class is very interesting and he's a good teacher - if you come to every class and pay attention! Not much homework but tests are tricky. If you prepare well, you will find that the exam problems are JUST like the class ones.
Tough grader. Minimal curving. Prelims/Final are very hard. Confusing lecture materials.
He explained economics in such a confusing manner. Had to basically self teach myself all of the concepts. He is aware his handwriting is barely legible, but refuses to change his method of teaching.

He's very accessible outside of class (OH almost every day). Exams are okay (although the second prelim was pretty hard). However, he can also sound harsh when talking to students and he doesn't release the answers to practice prelims. There are group quizzes almost every class. Homework is easy. Discussion sessions were basically useless.
Never posted correct answers about exams or gave feedback. TA discussion sections were useless as were lectures
Frequently went off on tangents and always gave long-winded answers about concepts. Never clear or concise.
I could not read his handwriting. He also made a lot mistakes during lectures that he had to correct

love terry. had him for my hotelie micro class and loved the way he lectured (would write everything down on paper rather than have monotonous slides). incorporates stories to make the lectures more digestable. the info i learned in this class was so valuable and i def understand markets way more now. if u know ur lectures WELL, tests are easy.
horrible; no feedback on any tests or assignments

Terry is patient to explain anything during and outside class. Extremely accomodating with deadlines. Group quizzes on every other session on average. Prelims and exams are fair. Practice with HW and previous prelims for the numerical part. True or False questions separate the A students from the herd so make sure to understand the concepts fully.

Terry is an amazing professor for a rather difficult class as I didn't come in with a good micro/macro foundation. He is great at explaining concepts and was also caring during this hectic semester (made prelim 2 optional and bought us all ice cream). Beware of his pop quizzes in class though.

Terry teaches the class material well. The issue is not with him but rather with the class setup. Tests and homework are assigned randomly, instructions are unclear, grades are stalled, etc. There were not enough TAs for my class so things were very messy. Considering the other options, this Macro class is a solid choice.

Took his class for 2600 last semester, and though my grade was not what I had hoped, I thought Prof. Alexander was one of the best people I've had as a professor. His lectures can be a bit odd sometimes, but he's genuinely trying to help you succeed. I reached out to him because I was struggling with mental health and he was so caring and helpful.

One of the best human beings I have ever met. He was so charismatic, and cares about each of his students. Made concepts very clear, and was really patient with re-explanations, reviews, and introducing material. He goes out of the way to make everyone feel valued, tells stories about his personal life, and makes his expectations clear. LOVE him.

Terry is not only a fantastic and knowledgeable professor, he is a great person. No matter the difficulty you're having reach out and he'll be there to help. Tests are fairly written, yet cover a lot of content so you cant bs your way through the class. Again, terry is the brotha, love this dude

Terry is by far my favorite professor here at Cornell. He is kind and understanding to all of his students. I know someone who slept through their prelim, only to email Terry in a panic and find out that he would be allowed to make it up the next day. He is also funny and even though attendance is usually mandatory, it is well worth it to show up.

Terry Alexander is the best professor I ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and their success. He once wrote my name correctly on the board, and when he asked if it was correct I simply replied it doesnt matter. He promptly turned, made direct eye contact, and said of course it matters, its your name. Take his class.

Alexander is a nice and interesting person, but his teaching style is unfocused and confusing. His lectures are handwritten notes and unreadable, and many of the examples he gives are far more confusing than those provided in discussion. Tests are mostly fair but contain ambiguous short answers. Regularly goes on tangents that distract from class.

Grade weighed heavily on prelims and final exam (25+25+15 --> 65%) Lab session twice per week, assignment once per week. Generous on general marking of works, just submit the things on time and you'd be fine

His lectures were interesting and engaging, he clearly cares a lot about the material and that always makes for the best professors. My TA was great and the grading was really not that hard at all. You'll do best if you're keeping up with the readings, which are substantial but not excessive. Would definitely take another class with him

Great material, inconsistent lecturer. Some days are better than others, but the really bad days make you feel like a captive audience. Pretty tough grader, and it's difficult to get an A in the course. Even though he seems like a great guy with great material, it can sometimes get boring.
The professor is good, but TA is awful.

While Professor Livingston is clearly knowledgeable, he and his TAs especially have a very heavy left wing bias. This is of course a feature not a bug of Ivy League education and, although I may agree with the bias, it is too extreme sometimes. Be prepared to write what the TA and professor want to hear. TA also tolerated anti-white racism in class

By all means the best professor I have ever had. Not only is he absolutely dapper, he is exciting, reflective, sharp as a knife and very very interested in his students. Every lecture made me question my own assumptions about democracy, civility, punishment and social justice and always left me inspired, motivated and provoked. Take his class!!

Livingston is an wonderful teacher and an incredible human being. He taught GOVT 3675 at 8:40 AM this past semester, and I stumbled in bleary-eyed but excited for his lectures. Taking GOVT 3675, I felt like I learned an incredible amount and that my interest in political theory skyrocketed. All because of the wonderful teacher that is Livingston.

Professor Livingston is a really remarkable professor who enables students to develop their own perspective and ideas through his wonderful lectures. I had a truly transformative experience in GOVT 3675, much of which was due to Livingstons fascinating lectures.

I've never had a professor that moderated discussions better than Livingston. His probing questions made the readings fascinating, and I was always excited to come to class and discuss democracy. He was very funny and nice, and a fair grader - hands down one of my favorite professors. I only wish I could've taken more classes with him.
Even though I struggled a lot in 2940, I love Alex Townsend!!
Great professor. Enthusiastic about the subject. Cares about the success of his students.
Absolutely would recommend for Linear Algebra

MATH2940 with Professor Townsend was one of the best classes I've ever taken. His lectures were clear, funny, and constantly inspiring; his graded problems on homework assignments really challenged me to think and work outside the box; and exams were always fair. I learned a lot with him and now have a fantastic foundation for the future.

His Majesty, Alex Townsend, is THE MAN. His lectures are incredibly engaging, and he has a great sense of humor. Just don't say "Hi" to him in the changing room at the gym :)  2940 is a fun class, and I'd highly suggest taking it with Townsend. He drops bombs every single lecture and is extremely approachable. Cares that you learn, isn't stressful.

Townsend is my favourite math professor at Cornell. He loves Harry Potter, banahnah splits, Blue Peter, Ed Discussion, MATLAB, and chalkboard erasers. If you love any of those things, take this class. If you don't, still take this class.
Alex is awesome. Great lectures and easy to understand, not a ton of homework, office hours are definitely helpful.

Cares about his students beyond the scope of his course. Lectures were very interesting, he always showed us examples of how linalg is used in real life. Great guy, highly recommend taking this class with him

The exams are actually hard, but the curve/grading is VERY forgiving.Townsend is legit a motivational speaker, bro casually drops life advice sometimes, probably the best math prof at CU. The lectures have thought put into them, for example he printed out images to show matrix transformations, pretty cool; but linear algebra is still hard though.
Professor Townsend truly cares about his students. Great professor, better person.

I don't know exactly how well I  did in that class, but his office hours were pretty helpful and he was such a nice teacher! Very friendly and entertaining overall, and his lectures and lecture notes are very good as well. Do take him, love that British guy.

Comfortably the best Cornell professor I've had, and pretty unanimously loved by this semester's 2940 students. An excellent lecturer, lighthearted, very caring about his students, and made linear algebra a fun and fascinating topic, at least for me. He brought us some banana split one lecture!

Townsend is the GOAT. He really cares about teaching linear algebra and does cool computer demos. I honestly found his lectures more important than the textbook. His lectures are fun as he uses colored chalk and a wet sponge to clean the board.

HW graded on correctness only helps kids whose friends have the answers. Guess I get punished for trying it all myself? Also, the math department needs to cut the crap with the artificial difficulty on exams. The mean should NEVER be near a 50, it's inexcusable and shows how hard Cornell tries to make things stressful and difficult for NO reason.

Very caring and devoted professor who clearly loves math. Tests usually included a few proof-based questions; I never got any of them right (proofs are too difficult in general for me) but I was still able to do decently on them. The homeworks have two separate components and can be very challenging and time-consuming.

Best math professor I've had hands down. Made the content very approachable and relevant. Always went to lecture even though I took it Fall 2020 at 10am in the morning. Fantastic dude, even better lecturer, and you can tell that he puts in extra effort into teaching. Most importantly he's fair. Lectures in combo with textbook should be enough.

Linear algebra is not an easy topic, but Professor Townsend made it more digestible for his students and explains the concepts very well. He is patient and super caring towards his students. With that said, his exams are brutal. To do well, I would suggest not missing any of his lectures, reading the textbook and going to OH.

Townsend is a fantastic professor. He has a deep understanding of linear algebra and tells us why each topic is important. He also took the time to look through my exam script and gave me detailed advice on how to improve. His homeworks are challenging.

Townsend was probably the best lecturer I've ever had. The lectures are extremely interesting and frequently reference CS and involve a lot of real life topics. He also shows genuine interest in student's well being and spends most of the class involving the rest of us. The homework was difficult but very beneficial for learning linear algebra.
Townsend is concise, smart, quick and entertaining. He is passionate and organized. One of the best professors Ive had. Get ready to work

Prof. Townsend is my favorite math professor at Cornell. His lectures were well organized and he tried his best to make the materials easily comprehensible. Besides, he himself is very nice and personable, and I very much enjoyed his jokes throughout the semester. He made linear algebra not a pain for me. Highly recommend.

Professor Townsend, with his witty humor (both during lectures as well as on our Piazza discussion board), embedded real-life applications into his crystal-clear lectures, leaving me with a newfound confidence in myself and a deeper appreciation for the beauty of mathematics.

Townsend's lectures are very well put together- you can tell he puts a lot of time into thinking about the best way to present topics. Easily the most engaging math lectures I've had. The prelims/homeworks were also very fair. The only parts of the course that weren't that good were those managed by the TAs, like discussions and quizzes.

He truly cares about the subject, and this shows through his engaging and well-structured lectures that heavily aided my understanding. He is very accessible outside of class via email or on Piazza, where he gives detailed responses and encourages students who are concerned about the course. His tests are challenging, but he curves generously.

Professor Townsend was one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. His lectures are clear and engaging; even though the class was online this semester, he encouraged participation and paused often to answer our questions. His exams and homework assignments were very fair.

Townsend is a great prof. He tries to make his lectures accessible, whether via humor or real-world applications, and attempts to incorporate student feedback into the course, which is more than I can say for 80% of the other professors I've had at Cornell. If you can choose between taking 2940 with Townsend and someone else, choose Townsend.

The class is mostly online this semester, but he teaches with a chalkboard and webcam. His lectures make me realize that I greatly miss in-person classes. His lectures are fun to watch and structured. I am finding that I need to read the textbook very closely.

You could tell that Professor Townsend was passionate about the subject and wanted to teach the class the best that he could. His lectures were well-prepared, enjoyable, and he is humorous. I really appreciate that we were able to give him feedback on notecards early in the semester and he implemented those changes.

Would consider taking that class another semester if you can, if Townsend is teaching. He has an amazing personality, puts in a lot of effort into teaching and cares about his students. However, his exams are brutally difficult. There were questions that you won't be ready to solve unless you're a math major. I was stressed out all sem cause of him
Alex Townsend has clear lecturers but expects us to apply a lot that we learned on exams.
Townsend really expects a lot from and cares a lot for his students. He is amazing at explaining things in lecture and during office hours. His exams were conceptual and I found them difficult.

Amazing professor! At first I wasn't sure about Townsend, but he changed the lecture style as the course went on and I found myself so engaged by midsemester; the type of engaged where you forget to take notes because you are so absorbed. Yes, the prelims were hard. But in the end I learned so much from this class, a few points off meant nothing.

Meh. His lectures are pretty boring and not fruitful, although he is a pretty nice guy and has a good sense of humor. Also, made midterms super-hard because last year's mean was too high in his opinion.
The most dedicated math professor. His class changed my attitude towards math. He handed out the lecture notes early, which was very helpful. A very rewarding class.

Townsend is one of the most caring people I've ever met. He responds to feedback throughout the semester to improve the course. Lectures contain everything you need to know to do well (I never read the textbook), and include interesting real-world applications. Exams were very difficult but he curves generously so it works out alright.
His homeworks and exams are hard but I really enjoyed his amazing lectures. He is always so excited to teach and listens to student feedback. I learned a lot this semester from him.

He literally wrote a practice final just because the students demanded him to. Also, he is very active on piazza, and takes the student's feedbacks very seriously throughout the semester. His teaching style isn't for everyone: he focuses on a lot of cool real life applications during lectures, and some students don't like it. I loved it a lot.
Horrible presentation of material; cumbersome and counter-intuitive explanations; boring lectures. A very bad prof. Hopefully never get him again.

I understand that Prof. Townsend has an incredible experience in the area of Mathematics, but I feel like he's just too smart to teach it to anyone. His explanations are obscure; he writes down equations, often not explaining how he derived them. 10 minutes of Khan Academy explained exact equations to me better than 1 hour of his lectures. Awful.

Townsend is a really passionate and good lecturer. He prepares you for the exams really well. The textbook was frustrating and the distribution of quizzes (given during discussion) was not organized well, but you can tell Townsend tried his best and really cared about the students.

His lectures are interesting and very well-planned. He is very open to feedback and is always available and very receptive to questions. He clearly cares a lot about his students and how they do. Difficult class but if you go to lecture and office hours you can absolutely succeed.

Clearly puts in a lot of time and thought into teaching. Very smart, excellent lecturer and presenter, and highly receptive to student feedback during the course. HW is usually difficult, but that should be expected.
Took Prof. Gaeta's Quantum and Nonlinear Optics class as a masters student. He grades grad students and undergrad separately so that takes care of grading worries for undergrads.

There is no question that Alex Gaeta is the best professor I have ever had.  He is clear, profound, a leader in his field, and you are very lucky if you get to have him teach your course.  The cherry on top is that he is supremely nice and will help you with any problem.

Great class, although it is an introductory level course so there are some parts where general function of a component are described but how that process is accomplished isn't explained. Tests are more than fair, and he is an overall great teacher. Easily one one of me favorite classes/professors at Cornell.
The homeworks are much harder than the exams.  The labs are fun and building a functioning laser is awesome.  Pay attention during lecture and you will be fine in the class
Class is easy and informative. He is clear in his explanations. Labs are interesting and informative as well.

I really enjoyed this class. The lectures are interesting for the most part. Sometimes it is a lot of review of basic physics principles, but he makes an effort to teach you something interesting every week. The homework and tests are not extremely difficult, but the labs are very important, so do them.

To score well for this class, pay special attention to each and every lab report. It counts more than you can ever imagine. Gaeta is a great professor who knows his stuff at fingertips. exams and hw are crucial too. In sum, this class is neither easy nor difficult.
his hand-waving argument for all the laser stuff is really too 'hand-wavy'..well, but what do you expect it is QM...for a freshman class

Excellent, interesting lectures; willing to help you out if you go to office hours.  Tests are easy compared to HW's. Every couple lectures he would explain some cutting edge technology in optics just for fun.  Great class!
No Comments
He can't teach.  He doesn't explain things.  He puts lots of variables on the board without explaining what they mean.  His assignments don't make any sense.  I could go on.
Good class but not an EASY A. Do the readings + study and you'll do well.
Can't get over after every sentence he either says "alright", "okay", or "you know".

Great professor and great class.  Series (8 total) of short (2 page) reaction papers to in class exercises (aka you have to show up to class a lot), one midterm and a final.  All slides are posted and readings really aren't necessary but help with exams.  Colvin really make sure you understand the material and gives great real world connections.
Very comprehensive employment law class.  I couldn't have gotten through my internship without it.    Hotness is a combination of being a tall blond and British accent.
She only teaches you the basic mineral and expects you know a lot of stuff for the exam. Her exams are 11 pages long.

Teaches at the middle/high school level, and assumes that her students have no experience in intellectual thinking. Also, she and her TAs believe that there is only one way to interpret text, and thus only one correct essay format. And she is unresponsive to student feedback. Hands down worst professor/class at Cornell.

This class could have been so much better, but at least some of the major medical ethics topics were covered.  Essayscommentaries were graded difficultly, and too many lectures were simply students talking in groups, in a lecture hall.

Bioethics. Erin Taylor is incredible. Her lectures are very clear, the workload is not overwhelming, and the class discussions are very useful and engaging. She is very passionate and makes other students feel that way too. Also, she's really easy to talk to.

Her lectures are appropriate for middle/high school level courses. Also, she uses outdated data so nothing you learn is relevant. She is not open to students' opinions and is very unhelpful with developing ideas as well. The TA's are very subjective and the assignments are pointless as well.
Admittedly her lecture style is a tad too rudimentary but she's amazing about meeting with students and actually quite smart and lovely in person.

Ethics and Healthcare. Best lecturer I've had at Cornell. She is very clear, organized and coherent.The topics are engaging and contemporary.I recommend this to everyone, especially those who are pre-med/health.

I'm used to assignments with very objective grading and straightforward expectations, so this class threw me off. TALK TO YOUR TA before writing any essay, since each grader for this class expects something different. Readings were relatively interesting, but leave all the interpretation to your TA, or else you'll be "wrong".

Her lectures are at an 8th grade level, despite the intricate nature of the texts and assignments. And I'm pretty sure she misinterprets the texts. Without my TA, I would be lost. And I am certainly bored in class. From what I can tell, everyone else is as well. Hardly anyone comes to lecture, though almost everyone goes to section.

She is an extremely boring lecturer. She says nothing of interests and just repeats the material from the reading. There's no real reason to take her class. If you do, you just have to do the readings for the homework and essays and you'll be fine
Excellent professor - class topics were interesting and the handouts were very helpful. Always made time to talk, even outside of office hours.

Class topics were very interesting but she isn't a great lecturer. Does not keep you engaged and makes the topics less interesting. However, there are only 3 essays and weekly blackboard assignments and no attendance is taken in class or discussion. If you do your own reading you can do well in the class.

Great prof, really went out of her way to help me by providing extra tutoring since I enrolled late in her class.Her voice is a bit soft,so sit close to the front of the class to hear her clearly.Very meticulous in her notes on the blackboard and eager to discuss interesting points of the readings with students.Definitely a class I'd recommend.

I found professor Taylor very clear and helpful in her lectures. We were studying Kantian ethics for about half of the semester and for such difficult material, I though Professor Taylor did an excellent job.

It's VERY hard to hear professor Taylor in lecture and she can be EXTREMELY dry since she waits till class starts to write EVERYthing on the board.  Even the TA's slept in class. She (and the T.A's) are only looking for specific points in each paper and each look for different things, so be sure to talk with YOUR TA. I do not recommend this course!

Seemed like the perfect, easy elective class at first. She doesn't use powerpoint, just sloppy writing on the board. Nothing useful was ever added to the blackboard site. Issues are NOT contemporary, nor presented in an interesting way. Must know how to write a philosophy oriented paper.
No Comments
The nicest teacher you'll have at this school. Incredibly genuine and kind. The readings are excellent, and there are many different options for each essay. Gives great feedback on all essays.

Sophia was incredible. I enjoyed her class a lot. Took this during COVID, and Sophia was super understanding if we had anything going on due to the pandemic. 100% recommend this FWS, take this class!!

She teaches her FWS: Short Stories VERY WELL. I am not even an English major but I would look forward to her class. Not because it was easy or you could sleep through it but because you feel like you can learn without major academic pressure. She ensures that if you put in enough work there isn't any need to worry about the class grade-wise.
Awesome Professor! Always there to help give guidance and support. Take this class...Amazing class...
Tough class but very interesting and Estroff is more than willing to help. One of my favorite professors!

Uses a textbook that is both expensive and essentially useless. An overload of prelims and work. Her notes are useful in some areas but doesn't really help toward exams which are graded extremely harsh.

:) Nicest guy ever. Grades essays kind of hard, but discussion is always very animated, and the students really get to lead it. He's so into the material, it kind of gets you to be interested, too. And he's really, really helpful. Hopefully, he'll get professorship here (he's a grad student now)...

He is a great teacher! I absolutely loved him. Anything he writes on the board you won't need to know, unless you plan on using that material in your essay. If you want him to really like you, talk to him about yempe trees, faeries, and tae kwon do. If you are lucky enough to have his class... enjoy it!! It is one of the best here!

One of the best professor I had. Super passionate and caring. A lot of emphasis on hands-on learning. He's the kind of professor that really cares about your growth and would always try their best to help you. Be ready to use a lot of Python for his assignments.
he's amazing
Monroe is my favorite professor in Cornell, always and forever. He is amazing!
Monroe is GREAT! He is a very busy guy but always ready to help. And he is full of ideas!
Highly recommended
Amazing professor. Makes everything understandable and applicable
AWESOME! super awesome guy, makes it real-life, not just the crap they want you to learn. hands on and really interactive. awesome awesome awesome!
The AguaClara project team was kinda disorganized Fall '08. I'd expected far more leadership and guidance from Professor Weber-Shirk than we actually got.
He definitely makes the class fun and gets you interested in the subject. Lots of hands on work- different from the standard textbook labs which is great.
monroe is awesome, and the class isnt too bad
No Comments
Monroe is the best prof ever!  Lectures were clear, and he makes engineering look like fun.
Great experience building the water-filtration plant.  Very easy to talk to about class, engineering, life, whatever.  Usually entertaining lectures, if a bit repetitive of some common knowledge.
Great guy, he really *loves* teaching.  He has an extremely clear lecture and a great method of teaching.  He made fluid dynamics clear and easy!
Monroe is an amazing teacher who loves what he does.  I would take any class that he teaches.
His smile looks like this: =D
Monroe is awesome.  He loves what he is doing and makes you interested in it too.  This class was really hands-on and a great class to take.

Very cool professor.  Really passionate about his work and enviornmental issues.  Made class a lot of fun and very friendly with students.  113 was pretty easy and the water treatment plant competition was a lot of fun.
Monroe is cool. :)

Very out of touch professor. Frequently went on tangents about his business not in a real world example way more of a disconnected interjection. No feedback or grades are given back to students on HW despite this being one of the grading factors ? Midterm had an average at about 45%. Very disorganized course.
test

Nice guy, but severely overestimates the intelligence of the students in his class. The first 1/2 is just as difficult as any Cornell ECE class, but after the midterm (average was a 45%) he just starts going off on complicated, real-world topics that he personally works with and nobody has any clue what's happening. Final project(s) are super hard.

an absolute genius in his field.  Started his own business on the side and is killin' it.  He's taught this class for many years, and knows just how to teach the fundamentals.  Highly recommended.  He's also just a great guy.  thumbs up.
Superb professor, arguably the best in ECE.  I cannot recommend this professor enough, you will not be disappointed taking his class.

This guy is awesome.  One of the easiest professors in the department because he cuts out the junk and effectively teaches you what you need to know.  He is also extremely helpful and has tons of office hours at useful times (like late at night).
Unbelievably smart, an expert in his field.  Taking a class with Prof. Chiang was a great experience - learned so much about power systems and about engineering and business in general.

Easily one of best professors in the department. He is clearly a genius when it comes to his work in Power Systems. Teaches the course well and cuts all the b.s. out of it. Makes great effort to help his students. Definitely a great undergrad course. Highly recommend.
One of a kind. Challenging in every respect.
the class is a disaster!
Intellectually challenging. His knowledge has no boundaries. Counfounds the mind but warms the hearts.

Saetti is a great instructor, I had him for flight dynamics. Lectures are a bit heavy, but he gives great examples which makes the lecture interesting. Homework and tests are similar to the examples and notes given in class. I wish others are as nice and as caring as he is.
VAGUE unfair grading
Great professor for second semester intro to Italian. Clear, funny, and caring. Highly recommend, he absolutely loves his students.

I enjoyed Professor Taccheri's approach to teaching Intro Italian. I've never taken Italian before, and I was a complete newbie. His approach was clear, and he genuinely cares for his students. I, a newbie, was inspired to pick up an Italian minor because he made me love the language!

Lots of homework, but very simple homework. The first part of the semester was easy and comfortable, and then all of a sudden we were supposed to be fluent it feels. Its a lot of memorization, but make flashcards over everything and just study them all the time, its stressful, but if you study before the class, youll do great.

Such a good and fun teacher, makes it very easy to get higher grades with extra credit and curves.  Wants you to succeed.  Participation is graded, tons of homework (mostly busywork).  Very active teacher during class, so funny, super fun class honestly.
You need to participate in class and turn in homework

Professor Taccheri is an amazing professor. He calls on everyone every class so make sure to pay attention. Many tests but if you do the daily homework assignments you will be fine. He also offers extra credit at the end. He makes his lectures interesting by talking about his life in Rome. Would 100% take again!

I took professor Taccheri's Italian Cinema course and it was by far the best course I took in college. He was my professor since MLIT 101 and the reason why I decided to second major in Italian. He will make sure you learn Italian, prepares you for Rome, and guides you on how to do well on his class and exams. He is glad to help outside of class.
Umberto is a great professor but he assigns a lot of homework. He talks a lot about his life in Italy which is very inspiring. Very nice man.

Taccheri is by far one of the best teachers I had at Saint Mary's. He will go out of his way to help you, participation and homework are keys in his class, however, if you do the work, you are good to go. He knows his stuff and makes learning Italian really fun.

He is a very caring prof who loves Italy and everything about it! He was always available outside of class which made it easy to ask question when homework got confusing. Assigns a lot of homework but never takes a lot of time (just make sure to set aside time so you can correct it before class). I 100% recommend taking his class!

Dr Taccheri really cares about every student passing. He is organized and always prepared. He is incredibly respectful and understands that learning a language isn't easy. He assigns daily homework but it is genuinely useful and necessary to get enough practice in a foreign language.

Umberto is an amazing teacher who truly cares about the success of his students. This class is an easy A as long as you pay attention and participate in class and keep up with homework. He is flexible and understanding if you are struggling.
He is a great teacher, always helpful. You do have to participate and the tests are hard but totally worth it if you are planning to go to Rome. In my opinion best Italian teach at Saint Mary's

He's a very kind, positive teacher. His english is very good, especially for someone who learned english so late in his life. There is homework every day, but it's very manageable. If you make an effort to understand the language, the A is yours for the taking.
He makes this class is harder than the other professors make it. It wasnt all that bad, but if you don't know what you are doing, he calls you out a lot. You should do alright, just really try.
Great professor, very funny and willing to work with you. Class is MUCH harder than Morse and Checca's intro classes but very much prepares you for Rome.
Not a bad Italian teacher. A little unclear at times but not too bad. He lets you know what's on the tests and they're not too hard. I learned Italian so he did something right.

Prof Ciri is very knowledgeable in this course. The material seemed a little complicated but he was able to explain each concept thoroughly as best he could. If you are stuck, then hell help you out on what youre confused on. Not a lot of HW but they can help you prepare for exams.

I am going to be honest and say that I don't agree with what these other reviewers have said about this class and this professor. This professor does not know how to teach at all and I was struggling this whole semester on this class. If you can please take someone else and stay away!!!
Pretty straight forward class. The homework is helpful. The test are very similar problems to the homework. He is always there is help the students and is open to questions during the lectures.

Ciri tends to read his slides a bit but he is very open to students asking questions. Homework was very reasonable and much less conceptual than other fluids courses. I actually felt that I was able to learn the fundamentals of fluid mechanics. With some practice he has on track to become a great professor.
Teaching was a bit obtuse, doesn't have a innate skill for teaching. Just reads off the slide and doesn't have too many examples that he works out.
Engaging lecturer, but sometimes disorganized. Only two papers, a midterm, and take home final. Exams were very easy.

Very easy class. Though the readings were long, most people (including myself) never did them and still did fine. Grades consisted of three larger papers and a few shorter responses, as well as showing up to class. Graded fairly, was always more than willing to help, and gave many extra credit opportunities. SUCH a nice and chill professor

Prof. Haenni is a very good teacher who you definitely should take a course with if you're interested in film. She knows a lot and has interesting things to say. Her class is also structured and graded nicely. She is very disorganized though, but if you don't mind that, it's not a problem. Highly recommended!

Sabine is a great teacher and you'll learn a lot and she can keep you engage for a long course. If you want to learn about film definitely take a course with her. The only thing is she is really disorganized and changed the grading scale in some ways.

If you're interested in learning about film, definitely take this class. Sabine is very enthusiastic about the subject, and extremely approachable. Lectures and discussion involve deep analysis of certain scenes, but also the history of Hollywood, filmic techniques, etc.
