Knows a ton about film but she never stops talking.  We would watch a two minute video clip, and then she would talk about it for ten minutes.

Sabine is easily one of the best profs at Cornell. Her excitement for film is overflowing, and her selections of films is always diverse. She pushes you on an individual basis (most of the grade consists of individual projects) but it's well-worth it.
No Comments

Most enthusiastic and warm prof I've had at Cornell! Really knows her stuff and her excitement is contagious. Interested in students' ideas and facilitates discussion. Even brings in snacks! Really cares about students. Gives constructive comments on papers, and is always willing to meet w you to talk about anything. Definitely a kid at heart.

Sabine is amazing! She is the best professor I've ever had. She is always willing to help her students and is extremely knowledgeable, but is still very open to student's comments and ideas. She is very fair and does not play favorites to the extent that she even calls on the unprepared students if they raise their hands and doesn't ridicule them.

While she does encourage open discussion, she will actively discriminate between film majors and non film majors.She calls on predominantly film majors to carry on class discussion and this becomes highly infuriating for a non-film major like myself.Participation is 20% of grade but she will not allow you to participate if you are not a film major.
Sabine is great; passionate about her subject and knows a ton about it. I highly recommend FILM 276...
I absolutely loved Sabine.  She is a super-smart, super-nice lady who encourages lots of open discussion in class but still manages to keep it relevant.  Great lady!

Sabine's class was interesting, although I sometimes found some of her ideas on the films to be a little odd, she had a wealth of knowledge.  She was also EXTREMELY helpful in every aspect, and took the time to sit and talk with me outside of class.

Prof. Haenni loves teaching film and it came through during class discussions, which were largely student-directed. She listens to students, is very receptive to their ideas, and tries to engage everybody. This was a great class.

incredibly enriching and enjoyable.  Sabine at first seems aloof, but she ends up being very personable, and willing to meet with all her students.  she is fair and flexible, and full of knowledge.  Definitely take this class if you like film.
The grade on the final was literally a D, but he did not curve it. Very unclear instructions for every essay with no fair rubric and pretty subjective grading as well.

Professor Friedman is the biggest yapper teacher I've ever had. Not only did he extensively talk about not so important topics during lecture but he also did not reflect that in his powerpoints, having 4 slides of 3 bullet points at most for a 50 minute class. His Quiz was very reasonable but his final exam was A JOKE. 0/10

Friedman's class was very fair other than the final. You're seeing all these bad reviews because he'd created an unconventional final exam, but overall he wasn't bad. He was a good lecturer, and was one of the few that explained and never read off the slides. If you did well on the papers, and ace the prelim (easy), there's no reason to complain

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Lectures are not helpful at all, especially for an impossible final with a 68% average and no curve. Maybe spend more time on the classes you're teaching than joining the encampment that's supporting terrorism.
No rubrics for his papers, boring lectures with minimal information on slides, and is inconsiderate to students. However, if you pay attention and study for the final, you will do well.
No no no.

Had Friedman for ICL 2350 and ILRID 1530. Made a super hard final for 1530 and one that seemed easy for 2350, but was graded very harshly. Barley puts anything on the slides so hard to follow along. Don't take!

Ok until the end of semester -- created an incredibly detail heavy final that was only 15 questions long 3 days before the final -- scheduled a test review at 10pm the day before the final and EXPLICITLY told students that the exam was 'not about any specific details in the readings' -- the final ONLY tested on obscure parts of the class. Awful.

The professor told his TAs to not give too many As on the papers because he didn't want the class median to be high and then he made the final impossible 10/15 avg. He lied about curving the final. All this to not mention the fact that his lectures were dull and unengaging, at times it felt like he hadn't even looked at his slides before lectures.

Prof Friedman did nothing to engage us with his very boring lectures. At least pose a question or two to the class, instead of yapping about material that will not be on the final exam. 

The final exam was multiple choice, some questions ranged from A-H. Even the current professor of the course pointed out where he went wrong, not a good look....
MISERABLE POS GAVE IMPOSSIBLE EXAM QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS TO PURPOSEFULLY THROW OFF STUDENTS
Implemented an arbitrary negative curve to the first half of graded papers when students scored too highly on the first paper. Final was made on purpose to trick students and even TA's were stunned.

Awful. His lectures have 3 words and when the test comes around he wont give you any notes. All the questions on the final were different than the review session, and 75% of the questions about random statistics in 1 reading that we never discussed. The average for the final was a 65; he refused to curve and didn't release final grades for months.

His structure of the course was completely unreasonable with a final exam that doesn't represent anything relevant from the course. Both TA's and students were blindsided by Friedman's choices and left everyone in an unfair state.

He gave an impossible test that covered specific statistics which were irrelevant to the broader concepts of the course. The average of the exam was a 68% which he decided not to curve, citing the class average of a B+ to somehow justify the final. The people who did well guessed and the people who knew the content likely failed.

Professor Friedman's made it incredibly difficult to do well in his class - the slides have few words and difficult-to-understand concepts are never fully explained or reinforced during lecture. No detailed rubric is provided for either writing assignment. The final exam was 15 vaguely-worded multiple choice questions with up to 8 answer choices.

Got mad everyone did well on the first paper and added in a criteria AFTER we submitted so no one could get 100. Made the final the most insanely hard exam anyone has ever seen in their whole lives. Finalized it the night before too we took it. The median average for my section's final was 10.4/15!! 69%. Petty.

Although Friedman was unpopular because of the final, I thought he was great. Very interesting material and great lectures (you have to really listen though because the slides are pretty blank). Essays were really fun and midterm was extremely easy. The final wasn't great but not as bad as people say. I disagree that he's rude/unprofessional

He is an intelligent professor who not only has detailed lectures and cares about his students, but works with them if they are struggling so they can succeed too. Although I liked him and his lectures, it was a bit difficult to study for exams and write essays because his slides were somewhat general, and he did not provide his TAs with rubrics.

Multiple choice final that goes up to option H thats worth a quarter of our grade is absurd. This guy is also very disrespectful to students to the extent that he doesn't even acknowledge our presence when we simply say hi to him. Tests involve material he didnt teach

He knows what he's talking about but is probably better for higher level courses. He clearly did not care about this class and made no efforts to connect with students. He seems to want students to fail and he through very hard working TAs under the bus.

Friedman is an unnecessarily disrespectful professor. He is arrogant and rude to students. His exam reviews do not prepare you for his tests. He has intentionally made exams different from what he tells you to review for just to bring grades down. He should not be teaching intro classes.

Professor Friedman repeatedly showed the lack of effort he put into this course. His lecture slides were very lazy and hard to follow. He did not give TAs rubrics for essays until after they were due, harming students who sought help. With only 15 questions, the final exam focused on minute details from lecture slides and readings.

Was not my teaching style, had no words on the slide and gave no rubrics when grading essays so we had no idea what he wanted us to write about. Also the final exam was 15 questions (25% or grade) all with 5-8 answer choices on things we did not talk about in lecture. I was very prepared for the exam based on lectures but I think I failed.

Never before today have I been moved to write a negative review here. Professor Friedman purposefully wrote an incredibly confusing final. On top of his reputation for being rude and unprofessional, he failed to plan ahead to create a fair grade average in the class. To artificially lower the average, he wrote the final incredibly poorly.

His lectures gave me chills and I found his module the most compelling and easiest of the 4 (though I don't know my grade on the last one yet). Lecture is not mandatory but go, well worth your time and his slides are only a few short bullet points and a some pictures for an an hour and 15 minute lecture.

Very knowledgeable about Chinese affairs and an amazing lecturer. Attendance is not mandatory but you should show up to class since his slides are very simple (sometimes only pictures). You will also learn a lot more if you participate in discussions on the readings and current Chinese affairs, but in-class participation is not graded.

I absolutely loved Friedman's lectures, but outside of class, I thought he was a bit of a jerk. He acted like he was above everyone. He also had a really unfair late policy for the take-home where he took 2% off regardless of when you turned it in and marked people later who submitted exactly on time.

Have to be in person for the lectures to do well on the module exam but it's worth it. He is a very compelling lecturer and one of the best professors in the class. Ties lectures to present day current events making it even more interesting. Also, the module exam wasn't too hard.
Great professor, knowledgeable, you will learn a lot

Best class I've taken at Cornell - you'll learn so much. Engaging lectures, take lots of notes & do all the readings. 2 reading quizzes and one final paper, very manageable to do well. Mandatory attendance & participating. Great teacher & researcher, presents information in an engaging & accessible way. Take this class!

Taken online. The prof is a smart guy but lecture is pretty boring. There isn't any work except for a few short reflections and a final paper. A bit hard to follow if you don't know anything about China but you can still get by. This class won't blow you away but there's nothing to hate about it. Grading seemed pretty lenient.

Shame for Cornell to have such a professor who cannot think logically nor incorporate any quantitative data into the context, but rather only good at blaming China to appease to his masters for grants.
such a cool guy and brings a really interesting perspective. Ive taken two classes with him and one of the best/ most relatable profs in ILR

Took Friedman for a writing seminar and loved it. By far, the brightest prof I've had in ILR , and a cool guy too. Really knows his stuff. Serious on attendance and participation, read the material and give thoughtful answers. He's a fair grader, not harsh but not easy, go to his office hours and get feedback. I would absolutely take him again!
Amazing professor, very clear, informative, and engaging. Every lecture is well presented. I wouldn't pass up an opportunity to take a class with him. I've learned so much.

Very into his own research work, but is also too pompous in that regard. The grading is too harsh and he does not really understand East Asian labor at all. He thinks he's rather superior to his students and the people he studies

Chinese labor.  Very informed guy that has done research in China about workers and speaks the language too.  Need to do readings and had 3 quizzes with a final research paper. Class attendance is required (signin sheet) and participate and ask THOUGHTFUL question.  I think he has a good BS meter, and it might hurt you.  Very knowledgeable!

One of my favorite professor! He is so helpful with my class, and I was so impressed by his way of solving problems. Other students and I always ask him problems right after the class, and he always stays 20 minutes or 30 minutes later to answer our problems. His homework is tough, but his tests is not hard at all.

Wonderful professor. Occasionally lectures seem off topic, but if you go the extra mile to understand them you get the chance to see something really beautiful. Not so good at arithmetic (what kind of self-respecting mathematician is?), but gives fantastic geometric views of the material. He's also quite friendly! Best of  luck at IC Dr. Marshall!

The class is super hard, and requires a lot of work, but Prof. Marshall's lectures are very clear. He's also pretty funny. I just wish they hadn't been 8am lectures, because if you miss class, the course will get much harder than it needs to be and work will most definitely pile up.

Marshall clearly cares and as such prepares pretty good lectures, especially for a Math professor. Lecturers for the same class didn't feel as adequate at explaining ideas. Marshall is willing to help and is very approachable.

I was really grateful for this class and am glad I found out about Roger. I was so busy this last sem and his class allowed me to get so much done! There really are no expectations. Just take it and get your A. The benefit for you is extra breathing room in your schedule to focus on actual subjects and a free Gpa boost. Works for me!
This class saved me. Roger is a blessing. I would've never graduated without his class. It allowed me to accomplish so much.
Roger is the perfect professor. He is selfless and only wants to educate you. He is so so helpful!!

Roger is my favorite professor because of the way he engages me in the classroom and the way he facilitates a safe space for discussion. He makes me feel like I'm doing well and improving. His feedback on my essays is generous and helpful. The poetry he assigns is fantastic and rich. I only wish he assigned a little more reading.

Amazing! I loved his style of teaching. He allows students to really develop their ideas about the content through open discussion. 

We even met his dog! and discussed our book outside on the grass. What I loved most was the chosen material. I found myself laughing and weirded out sometimes but it was difficult to put the material down.

Professor Gilbert is clear with instructions and deadlines. The assignments required a good amount of reading, but he does not ask for too much from students and gives thorough and helpful feedback. The reading assignments were pretty interesting but could have been a bit more varied regarding themes. Easy to reach and quick to respond.

Very boring and probably not the best value. The prof added little the conversation, and most of the students weren't taking it seriously. It reminded me of my high school study hall. E-Z way to get credit if you're just looking to zone out, get other hw done, or hide in the bathroom.

He's very similar to Tom Hill. You won't learn anything at all, and you can count on getting an A without doing any reading, ever participating, or even attending class. Intellectually, his class is terrible. If you're just looking for credit, however, it's fine. He's too anxious to talk back to or correct students. He mostly just keeps quiet

Professor Gilbert is great. You can tell how much he loves what he studies and he gets so excited teaching it. He assigns a lot of readings but I thought they were all interesting at least. Definitely graded the papers harder than I expected but gave enough feedback to be constructive.
Not the most animated, but still clear and fair. I have much more appreciation for poetry now that I have the patience to understand it. I've even tried writing my own...
Overall a good teacher, especially considering all the trouble I made him put up with last semester, being the wild/rowdy freshmen of the bunch.
I love his sweaters.  And what can I say--he is hot, hot, HOT.
belittles poets by finding them "cute"or "funny"; seems unprepared for class and claims not to understand john berryman as if that is berryman's fault
Easy to get into contact with. Such an interesting and intellectual guy. You know you're in the presence of a great person and scholar.
He's incredibly talented.

He's very non-elitist (I'm not classically-trained) and prioritizes accessibility, is very empathetic and cares for individuals, and is knowledgeable enough to make accessible obscure schemas and 18th-century music terms. he's also interesting, buoyant, and injects life into what is otherwise distant. Solid human being great lecturer

This gentle man is a master of British humor, a fan of Mozart, and just a good pianist. His vocabulary is astounding. Very approachable and respects your input. Never condescending at all. He makes learning about classical schemas much less painful. Oh, and he teaches well too. I honestly can't ask for more.
GREAT PROFESSOR! He was really helpful - all you need to do is hit him up with an email and he's there to help you.
Awesome British accent! He makes class really fun and engaging and always very approachable and nice to students. Definitely one of the best Cornell professors.

Awesome professor, witty and engaging. He is one of those extremely intellectual people that sometimes use words no one uses in conversation, but he comes across as friendly, not egotistical. Material for this class can be boring at times, but his always makes it seem interesting and relevant.  Take a class with this guy if at all possible.

Professor Loring was a really good lecturer and the material he went over in class matched up nicely with the topics on exams. The workload was manageable, and although the material was hard, he taught well. He was really helpful during office hours and I enjoyed this class.

Best organized professor I've ever had. He explained things clearly and excelled especially at teaching one-on-one in office hours with a socratic method. The content can sometimes be dry. Take good notes during class, try hard on the problem sets (go to office hours if you need!), and you'll ace the tests. Very reasonable course.

A really amazing course. Loring was very organized and receptive. He was one of the best professors I have ever had. Quantum mechanics is difficult and mind-blowing (the perfect combination, truly!). Take advantage of all of the extra help available.

He makes the class extremely difficult. While his lectures are interesting and he is clearly a very smart guy, his homework questions come out of nowhere and it is impossible to do the homework without spending countless hours in office hours. The TAs are willing to help, but it takes forever to even get help because there are so many people in OH.
One of the best classes I've ever taken, and it wasn't even very useful for my major

Class is really hard, but he prepares you well. Homeworks often take upwards of 5 hours bare minimum. Speaking from experience, prelims are sort of similar year to year so you can get some insight from previous prelims, but the best way is definitely to do a lot of practice problems.

Loring goes through the material so clearly and knows his stuff. Material is insanely hard that you will get lost but the homework tries to reinforce the key points though it will take you hours (or days). Tests are challenging but fair and tests concept, almost zero memorization.
Very organized and clear. Kept the focus on the important stuff and elucidated it using excellent HW questions. Cannot ask more from an instructor.

Professor Loring is an incredible communicator. Lectures were the best I've had so far. Even though the class was very difficult and tests very hard, there was rarely anything unreasonable or pointless memorization.    It was a true blessing that he taught the course. I'd love to  have Loring for every Chem class

He knows his material like the back of his hand, AND he knows how to teach with a clarity and precision that not many professors can achieve. He's very easy to get along with and extremely helpful during office hours. He's definitely someone you should get to know if you're a ChemE or Chem major.
Professor Loring is awesome. He knows how to make even the most complicated topics at least palatable and interesting. He's one of the smartest professors I've had. You're lucky if you have him.
clear but boring

He's boring in lecture. Once I asked him a question after class, but he'd rather us ask these to our recitation T.A. Do HW problems by yourself (without copying someone else's). Tests were somewhat hard. Read book. Practice as many HW problems as you can.
great professor.  really nice, really good at what he does.

Professor Loring is such a short and adorable old man. I LOVED his lectures. I mean, I didn't even like chemistry that much, but his lectures were too intriguing. His tests were fair too. I also enjoyed how he made side chemistry jokes.. and no one laughed (except my chuckle of course, that no one heard), but those were funny.
Gives very fluid lectures that are well-organized and relatively clear.  Tests are certainly challenging, but they're not unfairly difficult.

His half of the semester was infinitely easier than Crane's , and he was a clear and informative lecturer. But if you ever went to office hours, you would want to punch the guy because he is one of those people who flaunts how much smarter he is than you. Also he never really answers your questions because then he might be "giving away the answer."
Clear Lecturer, nothing unexpected.  go to class and know everything he writes on the board.  Far less difficult than other premed classes
Very clear and organized in his lectures. Exams are fair and accurately reflect the problem sets and old exams. Much better than Crane

Presents the material clearly & methodically (unlike Crane), though i could just read it in the textbook. like someone else said, if you can do the p.sets on your own, you're golden for the exams. Nothing he does makes/breaks you in the class.

CHEM 207 is really not as difficult as most people/pre-meds make it out to be.  Loring is a very good professor and very clear on what you need to know.  People have said he's mean to them when they ask questions, yet I'd be mean too if someone handed me a problem set without any writing on it for help.  If you make an effort, he'll help you a lot.
He's very clear, he tells you what to expect for the prelims

Good teacher.  Wrote and spoke clearly, unlike Crane.  The exams aren't ridiculous, so if you do the problem sets and readings you'll be fine.  Not a bad class, but I'm just not too fond of chem in general.
Not a horrible class but not one that I would want to take again.
Although very informative, his lectures were boring. He didn't seem to cover the material well enough to just learn from them. Do the readings ahead of time!
No Comments

I learned so much from Dr. B this past semester and would recommend this class to anyone interested in the US Health Care System.  TA's wrote Takenote, as well as the quizes, midterm and final, and graded all assignments.  Invest in Takenote, forget the book (unless you want more depth), and you should do just fine.  Overall, great class!

Class was easy to pass, but hard to attend.  Prof. Battistella lectures with no apparent plan or coherent thought.  Quizzes are easy if you do the supplemental reading, but the textbook is incredibly boring.

Professor Batistella knows so much about the US health care structure today.  It's amazing that any one person can be so up to date with the material.  He's so friendly.  But his lectures are a little all over the place.  Questions about exams and gradings should go to the TAs since they wrote and graded all the exams.
No Comments

Material is interesting. Prof is a bit flaky. His lecture notes are all over the place. TakeNote saved me. TAs grade everything. Prof is always willing to help if you approach him or just sit and have a discussion. Cool guy.

Roger is one of the best teachers I've had. A real visionary in the field & completely on top of all emerging trends. No one knows the healthcare industry better than Dr. Batistella. Insofar as his class, if you like the McNeil Report then you'll do fine in his class.

Prof. B really knows his stuff. His material is always up to date so you learn all the relevant things about today's health care system. If you pay attention in class, the quizzes/exams are a breeze. The subject matter is always interesting and he MAKES it interesting.
awesome prof! :D

Super nice and caring prof, put in the work and show that you care and the prof will be super nice and helpful. Accessible outside of class & loves meeting with students to talk out ideas. A LOT of work and reading, the content is interesting but the workload is extreme for a 3cred course (many indicated this in eval's so workload may be decreased)

Took this class for a distribution requirement for Arts & Sciences. Would never recommend this professor to anyone. My participation grade was completely inaccurate and we were told final grades were "non-negotiable." Instructor made me feel extremely uncomfortable when discussing grades or anything regarding this class.

Ashley is the best professor I’ve had at Cornell. She’s very relaxed and class is a nice atmosphere and the time passes quickly. She also encouraged me and made me feel confident in my writing for the first time whereas teachers in high school would only criticize.

Ashley is the best teacher Ive had at Cornell. Ill never look at reading the same way after taking her class. She starts from ground zero on how to analyze stories and then shows you how to use the various narrative elements as a springboard to write your own story. The only class this semester I actually enjoyed attending.

Its early on in the semester but every class has been awesome. Im excited for the rest of the course. She breaks down the readings in a way that will sort of blow your mind. Shes also super hot and funny so that doesnt hurt either.

I absolutely loved coming to this class. Ashley is so caring and so funny. She makes you look at reading in a whole new way. She also teaches you actual strategies to get better at writing. The course isnt demanding per se but she makes you want to work hard and give her your best. I wish I could take it again!

Ive learned so much from this class. Ive liked reading and writing at a young age but at high school, English classes have been taught in a way that discourages that. Hand is caring and passionate about writing. Her class is a breath of fresh air. You will learn to become a much better writer in this class.

Ashley is one of the most caring profs at Cornell. Her prompts are broad, so you're really able to run with the assignments and do what you want with them to make it your best work. You'll get out of this class as much as you put into it. Ashley made me view literature in an entirely new and exciting way, and I'll forever have this class to thank.

Hands down the best teacher I've had at Cornell. You're lucky if you get into her section -- the class is pretty easy, but it's memorable and makes you look at the world differently. Assignments are pretty open-ended. Lots of freedom to do what you want!

She is so unbelievably kind, you can tell she actually cares about you as a person. I do find myself spending a lot of time on the assignments. The instructions can be sort of complex but she's a forgiving grader as long as you put in effort. It does take a while to get your papers back, but she gives great comments and is really encouraging.
She's charismatic and kind and keeps class interesting. Favorite prof so far.

Professor Fahey is incredible and easily one of my favorite professors I've had at Cornell. He's super passionate, and his deep wealth of knowledge is clearly built from years of staying up-to-date with the literature, not to mention his own research. Definitely go to lecture, you won't get much from the slides alone. The lab portion was super fun.

Knows his stuff, but bad with technology which hampered covid semester. The lecture was entirely just listening to him with PowerPoint visuals (no text on ppt), sounds like you are listening to NPR podcast + hard to take notes. But interesting material, not difficult class so long as you listen to the lectures and do the weekly homework question.

Best professor I had at Cornell. Forest Ecology was incredible. The field trips we went on to the White Mountains and the Adirondacks were memorable and educational. I agree with the commentor who said: "some people just don't get his genius." Compassionate, intelligent, and hilarious human.  You do have to work for your grade.
I did not learn anything from the lecture. The discussion sections were somewhat interesting, but overall not an enriching experience.
Not the most exciting teacher, but not a bad guy. Has a very standard lecture style but leaned towards the boring side. Class was too easy and didn't teach me that much.

By FAR one of the most intelligent people I have ever met!Being exposed to his seemingly endless knowledge in the topic of ecosystems is something I will cherish for life.Tests were hard.Lectures were not mandatory,but if you want to Ace this class, don?t miss one.Some people just don't "get" his genius, but i guess we can't all be rockstars.
Awsome guy with a great sense of humor. Easily one of my favorite professors

Fahey was my favorite prof at cornell. The material was really basic, but they way he lectured made it my favorite class.  Very rhetorical and thought provoking.  You'll probably get low grades on essays, but it's not a good predictor of your final grade.  talk in section and you'll be fine. Take this class if you can!!

awesome person, but fails as a lecturer. attendence in class is largely due to pop quizzes. otherwise, i doubt very many people would come. cross your fingers that you get one of the few easy essay graders. otherwise, prepare yourself for extremely low grades on your essays. i got the highest grades in my section with an average of B+ on the essays
Such a waste of time. Fahey's knowledge is rather limited. To quote a poem written about Titanic is a bit too extreme. If you put minimal effort, getting at least an A- should be really easy.

He's a little eccentric, but it's good clean fun. Quizzes not as difficult as they're made to seem. Protip: half the class leaves early after quizzes, so do yourself a favor and explain your answer. Gripe: TA paper grading scheme. Few good grades. I got an "A" and to be honest, while my papers were awesome, I was a lil surprised I got it.

Fahey is the best professor I've had at Cornell! The only bad thing about this class is that people take it to fulfill a science requirement, so some of them are a little dim/uninterested. Any bad ratings are clearly because the person was confused by the brilliance that is Tim Fahey.
Simply terrible

While there is no doubt that he tries to get students to care about the environment, outside of class, he is not helpful at all. His quizzes are ridiculously specific; only 2 came from the book, the other 10 from his rather boring lectures. In my section, only 1 person got A's on the research papers. An okay course at best.
my hero, who else does a jig in class!!! KEEP ON ROCKING IN THE FREE WORLD! AINT NO POWER LIKE THE POWER OF THE PEOPLE CUZ THE POWER OF THE PEOPLE DONT STOP!

The first few lectures grabbed your attention, but after that, it was a spread out semester of different environmental issues, which in itself is boring.  Fahey does an alright job presenting, but he becomes a white noise after awhile.  The quizzes are easy one sentence answers, and you dont really have to pay attention to do well.

Be careful with this class. It seems like an easy A but if you miss a couple of quizes andget a bad TA to grade your papers (which is not the TA you have for section.. makes no sense) you could end up with a B.
Bad & boring

The lectures were really interesting, and you have to go because of the quizzes, but the paper grades are really dependent on your grading TA, who is not your section TA. Mine was horrible and never contacted me when I tried to talk to her about the papers which were graded ridiculously.

The primary reason this class is great is because of the amazingly helpful course coordinator and the TAs. Lectures are extremely boring, but you better pay attention--the quizzes are overly specific. You will also have to write 3 research papers, 6-7 pages each. Office hours? NONE!

Fahey is the best, his lectures are easy to follow without taking notes and there are no tests (just occasional quizzes)...he plays jokes on the class, i.e. pretending to be captured and held for ransom by natives in the Dominican Republic.
Easy way to fulfill science requirement. Lecture is interesting, no real need to take too many notes, and no tests.
Fahey is the man.  If you are not a science major and are required to take a science class, take this one.  It's fun, interesting, and easy.
Fahey's a great man. Hilarious, and definitely knows his stuff! I **highly** recommend any and all of his courses.
Dr. Fahey is the best.
awesome class! easy A with a funny prof who knows his material inside out, lectures are interesting and workload is a breeze, this class is a must take
TAKE IT TAKE IT
He was my advisor and my professor for several classes. I can't say enough nice things about him. Just make sure you stay on his good side.

He was good for the first 2 lectures or so. Afterwards, it was downhill and I couldn't keep awake in any lecture afterwards. The pop quizzes are easy if you take notes. But the big portion of your grade does not depend on lecture material...
Fahey is great.  He's dynamic and fun.  The lectures are truly the best part; everyday is different.  Esp. for non-majors 210 is a must take.
Keeps lectures interesting.  Good class if you have little background in environmental issues.  Sections aren't so great, but lectures are fun.
Awesome class- really interesting- mostly worthwhile for the lab though.  The lectures are hard to follow.  Learning a ton though- Forest Ecology rocks!
A little crazy, but good class
Great class!  Take it...you know you wanna..

Interesting lectures, though they were very biased.  Sections were absolutely useless.  An ironic requirement for the natural resources major, as it's so similar to other department courses that it's really only useful for non-majors.
Class rocks. Take.
Although this course is an easy A, it is comepletey worthless.  The professor spends class time giving a completely one sided view of environmental issues. I did not learn anything.
No Comments
No Comments
I'm glad that we had papers and not finals. He would be kind of hard to follow.
Best professor ever!!!
Really great guy. Classes are always very interesting.

Great class--highly recommended! Tim was great at facilitating discussion, and very knowledgable about ancient history (Achaemenids, Greeks, Macedonians, Romans). He was funny, approachable, and a fair grader. Definitely take a class from him while you're at Cornell!

Tim is the best teacher that I have had at Cornell so far.  He is always willing to help students when they're struggling with papers/coursework, he gives great feedback on papers, and after taking his class, you will become a better writer.  I wish he could teach more of my classes at Cornell.

Tim is an amazing person and professor! He was always there for me when I needed him and gave excellent feedback. He's very approachable and helpful so don't hesitate in asking him for help whenever you need it. He does give pretty long readings, but you can definitely get by discussions by just skimming the readings if you understand the concept.

I really enjoyed taking differential geometry with Professor Healey. I He very much cares about his students a lot. His lectures were very clear and informative.His exams were fair and had the potential of being very challenging, the killer questions were the true/false where he would take off points if you marked the incorrect answer.

Took in SP22. Prof. Healey is an interesting man, clearly passionate about what he teaches. Lectures were occasionally disorganized, and a few too many proofs for my liking. Exams were very fair given what we learned in class. HW assignment were pretty straightforward, and weekly discussion quizzes were easy. Solid prof!
The mustache goat
He is amazing.
He's a gruff sweetheart. Lovely man <3. Compliment his mustache whenever you can.

He's stern on attendance and assigns regular homeworks. The weekly quizzes follow directly from the homework. His exams tend to be on the hard side, but they're all fair. The practice exams, especially for the final, don't match the actual exam. His biggest weakness is too few examples IMO. He has a dated sense of humor that's consistently amusing.

Great teacher. Explains material with ease to the class. He makes Linear Algebra interesting.   The final is worth 40% of the class though, so messing up on that can ruin all the work you put in the class for months.

I love this guy. He's hilarious in a unique way, and he made linear algebra incredibly accessible. He's a little on the quiet speaking side, as he preferred not to use a mic my semester (so sit closer if you can), but he's very thorough and approachable. His lectures were clear and he was always ready to help students. Highly recommended.
An amazing professor. Really got the material across to us effectively, and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. Very funny and helpful too. A first rate prof!
Healey is hilarious. Tough course though but he tries to make it fun. Try to follow him up in the lecture.   he covers a lot
Great Professor

His lectures are clear, crisp, and entertaining. He explains difficult concepts in a way that is easy to understand, and all the while throws in his own hilarious stories about his experiences as an engineer. His tests are challenging but reasonable if you do the homework, study well, and -- like he says -- think it through. Excellent professor.
Even english majors would find his class enjoyable. He is everything you would want a professor to be.

Professor Healey is a fantastic lecturer, is approachable, and always helpful. His lectures offer helpful proofs- enhancing clarity. He's hilarious in general and you can tell that he enjoys teaching this course to engineers.

Healey is amazing! Explains things in a very clear and concise way, while constantly entertaining the class with anecdotes about relevant engineering fields.  Always manages to keep lectures engaging by squeezing in some humor without wasting a minute.

Absolutely amazing! He could explain things in such a way that I understood it immediately. He stayed ahead of the other teachers, but still managed to take time for humor which made me look forward to lecture. The fact that many other students ditched their assigned lecturer to come to Healey's lectures (people sat in the aisles) says it all.
Healey is simply amazing.  Funny, incredibly smart and actually cares about his students.  Loved every second of lecture.
Healey is amazing. He is smart, funny, composed, and clearly very familiar with all material. He is conveys it well. Not the easiest class, but he is a joy to have lecturing.
Fantastic teacher. Crisp, easy to understand, incredibly intelligent and funny. One of the best professors I have ever had.
Best professor I had yet. Teaching is clear and tests are simply a reflection of lectures and hw...nothing unreasonable.
Healey is awesome! He made things a lot more straightforward than any other professor I've had at Cornell. The class gets a lot harder after the first prelim, though.
Tim Healey is THE MAN. End of story.

I took this class my third semester, and am now approaching my fifth. Of all the classes I've taken in the engineering school, Healey is BY FAR the best teacher I've had thus far. He attaches theory to real-world examples, is absolutely brilliant at explaining things, and has a great sense of humour besides. Completely amazing. :)

Healey is a great guy.  I went into this class with a lot of interest in the subject and came out with even greater interest.  He constatntly jokes and tells numerous "back in my day.." stories.  Very helpful in and out of the classroom.  He wants every student to understand what's going on.  Tests aren't bad as long as you do the homework.

Professor Riley is a gem. I took this class to explore proof based math and was enchanted by his enthusiasm and course. Lectures are engaging and rewarding. Homework can be challenging but also rewarding. The two TAs were great. Exams were challenging but the course was curved a bit. Perfect course for intro real analysis and fair rigor.
Good professor, fun class

Relatively low workload as a 4-credit course. Tests are much easier compared to homework sets and past exams. Two lowest homework can be dropped which is great. Good professor but not an interesting class for a non-math major.

He is a funny, personable guy. He's ok as a professor. He spends a lot of time proving things instead of giving concrete examples and applications.  Always willing to help during office hours. For this class, he didn't give in class quizzes and worksheets like the other instructors did, might have been more helpful. Love his accent and hair though.
good

Professor Devoogd class is the reason why im pursuing neuroscience as a career. His class was really interesting to me and I genuinely learned alot. The content is heavy and you need to go to class to pass as it is mostly graded by weekly quizzes. However his teaching style was very clear and he tries his best to make the class engaging

I enjoyed this class, but it is definitely challenging (lots of info and he goes quickly). However, if you attend lectures and the TA review sessions, it is manageable. Overall, he is a sweet and charismatic professor who is very knowledgeable of the subjects he teaches and he does his best to engage students with stories and personal experiences

ATTEND LECTURES!! Devoogd's lectures are super interesting, and it's essential that you go to them. Grades are heavily prelim/final based, and all of the questions will be taken from content/examples discussed in lectures (eg: experiments mentioned, how content pertains to real people/animals...). Readings aren't necessary, but supplement well.

Unclear what would appear on the tests,
extremely touch grader
Doesn't understand how difficult is class is and doesn't respect student's effort. Scale, grading, and extra credit is very unclear

Professor DeVoogd is honestly one of my favorite teachers so far at Cornell. The class is very hard as there is a lot of information, tests are open ended and extremely specific (though you can have a cheat sheet). 78% of ur grade is made up by tests. However, prof is very knowledgeable and sweet, lectures are not too long and are very interesting.

I believe Tim doesn't understand neuropsychology but is able to pull it up so well. You can sense that in his hesitation and slides-over-reliance. Even asking him questions can easily shake him up. Nevertheless, this is a fun class and Tim is able to add his own touch to lectures (almost like any old prof here)

I thought I wouldn't like this class at all but ended up loving it. Tim's tests are entirely lecture-based and I didn't open the textbook once. Also, given that there is no homework, I recommend making some schedule for yourself to study regularly. It doesn't have to be too much but the tests can be really hard if you don't study in advance at all

Professor DeVoogd is an amazing professor. His class is difficult, but it's neuroscience, so you can't expect it to be easy. He's a very sweet professor and cares a lot about his students. You don't have to read the textbook, but attend all lectures because sometimes he puts things on the tests that weren't in the lecture slides.

Never take any class with this professor. The entire grade was determined by 3 exams and two assignments(Worth 12%). You must memorize every minute detail in the class. The averages were 57% and then 69% on the prelims however, the curve in the class is determined by the highest grade achieved, not by the average.  AVOID THIS PROFESSOR.

Class grade is based solely off 3 major tests and one writing assignment. Very rarely responds to email. Promised an extra credit opportunity, students carried out with this, and he never followed up again. Dismissed major cheating violations although this is an entirely curved class.

My best recommendation: don't do all the readings. You will never have time for other things if you do. I suggest taking good lecture notes in the form of questions and studying off of those as well as the reading discussion questions posted on canvas possibly with a study buddy.

I really liked this class, and the textbook was interesting to read. Professor Devoogd knows his stuff. The tests required a lot of detail memorization, which was the main con, but I did enjoy the class overall.

I absolutely loved Professor DeVoogd. Extremely accommodating & the class has weekly quizzes instead of prelims. Each quiz is very detail-oriented but it is only based on the prior week's content so I didn't find it too bad. The final is a cumulative big picture understanding (not too difficult). Offers a lot of Extra Credit. Really nice professor!

I took Psych 3320 with Prof Devoogd. He's extremely knowledgeable about the course material and covers the vast majority of the quiz/final material in the content-heavy lectures. But if you ever need to talk to him, office hours or raising your hand in lecture are really your only shots as he will never acknowledge his emails

Gonna be real frank about this - one of the worst decisions of my life was taking this course. Terribly unclear lectures, incompetent professor, harsh and arbitrary grading, and extremely inconsiderate attitude towards students. Upon contemplating the fact that he is a professor at an Ivy League, I found myself close to a mental breakdown. Disgrace

All jokes aside - worst class you will take at Cornell. Unbelievably incompetent, at times self-contradicting, unclear Professor. Any remotely positive reviews are lying - do not listen to them. Very difficult tests with unanticipated questions. Multiple attempts should be made to get Professor removed from Cornell. Disgrace to Cornell.

Honest review: Hardest class Ive taken at Cornell (Senior, 4.0 GPA). Its honestly shocking to see any positive reviews of the course on here. The class wasnt so difficult because of the material - but because the Professor is extremely unclear & tests have ridiculously unanticipated, specific questions. I dont understand how he is a professor.

This course was fairly straightforward. Tests are all short answer, and they are based almost exclusively on material covered in the lectures (though questions are occasionally ambiguous). You do not really need the textbook. Just study the slides and recordings. For some reason, DeVoogd doesnt always emails, so use office hours if needed.

Weekly short answer quizzes over the lecture material from the previous week, final paper, and long short answer final. Will need prior bio experience since this is a more advanced course with niche material. He cares about students and is good about replying to emails. I didn't do the readings and still did fine.
He gives no information as to what you should focus on for the prelims. The prelim questions are kind of a surprise which makes it all the more difficult since they are all short-answer questions.

The Behavioral Neuroscience (biopsychology) class was all lectures. There was nothing interactive about the entire class; just lectures and then the prelims. The lectures were dry and mostly stuff from the textbook. The syllabus says the textbook is mandatory, but I never had to use it. The prelims are long and many short answer questions.

He is nice person who is passionate and kind. I would not take this class again though bc the 3 exams that make up 90% of your grade are ENTIRELY short answer & he expects ridiculously specific answers without giving clear specificity in the questions.
DeVoogd is an all around great guy. Cares about his students and is very helpful outside of class. You definitely need to work hard, but the resources are there and he wants to help.

I personally feel that this class wasn't as hard as the reviews suggest. Exams make up 90% of final grade. He gave 5% extra credit, which I had 4. GO TO THE LECTURES, or you can in no way figure out how to answer some of the questions. Before exams, memorize his slides carefully, and study the pictures and reviews in the textbook. Median was a B+.

This is an interesting class, but the professor gives no details about what he expects and everything is a surprise. On test, each question is graded separately but no correct answers or feedback is given. He goes on tangents about animals and his research and his friends' research in lecture and tests on small details so pay attention.

Good, interesting and inspiring lectures, which explain the topics well. Attending the lectures is important to score well. Most of the test material is covered in class, and things he teaches in lectures are far more likely to come on the tests than the general stuff in the text, you can probably just study from his power points and do fine.

Impossible tests. Do not take unless you have photographic memory so you can memorize the textbook. Expects essays on short response.  No multiple choice at all. Lectures are too one-dimensional and are really quite useless. His lectures, however, go over small details that somehow show up on the test.

Last sem was the first time Devoogd taught this class, and it was definitely more challenging than I expected. However, if you studied (focusing on what he covered in class and using the book to get the smaller details), you do fine. Extremely helpful at explaining concepts if you can go to his office hours. Doesn't respond to emails very quickly.

I never write reviews. However, I needed to in this case. AVOID THIS CLASS if it's taught by him. Students have no idea about what's going to be on the test. Literally studied like crazy for this class and still got a C- because tests were so random. barely learned from reading the textbook and going to lectures. All around HORRIBLE TEACHER

AVOID THIS CLASS. Does not respond to emails. Lecture slides are vague. First year teaching this class, an INTRO level course. Blackboard has nothing useful, we have 2 "writing assignments" due at our final, NO information has been posted regarding it. Ridiculous amount of content for tests; mix of book & lecture. Class avg is around C-. Miserable.
not helpful, absolutely irresponsible and NEVER responded to any emails - just plain disrespectful. I loved the subject before i took his class, HATED it after!

He is very detail-oriented in his exams.  Be sure you know ALL of the details in order to pass or else you are screwed.  He is a VERY harsh grader.  In his own words "It's easy to get partial credit, but hard to get full credit".  Don't expect full credit unless you write a novel for each question.

I took Tim's class in Biopsychology Lab years ago, and found it truly a great class which taught one about research protocols.  I also had the honor to work with Dr. DeVoogd in his bird lab, it was a great experience. His class inspired me to go on to medical school and pursue a surgical field.  Highly recommmend it.

Awesome guy...great teacher and advisor. He taught me a lot through his class, but it never felt like much work. The brain identification test is hard, though. Really easy to talk to and knows tons. This lab class requires a lot of time, but is sooo worth it.
This was a great class with a great professor.

Probably the best professor I've ever had. I don't know about his lecture course, but the lab course was my favorite class ever! The experiments were really interesting and I learned a lot. He was also very helpful and I don't know what everyone is complaining about because he always responded to my e-mails within hours of when I sent them.

Used lots of overheads which made class very boring, and didn't provide the overheads anywhere else, so if it was blurry, which it often was, or if it was only up for a moment, which was often the case, you missed it.  All of the tests were graded way too subjectively.
Never has real lesson plans...wouldn't take the class if I could do it over again! Not very reliable and doesn't reply to emails. Tests are really hard.
He was my advisor. waited for 3 hours in his office for my PIN, he never showed, then never responded to my emails after that. Hard to find.
really cares about students.  helpful if asked
more than scatterbrained. completely unable to maintain a coherent lesson plan, much less an organized and fulfilling course as a whole.

graded completely on discussion section participation and three 25 question MC canvas quizzes, super light work if you show up to lecture but easy to tank your grade with a few questions wrong. would recommend if you can stay organized and on top of the big lecture topics

Kind man, just very dense lectures that were very easy to get distracted from. Tests were oddly specific, but material mostly came from lectures and interpreting them. What you get is def what you put in

If you can memorize, you can do well in this class. And by memorize I mean be able to explain every tiny detail from the slides. If you took AP bio most of the first half content is review, and some of the second half content. The lectures definitely go fast but they aren't that important. You just have to study the slides and teach yourself.

Took 1350 for the Fall '22 semester. He goes very fast but the lectures themselves weren't too difficult to keep up with. The worst part is the exams - the questions are not straightforward and if you don't know the small 5-10% of the material they ask about, you're screwed. Worst part is he's the better lecturer of the two professors.

He moved through a huge amount of lectures quickly, and didn't explain well what was important to each slide. The prelim and final questions are not straightforward in what they're asking, and requiring an incredible level of understanding of the material to do well.
Lectures go very fast but contents are very clear.

The lectures were well organized and there were lots of supplementary materials available for the class, however sometimes the lectures got a bit boring/monotonous. Make sure you study and have a very in depth knowledge of the course material for the prelims.

This class is very difficult and the professors who teach it do not make it interesting at all. The averages on all the Prelims are failing, however, they do curve. Professor Huffaker was a better lecturer than Professor Tumbar. Lectures move fast

Dr. Huffaker creates great PowerPoint slides and explains them very thoroughly during lecture, making it very important to attend. He is easy to reach outside of class and evens sticks around for a few minutes after lecture to answer questions. He was very accommodating considering COVID, and made sure the course and its material was organized.

I was told this class was a premed weed-out and that is absolutely true. The tests were incredibly hard with a class average around mid 60s. His lectures were clear and well organized. He was very helpful in office hours too. I recommend going every time if you can. There is not a lot of formal homework but doing the readings w notes is essential.

Tim adapted really well to zoom lectures and he's definitely a thorough lecturer. Despite the course's difficulty, Tim's teaching style made it easier for me to understand the material. Definitely need to study hard but that's expected!

Talks quickly and quietly but you get used to it, just sit closer to the front. Tests are very fair and come straight from the lectures. Understand everything from section and from the slides and you'll be good. I read the textbook and found it helpful to review material from lecture, but I know many people who didn't read at all and also did well.

He talks fast in lectures but once you get used to it, you can keep up. His tests are usually fair not too many trick questions and you can get an A if you study hard. Make sure to study every tiny detail though. Everything in the readings are fair game.

All tests are multiple choice. Your final grade with either be determined by the three prelims and final OR two prelims and the final (in this option the final is weighted heavier). Gives you flexibility if you do really bad on a prelim. Have to study outside class but its really well taught.
Solid professor

Lectures are just summaries of the textbook and basically useless if you want to learn everything he might put on the exam. Exam questions are worded painfully. He tries to cram multiple questions into one multiple choice option and includes briefly mentioned information profusely. Study sections, or at least try to.

Huffaker is a bit monotone, but he's by no means a bad teacher. 1350 is a specific class that requires lots of memorization (you can't get around it) but he makes all the information he could possibly test you on readily available in his lecture slides, summaries, and section materials which is all you can ask for. No surprises if you can memorize.

Professor Huffaker is a very knowledgeable lecturer with a contagious passion for biology and its advances! Expect a lot of reading in this class; however, the readings are helpful and interesting. Overall, a fair class with a depth of content that engages yet stays close to the introductory realm.
He is very monotone and talks very fast, it is hard to catch everything he is saying. You need to memorize every little detail in his slides and summary points to do well.

1) His tests make up basically all of your grade, and test questions come from lectures, so try to pay attention in class even though his voice tends to put people to sleep 2) Make sure you know the summaries for all lectures by heart since the curve is brutal 3) Ask him stuff you don't get during office hours because he's very willing to help

If you focus on just straight memorizing, you probably won't do well. But if you actually try to understand the lectures you're memorizing (test questions come straight from the lectures), you'll be fine. It is definitely possible to do well if you put in a lot of work. One problem is that he goes through the material too quickly and is monotone.

The only way you will do well in this class is by memorizing every detail in the lecture notes and slides. Even then, you'll only get the mean grade because he asks some wordy questions. He is incredibly boring, but you have to go to lecture for clicker credit. The material isn't difficult to learn. Only take this class if you have to.

Huffaker is the most monotone person I've ever met. He is older which makes sense how unenthusiastic he is. The class itself is interesting, but it is hard to learn from him. Sometimes he says jokes when he messes up but only the type where people laugh because no one wants to deal with the awkward silence. Hard to stay awake.

"Beware of pop quizzes"  beware of clicker questions from previous lecture's material. He's a good professor in the sense that the test material comes straight from the lectures (or discussions), but sometimes the littlest details make it into the test, like a header on the Powerpoint slide. If you have a photographic memory, this class is easy.

Huffaker is the worst. His tests asked about the tiniest details on his lecture slides that you would only know if you memorized every slide from every lecture. Lectures are incredibly boring and he goes at lightning speed so you can't really keep up anyway. Very rude in office hours too. I've seen him make multiple people cry.

Huffaker is a nice person but his exams are worded in a way that even if you memorize his notes and the textbook, you can still mess up on the questions. Class material isn't too hard but this class seems like one of the hardest to receive a good grade in because of the harsh curve.
great professor, knows his stuff!

Lectures are incredibly fast-paced and his voice is very monotone.  He is one of those teachers who knows what he's talking about but doesn't know how to convey it to students.  The prelims are also placed at the worst of times-- one right after Homecoming weekend, one right after Parent's weekend, and one right before Thanksgiving break.
Great professor and is very clear. But he goes VERY fast and can be boring. If you go to lecture every time and fill in what you didn't understand with the textbook you should be fine.

The material was interesting but the lectures were just really boring. He kind of speaks in a monotone. If you want to get an A, make sure you memorize lots of little details from his lectures. The lecture summaries are helpful.
