A waste of class. Easy A, but lecture notes are useless (spelling errors, contradictory, non-congruent with textbook). Prof can't explain a thing to save her life. Group paper with 5 parts, marking takes weeks, even following the rubric you won't get full marks. Prof will not answer questions before the final, worst prof ever.

Dayuma is by far the absolute worst professor I have EVER had. The amount of effort required for this 200-level is ridiculous. Group participant is worth 30% (just as much as the final). Her lectures are ambiguous and she provides the most abstract of ideas, nothing concrete. Exam questions are poorly worded and misleading. AVOID, AVOID, AVOID!

Dayuma is a nice lady but she seems to be on a bit of a power trip. She expects assignments to be brought to class BEFORE it starts and if you hand it in even 1 minute late she will dock you marks. She is also just not very engaging in her lectures; she tends to ramble on and on unnecessarily. Also just dry course material in general.

Dayuma knows what she is talking about but sometimes spends too much time talking about one simple topic instead of moving on. The textbook is necessary to do well on the test, but they aren't too difficult. Group project is set at a reasonable pace and and the weekly online quizzes are for participation marks which is a nice grade booster.

I took her class for psych 105, she was amazing then. This class, not easy, ambiguous marking criteria, her lectures are useless, MUST read the textbook, as most to all test material is based on this. stuff from her lecture is not fully explained. would not take again, terrible.

I really liked Dayuma - her lectures were fairly interesting and I liked her grading system. It was a bit tough having a 'midterm' a week before the end of classes, but I liked that there were so many different aspects to the course. It forces you to keep up with the class and one bad exam doesn't destroy your grade.
She's not accessible or helpful outside of class, her exams are really unfair, the papers' grading criteria is ambiguous and she is not a very good lecturer (very rambly).

Worst professor I have ever had. Her exams have questions that don't make any sense and don't comply with text. She's also rude in her emails and is unwilling to answer questions. Her lectures are not helpful, dry, and often far behind in the material.

3 midterms, a final, quizzes and participation. It seems like a lot, but it means that the course is very easy to do well in. The lectures are boring, but go for the iclicker participation. If you like developmental psychology take her, she emphasized it a lot.

Avoid at all costs! 3 midterms (10% each) 1 final. In class participation iclicker questions that force you to attend a very useless prof's class. She doesn't teach well, and rants about useless things. Awful marker, and tests have so many parts to them. Sucks at replying to e-mails. Very condescending tone whilst asking for help.

She makes you do online weekly quizzes for every chapter. Each quiz is worth 2%. She has three midterms and a final exam, which include multiple choice, true/false, matching, and definitions. She uses iClicker to measure participation. She likes to ramble which leads her to falls behind and skip topics
Awful prof. Super boring and not a good speaker. Avoid if you can

Class is divided up nicely for marks - easy 10% participation (iclicker), 10% weekly online quizzes,  20% midterm, 15% paper (easy, summarizing journal articles), 15% group paper (fairly easy as well), and 30% cumulative final. Notes are fill-in-the blank which is nice. Interesting topics.

She is a good professor overall- makes class interesting, funny, and pretty clear grading material. Tests are a bit harder than expected but if you go to class and read the textbook, you'll be fine! She grades with both tests and papers so get ready to write.
Expects you to learn all the material before she teaches it. Quizzes every week on the textbook and then teaches the notes after. Does not answer emails, one of the worst i had. Avoid if possible.

Not much point showing up to this class as you will likely need to teach yourself the course from the textbook in order to keep up with her quizzes, even though you will likely be far behind that point in the actual class. (ex. quizzes in chapter 14 but only on chapter 12 in lecture) Her time management is also not very good.

She's really nice, the marks in her course are very well distributed between 12 online quizzes (20%), 3 midterms (10% each), iclicker and a final worth 30%. Lectures can get a little boring sometimes but her exams are really easy, so one bare the boring lectures. She has office hours 3 times a week, makes it really easy to get any doubts cleared.

I haven't taken notes in this class. Literally no point. Has 1 or 2 quizzes a week before material is gone over, 3 midterms, participation (only reason to go to class), research participation and final. Way too much to not actually be taught anything by teacher.
Every time I've spoken to her or emailed her she came off as condescending and unwilling to answer questions. It makes it harder to stay motivated to do well in this class.

Can not recommend. She never directly answers questions or explains concepts in her lectures, and instead rambles often about vaguely related examples. She is very unclear about the material that will be tested, and her dry lectures and disorganized notes do not help. There are plenty of other intro psych profs - take literally any other one.

Not an organized speaker. Lectures often conducted in a rambling style, while taking a long time to get to the point. Has online quizzes for chapters ahead of what you have covered in class, which are worded strangely. Very vague in class on what will be tested, but then picks the tiniest minutia from the textbook for her exams. Hard to decipher.

Personally do not understand her style of teaching. Lectures consistently went over class time, yet contained about a third of the actual information being tested on. Weekly quizzes online to test you on your textbook readings before the topic was discussed in class were frustrating and worded difficultly. Would not recommend.

Literally one of the worst profs I've had in 4 years at UofA. He lectures are dry and don't include all the relevant information she tests on. Her notes are unorganized and confusing. Presents slides in class that she doesn't even include in her lecture notes. Overall a VERY unenjoyable course. Avoid if possible

Took the course in the spring. Spent WAY too much class time on lectures to the point where we fell behind 1-2 classes, which is a shame considering the fact that the lecture slides don't cover everything in the textbook. No point in going to class except to fill in the awkwardly placed fill in the blanks on slides. Read the textbook instead.

Hard marker, gives way too much detail in her lectures and it's all from the textbook anyway so it is very hard to stay focused.  She is enthusiastic and seems to know what she is talking about.  But this was a first year course and she marked the assignment like we were in grad school.

loved her, learnt so much in class, attendance only mandatory to keep track of what she testing on onlne quizzes and some questions from inclass, took it in spring  textbook reading necessary to pass, online quizzes 30%, no midterm 2 inclass very easy assignments, 1 brochure project (also easy) and 1 final, read the textbook chapters!!!!

Avoid this professor. I learned more from the textbook. Lecture notes were not helpful, and she spends too much time on minor details and trying to engage the class. The midterms were ridiculously easy, although she throws in pointless questions about minor details. Final was more difficult. Movie assignment is easy but you work in pairs.

I loved learning about developmental psychology with Dayuma!  She is really knowledgable in this field.  All midterms and finals were a walk in the park if you read the textbook and lecture slides.  Finished final in 20 minutes.  Gives you marks for participation.  Marked research proposals fairly and gave good comments.  Easy class with effort.

she is very nice but does not seem to care about t students success. her notes are just an outline of the course they don't go into any detail but her exams are all about the details that she never talked about. the exams will tear you apart. Nice lady but is not made to teach. recommend the class but DEFINITELY NOT her.

Unreasonable course load (2 midterms, final, 2 projects, quizzes everyday) for summer-term, digresses often in lecture, i felt my time was better spent with the textbook. ambiguous marking, all in all would not recommend her as an instructor, tests on very specific aspects of the course without disclosing what her emphasis will be.

Very heavy course load for a 6 week summer course. Hard marker, doesn't explain what she is taking marks off for. While she is very passionate and knowledgeable, I did not enjoy this class. Online quizzes every Mon and Wed, 3 in class reflections, 2 quizzes, 2 projects, and a final. Would not recommend her class.

worst proff. uploads slides 1 hours before class. goes over time. marking is really random and unclear. minimal to no feedback on assignments.   her blanks in her slides are also very awkwardly placed. tests are straight forward. okay lecturer.  Super picky about everything. i would not recommend her... AT ALL.

This prof is very passionate about developmental psychology. Exams are straight forward and easy marks for online assignments. You have to create a research proposal instead of raising an online baby like you get to do in other psych 223 classes which was kinda disappointing!

Ok prof. Exams were easy. You literally get free 15% for attending class and reading the chapters online. A bit nit picky on the assignment marking, but still fair. Gives good feedback if you go to her office. Overall would recommend.
Doesn't seem very knowledgeable and just reads off of her slides (which are just general outlines from the textbook). Seems like a very friendly and nice person however.

Developmental psych in summer. Good lecturer, not boring is nice and knowledgeable. Multiple choice exams super easy, just read the textbook. one essay that was worth a lot, but broken into sections which made it manageable. Lots of group work and presentations every day, TOUGH marker on presentations and anything you hand in.

You are only graded on a few exams and she grades pretty hard. Very helpful that you get a cheat-sheet for exams tho. Try to fit literally all of your notes on the cheat-sheet because her exams are very precise. As attendance is not taken, it is still very important to attend EVERY lecture or else you'll miss out on valuable notes for the exam.

I am rating this professor to describe my frustration with this course. Studying for the exams is almost pointless as the exams feature questions that are beyond any first-time philosophers knowledge and are not described on the courses "study guides". PHIL 170 has failed to prepare us with the depth of knowledge and mindspace for the course.

Lascano's lecture's allowed complicated philosophy to be interesting & accessible. However there are reading quizzes before every lecture, which the material is then gone over after the test is done. The readings are complicated & time consuming, however if you take detailed notes over them, ask questions, and attend the lectures you will be fine!

Before every class, there is a reading and a quiz about the reading due (most readings 10-20 pages). Unit tests had very specific questions. GTAs are very nice and helpful. Discussion grade is a big chunk of your grade, and it is subjective. They do not let you see where your points are in the discussion grade until the end of the semester.

this class was fairly hard, professor lascano is very nice as well as the gtas. this class is tough and test heavy. with each reading theres a test. unit tests are pretty hard as well. each question is very concise and looks into something that could have easily been missed. you have to have very clear understanding in the videos as well.

Had a great experience with Professor Lascano. She is passionate about philosophy and the meaning of life. Nearly all testable material is from readings that are analyzed in lecture. She makes fairly complex philosophy understandable to the beginner. PHIL170 had 3 total tests, 3 total video review assignments, and 2 weekly reading quizzes.

The teacher is nice and all but the lectures are long and the tests are hard. I just wished the material was more clear and concise than it was, then I think my rating would be a lot higher. The GTAs are all really helpful!

This class is hard to say the least. In order to know the content for the tests you have to show up to class where she speeds through slides but never posts them. TAKE NOTES ON YOUR COMPUTER. Get the basic ideas down and utilize your TAs. Theres readings you do before class followed by a quiz on canvas and then she goes over it in class.

while attendance isn't mandatory or recorded, still go because she basically goes over everything needed for the tests. not much variation to work, just quizzes and exams. all mc though, which was nice. also go to ur discussion sections

Great Professor with a passion for Philosophy. With the massive 20-40 page reading materials twice a week, this class would not be ideal for foreign students including me. Professor is competent however, you would learn Philosophy best outside of this class. Grades seems to be based on the TAs emotional judgement and also late responses.

Prof. Lascano was great. If you take this class and genuinely attempt to learn the material you will walk away with a new appreciation for life. The only complaint I have is with the quizzes because the questions are almost always worded in a way that is really confusing, but overall the class with her was great.

I wish I could've enjoyed her class, as the topic was The Meaning of Life. Unfortunately, although you can see her passion for philosophy, her lecturing style will put you to sleep. She doesn't engage with the class, and the discussion sections are uncomfortable because no one really knows what they're doing.

Loved it! Lectures were always super clear and the tests and problem sets correlated strongly. Psets got tougher as the semester went on, but group work is a great solution. If you read the textbook and take good notes on the lectures, you will do very well in this class. Very straightforward, knowledgeable, and responsive professor!

Astro 2212 with Nicholson convinced me I wanted to major in Astronomy. The guy's really been around the block in the field of Astronomy and often brought in guest lecturers who are experts on the topic, and his lectures were great. Grade consisted of 5 psets, the midterm, the final and a presentation on a subject of your choice in the Solar System.

Nice guy. Optional textbook and no reading. Five problem sets made up most of the grade: not hard but takes time to think about the problems, mostly high-school level math with some calc 1. One midterm and canceled the final; a 5-10 paged paper at the end of the course. Cool class; might be too much work if you don't think astronomy is interesting.

This was by far one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. My only critique is that the tests were HARD. If you have a photographic memory you will do amazing on them because you need to memorize all the slides word for word. Homeworks were very easy but tests were very difficult.

Must-take class for anyone interested in healthcare!!! Very informative class and has a nice curve which helps since tests can be tricky. It's also not very much work if you don't do the readings (only one or two true or false questions per test about them).

Professor Nicholson is a pretty decent prof but lacks some empathy for students' situations. The exams are harshly graded, but you can submit regards. Overall, pretty decent class if you show up to lecture and do the readings, but small details matter.

Amazing professor, tests could be hard but understanding the lecture material and demonstrating that knowledge gets you a good grade. Was super close to getting an A but final messed me up. Anyways though prof is really caring and always willing to meet outside class! Highly recommend

Prof. Nicholson is extremely knowledgable and I found it easy to get questions answered in office hours, assuming there weren't too many other students there. Tests are graded very harshly, however, and even if you have a suitable answer, you may not get credit because you don't use the correct stats or you may not have the correct wording.
Amazing lecturer and a great class overall. Prelims are quite tough though.

TAKE THIS COURSE! I don't know how he does it, but Dr. Nicholson somehow condenses the material in a way that makes this Byzantine system understandable. If you go to class, pay attention, and think critically, you'll come out with more than a good grade; you'll come out with lessons you'll take with you for years to come. Best professor ever.
Really nice and engaging lecturer, but the prelims are pretty tough. Otherwise, the homework assignments were relatively easy and you can tell Sean really cares about his students!

Incredible lecturer, easily one of my favorite classes I've taken at Cornell. Class is very lecture heavy, you basically cannot miss one or else you will miss a lot of important info. You have to WORK for tests but they're fairly graded. Rewarding class.

Solid professor. Well-versed in his field, & keeps contact even after semester is over. Curves final grade, not individual prelims. Generous on point-back system, and always wants to get to know his students more. Would definitely take him again.

Dr. Nicholson is a great guy and all, the content of the class is super interesting, but hes just a really bad lecturer. All he does it just ramble on and on during class. Prelims are really strictly graded, you have to hit the keywords in the answer key and literally pull straight from the lecture slides to get full credit.

One of the BEST lecturers I have ever met at Cornell. The content is super interesting and understandable. Tests are open-book and mainly based on lecture slides. Sean is great at explaining things so don't worry if you are confused about anything anytime. Course design is related to current events and very inspirational. 100% recommend!

One of the best classes I've taken at Cornell. Professor Nicholson is not only an excellent, engaging lecturer, but he's also just an amazing person. He was extremely accommodating during Covid/online learning, and made sure we all had the resources the succeed in the class. Assignments were easy and prelims were primarily memorization-based.

One of the best classes Ive taken so far. Exams are memorization heavy, but online it was open note which made them very easy and straightforward. Homework assignments were easy and took little time. Prof Nicholson is super caring and answered many questions despite a huge class. Also got us cinnamon rolls and brought his dogs to office hours!
He is the best prof I have ever met at Cornell. He is chill and gives really good lectures. He really understands his students. You will learn a lot from him seriously. He knows what he's doing.

Such a good professor. Made us cinnamon rolls, includes funny clips during lecture that reinforce points but also are a break up the lectures really well, very understanding with deadlines and timing, willing to adapt the course to covid circumstances, so many good things to say

Prof. Nicholson is a really great guy, very knowledgable, and a fantastic lecturer. The content he teaches is interesting for anyone interested in healthcare. I hear a lot of people say this is an easy class. Don't be fooled, exams can be tricky and the class is curved because of it. You will need to put in some work to do well.

Professor Nicholson is a great lecturer. Everything you need to know is on the slides if you miss anything that he says, because he does go through the material pretty quickly. He includes funny videos from time to time in class that make the class more interesting. He truly wishes to connect with students, which I really like.

Hands down, an amazing professor. His tests can be a little overly specific at times, but they are easy to study for - nothing out of left field - and his teaching style is engaging. He is a professor that is truly excited about what he teaches and you can feel that when he speaks.

Biggest lecture I've ever taken at Cornell, yet Nicholson still made every class engaging, relevant, and interesting. Powerpoints posted online contain all the necessary information, but I went to class anyway because he was that good of a lecturer. Stay on top of lectures and memorize everything for the tests (including graphs) and you'll get an A

Absolutely amazing class. Favorite class of my entire life's academic career. He knows his stuff (he's the director of the MHA program!) and this class actually made me want a career in health admin/policy. It's fun, invigorating, and inspiring. He also takes students to Banfi because he's just a cool, normal dude like that!

Very respected and very good lecturer. Disperses fun yet very relevant videos in his lectures that keep them interesting. But he also basically reads off his slides, and he posts them online, so no need to go. Tests are fairly hard, but the class is curved crazily nicely, so not difficult at all. The 3 assignments are easy 100s as well.

Prof. Nicholson is a great lecturer. He can get side-tracked sometimes, but everything he says always ends up relating back to the material. The exams are almost entirely based off the slides, which is good because the slides are well-organized. He knows what he's talking about and takes time to answer individual questions despite the huge class.

Most people would say this class was "easy," but, for me, I didn't do so well on the exams. You learn A LOT about the U.S. healthcare system overall and little things no one ever knows. Prof. Nicholson shows HILARIOUS videos in class and he is a good lecturer. Would I recommend this class: UM, YES!

Nicholson is the best professor I have ever had. He truly cares about the students and is a brilliant economist. The class is fairly easy, with only three fairly straightforward assignments and three prelims that are very fair in grading. I looked forward to going to class--he makes the dry material very interesting.

Very interesting lectures, unbiased analyses of current events. Easy homework assignments and tests, however TA grading of these can fall short sometimes but Professor Nicholson is very reasonable if you take the time to talk to him.

Everything you need to know are on the slides. The key to doing well in this class is 1) study objectives that he lists in every PPT 2) remember trends 3) memorize ratios. I think his prelims are getting trickier. I took another class of his, and they were straightforward. Questions more thought-provoking now. Write down what he wants to see.

Nicholson is one of the best professors at Cornell. SO precise and clear. Definitely go to lectures. You don't need the books, you don't need to read any of the articles at all. You have 3 Assignments all year, not too bad. And the prelims are very similar to past ones! He's great in office hours too.

Took in the Fall of 2013. He is absolutely fantastic, delivers lecture material in a very clear manner and really wants to get to know students!  The prelims could be a little tricky but overall not too hard of a class. Definitely recommend because this class was one of my favorite classes at Cornell!

Overall the class is very arbitrary, especially when 60% of your grade is based on what decides to give you on prelims and your "class participation" . Overall he is a very tough grader with the average in our class being a B. You come in thinking he's a nice guy but there are easier classes to take for your concentration with a higher mean

Made a very challenging subject, usually taught at graduate level, very digestable to this undergrad. He supports interaction during lecture to clarify key concepts and gives an incredible amount of helpful feedback to every student on weekly assignments and exams. One of the most professional, gracious, and capable professors at this school.

One of the most interesting classes Ive taken at Cornell. It is essential that you thoroughly do all reading homework because she cold calls students in class. This can be stressful at first but is honestly not a huge deal. I honestly never felt bored, and as long as you show up to every class (attendance is huge) and take good notes you'll do well

Really an amazing class!! Prof. Hans is an accredited expert on Juries and brings a lot of her interesting research into class. However, the assignments were graded a bit tough by the TAs. Also, they did law school style cold calls, so be prepared!

Professor Bambha taught my favorite class of my freshman fall semester! Her FWS was fun and engaging by having the actual interests of the students being the main focus of the essays. The class in total was only 4 essays with a final project. Topics included reviewing popular media articles on play and reviewing toys!

Valerie's FWS class was by far my favorite class of my fall semester of freshman year! You can tell that she's very passionate about how children learn through play, and she makes the lessons super engaging and fun! The papers assigned were so fun to write about, that it didn't even feel like mandatory assignments. Totally recommend this FWS!

She assigns 3+ journal papers with associated pre-recorded lectures that can be 1-2 hours long each every week. The in-person class is boring and isn't helpful for the exams. Your course grade is 100% exams. The content and exam questions are difficult. There is nothing to help you prepare for them. The class average was a B+. Would not recommend.

This professor does not really teach. She assigns you pre-recorded lecture videos to watch outside of class, and a fair amount of scientific articles to read as well. During the scheduled class time, you just discuss the readings with your classmates. Testing unfair because a curve is necessary, but she allows people to take it at home unmonitored.

A truly great English Prof. at Cornell. Super approachable and with absolutely no ego or intellectual snobbery, which is rare with older white male English profs. Taking Decadence from his is truly a privilege considering it's what he specializes in. I'd recommend this course to all Cornellians perhaps as the most ingenious English class here.

Prof. Hanson's is the one class you must take on the Victorian period. He lets out all the gas and shows you why the 19th century is not only stuffy 'n boring but sometimes cool, even spicy. Prof. Hanson will teach you why the Victorian period still matters. He will show you that the 19th century can be for you even if you thought it wasn't before.
Prof. Hanson taught me why Dorian Gray matters, and he taught me how to understand Oscar Wilde. He is such a talented teacher!

The literature assigned in decadence did not disappoint me. Prof. Hanson is very suave, has great insights and is very approachable.  He facilitates a safe space for discussion of taboo subjects and assigns some raunchy and exciting texts.  If you like Edgar Allan Poe and that kind of Gothic aesthetic, you can't miss out on this class.

Hanson nefariously picks apart essays with hypercritical comments. His interpretation of the material trumps all, and he will let you know you are reading something slightly wrong. He has shown nude material in class in an immature way multiple times, including when we played spot the phallic element in Beardsleys' drawings. Made me uncomfortable

Professor Hanson is fantastic. If you're looking for a two-credit course to take that is easy, Oscar Wilde is the one. Very flexible on deadlines, easy to do well without completing the readings, or watching the asynchronous lectures. Definitely a must take!

Fundamentally careless, redundant, and painfully desperate to be Foucauldian. He doesn't seem to know or care at all about what the difference between Decadence and Aestheticism is. He seems to have never grown out of the bad habit of trying to assimilate the authors one admires. Be yourself! And stop playing long videos in class!

He has an ego but his teaching is mediocre at best. He may be a first-rate intellectual, but his contemptuous indolence is tiresome. I'm not sure if it's arrogance or just a general sense of ennui, but there's something irritating about him. That he holds ONE office hour/week and neglects to put his email on the syllabus tells u all u need to know
His lectures are the most poetic ones I've taken at Cornell. He is nice and caring and very responsive with questions and emails.

The best lectures I've ever had. ellis absolutely knows his field and can always articulate the matters very fluently and elegantly in the lecture. He gives very detailed feedback and might be a bit picky on the papers, which you probably won't get from other professors, but that is extremely helpful. also VERY willing to help.

Ellis is a talented and engaging speaker. Material was always a joy to read and I looked forward to his discussions. As for grading, he makes you work for it. He can be intimidating at times, but he's mostly friendly, witty, and helpful. Did I mention he is hot as hell??????

Hanson's lectures are the most poetic and fluid I have witnessed so far. Don't take this class if you aren't comfortable with various interpretations of art-- they may seem off, but Ellis always has his reasons. I always looked forward to going to lecture in the evenings and reading the material was enjoyable.

If you are interested in Oscar Wilde or Baudelaire then Decadence is the course for you. Hanson is a man who embodies the words he speaks. Sometimes class is more  performance than lecture. He rambles sometimes and he will grade your paper harder than most. But we watched bdsm in class and for sheer entertainment factor he can't be be beat.

Probably the most fun lectures I have ever had at Cornell. Prof. Hanson uses video clips and images extensively, and the lectures seem to go by quickly as a result. I learned a lot, and the grading was not difficult. A really good elective if you have some interest in studying sexuality.

this class is what you make of it - ellis is a really friendly, intelligent professor, but he also has a bit of an ego. if you really listen to what he has to say and take it seriously, you can learn a TON from this class. however, it is easy to coast through and do decently. TAs were outstanding. i had kaelin alexander and he RULED!

He's a strong lecturer--he knows how to perform for a class and how to keep students engaged. However, the quality of the lectures varied--some lectures were brilliant, while other lectures were filled with fluff. The class wasn't difficult: he gives you topics for the 2 essays, and the 3 quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention in class.
WORST TEACHER EVER!!!!
horrible prof! this guy may be smart but he is the worst prof ever. fire him cornell!!!
bad bad bad bad bad

Lecture is always interesting and I enjoyed the reading and discussion sections a lot. Relatively helpful during office hours, although it's probably better to go to TAs since they do most of the grading. Easy to ace the quizzes. LOVED the Ellis holidays.

Best class I've taken at Cornell. I thought this was an english class at it's best. If you go to lecture and study at all you can ace the tests and paper grading was fair. I would go to lecture just out of interest even if I weren't taking the class. There is a lot of shock value, but the literary analysis was genuinely incisive also.

Ellis' Desire class is worse than oral sex with teeth. Classes are just flamboyant ego displays. Lectures are remarkably unhelpful and curiously labeled as part of a Cornell "English class." The TAs are mostly brown-nosing, self-involved "PhD candidates." 98% of people taking the class are looking for titilation, not English scholarship/literature.

Provocative and highly entertaining lecturer - holds attention effortlessly for the entire hour and is delightful to listen to. Quizzes are not difficult if you pay any attention in class & the papers are fine if you put in the effort. Section was unwarranted. Sometimes seems to say things for pure shock value and seems wholly uninterested in interacting with students outside of class, but definitely worth it nonetheless.

i took both 355 and 276. this man is amazing. the class is fun and he's beautiful. i had to miss a few lectures and was more upset about missing the opportunity to hear him speak than missing material for the quizzes.  great class. amazing professor.

POOR lecturer! style is stream of consciousness, unorganized, and redundant.  class is more FLASH than substance.  Hanson was inaccessable, thankfully i had a wonderful TA: peter bailey.  Most people seemed interested in this class for the SHOCK value, not for intellectual development.  several misogynist comments during lecture as well.

His lectures are brilliant and the material is amazing, but he's an aloof intellectual. He's hard to reach: you must sign up for appointments to talk to him and I had to use the directory to get his email. He considers sticking to his own policy more important than helping students out in hard times. Take the class, but beware of him.

One hell of a course. He is a fantastic lecturer and the readings are excellent. He's the english teacher you've been waiting for--off the wall, with absolutely no fear of offending. I couldnt take notes fast enough in his lectures.

I can't gush enough about this guy. From his invented class holidays (which involve lots of latex and hilarity) to the amazing lectures which had me racing to get his words on paper regardless of whether or not they would be "on the test..." Some people are just born for teaching. Take his class.

OMG! Best class ever! I went to the first lecture just for fun, and enrolled the next day-- one of the best professors on campus, fun, and passionate about what he does. And hilarious, I want to be an English major just to be in the same building as him!!!!!!
never met anyone with such intensity and charisma! Brilliant class, great readings very stuctured and organised. did i mention he is hot as hell??
take this class!  eye opening and engaging!

3 words...best class ever! He's a crazy man, in a good way. Lecture is very fun and his quizzes are awesome. Just go to class and you'll be fine. He's amazingly brilliant and fun. An absolute MUST take before graduating...like wines :o)

Ellis is the MAN.  He speaks so smoothly, it's awesome.  If you take this class, don't waste your energy taking notes, you'd be ruining a great opportunity to listen to a very fine speaker.  Everyone deserves one thoroughly entertaining class like this each semester.
No Comments
No Comments
ellis is hot and so is this class

Though this was not the course number when I took it, Hanson's course on The Sexual Child is a tour de force and must not be missed.  It combines all of his strengths--edginess, wit, and intellect--with fabulous material.
Ellis is amazing (and so hot). his lectures are always interesting. decadence is an amazing class, so off from the typical CU class.
No Comments
Excellent and absolutely marvelous!!!
this was the most fun i have had in class at cornell thus far.

Nicest professor at Cornell.  Genuinely cares about his students understanding of the material and also their general well-being.  He really knows his stuff and he's a lenient grader when it comes to essays.

Excellent Professor. Initiated my interest in the Indian Ocean World. Extremely helpful and approachable. His love for the subject is contagious. Tagliacozzo is the man.  He is fabulously brilliant and yet so genuinely kind. Great professor!! Really easy class and she genuinely wants you to do well. She's always willing to meet with you and help you.

Joanie's passion for her field of study clearly comes through with how much personal attention she provides to her students. I've never had such productive meetings with professors before. Joanie herself is a poem. First impression: confusing, tangential, not fully present; once fully invested/committed to learning from her: in the top 3 most rewarding experiences of my life. Class with Joanie is always an adventure. Her whimsical personality energizes any room and she makes students feel comfortable not only digging into texts but also sharing what they've exhumed. Assignments are fun and thought-provoking. Joanie's is a class not to be missed.

Joanie meticulously prepares for interesting discussions and keeps every class organized and engaged. She challenges and intrigues; she keeps you on your toes and welcomes you with open arms. She is always willing to work with you one on one, and she is a joy to learn from in lectures and seminars. Plus, she gives awesome grades.

Professor Pulsoni's emphasis on participation may shy people away from the class, but he is definitely an amazing instructor and ensures that you understand the material to the fullest capacity. Pulsoni was a very engaging teacher, making sure students learned through participation. Class was always fun and interactive. Would definitely take again.

He teaches in a very unorthodox way - doesn't really follow lesson plans, but he cares about your learning. Will grade leniently if you put in the effort. Very funny, very sarcastic (in a good way), and helpful. I enjoyed learning Italian from him very much and had a great time in class.

Professor Pulsoni really cares about teaching his students Italian. He encourages students to have conversations with each other and wants them to speak as a true Italian would. He fosters an environment where it's ok to make mistakes without being ridiculed.
Very caring and reasonable professor. You will get an A if you attend class, do the readings, and complete the homework assignments, of which there are many.
David Powers is an expert in his field and you will learn so much through his lectures, but don't take his class if you are mostly there for an A; the medians in his courses are B or B+.

He's a nice professor and his course can be very interesting, but sometimes all of the different Arabic terms for places/other things are very confusing. I feel like I am learning a lot, but also sometimes the content can be very dry and not engaging enough during lecture.

Ugh literally horrible... Essays were ridiculously graded (he has a very specific way of writing and if you don't perfectly conform to it he'll destroy your papers).  Class is unbelievably boring and the course content makes me want to cry blood... just plain terrible.

Very difficult class for those outside of NES program/educated in Islam. Fantastic professor who really cares about the quality of your writing... Absolutely loved his class. Overall a VERY fair grader.

Great teacher
AMAZING. Definitely tough but in the best way - makes you work but you learn so much. He's the reason I picked this major.

Nice guy. Tests are easy, study guides are provided, and all answers are revealed in lectures, so it is advantageous to show up for every one. One short paper due every week is basically the only work.

he was very helpful and kept the class fun

Funny jokes at times. Good grasp of material with very easy tests. If you want to get an idea of basic islamic history, take this. If you want to understand the issues with the islamic world today, take a different class.

He's passionate about the material (Islamic Civilization), and this is always an asset. His lectures were coherent and the readings were enjoyable. The exams are easy -- pure memorization. Terrible lucturer, cannot handle being challenged, anything beyond his knowledge is unacceptable to him... very tough grader, he takes off points for having a comma placed in the wrong place.... At first, I thought his lectures were boring, but then I realized how interested he is in the material and that got me more intersted in it too. His tests are pretty easy--just memorize terms.  Sections were great too.  A very nice, understanding person as well.

Knowledgeable, friendly and fun. Could stand to be a little bit more structured and clear in his lectures. Exams are fairly easy, and essentially factual. Just come to all the lectures, take good notes, and study the term sheets he gives out. Course readings are a bonus, but not crucial.

Very knowledgeable, but terrible lecturer.  Seems like he really knows his stuff and doesn't really need notes, but was just so bad at presenting material.  And seriously, learn how to use a projector.

too much info w/no way to know what will be tested- tough grader

Amazing class, topic and all presented by a super enthusiastic professor.

I absolutely recommend this professor. His tests are absolutely fair and the class is very hands on and interesting. He is enthusiastic and also very willing to help and accommodate you. Definitely my favorite class so far in Cornell.

Very helpful professor.

She is enthusiastic about her material, but her exams and problem sets are extremely confusing. Organized, clear and hefpful this professor really makes an effort to that your presentation and writing skills improve. Excellent course to take regardless of your major. Do not be discouraged by seemingly intense course load, its really is not that bad and help is always there.

Best teacher I have ever met!

Great guy. Material is hard but the guy is helpful.

Easy class but requires no thought, very disappointing.
One of the worst courses I have ever taken.

SUPER interesting course material, and a caring professor, but I didn't like how the class was structured. Prof Sullivan is a really great Professor: one of my favorites at Cornell! Pat is so awesome. He's a great lecturer and a good person. I learned the most from this class out of any I've taken at cornell but it taught me the most
Great professor, everyone should take this class if they want to learn R and stats. Not a very hard class if you put in the work

Sullivan is the nicest man, let alone professor, on Earth. Not only did he make stats understandable my freshman year, now in my senior year he is advising my independent research. He is the nicest prof ever!! He is so helpful and is always approachable for Qs! I am taking btry 3020 with him now as well, and i wish he would teach more btry classes!!
Great guy, boring lectures.

P-dog (as he is referred to by his students) is a really nice guy. If you bother to go to class and pay attention, you might pick up something but attendance is not mandatory. Easy grader and great professor overall. Take his classes!

HE IS THE BEST!!! everyone should take his class. he is so nice and helpful if you ask questions. and he used to teach little kids so he makes jokes. yay!

Prof. Sullivan is great! Really nice teacher. Even though the classes are so boring, but he's very nice on the grades and the assignments.
Great professor, great class to learn.

This guy does not know what he is doing. Professor Rana is an amazing lecturer - he has no notes but still presents information in such an engaging way. okay so great teacher will give 5.0 for teaching... HOWEVER, it is a tad difficult. Also how could you make the final design night lab wednesday.... This is absolutely ridiculous in terms of timing. This was the best class I have taken at Cornell so far. Rana is out of this world. He is the most eloquent and coherent professor in all of Cornell. Listening to him is like listening to Mozart - not a single word is out of place. Why aren't there more people like him in this world.
He is a terrific teacher, crystal clear, speaks a little too fast, but very hot!

He is one of the best teachers i have seen simply awesome

TAKE THIS CLASS!!! Professor was an awesome guy, super knowledgeable and made class fun to go to. Grading was extremely generous and assessment was all based on lecture material. Professor Yang is the goat for intro to marketing. Super nice guy, with easy quizzes/final. He also incorporates a lot of his cutting-edge research into the class as well which is really interesting. TAKE THIS CLASS!
