Absolutely the best prof I've ever had. Engages you with the material, not simply because she cares about it (she does), but because you have realized YOU care about it. Every class was a pleasure. She generates great classroom atmosphere, and more than anything will make you write better. Great at teaching close reading of text. And hot to boot!
really great, very helpful. definitely improved my writing.
Very Intelligent. Very Engaging. Very HOT.
awesome class. really intelligent, knowledgeable and extremely nice. class dicussions help you understand the material a lot better.

HIGHLY recommended.  She's fun, engaging, intelligent, understanding.  She's very committed to getting her students involved and interested in the subject and very enthusiastic and knowledgeable.  This was my favorite class--lots of fun!

Great professor. the whole class is discussion and seminar based so be ready to talk. work and material is easy

The only gripe I had was the grading criteria was incredibly unclear. Ambiguous number of points would be deducted from papers and assignments with no real explanation. perhaps more of an issue with the TA than Kreps but still a problem

(I would not recommend) The lectures were boring with a heavy emphasis on PowerPoint, so the only time you may learn is on your own, with about 100+ pages of reading assigned weekly. overall would highly not recommend

she is mean.

Granted, she is a good writer and does give good tip. Ff you want a chill FWS, it's not worth it. If you want to get better at writing, I'd still pick a diff FWS.

She's a nice person but that's all. This is the most terrible course I've ever taken at Cornell. She requires lots of meaningless readings and never teaches anything useful in class. If you need ENGRC3500 to graduate, try not to take her session.

She will help you with all your writing as long as you seek out the help! As long as you work hard, you will become a much better writer!

Sarah is incredible! She is a very tough grader, but she is definitely here to provide all the help. Sarah is very clear, passionate, and inspiring. Doable if you're okay with his self-satisfaction and occasional rude behavior - he did once give trouble to a student who used the restroom during class for what he thought was a prolonged period of time. I also suspect he lowers grades just because his suggestions on what materials to analyze weren't followed. Competent at lecturing.

Schwarz is incredible. Even though he's been there for 50 years, he's accessible outside of class and cares about all his students. He can be self-absorbed sometimes but it can be funny. Most knowledgable professor I've had at Cornell. You can get away without reading some books but makes class more difficult/boring.
Great sense of humor. Wise and kind.
He is just brilliant.
Love Dr. Swartz! He is so wise and kind and knowledgeable. I have no idea why people are writing about his ego. He's a famous dude but so humble!
Great, great teacher. Prof. Schwarz is kind and compassionate, wise and experienced.

One of the most pompous, self-obsessed men I've ever encountered, but don't let that deter you from his classes. His lectures are very interesting (he clearly has recycled them for 30 years). For better or worse Prof. Schwarz is really involved with students--often invites class to Cornell events, plays, etc. Though he knows his stuff, and seems to have lectures down pat, he always tries to open it up to students

Not too difficult, lots of reading.  My first English class and I did surprisingly well (I'm Gov.)  Ienjoyed the reading more then I thought I would. Take it!

Great class-- TONS of reading, but it's good stuff. plan on about a novel a week. prof knows the material very well and gives clear, interesting lectures. only 2 papers, midterm, and final-- so not too much writing.

Great teacher, really knows his stuff and makes the material interesting.  Offers lots of opportunities to get to know him outside of class (trips to art museum, plays, etc)- take advantage of these!

my goodness, what an incredible professor! what an incredible class! definitely intimidated when he said we would have three ten page papers due throughout the whole semester but they are so easy to write. it's just your opinion with some quotes. my favorite favorite FAVORITE class ever. i don't know if it'll be offered anymore but it was incredibl

Provine has a great reputation and it is well-deserved. Lectures are interesting and entertaining. I was nervous about the science requirement and this ended up being my favorite class. Provine got me thinking in a whole new way. He is one of the best of the best.

Loopy guy, but really sweet. Lectures have very little to do with reading/section, and there are no exams, just papers. A real expert on his topic, and incredibly devoted to evolution as a concept. Gave me an interesting new perspective and worldview. Perhaps we have no free will...

he's an evolution teacher, of course he's an athiest. if you can't stand athiesm then take another course. extremely helpful and incredibly knowlegeable..he talked to me for two hours in his office hours about random stuff related to my research paper.

To make an understatement, Dr. P is remarkable. Lectures are thought-provoking, and the small discussion groups are a blast. Readings and papers are challenging but rewarding. By far one of the best classes I've taken at Cornell; I highly recommend it.

The lectures (not required) & sections (req) are at times thought provoking. Dr. Provine is clearly passionate about the subject, though biased. Do S/U option or don't take.

Lectures energetic and interesting, although not really required because exams are based only on papers and entirely up to the discretion of the TA. Pretty hostile to religion, a bit close-minded, but definitely makes you think.

wonderful lecturer, very interesting. grading depends a lot on your ta though...
Besides being brilliant, the man bent over backwards for me.  I learned a LOT.  He challenged me but guided me.  He is an awesome human being.  Take any course with him.  You'll be glad you did.
Interesting to listen to, so accomplished it's almost intimidating, and inspiring in a non-bitter atheistic sort of way.  Tends to tell the same stories over and over but it's forgivable.
I love Will

Took an IDSEM with Jenny at NYU this past fall and absolutely adored her class. She really values student input  and puts in the effort to know each student on an individual basis. She is always willing to meet with students outside of class time as well. Would highly recommend.

Jenny Mann is pure sunshine. Going to her class is always the best part of my day! I've taken her Lit Tradition and Utopias, and she is simply amazing! So intelligent and gives wonderful lectures! She is AMAZING. One of the best teachers at Cornell, hands down.

She is a great teacher who will get you excited about Shakespeare and teach you how to write. Take her class.

Dr. Jenny Mann is, to be frank, amazing.  Walking into her class at the beginning of the semester, I had no interest in English or Literature.  Yet, throughout the semester I grew to adore the subject.  It is because of her that I am double majoring in Biology AND English!

Best professor I have had at Cornell! Very clear with explanations and the audio recordings were helpful as well. Made me genuinely interested in the topics and the final grade I got reflected the work and consistent effort I put into the class, which was very rewarding.

Very good professor that is knowledgeable in this area. Go to office hours so that she knows your face she is a very sweet lady. Read the text and go to lecture although its early and can be boring.

Professor Brannon knows her stuff! The class is difficult but do-able as the TA's are extremely helpful. At times Prof Brannon seems intense/mean but one-on-one she is amazing! Go to her office hours and meet with her to discuss the paper and exams and she will definitely help you to do well!

Her lectures can be interesting, if you like the subject matter, otherwise they are boring. She really knows her stuff and wants to help everyone any way that she can. Her tests can be hard. Her graduate TAs she has are awesome also.

very very boring. not a easy class. I did not get a A. I did sleep through 95% of all the lectures.

demanding but totally worth it!

I like her she is very engaging and it is an easy A if you go to class, participate and try your best for your essays.

Wide range of class topics introduced through a variety of means and interesting discussions make her FWS a joy to be in. She focuses on writing structure and grammar but also allows students to write in their own styles and express their personalities through writing. Wonderful professor and wonderful class!

The professor is very considerate and understandable. Class is interesting. I appreciated the work that was put into it. There are readings for hw, but they are usually short and interesting. This class was not work heavy at all.

Standard FWS class interesting topics covered, but not necessarily focused on love as originally intended. Zero feedback on papers other than "good" and "okay" on certain paragraphs, but I got an A so can't complain. Final Paper and Presentation. Overall easy though.

Easily my favorite professor of the semester. So funny and caring. Really fun content between books and movies and you get to choose your own topic for the final paper. Essays every 2-3 weeks with a rewrite allowed each time. So fun, low stress :)

My favorite class this semester by far. Readings and movies were carefully picked and captivating. You can tell she cares about what she teaches and about her students. Very understanding of the difficulties learning in a pandemic, and flexible if you explain your situation. Participation is vital to your grade and makes the class more enjoyable.

Participation and attendance are required, but the discussions are never boring. She picks a wide variety of readings and movies, almost all of which are quite interesting. She is very approachable, and she understands conflicts for assignments, and is willing to work with you for extensions. Her class is not an easy A, but she wants you to succeed

Great lecturer who is super engaging with the class. I recommend any class with her. She always finds interesting films, books, and short readings which are engaging. Discussions can be slow at times if you do not have a well-read class. She is a tough but fair grader.

Interesting readings and movies picked for class. You can tell that she was very interested in the topics that we discussed. Sometimes I was so entertained by the discussions we had in class that I forgot that it was a writing seminar. It is easy to do well in the class, but she will make you work in order to get an A.

INCREDIBLE professor + WARM person. My favorite prof. last semester (and yet @ college). I was reading pieces of literature that I did not know existed (!), and it is so clear that her passion shines through. chill class w/ super reasonable amount of work + readings. commit yourself to the work + participate and you'll leave w/ much more than an A.

I took her writing seminar on Queer Hispanisms. Simply amazing. She assigns a very reasonable amount of readings and she will make sure that they are NOT boring. Her lectures are interesting and very clear. She has a great personality and she is very REAL. Understands the lives of college students very well, so she's flexible on deadlines.

He's a really great prof!! He wants students to do well - if you are struggling/need help/want something to be different, tell him. Super accessible outside of class. Make sure you find a friend to do the end-of-class quizzes with (it's allowed). He is so nice and enthusiastic. Applies concepts to specific examples really well.
I loved this class, the lectures were very interesting and accessible! a rare for cornell classes

Okay class. DeGeatano clearly cares, but he's just a very poor communicator, and the class is not organized in a way that makes it engaging. Would be a lot better if it were split up into sections so that we can discuss rather than listen to lectures. Also, dense with material, yet geared toward non-science majors. Reinforced my dislike of physics.

One of the coolest profs at Cornell! Very clear, funny, personable, informative.  Excellent at explaining material, but you have to go to class. The slides he uses only have graphs and figures that you won't understand unless you actually go.  Gives a few short homework assignments that are helpful to reinforcing class material.

So this is one is coming from a meteorology major. The man is in his element with the smaller classes, like EAS 341. He's a very nice guy, more than happy to help you out in class and in his office (he never has regular office hours). Likes to call on people at random though, and gets flustered when he loses his place in his notes.

This is coming from someone who took this course to satisfy a science requirement. That being said, the course is dense with material, and no sections don't help. Take this if meteorology is your focus. Also, don't be that kid who tries to wing it w/o talking to Art. He's a good man, and very approachable.
Great class in which you learn about the cool stuff in Meteorology(Lightning, rainbows, halos, radar...)
The nicest man ever.  The tests are exactly from lecture notes, don't read the book.  Only about 6 homework assignments.  Lectures are interesting.  Would take this class several times over.

Physical Meteorology is really tough, and your notes will just be derivations, and then derivations won't be on your test. His problem sets are tough, but there are only three.  He is very approachable and a very lenient grader, although his exams will make you (want to) cry.

He went at just the right speed during class. He is very friendly and always welcomes students who need extra help and have questions. He always showed how he got equations, rather than simply writing them on the board, which was useful. An overall good guy!

Excellent lecturer... Worked through in-class examples very thoroughly, and made sure everyone understood... Always available for homework/pre-exam help...  Be aware the tests can be tricky, and he WILL call on random people during class.  Otherwise, made thermodynamics almost enjoyable!
Genuinely enjoyed almost every lecture. Covered a good range of material, and the problem sets and programming assignments did a decent job of forcing you to understand it.

Most concepts taught in this course are very very useful. If you want to pursue your career as an ML/DL engineer/researcher, this course is basically mandatory, although many concepts are indeed difficult to understand.
Hard core course but moderate exam (for the year that I'm taking).

He is very good at lecturing and clearly explaining concepts. However, CS 4787 has many assignments; I believe he managed to squeeze in 6 programming assignments, 6 problem sets, 5 paper readings, and 2 exams into a 15 week semester.
AWFULLLLLLLLLL

Great lectures, delivered with a lot of passion and vigor. Clear explanations. He is a genius so often time you have to ask him for clarification when he jumps 5 steps in a derivation, but other than that he's great. Exams are hard, but he gives a nice curve

De Sa was super nice, helpful at his OH, and gave awesome print outs of his lecture notes. The programming assignments (in python) build off each other so sometimes your just copy/pasting code and didn't take too long to complete. Overall I learned ML much better than CS4780 and used many of the concepts at my AI/ML internship, highly recommend.

The course covered a lot of interesting topics, but since there were few homeworks and no exams you'll only learn if you engage with the material yourself. Chris was exceptionally approachable and a genuinely caring/considerate person. Lectures were organized really well and not too hard to follow. I highly recommend taking any class with him.

Highly recommend 6787 w/ De Sa for anyone familiar w/ ML who wants to get acquainted with how ML research is conducted on all sides---statistical to hardware. Took away a lot of messages and ended up thinking about/reading material outside of class. He lets students lead paper review lectures, and mainly moderated/clarified things.

De Sa was excellent in Principles of Large Scale Machine Learning. His lectures were clear, organized (notes on website), and very rigorous. I came out of the class feeling like I had strong skills in supervised learning, and good intuition for any related to ML or optimization. Material is used in practice in and is cutting edge for a ugrad course
He's new to Cornell so, he was not well adjusted to teach CS 4780. Killian is much better and completely took over the course towards the end of the semester.
Chris de Sa is the Josh Peck of the CS department, beware you could get a newscaster incident. Also cares a lot about ML, and is invested in students learning the material.

Literally the kindest professor I've ever met. Explains labor economics very clearly and he truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Manages to make econ interesting and not too difficult for a humanities oriented student!

Professor Fields is one of the best-loved professors for all ILR students. He is so caring for the students, not only your academic performance as a student but also your health and wellbeing. His lectures are easy to understand - he has the magic to simplify complicated theories/models into something that everybody can relate. He is so amazing!
Two tests. First one is easy. The second one is crazy hard
Not good professor. Very unclear. Do not take if you have the chance!
Awesome prof.

Professor Gary Fields single handedly makes the study of Economics  -dare I say- enjoyable . His lecture content is organised and he his crystal clear and methodical in his delivery. He humanises the subject through personal anecdotes and real life examples. Even if you absolutely hate Economics, you MUST take his class. You're welcome.

What can I say that hasn't been said? This guy is: The Man. The best professor I've ever taken. A legend. An absolute genius when it comes to not only his field but to teaching itself. The material is not easy, even totally foreign, and he makes it crystal clear. He's also hilarious and each class is a really a pleasure.

Fields is a phenomenal educator. He's one of the most cited and well-respected economists in his field, but manages to still relate to students on a personable level. The material is extremely interesting and life-changing, and taught in an anecdotal fashion that made the class unforgettable. Grades are based on the midterm and final only.

Very hard-working, fantastic professor. Expectations for the course were very clear. Presented the material in a way that made it accessible to students with no previous econ courses. He made labor econ enjoyable! Gives out copies of previous years' exams, which pretty much mirrored which type of questions were asked. Excellent!

Great/best professor and super clear. He inspires and cares for  students.  Introductory labor economics class for mostly MILR and MPA students so different from usual econ undergrad courses, he doesn't focus on theory or math that much, which means course and exams are not so difficult:-)
Take Fields. I'm approaching my last semester at Cornell, and made sure to enroll in another of his courses before I leave. He is awesome; you won't regret taking classes with him.
Best professor for international student because he is crystal-clear and almost never uses American slang. Funny, positive, helpful and extremely organized.
Best!
Really makes you excited about the subject matter.  Extremely approachable, and very helpful.  One of the best profs at Cornell.
I just wish every professor at Cornell was like him: crystal clear, passionate, helpful, approachable.

Adore him and his teaching style. Got to be one of the most hard-working professors at Cornell. His lectures are organized, methodical, and crystal-clear. The amount and level of material he covers is the perfect balance between covering the essentials and stretching to keep it interesting. Exams are fair and straight-forward.
one word: amazing

He is absolutely an amazing teacher of economics.  Very good at explaining difficult concepts in a way that makes it seem simple. If you get the opportunity, take as many classes with him as possible. There is a reason he is a leader in the development economics field... b/c he knows his stuff.
I expected much more out of this class :(
I agree, Fick is the man! CSS 1900 was a great class. Lots of field trips and not too much work. He is the nicest guy and the class was really interesting.
The class overall is fairly easy based on the subject but there are a handful of essays and quizzes and the tests can be tricky. Fick is the man otherwise.
Ok, uses old research, some things aren't relevant or have changed.

Professor is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about forages, agronomy and agriculture in general. To get a A- or better, you really have to know the information thouroughly, cramming won't help. Fick is a very genuninely nice man. One of the best courses I've ever taken at Cornell. Highly recommended.
Easy class, nice guy, tends to ramble but doesn't require that you remember his rambling for tests.
No Comments

His lectures are interesting, but slides are only pics so you HAVE to go for notes. barely any homework, except the readings (optional). The projects are kind of annoying. For prelims, you get 10 questions ahead of time, 4 are on the prelim. The q's have part a,b,c and he looks for specific answers. Go to office hours! Its a minimal effort A.

Kinda overrated class. He doesn't put any words on the lecture slides, so you're forced to go to lecture. The content is pretty much all common sense, but you have to know his made-up vocabulary to understand what's going on. It's a very easy class though since there's barely any homework and you get the prelim questions before the test.
Very few classes at Cornell where just showing up, taking half decent notes and reviewing (verbatim) questions for exams gets you an A- at least

- attendance not mandatory but you pretty much have to come to each lecture to effectively prepare for classwork/exams
- assignments are easy points, it's very hard to do poorly
- offers extra credit
- gives the exam questions beforehand, you have to prepare before the actual exam for the questions using notes/OH
- always regrade! TAs r everywhere

if you like lecture-based classes and take good notes this class is perfect. if you like cramming right before the exam, not paying attention during lectures, and teaching yourself the material (me) this class is extremely difficult. grading is really varied too which is frustrating. just not for me
Good professor and a great person. He truly cares about his students. The prelims are short-answer based and there are a few writing/design assignments.

i did the extra credit without realizing that it didn't contribute to getting A+ but that's fine. He's very nice and holds lots of office hours which were very useful to the prelims. His presentation notes aren't very good so you pretty much have to show up for class

Great class. Would definitely recommend! Prof.Evans is very friendly, and his lectures are engaging. However, make sure you download the lecture outlines and organize your notes accordingly, because he does not always mention explicitly which section he is in so you could get lost. Grading is very fair. Go to office hours and you can surely get A!

Professor Evans is such a great professor. The material in this class is super interesting no matter what your major is. The work is very manageable. It's clear that Professor Evans loves teaching, and he is very kind person and wants his students to succeed.
Fantastic professor. Very interesting and relevant material. Always willing to help out students!
Elite... that's all.
I was genuinely interested in the topics that he covered. As long as you fill out the practice questions for the prelim ahead of time you should do well in this class.

Very interesting class. Dr. Evans is accessible and truly cares about his students. Grading is very fair, but not an "easy A" class. You have to work on things thoroughly and ahead of time to make sure you get all the points. Some people don't do this and underestimate the workload. Then they get points off and think the grading is harsh.
Professor Evans is a fantastic lecturer and you can tell he really cares about his students. Highly recommend!

I can't rave about Gary enough. He is extremely caring and accommodating to students. He has no problems with giving extensions. The class itself is pretty easy. If you went to lecture and took good notes, exams should be a breeze, but still pretty time-consuming. Assigned readings aren't necessary to get an A. The class material is also very cool.

I really enjoyed the lectures, but the exams were extremely intense and graded toughly (despite questions being released ahead of time). The TAs are tough graders too when it comes to the projects. This would have been one of my favorite classes if the exams were not as excessive/detailed. The professor is really insightful.

Very straightforward and easy class. Lots of opportunity for extra credit (with SONA), and the rubric is very clear. Going to lecture is pretty important as his slides/slide summaries aren't very informative on their own. He's a very engaging and good lecturer though, and it's very clear he knows what he's talking about.

Absolutely a great class. Makes you think beyond simple principles and forces you to apply your understanding to real world, environmental examples. Prof. gives ten essay questions before the test, and the tests consists of four of the ten, randomly given. Very very fair, and the class makes sure that you understand the material. Tons of extracredt

Gary Evans is a wonderful professor. He really loves teaching and is very willing to talk to outside of class. The tests, however, are a series of incredibly specific questions that are given out a few weeks before the test. Prof. Evans does hours of prelim review, which is essential for doing well because in grading he looks for specific answers.

Evans is such a nice guy. Go to lecture, pay attention, and you will breeze by with an A. Distributes ample exam questions well before tests - answer them thoroughly, because he picks 4-5 of them of the 8-10 given to place on the exam. Don't buy readings, just take notes in class. Tests feel long, but if you answered the ?s beforehand it's easy.

I took an economics class with the allegedly distinguished professor Evans. When I had received a puzzling low mark on an assignment, I had asked him for Office Hours, where he repeatedly made clear he only takes students alone. When I had arrived, he seemed very distracted and was constantly jingling change in his pocket. Unprofessional boomer

Gary is an amazing professor and his teaching style has really contributed to making my life simpler. You have to go to lecture or make sure you know someone who takes good notes because his slides are hard to understand if he doesn't explain them. His grading system is fair and office hours are a very beneficial. Also make sure to ask questions.

Professor Evans is a great lecturer - I took this for a distribution requirement and loved it. Just make sure you go to lecture and take good notes, he encourages to use group effort to prepare for all exams and all answers to 10 essay questions are covered in lecture. No need for any readings, so don't buy them! Just go to class, and listen:)

Took this class not knowing anything prior about the subject to for credit requirement. Lectures were really interesting. Pay attention during them because slides won't really help much and office hours before prelims are packed. love his prelim system, and the extra credit helps a lot. Dont be afraid to approach him before class!! fun guy

DO NOT buy the required textbook material. Don't need to do readings to get an A go to lecture and write down examples for exam. You get possible 10 questions on exam and 4 are actually on it. If you go to office hours he literally goes through them and gives you answers & you can do psych studies for 20 points of extra credit.

Professor Evans is amazing! His slides are easy to understand and he makes them so applicable to our lives! The class is interdisciplinary and very interesting, and his method of preparing students for exams is really effective and shows that he cares. Definitely recommend!

Don't expect to be able to ask your TAs about making anything clearer before tests or projects; they aren't responsible for grading, and some (if not all) of them don't even go to class. Gary Evans is a fine lecturer (if he would just put some words in his slideshows instead of just pictures every now and again), but the class is disorganized.

LOVED this class and Professor Evans. Such interesting material that changed the way I think about the world around me. The readings aren't necessary, but they're interesting. Taking thorough notes in lecture will give you everything you need to do well on tests and projects.

Professor Evans is very helpful and clear in lectures. His lectures are engaging and usually interesting. His tests are not too bad but sometimes his TAs grade a bit harshly. Professor Evans is very helpful in his office hours and very fair. He has done a lot of famous research and written several books but he is very humble in class.

This is an interesting, low-stress course that gives you a language to think about the environment in. Gary is helpful, exams are fair, and projects are relaxed. The one frustration was that many studies seemed vague or even outdated. We needed to think about fewer studies in more depth rather than brush over sketchy data.

This class is great for anyone interested in design, human behavior, or a little self-reflection. TAs grade prelims kind of harshly, but you can easily make up for it with the projects and attendance grade. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT; it will help a lot. Overall, good lecturer, VERY interesting class.

The only redeeming aspect of this course is that attendance is not required.  Gary Evans is a nice human being, but shockingly stupid.  Class is rampant with overgeneralizations, confusion of correlation and causation, and old, weak data.  If you wish to become a more critically thinking person, do not take this course.

Class is very interesting for anyone. Assignments aren't hard. Tests are doable, but sometimes the TAs grade too harshly. After one exam, I got a pretty low grade and asked the TAs why I lost certain points. They couldn't explain some to me, so I went to Evans and he offered to meet with me for 2 hours going over each little point. Recommended.

Talks about things that really make sense and can be applied to everyday life but are still unique and insightful. Great for anyone interested in design, and for anyone just interested in how people of different cultures and in different settings interact with their environments.

Gary is a great lecturer, very insightful and fun to just sit back and listen to. You can do pretty well without doing the reading, but the readings are actually pretty interesting and you end up getting a LOT more out of his lectures if you've done the readings beforehand. Also he's very approachable and great to talk to.

Tests are very lengthy and may be only 4 short essay questions, but each question has an 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1e, 1f, etc, so really it's like answering 30 q's. Wish I were kidding. you really have to prepare, & even then it doesn't guarantee you'll do well. Take the WIM section. it reduces the test grades to only 25% of your grade. Much easier that way

Professor Evans is a clear lecturer, is interesting, and is very helpful in his office hours (especially in that he has many many office hours near prelim times).  The tests are short essays, but you are given a bank of essay questions (4/10 questions chosen) before hand, which is nice :).
Organized and helpful.

He is literally the nicest person I've ever met. Super reasonable when it comes to work and he doesn't try and trick you on tests or anything. Understands that kids are busy and is willing to work with you. Listens to students' suggestions.

Class is no longer an easy A like it seemed to be in previous years. Going to lecture is not mandatory and I don't think I opened any of the textbooks all year. Unfortunate that no one really watched all of the movies either. Prof. Miya. is really quiet and hard to understand. His lectures are rambly and tend to make no sense.
boring guy. Not an easy A+ class anymore tho he is really nice in gradings. Friends who never went to lectures managed to pull an A+, while I couldn't.
VERY nice guy. I felt bad for him as no one came to lecture. His reading and movie selection is no longer from light easy anime. But easy grader.
The easiest A+ class ever. Never attended a single lesson. Never learned anything.
No Comments

Okay... so the guy's a little boring, but he chooses great readings and links them together really well.  His essay topics tend to be a bit ambiguous but he is very willing to answer questions and help you out.  Overall, not the best prof, but was good enough that I am looking forward to a second class with him.

Okay, the subject matter was interesting but as the semester progressed I found myself losing more and more interest due to super long readings, ambiguous essay topics, and uninspiring lectures.  A very nice guy though. I guess I learned from this course.

Content was interesting to analyze but made the material way harder than needed. Half the time, I couldn't understand what she was saying. Class involves discussions and busy work, which are easy but repetitive. Isn't very accommodating towards absences (only get two absences before your grade goes down, including illness and death in the family).
He's awesome! Really nice guy and truly a brilliant scholar.

I took an FWS with Professor Weiss in the fall. He is extremely passionate and knowledgeable about linguistics. I am only hoping that my next FWS is going to be as good as his. He gives you good feedback on your papers, and I, as someone who doesn't like to write much, thought his prompts were very compelling. An awesome professor all around.

Historical linguistics (an FWS) with Michael Weiss is an absolutely fascinating course. Not only is he a great professor whose lectures remind me of reading National Geographic but the course was an easy A. You have to put in effort, but I had by far the best FWS experience among all my friends. If you need an FWS and this is open, TAKE IT!

Not much reading, but all of them are quite informative. He motivated us to read some classic paper in linguistics. However, if you happened to read a bit about linguistics, you should know many of the anecdotes he will share.  Most lectures are self-contained units about a certain ancient language/unrecorded history of existing languages.

Just fantastic. His lectures are a flood of knowledge from his massive mental store; this was the only class I actually enjoyed taking notes for. He's laid back, pleasant, and a bit goofy. You'll get both a wealth of general knowledge regarding the historical method, and a great deal of fascinating tidbits from taking his introduction course.
Laid-back, funny, and engaging. Good guy.

Have taken a couple of classes with this prof, (historical ling and Intro to ProtoIndoEuropean) incredibly knowledgeable on Indo-European and Historical Linguistics.  For people interested in linguistics, definitely take his classes.  His classes are not really for those looking to fulfill requirements though.  Awesome prof and awesome classes.
very, very knowledgeable and helpful. very organized and responsive.  however, this course is not very interesting unless you;re a true linguistics fanatic, don't take it.

It was a very "interesting" class; we learned lots of neat tidbits. But for anyone majoring in linguistics it's not deep enough. We did the phonology for almost the entire semester, and the one thing I was interested in (syntactic change) was hardly mentioned. He also missed a few classes without telling us beforehand or explaining after.

From a distance he looks like your average guy in a T-shirt and cargo pants. He's not. He knows an heck of a lot, and keeps the class really fascinating. This course can feel a bit fractured (a lot of mini-units), but by the end it doesn't matter. And it DOES help to take notes, even if he says you don't have to; little details show up on  prelims.
Great Class. Great professor. Very knowledgable
I found his class to be a touch boring, but an interesting subject nonetheless. Do you know anyone else who can write in Tocharrian A?? I sure don't...overall, pretty good
such a nice and competent prof. and an easy A class. he got me interested in Indo-European languages (his specialty).

There were VERY few instances where he did not know an answer to a student's question, not matter how in depth, off the top of his head. He has an EXTREMELY good knowledge of the subject matter. He was always willing to find the few answers he did not know. I give him the highest ratings.
very easy but interesting class! he's so knowledgeable about his field. also, he's a great lecturer.
No Comments
just amazing.
Absolute sweet heart. Didn't learn a thing.

Clearly passionate about the work that he does and the material that he teaches, but lectures are extremely disorganized and thus difficult to follow. Grade is based on a project (which you can get a good grade on if you put in the work) and take-home exam (three 4-5 page essays). Surprised by grade received b/c I didn't read at all.

fantastic professor! never met one more caring about his students. doesn't use TAs for this class so it just enhances the learning and experience. the few assessments he assigns are substantial but very reasonable and manageable over the course of the semester. TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM!!!

Weiss is a fantastic guy, super knowledgeable about WWII, the world, and humanitarianism. His lectures are extremely disorganized to the point of not being very useful (for completing the assignments). You don't really have to go to class. Many readings and weekly discussions, but you can bs the discussions if you understand what the book is about

Weiss is hilarious and if you show up and read our stuff, he will notice and help you out a lot. I wrote a paper that was presented in Washington DC and it was the best experience I've ever had at Cornell.
Passionate about the material. Engaging professor
Lectures were disorganized but discussions were great and Weiss always goes above and beyond to engage you in the course material as much as possible. Very likeable and friendly guy

Prof. Weiss may not be the most laser focused professor Ive ever had, but he certainly is the nicest professor Ive had at Cornell. He goes above and beyond for his students and really knows his stuff. You wont do poorly in his class if you do the work but you will learn something and meet a great guy, you have nothing to lose if interested in ww2

Weiss is unconventional for a CU prof.–class is free-flowing and discussion-based, which is nice but leads to organizational challenges. He is exceptionally kind, reasonable and goes out of his way to help students. Unbelievably smart, willing to tap every resource from textbooks to his connections– he lined up great, big-name guest speakers.

I absolutely recommend any class with Professor Weiss. He is one of the nicest and most supportive Professors you will find at Cornell. He has his own style of teaching, but if you take the time to get involved in discussions you will find you learn an incredible amount.

The mid term for the WWII history course was barely comprehensible.  Not that it mattered because it didn't count if it hurt your grade.  This class is a great filler class for busy semesters-- you don't have to attend lecture or section and will probably get an A anyway so long as you skim the readings on your own and aren't an idiot.

The professor was very poor in lectures, but he is a great guy that is very passionate about the material. The class itself education wise was not the best, but it did open me up to a new world. Professor is not bad overall. No better, no worse.

If you don't appreciate/like Professor Weiss then you're an idiot.  Yea some things in his classes aren't conventional.  Hey guess what, if you go to class and read the material then you will learn a LOT.  That's what he cares about and that's what really matters.  Take his classes!

Great, fun, relaxed class.  Weiss is a WWII historian so you learn about Iran as the course moves along.  He has ambitious goals for the semester, don't worry if you don't reach them.  Also no pre-lim, no quizzes, basically a guaranteed A with an amazing professor.

I step into class wondering how he has slipped through the cracks. While the readings and subject matter are fascinating, his lectures consist of him rambling about unrelated topics totally unrelated to WW2, and generally disregarding the curriculum which he set forth. His lack of structure in the class room is really a shame.

Lectures were completely pointless, and none of the notes were ever needed. Weiss did provide an extremely interesting reading list and was very enthusiastic about is subject. I never went to class, got an easy A, and learned a lot about the subject from the readings. Would absolutely recommend this class.
Lectures were pretty useless, otherwise tried hard to get people to be proactive.
JW is fab, fab, fab; the best teacher at cornell. take his class before he retires - which i hope is never; an asset to all undergradt

World War II - Prof Weiss is a very nice guy. The class might be difficult for someone who does not have a good background in the material - it's very unstructured - but for those who enjoy WWII history this clas is right up your alley.

Provides many different perspectives on all sorts of topics relating to WWII in Europe.  Some might say it is disjointed, but I don't think they get his style at all.  Weiss is very nice and approachable.  Great discusion sections, good lectures. It is true that the lectures aren't a chronological account of WWII- but that is what readings are for!
not a great lecturer, but a really interesting and enthusiastic guy.

His lectures are awful. He has no focus. His ideas are actually pretty archaic, although that's de rigeur for the history department. On the plus side, he does send out loads of irrelevant emails to people in his classes, so that's an ego boost.
great professor with a ton of interesting perspectives on how to learn about world war 2. his discussion sections are some of the best classes at cornell. i can't recommend his courses enough.

A hisory buff who knows everything about French history & WWI/II.  He's a great guy to talk to, and a good professor, though he is best in small, discussion oriented environments.  His lectures tend to ramble as he's trying to convey too much material!
Great teacher, very helpful.
He thinks he knows grammar but he does not. He corrected me a paper that it was revised by a english teacher.
Ro does a fantastic job at being accessible and kind, he's an amazing teacher and an amazing person. He cares about his students.

His overall concept of the class- a social based group project was great in theory. However, there were no guidelines or direction to project and he would get frustrated if you didn't do it the way he wanted (but never told you how he wanted it). Overall he grew very frustrated with the class. Don't take this class if you don't like group projects.
Great professor! have to earn your grade and put in the work

Dr. Serrano is a brilliant professor. He presents the theories using clinical examples that allow you to understand the concepts better. He is knowledgeable, answers questions and is very engaging. Be prepared to be inspired.
