Good professor who cares about what he teaches. Easy A. Two midterms + final (non-cumulative). Have to attend a certain number of classes to get full participation credit but can afford to skip some. There are one or two graded questions during each lecture, but they don't count for much.

As someone who nearly failed Adam Fry's BIOL1102 until I switched to pass/fail, this class was a godsend. The labs are by far the hardest part, but if you have 1 smart teammate, a nice TA & do the extra credit, you'll get an A. The TA's just want effort. The lectures are ez if u don't miss a class & u can even submit the quizzes late within reason.

I absolutely love Tammo as a professor! His lectures are interesting and he offers many different ways to get grades into the grade book. The lab is boring and not that fun if you do not have a good TA. TAs are important to  getting help and I think he could improve on his own TAs in my opinion.

Overall he is a good professor and is passionate about what he is teaching. Going to class and doing the polls is part of what adds into your grade. He gives 2 prep quizzes a week which also adds up to your grade. you need 92.5 points in the class to get an A to not have to take the final.

Tammo's a great guy! Laid back and totally understanding when it comes to missing a due date or deadline. Class is mandatory as there are participation polls every class, but it's not too bad. Not a big fan of science, but I did find the class interesting and enjoyable.

Professor Reichgelt is an awesome professor, and it's very obvious he cares about what he is teaching. Class is very laid back, and you answer questions using polleverywhere for participation. If you submit all of your assignments and go to class, you should be able to avoid taking the final and still end with an A thanks to his grading process.

Great professor. Definitely one of the easiest labs at UConn. There are several opportunities for extra credit and the lectures are fairly interesting. The labs can be annoying, it basically just depends on the TA you get. This class is a good option if you need to take a lab course, just be aware that the lab can be tedious rather than difficult

Hands down the EASIEST lab class at UCONN. Course is extremely straight forward, and quiz answers are on Quizlet. Exams are a little tricky, but if you study you'll be fine. Lab section isn't terrible, but the only lab practical at the end of the year is very hard, so make sure to study for that. Easy A class, with a good amount of extra credit.
Awesome professor. If you show up to lectures and do the homework, you're guaranteed a good grade. He's a very wholesome professor who cares about his students.
He's the man. Great professor, and an even better guy. Nice, funny, and passionate about rocks. Just show up 70% of the time and you'll do fine.

He is great, very funny. Lectures are required bc he uses PollEv, but it is easy. Hw is readings before each class and a quiz that goes along with it, every week. Besides that, midterm was a little difficult, but if you read the textbook it will be fine. Open note everything. 2 major projects, not bad. Overall good guy, easy class, 9/10
Keeps class interesting and is very knowledgable

Professor Reichgelt is a great professor. There are a lot of weekly assignments, for example, 2 quizzes, 2 essays, and a forum. He is very generous with the grading. He wants his students to succeed and truly learn about the Anthropocene.

Amazing professor. A lot of homework/ class work, but it's do able for the most part. The hw gives three attempts, and if you're stuck on questions he has no problem helping you to find the right answers after class. Very caring and funny prof, made my semester a lot less stressful.

Take this class!  For those who need an easy class, this is the one!  However, if you also care about the content, it is a great place to start.  I am not a geoscience/earth-science teacher, but I loved the content given.  Also, the professor is very understanding and will listen to you!

GSCI is so far outside of my major and yet he made this class so interesting and enjoyable for me. Tammo is very passionate about the material and it shows when he teaches. He can be pretty funny sometimes, even when he's not trying to be. He just wants everyone to succeed and makes it easy to get an A. Definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Great teacher, definitely recommend. You can tell he cares a lot about the subject and his students, I am going to miss taking his class. The grades are very spread out, so if you fail a couple of tests or assignments it won't affect your grade. You get 3 attempts on quizzes and he tells you where to find the answer for each question.

Took this class for a mandatory science credit, and overall it was fine. The lectures were boring as most of it was just reading off of slides, but Professor Reichgelt is really sweet and genuinely cares about the subject that he is teaching.

Very easy class. Tammo is a young, passionate professor that wants to give you the A in the class. You don't even need to go to class, you can get by with reading the textbook and reviewing the lecture slides.

I love this prof! Tammo is super passionate about Geo science and brings it to his lectures (def don't skip!). Assignments are clear and easy to do, and he provides ample extra credit. Genuinely caring professor. Take any of his classes if you can!

His lectures can be a bit boring but you can tell he is passionate and is very chill and approachable. Very easy class, as long as you go over his exam review, you will get an A. Extra credit is available too
Tammo is one of the best professors I've had at UConn. He's a young, chill guy and makes it pretty easy to get a good grade in his class.
Such a good young guy and one of the easiest courses ive taken. Really chill vibes, don't have to go to lectures to do good in class, no textbook necessary.

Professor Reichgelt is wonderful. You can tell he's really passionate about his job. I went into this class with 0 expectations but he somehow managed to make me excited about rocks lol. He does do lecture participation but the lectures are so chill it really wasn't a big deal. Homework is easy as long as you read. Great professor.

Professor Reichgelt was a great teacher for this class. There were a lot of assignments but they were all very easy. We had a lot of exams, but he dropped the lowest grades in each category including exams so the final is optional.

Pretty easy gen-ed class. Some prep quizzes were a nightmare and had some overly tough questions. Prep quizzes had 50% easy questions, 35% annoying medium-hard, and 15% questions that felt impossible. The remaining work, making and answer questions from lecture, was pretty easy. I liked how his lectures were short and to the point. Exams were fair.

Very easy Gen Ed class and professor Reichgelt seems actually interested in the subject he teaches. The entire class schedule is laid out on day one so you always know what and when everything is due. Some quizzes can be difficult to understand but you are given two tries which makes up for some of it. Solid choice of a class and teacher.

Class was extremely well organized. Professor had a deep passion for the subject, and gave a very detailed outline of what was going to be on the test. If you do the assignments and take notes during his review sessions you'll get an A. Quizzes are multiple choice and have 3 attempts.
class is completely asynchronous super easy, just watch short videos on each topic and go over the module review and its an easy a. Final is optional if you are happy with your grade before final.

It was an odd class but easy if you do all the work. I only saw Tammo on the occasional Webex call before an exam (in which he went over the whole test). Four 2-4min videos were 1 day of lecture, then a mini prompt/quiz but you had to read the coursebook/textbook to answer some Qs. 5 tests, all open-note and MC. Many small assignments but all easy.

This course was very easy and I recommend it. He provided his own recorded lectures for every topic and make the lecture quizzes based on them. The prep quizzes were sometimes a nuisance, but manageable. You can receive up to 3 extra credit points as well. A plus is that if you take GSCI1052 LAB, you can knock a lab out of the way easily.

Probably the easiest E course UCONN has to offer if you keep up with the content. He outlines everything that will be on the exam, which is completely open note. Probably the easiest E course UCONN has to offer.
The class is very interesting and he is very lenient with deadlines. The tests are not that hard, just do the weekly assignments and you will be fine.
Took a class online with him. He highlighted every single answer on every test, and they were open note.

She is super nice and cares about each student's well being. She lets you take 3 mental health days a semester on top of her cancelling class a lot. Graded on some participation and 3 papers, which are graded easily and thoughtfully (just word vomit and you'll be fine).The class was boring especially after the first month, but she was great overall

Prof. Steenhuisen is amazing; she cares about her students and is clearly very knowledgeable in her field. Graded by three papers which are generally easy to write and on interesting topics. Her emailed feedback is so detailed and truly shows that she reads and values student opinions. Definitely one of the best professors for pog!

Prof. Steenhuisen is very sweet and very intelligent. There are a lot of interesting readings and we had a lot of interesting class discussions. I wouldn't say the class was life-changing, but it was certainly a great experience. The papers are meant to be very manageable and stress-free but make sure you get to 10 pages!

Great professor who cares a lot for her students.  Participate more than you think you need to as feedback is not given about participation grades.  Class was graded on two graded discussions, overall attendance and participation, and three papers.  Really thought provoking class.  She single handedly persuaded me to major in theology.

TAKEE HERR! By far my all time favorite professor I've ever had. She's not only enthusiastic about her work but she is also caring and emphasizes using her "mental-health" days which she gives to all of her students. We are graded on three 10-paged papers which seem like a lot but can be tackled and done very easily.
Amazing woman absolutely take her! Interesting, discussion based lectures. 3 ten page papers, but grading is very easy. Very supportive of students' mental health.
Prof Steenhuisen is incredible, easily one of the best profs at Georgetown, very light grader and she made the subject matter very interesting
Take professor Steenhuisen! She's an absolute gem, putting her students mental health first while maintaining a great learning environment. I'd take this class a million times more if I could!

Amazing professor. Extremely knowledgeable, and talks about a wide breadth of religious information. Very caring about students; she really makes an effort to know everyone and takes major steps to accommodate mental health/general wellbeing. Take her at any cost.

An absolute icon. Take Professor Steenhuisen for POG!!!! She cares so much about her students. The 10 page papers sounds really scary, but they are not bad at all and grading criteria is super clear. BEST TEACHER AT GEORGETOWN!!

Professor Steenhuisen is a great professor! The class was very easy and the content was interesting to learn about. She values all of her students and provides clear grading criteria for the writing assignments. Easy A but also an engaging class.

Fav prof of all time! Classes are boring and I dozed off a few times (it's not necessary to listen). The 10-page papers seem long and take time but they're definitely worth the A. Dr. S is the most beautiful-hearted and inspiring person and is super understanding and pushes back deadlines if necessary. Thought-provoking papers for self-reflection.

An amazing choice for the problem of god core requirement. The class is graded by 3 10-page papers and as long as you put in some effort you will be fine. Professor Steenhuisen is also such an understanding professor and genuinely cares for her students' wellbeing. Take her if you can!

By far the easiest option I've encountered for POG: you are graded only on three 10-page papers that are far easier than they sound. I have yet to talk to someone who didn't get an A on all of them. She is an absolute sweetheart, and truly cares about your mental health. The only reason she didn't get a 5 is because I frankly did not learn much.

She is such a sweetheart and it's clear she loves what she does.  Assignments are VERY straightforward and easy to do (make sure it makes sense).  Class can be boring sometimes but that is expected for core requirement classes (+ she involves the class too so its not just her lecturing).  100% recommend (this is the pog to take froshies)

She is very nice and a fair grader, but to be honest I found the class to be a bit boring.  Three ten page papers but as long as you don't start them the night before you'll be fine.  Not a big theology fan myself, so perhaps this class was the least painful option.  Overall, solid choice.

Not sure what more there is to say. The nicest prof by far that I have taken at Georgetown. You are graded on three ten-page papers but the averages are very high. Readings are few but very interesting. She's very available for office hours to work on your paper if need be. No complaints.

I love her. Would take her every semester if I had to. She gave us three optional mental health days to take at any time if we wanted. She gave us days off from class for no reason sometimes, and she only assigns three major papers/assignments throughout the whole semester. She is super nice and creates a stress-free environment during classes.

Great choice for POG! She is so sweet and a really remarkable professor. She likes participation but I would have preferred to hear more from her and less from what random freshman thought about things haha. Beware the papers are long but super doable. One of the easier POGs from what I hear.
One of the most caring professors you'll come across at GU and open to all backgrounds. Take her and you won't regret it.

She is excellent, an expert in what she teaches. She is as caring as they come, and I would highly recommend the class as a relaxed course with a few low-stress assignments. You write three "credo" papers, each 10 pages long. In my experience, if you write 10 pages, you'll be fine with your grade. It can be a little dull at times, but it's chill.

Literally the kindest and most understanding professor. She gave us 3 mental health days which counted as excused absences. No exams, just 3 papers and if you try on those papers, your grade should be fine. And even though I'm not religious, the readings and class content are all pretty interesting! Definitely take her class!!
Such a sweet professor. She genuinely cares about her students and gives 3 mental health days a semester. 100% recommend for POG!!!!
Best prof I've ever had  love this woman with my whole heart. Taking her again because she cares so much and genuinely wants her students to both learn and do well.

Great prof! Really respectful of students other commitments and offered mental health days where we could just not show up to class. Most readings were provided on canvas, but a few I had to buy. Easy material; only three papers and they are graded fairly. Great POG professor!

Outstanding choice for PoG! This class is much more about introspection and reflection than dense theological reading - you'll discover so much about yourself. She is flexible, caring, respectful of all (non)belief systems, and considerate of mental health. Effort is rewarded on papers. Go to her office hours. Life-changing course if you let it be.

Her class is not that hard: although there are four books and three 10-page papers, if you care about the class and do the work, you will get an A. She is caring, willing to discuss with students, and gives detailed feedback. The discussions in her lectures are particularly inspiring: you learn from your peers and they help you frame your thoughts.

Steenhuisen is so wonderful. So kind and gives mental health days because she cares about her students so much. Take this class if you're looking for a really engaging POG course and actually want to dive into the subject. You will learn SO much about yourself and she is also very willing to chat on office hours. Can't recommend her enough!!!

Steenhuisen is an absolute gem. So kind and gives mental health days because she cares about her students so much. Take this class if you're looking for a really engaging POG course and actually want to dive into the subject. You will learn SO much about yourself and she is also very willing to chat on office hours. Can't recommend her enough!!!

Dr. Steenhuisen is an incredibly caring person and a wonderful professor. The course has two short papers, with a group presentation and a 5-page final paper. There are a good amount of readings and documentaries in the syllabus, but they are all very interesting. I can't recommend Dr. Steenhuisen or this class enough!

Took a class on cults with her and it was my favorite class I have taken at Georgetown. Professor is amazing; great insight and very understanding. An easy grader, but she is so great you will actually want to do your best work.

this lady is so funny. it was so fun to be in her class. shes always talking abt something. shes really so funny and cares abt her students. i really appreciated her talking about all of the permanent changes shes going to make to her class because of the pandemic.

Her class is 30% graded discussions, 60% papers (3 10-page papers each 20%), and 10% participation. She is the sweetest professor and always understanding. She has high expectations for the papers but is a very fair grader and always gives ample feedback. Highly recommend going to office hours and starting papers early. The best choice for POG!

Professor Steenhuisen is a perfect choice for POG. She is so nice, clearly cares about her students, and gives a lot of feedback on papers. The class is extremely interesting, and the books you have to read are short and eye opening. Papers are graded fairly tough, but you can make up for it by participating in discussions. Highly recommend.

So caring and super accommodating during COVID. Class was interesting and an easy A, 3 short papers and a group presentation, all graded easily & timely. Prof is super sweet, cares about mental health, and very accessible outside of class. Reading not necessary except for before essays/graded discussion days. Great way to fulfill 2nd theo class.

Lauve is a very sweet lady! Her class is very chill (Grading: One memorization test 20%, 3 essays 20% each, participation 20%), and she gives good feedback. The essays aren't the easiest A's, but you can make up for it by participating and doing well on the first test. Kind of asks invasive questions and exposes students in class sometimes.... huh.

I took her Religion and Cults in America Class this summer and I have to say that it was one of the best classes I've ever taken. The classes were heavily discussion based, and there were some readings for the class to complete. There were only 3 papers to write (2 5 pagers and 1 page) and she really cares for her students to do well in her class.

Professor Steenhuisen is amazing! She is the kindest person, and truly respects and believes in her students. Essays are long (3 10-pagers), but talk to her individually and she will help you gather your thoughts, she is so knowledgable!

Professor Steenhuisen is an amazing professor for problem of God. Her class consists of one Aquinas test, three 10 pg. papers and participation. She leads great discussions and is very welcoming of differing viewpoints. The class has distinct units which look at God's existence/non-existence, world religions, evil, and forgiveness. Overall, great!

Amazing woman. Literally the kindest soul! Her class is eye-opening, and your grade is based largely on 3 long papers, but they are really easy to write. Participation is key though, and it correlates with higher grades on papers. Go to office hours! She knows so much and can talk for hours about anything!!

Professor Steenhuisen is one of the most caring professors I've met at Georgetown. Always makes time to speak with students outside of class. Also very open-minded and open to criticism; encourages students to speak their minds in class, and looks at each religion/belief that we study in class with an unbiased and open perspective. Highly recommend

I wasn't too excited to take this class given the reputation of POG at Georgetown, but Prof. Steenhuisen is the best professor I could have ever had for this course. Her assignments are very straightforward and she is the sweetest person on the Earth. She is passionate about teaching while understanding everyone's views about the subject. TAKE HER!

Lauve is wonderful. She leads great discussions and is super knowledgable about the topic. The grade consisted of six discussion question posts, three papers (none longer than 5 pp), attendance/participation, and a presentation. Would recommend her for anyone needing a Theo prof.

Prof Steenhuisen is a sweet and caring person who wants the best for her students. She is well-versed in class content and uses readings, lectures, and more to ask challenging questions of deep personal reflection. I enjoyed the depth and intrigue of this class. Not too hard, but really makes you think if you buy into it.

Prof Steenhuisen is the best- she truly cares about students and her classes are pretty interesting. The work itself is not bad, there are three 10 pg papers but the prompts given are very explicit. Her grading is very fair, but not too harsh. Definitely take this for POG.

Phenomenal professor. Lectures are consistently thought provoking and interesting, and occasionally inspirational. Religion and Cults in America is maybe the best class I took at Georgetown, don't miss it.

I loved Prof Steenhuisen. She is hilarious, loving, and highly intellectual. Three 10 page papers - it is really not too bad, as the prompts are explicit and detailed. Though classmates criticized some of the literature, I found all four books we read to be intriguing and valuable. TAKE PROF STEENHUISEN FOR PROBLEM OF GOD!!!

This class is incredibly easy if you pay attention and go to office hours. Professor Steenhuisen is one of the nicest professors at Georgetown and truly cares about her students and their lives outside of school. The readings are really interesting and it's not much work at all- 1 test and 3 papers (10-page, but there's like 8 questions to answer)
Lauve is the bomb!!! She cares so much about her students. Pay attention in class, write a solid paper, and you will get a solid grade. Easy as that. I would love to take cults again.

Professor Steenhuisen was so sweet but SO unpredictable with grading - she'll tell you that you're paper is great and not to change a thing and give you a B- (btw wasn't me). 3 10 page papers throughout the course but not too bad if you get started early. She's big on participation so make sure you speak up in class!

Professor Steenhuisen is one of the best professors you can take at Georgetown. Her papers are super fascinating and fun to write - they will completely change the way you think. She's a truly LOVELY person, and always available in office hours or for a coffee. 3 papers, 8-10p/e, otherwise no weekly homework or reading (not hard). 100% recommend.

Take Steenhuisen for POG!! If you're looking to just fulfill the requirement, this is the one. Steenhuisen is super nice and openminded, very sweet lady. There's 1 super easy test and 3 10 page papers, which are seriously not that bad. I'm terrible at writing but still managed an A without putting too much effort.

She's a really nice and caring lady, but a tough grader. Her class is interesting but not really connected to the assignments which are 3 10 page papers. I recommend writing A LOT for her class, especially for the test at the beginning of the year.

Professor Steenhuisen is one of the most caring Professors that I have known. There is some reading but nothing outside the norm. Papers are long but super easy. She is willing to look at every point of view that you may have even if you completely disagree with the religion that is being taught. I recommend her for Problem of God.

Really sweet lady who genuinely respects and cares about her students. My biggest critique is the class was supposed to be a survey of world religion, but it focused almost exclusively on White American Christianity.

I cannot say enough good things about Professor Steenhuisen. She cares deeply about her students, not just in the classroom but on a personal level. Just an outstanding person. She is always accessible for help and grades very fairly. Lots of writing, but plenty of room to share your own thoughts. Very possible to earn an A. TAKE!

LIVE LOVE LAUVE! take her for problem of God!! The long papers may seem daunting at first but they're really not that bad! She is a wonderful professor and an even better person. Take the time to go to her office hours just to get to know her! Wonderful class experience, 10/10 would recommend

Really good professor for PoG. I just wish I had known that you have to go to office hours to get an A or even an A- in the class. Her comments on graded papers are vague and not super helpful, but the papers themselves are easy to write. Take her class, but beware that you'll probably get a B+ if you don't go to office hours.

Professor Steenhuisen is a great choice for Problem of God. She's an amazing woman, always very kind and respects everyone's ideas. There's no day-to-day homework, which is a plus. One exam and three 8-10 page papers. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. She makes you work for A's on the papers but it's worth it I learned a lot about myself during this class.
Very sweet lady, and is down to sit down with a student and have coffee with them. Her grading is confusing, and it lacks clarity. I would take her class, but don't be upset if you end up with a B+

Dr. Steenhuisen for POG was a great choice, I lucked out randomly getting her. Class grade depends on a few big papers, but she's more than willing to help. As long as you keep up with readings and go to office hours you'll do fine in the class.
Her class was amazing, I realy enjoyed her lectures. She assigns three 8-10 papers and one test the topic is very easy and you find yourself needing more pages.
She is really the best. Her class is engaging and fun, and she does not give much work. I had her for Religion In American Political Life

One of the best professors I've had so far at Georgetown. Readings are interesting, and she facilitates great class discussions. Overall she's so nice, and she makes this class great. Also a pretty easy grader, three papers and one test (she tells you the questions beforehand). I'd take her for my second THEO in a heartbeat

Professor Steenhuisen is amazingly kind and dedicated to her students. Her Problem of God class is interesting, objective and full of fascinating discussions. I couldn't recommend it enough. I loved her and would take her for a second theology - but I also don't mind 10 page papers and participate in class, two important traits for her class

Amazing approach to a theo class. Read some of my favorite books so far. one test on aquinas, very simple told us the exact questions, 3 papers(10 pgs minimum) would recommend. really made this class a great self reflection. fairly simple. grading is clear. hard not to pass. Is very objective on what she teaches and truly values everyone's opinion

Would highly recommend her Politics of Gender in World Religions class.  Hands down, best professor and class I've taken at Georgetown.  She is very knowledgable on world religions and challenges you to expand your comfort zone.  There's a 15-page paper right off the bat, but there are graded discussions instead of tests which is a plus.

Professor Steenhuisen's course could not have been more interesting. Her emphasis on discussion made the classroom a dynamic place for debate, something I thoroughly enjoyed. If you're looking for another Theology, take this class!

I really enjoyed Problem of God with Steenhuisen, her lectures were fun and engaging. I feel like a learned a lot about theology and different religions. She does assign a 60 page paper (split into 4, 15 page submissions) so do not take her for Problem of God if you are not prepared to really write.

She is such a nice person and the lectures are interesting. She tries to make the class fun and was always really energetic at 9AM in the morning. I would definitely recommend her for Problem of God if you do not mind writing a lot.

Took her for her State & the Veil course. Very interesting course & she facilitated stimulating discussions with students. She was super helpful and friendly. Three short papers & a few smaller assignments. Attendance was optional but the class discussions made it so that I wanted to attend and participate. If she offers this course again, take it.
Can be a bit unclear about grading standards but is a lovely woman who is always willing to work with her students.

She is quite possibly the worst professor in existence. She gives false info about religions. She has a general ignorance about the subject and constantly pushes her Lutheran beliefs on others. The 15 page papers are not at all well explained and the grading criteria is vague at best. She is a sweet person but has no filter. Also 8 am is never good
Professor Steenhuisen was awesome for POG. She's really fun and engages the class in a positive way.

Prof Steenhuisen is one of the most wonderful and kind professors I've ever had. Even as an 8am class, she kept things lively and I was always excited to see what she had in store for us. Two relatively easy papers in the beginning of the year, one group presentation (lots of choices), and a final paper to replace the exam. I'd recommend her.
Smart, very 'present' in class, keeps classes moving and entertaining--charismatic teacher. Very accessible and warm. Highly recommended!

Professor Steenhuisen is extremely friendly and her class is definitely worth it. This was my favorite class and I had it on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. She is really helpful and will basically understand if you have a conflict with something. There is no final but you do have to write 4 15 page papers. Once you start writing though, it is easy.

Very knowledgeable and caring, which is why I took her for a second time. Learned a lot about roles of women/politics of gender in diff. religions through reading and assignments. She spends too much time delineating the tenets of different religion (w/o specific regard to gender politics). Engaging class discussions. Doesn't care about punctuality

Nice lady, reasonably easy grader. Required papers are rather unnecessarily long, but requirements for the papers are clearly outlined. The subject matter is also quite interesting, and wasn't nearly as "preachy" as I would've expected from a gender studies type of class.

A great professor for Problem of God. Cares deeply about the class and her students. Writing load is heavy, but doable and actually can be really interesting to write. Encourages a lot of discussion. Not your typical Problem of God, but definitely recommended.

Incredible professor who has designed an awesome class that blows every other Problem of God class out of the water. Though the writing load is quite heavy, it's spaced out pretty well and in between you really have no other assignments. Fascinating discussions and you will learn a lot about yourself. Prof who truly cares about students.
Fantastic teacher.

Warmest professor I have encountered at Georgetown- seemed to take a personal interest in my essay responses and asked me to coffee to discuss them further. While her four 15-page papers make for an egregious time commitment, responding to her questions about my personal beliefs made me think about myself on a deeper level than ever before.

When in your life is someone going to ask you what you believe and take your answers seriously? This professor is wonderful: patient, deep, insightful, edgy. She pushes you to examine your own core. Those who say she doesn't provide good critique didn't get good grades or do good work.
Stimulating course, taught early in morning. Prof kept us awake and engaged. Mock Trial a good way to learn Supreme Court material, especially if you are headed to law school
Professor is super smart and energetic. Knowledgable about her field, very helpful. If you want to learn about higher consciousness and enlightenment, she is incredibly gifted in teaching these.

This professor is wonderful.  I took her for Problem of God, too.  A 15 page paper is not that hard when more than half of it is just your own musings.  She makes her expectations clear, is available to help her students,  and is accepting of the beliefs of all her students.  Whoever said she's not accepting of atheists or agnostics is full of it.

Great class. Some of the students were a little feminist-crazy, but Prof S. was evenhanded. Three papers and a group project. Papers on the long side, but broken up into small straightforward questions. No final exam or paper which was amazing. GREAT READINGS!

Covered very wide range of pretty interesting topics,which also meant lot of reading(which you sort of need to do for essays).Takes roll.While she listened to the comments,didn't lead discussions quite well(doesn't respond to things out of her expectation).The writing killed me(a LOT, 4 15+ papers),which aimed for quantity over quality.Got A-.

Very nice and cares abouther students. No tests or finals, but there are 4 15-20 page papers per semester.  Half of the paper was your personal reflection but 20 pages is a lot.  I also didn't get a lot of constructive criticism on the papers- I went from an A+ to a C+ with little explanation. If you don't mind writing a ton, an okay class to take.

She's easy in class, but her requirement of four twenty page credos per semester is crazy. To be honest, it really isn't worth while taking this class to fill up your course requirements. She's a nice lady, but not very accepting of atheists and agnostics. If you are Jewish or Christian, you'll definitely love this course.

very easy class, easy A to get ride of your problem of god requirement. you have to write four 15 page papers but there is no final or midterm. however she is very uninteresting her class is pretty much worthless and she has nothing interesting to say but hey its an easy A

She is one of the nicest profs. Understanding & caring, really wants students to like and understand the info. Interesting and relevant topics of discussion. Enlightening class.  Pretty easy too, no final test or project. Take this class.

Brillant woman, passionate about her field,makes you think despite yourself. I didn't want to take this class, but the material and this professor made it worthwhile. Great quotes and stories to provoke thought!

Hands down the best professor I've had so far at the Hotel School. Professor Lawrence is HILARIOUS and gives amazing, informative, and interesting lectures. One of the few classes I always looked forward to going to!

Lawrence is an incredible professor. He's extremely engaging, passionate, and straight up hilarious. He makes food ops extremely fun, and has been my favorite professor I've had at the school. Lawrence is a really good teacher who gives engaging lectures. He knows his stuff well.

Bonassar is the man. He is brilliant and it really shows in his lectures. He is always prepared and knows the answer to everything. The prelims are pretty much impossible though and the homeworks can be a struggle without going to office hours.

Prof. Bonassar is a very good lecturer. The best part about him is that he is very organized in his lectures and passionate about the material. Professor Bonassar is an amazing lecturer. He really makes you want to come to class and you can tell he's passionate about the subject. HW requires office hours, which are very helpful. His test are challenging, but not unreasonable.

Class before the prelim: "You will not finish my test, and the mean will not be pleasant". He basically fit a 3 hr prelim into 50 min. Homework poorly written (needs office hours). But class is moderately interesting.

Professor Kahn is a boring lecturer and gives unclear instructions. The prelims are two essay questions that are 50 points each. There is also a group project that is a major portion of your grade.

I think professor Kahn is given a bad rap. I was unsure on whether to take his collective bargaining in sports class after reading all the reviews below, despite being a big sports fan. Unfortunately this class makes an interesting topic very boring. Kahn is a very nice man but a monotone lecturer. So much more could be done with this class to make it truly engaging and interesting. The group project on salary arbitration can be a hassle and it's a third of the grade.

Not the best teacher around, but a nice guy. Amazing knowledge of subject matter. Do all the readings and go to class and you should do well. Willing to help in office hours/after class. Test questions can be either overly vague or demand an unreasonable amount of detail. Okay overall class.

I don't know why Larry's getting such a bad rap... sure he's not the best teacher around, but he's a nice guy and will amaze you with his sports knowledge. Just do all the readings (which are mostly interesting) and write everything you know on the essay tests and you'll be fine. The baseball salary arbitration paper is really fun. Not a hard class
this professor is the worst ever, someone forgot to remind him that he has a duty as a teacher as well as a researcher...thanks larry

Kahn seems to know a lot about Labor Econ but I could not get past the constant licking of the fingers. The class had 4 professors and I think I learned the least from Kahn - just not a great teacher but very knowledgable.
he is a tad boring, but he can explain the material well.
awful

Not very clear in his explanations.  Lectures tend to be pretty boring.  Funny jokes sometimes.

No Comments
the lectures are really unorganized... he just rambles about whatever he feels like that day.
The class had 4 professors! Kahn's section was the worst. Having 4 professors hurts grades and understanding of the material.

Lawrence's class was one of the most engaging and thought provoking classes I have taken at Cornell. While essays were few and far in between, they required a close reading of the text and a well structured argument. Anyone with the slightest interest or prior experience with philosophy would enjoy his class. I myself am a ChemE maj and I loved it

He was very passionate about the subject matter. Certain parts of the Descartes text were interesting, but after a while the class got repetitive and boring. He is a fair grader and wants to help those in his class. Very approachable. Just watch out for being bored to tears by the seminar and the reading (even though its short). Overall, so-so.

Good professor... very interesting class. He grades very hard though. Getting an A , regardless of how well you write, is pretty damn hard unless you analyze philosophy very well. Getting a B is not that hard though. As long as you do some work, he'll give you a B. Not a lot of reading involved.

He is a good person and really wants to help everyone understand philosophy, but lectures are long,boring, and if you haven't had philosophy before, over your head. Reading is light but EXTREMELY dense, and papers are short but likewise they must be excruciatingly well thought out. My biggest challenge was learning to interpret it. Not a bad class.

Knowledgeable about the text but does not give grades, only comments on papers. thought-provoking but you must really read into the text to get at Descartes' meaning. Very little reading and short writing assignments. If you can analyze philosophy decently, you're set.

Very intelligent and thought provoking. If your interested in philosphy, he is the teacher to pursue. There is little work, but the material is very profound and dense, and for that reason, the grades are relatively low.

Really smart and helpful guy. Definitely knows his stuff and can answer about any question you come up with. One qualm is he didn't grade papers in the Descartes class Fall '04 so it's difficult to get a good idea of how you're doing. If you're interested in philosophy, however, this guy is great.
He is a very good teacher. If philosophy is your subject and you love to discuss descartes, this is the class to take. He is very understanding and helpful. You won't regret taking his class.

Essays are self-reflections about your personality. Other grades are group assignments that are online game simulations. One group receives 100, one 80, 60, 40, and 20.

If you are in failing groups both times, you won't do well in the class (3/5 groups fail each time).He is comfortable giving you 20% on essays that are fully completed and on time.

I'll be honest, I didn't learn much E&M. His lectures are math-heavy and I often got lost. His class is tough, but he truly cares about your wellbeing.

I think other students on here are too hard on Professor Gibbons. He did a solid job of walking us through this class's abundant material. His handwritten notes are very informative, and his assignments are excellent. However, he often seems to have trouble engaging with students' questions, so it's hard to learn from him directly beyond lectures.

Professor Gibbons did a fabulous job with the course. His homework was interesting, his tests were consistently middle-of-the-road fair, and he did a fabulous job making his lectures engaging and interesting. As with any physics class, expect to spend time reading the textbook. This course was a joy.

Professor Gibbons was a very engaged professor. Presenting from a theoretical framework, he started with force laws and derived the rest yet also had cool demos. He was even humorous with relevant Batman quotes. In short, the class was very enjoyable.  Gibbons provided ample assistance outside class with office hours and time to help with homework.
I had no idea what he was talking about during most of the lectures, I tried to talk to him but he refused to help me.

He does a lot of demonstrations which is nice but the lectures are otherwise unorganized and not helpful. The homework is challenging as expected, but the tests are comparatively very easy. Course did not feel indicative of other honors physics courses.
Doesn't seem to understand the material, and no help. Gives the entire department a bad name.
Easiest A of all my physics classes - just don't expect to learn anything from this prof.

Professor Gibbons made his class my favorite of the semester. His knowledge of physics is very deep and insightful, and his explanations are generally very clear. If you ask him for help, he can be a bit vague, but definitely  cares for his students. Also appreciates their feedback. In short, a wonderful mentor!
Useless prof. Avoid if at all possible. Thank god for the TA.

I found Professor Gibbons to be a very good lecturer.  It was challenging because it is honors level, but he did a great job of showing how and when concepts would be relevant. Professor Gibbons is so far the best professor i've had at Cornell.  He always made himself available and really cared that you do well in his class.  Yes, the material was very challenging and i spent many hours studying and preparing for exams, but it is an honors level class.  He made it interesting and encouraged you to do your best.

Yeah, this class was ridiculously hard, but its an honors level at an ivy.  While his lectures weren't the absolute best, he was really helpful and when I went in to visit him during his office hours, he was beyond helpful and he even took an active role in giving me ideas for extra practice.
he doesnt teach you anything.. the class is very challenging.. VERY challenging. if you take this class be prepared to self teach !!

Horrible, horrible professor. If you have any option other then his class, take it! Better off taking the class independent study because his lecture adds nothing to the textbook. The homework takes an absurd amount of time and the tests are confusing and come out of nowhere.
Worst teacher ever!!! Do not take a class with him. It will be a huge mistake! No redeeming qualities!
This class is really hard. Go to every section you can. He is a pretty boring lecturer, and fairly tough. Approachable most of the time for help.
His lectures are a waste of time.  I learned everything from section.  A good lab TA will make labs a pain, but you will ultimately learn much more.
Sections are useful, Lectures are completely useless.  Get a good TA.
The TA's make his class understandable.  Thank your TA every day.

attention cornell administration: GET BETTER PHYSICS PROFS. phyiscs department hands down has the worst professors in the school. tests are harder than anything covered in hw or class. this joker doesnt even give all the formulas and expects you to derive them....
bad, but not quite as bad as everybody says.

VERY boring. I skipped lectures because I knew I would end up sleeping. He also curved everything to a C+. I recommend reading the textbook, learning from the TA, and attending those 0013 classes (led by a really cool prof).
Horrible. Puts you to sleep in a second. Would not recommend but isn't that bad if you don't have any other options.

Almost every professor I've had has at least one redeeming quality. Unfortunately, this one has none.  He's boring, confusing, monotonous, and worst of all does not seem to care about his students.  He cares enough to assign large amounts of work, but not enough to explain concepts or give extra help when you ask.  Only passed thanks to awesome TAs
It's all true...all of it.  Avoid him like the black death.

Yes, this class is painfully dull. Gibbons is very monotonic, and is not helpful when u go to talk to him. I suggest being nice to your TA, and go to the 013's... they're relatively fun, i learned all the material there, skipped lecture, and did well in the class.

Gibbons sucks at life. Worst professor I have ever had...boring, useless, oversimplified lectures. Hard, long, homework on topics we had to 'teach' ourselves. Hard tests, especiallly the nearly impossible final! very unrepresentative of what we were supposedly taught. bad bad teacher.

Worst professor I've had at Cornell.  I'd rather have my head slammed against the side of Rockefeller for 50 minutes than attend one of his lecures.  He cannot teach to save his life (don't bother with lecture), homework assignments are long and tedious, warmups and quizzes can only hurt you. Acts like his is the only class.  Avoid him at all cost!

one of the worst profs at cornell. I suggest reading the textbook closely, but skipping lecture altogether. Prelims and final were very detailed, and mostly focused on material not well-covered on the problem sets. I agree with everyone else, this man cannot teach. It's very boring. Do the reading and you can skip lecture. His prelims weren't too bad, but the final was the hardest test I've taken in my life. I expect the mean to be below 50 (from what I've heard from others and how I did myself).  He ruins a potentially good class. Hard, meaningless homework.

Gibbons wants to teach his students, but he can't, he lacks the ability to keep his students involved, entertained and even interested in the material. he tries and cares, to an extent, but is just a very poorlecturer, and very boring.  You can do alright in the class if you read and do everything on your own and have a good TA. Still a lot of work

Might as well not wake up at 9 am to go to class, sleep in, and then just study on your own or in a group later.  Good suggestion, go to the physics 013 class, now that guy, although old, he can teach and is interesting

Gibbons is boring. He genuinely cares about the students- he wants you to be involved. You can tell, because he tries to involve the class through voting, discussing, and "warm-up" exercises. Problem is, it doesn't work. He can't teach himself out of a paper bag. He's boring, and that's incurable.
SO BORING and cannot teach to save his life. Once he tried to do an example in class - emphasis on TRIED. SO BORING. Lecture was nap time.

This man does not know how to teach, which is a shame because I really looked forward to taking this course.  I'm teaching myself the course at this point.

He came to lectures half-asleep and talked in a monotone with lots of um's and uh's. He didn't say a word that was not in the textbook, so I just stopped coming to class. The warm-ups questions were ridiculous and unscientific. He didn't even know the right time for the final.

You can either go to lecture or sleep through it. I vote sleep through it. He has some interesting demos and he does some interesting derivations. The textbook sucks, but we don't cover anything outside of it. I got a B and I attended roughly a dozen classes. The daily warm-ups he gives suck.

The lectures are boring and hard to follow with his mircoscopic handwriting on the projector slides.  I def learned more by reading the book than by going to lecture.  It's a teach yourself class. You learn a lot from hw and the TAs are gernally very helpful.  Tests arent too bad though.

Terrible lecturer. You're better off printing off the slides from lecture and learning them on your own then going to the Physics Support Cener for any help. His tests are impossible and his problem sets are unecessarily long.

Class is a waste of time. He outlines the book, without adding anything useful.  The tests and hw are both challenging, but barely any partial credit and no calculators-long division takes up more time than the actual work if you know the material.
He goes over really oversimplified stuff in lecture and the problem sets he gives are impossible, but the exams are very fair, and a lot easier than the homework
Probably my favorite professor at Cornell.  Thanks Steve!
Professor Pond is an amazing professor and lecturer. Lectures are thoughtful and interesting, regardless of previous musical experience. Highly recommend MUSIC 1101 for anyone regardless of major.
Professor Pond was easy going and he treats everybody really friendly. If you do all of his assignments on time, you'll most likely get an A
Very kind, helpful professor. Lots of interesting guest lecturers. Class was very easy--only necessary to do readings for assignments. No exams
Great teacher. Did not require a lot of effort - but not necessarily for those who really want to write in an fws.
He's the best. Quite a few papers in this class- and the TA's aren't necessarily the best. But it's totally worth it. His lectures are great.
Fantastic teacher. Professor Pond is a good lecturer, and is easily approachable during office hours. He really knows what he's doing and is incredibly invested in his teaching.
Prof. Pond is always interesting and knows how to spark a good discussion. He's very encouraging and also creates a good atmosphere for learning.

Now that the class is over I wish I had taken it more seriously. Pond is a man genuinely interested in students and really cares about teaching. One of the best profs teaching at Cornell. Should definitely get tenure.

I was only with him for a few days in this class, but got to know him very well.  My friends in the class said they had very little writing to do, and that the topics were awesome (Jazz Fusion).  He is a really nice, fun, and interesting guy, and a good musician too.
Just take this class.  You'd be a fool not to.
poser.
fantastic prof. one of the best.  so intersting, approachable, and professional.

An awesome class. I wrote my final paper on the Beastie Boys. Got an A. What more can be said?!
A great prof. This class is awesome with a lot of visitors to demonstrate the material. Pond is a great guy who remembers your name 3 years after the class. He really cares about his students.
really top-o-the-line
Awesome guy, great drummer, and designed a great course to boot.
Easily the best Professor I've ever had.  ALL his courses rock.
Easily the coolest teacher at Cornell.  Wrote his thesis on herbie hancock!

Incredibly boring and unstructured. Makes it hard to focus let alone understand material. Thankfully the material itself is not so hard so you can pick up from self-study. Class was easy enough to follow, but is more math-oriented than maybe some econ students are prepared for. I found the tests a little difficult but fair, mostly because I just tried finishing the hws instead of understanding how to arrive at the answer. Overall a good class and prof, but he isn't the most inspiring which made class more difficult

While Denti is a nice guy, others are correct pointing out his abhorrent teaching. Lectures are disorganized and non-intuitive, especially for a subject like game theory which isn’t that complex. Provided plenty of study material for each lecture and was very helpful in office hours.

He has a great sense of humor and made the class very interesting. I was afraid to take the class because I saw reviews on here saying it was disorganized, but that was not the case at all. He was very clear in his expectations, posted slides before every lecture on blackboard and posted notes after every lecture. I really enjoyed the class!

This class was always disorganized, but as it went on it became harder and harder to follow. I genuinely like game theory before this class. I passionately hate it now!

With a curriculum that doesn't really follow a textbook and no PowerPoints, missing class makes it almost impossible to follow the class. Unfortunately between his bad handwriting, confusing symbols, and poor explanations, going to class does not help much either. The workload is not too bad, but the class is confusing and super disorganized.

Yo f*ck this class. Literally go in, listen to her say "sigma wah wah" twenty times in a lecture,  then end up asking yourself, 'Da f*ck did I just learn?' TAs don't know the material; claim the class is messed up. Pass a prelim, do some projects, have your ears bleed two times a week, done.

Lecture was well organized, printable slides were very helpful. Could have covered some more content. Didn't dig into fundamentals as much as other courses. This is a pretty cool class and Prof. Gao is definitely in her element. She is clear, organized, and always prepared for lecture. She is helpful outside of class and is always willing to make time to talk to students one on one. She's also really funny!

Prof. Gao is adorable and a really kind person. She is understanding and super helpful in office hours. She really cares about teaching and always asks for feedback on how to be a better professor. She is fair in grading and her tests reflect exactly what has been covered in class and readings.

Professor Gao certainly isn't the best professor that I've ever had teaching me, but then again, the material for 325 is pretty awful to begin with. She improved over the course of the semester, but she needs a few more classes to get comfortable- you could tell she was nervous.

Worst professor I've had yet here. I'm sure she knows her stuff, but tops even Max Zhang for the Incomprehensible-Chinese-Accent award. Often can't get across what she wants to, which can lead to wording on tests being vague and confusing when she tries to get clever with a question. Uses iClickers to ensure you basically have to go, too.

Terrible. Often will give examples in class that she hasn't worked out on her own or that she will not review the answer. Makes mistakes OFTEN. Admits to not having notes prepared for lecture. Will argue with students when she is wrong. More of a grad student than a professor. Has not taught in the past and it shows.

Her chinese accent and lack of good often grammar makes following lectures nearly impossible. She doesn't follow the same methods prescribed in the book. She often makes grammar mistakes in problems which completely changes the meaning of the problem. She often gets in arguments with students over the correctness of her methods.

Unsure of syllabus structure, which can be confusing for students. lecture material doesn't always correspond to prescribed textbook, which makes it doubly difficult to follow the material as there is often confusion between the material in homework and material from textbook.
This is her first time teaching undergrads, so she is a bit inexperienced. She is a nice lady with good intentions, but could use some practice communicating with students.
Very difficult to understand.  Doesn't follow 212 conventions.  Very high pitched voice.  Recommend reading the book instead of listening to lecture.  Doesn't listen to student voice.

I actually enjoyed this class. Biggest tip: sit up front! It can be boring, but you will have a much easier time following her and staying interested. Papers (2) not too bad. Some very specific MC on tests — she likes facts, figures, and definitions — but fair overall. Annoying and pointless sections on Fridays, but my TA was extremely laid back.

I actually found the material and most of her lectures pretty interesting, and the class wasn't work-intensive at all. The prelims were between fair and easy, just do the readings and you'll be fine. Grades essays pretty hard (at least mine were), but I still came out with an A-, and skipped quite a few lectures.  Overall, not a bad professor.

Unengaging lecturer - is more suited to a small class setting. That said, she has to put up with a lot of crap like students talking and being disrespectful, needs to be firmer with such people. Occassionally leaves town on business but will notify students ahead of time and make sure to have offic hours before and after.
Her lecture is boring most of the time, but she is willing to give you a good grade

I took families too and found it to be the same as most people -- easy to do but hard to sit through.  Her teaching style is much more conducive to smaller classes and when I took a few with her I had an amazingly different experience. Things were clear and very interesting -- try it =)

This woman killed what could have been an interesting class.  I feel bad for HD majors.  I took this course as an easy elective and it was just that...
Prof is not a good teacher.  Hard to stay awake in class; very boring. Do not recommend.

She has an odd teaching style...a weird speech impediment thing where she repeats all or most of the words in her sentences before getting a point across.  Lots of reading, but an interesting topic in itself.
She's great! Her lectures are pretty interesting although her teaching style isn't that great. Do the readings and go over the lectures and you'll do fine on the prelims

TERRIBLE, TERRIBLE CLASS. This woman does not know how to teach, or how to stay focused on things that aren't totally arbitrary. Don't bother going to lecture, and just skim the readings, they don't do you much good anyway.

DEAR LORD DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU CAN AVOID IT.  She is a nice lady, my advisor, not exceedingly helpful, doesn't respond to emails.  Terrible lecturer.  You can do zero of the reading (ie practice q's instead), skip class, and get a solid B.

Lectures can be really boring, and there is a TON of reading. Tests are not very easy and grading seems arbitrary at times. Unfortunately, this is a requirement for HD majors, but don't take it if you don't have to!
grading was messed up, she let her TAs grade however they want...so if they like your writing you are set1
Amazing professor. Sometimes we would get distracted from what we are supposed to do, but overall, a great professor.

Professor Shi is very passionate about her subject and it really shows when she is lecturing.  Her lectures were okay (got a lot more interesting at the end) but she has been one of the professor i had at cornell that went out of her way to help us out whenever we had a question.

Lives up to her first name. Easy class but can put you in trouble if you procrastinate everything until the end of the semester. The most socially unaware professor I have ever had. I don't think she even knows what she wanted the students to learn from lecture. Doesn't create slides, speaks in a stream of consciousness manner. Would not recommend.

Pinkus is great.  She's pretty chill and laid-back, and while the class requires a lot of participation, she's pretty understanding of different comfort levels with the language. She is hands down the worst professor I've had at Cornell. She's genuinely mean and seems to be lacking any social awareness in what she says! Her course lacked any structure and she graded so harshly, always looking for specifics that were never originally asked for. AVOID HER at all costs!

Prof.Bennett is a pretty good lecturer that asks a lot of thought-provoking questions. I took the writing intensive section, and dependent on your TA it can be easier or harder. The readings are interesting and she allows extensions on any of the four papers.

Awesome professor! Understands that the readings can be a bit dense and does a great job summarizing any necessary material for exams during lecture. One of the best professors i've had at Cornell. I added a philosophy minor after her intro class

Really good lectures that covered basically everything the readings did, and a lot of super interesting content presented in an engaging way. Loved her lectures. I didn't even take notes, I just sat and listened because she's that engaging. Not a whole lot of work, easy final, and the discussion section is really fun. I loved this class

Can take the most rambling discussion of a student and spit out a perfect one sentence explanation. Excellent, clear, lecturer.
Very clear, helpful, pleasant. would recommend

Great Prof!

she is a great professor- probably the best I had at Cornell University.

Probably the best lecturer I've had at Cornell. Very engaging and passionate about what she's teaching. My favorite part of the class was when she explained the lore behind Hulk Hogan's sex tape. There are no exams which is great

LOTS of help from Professor and all of the TAs in the class. Very knowledgeable, took into account students' physical and mental well-beings, and problem sets and the final were very straightforward and reflected what had been learned in class.

I really enjoyed this professor - by far my favorite at Cornell. My very first class at CU was his biomechanics class; he was hilarious, witty, and so knowledgeable. Do the homework with other students and/or the TAs. Light studying. INCREDIBLE class!

Make sure you go to class because he will test you on things he says, but are not explicitly in the slides. He did throw in a few jokes though. Not the most understanding prof. He throws a lot of information at you at once so be ready to record his lectures. He also is hard to understand sometimes. The test questions are based on minor details so when you study make sure to throughly look through your notes.

Professor Qian is one of the worst professors I've had. Hard to understand lectures. Prelims are ridiculous true/false questions that don't test actual understanding of material. Very rude! Makes fun of questions in lecture. Doesn't accommodate students needs. But! It's easier than the other biochem classes and is more pre-med/vet focused.
Good professor in general! But the material covered is more like cell biology and I am a bit disappointed by that... Would love to see more chemistry.

Professor Qian definitely challenges you. If you want to do above average in his class you need to put in the work for it, but he's extremely helpful if you utilize his office hours. He wants to see you succeed and definitely believes in you.

Avoid if possible. He is not easy to understand and his lectures are so lackluster. Course is very, very interesting and you learn a lot. However, the workload is high for 2 credits. If you put in the work, it's an easy A. Don't just take this course because you want a freebie with minimal effort. 

Great course for pre-health students or people interested in pharma/industry.
Very detailed questions on her quizzes but otherwise courseload is manageable.

If you're NYU, don't listen to these Cornell reviews. Micro w/ Calc is tough in general, but she is the nicest and smartest professor I've had. Very solid choice for micro with calc at Nyu. Good teacher and the material is easy enough to understand on your own. Very nice and willing to help outside of class.

The professor is nice but her lectures are confusing. She goes very fast and often makes mistakes that even confuses herself. The lectures are very hard to understand even when you watch the recordings after.

Professor seems like a kind person but was very hard to understand and the lectures were heavily rushed and disorganized. Don't take this professor.

I took her for microeconomics at NYU. At least for us, she's way better than the reviews say. I read the textbook before her lectures so only had to pay attention when she did example problems. The homework is easy and the tests reflect the class/problem sets. She usually doesn't finish her lectures, but I don't mind because it's less work for me.
Teacher is nice but the course was impossible. You have to teach yourself the material because she goes way too fast. SO many other easier 4000 level

This prof is so kind and caring, but she is the worst professor I've had in at Cornell so far. She's disorganized, not engaging, and sometimes seems to not know what's going on. I had Prof. Andreoni for my montserrat so I don't know what she's like in a language class but she was always trying to be available outside of class and offers great advice for writing assignments.

Prof Andreoni is so sweet and an incredible Italian teacher. Literally one of the nicest people ever and makes an effort to have everyone participate each class. If you get something wrong she is so sweet about it and never makes you feel uncomfortable or embarrassed. Textbook HW is also super quick. 11/10 would take class with her again!
he has a mean-streak.  in class he waste time and picks on students.  I did learn my probablitly and stats but it had little to do with him.  basically he comes off an an entitled academic.
Great prof who makes funny although occasionally mean comments.  Does a great job of making it easy to understand and holding your interest, I'd def recommend it again.

Mildly offensive; sometimes mean to students but unintentionally. Goes off on tangents for very long periods of time in attempts to entertain bored students (which rarely work).  When it comes to actually teaching, he's very good: clear, well spoken, very well organized, fair, good handwriting....overall a good lecturer, but sometimes a major assho
Professor made a boring class, interesting with his jokes, which were funny about half the time, and dumb the rest...overall class was pretty easy

Statistics is a boring subject.  This prof. tries to cut through the boredom by poking fun at students or making decidedly non-PC jokes, both with mixed success.  If you're a sensitive type, don't worry, because you don't need to attend class to succeed.  Learn the easy material from the textbook.  Homeworks graded and scores posted VERY promptly.
out of all my ORIE courses, this is my fav professor. he recently won the INFORMS best OR prof survey. the class is enjoyable and he's good at making difficult concepts easy to understand.

Rips on students in lecture, sensitive types may cry. Tests are straightforward and follow homework pretty well. Lecture is unusual, he sidebars with jokes/news a lot but if you take good notes then you should be set. Also a nice guy at office hours as long as you have specific questions.
makes lots of jokes...be careful...dont eat in class if you're fat
eehh... whadda guy.  Real funny, and when he does teach its clear.  Enjoyable class.
not a great teacher.  joerg def. got me and many others through the class.
Very tough class. His jokes are often harsh and unnecessary.
Funny guy.  Good Prof.  Actually pretty nice if you talk to him.
Spends most of his lecture hr cracking jokes.  However his TA's seemed to teach the course better than he did!
One of the more entertaining professors I've had.  Class is no joke though.  And DON'T ask him for a regrade for your exam!
Barely covers any material.  Thinks he's funny but he's just insensitive.

This class seems like it was created to be an ego boost for the professor. He only promotes his ideals with his textbook (that is hard to follow because it's poorly written). I loved my TA and he made the class bearable but overall McMichael just rambles and is not responsive to students making the class more difficult than it needs to be

Lectures are styled to promote dialog, but nobody responds to his questions. Very knowledgable on the subject matter. Readings outside of the textbook not necessary but helpful. Attendance is counted but participation will get you further. I can see why some people might be at odds with his personality/methods; not for everyone but he tries
Worst lecturer I have had by far. Class time dead silent as he asks questions nobody tries to answer. He also tries to be provocative and ends up being really rude to students. Wouldnt take again.

I had lots of prior classes in this subject, was interested in dsoc and did well. He had good points but he needs to allow for opinions since this material is subjective. Agree with prior comments, professor grades you on saying what he says in class and his books, this subject matter should be flexible and subjective and you should have your own opinion but you are penalized for that. I had lots of prior classes in this subject, was interested in dsoc and did well. He had good points but he needs to allow for diff.

Unfamiliar with economics as it applies to development, and  uninterested in those who are. I think everyone should take this class. It's eye-opening. I feel like I now know how the world really works. But his ideas aren't as organized and clearly expressed as they could be. Powerpoint would help. He's a likeable guy, but I hated that he encouraged people to talk and was rude to them when they did.
Though his lecture style seems dry at first, the material in the class is very interesting.  This is not a class to take for an easy A, but it is very interesting and worth while.
