My top 3 teachers for sure, going in I knew nothing about German. But this professor is well aware that German is not easy and she is willing to do anything in her power to help. Many of times I needed one on one help and she was always there to help. Take advantage of the fact she basically hands you the test before hand with the packets received
Professor Halle is wonderful!! She is one of the best professors at LBCC. She is very friendly and helpful. Test are easy.
Katja is a great professor. She makes learning German fun. shows lots of music videos and film clips. She will always help out if you have questions. Take her!!!

This human rights class was awesome! She led engaging discussions and kept them cordial. I loved that she gave great feedback for papers. She was willing to meet with you outside of class to discuss the big research paper, and she's a great professor to talk with and learn from. I would take any class that she teaches! Challenging but influential.

An awesome professor, but not an easy one. She's so knowledgeable and really makes you work for your grade, but she also cares about your overall success. Her lectures were really interesting and interactive, and her feedback on papers is so helpful. I loved learning from her even though it was a difficult class. Would take again for sure!

Dr. Weber is a great professor. This is a required class, but she tries to engage students with the material. Instead of lectures, students created presentations on the readings, which made them more interesting. You have to talk in class. She gave great feedback on assignments and was so accommodating with covid.

Katja was amazing this course. I still have to finish my last project but the course was extremely interesting and it didn't feel like I was being forced to learn she made it genuinely interesting. She was super easy to reach, not strict, and so caring. I would definitely recommend this course and her!!

Overall she was a very easy going prof and majority of the lecture was online based which was a nice touch. I will say the course content is very boring, I only attended 2 classes but still passed with an A-, which goes to show how easy the content is. The final paper is 3000 words so be wary of that if writing is not for you.
this might be the worst class i've ever taken. whole class needs an entire revamp and a 3k word paper for foundation class is awful. avoid at all costs

Great professor! The course seemed very easy with her and the grading was very generous and clear. All the marks were valid and katja was an amazing grader. There was plenty of reading but nothing to stop me from taking this prof again.

I think she is honestly the best professor. She genuinely cares about her students. During my time, she actually had some tragic family conditions that she needed to attend and yet, she still managed to made the topics of the course interesting and genuinely help us. Very straight forward course, and so interesting, CANT RECOMMEND HER ENOUGH

Mostly done online. Lots of reading but interesting topics at least. Unclear grading criteria but she's an easy marker. Lectures I did attend were very boring could have gone without them. Also a 10 page paper for a GNED is a bit too much imo

super easy class if u put in the minimal work of reading the text, quizzes are easy & from the text, the class is well organized & the term paper has really clear guidelines. if she can tell u put in effort, you'll get good grades. the class is good for self-directed ppl so if you're not good w deadlines/keeping urself on track its prob not for u

Cannot recommend her enough. She chose very interesting subjects for each unit. Class was designed extremely well. She is very quick when it comes to replying to emails and providing feedback. Walked away from this class feeling like I actually learned something. One of the better classes and professors at MRU. Shes awesome!

GNEDs are often the bane of a degree program, but Dr. Pettinen designed this asynchronous course to be accessible & insightful. Completely manageable workload, released most of the content early, so you could work ahead, & very well-curated content. More than fair grading standards. By far the most interesting GNED I've taken so far.

Each week has a quiz that is based off of the assigned chapter of the textbook. Answers are clearly in the readings so it's an easy A+ on each test. Sometimes you had to watch videos and write a para on it, very easy A. One big paper that was very easy to achieve an A on, final exam was same format as quizzes, also easy A. Def a GPA booster.

Katja is my favorite prof I've had this semester. The lessons are self-oriented and very well laid out. She is very clear and concise in her expectations and the requirements of assignments. Read the provided content, write a few papers, and an A will be easy to maintain.

This was such an easy class. It was completely online with no lectures. Katja has a written explanation for each lesson, after you finish watching the documentary or reading texts. She marks very easily and gives great feedback!

Didn't enjoy this class because it was all lectures which made no sense and then her notes made no sense at all. Only way to get a good grade is too read the whole textbook. Also only marked off of 2 test and a final exam which I don't think is fair.
So many readings. Have to do a 8 page term paper in a foundation GNED course

Taking a Gned class should be a GPA booster. Not for this one! Expect an easy multiple choice midterm to later be shocked by needing to write a 3000 word/6 page term paper and an all written final. The final is 2hours to write short paragraph form shot answers and a single spaced 2-3 pages long answer essay format. Avoid this class at all costs.

Katja was a easily approachable, friendly professor. The subject that was talked about in class was very interesting, despite lots of readings, and as long as you paid attention and did the readings you passed. Her tests seemed like jokes, honest to God, because they were so easy -- again, attend the class, you pass basically.
You need to take this class if you are at all interested in Chip Design. Prof. Batten is a great guy. Extremely well organized and fair with grading.

The best lecturer I've had at Cornell so far! Really clear, organized, and enthusiastic, very responsive and open to questions, and while assignments/tests can be difficult it's in a way that stretches and challenges you instead of bewildering you. Wayyyy better than CS2110.

Professor Batten is hands down the best professor I've had at my time at Cornell. You can see how passionate he is about what he teaches, and he gives so much support as long as you put in just as much effort. It's easy to score well in this class but you need to put a lot of time into it. Lots of emphasis on the reports.

Professor Batten was a great professor who taught material clearly and had good organized lectures; I probably got a better understanding of data structures/algos from ECE2400 than CS2110. Also cared about his students' mental health and pushed back assignments if needed.

One of the best professors I've had at Cornell! I'm from another engineering major, took this class for fun. Great lectures, super responsive, you can tell he really enjoys teaching Coursework is reasonable, there's clear criteria for getting a good grade, and you're not curved relative to other students.

Hands down one of the best professors at Cornell. Although some of the reports are rough, you can always seek help at his office hours or his great TAs. I extremely recommend that ECEs take ECE2400 instead of CS 2110.
One of the best professors in the Engineering department, if not Cornell. If you pay attention in class, you will do well for sure. Only hard part was the long lab reports we had to write.
His lecture is great and you do need to put effort to study

Great professor who really goes in depth to make sure you understand each topic he teaches. He's always accessible outside of class and gives helpful feedback on exams/homework assignments. Pretty tough grader and assignments are challenging, but you'll learn so much from this class.
best professor of all time

Batten is simply one of the best professors at Cornell. He is well prepared before every lecture and explains concepts very well. Video-notes are still very helpful. Homework is  long and difficult but you can learn a lot. Project can be challenging, but Batten will help you find your bug. He is as dedicated a professor as they come.

One of the best professors I have ever had (I am a Master's student whose undergraduate institution is not Cornell). He is funny, he knows his stuff really well. He is extremely willing to help students learn. He explains concepts remarkably well. Very enjoyable class. He is tough on grading though.

He is an awesome Professor. He helps us in learning every concept by giving a real-time analogy. All his assignments help us in strengthening our knowledge in all of the important concepts. He makes us approach every problem from a different perspective. We are confidently able to talk about design trade-offs after attending this course.

Hands down one of the best professors in the ECE dept. Class is challenging but the effort from the prof to help out, in class, in his office or on the online forums makes you an expert in his subject. Explanations and notes are clear and always encourages constructive discussions! Labs are hard and do require time, but you'll be proud of the work!

Dr. Deitcher is great. Overall the workload was pretty managable and he was very helpful. The class is very fexible. We are meant to meet 2x per week but are able to get everything done so we only meet once. There are no tests which is great. There are quizzes before each lab so be sure to read the protocol. Lab reports can be dense to complete.

Unclear grading standards, unfriendly/unapproachable, can sometimes sound like he is making fun of you if you are struggling. Grading standards were inconsistent, numbers did not add up and you could not ask about it. Need help? Don't ask, you will be made to feel stupid for asking.
Genuinely wants students to do well. He goes out of his way to award you credit on test questions even if your responses are not ideal. Such a nice person (not just in terms of grading)
Deitcher is a great guy and really wants you to do well. If you participate and put in the effort you can get an A in his class. He is funny and super down to earth.
great guy i really enjoyed working with him

Prof. Goncalo has such a great sense of humor- as others have said, such an asset to the Cornell (and ILR). Just a heads up, his name is pronounced "Gonsalo," not Goncalo. In other words, the C is soft. Take any class you can with him. He's so awesome.

Great professor! Such an asset to Cornell. I've taken several classes with Goncalo and I'd take several more if I could. Very interesting research, clear lecturer, fair grader. He can make any topic interesting.
Love this guy!  He's laid back, funny, and very interesting!  An asset to Cornell.

Professor Goncalo is truly an asset to Cornell's ILR School. He brings enthusiasm, knowledge and creativity. to the classroom and is generally clear, fair and engaging. Outside of class, he is willing to work with students during office hours and share his expertise. Do the readings and participate and you'll do fine in the class. Would take again.

Goncalo is intelligent, funny, approachable, and interesting. Most of your grade depends on papers and participation, but his relaxed lecturing style and receptiveness to student ideas makes participating easy.  Unlike some professors that give seemingly arbitrary grades, well-written papers with good ideas will be rewarded. He is an awesome prof.

class is unbelievably boring and useless. professor comes to class, gets his work done, and everything else left to his horrible TAs. Never understood what the TA wanted out of me, and the fact she didn't speak english didn't help. this class disillusioned ILR.

This class is almost the same thing as HR 2600. The Prof seems to be a nice guy, funny and entertaining, but this class is absolutely useless and boring. His TA's are the worst, and they pretty much control the grade. Things that you would normally find on your own and think are inconsequential have been given scientific name - the class in a n she
Terrible prof, made an easy class hell.
Great guy and I would highly recommend him.
Hated the first prelim. His TAs are awful.

Always has a smile; energetic and easy to talk to. My only qualm was with the first prelim. I knew the class notes backwards, but the prelim was 75% minute details from the book which I kept up with but didn't memorize verbatim. Alot of ppl were surprised. Everything else was fair and he seems genuine. Hope it lasts past tenure.

Easy class, but didn't like the professor. A bit too passive agressive. Lectures online so no need to go to class. Go to section for the grades. Be nice to your TA or they will screw you over. Make sure you report if members of your group are not participating.

the professor is a really nice and great guy. make sure you go to lectures since all of the information he covers is on the exams. he's a fair tester--the TA's may not be fair graders for your essays so go get them regraded.  DO NOT SKIP SECTION! i skipped twice and my participation grade went from 100% to 50%... making my A for the course a B+...

Goncalo is a great prof; funny & entertaining. Liked going to lectures… always interesting. Sections were pretty boring and the prelims were extremely textbook specific- didn’t reflect most important concepts in class- but overall I enjoyed the class and definitely recommend taking it (even for non-ILR majors).

I'm a huge fan! Professor Goncalo is young, funny, and energetic, which is totally much appreciated early on a Monday morning. If you pay attention in lecture- which isn't hard because he's so engaging- and keep up with the readings, you should do well.
Great professor, interesting lectures. Very funny and class is simple. Easy A if you do the work and read the chapters

Prof Goncalo is awesome! He has a dry sense of humor that makes lectures fun to attend. His research is very interesting, and he is very down to earth despite his prominent status in the field. The tests are very hard compared to lectures, so make sure you take very detailed notes from the book or you're screwed.

Professor Goncalo is great! He was always available for office hours to help in any way he could. Class was ALWAYS fun to go to! He is the kind of professor who believes that it is all more than just information but an opportunity to take knowledge with you to help you be a more valuable and observant contributor at your job & in teams.

He is awesome! If you want to learn something in an informal environment -TAKE THIS CLASS.  He actually appreciates it when students disagree with him because then everyone in the class can learn.AWESOME!! Dresses well too!
Easy grader and interesting lectures.

Jack is an amazing professor for intro DEA course, he is passionate and easy going. It was a long semester, and everyone learned so much about design at the end of the year. Highly recommended if you want to look at the world from a designer's perspective.

very nice person. I think he told us that he became a looser grader for us this year but can be hard to reach during the limited office hours he offer cuz everyone wants to ask him about clarifications/feedback

The class was interesting and took me out of my comfort zone. Jack was also very accessible through office hours and would get back to you on any questions about the assignments. It did get difficult to sit for three hours and listen to lectures for an extended period of time.

Unclear expectations and always returned grades very very late. Has his own method of calculating grades and does not tell students how assignments are weighted. Has office hours and is usually accessible.

i enrolled in this class. I guess it was my fault for not understanding the times but this class is three hours long. You sit in the studio for three hours. the class seemed interesting, but it was boring and long. i switched out within the first week bc i just couldn't sit in a class for that long. the class also seems hard and confusing

Jack has been a great professor! I've really enjoyed taking his class and even though it's a lot of work, I feel like I learnt a lot. You'll get to know your classmates really well if you work on projects in the studio so you should do that. Also, presentations take a lot of time so be prepared for that! Jack's feedback is very helpful though.

At first, this class really stressed me out and I thought Jack was really intimidating but this class has been my favorite class at Cornell still. I got to know all of my classmates really well because we spent a lot of time in studio but we are all still good friends!

You might be intimidated by Jack at first but honestly he's awesome. He really gets to know his students and everything he does is for a reason. You will spend many, many hours in the studio, but it's worth it. I think i got a lot more out of this class than any other at cornell so far. So long as you commit, i definitely recommend this class =]

Very tough to get full points on the projects, but you get a lot of feedback so you always know why you get the grade you do. You will definitely invest a lot of time in this class, but Jack is always willing to help and is a really great guy and professor.
Gave out assignments that the class didn't understand, then made extra work for the class.
Very good with students and very involved, and cute and funny in a hippish way. Expects a lot from the students but is equally responsible in providing feedback.

You will spend HOURS (anywhere from 4-15) doing each [weekly] project, esp when you get into the second half of the semester. The content has nothing to do with interior design as much as just general ideas of color/light/form/etc. It's a tough course but you do learn a lot & Jack is really good. The reading summaries are tedious/time-consuming tho
Jack's class made me decide to transfer out of Arts and Sciences and into Human Ecology so that I could major in interior design... = ]
No Comments
I really liked Jack's DEA 101 class.  The projects were pretty interesting, esp the latter ones.  He gave useful comments and he's a funny guy.

First of all, Jack's classes are really interesting.  The guy knows a ton and his lectures cover a lot of ground.  On the other hand, there are too many projects and it is almost impossible to get questions answered in class or during office hours.

This guy is cool as long as you are liked by him.  Do your work and maintain his interest in you and your work and he will treat you well.  He likes good music and is overall a pretty fair teacher.  If you are at Cornell and on the Interior Design track in Hum Ec, you will most likely have him a few times so keeping a good rep with him will be pretty important.
He's a very helpful professor with a strong grasp of knowledge from various fields. He cares about his students. Serious, but funny. Difficult, but very fair.
No Comments
He's pretty cool and very helpful. The class is sometimes challenging but you will get through it!

Freed is, without a doubt, one of the worst professors at Cornell. His exams are completely unfair and frequently test material that he skips over in lecture/on problem sets. The textbook is almost completely useless, the lectures are boring and riddled with mistakes, and problem sets are verbatum from other sources. Do not take any class with him.

Worst professors I've had at Cornell. Condescending, boring & lazy. VERY unstructured course.  Takes oset questions from 6th or 7th edition Adtkins manual (find at Mallott Lib). Don't waste your time going to class. Know diff n integration COLD, read the book and complete problems from adtkins books/sln manuals. Prelims very different to Psets.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Clearly does not care about the students or the course. Doesn't allow equation sheets on the exam and emphasizes derivations on exams. He does not make any of the questions on his own, and instead takes them from other sources. Do not take any class with this professor if possible.

Very unapproachable and not very helpful when asked. Can't decide if he doesn't care or is completely lacking in tact. BUT, clear and well-organized lectures, reasonable tests and homework assignments. Gives generous amount of time for both. A solid if not inspiring teacher.

Well i had Freed this past semester for Chemistry 290 lab -- what can you say? He was fine I suppose ; reviewing lecture notes morning before a quiz = good quiz score ; I felt like I failed the final but still got in the A in the class since the class is curved to an A (it's not meant to be hard).  Anyways, it was a fine lab class; Freed was good.
Simply terrible.  He ignores questions and never smiles and his exams are completely unfair.  Didn't learn a thing from this class.
No Comments
i heart freed

If there were a more disinterested professor here, Freed would kill him/her, because i think he loves to be the worst professor EVER at cornell.  Impossible prelims, boring lectures, terrible TA's...if a visiting student ever saw this class, they wouldnt come to cornell.
I'm pretty sure his lecture notes are photocopies of our textbook pages...
No Comments
No Comments

Really nice guy who clearly knows what he's talking about if you talk one on one, just isn't great at teaching it in lecture. You need to teach yourself most things to do well on quizzes. The final was unreasonably hard.

He teaches as if you already have a background in real estate. Does not have engaging lecture style at all; he reads off of the slides which are hard to comprehend anyways. The good thing is he curves a lot at the end of the course.

Just a really bad professor. Basically stood in the front and mumbled so sit up close if you want to hear him. Tests were hardly related to lecture/hw material. I'm getting the real estate minor and his intro class almost made me give up on real estate. If you want a good teacher, take Lebret. He actually cares about students and learning.
Great class, definitely difficult but worth it if you have any intention of getting into Real Estate.  Used more concepts in my summer internship than from any other class
Nice class to go
if you are interested in hospitality real estate finance, thats the way to go
Corgel is self described "Academic Traditionalist." Lectures are dry, but information is very useful. Concept comprehension requires an interest in Real Estate Finance
Great class, prepare to take it in the ass though

EDUC 2610 is an annoying and tedious class. Much of the curriculum and content in every 3 hour class period is pretty much spent on discussing how good and valuable the class and program (Intergroup Dialogue Project) is. There's lots of talk of changing society through education, but this class does nothing for that goal. Lots of work and it sucks.

An aimless class with no goals or meaningful takeaways whatsoever. Weekly sessions are led by student "facilitators" and 3 hours long -- but still accomplish nothing. Tons of reading that serves no purpose b/c irrelevant or repetitive. Strict grading criteria for annoying papers. Can't discuss grades over email as they claim it's "against FERPA."

EDUC 2610 is the worst class I have taken at Cornell. 25 students have a pointless discussion for 3 straight hours. The content is useless and you spend the first 8 weeks covering common sense topics like respect. I got a B on my first paper, and I only got an A after I started making up stories about discrimination (that's what they want to hear).

I studied under Professor LaFeber back in the late 1970s as an undergraduate at Cornell.  He is the best teacher I've ever had.  He has the ability to inspire you with his command of and passion for the material.  He demands excellence.  The lectures were a high art form, organized around a 3-word outline and including great anecdotes. Magnifcent.

I took three classes from Walter Lafeber back in the Stone Age, and they changed my life.  My son is now a Cornell undergraduate; I truly regret that he will not be able to benefit from someone who was at one time brilliant, articulate, and compassionate.
Prof. WLF is perhaps the best professor I've ever had.
One of the best profs at Cornell!

I've had him twice and have always been amazed at his amazing grasp of such a wide range of material. His reputation as one of the best profs on campus is more than deserved, but on top of that he is one of the most down to earth, caring people around. One of those professors you tell your kids about thirty years out of college.

I did like this class, but I think LaFeber is far too hyped. I thought some of the stuff he talked about was random. Get to know him personally and you'll appreciate the class -- and this professor -- a lot more. Don't let his rep scare you into not coming to office hours.
I had Walter LaFeber for American History in 1962-63. A wonderful teacher. I thought I knew everything then and didn't get as much from his class as I should have.

This guy is the best prof. that i have had at Cornell. His lectures are literally works of art. This is the type of class where you could just sit back and soak in the material becasue it's so interesting. You must have him before he retires.
obviously one of the better lecturers at Cornell, but can also guide a discussion in a seminar. Take any and every course he offers.

I took a class with Walter LaFeber in 1998 and I still remember it!  He is an amazing lecturer.  I thought the tests were fairly easy as long as you paid attention and skimmed his book.  This was one of the best courses I have ever taken.

Although in semi-retirement, Prof. Lafeber is one of the foremost scholars in the field of US Foreign Policy, and it shows. Although he uses his own book, the lectures are outstanding. Tests are pretty difficult, but manageable.

Take him while you still can, he is getting up there in age. But he is one of the best professor's at Cornell. Clear, persuasive, and its amazing how he constructs his lectures. Try to attend his optional sections, though I only made about half of them.
I was blown away by the course I took with Prof. LaFeber. His lectures were works of art. He was incredibly accessable outside of class, and it's clear that he enjoys interacting with undergrads.
Unbelievably good! Best prof I've had at Cornell. Gives amazingingly organized and detailed lectures totally from memory. Very nice man who cares greatly about his students.
Excellent
interested  & supportive
Lectures were very entertaining and informative.  Tells a good story.

AWESOME professor. He's hilarious, knowledgeable, and easygoing. You can have a conversation with him about absolutely anything in the field of behavior - he knows everyone too. He also really wants everyone to do well in the class. Wish it had gone on the whole semester, rather than occupied six hours every week just for the first eight weeks.
What a waste of money. Very insecure and needs to leave Cornell.

Professor Boudry is one of the best professors I have had at Cornell. His lectures are fast, but he breaks down real estate finance into bite sized pieces that most everyone can understand. He is clearly passionate about what he does and this class will prepare you for an entry level real estate finance job after graduation.

While Prof. Boudry definitely knows what he is talking about with regards to real estate, he also expects students to come into the class with a much higher level of knowledge than is gained through the principles (pre-req) class. His expectations make it impossible for the majority of the class to succeed and his midterm was overly difficult.

Worst teacher ever! I don't recommend him at all. He is not clear at all, he alluded to curving the class which he doesn't. Take this teacher only if you are willing to slave yourself to get a "C". Also uses out dated software from the 80s to compute linear programing. Test (2 of them) are really hard (6 questions each). Never would take him again.

your mental health will deteriorate taking this class. By far one of the hardest 280 class professors on campus. multiple papers, presentations, book readings, as well as a 2500 word research paper final. do not take if you have a lot on your plate already. This class alone should classify as 5 classes.

Dr. Dror is a good professor and easy to work with when asking for help on assignments. Lectures did not matter as we were never tested on them, but attendance still mandatory. It felt like a waste of time since our final is just a paper. Lots of reading outside of class, a lot of writing too but it is a writing-intensive course.

If you value your time and mental well-being do not take this class. Attendance is mandatory, 4 page paper for any quiz grade below an 85. Cant read her handwriting and she grades ridiculously hard. Dont expect any help from her except for a "tough luck" attitude. Steer clear

If you're having any sort of personal or mental problems, don't take this class. It takes up a majority of your time and is graded in the most ridiculous way I've ever seen. The amount of reading makes it seem like this prof expects this to be your only class that semester. Failing a quiz (<85) means a 4 page paper in your future. DONT TAKE!!!

I'm currently in History 352 and there's a lot to say. Her class is extremely time-consuming, but you will definitely learn a lot. Reading is required in order to pass the class, but the quizzes are very easy. You will be reading entire books weekly so plan ahead. Write your essays as if it were going to be read by a 5th grader.

I took her for two semesters. The first time, I got a C. But this past semester I go an A. She can be a tough grader but she just wants the best out of you. Her lectures are very unbiased as she tries to give you both perspectives. I learned so much from her classes. Also, read the books she assigns. You will be quizzed over them
Not an easy class, but she'll help you get a good grade.
I meant to say she is very helpful!!
I meant to rate her high on helpfulness!!

Taken my last semester, this is the only real/serious college class i feel like i've taken.  Dr. Dror is very passionate and knowledgeable and expects her students to read, participate, and have opinions.  Be prepared for a lot of reading and essay quizzes and exams.

The class is not difficult if you read the material. There's no final for this class, one major paper, discussion weekly and quizzes every week. The professor gives you great feedback and is quick to respond. Highly recommended!
Great Instructor!

Dr. Baron is a great professor and excels in a small classroom setting. However, he does not provide any digital notes, and some aspects of the course do not map to a specific section of either of the two textbooks he uses. Due to this, you will need to take diligent notes to understand the material.

This is for the Quantum Computing Special Topics course. Prof Baron is great, he cares about making sure everyone has an enjoyable and productive experience in class. His lectures aren't so exciting, but he tries to be engaging. The class had short weekly homeworks and quizzes that weren't too intense. Not a harsh grader, and very flexible.
Cares about students.

His material is extremely scattered and hard to follow and his lectures are boring but he is very sweet and open to feedback. His tests and assignments are hard but he curves just about everything so it is easy to get an A

His tests are open notes. However, he doesnt make tests represnetative of homework or examples. He puts questions and applications on the exam that we have never done or practice. Quote from the last midterm "Number 5 is a question you have never seen before." Not good at teaching/communicating material.

Took him last semester. He is absolutely amazing! He REALLY cares for his students and is open to feedback. His lectures are not the best but still pretty good. Although there are a lot of hwks and projects, all the material is super helpful. Tests can be kind of tricky but still very doable (all tests are open book/open notes). Curves if needed
Has gotten much better at teaching 308, He is very receptive to feedback and input from students

Simply put, Dr. Baron is an atrocious professor. He barely understands the material himself and so will not be able to help you with the assignments besides reading out of the solution manual. His lectures are poor and he skips many examples as he can't solve them. And not to mention, he is very obnoxious to students. Do not take his class.
He wants explanation for everything. Will take of points if you don't explain. Hand writing is worst possible. Made an easy class unbearable and very hard. Wish I could Rate 0

The grade is only three exams. If you go to class, follow the study guide, and read the book you will do well. Attendance wasn't mandatory but the pop quizzes are extra credit if you are there. I got an A as a lazy student. Overall good teacher would take it again.

His lectures felt long and drawn out, but he taught well. Personally, I didn't find the study guides helpful but there is a Webex before each exam where you can ask questions so it makes up for it. There is no homework or classwork just three exams, so there is a lot of pressure to do well on all them. Solid 7/10 class.
Really funny and engaging professor! Great lectures and he gives good feedback on essays.
super arrogant and condescending

Dr. Walter is a really nice guy and gives good lectures. Only thing I hated was they were super long sometimes. You can read the textbook (I never did though). Discussion posts weekly but you only had to do 7. 2 tests, 1 paper. He held webex sessions before every test which were helpful. Also responded fast to emails. Easy class.

Dr. Dror Walter was a great professor and he provided a lot of information on the communications. But this is quite the difficult class. Their is 2 exams and one essay as the final. The final essay was pretty hard. Def not an easy A and requires a lot of effort.

I took this class in the Spring of 2021 and Professor Dror was so awesome. His lectures were so informative (screen recording of a PowerPoint) and he was very good at actually teaching the information rather than a learn on your own kinda thing. Although I'm a pre-med and not necessary looking at a career in clinical psych I've taken his courses just because of how great of a prof he is.

Professor Segal is one of the very few Clinical professors on staff. He's very caring about his students and his lectures are interesting. Tests are fair and the final was actually incredibly fun. Another rater commented on email, it's much better to go to office hours, he gets a ton of emails and isn't quick to respond but he definitely cares!

by FAR my favorite professor at Cornell.  he is laid back, smart, direct, helpful, and really cares about his students. exams are fair and easy to do well on as long as you prepare. bonus: he usually makes his multiple choice questions have 1 choice that is clearly a joke, simultaneously making it easier and entertaining
Definitely one of my favorite professors/classes at Cornell. Professor Segal is funny, interesting, and down-to-earth. The tests are fair and as long as you study you will do fine.

Segal is nice enough, but his lectures don't really have any substance. Him reading hundreds of words off slides and acting out Hamlet are annoying. But course is simple, only two prelims and final. Readings are fairly light and you can probably do well just by going to class and review sessions. Easy A and all in all worth the occasional headache.

Dr. Segal is an interesting teacher. He wasn't particularly well suited to be a lecturer for such a large class but he kept things interesting with personal anecdotes. However, his tests were at times unclear and relied heavily on insignificant details aimed to see if you attended class (not if you actually knew basic psych).

By far the best professor I've had at Cornell so far. I learned so much from him. The course challenges you to think about yourself and the people around you in a different way. Absolutely loved it, and him.

This professor is ridiculously boring. I fell asleep every class 5 minutes in. I had an urgent issue during the semester, sent all my professors an e-mail and he was the only one who didn't respond. I e-mailed him 6 more times in the next week or so and he ignored every one. He obviously doesn't care about his students.

He's really nice but it is hard to get a lecture of 900+ interested in intro to psych. The tests are very fair if not a little easy. If you are interested in the material, take it with him--also visit his office hours he is SO SWEET.

Loved this class and Professor Segal.  The tests are extremely easy, if you study.  If you do not study, people say they are hard.  Studying really pays off in this class and if you put in the effort you will get at least an A-.
Test wasn't the most clear but the gives you 10 free points a test.
Overall good very fair test but questions are sometimes not related to psych

Harry's ability to tie anecdotes to subject matter is uncanny. Unfortunately he consumes too much time reading his own lecture slides and acting out scenes from Hamlet. As such, class was very hit-or-miss. Psychopathology was not the best psych course I've taken, but it was still worthwhile.

Professor Segal is so entertaining and makes the material interesting! Although lectures can be a bit scatter brained, he tells really great personal anecdotes from his therapy career and cares for the success of his students! One of my favorite professors at Cornell for sure.

Harry Segal is AMAZING. There's a reason Adult Psychopathology fills up in less than 5 mins during CoursEnroll. He brings the material to life w/ anecdotes about previous patients, etc., and soothes the class with his "therapist voice." He's the same way in office hours, and truly cares about students. A little eccentric, but a great prof.

The class can be hard to get into for sophomores since it is so popular, but definitely take it if you can and if you have any interest in clinical psych or are premed. The workload is not bad, and he is such a fun, easy-going lecturer. A tad disorganized but he really cares about his students.

Segal is the BEST. I've had the pleasure of getting to kno him thru many classes, & the more I learn from him the better my life is. He is genuine, wicked smart, and humble. Not even kidding, I'm naming a kid after this man. He will require you to work and really engage yourself, but you owe it to URSELF to take all his classes! Def changed my life

its only the second week of class and is probably my favorite professor in four years. absolutely hilarious, able to inject humor into his lectures to keep things interesting. HIGHLY recommend prof and class

Entertaining and fun class, going to lecture was the highlight of my day.  Yeah he doesn't really know the neuroscience and isn't totally organized...but still a great class.  He tells lots of anecdotes about patients which makes the material come to life.

hands down the best class i've taken at cornell in 3 years. prof may not be the best at teaching the science parts of the class, but he chooses good textbooks that explain it & everything else about the class makes up for it. amazing professor who's really nice, really likes teaching, does it well & wants to help his students learn the material.
great guy and excellent, engaging lecture.
absolutely wonderful! could not have survived my undergraduate years without him
interesting material but very poorly organized which makes it difficult to fully understand
Segal is not at his best in this class. The readings are great, but lecture is simply rehash and is not worth the time. An easy A, meets only once a week. Always late.

Segal brings a wealth of clinical experience into the classroom; it's not about memorizing diagnostics but really coming to know what it is like to be mentally ill. He genuinely cares about students and remembers names from a 300+ lecture. Can't teach the neurobio worth anything but is incredible for everything else!

segal's awesome, very funny and understanding, interesting topics with even more interesting case reviews. exams are fair, verging on easy if you go to lecture. really good with psychological aspects of class, not so much with science (slides are copies of textbook material) but TAs covered that. really wants you to do well in his class!
Starts class late EVERY lecture then often runs over.  We took a prelim 5 weeks ago and still have not received grades. Its unacceptable.
the most wonderful professor i've ever met. i would be lost if it was not for his encouragement throughout my undergrad years

What a lovable guy! The girls go nuts for him because he is such a sweetheart. Gives you practical pointers for life. Lectures are ridiculously interesting because they feature case studies, readings are interesting as well. Tests are very fair. Exam reviews pointless because they are disorganized.
This was a great class, comes highly recommended. Not only is the material interesting, but the tests are extremely fair. Go to office hours if you can. Segal's a lot of fun!

He was one of the most incompetent teacher I've had at Cornell. I don't know why there are so many good reviews of him. While he may be a good "person," his credibility in teaching this class is dubious. You'd come out of the class learning very little and many useless accounts in his lectures.
No Comments

this man is amazing. he's the cutest thing i've ever seen my life. you can tell he really likes what he's doing and cares about people. he's got an adorable way about him and a great sense of humor. he's emotional and sweet and generally a great guy. he uses a lot of stories and examples. i look forward to his class all week. he just makes me smile

I was very disappointed by this class. Readings were assigned that were later "unassigned" right before an exam after some people who tried to keep up with the work might have done them.  Don't buy the books. Professor Segal has a hard time keeping his mind on the lecture and makes many tedious digressions.  Prepare to be bored or angered.

Prof Segal is a great pedagogue in many ways, but know this: he teaches using examples and emotionally connecting with the students. This is great for about 80% of the course. However, he is NOT great at teaching "systems", which is the other 20%. He reverts to his use of examples, but the mechanisms often go unexplained at the fundamental level.
Best professor ever
Wonderful professor, and one of my favorite at Cornell. Excellent class, and I highly recommend taking a course with him! Very understanding and good at interacting at a personal level

3 years out of Cornell, and I still think back to the days of senior year psych field practicum with Harry. I highly recommend Harry and his classes. He is a great person, a great teacher, and a great academic. (try to get him for your advisor too!)

Prof. Segal is great! I looked forward to his lectures every day. Often tells stories and anecdotes to illustrate the point. I enjoyed his lectures so much that I went to office hours just to be able to talk to him. Great, funny guy! One of the best profs I've had, and the class was very interesting.

Prof Segal is awesome. His lectures are engaging and informative. The tests are incredibly fair. You will do as well as you want to in this course. I wish there were more profs like Segal, who actually loves teaching.

Harry is one of the greatest people you will ever meet in your life, and one of the most respected profs at Cornell. Standing in line for office hours is very much worth the wait. He has a quirky sense of humor, and he is brilliant... and effectively covers very interesting material! Plus he's the cutest person ever who simply makes you smile!
One of the best lecturers I've ever had. Very interesting material and an amazin teacher. Grading; not too hard...he'll make it easy on you if you study.
I know!he is such a cutie.  /the most attractive prof i've had in 3 years!  and the best teacher too. :)
He's in over his head.  He gets his feeling of worth from the students around him.  But he's a total sweetie, a teddybear, and a great lecturer.  C'mon guys, give him some hotness points!
One of the BEST in Cornell, period.

dr. segal is very warm and cares a lot about his students. i have had a lot of contact with him over my time at cornell, and he has helped me out with many things. sometimes he is frazzled, yes, but his interest in his subject matter and students is genuine!

Segal is charismatic, but anyone who has worked closely with him will find out he's VERY insecure & needs admiration from EVERYONE. He is always overbooked and cares first and foremost about his ego. Academically he is not helpful: he only wants to lavish praise bc he needs it so badly in return.

Segal is one of the greatest professors Cornell has.  He's the sweetest guy around, and he really makes sure you know the material.  The man has his own cappuccino machine in his office.  Gotta love him.
A must take class with a must have professor! Don't miss out on this great opportunity to learn and be entertained while doing it.

One of the best professor at Cornell ever! He is so smart, caring, funny and inspring!!! Cornell is luck to have him. He tells some amazing stories to illustrate his concept and broaden your perspectives. Amazing TAs, very dedicated.(especially Bernie).

Professor segal made my semester, always looked forward to his 10:10 class.  Amazing lecturer, very engaging and caring.  Presented interesting stories and illustrated his concepts very well. Amazing professor, we need to get him tenored.
Absolutly wonderful. He is funny, intersting, informative, and -- nice! This is the best class I've ever had.
FunFUnFun.EasyEasyEAsy.
SO easy!!!!!! very very informal and scatterbrained!!!

A compassionate scatterbrain.  Hints of pretension, but that’s relative.  He may be the most empathetic professor Cornell has, but is alas cursed with a capricious lecturing/grading ethic.  Not to worry.  He’ll make it easy on you.
The best professor I've ever had.
Harry Segal is amazing.  Great Lecturer. Captivating.  A bit disheveled...but who cares?
the most awesome prof EVER!

He's an amazing lecturer. Because he's a clinical psychologist, he knows how to talk TO you, not AT you. Tells the funniest stories! He could be a little bit more organized and clear with what we need to know, but Segal is amazing!!
Tells interesting stories and brings a sword to class.  Very friendly, interesting guy.  Likes to talk about his daughter too much, and gets many guest lecturers when he doesn't know the material.
No Comments
Best prof at Cornell
Most incompetent professor ever, No organization, Give no indications or false indications of what is expected, Completely arbitrary grading
No Comments

Amazing and respected professor. No one better with this much experience to teach this class. Doesn't overcomplicate anything and provides great understanding with real life examples. Exams are pretty easy and writing assignments are fair. Listens well, all past reviews are talking about harsh grading from TA's, writing assignments are now P/F.

Love this guy. He gave me an A I'm pretty sure I did not deserve by the numbers. Attendance is not mandatory, but he tends to let the class out early. Tests are pretty easy - he tells you more or less what will be on them. Other assignments require minimal writing. Best of all, you get to learn from the legendary Harry Katz

Amazing and knowledgeable professor. Three exams, non cumulative. His outlines are what to study for the exams, and the cases discussed in class. No need to read the textbook if you understand the lecture, and video lectures are available on Canvas. Class average for Fall 2022 was an A
good lecturer, literal decades of experience on the matter. he's literally written textbooks on the subject. doesn't make the class harder than it needs to be. is a fair grader and professor.

I had Katz in Fall 2021 and he was wonderful. He gives outlines with everything you need to know for exams so that you don't have to take notes in class. You don't need to read or even buy the textbook to understand the course, just make sure you skim additional readings. He is extremely knowledgeable and his lectures involve student participation.

Katz is cool and you can tell he cares about his students. He's pretty laid back, but the TAs are VERY harsh graders and papers require super specific verbiage, so watch out for that. Exams are fair. Watch the prerecorded video lectures and follow the discussions about the movies/case studies and you'll be fine.

Prof Katz is the best. The only thing that's hard is the assignments are graded by TAs who grade harshly. Lectures are actually really interesting and the tests are extremely fair. The way he handled online class was probably the best approach, you just watch a video lecture and don't have to even go to the zoom unless you want more clarification.

He seems very nice and chill and knowledgable but the TA's are the ones doing the grading and they're HARSH. there are several papers and a project but he lets you work in partners or groups of 3 so its more manageable. The assignments seem simple but again, they grade harshly so beware. The tests are very fair though :)

His class is the best introduction to labor relations! He's so passionate about his subject and wants you to learn. Plus he's the kind of professor that wants everyone to do well! Readings are recommended but not required!
His extensive experience in labor relations makes lectures interesting Lectures are on videonote, so you don't have to attend class
Lectures are interesting at most times. TAs are really harsh graders... Textbook is not necessary for this class, just attend all lectures and you'll do fine!

Professor Katz has a ton of knowledge and experience in the field of labor relations. You can really learn a lot from him and his lectures were always interesting. He's also very approachable and clearly cares about his students.
Great guy who has clear expectations. You really learn a lot from him.

Great professor, you're absolutely going to learn a lot.  The material isn't really that hard, and if you go off the lecture outlines you'll get a decent grade.  Grading is harsh at some points, but overall if you put the effort in you should be able to get a good grade.

The grading is completely arbitrary. His lecture outlines are vague, he rambles about nothing every class, it's boring. This is a bad class overall and he's just a bad professor. Doing well is based on luck.

Harry is a pretty good prof. He knows the subject and the class is pretty damn straight forward. Go to lecture, take notes and read the book, and you'll be fine. Mock bargaining isn't really that bad, just need a decent group who cares. Other than that, it's a pretty straight forward class that is very doable.

Seems pretty nice, if not a bit arrogant. The course is horrifically boring. Mock bargaining exercises are especially painful (doubly so when you're grouped with morons, as I was). The class is easy, at least.

He's excellent. This class (taught by Katz) should be the 1st course every ILRie takes. Great introduction to the field of ILR. Katz has an amazing clarity of thought + cool and confident lecture style. Doesn't bog you down with minutia and trivialities. He's about the big picture and he gets it. And he's a reasonable human too. Strongly recommend.
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! His grading style sucks, and the class is confusing as hell... The man is full of himself! If you don't believe me, take it!
I hope he wasn't appointed dean because of his teaching skills...

Collective Bargaining: Wrote the book, teaches the class, runs the school. Very knowledgable, guest speakers were enjoyable, material over all though is kind-of boring. CB not my thing, but if you have to take it, take it from Katz.  Class size is very large, mock bargaining project is enlightening.
Katz is very knowledgeable. It is a shame he is not a great conveyer of that knowledge in lecture. The material in class is interesting at times, but redundant and painful at others.
He was amazing at teaching this stuff, but then, he wrote the book too
Good professor, doesn't try to trip students up on exams, papers, etc.
When it comes to this material, Katz is THE guy to talk to. Has a lot of passion for the material; will help you out if you need it, as long as you study what he says to you shouldnt
awesome, katz is the man it's a shame he didnt get the position of dean take him before you graduate it's a must!!!!!
Fair good guy.
Great Prof
No Comments

plays AKB48 in front of class, singing in class with baritone voice
lets you explore your own interest and guide your research, overall pretty good
Good professor, good class, good material.
There was a lot more reading and response writing than anyone expected. Other than that, I enjoyed the class. He really knows his stuff, and it was fun learning how to play the instruments.

Chris is a great teacher. He does expect you to do the work and show up for classes - nothing unusual there. But actually, the last month of classes is just playing the instruments - no reading or stuff. No final or midterm! And Chris is a friendly guy and is willing to help out and accommodate people in terms of assignments.

Unclear, poor time management (ESP when deciding how much work is appropriate for the class), expect to have unruly amounts of reading and responses due, and be reading 3 page long directions over-complicating every assignment. Could be a fun class, Miller takes it way too seriously, Disappointing.

Knows a TON about Gamelan. But he makes it really really hard to take this class as something enjoyable. You can tell through the assignments and his attendance policy that he's being over-serious about it. The assignments are pretty ridiculous and you will be listening to entire CDs as well as writing multiple page papers per week, don't even try

Knowledgeable in Gamelan but extremely impatient and will never allow you to miss class, or he'll pull down your grade. Over schedules performances and poor time management for rehearsals. Expect to endure numerous extra classes, especially during study week. If you are unable to learn your part fast enough, he will replace you without warning.

Profesora Hendrickson is an incredible instructor! Classes are very engaging, and she is very friendly and helpful. She genuinely cares about her students. There is a lot of HW, though, so be ready for that.

Hall is very kind, fair, and understanding. Gives extensions + lots of extra credit opportunities. However, this class had a TON of busywork. 2 group projects/presentations, 3 or 4 writing assignments/essays, a very long midterm, graded participation. Everything was take home and he gives a lot of time though. Lectures are very in depth and good!
Loved his immigration class! Is super kind and caring, was very accommodating after we shut down in March.

Professor Hall is outstanding . He is an extremely knowledgable prof. and does really well communicating the material. Beyond this, he is also very caring and will go above any beyond to make sure you understand the material and he also works to understand you as a student. Highly recommend this professor.

I'm a second semester senior - easily one of the best classes (if not the single best class) I've ever taken at Cornell. If you put in the effort, you will do well. He is organized, clear, and the lectures are some of the most engaging I've ever listened to. You also learn a ton, and he is very understanding and supportive. So glad I took this.

Hall was a really good professor! His lectures were easy to follow and he did a great job breaking down concepts so that students could understand them. Obviously very passionate about his work and wants students to succeed. The Stata component of the class was a little confusing, I wish we could have covered it in lecture as well as in discussion.

Great prof, lectures were interesting and easy to follow. I'm not a "math person" and I was dreading this class, but I ended up enjoying it! Hall does a great job of showing the step-by-step processes for each equation and his slides are easy to reference for the psets. Psets take a while but he allows you to do corrections to get some points back.

Great guy, very clear lectures. The course is well designed, HWs are reasonable and intended to help you understand the concepts. Office hour every day is very convenient. Lectures are organized and exams are reasonable. I agree he is very forgiving

He is the most forgiving professor I have ever seen. I have seen some students taking advantages of his kindness. His lectures were quite boring but he answers your questions through emails outside of his office hours. The course has a lot of TA office hours. This course is mandatory and only provided to PAM students. Should take it in freshman yr
I really enjoyed this class. I felt he did a good job teaching the material and even though it was an early morning class it was interesting and fun to attend.

Professor Hall is a really reasonable professor. As long as you do your homework and attend lectures, you will do fine because tests reflect exactly what you learn. Tests are also open notes, so you can make study guides and bring them. Also, his lectures are super clear and easy to follow. Would take his classes again.

Balaji doesn't do a very good job lecturing. I self-studied pretty much everything using the textbook, and I suggest you do the same. Not that you even need to, since it's very easy to cheat most of the quizzes. The class is fairly easy if you're good at math/stats, but I'd suggest another professor if you're not.

He's not the most accessible outside of class nor is he very engaged withs students, but, he makes the class pretty easy for all of us and always gives extensions. If you go to class and are decent at math you will be fine in this class. Don't expect his office hours to help though.

As someone who has taken AP Statistics, he doesn't help you understand statistics. He teaches without using calculators even though the problems he gives can easily be solved on calculators. The first test was in person, but the final was online. I don't think I would've passed if I hadn't taken AP statistics.
Material isn't difficult, but Balaji is. Better off skipping lectures and learning the material on your own time. Don't bother with discussion sections either.

Some of these reviews are excessive. Balaji, while very inaccessible outside class and a fast teacher, is a fairly decent prof. HW+quizzes are all take-home (40% of your grade!) and he constantly gives extensions. I mean he even gave a whole midterm rework so those who failed could get points back. If you need the credit, I certainly recommend him.

Good professor to take Stats class at GWU. Weekly homework and quizzes that are take home and easy. Midterm is difficult, but gave us corrections to boost grade. Final is 20 questions online and is easy if you pay attention in class. Gives extensions on most assignments. Overall, good professor.

the biggest problem is the language barrier. hard to understand purely bc of his heavy accent that he can't change (but that's with every math prof). midterm will TANK your grade (study). easy online take home final that's all MCQ but each worth 2 points. weekly quizzes that boosts up ur grade. will curve at end of the year (went from 79% to a B).

Quizzes are take home and homework can be done as many times as you want for a grade. He will always give extensions and is a very understanding guy. The midterm was kind of hard but he offered a rework at home and gave tons of credit back. The final was multiple choice/take home. I would definitely recommend Balaji if you need the credit.

Rough class for an intro level. He does care about his students and gives extensions on almost every assignment if you need it. Overall not that hard if you pay attention and do the work but he doesn't make it easy.

this man cannot teach. he is late to lectures every single day without fail and is unbelievably bad at answering questions/ clarifying guidelines. the homework assignments through mystatlab are the only things that were helpful to learn the content. sample midterms and finals that were provided were probably the only reason i passed those.

This class is awful. It is so unorganized and he is literally impossible to reach outside of class. He always shows up late. Lectures will not help you, just get ready to teach yourself. Everyone failed the midterm but he did allow us to correct it for some points back. Do yourself a favor and avoid him if you can.

Prof. Balaji is an incredibly hard person to deal with. Not only is he late to almost every single lecture, but it is impossible to understand him when he speaks because the class is in a lecture room and therefore needs a microphone to talk, and even so, the volume is too low. He is monotonous and disorganized. Very disappointed in GWU.

Prof Balaji is such a good prof and asks every class if he is going to fast and leaves room for questions. this is an intro stat class and the content is very watered down and obviously not supposed to be super difficult. all you need to do to do well in this class is go to class AND pay attention. He does everything he can for people to succeed.

He seems like a perfectly nice person, but honestly, none of the people in my class nor I, can really understand what he is teaching. His accent is extremely thick to begin with, but mostly, he just moves too quickly and doesn't review what we've learned at all. Sometimes he just moves too fast, even if pretty much no one understands the material.

Never had a course like this where the professor didn't engage with the students while learning. His teaching style and accent are difficult to understand. At the start of his classes, he NEVER goes over what we learned or the new topic he randomly starts. My peers and I never know what's going on. He never teaches us shortcuts with the calculator.

Me and my friends are currently studying for our midterm, and we are all close to tears. He doesn't explain concepts in class well at all, and when students ask questions in class, he responds very rudely and expects that we should know the information that he's failing to teach us. If you hate yourself, take this class. Not worth the frustration.

he is impossible to reach, doesn't answer emails, and if you ask a question he never actually answers properly.  the actual midterm was considerably harder than any of the practice ones given. he does give a lot of quizzes though, so there is a decent amount of room to make up for a bad grade. don't recommend his class if you're not a stem person.

Relatively easy course for a math credit as long as you put in the work. The first half of the course was super basic statistics, but I found the second half a lot more challenging. He posts all of the lectures and slides on blackboard

Tests and quizzes weren't hard but lectures were exceedingly boring and felt unnecessary. The examples in class were helpful if he wrote them out but honestly, if you go through the slides on your own and only go to TA recitations you'd probably be fine. There's a required textbook but you don't have to read it to do well.
Learned a lot in lecture and was lost if I didn't go. Recitation was unnecessary. Balaji is a chill dude but didn't seem too concerned about anything really.

He is such a kind and knowledgeable person, but I really was not able to learn from him. His teaching method is just doing problems on the board to explain content. TAs/recitation was even less helpful. Take it if you have to and just try your best, but if you can take something else instead, I would strongly advise that.
It is so hard to understand him that I cannot help but zone out in lectures and then fall behind, exams are much harder than you will expect

I really liked Professor Balaji and thought that his lectures were very straight forward and easy to understand. The weekly quizzes were sometimes difficult but as long as you do the homework and pay attention in class you will be fine
Writing this in class right now. Do not take this class unless you hate yourself. He makes no sense. I can not do this anymore.

You will be fine. There are barely any homework assignments, quizzes are online, the midterm was reasonably similar to the sample midterm, and the final was very manageable. He is very understanding, and TAs are helpful.

He does mean well, but his lectures are just hard to understand. Everything you learn you can basically do through a graphing calculator, but he insists on doing it by hand. I ended up teaching myself everything for the final online.

Overall, he is not a terrible professor but the class itself is hard. Weekly quizzes and homework which does help in some ways until you take the midterm and final that ruins you so hard. If you need the credit then you just gotta hope for the best and know how to self-teach math because no one else will. Just, good luck

Professor Balaji isn't a mean person, but he is always late, hard to understand and just isn't a very good teacher. His TAs are frustrated with him and he never posts quizzes at the same time each week. If you need to get the class over with, then you can probably push though, but if you want to learn about stats then avoid this professor.

Impossible to understand the content in class, you will be teaching yourself everything. Tests are hard: 1 midterm, 1 final, weekly quizzes and homework. A LOT of annoying homework. Content is very confusing and little to no support from professor. Class does fulfill a lot of requirements though so if you're organized it can be worth it.

One of the most disorganized classes I have taken at GW. Balaji showed up to lectures late almost every class period, had disorganized lectures, did not introduce us to a TA until almost halfway through the semester, and would assign homework that he would not tell you about. If you like teaching yourself statistics then this is a great class.
often late to class

I am not sure why Balaji has some iffy reviews because I absolutely love him. First, he is genuinely so caring and truly cares about the well-being of his students and what is going on in their personal lives. He is supper accommodating and understanding which I really appreciated. His lectures were straight to the point and easy to follow!

Wanted to give him the benefit of the doubt, but he's just bad. Very disorganized, was frequently late to class. Bad presenter of info, partially bc of language barrier which I won't blame him for. I left class more confused than when I entered. Just use his PowerPoints, and other online resources you can fine. Recitations aren't required

Weekly quizzes + homework (although we only ended up having like 6 homeworks the entire semester) and doing well on those will give you a good cushion for exams if you're worried about them. Covers A LOT of content in lecture. Pretty inaccessible out of class - getting a good grade is possible, but you have to work hard for it on your own.

Do not take this professor if you want someone who has any ability to communicate well. He would not respond to my multiple emails until I contacted the dean about an urgent issue. He sends multiple emails to the whole class going back and forth on his own decisions. I have met literal toddlers with a better ability to communicate than this man.

Take Balaji only if you are willing to do practice problems and not bad at math. His lectures are fast but clear, as long as you review the PowerPoints and do practice problems you should be fine. He doesn't reply to his emails and the sample exams he gave or midterms are much harder than the real midterm.

Professor Balaji is really inaccessible outside of class. He never responds to emails and does not make things clear until the last minute, or until enough people complain. His lectures are incredibly quick and unclear. Do not take his class unless you are extremely confident in stats.

Heavy and fast lectures. He reads all his emails but never replies to any. He used 30mins in class to complain why everyone did so bad on the midterm. The sample midterm he posted is MUCH more easier than the actual midterm! Be aware of weekly quiz and homework

he never replies to emails so it's hard to ask questions. it's easy to understand the lecture but his lecture is super fast. be aware of weekly quizzes and assignments. his midterm is extremely hard and nothing relates to the sample exam.

The content isn't super challenging, but the lectures can be confusing. He isn't always accessible outside of class and didn't put a ton of effort into making the class engaging or enjoyable. The homeworks are helpful in learning the content and the weekly quizzes are pretty easy!

As someone who is from a non-math background, Prof Balaji was a great choice. hooorrrendouuusss teacher. she fails at teaching. her class times consist of her babbling incessently about nothing and then targeting students at random to drill them. She is terrible but if u find urself in her class through error of judgment, cannot switch out and are not one of her favorites, then u need to suck up to her and her favorites, hound her via e-mail and office hours and u will be able to exit her class without any GPA scarring. Worst professor I've ever had, by far. I actually felt like I knew less after taking the course.
This prof was so bad her class made me decide to leave Cornell. The fact that she made it so far academically reflects very poorly on academia in general.

She not only was my worst academic experience at Cornell, but also is a horrible human being. She's cruel and not a good teacher.
