This teachers class was like an academic chamber of horrors! I cannot believe she is a teacher, and she was so intensly mean to some students and nice to others without any logic behind it. She made one girl cry and graded so unfairly it was amazing! If you can take this class with someone else or transfer the credit in...do it! Avoid her classes!

an absolutely terribly class. readings, lectures, assignments were all boring and a waste of time. theres nothing i can say to emphasize how awful it was. she was the worst professor ive ever had at cornell.

She is mentally disturbed and plays favorites all the time. Her class is a minefield of politics and insanity. I have never taken a class this poorly structured. It was a complete waste of money. I could have found better instruction in an insane asylum. If you can help is stay away from her!

This woman is the worst teacher EVER! Tons of reading, most of which was never touched on in class. Very boring, so hard to stay awake. Expects you to spend hundreds on books & print outs. Doesn't stay w/syllabus at all. Expects so much from you (time & $), but doesn't appreciate effort. MEAN ****!

She is interested in the topics she covered, but there wasn't much of a connection between all of them. She does give great insight into learning German better, and her feedback on papers is also great.

Elke Siegel is hands down my favorite professor at Cornell. I've taken three German classes with her and it is very apparent that she is there to teach you German - she doesn't give busy work and she doesn't grade unfairly. If anything she is a too nice a grader. If you have any interest in taking a GERST classs, take Siegel's!!!

My hatred for poetry is long and enduring; I was in the class to improve my German. I agree with the previous reviewer, that anyone who speaks German should take a class with Professor Siegel.   If you only have time in your schedule to fit in one German class, take whatever class Siegel is offering. You won't regret it.

I took Frau Siegel's class Lyric Poetry, which I never thought I would take because I hate poetry. But she made it super interesting and I would definitely recommend this course if she teaches it again! If you're into German whatsoever you absolutely have to take a class with her. And on top of that she's a really nice grader.

He is a generous grader and is a very accommodating teacher when it comes to the difficulties of learning a language as it is not easy often. Attending lectures are important as there is a participation grade and its important to reinforce what your learning. This class is 5 credits so do prepare to do the homework equivalent to it.

Miura is a generous grader. Despite the mistakes you may make throughout this course, as long as you try he will be lenient. His class is something to look forward to, as he is very engaging and funny. Expect to be called on at least once a day, as participation and practice is very important in his class. Homework is given daily, but is easy.

As you can probably tell by the 5 credits, this class requires effort.  Despite this, I enjoyed this class.  Miura grades generously, sometimes only taking off 0.1 points for mistakes.  Attendance is mandatory.  This class has lots of small homework assignments but they never took me too long to do.  If you try you will probably end with a 3.5-4.0.
He is the best instructor I've ever had. He is funny and he does a great job making the course interesting.

Miura sensei is a very good lecturer and professor, but he wasn't my cup of tea. His classes are very heavy on lectures interjected with class participation, and he takes participation points throughout the week that counts toward your grade. Take the extra time outside of class to prepare even before the lecture.

The lecture slides were engaging, often funny, and well thought out. One major thing I noticed is the information was easy to retain due to his teaching style. Also, prepare to get uncomfortable in class, because everyday he will call on students to answer questions in Japanese, so you are on the spot. But, it's necessary to develop speech.
He is a good professor

Considering this is an entry level Japanese course, the course load was not any harder than expected. Although there is a lot of homework (workbook page every day at the least), this is of no fault of Professor Miura but instead of the language. I really enjoyed class with Professor Miura and hope to have him again next semester!
This class was half online and half in-person. Professor is very funny and very good at keeping you engaged. Had a lot of fun during class but still was able to learn all the material.
Super chill dude

Takuma is an amazing Arranging teacher. He definitely makes you work hard but if you are willing to try your best and work hard in the class then you will succeed. But Takuma is not only a great teacher, he is an amazing guy who wants all of his students to be successful.
Very funny person, he makes a lot of jokes in class and teaches good lectures at the same time. He gives a lot of good feedback on all the assignments he assigned. HE THE REAL ONE

Man, what can I say. Everybody who is interested in sound design should take his class. By far the best teacher I ever had in Berklee, very accessible outside class, giving out very clear instructions of everything.If u know nothing, he will literally explain to u by using 4th grade terms. Get a spot from his class as soon as u can!

Takuma is a joy to have as a professor. He's always cracking jokes and making sure everyone has fun during class while also never deviating from the focus of his curriculum. He also seriously knows his stuff
Takuma is one of the best, so nice!
I love him. I learnt so much. Take him over any professor for MTECH classes.
Definitely a great professor here.

Professor Matsui is incredibly funny and made the transition into my first year a lot more comfortable and accessible. He's very patient with going over the ins and outs of music tech that I never would've dreamed of understanding till I took his class. He grades pretty hard but gives you immensely valuable feedback.
He gives incredible feedback and constructive criticism, and he cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He's pretty funny too and his classes and lectures are very engaging.

Professor Matsui gives the best lectures I've ever been a witness to! He's quick and concise with the information and always willing to listen to questions. Also, the teaching style is right up my alley since I love humorous professors. Although the course I'm taking is easy, he has mentioned that his more advanced classes can be quite challenging.

Prof. Habu is by no means an easy professor. Her class is demanding, with lots of reading and tricky topics. However, I learned so much from her, and she really pushed me to grow as a student, so I would recommend taking one of her classes. You may struggle a little, but it's totally possible to get an A as she is caring and accessible out of class

Professor Habu is a very passionate and kind instructor. Her lectures are easy to follow and she always makes time for questions. The class only consisted of three tests and one final group project. She goes easy on the grading, as long as you can show that you understand what you're talking about. Also, attendance is mandatory.

Extremely reading heavy and you need to do the readings each week just to keep up (100-200+ pages per week). That said the readings are very interesting and you'll learn a ton from them. The class itself isn't too challenging as long as you keep up with the readings. The tests aren't that tough but they are in class hand-written essays.

Prof. Habu is very knowledgable and kind but her class is difficult. Grasping the theories and ideas requires lots of studying, and the amount of reading she assigns weekly is very hard to keep up with (~100 pages of scientific papers/week), especially if archaeology is not your specialization. The tests are fair, and the grading is not very hard.

Junko is super kind and creates a really nice class environment. My biggest complaint is that her theoretical lectures can be incredibly hard to follow - lots of big words and not a lot of explanation. You really need to do the readings in order to have any idea what's going on. But she's a very easy grader and super accessible for questions!

Junko is a wonderful person! I've had 2 classes with her. Really cares about what she does & emphasizes how archaeology can be applied to contemporary issues. Genuinely kind. Really interesting ideas. Makes meeting outside class very accessible. Normal amount of readings for anthro. Grades based on group presentation, 3 total exams, & attendance.

I made my ratemyprofessor account just for professor habu. I am now a senior, and looking back this was my favorite class that I have taken throughout my time here. We covered topics that were current/intriguing and she encouraged us to build our own opinions on how subjects like nuclear power should be dealt with. Learned a lot- and got a solid A
lectures were incredibly unorganized and boring. Midterms and final were easy, but your grade depends on the GSI's. I do not recommend taking this class.

Professor Habu was amazing. She is extremely fair and lets students know what's going to be on exams beforehand. Very accessible outside of class. Overall, amazing experience with a brilliant professor.
The sweetest professor, but too lenient. She'd be perfect if she demanded more from her students.
Fieldwork was poorly organized. It seemed as if she didn't know what she was doing.  This was a horrible experience and a big waste of time.
The lectures and field excavation were poorly organized. In retrospect, I did not learn much of anything from the whole field school experience. a total waste of money and time.

Junko Habu is a one of the most respected Archaeologists regarding the Jomon Culture of Japan and that is reflected in her Japanese Archaeology class. The only downside I can say about her is she teaches the class a little too much like a Japanese History class, and there is a bit too much arbitrary memorization. She's a great professor to take!

The subject itself was not very interesting to me, however, I give Professor Habu credit for her effort.  She really tried to keep the class interested and she was also very nice.  She tried to help the student's grade as much as possible by lowering the grading scale and etc... I got a A- in the class without much effort.

She speaks fast and doesn't post her notes on b-space so if you try to keep up with the slides expect hand cramps by the end of class. She's kind and can make funny comments, but lectures are hard to stay awake in. The movies she shows are interesting...look forward to those
not very good.
unorganized and unprofessional
Professor Habu is fantastic.  She is enthusiatic and knowledgable about her subjects, and is extremely open to helping her students.
I'm just in her URAP program this semester, but she has been really awsome and is super nice. I'd totally take a class from her given the chance.
Professor Habu is very helpful and thorough in her lectures.  Her lectures are interesting and don't just regurgitate the reading.
Professor Habu's super nice and I learned so much from this class. She really wants her students to do well so she let us resubmit our labs and homework for a better grade.
She has very high expectations and her class was hard, but she was very helpful and the class was a good methods course.
She has very high expectations (graduate level) that she does not make clear to her students.
No Comments

Kat is a really genuine and a good teacher. I really enjoyed her accent as well as her excitement for the class! She is VERY smart and that shows through during her lectures. I think that sometimes that means you may have to go back and review some topics because they are covered quickly, but the TA is accesable.

Kat is a good professor, but her teaching style is pretty different. She is very lecture heavy, and her lectures are hard to follow along. I got more out of reading the text book. Her lectures follow it closely though. Her tests are hard and the questions can be very indirect and confusing. Overall a challenging class

The most terrifying moodle page you will ever see (entirely in japanese and often quite hard to decipher). But she is a brilliant teacher, legitimately caring, and so sweet. Expect a lot of work, but forgiving grading (I missed a lot of smaller assignments and still got a B+ through good grades on tests and projects).

Habuka sensei is absolutely amazing. Her only flaw is that she works too hard sometimes and might care too much (I'm not kidding)

Her class is definitely hard and be prepared for a lot of homework. However, her class is very fiar and you can really learn a lot of Japanese. She is amazing outside of class time and is a super smart and caring person

Habuka sensei might be the best professor I've ever had. She is not only an incredible lecturer but also really caring and invested in your personal success with the language. The constant homework can get brutal but a lot of the projects end up being fun and it's hard to have a bad time during class.

Habuka sensei's great personality and highly engaging teaching style are her hallmarks. Having taken JAPN204, 205, and 206 with her, there were definitely times when the amount of daily homework was borderline excessive, but she was very supportive whenever I was struggling and asked for help. She's a wonderful addition to the Japanese department.

Habuka-sensei is the best professor I've ever had at Carleton. Her teaching style is very engaging and her enthusiasm makes learning enjoyable and fun. The pacing of the course isn't too fast or slow and the content of the quizzes and tests are very fair. If you're taking Japanese, I can't recommend her enough.

Habuka's workload can be ridiculous sometimes, especially towards the end of the term where everything is piled on. She's still disorganized and scatterbrained but super lovable and one of the funniest/most energetic people I've ever met. I'd take her for 206 over Kaga any day!

Miaki rocky her socky! She so nice and very friend to the student. She speak Japanese like native speaker so very fast but her class is very ease for me. I wish she teach more class in the Japanese but usually Kaga do so I be very sad.
Her workload can be a bit much but her class is easy. Ended up liking Habuka-sensei more than the class itself.

Habuka is so, so, so perky and sweet: it's impossible to go a day without seeing her smiling and excited to teach you Japanese. She really cares about students and the way she acts is incredibly hilarious in the way she overreacts inclass. She rarely speaks English to you even outside of class and this really helps reinforce conversation skills.

Habuka sensei is extremely nice and has one of the bubbliest personalities on campus. She speaks very fast Japanese and oftentimes only in Japanese to you, but it helps develop your listening skills although due dates and directions might get confusing as a result. However, she is a bit disorganized and has trouble clarifying.

Habuka-sensei! What can I say, I loved her class. She's really sweet and has a fantastic sense of humor in her teaching. On top of that, she's quite easy, but she will make the class a bit harder for 205.

The class overall was pretty easy, but then again language learning comes naturally to some people. We only covered a few chapters in Tobira, but it was still a lot of content. She gave us a study guide prior to the final which was very similar to the final so I didn't have to study very much.

Professor Habursky structured the class in a way that was meant for students to learn through real world assignments. We were treated as consultants working on theoretical events and I left the class knowing first hand of what it is like to plan and promote events of any size.

Prof. Bloomfield assigned a lot of reading at first, but lessened it when told by students that it was too much. Essays were graded fairly, always gave good feedback and was available to help. Towards the end of the semester became lenient and allowed us to do whatever we wanted for the final project, such as a group project on a current event.

Professor Bloomfield ensured that material load throughout the semester was always at the right level and offered substantial feedback throughout essay writing process. An already interesting topic was reintroduced to students in more formal readings such as scholarly articles and primary documents on past climatic events. Good first year class.

The amount of readings assigned was an overload and I wasn't able to balance the rest of my classes with his class. He talks extremely pedantically and makes overly worded jokes that make no sense. Also the amount of essays assigned were a lot, it was like 4 to 6 essays per month each being minimum five pages with a ten page research paper later.
Excellent teacher, amazing person really wants you to do well.

Suzuki-Sensei is absolutely amazing. Class goes by so quickly with her and, despite always needing to do quite a bit of preparation and homework for class, I've never been stressed. She grades quite leniently for daily grades, but make sure you're prepared for written, oral, kanji, lesson, and vocabulary tests

Suzuki sensei is amazing! The class can move at a fast pace at times but the fun and encouraging atmosphere she creates makes it so that nobody is afraid to ever participate. Despite the workload I think it was one of the only classes that ever actively de-stressed me, and sensei played a large part in making that possible.

Suzuki sensei is so nice and hardworking. She's probably one of the best teachers I've met at Cornell. Even though everything became hard under pandemic, she still made the online version of japan3302 worth it.

AMAZING. I don't think I've ever had a professor this clearly dedicated to making their class as great as it can possibly be. If you make a mistake, she will sometimes act as if it wasn't one to help you realize what you did wrong, while nudging you in the right direction. I learned so much from her class. Challenging, but worth every minute.

I'm shocked she hasn't received any reviews in the past DECADE. And, all the reviews here are from 1101! It seems her strictness and dedication has moved her to the advanced Japanese courses. She is a very welcoming presence and extremely present for her students. She will really push you in order to make sure you get things right.
You have to REALLY want to learn Japanese to do well in this class. Suzuki is very nice, but she works hard and expects students to do so too.

Great Professor. Teaches very clearly and is friendly all the time. In order to get an A, you DO have to attend every single lecture and discussion (a total of 7 times a week); be very well prepared every day and hand in every homework on time. This way, you will find Japanese interesting. Overall, you will learn a lot in her class, and have fun.
Suzuki sensee is a stickler in class for being prepared, but overall, nice and helpful.
Suzuki is too sweet :)
Suzuki-sensei is the most professional person I have met at this university. She is always SO prepared, but still seems very relaxed and natural in class.

Suzuki-sensei is very friendly, and runs a highly competent crack team of TAs. You do have to go to the language lab almost every single day of your life, but the class is amusing with a great atmosphere. Totally worth it to take Japanese!
No Comments

Such boring class, barely has interaction with students. She just read the slides and didn't allow the use of laptops. No exam for this class, only one paper, so if you have bad teammates you are done.

Fun and intriguing professor. Exams can be a bit tough (even though they are open note) so listen in class and make a good study guide. He wants you to succeed and really is passionate about the class

Great professor. I didn't know anything about the hospitality industry, but I walked away with learning a lot more than I expected. One of my best things to do is participate in class and go to office hours (he usually has a small treat there) to show participation and build a relationship with him.

Professor Roberts is one of the most approachable and respected professors at Cornell. His exams are open note but they are graded very toughly by the TAs. His lectures are very tedious and he uses his own terms a lot that you will not use in the industry. Students don't do as well as they would think in his class.

Mr. Roberts is an amazing teacher and person. He is very well respected among the Cornell Community. Make sure to pay attention and take notes and you'll do just fine in this course. Make sure to also go to his office hours. He will talk about anything and he has incredible insight.

Prof. Roberts is incredibly organized and clearly demonstrates his knowledge and excitement for the course. He is very accommodating and an all-'round nice person. Exams are open-note, and he releases his slide decks (just cmd-F). Befriend him and send him pictures and anything you think he'd like.  He's the nicest professor in Statler Hall.

Professor Roberts is truly an amazing professor. Though I am not interested in Hotel Operations, I have enjoyed being in his class this semester. My biggest tip is to try and pay attention even though he sometimes gets very excited and speaks super fast. If you participate and try your hardest he will see that and reward it.
Such an amazing person and professor!!
Amazing guy. He is super nice and really understanding of all different kinds of issues or scenarios.

Professor Roberts is easily the best professor at the hotel school. While the class itself may not be the best, Professor Roberts is. Being able to pick his brain was one of my most favorite things to do.
Absolutely incredible professor

Dave Roberts is far and away the best professor at Cornell. He puts in a ton of effort to make sure his students enjoy the class and get as much as possible out of it. He is one of the nicest people around and really cares about his students.
Might be the nicest dude Ive ever met. One of few professors who truly cares about his students and will go out of his way for you. Certainly a nice break from other professors *cough CG*
The best professor ever! Such a kind guy.

Professor Roberts is the BEST. He genuinely wants all of his students to do well and does not want his class to be stressful; there is hardly any outside work for this class and exams are open note. HADM1350 is so interesting, and Roberts has so much experience from his time at Marriott that he is the perfect person to teach it.
So kind and awesome! Always make you feel engaged and never makes it boring. One of my favorite professors to date.

Profesor Roberts is both the most knowledgeable, kind and considerate professor. Not only does he have an insane amount of industry experience but he doesn't act like a god in the classroom, he takes questions and makes time to connect and talk with students both about his class and about the industry at large.

Cliff is a great instructor.  He's more than willing to meet and talk over the material or current assignments.  He is very knowledgeable, and makes the material really clear.  You'll definitely learn how to analyze complex arguments and write a good philosophy paper.

Professor Roberts was incredibly helpful and absolutely instrumental to my understanding of the material. I didn't do that well in his class but I learned a great deal about the material and about how to write a great philosophical paper (it's harder than it looks!). Plus, he's pretty easy on the eyes. :)

Theo seems like a very strict teacher, however, he is very lenient on submission time and attendance. As long as you do the work, you should be fine. He does talk a lot in class and get off tracked, but his lectures are very interesting and thought provoking. When you ask questions though, he will question your thoughts harsly.
He is quite a nice guy, despite his constant mumbling in class. Yet once you get used to it, he is an insightful and very interesting professor to be with.

At first he is a bit of pain and not extremely pleasant. Consequently, people do drop his class. However, once he becomes comfortable and he is actually kinda funny and nice. The readings are sometimes painful and the essays are few but tough. He prepares you well for them, if you can understand his occasional mumbling, and always likes to help.

Korzukhin is nice guy, but he is genuinely incomprehensible during lectures. He mumbles constantly and talks to the blackboard. Problem sets were ludicrously difficult. Nearly the entire PHIL 2830 class needed to collaborate for around 14 hours per pset. Avoid at all costs.
Very honest, but very interesting

Lectures can be boring, but are also often very interesting. Grades are only based on discussions, participation, and essays. The essays can be difficult to write and he is a very difficult grader, but his feedback usually helps. He's overall a funny and nice guy when he opens up.

This professor made you feel like you were an idiot just for asking questions. Additionally, there is a great deal of software you must pay for and use consistently, but there is zero instruction from the professor on how to use it. His lectures are confusing and difficult to hear. Definitely do not recommend.

Took a very convoluted route to explaining basic concepts in deductive logic, will make you feel silly for asking questions. Overall avoid him if you can help it, a lot of software involved for homework and not much guidance on how to use it.
felt like this class was a complete afterthought to him. slides were never posted online consistently. also was stingy about sharing readings online. hard to hear in lecture as well. overall, not fun

Theo is an incoherent lecturer and his quizzes have very little to do with lectures. He quizzes very niche topics that are barely covered in the readings. His grading scale is generous and papers aren't graded harshly, but it will be hard to get an A in this class unless you know a lot of philosophy going in. TAs are super helpful but not enough.
Lowi probably used to be a great lecturer, but now he just rambles all class and occasionally says something entertaining.  Everything depends on your TA, so try to get a good one.
Great guy. Not the best teacher. Class is really boring and TA's do literally all the work. Get to know your TA and be really nice to him/her.
Take.  This.  Class.  Ted Lowi is entertaining and brilliant.  My friend and I quote him to this day (15 years later).  If this isn't why you came to college then I don't know what you're doing.
Very subjective grading by TA's. Class was pointless to go to. Just read the textbook and you will be fine. Dont need to read the other books given.

A good class, but grading is done entirely by TA's and can be very subjective. Don't need to ever go to lectures to get an A, but in general I did enjoy his lectures. Not sure I would take it again since I didn't learn much (had previous knowledge) and expected to learn more.

Lectures have no relation to the graded course material, the grading is done only by TA's and is entirely subjective, and some of the TA's are absolutely unforgivably awful. If you have an easy TA this class will be a breeze.  If not you can be completely screwed.  Nonetheless, for one of Cornell's most famous Professors, this class was really bad.

Lowi's class certainly had a bit of a disjointed feel to it; the few assignments (midterm, final, two papers) seemed random and not directly related to course material. That said, Lowi's lectures are fantastic, and well worth going to for his learned (and fiery!) commentary on both past and current events. A fun course to take for sure.

Lowi is an awesome lecturer. But don't look at the 1111 designation and think you can blow off this class, there's a ton of reading each week (you can get far behind if you don't skim some of it going into section). The grading is pretty hard/arbitrary as well. Exams are based on pre-posted essay questions, and outlining them is time consuming.

Although Lowi is an interesting lecturer and a pretty cool guy, his lectures are totally irrelevant to the course and to the tests/papers. The class itself wasn't that great--grading was done by TA's and seemed totally subjective. The tests weren't that hard, but seemed to be graded arbitrarily as well. I wouldn't recommend this class.

Not such a fan after taking this class; grading is subjective (that's up to the TA, who was a joke), and lectures aren't as clearly organized and unbiased as he promised they would be.  They were also pointless, not necessary to attend.  Interesting lecture style but overall the class was unsuccessful at teaching me how to think about government.
The lectures were really long, boring, and irrelevant to the readings and the tests.  Grading is very subjective.  Section was not helpful in reviewing the material.
Best professor ever! Teaches like he's a preacher. Always has entertaining, relevant stories. He brought in Janet Reno once to guest lecture. Great professor, great material, best class ever.

As far as Gov 111 goes, you will only see Lowi in lecture. He is brilliant, but information given during lecture is rarely tested (but they are worth listening to anyway). The class is pretty easy, get to know your TA and you are golden. Four grades the entire semester. I'd give it the highest "easy" score but A+'s are non-existent.

Professor Lowi is a god...his lectures are accessible and engaging but offer such new and brilliant insight into American Government. Listen to his lecture about the problems with bureaucracy in order to make sense of why this class has big problems: the tests are poorly constructed, no one has to attend lecture, and some of the TAs are awful..

Lowi is one of Cornell's big-time professors, but seems to really care about his students. The class has quite a bit of reading, and lecture wasn't always helpful. Really take advantage of your TAs because they'll be your main source of info/help.
Lectures are amazing, not mandatory but the only way that I got anything out of this class was from his wonderful, funny, brilliant lectures.

Great teacher, although sometimes over everyone's heads.  Not a hard class, and only one (although 15page) paper outside of preparing for exams, no other work.  for exams, he gives you 6 essays ahead of time and then one-two on the actual test.  You need to do some outside reading for the exams/paper.  Manageable class and interesting professor.

Class is really pretty ridiculously easy, but if you actually want to get something out of it, you definitely can. Most stuff on the exams are pretty much common sense, but lectures are at a higher level (although because it is an intro course and the TA's do the grading, most of this stuff doesn't show up on exams). Lowi's a genius.

By far the easiest gov. course. Entire semester consists of just 4 graded tests/essays. All the grading is done by the TA, so make sure to get on his/her good side. Midterm and final consist of 2 essays and 8-10 IDs each. Essays are given BEFOREHAND, and IDs come straight out of the textbook's vocab. section. Lectures are unecessary. Very Very easy
You don't really need to go to lecture, just read the textbook. But Lowi is hilarious but sometimes difficult to understand.

LOWI is hilarious and amazing. You don't really need to go to lecture or read the textbook, but the textbook is a good foundation if you're gonna be a gov major and teh lectures are well worth the walk to Uris. Lectures like this are the reason I pay 40000 a year to be here. we all love lowi!
Intellectually stimulating class, none of his lectures are testable so it's up to you to go. TAs grade everything. Not too hard overall
He's a genius. And his lectures are quite interesting. All your grading is from the TA, so love your TA. The tests are easy, and if you meet with your TA for the papers you'll do well.
The man, he is sometimes hard to follow but offers brilliant insight and original thoughts.  A pleasure to listen to.
he's bat-shit insane. honestly, by the end of the course, i still had no idea what he was talking about

The man is brilliant and passionate about politics.  He offers more information than we need to know, which is so great if you are interested in a gov major.  He gives 100% of his effort in every lecture.  I could practically hear his voice everytime I read over my notes, thats how good he is.

As others have said, it is a fairly easy grade if you have any knowledge of American government at all. Can get snappy if he feels you are not asking a question with real thought, but fishing for an easy answer! If you're looking to learn, willing to put forth the effort and have a great mentor.....then this is the professor for you!

Takashi is one of the best professors I have ever had. He has elevated the Interior Design program at FIT because he expects excellence. I graduated 3 years ago and his lessons still carry on in the real world. I've learned how to work hard, exceed my own excpectations and meet very strict deadlines, which is very useful in today's working world.
over all he is ok. you can learn a lot from him but only if he likes you.

Surprising that he still is a chair.  FIT should take a close look at this guy, he doesn't deserve to be where he is at.  Some will know what I mean.  Get rid of him so FIT can hire even better dedicated teachers
awesome!! BEST ever!
Do your self a favour and dont take him.

I am a huge fan.  He has really high standards for everyone but is extremely sympathetic and helpful if he sees that you are really struggling after working hard on your own.  Improvement counts toward your final grade so don't be discouraged even if you start out really low.  He also loves creativity!

takashi is the best teacher i have ever met he challenges you. he pushes you to work your ass off.his door is always open, im lucky i met him. im glad he is the chair of the department. he knows every student by name.and if he likes you you are dead( he will kill you with work)

Allows students to do their own thing with their designs & encourages radical & creative thinking.  Does not promote mindless conformity and mediocrity. It is surprising that even though he is head of InteriorDesign dept the majority of the other professors ther DO insist on assimilation.  Design is supposed to be GREAT not just fine.
I like him, he is a knowledgable person, but also unpredictable. You have no sense when he likes you or not. anyways, he is the best professor in my life.

he speaks with non-sense and very unhelpful...  i would like to ask him to take a speech class first and then come back to teach...  consider that he is the chairperson of the department so he can doing nothing in the school all day.. all he does is just walk around and "chit chat" with his co-workers..... bad bad bad....

Considering he's the chair of the department, you would think he would have a sense of professionalism and ethics. However, he is insecure, lame, and freakish. He has never practiced interior design, has no idea what he's talking about, plays stupid mind games (and holds a grudge if you don't "play" them with him).
The most evil person. Gives you looks. If he doesn't like you he has no problem showing it. Should get fired. I feel like its a conspiracy, how can they be allowed to teach!?!?!?!?!
he can be helpful but can be nasty too.
He'll work you, but he's the most dedicated person in the department.

HST 385 I found very hard and difficult to keep up with. (Non-history major). This class was awful online after COVID-19. Very boring and non-interactivepdfs and videos embedded in them. This was very, very stressful and frustrating for me!!! Very nice prof though. Was HAPPY when it was finally done forever!!! Dont miss it at all!!

The material was understandable for non-majors.Readings are assigned a lot, but I read none. Attendance is mandatory since it is a lecture-heavy class.Graded off 2 exams and 3 writing assignments (lowest is dropped).The final is a group project, but he makes the groups and grading extremely fair. Strict on what he expects to see in assignments.

At the start of the semester, I almost dropped out of his class. You can't have any kind of technology, he is a harsh grader, there aren't many things to grade, you are only allowed 3 absences, and each class is a lecture. But if you keep an open mind and take time outside of class, it's easy to get an A. He's strict at first but he gets better.

Gave me my lowest grade ever. Found his assignments to be really abnormally structured and stressful. I wouldn't say 'avoid at all costs', but if you're looking for a history course try to pick another professor.
Dr. Nishiyama is a little strict on grading, but as long as you show up to class prepared, you'll be fine. He's very funny and has a lot of really interesting stories to tell.

I really enjoyed Nishiyama's class. He is a great guy that tries to make connections with his students. As long as you're nice to him and pay attention in class you will be more than fine. Class is simple, but the papers are a little difficult because he is super strict on criteria.

HST 202 felt like a high school class. Papers aren't really papers and don't allow for exploration of ideas or real research (felt more like answering short answer questions). My greatest qualm was his unclear and at times ridiculous grading policies, they left me with much unnecessary anxiety that could have been avoided if he had clarity.
Super nice guy!! Definitely recommend this course. Easy A. Allows you to retake the midterm and resubmit an essay. Only 1 test (midterm), the final is a group project. Attendance required.
Very tough grading system. Is often not clear on requirements for projects. However, the content and information you need to learn for this class is very straight forward.

1. He's fantastic. I don't know what he's doing at Brockport. Could definitely go Ivy League, I think. 2. He gives you everything you need to succeed. Do all the questions that go along with the readings on time and you're set. Trust me. It'll save you a lot of headaches. 3. Participation  show up + ask good questions. Seriously, do it.

Professor Nishiyama is a fantastic professor. He really cares about his students and will help you if you're struggling. He assigns a lot of papers, but he drops the lowest one. Participation counts for 25% of your grade. As long as you show up to class, participate, and do the writing assignments you should do very well in his class.

Did not like Professor Nishiyama that much. He doesn't explain the content well, and grades like a 400 level course on a 200 level course. Super hard grader and would not recommend taking any classes with him.

Dr. Nishiyama is a wonderful professor! You'll definitely  have to put some effort in, but if you take good notes, participate, and do your papers then you can do well. Going to his office hours are very helpful. He's a professor that wants you to do well, and will do his best to help you succeed.

Dr. Nishiyama is not a good professor. There was no discussion about any topics or any historical events and it made the class difficult. The textbook is nothing but a book on how to cite in Chicago style and the entire time he made me feel like I didn't know how to write a research paper. Would definitely avoid.

Amazing professor, very intelligent. Really makes you think about the world around. I feel like I had a much more unique learning experience compared to most other professors. Really cares about his students. But, he is tough teacher but that is just because he expects the best of us.

Dr. Nishiyama is a great man, a great teacher, and a great scholar. He is incredibly particular in how he wants responses to questions in writing. Best advice, be prepared to work as hard as you can and talk to others who have taken his classes previously. Also, be ready to learn. This guy brings his A game. Bring yours as well, or you will fail.

One of the only real college professors at brock, Dr. Nishiyama is wasting his potential. He should be somewhere much more prestigious. You will become a better student by being in his class. He teaches you how to undertand and view history accurately. You will learn how to write a paper like a college undergrad should.

Main drawback here is that he is a draconian grader compared to other professors teaching at the same class level. Highly educated and gives engaging lectures, and you certainly come out of his classes stronger than you went in - but don't expect an easy time of it. Hope you like writing!
A hard grader but he is nice overall. I don't mind having him in a different history class later.

Teaches about Asian history in a non-American perspective which made the class interesting. A lot of work though and reading is an absolute key to success. Class time could also be spent better on going over readings, but course objectives are clear and Dr. Nishiyama makes the class interesting! Recommended if you're willing to work hard.

Pretty difficult grader, even for a 300 level course. Sometimes his grading just doesn't make sense as well and he  seems to expect way too much on the papers. Course itself isn't too difficult and he gives a lot of bonus points if you do the work. Course objectives pretty clear mostly. Take this class if you have to get that Asian requirement done

Nice Prof. but very difficult grader. He definitely does not treat the class like a 100 level class. Material is straight forward, but his level of grading is ridiculous. I had 400 level classes easier than this class. Good luck.

Even though I'm not a history major I really enjoyed taking this class. He has a very funny sense of humor. Extremely helpful and very clear. 5 quizzes, one group project and a final exam paper. I recommend taking this class to fufill civilizations requirement!
All is pretty straightforward. Study guides are a must to get 5 quizzes done. Many extra credits here and there in class, which is pretty good.

Overall he's a good professor. He gives out study guides with important points that will be on the quizzes. You need to read the text book in order to find certain information that will be on tests. He's got a good sense of humor also. He takes time and answers everyone's questions until there are no longer anymore questions. Very Straight forward.

he likes to give about 5 quizes in which he gives all the info but u will have to read the textbook it is key to passing the class.But he is very funny and extremly helpful. I really enjoyed his class he also loves anyone whom likes to participate alot so be ready for that. Overall i would give him a 4 out of 5 he is a great professor.

I think he is overall a good guy. Gives asisgned seats like we're still in highschool. Treats a 100 level course likes its a graduate course. Very hard, you have to pay attention, read the book A LOT and then add more to your notes. Quizzes seem easy but they're not at all.  Do not take this class with him.
Good professor. Extremely enjoying this class! recommend to anyone.

Don't listen to any of the comments that have knocked Dr. Nishiyama; he is a great teacher; one of the best ive had at B-Port! He lets you know exactly what to expect on quizes, exams, and papers! I will take my Asian history course with him next year and any other courses that he may teach that I need.

Great teacher! He is extremely organized and you will definatly know what to expect on all quizzes and exams. He gives out study guides before you even start going over the material in class and in the readings. My only knock is that the multiple choice part of the quizzes can sometimes be tricky. I will definatly take future courses with him.

He is very hard to understand, dosnt offer much help if you attend office hours, least favorite history prof at brockport. He does enjoy what he teaches but it comes off as being snotty. would never take a class with him again

This was a good and interesting class.  He is very funny and is extremely helpful if you contact him via email.  There is one blue book exam, 3 five page papers, and a final paper of 8-9 and another smaller final paper of 3-4 pages.  Overall a lot of writing, but well worth it.

He expects his students to work. If he doesn't like you, you probably said something stupid. To get A, visit him during office hours and carefully go over materials he covered during exam reviews. Oh, one more thing. He needs to smile more often.

A good teacher, but expect to write as much or more than a 400 level course.  He has one blue book test, and the rest are essay tests that must use all the texts and angel readings. He also grades pretty hard, meaning that you have to put a lot of work and *original* thought in the essay to get a B.

Be aware: he makes you work, which means he will get you out of your comfort zone. He knows what he is talking about and he is extremely helpful. I worked hard and got what I had paid for at Brockport.
He is hard to understand and difficult to please

The worst teacher in the world. Want to feel like your taking 5 classes in one.?.?.?.here is your guy! Makes you feel like an idiot even if you try. Monotone, rude, and boring. Expect to write a 20-30 page paper for a final. For a survey course it was way to difficult. So much reading/studying/work that you have very little time for anything else.
treats an intro level course like a graduate level, horrible!

U must read all course readings, attend every class & make multiple visits to Dr. Nishiyama's office to survive in this class. Hardest class I ever took! With that being said, this was a great class. He makes U work, but U get the grade U deserve. He has no problem telling U what he thinks, good and/or bad. If U R a serious student go for it!

Only A&P teacher I would recommend for lab! He enjoys his work and it shows. He connects learning things like muscles to real-life by explaining how ACL & Tommy John's surgery work for example. I find things like that useful because I can see my learning has a purpose. I realized nursing was not for me but I highly recommend him as a teacher.

While A&P and nursing were not for me, I enjoyed Maie a lot. He was flexible, helpful, and would give you credit if he knew the answer (especially on lab quizzes). Ex. If an area of the body had two names but we learned only one for the lab quiz, you would still get credit. You could tell he loved what he does and he gets very excited about it.

Dr. Maie is a very good lecture professor. He tends to move quickly but uploads all his Powerpoints on Moodle, so you can easily go back and fill in parts you missed in class. However, he will say things in class that are not on the Powerpoint, so always show up! He is very funny and gives students the opportunity to assist in cadaver dissections.

Erik is a great guy and is very intelligent. He will help you understand the material and has a dry sense of humor. I thought he was hysterical although it seems as if many of his jokes go above peoples' heads.
Review sessions were very useful for the exams, other sessions were less useful but good for understanding the concepts better.

Erik is great. He is really passionate about what he teaches and enthusiastic about sharing his knowledge. Took an fws with him and he assigned 5 papers totalling summing up to about 25 pages in the end. Very flexible prompts that allow you to explore what you are interested in. Always willing to meet after class and is generous with extensions.

His class was great, he gave us a lot of leeway to pursue what we were interested in, and we got to affect the class material based on it as we went on. There was a lot of papers that were pretty intensive in the amount they asked for, so I spent a lot more time on this class than I normally do for similar ones.

Professor Florea is a great lecturer. She approaches difficult topics through literature, primary sources, and a good dose of humour. The selected material is very interesting and contributes to your growth way beyond her class.

She genuinely cares about your progress and you as a person.

Florea was one of the most passionate and caring professors I've ever had. Her lectures are amazingly engaging, and she makes difficult topics easier to navigate. Very accessible outside of class, Professor Florea always helped spur discussions with insightful, leading questions that challenged us. Fantastic class and professor!

HIST2958 is very well structured. The materials are great + the lectures are super engaging and packed with fascinating content. You're also graded on a lot of small manageable assignments, which I found very convenient. Also, Prof. Florea is a top-notch instructor. She transmits her passion and genuinely cares about your progress. I'd enroll again

Professor Florea is fantastic. The lectures are super interesting, she does a good job of integrating student discussions into a relatively large class, and she and her TAs give great, clear feedback on the papers. It is not an easy course, though, so be prepared to do the readings carefully and revise your papers.

Cornell is lucky to have her. Prof. Florea puts her students first and is always full of advice and encouragement, even a semester after the class. If you're looking for a survey of Soviet history, take the class. There is a LOT of depth and work but the films and novellas she's picked really provide a human element forgotten in other classes.

Prof Florea is so nice she genuinely cares about you doing well and understanding her class so is always available to chat. Tough grading (median grade B+) but if you pay attention and are interested in the material you'll have no problem getting that or higher. Not a class to take if you don't like the subject though because lectures are in depth
Unnecessarily difficult class. Would NOT recommend.

She talks to the board and asks if everyone understands her, she uses the most complicated way to explain the SIMPLEST of problems. She teaches to the smartest student in the class and forgets that we're not all math majors. For tests, she'll give you one thing to study, then put something completely different or ten times harder on the test.

This was hands down one of the hardest classes I've ever taken. She refuses to help even when she sees no one understands and her tests are a lot tougher than she makes them seem. She does give partial credit though. Her homework is insanely long and annoying. Very conceptual examples. Unless you decide on being a math major STAY AWAY.

Great professor who communicates the subject well. She's very "to the point" and her lectures were never confusing, even though the material in the textbook could have easily been a challenge. Homework was a reasonable amount and exams were challenging, but fair.
Out of the various 2210 professors, she is by far the best at teaching the material. Definitely take her class even if you have to switch stuff around in your schedule.
Informative classes. Helpful for homework and prelims. Fun person. A little lack of explanation in proofs though.
She is a great instructor. She always explains things clearly and thoroughly. She is very knowledgeable about the subject, and has a great sense of humor.
I love her. She's very easy to understand and has a very cute sense of humor.
she's a really good teacher; she makes things really clear and creates a great atmosphere. Too bad she's not in the discussion to explain the homework!

Good at explaining stuff, does a pretty good job at asking if people have questions, creating an atmosphere where it's ok to ask questions, then waiting long enough for people to actually think and ask them, and of course answering them in a helpful way. Plus she's pretty funny. Great English accent for it not being her native language (Portuguese)

He tends to ramble during lectures and he doesn't ever finish his lectures they always leak into the next class. There are 3 quizzes and 3 midterms (1 being the final) and 3 short essays. Attendance is mandatory. He's very reachable outside the class.

This professor is so boring. Drones on during his lectures, making it difficult to pay attention. Attendance is mandatory.  You only have 3 quizzes, 2 midterms, and a few other assignments, so there aren't many grades. Only 1 textbook is rlly required (SAMC), the other one you can get by without. The content is interesting, but he makes it boring.

Ok look.. Just know that at the beginning of the  semester I just knew I was going to get an F in this class. That didn't happen though. The lectures are so bad its not even funny, he takes attendance, response papers are very easy. There is a study guide that is basically the test so as long as you do the guide you should be good.
He is a little unorganized but other than that he's great! Cares about students and really appreciates participation.
Gonna need a good memory. Easy papers; Long and memory focused tests; Beware of maps quizzes!

Guy just simply doesn't know how to teach. Disorganized, bad time management, nervous, etc. Course is relatively easy but a such an energy drain. Others below have already said it: boring and a waste of time. Better off taking some other GE course and finding other avenues to learn.

Dr. Paulette is a nice enough guy, but his lectures are extremely boring. It's very rare that he actually finishes a lecture during a class period. Workload is manageable, tests and map quizzes are easy with a couple hours of studying, response papers shouldn't take much more than 90 minutes to write.

I personally enjoyed Tate because I love history, but I found the class very easy. He gives you everything that's going to be on the test beforehand so its incredibly easy to study and come in prepared. I didn't get a single grade below an A on the quizzes and tests. If you enjoy history then this professor is for you.

Dr. Paulette was very unorganized and his class was extremely dull and boring. Exams were based on readings, and there were readings assigned for every class period. The guy who sat next to me in class fell asleep every session if that can give you any idea about how this course went.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He is the most unorganized professor I've ever had. This class is just reading and writing 2000 word essays on the readings. He does not know what he's doing. Save yourself, and don't take this class.

This class is just reading, exams are online. You don't have to show up at all. He has slides that are mostly pictures and headings of notes that he shares but not his notes that he leads the lecture with. Until corona virus hit he didn't share those notes and lectured on tangents that didn't really help with the content of the course.

This class was incredibly easy. He is a terribly disorganized professor and you don't really need to pay attention in class to make a good grade. Study for a couple of hours the night before the exam and you should easily make A's on them. Map quizzes and short response papers are the only other assignments.

Lectures are by far the best resource, textbooks are a helpful supplement esp for exams, homework/quizzes are easy, up to 3 extra credit point on final grade for easy 1500 word paper, tests aren't brutal but do require some effort to study for and are matching & essay based, one of very few history courses I've ever truly loved 100% would recommend
Very good at explaining the subject with passion but can also be single minded when challenged.
No Comments

this class was very TOUGH the final was 65 questions but don't FEAR! for this class in order to pass 1. don't procrastinate, 2. attend class, 3. read the chapters and study guides, 4. ask questions if you don't understand, 5. record you can use your phone to record but make sure to ask. these are the steps to passing YOU CAN DO IT!!!.

Cinnamon is probably the kindest professor you will ever have. She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed in every aspect of life. She knows that everyone has different abilities and is great about pushing students individually to be the best that they can be. If you put in the work and give your best effort, you will do well.

Shes overall a great teacher. She just crams 5 chapters into one test and usually 3-4 pages full. The tests are true false and fill in the blank. The overall class is difficult for an theatre appreciation class. If you do not plan on furthering your major in theatre do not take this class. This class has been the most stressful course I have taken

Honestly just took this class because I needed a fine arts credit but she's pretty chill. All of the quizzes and tests are online and open book so if you are looking for an easy "A" definitely would recommend.

The class consists entirely of her lecturing about music from different decades. The lectures are interesting when she's talking about a decade you're interested in, but then the other lectures are almost unbearable. This is due to the lack of variety in the lessons. It's literally "just sit there and listen to me talk" for 115 minutes.

Professor Stevenson is wonderful, she is always ready to help assist her students and knows how to get everyone actively involved in the class. What is expected of you is clear and simple. Just do your work, follow the feedback she gives you and you will do great this course. She requires a discussion post on canvas about once a week so read!

Very easy class. We had four projects and they were all rather easy. The first two were papers and Dr. Stevenson is an extremely easy grader. We had a group project for our next project where we had to present on a building at ASU in regard to the the design of it. The final project was a video resume, which I really enjoyed. Easy A.

I loved her for an Eng teacher. 4 major assignments (3 written and one presentation) and weekly DB posts based on a chapter from the book. Fair grader and goes exactly by her rubrics. Class was mainly going over the topics and how-tos for the assignments. If you hate english like me, take her!

I took the hybrid class. There was a weekly discussion board, and four major writing projects. Class time was spent expalining the projects and peer reviewing drafts. She's a nice grader if you do the basic work.

This class was one of my favorites. I learned a ton and gained huge respect for rhetoric. The class is reading heavy, but the discussions are actually fun to participate in, and the final paper is not difficult. Dr. Stevenson also gives great feedback both in the comments section of the grade book and as video summaries at the end of each week.
I took her business writing course. Easiest business-related class I've ever taken.

She makes you do discussion boards on social issues which would be ok except they all come from one side so you never get to explore another viewpoint. Papers were easy , you have to post a video of yourself asking questions twice, if you do everything youll get an A.

While nice, Stevenson is not actually focused on teaching English. Rather, she prioritizes social issues, and has you write about them. If you want someone to teach you English structure, strategy, and convention, look elsewhere.

Great professor, great option for the English requirement. The class is online, and you have to post every other weekday. There are three essays, and though you still have to do the portfolio, it's not a big thing. She is really nice, and all of the material provided for the class is super interesting! You do have to record videos of yourself.

Online session A - 3 essays and weekly discussion boards. Not too time consuming, she is a fair grader with extremely clear guidelines and expectations! You get to learn about a lot of interesting topics as well. She offers a little extra credit but if you do all of your work, you won't need it! I would recommend this class.

Easy grader. Low standards across the board, so that's always nice. Very responsive to questions, quick grader. But, be prepared to not study English. With this professor, English is second to social issues. You can write poorly (to an extent), glorify feminism and whatnot in your essay, and get an A.  Not my cup of tea, but if you're into that..?

I  don't see how people could complain about her class. The expectations are NOT hard at al. You get three essays for the semester and I took the class as a hybrid so we met once a week which gave us time to write our essays and she even scheduled time for us to work on them instead of going to class. I actually learned in her class.

Honestly, the projects are somewhat difficult if you don't spend time figuring out what needs to get done. The blogs are done at the last minute by most of the class, and we all have to wait for the leaders to show their blogs, that's why I put mine out early. The lectures were a bit confusing, but we have to listen to them anyway.

A lot of discussion posts, 3/4 of the class can't do their work until the "leaders" post videos of themselves. The class is not set up to be worker friendly. If you have a job, do not take this class. 3 essays, third one is awful. Excessive workload for a 100 level class that everyone has to take.

Unfortunately i didn't get to finish this class due to my disabilities, but I took this class as a hybrid class. It is pretty easy as long as you do the once a week online assignments and show up to class. There are 3 or 4 papers but they aren't to hard but just be prepared to be writing them back to back. Stevenson is an OK teacher, not amazing.
3 major essays, which the topics are pretty clear. In-class lectures were pretty boring, however she would sometimes let us out early. She also gives good feedback. Overall, pretty good class!
Pretty good teacher. Has discussion boards but are pretty easy, and they are easy points. Papers are kind of tough, but as long as you work at them youll get an A.
I took this class as a hybrid course and it is definitely the easiest A I have earned. She is very kind and thorough and makes sure to help when needed. Minimal effort needed for full credit.

Awesome professor.  attendance is mandatory, 3 big projects worth %70 of your grade. she is really nice, there to help when ever you need her. she is a little hard grader tho. but highly recommended !

She is such a great professor and i would definitely take her class again. The entire class is essay based, and as long as you show up, participate, and write decent essays you will get an A. She is really helpful when it comes to writing, and gives great feedback. She really wants you to do well in her class.

Took this class as a hybrid. Very easy class that took minimal effort. Has one blog due a week  (so easy) and 3 writing projects that are easy as well. I thought class was pretty boring but you have to go because its only one day a week and she takes attendance! TAKE HER IF YOU CAN!

Cool teacher, enjoys her students and her Job. Is not a "by the book" type of personality or teacher, this is a good thing. Graded well and offered extra credit; I'd highly reccomend Mrs. Stevenson for english.
Professor Zillmer is an awesome teacher and is willing to help in whatever way she can! She wants to see every student succeed and she makes class interesting!

Best English teacher, she let's you pick your own topic for the semester and the papers are pretty straight forward. She was extremely helpful and cares about her students. Just remember to do the online postings!
Great teacher! She is extremely helpful and really cares about her students.
I took this class as a hybrid. One of the easiest English classes ever! She is such a great teacher and really cares about her students. I would recommend to anyone.

Formerly Paulette Zillmer (married now). Hybrid course - Online work and meet Fridays. Comes off as a ditzy schoolgirl at times, but passionate about English. Papers are straight-forward. No "cookie-cutter" formats. Understands different topics produce different results and grades accordingly. Overall good instructor and I liked her a lot.

One of the best teachers I've had. Paulette goes out of her way to help you understand. Explainations usually requires extra reading and research to get the full idea of suggestions and help, but your ideas will be better for it. She's  very demanding and doesn't take bs, but if you put in your time and work hard you'll learn a lot.

Overall the math classes at Cornell really aren't the best. This was one of those courses were the professors teaches a minimal amount of stuff in class and then the hw is crazy hard. The tests were ok I guess. The professor was decent I guess I skipped the vast majority of classes but still got a satisfactory.

Professor Tang's lectures are a bit hit or miss. He's better at explaining fundamental concepts than applications. Homework problems range from being very difficult to straight forward, but are worth a large percentage of your grade, so make sure you have friends in the class to work with. Exams are not similar to homework, so they are difficult.

I thought Prof Tang was a great professor. He was a really clear lecturer and went over things multiple times if we asked. He made difficult concepts seem more manageable. Recommend it for anyone who wants to go into banking or finance. It was hard work to study for the second midterm but well worth it. All homework is for completion and oyo

Johnny's Dyson's worst hire this semester. Dyson has been struggling to find professors and ended up hiring someone with no experience to teach a core finance concentration requirement. He will not curve the class despite low medians. Fairly difficult exams plus unfair participation points.

This is the WORST class you could take so DO NOT take it!! It was not a requirement for me but I was put into it anyways. The professor made so much stuff up during the final and had unrealistic expectations throughout the course. Also changing the final date and time to a time that was unreasonable for most!! Avoid this class at all costs.

Puts the bare minimum effort into her classes as well as grading. Does not care about her students at all. I learned nothing from this course and would have her fired. Terrible Professor and definitely should not be teaching
Very rude, disrespectful, and discourages students.

I had her for SCM 380, not 465 but that option isn't available. Her assignments weren't tough but her grading was and her explanations for assignments didn't make sense. She was also disorganized as she was missing links to articles and messed up to due date on a discussion board. The assignments are worth very little points. Do not take her!

Professor Vivek has a nice clear structured online class, some of the homework assignments don't have clear directions, but overall most assignments are pretty easy. My class was asynchronous, but she planned for us to have one synchronous simulation meeting which didn't go as planned, so if you have her online be prepared for that.

No one shows up to class because its a waste of life. If you read the book you dont know whats on the exam and she wont tell you what to focus on. She also deducts points for no reason.

If u want to actually learn chem. Then don't take this class. If you just want to pass then this is the prof for you.
