If you do not want learn CHM, take this class. This class allowed you to cheat!!!!!!! You will be fine.

She'e honestly a good teacher, everything comes straight out from her notes. Study her notes and the book. She even gives you the equation you need for the problem so you only need to plug in the numbers. She talks low so sit in the front, but you'll be fine if you ask her questions and study.
she is a good professor. she does grade hard and she expects you to read the lab book before coming to class. she is also the only professor who gives a final in lab.

This professor is extremely unclear, makes a lot of mistakes, and has difficulty explaining content so students can grasp ideas . I would never recommend her to anyone. I had to teach myself the course work via textbook. No thanks to her,i passed. I hope the other professors in the nursing program know how to teach
she speaks very low which makes her class very boring and hard to concentrate. I didn't learn anything in that if possible avoid taking her.
marks really hard. she can teach but u have to be seated in the front seat because she talks very low. u have to do work on ur own if u wish to pass

Not clear at all. I felt as though I was teaching myself Chemistry just to survive in her class. She gives homework and grades it after she gives you a test. So if your doing something wrong you have know idea. Her lectures are boring and it's hard to stay focused.
She is a good professor.

Dr. Karan knows what he is talking about when he lectures and does a good job at correcting your work and answering questions, however he does not always cover everything the outline of the course entails. I also believe he makes his assignments and tests way too easy to learn and retain that information.
Really nice teacher and very helpful. I was nervous for this class but he helped me throughout the whole semester. He has an accent, but he is easy to understand. I love his workbook.

You can barely understand what he is trying to tell you. I'm not sure he completely knows what he is talking about half the time. To make it worse he is the only one who teaches some of the classes FOR MY MAJOR. Avoid at all costs.

This class was one of the toughest accounting classes Ive taken. I went to SI which helped SO MUCH. Karan spends a lot of time doing problems but doesnt tell you where hes getting the numbers. Do the problems he covers multiple times, read the book, and go to SI. The pop quizzes are tricky, so stay on top of everything. Decent curve at the end

Vijay Karan was a pretty solid teacher. He expects you to have read the chapter before coming to class, so he doesn't spend a lot of time actually teaching much. He spends most of the class going over examples from the book. I feel like he did a great job explaining how to do things from the practice problems. The homework helps a lot on the exams.

This class is hard and Mr. Karan does NOT make it manageable. He is negligent and could careless if you are not understanding material. He goes SO fast. There were 8 people in the class RE-TAKING it, and the tests are not in the same format as the homework. For case studies he just picks grades out of a hat, you will never get 100%.

The class is almost half lecture and half practice problems. He tends to move very fast through the problems and skip some parts of the math; so If you have any questions, ask him when he's still on the topic. Overall enjoyed the class and he is very carrying. Go see him if you are confused on anything and be prepared to work for your grade.

Not doubt this class is hard, be ready to read before the class, and get familiar with problems that will be done in class. Professor Karan is super knowledgeable on the material, makes exercises easy to understand, and wants you to use your critical thinking. He is preparing students for their career not just to get a good grade.

Would not recommend. This was by far the hardest class of my college career. He simply does problems from the book the entire class, but doesn't explain where any of the numbers are coming from. No participation from the class because everyone is lost the entire time. I had to teach myself the entire course. Hard quizzes, hard exams, hard hw.

Professor Vijay is very nice when you talk to him during office hours and ask for help. However, he has an accent and is very quiet when talking. Combine these two, and I really couldn't understand what he was saying all class. Professor also tends to solve problems without clearly explaining where numbers came from or formulas.

The professor knows the material very well and he teaches techniques that make the subject less difficult to understand. The subject itself is not easy, so attending lectures and practicing assigned exercises are must to do well in the class. I thought his grading was fair. Sit as close to him as possible; his voice is unclear at times.

Possibly the best professor in Mihaylo. Dr Karan's amazing whiteboard notes get all knowledge points organized. He is always so nice and helpful. Took it in Summer. So 1-2 chapters per day and Accounting everyday all day. For each chapter, took 2-3 hrs to read first and 2hrs to do homework after class. Review often so you won't lose your way.

I think he is super nice and helpful. His class may be challenging but all the tests/ exams are exactly like what he has reviewed in class. And it is an accounting class, of course extra practice is needed. There are 3 essays, they are all applied theories from what you have learned in class with more analysis required.

You could barely understand his lecture especially with his deep voice. Simply solve the problems in class and does not tell you how he derive certain numbers. This leave students having to refigure the whole problem. For exams MC calculations are done in 1 or 2 step and working problem ranges in difficulty. Quiz are easy open notes. AVOID IF U CAN

This is my favorite accounting professor at CSUF so far. I learned many valuable cost concepts by attending his lectures, practicing homework, and preparing class work ahead. His quizzes are very similar to the classwork that he has taught you from the previous lecture. Tests are based on review and quizzes. The final is super easy if you study.

I'm still very split on this professor.  I learned a lot in his class (he always asks, "so what does this mean?"or "why does a manager worry about this?") His notes are very clear, straight to what you need for the tests. He doesn't collect hw or require attendance, but both are a must to pass. But without test notes or curve, this class is rough!

He gives out a lot of pop quizzes, but will count your top five. Also randomly collects homework. Biggest thing is that he does curve your grade. I got a D on the first test, and C on the second. Don't know what I got on the final, but my final grade was a B-. You have to study like crazy.
Take another one if you have a chance. He is not good in lecturing. He just solve the hw in class. So confused. Don't recommend him.

This class was so hard. Hardest acct I'v ever taken at CSUF. He randomly collects hw and gives a pop quiz (open problems/timed) almost every week. I kept up w all the reading and hw, and studied so hard to barely pass this class w a C. Exam avgs were Ds and Fs. Beware he does use C +/-.  Seemed irritated when students asked questions.

Nice person. If you ask for help, it's there. The class is kinda clear. exams are not that hard as long as you study the questions he teaches in classes. But his pop quizzes are not easy. you only have 10 mins to solve a problem. Overall, OK but a little hard.

He did not lecture at all. All he did is solve problems and you don't know anything if you dont do hw before hand. Test were so hard and ppl did so badly. Avoid him if you can. I passed his class with a B but I don't recommend him. He is not a good lecturer. He is nice but his way is not help much in class.

Need to read the chapter as he only does practice problems during class. No lectures. There's homework but he randomly collects. Pop quiz usually on the last chapter you just finished. 2nd exam was the hardest. Final was 50 mc. He curves depending on how the class did and it's at the end of the semester. Make sure to go to SI, it helps.

Toughest class I've ever taken! studied immensely and learned the material really well only to receive a C. insane amounts of homework. People did horrible on the tests because he doesn't give study guides and the tests were pulled out of a test bank so unrelated to class work. He is a good teacher but he goes over way too much material

GET READY FOR A WILD RIDE. He's a very nice man who know his stuff but he can't teach it. He just "reviews" stuff every class that you should have self-taught beforehand - doesn't work. Tests are BRUTAL, case studies are long/tedious... he doesn't curve but kept saying he would. Hardest class I've ever taken. I hate that it's required for an MBA :(

Just do yourself a favor and don't take with him t all! By far, worst professor I've ever had! Doesn't teach at all and have the hardest exams ever! Makes the course much harder !Don't recommend him at all!

Not recommended , he did not lecture at all. He is not a good prof to explain . I agreed cost is one of the toughest one but his way made it even more difficult than itself . Take someone else if you can. Tests are super hard , cummilative final .

Cost is a hard class! None the less, Karan teaches the way accounting classes should be taught: teaching a lot of problems in class and at home to practice. Take great notes, because I promise that he really does teach everything in class (I.e. reading can be less important but it always! helps). Think of the class as a bunch of templates. #advice

He is not a good professor for cost. He only solved problems and didn't lecture at all. You must know all materials before coming class. His tests are tough and not easy to follow him in class.  Take someone else if you can. I got a B+ but not recommend him. Good luck to all .

This class is a nightmare. Be prepared to study all day everyday! The professor basically goes through homework problems every lecture. I found it hard to follow at times and he didnt always explain where numbers came from. 2 midterms and a final. All short answer. Very difficult. You need to know the material well to at least get a C in the class.

Homework and pop quizzes are totally at different level. First test is super easy. Second and final will be brutal. His voice a bit low. If you don't like sitting in the front row, then you must pay attention in class. He goes over homework before each test. Must read the book and understand the materia. Attend his class frequently then you'll pass

Took this class during summer and got a B. Midterms and final were based on both multiple choice and written problems. Open book quizzes were all problem based (no multiple choice). Lectures focused on practicing how to do the problems. Never used a ppt during class. Do the homework! It was infinitely helpful for the test. Highly recommend him.
CONS: 6+ hr. Case studies, hard Midterm, excruciating Final, Unforgiving professor. PROS: Not much.

Nice man and a good teacher. While this is a VERY TOUGH class, he is always willing to help. Do as many problems in the book as possible; he posts the answers. Tests and cases are tough and time-consuming. You won't finish if you don't know what you're doing. If you work full-time, I recommend you take this class by itself during your term.

He is a very smart professor and knows material very well.  The textbook is very confusing and I barely used it.  He explains better than textbook.  So, it is very important to go to every class because his lecture is very clear and helpful.  Highly recommend this teacher.

This class is HARD. His quizzes are open book/open notes but don't underestimate the level of difficulty; always keep up with the homework!! First test was easy, the second was HARD. The final was easier than I expected. His teaching style is OK, but I wish he was more interested in our success than referring us to the tutoring center for help!!

He looks really nice and he gives you points (neutral feedback) for your home works which makes you think you are doing great but then gives a very low grade for your final. His nervous coughs during the lecture makes the lecture impossible to understand.He is also very biased. Don't take him if you have other options.

Professor Karan is a very nice person and he explained the materials really well. Cost accounting is probably the hardest class in 300 level, and the textbook makes students very confusing; it's not the professor's fault. His exams are hard, but he usually curved the exams.

Not a nice professor. Not willing to explain the materials for students. Quizs and tests are hard. The workload is heavy and he is helpless. This guy doesn't know how to teach. He makes the class harder than it should be.

ACCT 302: Most accounting students usually have good studying habits one might expect to do well. His quizzes are open note/book but...DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE and Exams are on another level! Reading material/ lectures do not correlate subject is difficult enough. Be prepared to begin a serious relationship with your cost book...and redo the homework!!

VERY CHALLENGING! The case studies took me days.His test a fair but difficult. You can't just know the material, you have to master it in order to do well.He is fair and very clear but moves quickly. Learn the material prior to class and attempt all homework  or you will for sure be lost in class.Loved the class, learned so much.
Pleasant demeanor and soft spoken.  However, as poster below said, don't be fooled by his smile.  He looks nice and pleasant but his exams are polar opposites! BUYER BEWARE!!!

Believe me when I say this class will occupy your mind, each day, throughout the semester. Dr. Karan makes the subject harder. You will need to put a lot of effort and time into this class. Do homework on time and do homework a second time before exams. Case studies consume a lot of time. Final is a beast! Karan is not easy and he expects a lot.

2 Exams, 3 Cases, 1 Cumulative Final. Don't be fooled by his pleasant smile, his exams are hideous!!! You must read & do homework to have a chance of succeeding. Do homework TWICE for higher probability! Exams are not like homework, they are 1 level harder!! Must know concept!! Cases take at least 6 hours to complete. Cumulative Final is hideous!!!

Great Professor; has a genuine interest in student's learning and has a clear teaching style. 2 midterms, 1 cumulative final, and 3 case studies. Do the homework every week and do it once again before the test. Pay attention to the lecture. There are no tricks on the exam. You MUST understand the concept.

There is a lot of material to cover in this class. He mostly goes over math problems in class, and he expects you to cover concept by yourself. He explains the material very well in detail. Class is 2 mid 1 final hw/quiz open book. The first midterm so far was 20 mc half concept half math (60% grade). 3 math problems with partial credit.40% grade

Honestly, the material is straight up hard. I would say the material is the hardest in 300 lvl acct class. But prof Karan is a very nice person who is willing to help you. His lecture is very organize, and the key to success is to pay attention! Quizzes and hw will boost your grade. 2 exams (15 mcq, 5 problems) and 1 final (50 mcq) take it with him

Extremely large amount of work especially if taken over the summer.  2 three page essays due every class period, in class midterm, group paper and presentation, individual paper and presentation, and take home final paper.  Yeah lots of stuff. But extremely good professor and a class meant to challenge the thought process of the student.
Very organized, very clear. The workload is a lot but necessary to learn the subject well. Very nice professor. Will take him as long as he teaches.

Took him over summer, be prepared to work! You have to learn everything and stay on top of the class. He covers material quickly and thoroughly, while focusing on book examples(provides answers). His explanations are clear and easily comprehendable. 2 MTs, 3 Case Study Papers, Final cumulative. The man knows his stuff and expects you to know it too
One of the best accounting professors I've had. Teaches hard topics clearly and there are no surprises on the exams. Highly recommend this professor

I got a B in ACCT511.  But, I liked his class so much, I signed up for ACCT521 as one of my electives and got an A from Karan finally!  He is perhaps 1 of the top 2 professors in the MBA program IMO.  If you're not afraid of hard work and real class discussion, take Karan's classes.  He doesn't blow smoke up your butt like most CSUF professors do.

OMG This has got to be the hardest class I have ever taken!! If you're in 510 and you think that's no walk in the park, beware of 511.  Though I think, Prof. Karan is the only prof you should take this course with.  Very approachable and certainly knows the subject matter.  His smile is very encouraging too!

This class is very hard. Very nice guy, show up to class so he sees you and sees your trying, he curves big time. DO THE HW PROBLEMS!

This is a hard professor to take for Managerial Accounting, but then again the subject matter is not a walk in the park either. If you study and show up you'll pass.

Very nice professor.he's got the knowledge and knows how to teach too. very clear and makes the subject easy to understand.He is very helpful and won't move on unless the material is understood by everyone.I will take other courses with him,exams are difficult, and need a thourogh understanding of the subject.3 projects,challenging but rewarding.
He is a good profssor and makes the material understandible. Exams are still difficult.

Cost accounting is hard - period.  This guy might seem intimidating at first but if you go to office hours or just ask frank questions in class when you don't understand something, he will make it crystal clear. He doesn't waste class time, a lot of material is covered but it never seems like he's rushing. Remember, no one can pass without studying

This is one of the best cost accounting profs at CSUF.  His class is HARD - do not underestimate the difficulty of the material.  You must study at great length, do the homework, and attend class.  While this class is difficult, it will definitely prepare you for upper division courses like ACCT 401.  Remember, anything worth doing is not easy.
A great cost professor. Study and you will do very well. Very nice guy and he is very patient. Go over the hw problems in depth and you will do great.
Very good professor. A lot of studying and tests are somewhat difficult. Just understand all homework problems and quizzes and you will do great. I definitely recommend him.

Very good at teaching the material. Gives open book/note pop quizzes and collects some of the hw. STUDY for exams b/c he teaches the stuff one way in class & then uses test questions that are much more advanced than what we learned. Curve not stated on syllabus, but obviously used b/c I passed! Not the worst professor I've taken.

omg this class is hard. Karan has a tendency to rush through the problems in class, sometimes he is difficult to follow. I suggest doing ALL of the homework, go to OFFICE hours, and take detailed notes @ EVERY class and u should be ok.

Difficult to understand at times, difficult tests, goes through examples at lightning speed. He only gives 3 examples for exam review, and then gives nothing close to them on the exam. Final also supposedly has exact probs from previous exams, but he completely changes them. Don't underestimate him - it will bite you in the behind if you do.
The best accounting prof. in CSUF.

Prof is very knowledgeable of the course and he demonstrates the easy way to understand the topic. He's very organized person. A lot of topics are covered in the course, however, just make sure you do your hw and understand the lecture well. He will go over a lot of exercises which is good. Touch class but payoff at the end!!
The best Accounting professor I ever had. Very knowledgeable and very easy to understand. He is always there whenever you need him.

He know the subject very well. I think he's a great teacher but he should have given us a break since Dr. Hoth didn't teach us anything for the first 5 weeks.  Karan took over and rushed without any consideration.  He didn't really lecture, only went over the problems. acctg 302 is only beginning class but Karan taught it like a 5oo level class.

This professor was our substitute for Hoth.  When Hoth left a month into the semester, Karan made us begin from the beginning of the text, so we were rushed a bit.  Now for the real rating.  Karan's class is pretty hard.  The hardest part is that he is VERY messy on the board.  His lectures are out of the text book's chapter questions.

Attend every lecture and pay attention. Study lecture notes and practice quiz will get you an A. He's not as hard as ppl say. I didn't do any homework after the first one. All I did is number the steps when he demonstrated so the notes did not look like a complete mess, especially calculation are jumping back and forth.

His tests are challenging and he sometimes lectures too fast.  That being said, you have to do the assigned HW, do extra practice problems, and attend every class meeting.  If you don't do any of those three, you will not pass the course.  If you do all three, then he is not as hard as many people make him out to be.

He is a very good teacher. The class is very structured and he really sticks to the schedule. If you dont show up to class you will not do well on the test. The test are very hard. He moves throught the lecture too fast and its hard to follow him sometimes.

My favorite accounting teacher at Fullerton. He knows the material very well. His class is well organized and structured. His exams are fairly hard, but if you study you'll do very well just like any college class.

I don't like him. I think he teaches good, but he made the exam unecessorily hard. I lost a lof of points on the conceptual questions, and those questions don't help in the real world.  Some students who had bank questions can do well in his class since they will not losse points.  He did not return my grade cards at all.

Dr Karan is a VERY NICE PERSON and approachable. He is willing to help you with questions you may have. In this graduate course THERE IS ALOT OF WORK and he is critical on presentations. He has take home final exam (2006) and grades on spelling as well. I must warn you tho- there is alot of work in this class.

Great teacher. If you want an A, you must know the homework and classwork backwards and forwards.  There are no tricks, you just need to know your stuff and study at least 10hrs for each test.  Very straight forward tests. He might curve a little but don't count on it.  Grade in class: A (after 2 tests).
I don't remember any thing from that class, cos I was asleep most of the time...!! Karan is really boring, to the extent that you lose him after 2 minutes of starting the class.

One of the easier Acct 307 Professors, be happy that you got him. And learning MS Access before you take the class is definately not necessary, so dont waste ur time doing it. VJ will teach you what you need to know in class, just take very detailed step by step notes on what he does. If u want an "a"; read book and b very familiar with hmwk.
Great Teacher.  There is a lot of studying involved but he is very sweet and approachable.  Do the homework and you'll be fine.

He is pretty straight forward in terms of his teaching. Focused on Access and Excel. Also has a group presentation at the end. Makes his statements sound like questions. Tough to understand sometimes and not always the nicest guy.
Nice teacher. He knows his stuff. Difficult class if you are not into computers and databases. Hard exams. Learn how to use MS Access before taking this class.

This course is so pointless. Karan teaches it as good as anyone could. Grade is based on 2 exams, 1 comprehensive final, 3 small Microsoft Access Projects, 1 individual research paper, & 1 group assigement which includes a PP presentation & paper. This class is not hard to pass just very boring.
Karan knows his cost accounting. He's a good teacher, but he grades hard.  No curve...no sympathy.  So, take notes, don't miss class

Do the online practice tests & the problems that he gives you in the book-they help (especially for the final).  He is difficult to understand and boring overall-bring your own powerpoint handouts to class to take notes on.

you won't understand him half of the time, because his voice is so hoarsed, and his lecture is so boring n straight from the text powerpoint. exams are tricky, and nothing like his lecture. bad prof to take for this class!
Beware.  He may smile and seem sweet in the begining, but his tests will kick your ass!

class was easily the hardest one ive ever taken,, your most likely an mba student if you take it so make sure you have some time to study,, he is a good teacher but the material is extensive,, study the homework and you will do fine-the exams are the same
One of the best acc teachers I've had.  The class is not easy and you'll have to work and study to do well, but Karan is very thorough and helpful!  You'll actually learn stuff. Highly recommended.
Interesting class, good instruction.

I've had him for many different classes.  He is one of the best for the program. He has a lot of experience. He cares about his students.  It is so important to have a teacher that cares about the students success.  He teaches the material that needs to be taught & you really couldn't ask for a better teacher.

If you take Ravi for intro to hospitality I wouldn't buy the book I didn't use it to study because the test was more of the slides then then the book. Also he gives you the test answers after you take the test and you can use them to make a quizlet for the final! Also make sure you attended every class, he uses it as a part of your grade.
Ravi Karen is truly a gem in the HTEM department like all of the professors in this department.

While listening to Dr. Karan can be enough to put you to sleep, he does give you every opportunity to earn points. Both classes I took were similarly structured, and easy to follow in terms of due dates and when exams were. All that being said, he won't help someone that doesn't want to help themselves.

He's very nervous about lecturing and it shows. Its hard to get a complete answer out of him. He is willing to help you, but you kind of have to coax him into feeling comfortable talking to you. To me thats just as much work as just getting the book and teaching it to myself. I'm sure he will get better with experience. He knows the subject.
Pretty easy class, I took it online and I heard it's harder in class. It can be confusing though, but you have to put some time into it.

Just average. Good person, lectures were pretty boring. Grading rubrics were not straightforward, even for some prelims. Still, not difficult and final project instead of exam. Doesn't give A+ (even for students who earn 98-100), annoying for ENGRI course
Amazing and understanding professor!

For each lecture there is a quiz the questions seem much more like word games. The course has everything to rate, including quiz, prelim, projects and written homework. The lecture is no more interesting than the reading materials.
Does't know how to coordinate. Not that knowledgeable.

He is very sweet but fails to realize that he is teaching an introductory course. He will present information in lectures which has never been touched before if you did not read the book throughly. The content itself is interesting and the exams were not terrible. It is probably possible to get a perfect score in his class if you put in the time.

This professor is very tough and the class is loaded with a ton of content. However, this class is very doable, especially if it is taken in the summer without the lab. The professor is very brilliant but struggles to understand that the material is introductory. As long as you read the textbook and do practice problems you will do great.

He clearly knows a lot about genetics, but his lectures focus almost enitrely on details, rather than the larger picture.  His tests focus on stuff that's covered more thoroughly in the problem solving sessions, so you should definitely attend them.  Lab is, as its reputation suggests, is very time intensive.

Class was really difficult, long nights preparing for this course. Almost the most difficult course I have ever taken at Cornell. Course can be very time consuming if you want to do well. The bad rumors surrounding it are true, lab sucks. Flies take longgg time to count while bacteria concepts are hard to understand! Take early & don't suffer late!
Ross is awesome, and he is really helpful if you come to his office hours. Despite the difficulty of this class, I actually enjoyed the lectures.

He is very nice and willing to help if you approach him. Although the course material is hard and a lot of work he is a nice guy and a genius in genetics! If you don't understand something, ask questions because he doesn't mind going over it again. The textbook is helpful.

spends a lot of time focusing on intricate parts of genetic processes, but fails to relate back to the big pictures. when studying, it's easy to get rapped up in the small details and forget to review the meaning/role of these details in the greater process (i.e. nondisjunction)
Ross is a really sweet guy, although the class is all it's rumored to be.  However, he does want his students to do well, and will do all he can to help, if you approach him

He's obviously a genius in Genetics. It's amazing the depth with which he knows the material, even for a professor and a researcher. But as a professor he expected the students to follow too much too quickly. He's one of those people that proves the saying that the smartest people don't always make the best teachers. Debbie Nero helped a lot.
HORRIBLE

He's a nice guy and he's obviously a genius in his field. However he assumes you understand everything and forgets this is an intro class, not a graduate study. His office hours were impossible. Debbie was a lot more helpful.

Macintyre is an average professor. He's not particularly open or receptive, and i don't blame him with so many hardcore premeds in the class.The people who do talk to him a lot are oblivious to how much they annoy him, and these are the same suck-ups who think mac actually likes them.
Mac's a nice guys and a pretty clear lecturer; gives breaks during class; knows his stuff. Nonetheless, Debbie Nero is better.
He is very confusing and not helpful when you ask questions!  Debbie should give the lectures!
the class just sucks.  debbie should teach

The breaks in lecture are great and he often lets class out early.  However, this class is still a ton and a half of work. He sometimes doesn't emphasize the main point you are supposed to be getting out of his examples.

Genetics at Cornell IS everything that it is made out to be.  The amount of work is absolutely incredible.  In the next three weeks, there are a total of 6 lab reports due (3 on flies, 3 on bacteria) to go along with lecture material and an exam!
Boring, redundant, and unclear
he is smart, and just because you are incompetent you should not be critical toward him.
This was the absolutely worst class I've had at Cornell.  He was mean, cruel, and absolutely useless!

Ross was great. If you don't understand something, take the initiative to go to his office. He will remember your name for the rest of the course, and talk to you during class. Gives breaks during long lectures. Go to Nero's review sessions--they are key!
Awesome guy.  Hard exams! Very smart. I hear he's better than other genetics professors.
Very knowledgable, but he never repeated important points. A no-no in genetics.

Professor Brann is a very memorable professor. Islamophobia, Judeophobia and Racism was an incredibly interesting course that I looked forward to attending. His lectures always had different formats which kept class interesting, and he always included snippets of current, relevant news which made the content more applicable!

The only thing that made me mad was how disrespectful other kids were towards Brann. Very passionate and knowledgeable about the field, and will (quite literally) get on his knees to beg students not to stress about essays
Excellent professor. Would not change a single thing. I came to lecture every day, not because we needed to for a good grade but because it was so interesting.

Opinionated, funny, and very unique style of teaching. No exams or big papers. Responds to emails within SECONDS. He is the friendliest professor you will meet, but some students take advantage of his kindness and do the bare minimum. I kind of wish he demanded more.

Professor Brann was a great lecturer who always made content relevant and interesting to learn. He was also very caring and receptive to all students, he pushed back a deadline when we were all stressful. Overall, a great class with not too much reading, grading is left to the TA's but they are always willing to meet. Overall, very solid professor.

Pretty good class, lectures were engaging for the most part, but sometimes class was a little bit hit or miss for me. That said, Brann always does his best to make the material interesting, explain larger themes of the class, and if all else fails, crack a joke. Makes the class easy but grade ultimately depends on TAs.

Professor Brann is an extremely intelligent, wise and kind person. The US and Middle East class is taught in an objective, broad fashion and Professor Brann's anecdotes are interesting. He makes an effort to get to know his students and really respects people seeking him (OH). Grade was negotiated at the end of semester!

The class is quite reading-heavy - at least 40 pages of reading for each class. There are bi-weekly mini essays which are do-able. There are no prelims/final which is pretty nice. If you struggle, Professor Brann is incredibly helpful, and I definitely recommend going to his office hours.
Awesome professor and easiest class at Cornell. Don't have to do the reading, don't have to show up to lecture. Overall an easy A plus.
Professor Brann is a wonderful person with great knowledge to share with his students. Take a class with him before you leave Cornell.

People disagree on whether Brann is a Zionist or pro-Palestinian, which tells you a lot about how objective he is during class. There's a lot of reading, but I was able to not do most of it, only what was required for weekly mini-essays. Easy class. Also we read an amazing textbook with Israeli and Palestinian perspectives.

Absolutely phenomenal... Was more than willing to give out As and class content was VERY interesting.  Clearly cares about students, is very easy to talk to outside of class, and is very interested in material.  I LOVED Professor Brann.

Brann is basically a rock star- he shows up to class in black jeans, combat boots, and Ray-Bans. He's great at mediating discussion and presents a tersely debated topic with levity and objectivity. He's a clear and thorough lecturer and very approachable outside of class for essays and such. Great guy and genuinely cool.

Approachable, fair, interesting, and clearly knowledgable. Just FYI: most of my discussion section and Brann himself seems to lean pro-Palestinian. BUT Prof. Brann makes a VERY admirable effort to not reveal his views. Given how heated the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is, he takes a very even-handed, informative, and scholarly approach.

This dude is chill...one of the best mediators of discussion and participation I have seen even in a large lecture class. Class isn't too difficult, and is very interesting if you are into studying different religions.

For a topic that is relatively difficult to present as unbiased, Brann did a good job in this class, especially with such a heartfelt conflict. Though I knew quite a bit of the background and material before the class, overall it was still very informative and improved my insight on the conflict. Overall, a not overly stressful, interesting class.
Brann is the best! He's classes are easy, lectures are engaging, and he is extremely approachable. I can't recommend him enough.

Terrible class, avoiding taking it if possible... Poor depiction of religions, not evenly spread over timeline either... Grading is totally objective- depends entirely on TA... Brann is nice enough and will offer extensions if necessary, but just rambles in class making it difficult to follow or take notes.
Great. Cool topic, nice guy, flexible with deadlines. Tried to present everything objectively.
Great course, great professor.  Very few assignments but a lot of studying needed for difficult exams.

brann is completely overrated. his lectures have no organization to them, and it feels like he's always mindlessly rambling. i got an a in the class, but only because i looked everything up on wikipedia before the exam. his lectures were way too confusing. he is a nice guy.

This guy is a great professor. I highly reccomend anyone to take this class. Not only was the class based on an interesting subject, but his lectures were clear, concise and fair. Great profesor. Also, exams and papers are not that difficult.

Great class; great professor! Brann really knows his stuff, and communicates the issues of today’s pluralistic, multi-religion society. He was engaging and extremely interesting (with breaks of levity also). I would recommend this class and this professor. Exams were easy, and papers were interesting to write.
Great class!  Brann is what a professor should be!  Provocative and approachable with a desire to see his students learn.  That's it!

He's a great lecturer, is understanding, easygoing, really cares about students and deals well with controversial subject matter.  Regarding other comments here, I was surprised to find someone thought he interjected his opinion too much--maybe he's changed, but I thought he tried very hard to not let his opinion be known.

One of the few professors who can lecture without lots of fancy visual aids and powerpoint and still be totally interesting. Clear, balanced views on controversial topics, sensitive to his students and fair. Lectures are like fascinating stories, and readings assigned are all relevant, interesting, and of reasonable length. My favorite professor.

I like professor Brann. He doesn't assign too much work, but his class is interesting nonetheless. Presents things coherently even though he has a tendency to generalize. Yes he's a leftie, and does tend to inject his opinion into lecture moreso than other profs. He's still recommended to anyone with even a peripheral interest in the Middle East.
No Comments
an excellent lecturer but a little too opinionated/far left for me.
No Comments
Loved 4740 a great class
terrible lectures - hes unclear and goes off on tangents. youre better off taking the AEW and not showing up to class. wait until you can fit strogatzs class into your schedule and take it with him.

Although sometimes lectures are a bit fast, he makes sure the class is following him. One of the best lecturers in the math department. Makes grading scheme very clear, and exams were manageable and were graded ridiculously quickly. Problem sets are relevant and not too difficult.

Professor Sosoe is my favoriate Prof at Cornell, he really makes you learn lots of stuff (e.g., reinforcement learing). Actually I worried a lot about my grade, but he is not a tough grader, I think I am not a top student in his class, but I really study hard. His exams, HW are really designed to reward to hard-working people, so don't worry.
Amazing lecturer, definitely one of my favorite classes at Cornell so far. Take it if you like history, food, Amstud, even if you're not in those majors

An engaging lecturer, but not a funny or chill professor. She took attendance randomly, gave a pop quiz on the first day back from a break, and had some assignments due on Friday nights. Overall it was a lot of work for an 1000 level class. She is passionate about her subject matter though - I'd say take her class, just don't expect an easy A.

Professor Wolfson is by far, my favorite professor. He is very thorough with his lectures, doesn't read off the powerpoint. He talks the entire class based on his knowledge and everything is as if you were reading the textbook. He prints out notes for everyone and is accessible. You def have to work for your grade, but you learn a lot in the end.
Dr. Wolfson is a wonderful professor. I took him for A&P1 and 2. I feel like he really cares about his students! This class is no easy A, but if you do the work it is enjoyable. HIGHLY RECOMMEND :)

This is a hard class, a lot of people come with the expectation to be spoon fed. Studying your notes and textbook is basic, Ive found eveeything on the tests in the book afterwards. Professor Wolfson has been amazing. He is preparing people for the intense health field. He explains well, takes the time to help out of class. He is knowledgeable.

This was the hardest class I've ever taken. I had him for both A&P I & II, both of which I got C's in. He's a real nice guy but the lectures are extremely intense & the tests are worded insanely different than the lecture. He gives you plenty of extra credit opportunities but I'm sure that's the only reason I passed both classes.

Very hard class!!! If you work full time, with a family, be prepared to dig deep. He explains the material well, but if you miss a class you can fall behind. He has no curve, what you put in is what you get, expect to spend 30 hours a week studying. His class is a full time job. You will learn allot!!

Knows the material. Helpful. Put in the effort. Do the extra credit. Get ready to study, study, and study! Work hard and you will do well. If you think you will skate through being spoonfed and it isn't going to work for you.

Everything on the exam are in the powerpoints, verbatum. You will have to write on the printouts of those, so attendence is very manditory and one can't just sleep. But there's nothing tricky there and he's not trying to fool you; just study the lecture and you'll get A's and B's on the exams. Focuses on the anatomy so you -know- and will remember

Lousy teacher.  I made a good grade but only because I studied and learned on my own. He assumes you already know the material.  Not sure he is too clear on much of the material and that is why he doesn't explain things to the class.
Professor helpful but talks as if you understand it already.Not a bad professor but his test are sure hard and complicated.

Heidi is really so so sweet and is so understanding but she does not understand how a cornell student functions. She does not give A+ when they matter so so much here and she is heavy on group work to the point where our final project was a group project. She is so kind but a LOT of work
I loved the course structure and knowing the professor's expectations. The depth on the discussion boards was fantastic.
Attention to detail. The professor took the time to read the students weekly assignment and write a comment. The course was very informative. I also liked the weekly video the professor posted.

Well-designed course. Good-balance of reading + lectures. Discussion Board emphasis: great, but cumbersome -many in class do not post until late in the week or on the day the assignment is due; recommend 2 substantial DB posts per week instead of 3 . Gives timely thoughtful feedback. Is Inspiring, challenging, brilliant. Best Prof at Cornell.

Reid Friedson's classes are challenging and inspirational. I have taken two of his classes and walked away, not only with solid base in the subject matter, but also with a desire to learn more. There are expectations, certainly, but that's required if we are to grow. Take a class with Reid Friedson. You'll be glad that you did.
A real pleasure! Looking forward to having him again in a future course.

Taught Quantum Mechanics II. Very unintuitive course material, but this professor makes the course as intuitive as possible and has great explanations. Clearly knows what he's doing and makes this course tolerable.

Frank Wise is an incredible professor and lecturer. He cares deeply about the subject and the students, and really wants everyone to learn. He continually adapts the curriculum to fit the students needs and is always very understanding. One of the best professors I have ever had.
Prof. Wise is one of the best professors I've had at Cornell. He understands the material extremely well and is great at explaining it/answering questions.

Prof. Wise is a cool guy.  He knows a lot about nanotechnology and can explain it on a lower level so it is easy to comprehend by people who have no prior knowledge of the subject.  Very interesting course material.

Since the course does not have a textbook, all studying must be done from your in-class lecture notes and other resources Professor Wise provides. The lectures and labs are interesting, though often covers unfamiliar material. Overall, a decent class to take as your ENGRI, though somewhat difficult.

Prof Wise is certainly a remarkable instructor. His clarity and quality is apparent in his lecture notes and homeworks. And he does a great job relating the theory to real-world applications and technologies. Take any course he teaches and you will be more than happy.
His lectures are well planned and but he can also adapt to answer group specific questions.  He is also willing to help and is anxious to use questions as a teaching tool

My favorite professor/class first semester of freshman year.  The class material can get quite difficult at times, but if you go to lecture and the occasional office hours, Frank will clear things right up. Also, he manages to make even the stupidest question an opportunity to teach something cool.

Prof Wise knows his stuff more than almost all professors at Cornell, but the class can get frustrating, especially during the problem sets. Tests are a challenge, but fair. Office hours are quite useful. Don't try to do the homework by yourself, talk to other people.

Professor Wise is one of the best professors at Cornell. His lectures are well organized and clearly presented.  His tests are difficult but fair.  He very much wants his students to understand the material and becomes concerned when they have difficulties.
Great Lecturer, CS4220 is a HARD class with a lot of linear algebra

Really knows his stuff and explains things clearly (but in that way where you're listening in lecture and you're like "ahh yeah makes sense" but then you have to synthesize it outside of class and you're like "????"). Really wants to help. Homeworks were very difficult and time-consuming; the class groupchat was necessary.
Great lecturer, committed to teaching the material and open for questions. Enthusiastic about the subject, really enjoyed his class.

The best teacher I've had my entire life. Understands how to explain concepts thoroughly and precisely, leaving little room for ambiguity. Homework took me a VERY long time (more than most), but the class was still well worth it.
A really good professor. Really smart and welcome. Can be considered as the best professor I ever met at Cornell.
Good lecturer. Homeworks were quite difficult.

Would not recommend taking this class with him. I took it when COVID first started but think about it to this day. He's nice and it's an easy A, but I learned the literal bare minimum of linear algebra. I occasionally am embarrassed that I don't know linear algebra concepts I need in my STEM classes now. If I could go back I would take ENGI linalg.

Professor Nerode is a fine mathematician, and a very interesting person to listen to, but I unfortunately learned next to nothing in his class. He gave us an overview of the subject matter more than an explanation of it. The main ideas seemed to be there, but we never got any real practice in order to assimilate them.

While his lectures were often confusing, he was always open to meet outside of class. He is clearly extremely well read. He doesn't care about grades, but is interested in students getting the most they can out of the class and their investment. If you can show that you are interested and care about the material, the grades should follow.
Don't take his class if you want to learn the material. Literally didn't learn anything. Got an A in the class. What he teaches and what's on the tests are completely different.

He is a legend in the Math world, but he is old and lacks clarity during his lectures. However, discussion sections are helpful, and as long as you hand in all of your homework assignments, you should do well. Also, there were two in-class exams and no prelims nor finals. Get to know him though; he is a very interesting man.

Prof Nerode is an excellent person, and always ready to help. His lectures can be slightly unclear at times but if you study the material, its almost fine and the Prof is always there to spend time with you to help you understand. Willing to help out beyond his class. Homeworks are sometimes long and hard, but fairly graded and exams are quite easy

Nerode is a really nice guy. His lectures are pretty pointless since he mostly reads from his notes that are online anyway. However, those notes (which he wrote) are pretty good. Tests are pretty easy. Homeworks are a bit harder and kind of long but not terrible.

Prof. Nerode is kind, approachable, understanding, and overall just a great man! The fact that he's still teaching at the age of 81 explains why his lectures can at times be a bit difficult to follow. But he was very understanding when it came to prelim conflicts so he has my utmost respect. Would definitely take any other class with him!

Took linear algebra with Prof. Nerode in Spring 2013. Professor Nerode is a very kindhearted and caring man. He's a great person, but unfortunately not mumbles to himself in lecture, but that's totally understandable since he is 81. Problem sets were mostly all proof-based (great for math majors) while prelims only had computation-based questions.

Nerode is an amazing mathematician but it's just very hard to understand him because he lectures on such a high level.  He is getting older and he can be very impatient and incompetent at times.  The class was hell, the assignments were very tedious and people at the support center even said he is odd, to say the least.

He has decided to no longer use a textbook so he has his long printed lectures that he just reads in class so there is no point in going to lecture.  Homework is difficult and for me, going to TAs office hours were a must- his were useless.  He is a nice grader though.  I got a 33% on the first exam and I still got an A in the course.
No textbook for course. No need to attend lectures. Homework is hard but workable. Extremely easy exams.
He's nice in grading and test. Useless lectures.
Greatest professor ever! His tests are just like the sample tests. The first quintile on a prelim was 118...out of 120. Take any of his classes.

I think he's better at teaching history of mathematics/logic than analysis. Classes are usually unclear and it doesn't seem to make much of a difference if you go or not since reading the book by yourself gives pretty much the same result. Plus you won't have to decipher his handwriting if you just read the book.
I know this guy is brilliant, but he can't teach for his life.  Very unclear, rambles and cannot answer questions.  The class isn't so hard, though.
Lectures were absolutely useless the entire semester.  Learned jack.  Doesn't seem to work his own problems for exams so doesn't know exactly how doable (or not) his own exam is.

Prof. Nerode is a really nice guy.  Unfortunately, he doesn't even understand his notes.  All he does is read them off and get himself confused. Class is 100% useless and the homework is really hard to do with no teacher. ALWAYS go to SECTION. Tests are so easy.
The class was pretty easy but I still felt like I learned something.

The class is ridiculously easy in that you hardly have to do anything to do well on the tests. Even so, his lectures are useless and I could not understand a single thing he tried to explain. It doesn't help that it is also impossible to read his handwriting on the board.

I took a "math in perspective" class with him and one other student.  I didn't get a whole lot out of the class content wise, but he told fascinating and funny stories and anecdotes about the history of math and his associations with other famous mathematicians.

The most kind and compassionate professor on this campus!  You will all do well in his class because he doesnt care about grades as much as he cares about teaching you how to logic, reason, and think.

He's a brilliant man, I wish I could understand all he tried to teach us. I think that was the biggest problem - teaching on a level that most undergraduate students could understand. Fascinating and intelligent.

Lectures consisted of him reading to us off overheads (which usually had errors).  Never looked up during lectures and mumbled a lot.  Nice person, but lectures were useless.  Only 25% of the class came to the lectures.
Easy assignments, useless lectures

I took Professor Netravalli's class as a non-FSAD major and personally found the material a bit difficult to digest. However, Netravalli was very understanding and was available and enthusiastic to help during office hours. He even held a review session for the final exam. Overall very fair testing and wonderful professor!!

The Fibers, Fabrics and Finishes class was an interesting introductory course. Professor Netravali worked hard to make sure his students understood the material, which for the most part, was very basic. Be prepared to do a lot of memorizing though! Tests were extremely fair and straight-forward.

Amazing class. I learnt an amazing amount in this class. I expected it to suck, but he made it not only fun, but interesting. The tests were very understandable and easy and he is a great professor overall who loves to talk about fiber science. He's AWESOME.

Instructor talks a lot but not too fond of lecturing from the Human Resource Book.  Lots of extra assignments, lengthy rubric for case studies, final paper includes interview and presentation.  Very slow at correcting assignments. She is heavy on participation - almost threatening students who don't chime in. Lot of tests & busy work. Fair grader.

She is an excellent professor, and you can learn a lot from her. She is very lecture oriented, and sometimes gets distracted/switches topics. Don't zone out in class. She goes over everything in class and is very detailed, which can sometimes be boring if you already understand the material.

Very nice professor, willing to listen and have conversation with class while lecturing. Very patient, doesn't mind explaining things repeatedly to students who aren't catching on to something. Strict on time spent in classroom (won't end class early, Davenport policy), but understanding if you need to leave early for personal reasons.
Great teacher, very knowledgeable. Class wasn't bad.

This professor a practicing attorney is used to teaching law students. She's (don't let the name mislead you)nice, respectful and has SO much experience, but has a difficult time explaining material to those w/o prior legal knowledge! Heavy course load, LOTS of reading, difficult tests and many case studies.  Very little application to BUSINESS.

The prof is a former attny teaching law practices to non-legal planning students. If i was a law student, i would like this but i am not.This prof was demanding with class legal expectations. Instead of helping the class by posting her detailed PP, she didn't & made sure the class stayed confused. This teacher lacks what it takes to be a good prof.
best professor ever. She relates pratical experiences to information in the text. She took the time to make sure you had clarity on the material.

One of the most boring professors I have had in 4 years of college.  She is unengaging and the class is uninteresting.  She takes all the potential fun out of criminal justice.  She makes you want nothing to do with the subject by the time the class is finish.  STAY AWAY FROM THIS CLASS, WHEN SHE IS TEACHING.  Frustratingly boring teacher.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had in almost 4 years of college.  She is unengaging, and boring. She does her best to make the tests difficult.  She is not good at returning calls, emails etc.  I was interested in the class going in, but lost interest after the first  week.  I DO NOT  RECOMMEND TAKING HER CLASS.
Best professor at this university.

Professor Wilkinson is a fantastic professor, on top of being a respected person. This course taught me a lot about topics in environmental law and regulation, and his method of delivery was well-suited for the content. He assures that each student has the appropriate resources to pass the class, and was available outside if the student needed.

He gives good feedback so ask questions in class and visit his office hours. He is one of the most knowledgeable professors in the program. His courses are mostly lecture based with discussion. He does extensive prep for his lectures this makes his lectures very comprehensive. Be ready to explore in depth the topics for each lecture before hand.

Dr. Wilkinson is a great at conveying the ideas he needs to get across each lecture period. This class is difficult and rigorous, but it is not impossible. Be sure to email him or meet at his office hours for clarity on anything. He is VERY understanding and is here to serve the student. He's also a very fair grader when it comes to exams/homework.

Dr. Wilkinson is an amazing instructor. He has been in the game for a while and understands the student. The way the class is set up gives the student ample opportunity to receive a perfect grade. Bottom line: show up to class and do the assigned readings (he only assigns what is necessary, not entire chapters) and you will be just fine.

At first, I was very intimidated by Professor Wilkinson. I was particularly worried about the tests. After a few weeks in, I found that he cares about every students success in his class, he is very accommodating, and he will do what he can to help you out. He does review sessions, answers questions, and is available outside of class.

He is the best professor in this school! I highly recommended taking his class! I learnt a lot! He gave a pre-lecture quiz for every lecture, but as long as you read the book, the quiz is easy. The exams are not hard if you do all the quetions on the study guide. For exam 3, 4 and the final, you can choose MCQ or short answer format of the exam.

Dr. Wilkinson is both an amazing vessel of information and resource for his students. He cares about those taking his courses, and he places an important value on each student's success. Don't forget to always read the textbook too! While some of the content may be challenging, he is the kind of professor that takes time to help you understand it.

GWW is the real deal. He is very knowledgeable and takes great care in developing his course materials for his students to be learned. The subject matter is not easy and neither is the class but he is the kind of teacher that you want to excel for. He provides all that you need to be successful and gives you the formula to do so.

Professor Wilkinson is by far the best professor University of Findlay has. Not only are his lectures original and not based off a PowerPoint. He has passion about the material and will keep you up to date about things happening in the real world. Professor Wilkinson will make sure you understand the material and keep his doors open always
Best professor I have ever had.
Hard class. Need to read and study a lot to make sure you understand the material inside and out. You Need to focus in class and cant skip one class, or youll miss a whole part of an exam

Best professor I've ever taken here. He is knowledgeable on environmental law and regulations, motivates students to do well, and truly cares about every student he teaches. He makes lectures memorable and even will go out of his way to help you with your future success (academic and even career wise). His classes are hard, but I've learned so much

Knows the material very well and can answer any question you have. Is always open to talk with any questions during open hours. Need to put in the time to study and do the exercise sets because he gives good feedback on them and are basically study guides for the exam. Need to read the book but the book has information to fill in his lecture.

Sets you up for success . Has multiple supplemental readings online, gives you exact book pages to read, uses questions from the exercise sets on the exams, doesnt hide what will be on the exam, wants you to learn the material not just remember. Is always willing to talk and is easy to get along with . Does not make it hard to do good in class.

Mr. Wilkinson clearly laid out what was expected of us from the beginning. At first it seemed like a lot, but if you do the work he gives and attend class, you'll do fine! He keeps class enjoyable, and really tries to get to know his students. Be prepared for a good amount of reading and come to class prepared, he likes to keep you participating!

This class is the hardest class in the major, however it is the class that I learned the most from. He does a great job in lecture with a lot of writing on the board, so be ready to take plenty of notes. He is also always willing to help you when you ask him for help. You are not going to be in cruise control, have to put in a lot of work to excel.

Professor wilkinson is the best professor UF has. He will take time out of his personal life to make you successful. He opens his office for questions , conversation and even mentors you to success. If it was not for professor wilkinson I would have not been as successful in the esoh major. Take all his classes and you will be the best!

Grant Wilkinson is the best of Findlay's professors. He has exceptional lectures with a passion to teach. He does make you work for it, but for good reason. His class contains very practical material. Don't think you can just skate by in this class. There is no one more dedicated to providing a quality education than Grant Wilkinson.
Best professor I have ever bad
Hands down the best professor! His lectures are interesting and keep you engaged.

Professor Wilkinson is a great man, in and out of the classroom. He is extremely helpful and wants his students to succeed. Every lecture is important, in depth and interactive.  There is no "busy work". Everything is applicable to your future. Work hard in his classes and you will be satisfied with the results.

I have taken every class The University of Findlay offers with Professor Wilkinson, because I have learned a lot from him. He is a challenging professor and expects a lot from students. However, he truly cares about every one of his students and will do anything to help you succeed. I truly respect this man and would encourage taking his classes.

Professor Wilkinson is one of my favorite professors I have ever had. He is very clear in his expectations and requires your participation in class. His lectures are very clear and he is organized in his presentation of class materials. Professor Wilkinson truly wants everyone to succeed and has high expectations of his students. He is a great man.
Hard classes, need to attend. study really hard or you wont pass for sure

Cant fit enough good things in this box about Dr. Wilkinson to do him justice. This was my 3rd class with him and though the course challenges you to be the best student you can be if you put in the work, your grade will reflect that. Stand up guy and someone you want in your corner in life. Will do anything for his students.

This was definitely one of my favorite classes.  Professor Wilkinson is by far the best professor I have ever had.  His class structure is organized and you really get a lot out of his lectures.  His exams are challenging, but if you study and know the material you will do fine.  He is very good about helping students succeed and truly cares.

Best professor at findlay in the esoh dept., if every professor was like him the program would be amazing. This guys knowledge about environmental law is unbelievable and will help you with whatever your question is he expects you to put time in before class but you will get a lot out of his classes
I had a great experience with this class and Professor Wilkinson.  I was challenged by the course and found him to be tough but fair

I've taken several Degree Completion/Online courses at Findlay & Mr. Wilkinson has nailed the format! Lectures are recorded, but specific to online class; homework's clearly defined; due dates are in-line with the online schedule. He provides OUTSTANDING feedback & emails are concise & constructive. No other online Prof. compares yet!

He is not only a great professor but a very nice person. He cares about his class and also the well being of his students. Go prepared to the class to get the most of his teachings. Every minute of his class is time well spent learning and is also fun.  He gives timely feedback to all the tests. I wish he taught more of graduate level classes.

The best professor I have had so far. Each lecture is unique and well constructed, not just someone repeating power point slides as usual. He cares more about you actually learning the material more than anything else. You truly get what you pay for with him.
great prof.
Professor Wilkinson is by far the best at The University of Findlay. Very intelligent! He makes you work hard but it's all worth it.
The best teacher I've ever had. Very fair, engaging, and witty! Pretty hot for a short guy!

Took course for science elective. Terrific experience. Great at explaining ecosystem functioning,sustainability and adverse impacts. Final part of course on carbon-based, nuclear, and renewable energy was insightful. Much to take away from this course.  Demands critical thinking but he rewards you. Higher education at its best. Findlay’s best.

Prof knows environmental laws and regs and knows how to teach it. Wicked sense of humor and delivery. Knows us personally and engages us. Teaches by first demanding that we read text. Then he interprets text via lectures and interaction. Tough tests but fair.  Homework returned quickly; feedback given.  Does EVERYTHING himself.  No TAs.

Wilkinson is the real deal.  Course material is current and applicable to work place.  Course covers reporting and permitting requirements (EPCRA, CAA, CWA, CERCLA).  Uses current forms and instructions.  Teaches us how to determine applicability of regulatory program to a facility.  He successfully educates us.

Prof. Wilkinson is possibly THE best teacher I've had at The Univ. of Findlay.  He cares, he's passionate, he's funny, and he explains the material in a way that is accessible to everyone.  I highly recommend this class to everyone.  I'm not a science person, but I LOVED this class and I loved having that man as a teacher.

This is my third class with Wilkinson and unfortunately my last.  He teaches you to APPLY environmental regulations.  The guy walks into class without a book or a power point and stands in front of the class, teaches and dialogues with us, and fulfills the written course objectives without fail every semester.  It's a gift to study under him!

Course covers the principles of environmental science coupled with governmental policy.  It is a fascinating class.  Course is taught by a great professor.  Other students and professors recommended that I take Wilkinson's section.  He didn't disappoint.  You wanted to come to class.  Could be the best instructor that I have ever encountered.

Course is a prerequisite for ESOH majors.  Professor makes it the cornerstone of the curriculum.  Excellent lectures prepare the future professional. Wilkinson challenges and prepares you intellectually. This guy wants you to succeed.  He reminds us that professional success demands effort.

Prof. Wilkinson is a dedicated teacher that is willing to go above and beyond to help out his students.  His class was well organized and beneficial.  You do not memorize the material but learn it.  This was the best class I have taken while at Findlay.

He is not an engaging speaker and lectures are incredibly dry. Great professor. Readings were insightful and informative. He expertly covers a plethora of interesting topics, including workplace cultures and discrimination. Class itself was not that difficult just incredibly boring and required you to do an obnoxious amount of reading which was NEVER talked about in class so you had to infer meanings on the tests. God, he is the absolute worst. He literally just chats, like no content comes out of his mouth, he just says words. I personally think his class is the biggest waste of time, but attendance is mandatory!!!

For a 1.5 credit class, the amount of readings and work given seemed unnecessary. Professor Ivory used an index card system that made lecture attendance mandatory. unnecessarily strict with his attendance/deadline policies and is unsympathetic to needing flexibility. he basically reads off of his slides, so going to lecture feels pointless, and rather than discussing the incredibly dense readings, he just puts "discussion questions" up on the board and reads them to the class. he doesn't even answer them.
Seems like a nice guy, but I couldn't hear a single thing. Talks into his neck. Tests were dumb. Like high school. Did not enjoy. Some readings were interesting though. Lectures were just not good.

Class is based on readings which are never discussed meaningfully in class, useless lectures, attendance is mandatory with mini flashcard assignments about readings, he doesn't seem like he wants to be there, must study hard, some TAs make class much easier than others, overall would not recommend class unless you have to take it as an ILRie
Very boring and useless lectures. He just reads off from the slides every day. And attendance is mandatory. Extremely heavy readings with few explanations in class lectures. Would not take it again.

By far the most disorganized class at Cornell. The only good part about it was the tour of the particle accelerator that Prof. Hoffstaetter organized. Everything else was unsalvageable. organization was a complete mess, rarely taught in a helpful way, was often dismissive of questions / responses from certain students, ignored TA requests to use canvas submission instead of email submission which slowed down work return

Outstanding professor who clearly knows what hes talking about. Such an incredible command of the material, both in and outside the scope of his class. Really nice guy as well who really cares about his students and cares about them learning. 11/10 would take again.

Accelerator physics is a fascinating class. Professor Hoffstaetter is really passionate about the subject and happy to help if approached after class/ via email.
Would be a decent teacher if he was less full of himself
Great teacher. Explains things clearly and neatly. He does quantum mechanics in a highly intuitive way and we learn a lot through analogies and comparisons with classical physics.
Clear and deep. I liked his 316 class, it was hard, it made me think a lot and Prof. H. was there to help.

Worst. Class. Lectures with Power Point.  Although the print outs are convenient, they do nothing to improve his teaching ability.  One of the most frustrating courses I've ever taken
A nice guy... but he shouldn't be teaching
He's a pretty terrible teacher, although he gives out lecture notes (photocopies of lecture slides).  Problem sets are easy as long as you're comfortable with doing bullshit math.

The book is good, but is not at the level he teaches. His lectures are confusing, and he doesn't explain things well. Problem sets are even more confusing, but it takes a while just to figure them out. Prelims don't cover the material he teaches.
Benissimo

This was easily my favorite class at Cornell. Dr. Zacher is super sweet and will always help you, as long as you're proactive about asking for it. Super fun person to be around too, she's funny and even brings her dog into class sometimes! Highly recommend.

Professor Zacher is absolutely wonderful! She brings enthusiasm to the class and makes the material engaging. She makes sure that we won't feel stressed but also stay motivated enough to keep on track. I took the course for requirements but ended up really enjoying Old English. This is one of the best classes I've taken at Cornell!

It is true that she ignores student emails, but also true that she is a good teacher when you are lucky enough to see her in class. It's a privilege to even see her and students should appreciate the privilege. Zacher is amazing, and just to see her in class is a delight. Don't expect more than you need

ENGL3280 Prof. Zacher makes high-level material accessible. You can be in any class year and take one of her 3000-level classes and succeed if you put in the work. Her class involves long readings and in-depth lectures, but doing the readings is enough to score high. She has a warm spirit that always brightens the day and makes even old texts fresh

She was so nice! I was dreading taking this FWS because it was a requirement but she was a pleasure. The work was not bad at all and she is very understanding. I would definitely recommend participating in class.

Zacher is an incredible professor and such a kind and caring person. Her classes are always interesting and informative. She is a fair grader but pushes you to be the best writer that you can be. Do not miss out on taking a class with her at Cornell.
Samantha is incredibly nice & fabulous! She's so energetic & passionate & enthusiastic, making obscure topics really interesting. Will definitely take her class again!

This class one so well thought out. There was a flow between topics that really made sense and the texts we read were fun! (Especially the section on John Mandeville). Would highly recommend taking a course from Professor Zacher!

As my first four-thousand level English course, especially one on the roots of anti-Semitism, I was nervous as to what this class would be like. Professor Zacher was amazing. Not only did she her happy energy lighten some of the heavy readings, every lecture was engaging. This class (and its professor) are wonderful. Would recommend highly!

Professor Zacher is incredibly knowledgeable, funny, and gets you thinking far beyond the classroom in "The Imaginary Jew." The course is a brilliant interweaving of films, manuscripts, books, and poems. There is lot of writing (which was a good thing) but the class was not only English majors. Fascinating and very well taught- TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Samantha Zacher is an incredibly warm, funny, engaging individual. Her enthusiasm and her teaching abilities make class easy and really enjoyable. She is also invested in her students and their work. She takes the time to read and comment closely on your papers, improving your knowledge and your writing abilities at the same time.

I love Professor Zacher!  She made an obscure topic (Icelandic lit) fascinating by her enthusiasm and obvious expertise.  She wants her students to do well and learn and is willing to spend time helping them do so.  Her class was not easy, but it was not stressful either.  If for no other reason, take her class to learn how to be chic!

Professor Z is an energetic and well-prepared teacher.  She works hard to get the best out of her students and is always fair when assessing them.  Don't miss out an opportunity to take a class with her!
No Comments

Professor Zacher is thoughtful, funny, fascinating to listen to, and extremely competent in her field. She is approachable and generous with her time, bends over backwards to help students understand difficult concepts, and teaches energetically, creatively and with heart. Horrible, pretentious, affected woman.  Boring class, dead discussions, nit-picky grader.

Literally just do the assignments and study the slides (which he provides) for tests and you'll get an A. He is such a gem of a teacher, I took 3 of his classes while at Cornell and loved them all. Great content, perhaps not the most dynamic presenter but he has a heart of gold (brought cookies that his wife baked for us at the final).
Really good professor. It gives long but interesting lectures.
Laid back, flexible and understanding with students' schedules. Lectures are inspiring and refreshing... Offers great (landscape) history classes.

Took a FWS class with her: Diverse Voices of the American Identity. great teacher - helpful and really wants to change the way you think about the world. Not too hard, not too easy, I recommend her to anyone

Prof Kennedy was an excellent teacher.  Class discussions were interesting and involved. I feel like prof. Kennedy really made me smarter and prepared me to move forward in the english department. he is very likable person

Great in office hours and comments on papers drafts are very helpful. Nice guy too. Although Kennedy is incredibly knowledgeable, I found his lectures a little boring (probably because I wasn't too interested in Shakespeare). Not much work: 3 papers of about 6 pages.

I get shakespeare is "dramatic", but the way he reads aloud in class definitely scares me sometimes. but then, he is suppose to be world famous and president of American renaissance society and stuff, so i guess he's ok. meh

Kennedy is the prototypical arrogant ivy league prof. I intended on being a comparative literature major but I found his class boring and tough to sit through. Discussions were dull and Kennedy is not a very animated lecturer. You can get away with doing very little work though.

If there is a better professor at Cornell, I don't know him or her!  Each time I walked into Renaissance Lit, I was floored by an interesting, engaging lecture.  Prof. K was helpful on papers, easy to talk to, and one of the most entertaining lecturers around!
Thoroughly knowledgeable in Renaissance literature and his passion for the subject makes the classes even more enjoyable.  His class was my favorite one of the semester.
Excellent!  The down with bush remarks are fantastic. More teachers should be politically vocal, especially about such a **** of a president.

Prof. Kennedy is brilliant and very excited about his subject.  He's an interesting speaker and still maintains a casual atmosphere in the class.

A decent professor, definitely knows CAD, sometimes went a bit fast with the demos. Computer lab format helps. The assignments were OK but a bit long for 1 credit, especially the 2 larger projects, and he usually took the whole 75 minutes leaving no in-class time for homework.
he is the nicest guy...totally knows what he's talking about and is willing to help if you ask. the class is hard and takes effort but if you try and ask for help u'll be ok
hard to follow, but is always willing to help
