Favourite Professor of all time. Super understanding and caring of students. Exams are all very fair pretty similar to practice and homework.

Prof. Scheinberg gave amazing lectures and made sure she delivered the best explanations possible so the class can understand. Great person to talk to and learn from during office hours as well. You won't have trouble understanding the material if you attend every lecture.

As much as I want to love this Professor, I have a hard time convincing myself. You can tell that she is nice and is trying to deliver the material, but the lectures are confusing and quite boring. Took in spring 2020. Despite pandemic mayhem, she handled the situation as best as anyone could have been expected to. Pretty easygoing class. Just read the book, attend lectures if you want, and make sure to do the homework. Prof Scheinberg deeply cares about the students and their learning.

Very nice professor that wants her students to succeed. Not a great lecturer, but the slides she releases are very helpful, those along with the textbooks will prepare you well for the exams. Not too hard a class (easier than 1920, for example), and really interesting content, in my opinion. Recommend taking!

Confusing lecturer; I stopped going to lecture since the textbook for this class is pretty good so I relied on that instead. Pretty standard course: weekly homework set, weekly quiz. She's an extremely mediocre (boring) lecturer, but I stopped going to lecture after a few times anyway because everything is in the textbook. Gilly is extremely unaccommodating. She never adopts students' feedback. TA's grading criteria is also very confusing. They always deduct points on assignments somehow. mean

I am amazed how Gilly made this huge class personal!

This class is so project-heavy but in the end you don't learn anything. The assignment instructions are never not vague and the grading is never consistent. Blurry grading rubrics and inconsistent grading standard across different TAs. The lecture is like a readout from textbook. This class should be inspiring since its about HCI and design; but its the opposite. You need to play by her rules and no room to be creative.

Listen. It's whatever you personally want to get out of it. She is basically a kindergarten teacher who encourages young adults to remember the imagination that many have left behind. Lectures are boring, but since there is an attendance grade, just show up and do other work on your laptop. She's fairly nice, but not the best lecturer, if only because the material is boring and straightforward. Work on the assignments and group project and you'll be fine.

INFO 3450 is a great and rewarding class but warning, it is time consuming. You will have to put in lots of effort, but in the end you should have a project  you can talk about in job interviews.   Gilly is a great, respectable prof. You can tell she puts in a lot of time and attention to her lectures which are always easy to read later on.
The professor tried to control students a lot. No phone and no laptop during the speech (are we elementary students?) The grading criteria is also confusing and doesn't reflect our efforts.

Lectures were uninformative, straight from the textbook, and nobody paid attention. Group activities took up half of lecture and were not helpful at all. Grading "rubrics" were ambiguous at best. The worst class and professor I have ever had here at Cornell in my three years.  No grading rubrics makes the class extremely confusing.  Takes points off on assignments for items not even mentioned in instructions.  TA's don't even know what is going on in the class or assignments.  This class was terrible. DO NOT TAKE IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO!
This class was horrible.
Lectures were deadly and the course was not structured coherently

Professor Leshed does a good job with the Online Communities Course.  Be forewarned it is fairly repetitive of other Info/Comm classes. Professor Leshed does a really good job to make lectures interesting and mixes it up every class. She's not bad looking either.

Easy Class, not to much work, expect 2/3 essays tops, and maybe a 300 word assignment every week/other week. You can resubmit assignments to replace your grade.
Prof is super sweet and caring. She's passionate about our lives and wellbeing. Super chill with extentions. Classes are rich, and interesting.

She's unorganized and does not keep on top of her work/our assignments. Very nice professor and very enthusiastic about the material. She can be a little bit disorganized when assigning homework through email. Very nice. Grades papers a little bit harder than what you might expect from her attitude in class. Can be disorganized sometimes.
Professor does not answer questions to the students that actually need help. Does not leave room for students individual creativity.
Awesome teacher

Bryan was my first art teacher here at UAFS and I absolutely loved having him as a teacher. He keeps the class light-hearted and is very quick to reply to emails. Honestly a great teacher. Always gave me constructive feedback and seemed like he really cared wether I understood what he was saying. He's really funny and laid back. He try's to make his classes fun yet educational.

Bryan is very laid back. I always feel free to joke around and have fun in class. He can be intimidating but if you get past that and ask for help or feedback you will do great. Intimidating to ask for help on projects unless you are a select few from the class that he favors (makes you feel dumb). However, he is funny most days and generally in a good mood. Very easy grader.
Teacher does not seem interested in helping students except for a chosen few.

I have never had a more positive experience. He is a wonderful teacher. Truly passionate about design.
blah! Refuses to compromise or listen!

This was by far my favorite course that I took. DA was very detailed and put in a lot of effort to outline exactly what was required for each writing project. This class is structured extremely poorly and many of her attempts to be helpful cause more confusion. She bombards you with so much material and then quizzes you on niche sections of the material which takes hours to find. Professor Alexis is the worst professor I've had in my college career. She gives undergraduate students graduate level work. If you can choose any other professor, do it. Cydney Alexis is a horrible teacher. I am in her Television Literature class right now at Kansas State and her expectations are extremely high for what the class is worth. If you plan on taking this class, do yourself a favor a do NOT take it with her.

Dr. Alexis has brilliant mind (and she even likes Grimes!). Her course in Evaluating Writing was a singular experience; I had never been challenged like that before. She's a badass with merit. Don't waste your time trying cut corners, she'll see through it. Use the opportunity to let her open up your mind and think clearly for the first time.

She's a great teacher, who really has a way around a classroom. She may seem a little difficult extensive at first, but she doesn't ask the impossible. She wants to get the best out of you, and she makes her assignments as enjoyable as she can. If you do the work and go to class, it's an easy A with a cool teacher.

Awesome class. Our course text was Breaking Bad! Although the workload was intense at times, the class was fun and interesting. Everyone participated and I learned more about writing in one class than in all of high school!!

very kind professor and also very helpful. she does assign a lot of work but as long as you try and revise you'll do well in her class. textbook is used frequently, so make sure you get it. she values creativity a lot so don't be afraid to try new things with your work.

I loved this class! Never a full moment. We learned about writing, but also Dr. Alexis taught us how to read popular culture in a new way. She takes her time on grading sometimes, but gives more feedback than I've ever received.

This class was a challenge, but a great one. Any student who wants to succeed with Dr. Alexis can; you have to work hard, though! She gave me more feedback on my writing than I've ever received. I loved this class!

This is a tough class and the professor treated us like we were graduate students when in reality it is a senior seminar class for writing arts majors. A lot of work was done for this class and it was hard.

The knowledge points in Harmony 3 don't need 2 hours per week to understand. The vibe of the class is always chill. He is a cut above the rest among the harmony teachers.
Class is very relaxed. He's fun and engaging, and very enthusiastic. He's an excellent professor.

David is so unbelievably nice and fun. He is a super chill professor, and if you are looking for a good time and an easy A, this is place for you. So I've taken David in all my harmony classes from 1 to 4 and this guys is just amazing. Take him if you want to learn while having fun and being relaxed.

David is a fantastic professor. He is one of the few teachers at Berklee that actually understand that we we came to music school to do MUSIC. Super wonderful professor. Very sweet and cares about your learning if you put in the effort. He is often late which is nice if you are late to class, but we tend to fall behind because he runs late and our class time gets cut short. Very understanding, doesn't respond to emails often though.

Super chill guy, doesn't use books at all. Kinda goes with the flow and spends more time on things the class doesn't understand. David is by far one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. He's there for his students always and creates a wonderful and fun learning environment at all times. Professor Alexis is a phenomenal person and teacher all around. He is an absolute gem who not only will go over something until you understand it but he connects everything to the real world rather than it just being a class. He is an amazing teacher and if you ever have the opportunity to take his class, take it. You will not regret it.

David's probably not a 1-star professor, but his 4.1 score on here is dangerously incorrect. David attracts students who are like him, interested in fun and uninterested in working hard. That's why his score is so high. Which kind are you?

Nice guy but didn't learn anything... Enjoy harmony &/or plan on moving on to advanced harmony classes?... DO NOT TAKE HIM. Just want an easy A and don't care about learning?... Sure, he's great. David is hilarious and so so brilliant. He knows every inch of the African Diaspora, and he reminds you of the power of music.

David's incredible. His class can sometimes be fast-paced, but he always makes sure everybody understands the material. Incredibly funny and kind, I've never seen somebody more enthusiastic about music & harmony! <3

David is the most amazing teacher I have had at Berklee. He is kind, smart, hilarious, and genuinely cares about all of his students. He wants you to succeed and will help you get there if you meet him half way. He is a teacher, and a friend. AND HE CAN SANGGGG. Thank you for such an amazing semester David.
David is amazing! He is a great musician and educator, who would never let you feel bored during classes. Take him if you can!

As someone who struggles with music theory, I was scared to go into this course. However, after the first week of this class, I felt that I learned a ton while not feeling overwhelmed. I feel like I am part of the class and that the success of his students truly matters to David. This is my favorite class so far and it is because of this professor!
David is really passionate about what he teaches, and makes theory, a subject I find really boring, really fun to learn. His teaching style is very interactive and animated.

David is fun, hilarious, passionate about harmony, and SUPER TALENTED. He plays really catchy R&B songs for examples! However, I feel like he isn't the best teacher and never uses the text. That being said, if you speak up and tell him you don't understand a concept he will go over it until you understand it!

David is hilarious and awesome, however he's not the best teacher. I had him for MAT, and luckily I already knew most of the material beforehand. He's super sweet and fun, but prepare to have to study and teach yourself material outside of class.

My fave teacher at Berklee. His teaching style is extremely engaging and entertaining. He is hilarious and caring and definitely fosters a sweet relationship with his students. You can hit him up for whatever help you need even if its a different class or even if it's something personal (like songwriting help). He is so precious. TAKE HIM!!!!!!!!!!

David is a harmony genius and hilarious to boot. His style is as quick and witty as Robin Williams', so PAY ATTENTION and you'll soar. She is a great professor. I would recommend if you are really trying to understand chemistry and your major requires understanding of it. She really cares about her students and is willing to help. She is a tough professor, but she will help you learn.

Mary Bojan is actually quite a fabulous professor. Very fair grading/learning system and quite organized as well. AS LONG AS YOU READ AND LEARN BEFORE THE LECTURE YOU WILL PROBABLY GET AN A. Don't even fall behind one class on the reading cause you will get run over by how quick Mary Bojan moves. If you learn how to do the material, you'll get an A

Everyone says that Bojan is a bad teacher but they're all the same. She's very enthusiastic but the real way you learn stuff is by reading the book before class which isnt too bad. Theres a decent amount of homework but you can just copy every question and its all online. Same with the quizzes. The tests are kind of hard but if you do the practice

Everyone says Dr. Bojan is impossible but honestly it wasn't that bad. You can tell she loves what she does and she isn't that professor that tries to fail everyone. Clicker questions do count as a grade so you really shouldn't skip and you might end up confused if you do. I enjoyed Dr. Bojan's class despite the effort needed to be put into it.

This was a unique class. She doesn't lecture and instead you do worksheets in class. Sounds strange right. In reality, you are getting your hands on hundreds of practice problems, a luxury most classes don't have. I would recommend this professor if you are willing to do the work, you will get a good grade if you grind.
good luck lol

Dr. Bojan has a reputation that she is a tough professor, but she just really cares about the material. She wants you to learn it and is disappointed if the class doesn't do well on a clicker question. I never read the textbook, I only ever watched youtube videos the day before class and I never felt behind. Highly recommend her. Just watch videos.

Like others have said, reading and comprehending the prelecture notes is a MUST. If you don't, you will never know what is going on in class because all you do in class is work on examples. I honestly didn't mind this however as it was a nice change from the usual lecture.

There really are no lectures. Instead, you are expected to read the pre-lecture notes (which are really just notes that any normal professor would give during lecture) and textbook before class. Then, when you arrive at class, she will do a few demos and then you spend the rest of class doing activities related to the material you read before class

First of all, I want to say she's a pretty nice person and always willing to help, but she does not teach. There is a lot of reading required if you want to learn anything and do well on the exams and you have to do quizzes before every class. In class, she does not lecture and only gives you worksheets. Exams are very hard

She has an interesting way of teaching that does not work for a lot of students. You have quizzes before every lecture and you are required to do a lot of work outside of class. Very difficult information to learn and her way of teaching does not help.

She is the worst proffesor ever, lecture are unclear. There is not even a lecture, she gives you problems and expects you to know it all from just reading the textbook. The tesr are nothing like the practice exams or homeworks at all. I passed all the practice exams but still manage to fail the actual exams. Honestly, just awful.

Most of the reviews on here are completely wrong, probably one of the best out of all chem110 professors. Bojan's class is straightforward and tells you exactly how to get an A. Doing the weekly homework is necessary and tedious but as long as you do that, getting a good grade does not require much effort at all

Her teaching style is different but is still effective. The people that complain that she doesn't teach are the ones who probably would still do badly if she just spat information at us. HW is annoying but helps you prepare for the tests.

Absolutely the worst professor to have your first semester freshman year. She doesn't actually lecture but rather makes you learn by using activity workbooks and reading the eBook. She's not understanding and she's certainly not helpful and just an all around terrible professor. Would've preferred a lecturer who actually lectures.

Going into this class, I had heard a lot of negative things about Bojan. However, to my surprise, I ended up really liking how they taught the class and I found her to be very helpful if you took the opportunity to ask questions and act interested. She loves what she does and she wants her students to succeed. Just make sure you study for the exams

Dr. Bojan has a different teaching method that works for some students, and not for others. She gives out lecture notes ahead of time, and has you practice what you learned during lecture where you have a chance to ask questions. I loved it and very much recommend her. Clicker questions every day so you MUST go to class!!!

Worst professor of my college career. Was never able to fully prepare the class for the tests. I attended nearly every lecture and left each time more confused than the last. Bojan runs this class as if you do not have any other class going on simultaneously and expects way too much from a 100 level course. If you can avoid her and this class do it

Mary Bojan seems to be really tough for some, but i thought her class helped me ALOT. She does class activities during lecture so you have to put what you learned in the notes to use which helps prepare for exams. If you learn better by listening to lectures rather than applying work though, i wouldn't recommend her.

I love Dr. Bojan! You do need to be prepared to put in a lot of effort but she is very clear when lecturing. She pairs activities with lecture so you better understand material. Super sweet and amiable lady. Her love of chemistry is infectious!

I can see why a lot of people don't like Dr. Bojan. She makes you read pre lecture notes before class, essentially learning the material before class and printing upwards of 100 papers for her class (yikes).However, she's very passionate about chemistry. If you take her class, pray to whatever deity you believe in that you get an engaging TA.

I hadn't taken chemistry for two years prior to taking Chem 110. She will tell you to drop if she thinks you can't handle it. She went over the lectures with a lot of content in a short amount of time and having the right TA's are what you need to rely on. She will not really help you with any questions you have. If you can, take a different prof.

Regardless of what a lot of people say, Bojan is a lovely old lady, willing to help you out, answers all of your questions. She gets so excited about Chem that sometimes she'll go off topic, but she makes this really tough course VERY understandable. If you miss class you'll have a hard time, and bc she is 8am lecture, it makes it harder to attend.

As someone who sadly had to take chem 110 twice because I had a terrible professor first semester I would highly recommend her! She really cares about her students if she sees that you put in the effort! And at the end of the course the final was curved which was amazing for my grade! Also look into chem 108 with this class.

I had taken AP Chem in high school and excelled! Just missed passing my AP test so I figured basic chemistry would be easy. I can say that was one of the hardest classes ever and Dr Bojan doe a horrible job explaining basic concepts. If you do take this course be sure to look into Chem 108 and expect to go to class a lot for the participation point

Bojan is tough. She goes off topic in lecture and is most likely crazy. My advice is to take chem 108 along with 110. Its a 1 credit class that'll help you a lot with the material. It extra work but it makes Bojan's lectures a lot clearer. Chem 108 definitely made a huge difference in my grade for 110. Take it

Unfortunately this is a class where no matter what professor you have, you will need to work extremely hard to get a good grade, even if you have a lot of experience with chemistry. Bojan really does not do anything for you. If you have questions she will usually refer you to your TA. If you want to do well, go to class AND learn on your own.

Bojan is tough, but it's possible to get a good grade if you put the work in. When you do it make sure  you learn HOW to do each problem not just get it done.

It doesn't matter if you took chem in high school. Trust me, your understanding is going to mean nothing. Having this professor will be the worst decision you can make. Only way to get thru this class is countless number of hours of hard work. Reviews and a good TA get you through. She wrote the ebook, so just know, stay away.

Tests are tough. Lectures are hard to follow, goes through mass amounts of material in short time. Do and understand all homework before test, got to reviews and find a good TA. I took AP Chem in high school with a final grade of an A and I found this class challenging.

No. No no no. Do not take a class with Mary Bojan. She was the worst professor I have ever taken in my life, bar none. I had chem with her in freshman year (now a junior) and I made a RMP account JUST NOW to warn others. Her lectures were 90% telling us how we'd need to study or we wouldn't pass, and 10% rushed-through material. Take another prof!

She's absolutely awful. The class average was less than a 60% all semester long and she just blamed us. This professor is only here for research. This was the worst experience I had in all my 4 years of undergrad, DO NOT TAKE.

Bojan is underrated, people give her hard time but I find her a good teacher, she does what she is supposed to do during the lecture and she explains examples during the lecture which helps to understand. When you take chem 112 you need to work hard, study constanly, do  homework questions and practice exams to get an A in the class.

If you can, take another professor. She messes up frequently, and barely clarifies when she does. She also is not very good with technology. She is a good person and you can tell she loves chemistry, but that isn't enough to make it a good class.
I only went to lectures for the first two weeks, and I decided to study myself with e-book. I probably should not rate her because I do not go to lecture, you know.

Take Chem 112 with another professor if possible. Dr. Bojan is in charge of designing the course material, but I felt she did not have a good ability to explain the material within the course.   When "explaining" topics, she mostly repeats the answer expecting students to experience an "ah-ha" moment, instead of explaining topics in new ways.

Bojan is a disaster. Before each test, she holds a review session where students can ask questions, and she never knows the answers! I remember the day before a test, she was doing a math problem in class and couldn't figure it out so she said it didn't matter bc we were testing and she'd email the answer. Boring and annoying lectures

Contrary to many of my classmates, I liked Bojan. She is teaching a weed out class, so I think many don't like her because the course is difficult. Sometimes lectures weren't 100% clear, but she had a lot to cover in a short amount of time. She will make herself available to help you and is quick to answer e mails. She's not as bad as everyone says

Dr. Bojan pushes the idea of independent learning, "Read the book and do your homework a week before lecture!" However, she spends more time talking to us about our learning habits than teaching Chemistry. She skims over topics in lecture, under the assumption that we already learned it ourselves. She does help if you ask, but I didn't learn much.

First of all, Mary is "all over the place". Her lectures are useless of going to because of her unorganized slides. Throughout her lectures she writes notes in the slide which everybody can't read or understand it. Although she is a terrible teacher, the TA's are great help. In fact, I most of the TA's get confused in her lectures.

The lectures consist of her either blowing up balloons, doing a problem wrong, or telling us that we should "already know the material". She moves quickly through her slides and her exam review sessions are a complete waste of time.

Dr. Bojan really wants you to understand chemistry but she doesn't understand it. She makes a lot of mistakes in class. My TA would email us if we should go to lecture or if she would just confuse you more than you already were. Attendance was optional but if you didn't go you'd be ok if you talked to a TA.

Dr. Bojan means well. However, that means nothing to me. She would not teach a lot of material because "we should know it". Most of us did not know it. After scheduling an appointment with her she told me that she didnt think it was possible for me to do well on the upcoming exams bc i did poorly on the first. But hey, she means well.
She is terrible!!!!!! Worst teacher at Penn State

For startes she is not going to motivate you. The day before exam 3 she came in and said if you want to drop the class after you take the exam tonight you have to wait untill we the get the scores, Like what the Frack? We have an exam instead of motivating you she is prophesizing your demise. She is a good professor she is not bad,

Bojan gets a bad wrap for being goofy during lectures, but people going into the class expecting her to spoon-feed them information so they can regurgitate it on the exams will be VERY disappointed. You need to read the textbook, do the homework, and study hard for the exams.

It is currently my second week of class and I've never been more frustrated in my entire life. Bojan writes on her prehistoric projector and talks to herself for the entire 50 minute lecture. There's no doubt in my mind that I'll fail this class because of her so called "teaching." Knock knock. Who is it? Retirement here, knocking on Bojan's door.
Confusing and makes it hard to pass the course

Bojan is an acquired taste. You either love her or you hate her. Her eccentric personality, in my opinion can be very grating at times. This does not mean she's not a good professor. Bojan has taught me the most of almost all of the professors I've had at Penn State. She takes teaching very seriously, but if you don't try, she can't help you.

She just left everyone to do ALEKS assignments without helping us. She just came to the first day of class and sent us bunch of emails basically saying 'ALEKS will do all the teaching so she won't be coming to class'. Let's not even start talking about the stupidity of her online assignments.

Bojan means well... but doesn't teach well. She will not simplify any information, so prepare to do some work. Do the homework every week, do the practice exams, learn from your mistakes, and you'll do fine. Although she's not a great professor, still attend class. She will supply you (occasionally) with the formulas and charts you need to succeed.

Spends entire class time doing practice problems and does not focus on teaching problem solving skills or the underlying concepts behind the problem. Makes learning extremely difficult and going to lecture a waste of time. You are better off teaching yourself from the textbook and going to lion tutors. Take any other 112 professor.

Absolutely terrible, didnt go to class for half the semester. I took her at 8am and it was a waste of my time. All she talked about was how we will fail. She shows no competence in teaching chemistry.Go lion tutors, do the homework, or get someone else. I'M SERIOUS IF YOU TAKE HER YOU WILL TEACH YOURSELF.

An awful instructor. She spent more time telling us we were all going to fail instead of actually teaching us. She is extremely disorganized and her methods of attacking problems are long and exhausting that set you up you fail. I am lucky I had a great TA too, as thats what saved me. Also, I ended up going to another profs class to get an A.

Her voice is so annoying. She spends about 50% of the lecture actually lecturing, 30% telling you you're going to fail, and 20% blowing up balloons. Also, most of the time she does a problem in lecture she does it wrong, according to my TA. I didn't really pay attention. Just do a bunch of old exams when you study. I got excellent grades that way.
Awful instructor , wastes a lot of the lecture time on useless things , plus being unclear at all.

Squeaky, annoying voice. Not very helpful, doesn't clarify, expects you to know everything before class, plus read the textbook nightly. Probably one of the better teachers in the chemistry department, but didn't make things very clear for me. Unfortunately barley passed the class.
Not the best professor one can ask for, but she might be the best of the worst in the Chemistry department. De motivates students a lot during lectures.

This course is just difficult... however, she makes things more difficult than they need to be and spends most of the class time lecturing the students on how to set up the problems using a format that is super time consuming. There is not enough time to use her methods on the exam

Dear Lord, find another prof immediately. DO NOT take Chem 110 with Bojan. "Teaches" the most difficult way to do difficult problems, and doesn't actually explain.

She is one of the reasons I got a 14 on the physical sciences section of the MCAT.  All you have to do is LISTEN TO WHAT SHE SAYS! Go to class, take notes, do all homework problems, start studying a couple weeks before the exams, go to reviews, take practice exams.  Not only will you get an A, but you'll also retain the knowledge you gain.

Dr Bojan was by far the best chemistry teacher I've ever had in college.  She made it easy to pay attention in class and explained everything so well that I barely had to do work outside of class and got an A in both Chem 110 and 112.  The exams are hard, but there's a lot of help available.
Horrible! Assumes you know everything beforehand and treats you like an idiot if you don't understand something.   Worst class I've ever had to take.
She is good!
She assumes that you are very smart and that you studied every thing prior conning to class. She will fly through the course. And she is annoying in class. Threatening students with failing.

If you remember chem from high school you will do fine, at least a B.  Go to class, print the notes and pay attention and you can get an A.  Having three exams and a final gives you room to work if you have a bad exam.  Exam 1-moderate, Exam 2-easy, Exam 3-Extremely difficult, Final is not hard as long as you payed attention  in class

You will hate her BUT she is not a liar. She tells you straight up how to do well in Chem. It's a hard class. The other teachers suck compared to her (foreign or just not good teachers). Seriously, I would recommend her every time.
She doesn't emphasize algebraic manipulations or thinking in symbolic terms. Quite the contrast with the physics department. Try to take Benesi; a bit boring, but at least you can follow him.

She just rambles durning lectures and doesnt take the time to explain. she is extremely intrested in chemistry but doesnt do the best teaching it. if you enjoy chem you will be fine in her class but if you dont like chem or arent good at it like me, then you might struggle
She is very enthusiastic and cares about her students. Although the class was hard to begin with, she kept me awake for an 8am and was a great teacher.

Of all the professors to get for the awful class Chem 110, Dr. Bojan is one of the better ones. She explains the information pretty well and actually cares about the class's wellbeing gradewise. She is REALLY enthusiastic but I thought that was a good thing. It made the 8am lecture bearable.
Great lecturer, and explained the material very well!
dr. bojan is awesome. she is very clear and a  great overall professor. go to class, take notes, study and chem 110 with her will  be a great class.
Bojan is the best! ALEKS helps so much, and her chem class averages are the highest :)

She is very unclear and makes no sense. I haven't gone to class and don't plan on going ever again. Got an 89 on the last test without her notes. If you want a teacher that actually teaches, pick someone else.

She was OK, not the best, but not the worst.  She does get annoying in class, but if you do what she recommends, the class will be a lot easier, but hardly anyone wants to do the homework ahead of time like she suggests.
Bojan is often annoying, but she does want her students to pass. Chem 110 is difficult and time consuming.

Annoying as hell. Doesn't teach, just goes over examples and automatically expects you to know the material. Class was summer session 1 so it lasted only 1 month which is terrible because everything is so rapid and the professor does not seem to realize this and accommodate. If you have to take 112, STAY AWAY FROM BOJAN
Don't even think about having this professor. She encourages you not to ask questions and to instead "FIGURE IT OUT!"  That is one of her favorite quotes. If you cannot avoid her, change your major.

Honestly, she's not the greatest professor, but believe me when I say the others are unbearable. I didn't enjoy the classes ever, but you'll manage to get through with her. Chem 112 is just a tough course. Make the TA your best friend.
She reads the text to you essentially, summarizing what the book says.
Not sure why so many people dislike her.  She was a great professor, knew what she was talking about, and encouraged her students to get the work done.  Not too hard if you do the homework each week.

Try to get a different prof if you can.  Bojan seems like a nice enough lady but her lectures are pretty painful.  She tries to keep things exciting by blowing up stuff but i found myself falling asleep on a number of occasions. The tests are not terrible, and the homework and quiz grades are fairly easy to get.Her voice is enough to make you crazy

I have never hated a professor with such passion. I feel she cares about her students, but treats us like first graders and actually condescends anyone who dares ask a question. She constantly makes mistakes during lecture. She then also yells at students, saying "this is easy guuuuuyyyyys just figure it out!!!" AWFUL PROF.

Honestly, she's the best chem 110 teacher penn state has to offer.  While shes not the best teacher in the world shes the only one that actually explains anything and shes entertaining so you can pay attention.  Go to class as much as you can, but if you miss a few youll be fine.

Honestly, she's a really easy teacher. She explains things relatively well to the point where an previous knowledge of chemistry will get you by with minimal book reading. I do crew which means that I'm usually working on four hours of sleep a night, so if I can tolerate her voice in the morning, anyone should be able to... deal with it...

Fantastic teacher if you're not retarded and can keep up by reading the book a couple times a week. She actually cares about her students and keeps you updated on everything going on for her class. Yes, her voice is very annoying, but she's also funny because she's so cynical about students (but not mean-spirited). Glad I got her for Chem110.

terrible teacher. lectures were completely useless. had to teach myself basically everything. learned more from my TA than from Bojan. her voice makes you want to throw pens at her. if you have an option, take an 8AM class instead of taking Bojan

Yeah this class was quite easy, as long as you read and DO the homework with reasonable time (and i don't mean the night before). Bojan was a good teacher and she did everything she was supposed to, dont blame her if you fail cause you were too busy at a frat the night before a test. Your book is GOD.
No Comments

Worst mistake of my life to take Chem with Bojan. Lectures are a waste of time, have not learned a SINGLE THING from her. Does not care about students, awful prof
shes great
annoying to listen to
didnt like her at all

Bojan is certainly a very nice lady and she tries to get her students to understand. However, that's not the same as being a good teacher. She does a poor job of getting the information across. no. no. no

She is a very nice lady who does everything to help you pass if you have failed before. But otherwise, she is pretty bad and doesn't clearly teach the material. She is a brilliant person but horrible professor. You will need a study group to learn the material well. TA's ROCK!

I was a bit hesitant to take Prof. Bojan for 112, having taken 110 with her, and done not so good, but I was pleasantly surprised with her ability to really convey the material this time around. I was a bit hesitant to take Prof. Bojan for 112, having taken 110 with her, and not done so well, but I was pleasantly surprise with her ability to really convey the material this time around. Dr. Bojan is a great helpful professor. The grading in the class is department wide. She is interested in knowing her students and she tries her best to get the information across. Mary, helpful and a caring professor. Wonderful

Ouch. What a mean lady...If you want to do well in this class, you actually have to torture yourself and do all the homeworks. Ask for help all the time. I went to most of the review sessions and SI sessions but damn, I think I'm getting a D :(.

She is a hit or miss. Some love her, others hated her. I found her very annoying to listen to because she treats you like you're in first grade.  Grading is a department-wide thing so you can't really put blame on her. You have to put the time in to do well in this class. If you don't like lecture, read the book thoroughly for an A.
Horrible teacher. Mean, impossible to please on quizzes and exams. Exams are IMPOSSIBLE.
Very Nice Lady..... Really Cared about her students.....

I think Dr. Bojan is  a GREAT teacher. She is nice and teaches well. Yeah her class is a little hard but as long as you work hard and you're not a slacker then you don't need to worry. I think she is the best professor ever! Her class is hard but if you study hard, you will do fine. Dr. Bojan subbed for my regular prof one day.  I can't really say whether she was good at lecturing or not.  I found her voice so loud that I actually had to put a finger in one of my ears. I hate chem to begin with, and this class didn't help much. This is basically how she teaches: "Ok we have this concept here. Here is one basic example. Possibly one of the worst Chem110 teachers you can have. I had other chem teachers sub in for her who made the class a lot easier to understand. Chem 110 is a HARD class.  You can't blame her for not being successful in it.  I did horrible in Chem in HS but did well in this class because I put a lot of work into it. I am an A student and I ended up with a D in the class. It says a lot about the instructor. She doesn't care about students, she makes the class to be dificult, she goes to fast through material and picks the hardest ways of explaining things. she is way too into chemistry. she wont shut up about organic chemistry.  she explains more of why things are important than to help you solve problems.  the tas arent that great either so pretty much you teach yourself.

Hope and pray that you understand the textbook or you get a great TA, because you're not learning anything from lectures.  I'm an honors student at Penn State, and I had one heck of a time dealing with this course and Bojan's lectures.

She is really passionate about what she does and really knows her stuff. She strives for her students to understand what they are learning.  There are no quizzes just lecture problems which are difficult at first but then you get the hang of what she wants and you will do just fine especially because the lecture problems that she gives help you out

One of the best profs I had freshmen year. She cares about all 1,000 of her students understanding the material. She does get a little scatter-brained in the middle of lecture, but that is expected. Graded lecture problems force you to know the material as she goes along, helps come exam time.

I don't get why so many people hate Dr. Bojan. I didn't think her class was that difficult and I thought she explained things really well in class by working out sample problems. Her voice will make your ears bleed. There are no quizzes during recitation, but she has pop graded lecture problems...only one question per lecture but you don't know when or how many there will be. She is very scattered and fairly hard to follow...

Her lectures were horrible, if I didn't fall asleep then I wanted to rip my ears off. It's bad when you have to keep catching the mistakes that your professor makes during a lecture... I absolutely loved Dr. Bojan. I think she is hilarious. This class is not an easy one, so definitely keep up to date on the homework and attend recitation, even though they arent mandatory. Dr. Bojan is a great teacher! It's just your responsibility to do the readings before class which helps a lot.  She does a lot of demos for Chem 112 which make the class interesting.

Despite the normal view of Bojan, I actually thought she was a great professor. She really loves chemistry and I believe her lectures are well put together. She is nice, caring, and very approachable. But the class is ridiculously hard

She is definitely my best professor! She actually cares about her students. She is always saying I know this is hard, so let me help you through it.  She also has a genuine interest in the subject. Her Halloween show is a must see!

She is an okay teacher.  It doesn't really matter which teacher you take, they all teach the same thing.  It seems that sometimes she doesn't quite know what she is doing or is not too prepared. Professor was super chill and understanding, and the class was fun and full of interesting material. I think we had great freedom/flexibility in essay topics. There wasn't a lot of work, but you need to put in some effort (it was nothing compared to my other FWS). Just show up prepared, and you'll get a good grade.

Professor Chun's online marketing course was easy. She explains everything concisely & before the prelim & final releases a study guide for you to fill out. If you fill out this study guide well, you are set. Tests are very easy if the study guide is completed in full. Other than that, participate in weekly discussions and you're set.

Loved this class. As someone with very little law/govt background, I found this class to be very easy to understand; prof. Chutkow explained things very well and provided great examples. You dont really need to do readings to do well in the class. Very important to take good notes and go to lecture, as problem sets rely on stuff she says outloud.

As many commenters have said, take thoroughly detailed notes during lectures. This will significantly help you complete the problem sets. Professor Chutkow is very knowledgeable in the law, and she made everything we needed to know super clear. I highly recommend taking one of their classes if you're interested in law school.

GO TO LECTURE AND TAKE DETAILED NOTES!!!!! graded based on 3 problem sets that are more like essays analyzing a case she makes up. office hours are closed while problem sets are open so its important to go to OH right away if you have questions (slides are just outlines). Lectures are great. Due dates are firm but she is understanding and kind.

Professor Chutkow was one of the best professors I have ever had at Cornell. The class lectures were very interesting and very relevant to current day affairs. There are 3 problem sets and all are manageable as they directly connect to lecture notes and readings. Would 100 percent recommend this class and professor to anyone. Easy A- class!

awesome prof, awesome class. lectures are super relevant and engaging. material is not too difficult as long as you do the readings and problem sets are fun to write. absolutely recommend and would totally take again.

Professor Chutkow is such an amazing and engaging lecturer, and taking her class(es) solidified my desire to attend law school after completing undergrad. I learned so much and really got to stretch my intellectual skills. Love her so much! She is accessible outside of class.

AMST 3821 is my favorite class taken in college. The material is complex but so interesting. I tried to rearrange my schedule to take another class of Professor Chutkow's. Truly amazing and so engaging.

Professor Chutkow is wonderful! She has super engaging lectures that make you want to come to class even though attendance is not mandatory. If you have any interest in constitutional law then take this class. I will say it's difficult to get above an A- on the problem sets, but it's also lowkey hard to get below an A- on the problem sets

Her lectures are very engaging and interesting and she spends a lot of time making sure she explains everything in a clear way. No discussion (instead we have a small section during class time three times throughout the semester). Grade is based on 3 papers that are relatively straightforward. Grading is a little unclear but fair, she grades not ta

Amazing class and a great professor. If you are interested in SCOTUS, take this class. Just three writing assignments which are very hard but if you take notes in class, you are all set. Skim the homework readings. She has so much enthusiasm and is a great person overall. Learned a lot and enjoyed this course. Ask questions and be engaged!!

Professor Chutkow is probably the best professor I've had at Cornell. She is fantastic to listen to and is very interactive with her students within lectures. Grading scheme of only writing 3 papers throughout the year is amazing--but make sure you show up to lecture, you'll need the information.
Prof Chutkow gives really interesting lectures and makes the cases memorable with her stories. The readings are all very interesting and worth doing.

Engaging lecturer. Assignments are interesting, lots of time to get them done. Feedback is detailed and helpful. It's ok to skip the hw readings. Chutkow really cares about her students. And the best part, no tests!

Professor Chutkow completely lacks any semblance of human empathy. You will be denied any and all requested accommodations, regardless of medical condition or extraneous situation. If you wish to be helplessly thrust into grueling problem sets with little to no formal guidance, Professor Chutkow is the one for you!
Phenomenal professor. Witty, knowledgeable, and makes lectures engaging. Grade is dependent on three essays and participation in section (only meets a couple times a semester). Would take again.
Very tough to get past an A-, but a really interesting class. Would recommend for anyone remotely interested in Constitutional Law
Best professor I have had at Cornell so far. She is great and gives engaging lectures. I looked forward to attending her class each week.

Very good law professor - unbiased, engaging, detailed. Funny & explains concepts well. Difficult to get passed an A- in the class - grading done by harsh TAs, and criteria is not well explained. Attendance & good lecture notes critical for the problem sets. Overall solid but have to work very hard to get a good grade on the few assignments

Lecture was online/asynchronous for SP21, with 4 live sessions with a TA. Still, lectures were engaging and topics were easy to grasp. 2 problem sets and 1 final that were fun to write and helped me grasp the concepts. You can't go to TAs for help on assignments so make sure to meet with them early if needed. Would take another class with her

Excellent professor. Very knowledgeable. Favorite characteristic was her level-headed, fair approach to explaining issues. Never got on a soapbox and preached, just presented the facts. Refreshing in the study of government. Only complaint, lecture was recorded, almost no live interaction with the professor.
She's honestly just majestic. I don't know what else to say. Literally amazing. Extremely smart, helpful, and engaging.
She actually wants you to do well. Very interesting lectures. THIS IS HOW PROFESSORS SHOULD TEACH.

Professor Chutkow is an icon. I loved her class so much that I took another class by her this semester (even though it is all online, I love her lectures). She is so so engaging and her assignments really help you learn the law and actually apply it, which I appreciate. The only thing is, the highest grade I have ever heard in her class was an A-

Chutkow is amazing. Manages to make even the dryest of subjects interesting and is so fun to be in a class with. Class is definitely hard and you have to work to get a good grade but it's by no means impossible to do so. If you're even thinking about entering law definitely take this

Prof Chutkow is an intelligent and well-spoken professor. She doesn't cold call. She is very understanding and makes sure students learn and challenge their assumptions about the law. The class is pretty hard. Midterm was incredibly difficult. But overall, great class. Make sure you ask questions after class.

She is a good lecturer, but the slides on their own are useless. Grading is extremely unclear but not arbitrary. The final is hard and the essays take a lot of time. cool class if you want to enter law though

Lectures are engaging and you will learn a lot, but there are two big writing assignments for which you really need to understand the material. Pay attention and do the readings. Grading depends on the TA but is typically tough.

Lots of reading (20-50 pages a night) but as long as you do the reading, you will be fine on the papers and the exams. Her lectures are super passionate and she is hilarious, she always makes sure the class is engaged with the material.

Chutkow knows everything there is to know about constitutional law. She's funny and her lectures are engaging. I learned a lot, and even though law is not my path, the class was interesting. Definitely read the cases- it makes the essays doable and following along in class much easier.

Prof. Chutkow is an extremely lucid lecturer, she makes you want to hear and understand Law. I loved this class so much that I am taking another class with her next semester and am probably going to venture the career path of Pre-Law as an undergraduate (and continue later on).
Prof. Chutkow is an amazing lecturer! Do the readings for class and you will enjoy it!
Enjoyed her class and she's a good professor, but wouldn't say she's incredible.  I've taken better courses in the GOVT Department.

Amazing! I absolutely loved this class. Her class was pretty much the only one I made sure to attend all the time because she's such a great lecturer. It's not that hard of a class but you need to do the readings and think hard about the papers. Luckily I thought the readings and assignments were very interesting.

Professor Chutkow is a phenomenal lecturer and instructor. I enjoyed each lecture, which were all engaging and clear. Professor Chutkow made complicated legal jargon feel familiar and has guided me toward a career option I never would have thought existed. An excellent class.
I LOVED Chutkow... but you have to work for a good grade.  You need to be willing to carefully look over your essays and analyze key points.  If you put in the time and effort, you will do well.

You have to work to do well, but she is straight up the best professor. She is so clear and organized. Her lectures are always timed perfectly and she never uses an extraneous word. If you are interested in law at all, this is a must take.

Professor chutkow is very engaging, likes to interact with the class. incredibly upbeat, lively and funny. really likes the material and wants students to as well. papers are pretty straightforward and she gives you two weeks between when she gives you the essay prompt and when its due. good law class though the lectures are a bit too simplified

Excellent professor who's very knowledgeable about the subject matter, answers students' questions, and presents the material clearly and in a straight forward manner.  Tests are difficult but fair.  Though lecture isn't mandatory, it is extremely useful.  Overall, excellent class and professor. 9/10 would take again.

Great professor, no doubt about it, just a few qualms about the class format (frustratingly broad paper topics, etc.) Still totally worth taking the course and getting to know her. She is the classiest prof I've ever had.

Probably my favorite professor so far at Cornell, and by far my favorite class. She is a great lecturer and puts very interesting readings on the syllabus. The only problem is that her classes tend to be early in the morning (8:40am).

Great Prof. One of the best i have had at Cornell. Really interesting subject matter and she tries to connect with all of her students. Every class and section is technically optional, however you wouldn't learn anything without them. Class is a must if you enjoy  politics, current events, or law.
She is really really smart and is able to connect all of the disparate constitutional issues together well so that even if you don't read all the cases, they still all make sense
Easy class. Great professor.
Cool class to take, he has dry humor that is actually very funny. This is an easy and interesting course!
Grading is based on curve. Getting an 89 average in the class will get you a B...

Seems like a very nice individual in person but his lecture style is a snoozefest and the material seemed to me like commopn sense. ALWAYS go to office hours prior to turning in the projects or your grade will suffer! Meet with both Sobal and a TA before the projects are due!

Professor Rzeszotarski is the best professor I've had at Cornell so far. He is witty, and cares a lot about certain things, but is a great professor that cares for students. I would take any course with him again

Great at explaining concepts and very caring prof overall.  The homework accurately reflects what is learned but is still very interesting and rewarding.  You do have to pay attention and keep up to do well.
well-organized and well-explained material. He uploads recordings so easy to review. Assignments echo w class material so easy to work on. nice class!

Overall one of my fav professors at UCSB. He was really passionate about the class. no midterm final, just two essays and attendance. Great lectures and he wants you to participate. If you're interested in the middle east he goes in detail about the subjects he teaches.

Very smart man, and very good professor. He demanded a lot from students and taught primarily via class discussion. Exams were by essay and oral defense, so you had to actually know the coursework to do well. Mastering the material was the students' responsibility, but he was always in his office if you needed to work through some stuff.

DO NOT TAKE THIS OR ANY OF HIS CLASSES. He is confusing, hard to follow, and the class had no structure.  Grades were from 3 essays and a defense in class. There would be no feedback on the essays (just an email back with a grade) and would expect improvement. Class was excruciatingly boring. Very smart guy, terrible professor.

Extremely confusing and difficult to follow.  He expected the class to be a "discussion-based" course, but talked the entire time, most often going off on tangents.  The midterms are 1 part writing and 1 part in class defense.  They are extremely difficult and nerve-wracking.  I got a B+ but it was not worth the effort.  I learned nothing.
see whoever posted before me. really helpful prof, crazy smart, well-read, very enthusiastic about material,

great prof and just an overall amazing human being. he is ridiculously intelligent but doesn't have the classic 'academic snob' thing going.  he's opinionated and kinda and knows his****. talk to him after class..he will help you and you'll have wonderful conversations. take his classes..seriously.
Love this man--he's a great teacher. And he gave me chocolate when I met with him during office hours. He rules, basically.

Good class overall. He did an amazing job of taking comments, adding to them, and fostering class discussion. Sometimes he assumed a little too much background knowledge of the subject for an introductory course but still a great prof.

I'll give him a better rating next time b/c I DO want to take another class from him. Was his first semester, so things were confusing and overwhelming to begin but he was hitting his stride toward the end. Liked some readings, some discussions, interesting material, willing to work with you in your area of interest. Go to the roundtables!

Ahmad Ahmad gave us a 3000 word essay with a 12 hour notice that made up our ENTIRE grade and told us that we all did a terrible job in his class. Not a single person has any idea what he taught us in the class because of his poor organizational skills. He is a smart smart man however he should not be a professor.

Took RGST125A. 
The class was graded with 50% participation plus two papers worth 25% each. There were a lot, and I mean A LOT of moments in this class where I didn't understand anything that was going on. With that being said, Ahmad is a nice guy, and while he goes off-topic more than he actually lectures, it was an interesting class.

not a religious studies course. The professor is obviously very smart but bases his class off of comparative law and anything relating to law because that is what he enjoys. Also doesn't communicate well with the students and dropped a ten page paper on the students for a final after saying the final would be either 300 or 1500 words.

His off topic digressions are the most interesting parts of the class because he knows an incredible amount about history and philosophy and is as well read as anyone you'll ever meet. The readings are short but dense and the course objective was a little unclear but he'll notice if you put in the effort and give you the benefit of the doubt.

He does digress off topic and the course objective is not very clear but you only have to read 20 pages per week so as long as you do that you should do well. He can come across as intense or condescending but he's an easy grader and dropped the lowest of 3 pop quizzes for everyone in class.

Prof. Ahmad is very knowledgeable, but his lectures are just a supplement to the readings and lecture material is usually not on the test. Sometimes he mumbles, so it's best to sit near the front of the room. Class was based on two books and wasn't too difficult to read either. Every quiz and test was accompanied by a study guide thanks to TA.

Dont take this class for an easy A. Dr. Ahmad is so smart but just rambles all class long and does not have any structure in his lectures there are almost pointless in going too(currently in one ). The topic is extremely boring, vague, and i feel like i havent learned anything even though i was excited 2 take this class. Save yourself b4 its 2 late

Professor Ahmad is incredibly knowledgable.  While the course was discussion based and thus not heavily structured like a typical lower div, it was incredibly engaging and I learned so much.  You need to do the readings.  There's no skating through his classes; if you aren't in it to really learn, don't take it. Participation is necessary.

Professor Ahmad is a brilliant guy.  With that being said, he constantly digresses, and sometimes goes far beyond what his original topic was about.  He knows so much history, theory, authors, etc.  With no certain course outline besides what he assigns to read, the course objective of the class is very unclear.

Prof. Ahmad is perhaps one of the most smartest men I've ever met in my entire life. You can just feel it, I mean like the guy got his PhD from Harvard. That being said, he has a tendency to ramble sometimes. Read the chapter for the week for R. Studies 2 and youre set. Fairly interesting class. No tests. Just an essay and presentation at the end.

Not very easy to understand in clarity of speech and subject. I had a hard time following his reasoning. I think it may be a culture difference as I have taken another class on Islamic studies with a different professor and had a hard time as well (and Im not the only one)

The course was easy but the professor is a horrible lecturer. He runs off on tangents and expects people to chime in even though no one can follow his train of thought. I got an A but died of boredom in lecture. Going to class was useless. The one thing that saved me was the awesome TA Nathan!
he is a very smart guy. Although he goes off the topic a lot, his lecture is very helpful

Lecture is totally worthless.  He doesn't touch the material needed to succeed in the class, you essentially learn everything from section.  I earned a solid A and never went to lecture at all.  Just make sure you read the book
Vey intelligent so he expects nothing but quality from his students. lower div class so i'm sure he took it easy on us. i can only imagine what he expects from upper div...

Terrible class. The lectures were dreadful. The readings were boring. The midterm was easy seeing as it was on a whole book. Lectures were very unorganized. He checked the syllabus right when he got there to see what he was talking about. I don't recommend this class to anybody although it's extremely easy to get an A. Elliot Bazzano decent TA.
Boring lecture that does not relate to text. not very hard but extremely difficult to follow the professors ideas
Ahmad is very  nice..Smart...and I enjoyed him speaking..to take his class you should keep up with the readings and know what he wants exactly...Love Professor Ahmad..he is Fun Guy :))

Professor Ahmad is an awesome professor.  While it is true that he can get off subject sometimes, that's what makes his class fun.  Being able to go discuss other subjects that tie loosely to the topic is thought provoking.  Also, if you know the material and ask good thought-provoking questions, you can be very liberal in paper writing.  Awesome!!
great professor! this guy knows his stuff

Ahmad is extremely smart.  The way he lectures, sometimes he'll just be off in the clouds somewhere and you'll be lost.  I was in his section which was considerably easier than the TA.  He did not have a final.  His philosophies are sometimes difficult to grasp, but he is very approachable and interesting to speak to.  Recommended.

I learned so much from this guy's class. While lecture was, for me, almost useless, the readings and papers we wrote were incredibly enlightening. Take a class with Ahmad if you want to see a perspective that we rarely get here in the U.S.  Overall a very challenging but intellectually rewarding class. Ahmad is one smart dude.

Loved this class! it's a lot of reading comprehension and class discussion but he is a fair teacher with a very open mind and he truly cares about his students. Go to his office hours...he's very easy to talk to.
He is very nice and very knowledgable. However he is often confusing becuase he is so philosphical. Hard to follow.

Professor Ahmad is a very kind and intelligent teacher. The readings are generally relevant and the work load is very mild. There were 3 papers and one presentation which is really just a summary of the readings. The only thing is he is so philosophical that he gets off track and confusing many times.

Really interesting class, covers a cool topic and the reading is actually interesting and very easy to do. to do well in the class you do have to keep on top of the reading, but if you show a genuine interest, he really likes it. very cool prof, office hrs are a really big help and he's very available if you can't make the hrs.

She does group work only.. everything in class is group based and that is just a third of her class. Every teacher says for a credit hour, study 3 hours at home, and she definetly gives the work for that long. We have two types of online homework, and in class all she does is check we did our work. The homework is what teaches you thats forsure

This terrible teacher told me to drop in the third week of class, because I'd missed two classes. There was no effort made to help me. After that, I felt like she hated me and I was no longer comfortable with her. I tried for another week, but it was too uncomfortable. I was just starting to have the confidence to go back to school and I quit.

This professor is inflexible and tough. get ready to feel like you are in High School. Very difficult to work with, although books have not been available and you work full time and are proactive. She rushes through the work the daily assignments and does give zeros if you are late.

Niamh is a great instructor. She really cares how the class is doing and tries to keep the class fun. She is very accommodating to people if they need to miss class or need extra time. If you put effort towards Irish, she will help you succeed. Classes are small (6 or less). Everyone will participate/talk in front of the class.
Nic is AWESOME! Best lab instructor ever and I hate chemistry.  To bad he is going to Washington for grad school.

Nic is an outstanding clinical professor.  She is knowledgeable, kind, gives helpful feedback and criticism without making you feel inept.  She is always available for questions or comments and truly wants her students to be successful in school and nursing.  I wish I could shadow HER for a day with patients.  I would love to have her in the future

I wish I could take all my clinicals with DuPree. You will no doubt succeed first semester with Nic by your side. She is there with you every step of the way. Clear instruction and feedback, responds back quickly through text/email, and very approachable. One if the kindest people I've ever met. She graduated from Saddlebacks program soshecanrelate

She is an awesome 1st semester clinical instructor!  She explained everything, took the time for questions, and encouraged all of us!  She also replied promptly to messages left and kept us all in the loop of what to expect.  I wish I could put her in my pocket and take her with me through the rest of nursing school!

I felt very spoiled having this professor as my clinical instructor in my first nursing class.  She is very supportive, encourages dialog, keeps a healthy professional boundary between herself and her students, challenges you when you need it, very effusive in her praise, spends time helping you gain confidence.
Professor Rhea is so helpful! I really loved his class and learned a lot, but my favorite thing was his sweet eyes.

Intro to performance was my favorite class of the semester. Nic made it so fun. He is really understanding if you have no acting experience at all, and wants you to improve. His assignments are very easy if you just do what he says. He's very clear on his expectations, but is still lenient since not everyone is a performer. Super easy A

This class was paper and discussion based. It was so incredibly illuminating and changed my perspective of the world. Nic is a fantastic teacher and I was so lucky to be his student. He was accommodating and understanding during the pandemic and made the move to online very easy. He is one of the best professors I have had.
Different from other professors. Challenging. Consummate professional.

I absolutely loved Nic. He's SUPER intimidating but knows what he's talking about and was definitely my favorite professor at SIUE. Really, he's the only professor I've done a positive review about on RMP. Be prepared to read and participate in lecture for brownie points. His exams are heavy, but you don't need to be a rocket scientist to get an A.

Dr. Guehlstorf easily comes off as intimidating but you learn very quickly that he is very kind and passionate. I had a 3 hour long class with him and there was never a dull moment. He gives good analogies for difficult concepts and truly wants you to understand. You can not go into his courses expecting it to be a breeze. You'll need to work hard.

He's a great professor! He may come off as intimidating at first, but he's a great dude. He cares a lot about the class and is very knowledgeable. He really wants participation and wants you to learn. He's one of my favorite professors I've ever had.
Excellent teacher - great at encouraging abstract applications of knowledge. I would recommend taking this professor before considering graduate school options.

Honestly, my favorite professor! He's not as intimidating as you think he is, he is a very animated person, and if you ask for help he'll clarify anything you need. I learned so much from his classes and he's hilarious!

DO NOT be intimated by his extreme height, big voice, 3 piece suits,hard eye contact, and stone cold resting face. Rambling lectures that dont generate heavy notes. Exams are based on chapter vocab (only 14 of tested terms are on the study guide) and online readings (one topic will always be on exam). Nic is my absolute favorite professor this semester. As long as you have common sense and show effort he'll like you. His lectures are hilarious and he always makes sure you understand the reading in class. Would definitely take another class with him.

Loved having him as a teacher! Nic is very knowledgeable and by far my favorite professor here. He may be abrasive but usually only to get rid of the students who aren't going to try hard in his class. I had him for another class and will continue to take as many classes with him as possible because I actually feel that I am learning something.

Dr. Guehlstorf is one of the most interesting professors I've had at SIUE.  This class was not so much about rote memorization but manipulation of information. Fair Instrucntor, easy to understand, makes it clear what he wants. Just show up to class and you get points. Basically if you just show up and pay attention you will pass and I am a lazy student, I got an A-

I enjoyed his class very much and had quite a few laughs in there. If you have a B+ or above you dont have to take the final. I found it easy to get an A and Im a lazy student

If you enjoy a challenge, take this class. Comes off as intimidating, especially to females (his words), and if you stay to the end, you'll notice the class size dwindle. DO THE READINGS AND THE NOTECARDS. They add up! A few challenging assignments, but if you stay to the end, YOU WILL BE SMARTER.

If you have any desire to utilize the opportunities at SIUE, it is imperative that you take Nic's classes. Dr. G is somewhat intimidating at first, but quite possibly one of the most entertaining and engaging professors at SIUE. He has great wit and knows how to relate difficult material to real life situations. Looks like Jeff Goldblum.

Freaking GORGEOUS!!!  If you are interested in environmental politics you should take this professor.  He's very intelligent, helpful, and good at relating the material.  Daily notecards kinda suck...but did I mention what a stud Nic was...?

Nic is funny as hell. While you really can not take notes, if you listen you will not need to.

Great teacher, extremely knowledgable. Good at relating Public policies to everyday happenings and keeping his own political opinions to himself. Makes INCREDIBLY boring subject matter interesting. Also funny and a sweet 80's hairdo.
