Young professor, still finding her groove.  Stumbles with words and sometimes has trouble conveying ideas.  Class is mostly a waste of time--although if you can listen it will drive it home--as everything is out of the readings and her powerpoints which are online.  Easy grader, tests are straight forward, the debate is kind of pointless but easy.
pretty boring. she doesn't look at you when she lectures; she just kinda stares up in the sky, which makes it kinda boring. fairly passionate. you'll need to know quotes for the MC part of the test.

This class turned out to be a lot harder than I thought it would be. You MUST do all the reading to do well on tests. Tests are MC, Short Answer, and Essay, discussion group attendance requirement, and a debate you must participate and write a paper for. Not a good class to take if you don't have lots of time!
Lots of reading. Lots of critical thinking.
She is the most boring teacher I think I have ever had.  Don't take unless you have to.

An interesting class...I enjoyed the content.  ALOT of reading to cover, but the tests are mostly based off power point.  You CAN get buy without really reading and still get a good grade (I got a B+ without really reading anything after the mid-term.)

Wonderful professor and class! Dr. Hsueh is articulate and intelligent, and has a very organized lecture style. Class concepts based off readings, so be sure to do them. The tests are essay, but graded fairly and reasonably. You will enjoy this PLSC 360 even if theory is not your thing - just take the class with Hsueh!
She is very knowledgable and wants you to be too.  Accomodating and very willing to talk to you outside of class.  Tests are more than fair, reflecting the study guide almost exactly.

She is such a sweet person and she is so smart. She is very good at lecturing which makes sitting through a two hour class easier! She is my favorit professor at western she actually knows what she is talking about. her tests are relatively easy if you like essay questions. She gives tests almost straight from the lecture notes!
class was tight, she's hella smart.  she assigns foucault, and that alone is enough to justify planting your ass in this class.
Very interesting.  Had her for two theory courses, and enjoyed both of them.

Her teaching style makes lectures and test material really clear if you come to class. She covers a lot of material, but pretty much doesn't test on anything outside of the lecture notes (which she provides). She's also friendly and fair.

This professor is always ready to help students. Although the quizzes were quite difficult, the teaching style of this professor is great, and inspires interest in the students. Hes a nice grader. I would take this professor again.

Most people find this class easy but personally it's difficult for me. The entire class is about MOSFETS and amplifiers. Make sure you study small signals pretty well and other topics that might repeat from ECE 65. Definitely review your ECE 65 prerequisite stuff as well as other things from ECE 100. Professor is very kind and answers questions.

Honestly incredible. One of my favorite professors. He comes from and incredible background in spacecraft engineering, and can elaborate to insane depths on almost any question you have for him. There's a reason he was CTO of NASA

Lectures had way too many slides, over 50 each lecture. Exam 2 was graded differently than the first easier one; missing one word in a definition would result in zero credit. Otherwise HWs graded on completion, no curve.

The class is not curved.  A lot of students I know from Cornell get A's. There are many students from other countries who probably are taking a class in English for the first time, and they seem to have real trouble. I've seen some cheat, but its probably because of their language problems and not because the class is unfair.

This professor definitely is not nice to the students. Would not let students take prelims early, curves the class ridiculously low, and just provides vague answers to any question you ask. Also makes ppt presentations with 80/90 slides. We were def. taught something different in engineering communications.

SYSEN 510 itself is just a BS course, from the fact that they need index card questions to force your attendance. Sets take-home final that does not make sense even to MechE, and provide very vague answers when consulted. Sets consulting hours from 9-12 for final project but left at 11. The only good is that its' a free-frag 500-level course.

Very open and approachable personality. He does good job with the lectures too - speaks and presents very clearly. He takes care to make his handwriting legible and visible to everyone in the class (sometimes through asking for feedback from the students).
No Comments

I love Professor Hay. He is very established in his field, communicates points well, and has a great sense of humor. Antitrust Economics was challenging but not unreasonable for someone looking to get a taste of a law school class. I only wish I didn't skip lecture so much haha.

While Professor Hay is a funny guy, his class format is abhorrent. He mandates attendance and will randomly call on students for economic or law-related questions and then keep pressing/ridiculing them until they say the right answer. He also makes sure the median on all tests is 50 before curve. Too much work for very little payoff.
Very knowledgeable and respected professor. As long as you're keeping up with the readings and show up to class, you'll have a good time in the course.

Took both of his classes - Competition Law and Economics and the Law. Highly recommended - one the best professors and leans more on the law side than Econ and incredibly knowledgeable with a fantastic experience. You just need to do case briefs (can be copy pasted) and you MUST go to class but if you put the work you can do well.

Prof. Hay is a legend: smart, experienced, passionate, real. Best class I've taken on this campus. However, Prof Hay has no sort of supplementary material for lectures so you really have to listen to him in lecture because besides the cases, it's all that can help you for exams. He doesn't hold your hand through the class but it's not unreasonable.
Love this guy 10/10 would recommend. Took both his courses.

Professor Hay is absolutely fantastic. You'll learn more in this class than perhaps any other law class for undergraduates. You don't even have to read the cases - just read the summaries on casebriefs since the exam is analysis-based and on concepts. Essentially, attend all the lectures (you'll be very sorry if you miss one) and make good guides.
Very moody. On a good day, he can be great and inspirational.

Really knowledgeable professor.  I like him a lot and will take his Competition Law & Policy class next semester (Econ 3805).  Read lots of court case summaries.  A few exams, but they are all manageable.

Huge expert in his field: funny, great lectures, really cool stories. The socratic style of the class is enough to scare anyone into reading all the cases before class, but he never assigned more than 45 minutes of reading per class. The only negative aspect was the lack of clarity when it came to what to expect for exams and papers and grading.
Hay can be kind of demanding, but that's because he takes the course seriously and expects his students to do the same.  If you really get into his class you can get a lot of it.
Really knows his stuff.  Fairly tough class.

Had this professor twice.  First time was excellent... one of the best (yet most demanding) courses I've taken.  However, the second time, he was extremely hostile.  When going to his office for help, the guy was just rude... on more than one occasion!  He can really flip, for very little reason.
No Comments
This course was quite difficult, especially for 3 credits.  Hay is an amazing teacher - I don't think I've ever learded so much over the course of a semester.  Do the reading.
Great Teacher, the most interested I have ever been in Economics. Be prepared to wite 2 16 page papaers. Still... one of my most favorite classes.
Really really good lecturer, full of interesting and relevant stories, great sense of humor, very smart, can be kind of a hard ass.

It's not the easiest class, but if you do the reading you'll do fine. The professor has a hilarious dry sense of humor and knows the subject cold. Professor Hay runs the lectures well and they are always entertaining.
Wonderful teacher. Intimidating socratic method, but he is fair. Interesting material and lectures. DO THE READING!
One of the most interesting classes I've had at Cornell, although the Socratic method can be a little daunting at first. Readings aren't that bad either.

Fantastic teacher.  He aims to teach you the relation between Economics and the Law and succeeds.  Class requires a lot of reading in that he calls on you randomly to see if you did it.  Lot of work + Hard Midterm + Easy Final = Good Grade = Great Class
No Comments

Great course! I`ve learned a lot about space and missions. The professor and guest lecturers are NASA members. I can definitely tell that my writing has improved, and I`ve learned how to prepare for and give the presentation. Grading is clear and fair. Your grade reflects your work and improvement. You are not competing with others which is great.

Prof. Hayes is excellent. His class is entirely discussion based and very interesting. He tries to engage students throughout each lecture and invites very prominent people in NASA/space policy to give guest lectures. There is a fair amount of assignments, but they're graded very fairly if you give effort.

He's probably much better for science specific majors because he talks in very scientific lingo and complex language even though the class is literally geared toward non-majors. Very easy class though. Small homework assignments once a week max and participation is 25% of the grade. Lectures can be a bit dry because all he does is talk though.

Extremely boring lecturer and repeats himself a lot BUT nice, fair, considerate guy and he'll take the time to give you really thorough and detailed answers to questions you have. Class and material are not hard if you pay attention (go to OH), exams are easy if you memorize his slides (no surprises).

Interesting material, great test review but hard exams, and a high though non-problematic level of disorganization. This class won't suck away too much time, too. At times when coursework is particularly heavy, Hirsh will give what amounts to a several-day extension on homework, and he provides many high-quality answers on Piazza.

I took Prof Hirsh's class when the Covid-19 situation first started and he was very caring and thoughtful of the struggles students would be going through. He cancelled both the midterm and the final and replaced them with manageable weekly quizzes. Additionally, his lectures were very interesting and greatly increased my interest in AI.

CS 4700 has historically gotten a bad rep at Cornell. I think a lot of things changed for the Spring 2020 semester. I was surprised at the good lectures, clear slides, accessibility of the staff, improvement in HW quality and understanding that I was able to gain from this class. Haym has also been an extremely caring professor during the crisis.

CS4700 was probably the worst class I took at Cornell. Everyone describes AI as an "Easy A" because the topics are simple, but the class is so unorganized and inconsistent that it is frustrating to prepare for it. Prof Hirsh seemed unprepared for class and his slides/problem sets had many errors. To learn similar content, take CS 2110 and CS 4780.

Most unorganized class I've ever taken. Prof promised weekly hws, have gotten 3 (12/15 weeks into semester). Office hours a mess because he doesn't provide TAs with intelligible HW solutions. Grade based on 2 tests (practice exams not helpful), and HWs which are hard to seek help for. Very apparent prof doesn't care about the course; stay away!

The homeworks (there are about 6) are pretty helpful in understanding the material. There were also some good example problems provided before the exams last semester. Overall, the class was a lot better than what I'd previously heard. The curriculum/course structure has changed for the better, and Hirsh cares a lot about helping students learn.

Poor lecturer, very disorganized. Tells class a homework will be released that night and then takes another 6 days to actually release it. Class itself is a joke, you won't learn anything but you will get an easy A. If you're a CS major, don't bother. If you're just looking to fulfill a requirement, I still wouldn't tbh.

I didn't go to lecture that much, but still did well on exams and homeworks. All you need to really do is study the powerpoint slides and notes from old CS 4700 websites to pass + go to exam reviews. Prof. Hirsh is a nice guy and good teacher, but the material in this course is pretty scarce so he ends up spending alot of time on simple topics.

Comparing Strandford or Berkeley, this course is a shame. Probably one of the worst CS courses at Cornell. Extremely unorganized. Professor was too busy to take care of the class. Spending a month on DFS and BFS (Remember this is a 4000level course). It only covers 1/5 or fewer materials than Berkeley. Don't take it if you are a CS major.
Was quite flexible regarding the projects, easy assignments, boring lecture, lots of extra credits activities. He was very unorganized and the exams were vague and quite difficult.
Never seen any other professor is as responsible and patient as Prof. Hirsh.  His recitations and replies on piazza are super helpful. He is really a nice guy.

Good professor. May be his first time teaching AI in Cornell but he led the class pretty well. HWs are not so heavy and everyone could easily get full credit. Exams are a large portion of your grade, so do prepare. Usually the test questions are harder than HW, or tricker.   Professor is nice and spent a lot of time of Piazza :)

Pelliccia was one of the most accessible professors I had. He was more than willing to meet with me and help me in this class. That being said, this class was hard. I really struggled with it. Homework every night, and lots and lots of quizzes and tests.

Loved taking Intro to Greek from Professor Pelliccia. He's passionate about the language, which comes through in his lectures and tangents. Make sure you come prepared to class with forms and homework, memorize principal parts, and you're good. Reasonable homework for an intro-level language course. Extremely accessible via email for questions.

Pelliccia is a god when it comes to greek. Though the subject matter has got to be one of the most difficult out there, he teaches greek with such passion & is so knowledgeable . He explains everything thoroughly, his expectations are clear, & his feedback on homework is so helpful. There were very few quizzes/tests, but the ones we had were fair.

The class was just the right combination of unbearably stressful and downright fun. The attention to detail was overwhelming, but the discussion was always informative-- we certainly came to appreciate the approach. The class convinced me to be a classics major. I will try to take as many Greek courses with him as I can, and can recommend the same.
Favors female students. Good at raising interesting questions. Not great at encouraging discussion.

tests are sooooooooo difficult, he'll put the most obscure material on them and then laugh as he leaves his students to struggle with the test in a room proctored by a grad student...but nonetheless he is a great professor and a teacher in the most basic senses of the words...he liberally shares his knowledge and will do his best to help a student
I love himmm!!!  He is super cool and smart and is actually really approachable and helpful, interesting to talk to as well.
What a great professor!  One of the most interesting and stimulating classes I have taken.  Difficult class but well worth it!

Professor Pelliccia has a knack for making learning unappealing.  He always finds the hardest things to put on tests, like exceptions to the rule, etc., to make sure you mess up if you are not in complete command of the material.  Very discouraging!!

She is caring and kind but it wasn't an interesting class. Her grading criteria aren't clear at all yet she takes off marks and doesn't give feedback. My grades were mistaken and posted manually twice and I had to contact her for the correction, which I did not find professional at all. The exams weren't easy and there were a lot of readings.

Most useless course I've ever taken. Boring lectures: reads off the slides and expects everyone to be passionate about a prerequisite. Material not difficult but she gives vague instructions and then poor marks because it's not exactly what she wanted. Attendance sheet and an $80 textbook that was rarely referenced. She makes me want to drop out.

Maggie is a great and funny teacher! Some of the material is dry but the other material is highly interesting (she is aware.) She provides exercises to help comprehend the content which is very helpful. Exams= a lot of writing but don't memorize just understand the material. She is understanding and approachable! TAKE HER! SHE IS GREAT!
Maggie is awesome! Her class is very interesting and she is very helpful. She tries to get everyone involved and is just very passionate about what she does. Take her if you can!!

This was the most interesting class I've taken at UCSD. This class highlights social justice in the world. It was intellectually stimulating and allowed for a lot of discussion between students. Professor Blaise was a great listener and was genuinely interested in what students had to say. He created a safe space for students to openly talk.

Professor Blaise was one of the nicest professors I have ever had. The class consisted of 4-5 mandatory zoom lectures, weekly discussions, and a 5-6 page essay for the midterm and the final. He is always accessible to answer questions and he gives you his number if you want to contact him and receive a quick response. Loved his class a lot!

Dr. Blaise is one of the most respectable professors I've ever come across at UCSD. He truly cares about his students, and verbalizes it frequently. Class consists of doing readings, submitting weekly discussion posts graded by completion, two papers, and showing up to lecture. Easy A if you try, and you learn a lot about social justice and equity

Both classes were very eye opening and important. I definitely agree with Prof Blaise that participating in discussions helps us remember these topics for a lifetime. Since then, I was also able to serve as a TA for Professor Blaise and he has been a great mentor ever since. I definitely rec this class!

Boring lecturer. Political agenda demonstrated within every assignment. Class was not interesting nor intellectually stimulating. Grading was all over the place (TA didn't know what she was doing). May problems with his computer(viruses would turn off laptop lol). Just appeal to his ideals and you'll get an A. Attendance is unfortunately mandatory

Prof. Blaise opened my eyes to the hardships that continue to plague modern societies. His teachings on social justice and equity encourage students to embrace the scholarship of cultural competency, illustrating that our characteristics and colors should underscore a sense of unity, rather than define us. He is truly an inspirational professor.

Dr. Blaise is my favorite professor I've had at UCSD! I actually learned so much about society, different cultures, social justice, and the importance of intersectionality in his classes. Do the readings because they're really helpful. Class discussions are entertaining and welcoming. This is the most impactful and memorable class I've taken.

This is one of the most informative classes/best professors I've ever taken at UCSD! There are a lot of papers, but that's basically all that's graded (and they're graded very fairly). Classes are just discussing the readings, so make sure you at least know what they're about. There's a group project, but it's basically graded on completion.
THE LECTURES ARE DISCUSSING READINGS. Yes the readings are heavy but not graded so you can lack in some. 25% attendance/participation, 25% short essays, 25% group presentation and 25% final essay.

Professor Blaise is my favorite professor I've had at UCSD. Not only does he prioritize his students' learning, but he is also so intelligent & passionate about the subject matter. He truly wants his students to succeed. Make sure that you do all the readings! His class made me more cognizant of inequities in society & positively impacted me.

I took HDP171 and 175 with Dr. Blaise, and I can vouch for his knowledge and kindness. he cares about his students and applies social justice in his grading and treatment to students. He is by far one of the top professors in social sciences courses and I wish there were more of him. He will make you think about life differently. I RECOMMEND HIM..

I found Professor Blaise's class to be excellent. As long as you do the readings and participate in discussion, you'll do great. He has a wealth of knowledge and experience, and I think he does a wonderful job at encouraging students to look at the big picture. I'd highly recommend this class as I think the subject material is very, very important

This teacher is terrible at grading. She constantly downgrades you for things "missing" from your assignment - pay attention or you will get a lower grade than deserved. There is no rhyme or reason to the pts she docks either, some things she will take 15 pts off, and some 2. If you ask for help, it will take days for a response that offers no help

She will give you a temp zero for "missing minimum requirements". Feedback will then consist only of a copy + paste of minimum requirements with no clarity. Slow to respond to emails when asked to clarify on feedback. I waited 6 weeks for correspondence on a temp zero. One assignment had feedback addressed to another student. Choose another teacher

THE WORST PROFESSOR. She is unable to clearly tell you what she looks for in assignments, then shell mark down points for not Reading her mind essentially. I was a 4.0 student until I took her class and received a B-. HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. If you can read minds, this will be a A+ class, but I cannot so I worked my butt off for a B-. HORRIBLE!!!!

An awful teacher who doesn't even know what she is grading. She also never gives you feedback. When you ask her a question she says "follow the instructions provided." When her instructions don't cover your question.

This class is not at all hard. The book gives you the instructions for each assignment. I didn't read the book at all because I only used it to do the assignments. A lot of the material I already knew. Quizzes are not timed except the final. I found the final project annoying but nothing too difficult. Professor Blaise is cool she always helped

This teach is TERRIBLE. The lessons don't teach you anything, and when I asked for her help on an assignment her reply was "I would highly recommend getting a tutor".  Really?? She also grades terribly. Your assignment can be 90% perfect, but if you mess up on two things, she'll give you a 60% if you're LUCKY. I would NEVER take her class again.

I was going to write a post about my experience w this teacher but I only have 350 chara, NOT ENOUGH! Overall this teacher doesn't really help you she just gives you the material & basically thinks "here. now do it!" When I asked her what's wrong w my assignments, she would write back in an email, "could not grade it, doesn't meet the requirement

Public speaking with her was good. Despite her reputation as director of title ix, she is a solid prof who really does care about her students and will go the extra mile for them. I didnt learn very much but I got some good experience.
Was an easy public speaking class even if you put in half the work can still pass with a decent grade. Sometimes you get out early and almost every time you pick your topics you want tp speak on.
A great professor and great course. Easy course if you take it seriously.
A great course, and positive professor. She is very passionate, and open-minded.
She is an Amazing professor, I took GWS 104 and GWS 345 both classes are so much fun and you learn so much from them. She inspired me to Minor in GWS

Butterfly is the only teacher at Plattsburgh that actually gives a crap about your well being. Of course the other teachers in the GWS department do, but Butterfly is the only one that will make sure you're okay.

Very good professor, I enjoyed the discussions in the classroom. If you participate and read your book, there is no way you won't succeed. I will take one of his class again . Be on time and read the book .

At first due to alot of cancled classes due to weather the first test was hard. Then he gave the class a chance to have a clean slate and gave a study guide for the midterm. It helps me a ton. I had to retake soc this is so much better since the questions are bazar. class time is manyly discutions, granted early morining talks are hard. Be on time!
Enjoyed professor Blaise class. He had everyone participate into groups which I Liked so everyone participated and had different theories

This class was easy.  You didn't have homework and he gave you the questions that were on the test/quizzes.  He likes to pick on people in class. I didn't really enjoy the class, it didn't interest me.
Very good professor, really helpful. Easy going if you participate and show interest in the class, very funny professor.
Go to class and participate and you will succeed. Put effort into this class and you can do very well. Great professor and very approachable.

I always wanted to learn ASL growing up, but I had no idea I would ever want to make a career of it. I have Mr. Blais to thank for that. Of course, this isnt a class you can just skate through, youre learning a new language! But Mr. Blais makes the difficulty of learning that language fun through his teaching, and I am so grateful for that.

He has inspired me to become an interpreter, even though I wanted to be something else before. But, that not what you care about. I just want to say that having him as a professor is fun, exciting, and very hilarious. I would take his class again without a second thought. Just make sure to review & do book questions!

Bill is an absolute joy to learn from. He is very passionate about ASL and tries his best to get students involved in the deaf community by integrating the culture into the regular vocab and quizzes of the class. Homework is a must and practicing finger-spelling will save you in the long-run.

I had Blaise for ASL 1 & 2. I've meet students from other classes who didn't learn half us much as we did. He really cares about his students and really sets you up for success. Blaise is passionate about teaching and it shows. I hope he will teach ASL 3 soon as well.
Incredibly fair and perceptive!
Not the easiest, but given that the subject matter is very complex I think he certainly helps students reach their full potential in the subject.
If you show up and study, you'll be fine. As for his personality, I found him to be one of the most caring professors I've had in college. Helpful outlook.
Always reasonable with work and incredible for students who do better when the professor gives regular heads-ups on assignments and essays. He's also amazing at helping revise essays.
Excellent resource, really glad with his class. It's what you make of it, and he really appreciates creativity and boundary-pushing in projects.

Like any professor, your experience with Dr. Blaise has everything to do with how much you're willing to dive into classwork and the concepts he discusses - if you actually make an effort, he sees that & rewards it. Definitely a brilliant leader in neuroscience at the college. Also, he's great at offering research positions to stand-out students!

He's passionate about engineering and neuroscience. This class was taken during COVID-19, so it was hybrid. He makes the content interesting, but the quizzes can be tough. The quizzes were 60% of our grade, so you could get screwed over if you don't get them right. Overall good class and great professor. GPA booster if you're motivated.

Professor Blaise's class should be relatively easy, but he always makes it difficult to get an A by adding in random questions on quizzes and tests that he barely mentioned in the lectures. Overall the quizzes and tests are simple. Just know everything on the slides.

I absolutely loved him! While the powerpoint presentations are very simple (on the verge of boring), he was very clear on quizzes and exams. If you go to the class and learn the power point slides, you will do amazing in the class. He is always free outside of class, and he goes off on some of the cutest tangents. A little monotonous, but worth it

I'm only not swearing because it says it will be deleted if i do. This guy didn't care about me and made the class incredibly boring and ineffective. The seminars are supposed to be a fun way to learn how to write, he made it drag on and would often mess up pronunciations and words so he would say the opposite of what he meant. avoid at all costs.

Blaise was terrible. Once upon a time he knew what he was talking about when he wrote his lecture powerpoints, which was probably about ten years ago. However, he only looks at them once a year which is in the lecture he is using them for. Completely unreliable for questions and can also be an unfair grader. Can't believe he has tenure.

Had him for Neural Engineering, a class I was thrilled to be taking but he absolutely ruined it. He simply reads off ancient powerpoints (often with patently false information) and his exam questions come out of left field. Avoid at all costs.

Guy makes the mentor do all the correcting and editing, then throws a grade on the paper based on your personality, gender and his current mood.  Tell you what he really doesn't like male athletes who speak their mind.

Was in his seminar class, Decade of the Brain. It was supposed to teach us how to go through the college process, how to write college level papers, etc. He expected college level papers before teach us how to write such, he graded very harshly and gave us more homework than all of my other classes combined. Made my 1st semester of college hell.
Very helpful prof, cares about students

A great guy, just not a great teacher.  Kind of schizophrenic grader: sometimes he'll throw out good grades, sometimes he'll grade very harshly.  Makes a lot of mistakes during class.  Smart man, but has some difficulty thinking on his feet if the class wanders away from his pre-planned lectures.
I had the worst experience ever with this professor. He doesn't know his stuff and isn't helpful at all. I recommend avoiding him and his classes.
helpful but he is terrible as a teacher. exams are easy though
This professor is terrible. He seems to have little to knowledge of the subject he is teaching, as he was never any help if I did not understand some of the subject matter.
Prof. Blaise is absolutely the best.  His seminar,  Beyond the Decade of the Brain  has convinced me to beomce a neuroscientist... I highly reccomend him for future classses.
Hes fine. Thats all.
Joel is one of the better teachers at Antioch.  He is intuitive and one of the few instructors with enough ego strength to handle a student who questions him.  I would take a class from him anytime.
He was extremely critical of the students who needed letter grades for the future PsyD.  He was condescending to them.  Very smug attitude.  Seemed like he didn't want to be in the class.
He really made a trauma class interesting.  He is pretty funny, too.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. From other students, all the other tech profs are EXTREMELY difficult. There are absolutely NO papers in this class. You make brochures, and fact sheets, and business letters. EVERYTHING is done in groups. Pretty lenient on letting you turn in things late. Take of points after 2 absences.

Take this professor. From what I have heard, all the other tech writing teachers are extremely difficult. There are ZERO papers in this class. If you just follow directions, you should make at least a B. Almost everything is done in groups. She is pretty lenient on letting you turn in things late. After 2 unexcused absences, she takes off points.

Very nice and enthusiastic about the subject (Linguistics). Class was pretty easy, a good portion of it spent on phonetics which I found easy as eating pie. I'd say the only downfall to the class was it was a bit boring, but if you need to take Linguistics and want an A I would certainly recommend her. ...Given that you at least give some effort.

This professor makes about 80% of the class group work, which I didn't like. Granted she did have you do a peer evaluation at the end of each project, but I didn't enjoy having to be liable for 3 other people pulling their own weight. We used the book maybe 4 times. She takes attendance every class. Easy to talk to and understanding.

I struggled with this class, not because of the work, because of the professor. The work is okay, it is all group work. She is difficult at times and annoying. She is knowledgeable and the assignments are clear. It is an okay class with her, nothing great.

Coming from an Anthropological background, i found the class to be dull and redundant. A lot of the students in the class seemed to struggle with the material even though she is very clear and easy to understand, in my opinion. Attendance is mandatory and if you want to pass her linguistics class you need to study. Overall good professor.

Her final exam requirements are a bit outrageous in my mind.  A comprehensive final is a bit much for anyone who is employed, takes more than 2 classes, or has children.   I would not take her again had I known about her final and attendance policies prior to registering.  Her attendance policies penalties deduct % from your final grade.
Professor Andres was great, and got me through Bio 226. I think some of these other reviewers literally just have never encountered anyone with a mild accent before.

Professor Andres goes extremely fast through lectures. I went into the course not liking genetics at all and I came out disliking the subject even more. You need to go to class because his posted lectures contain little to no notes besides textbook diagrams. Small amount of math involved but the concepts and definitions are what is difficult.

Jose does his best to explain himself and gives opportunities for questions. My frustration with this class can be attributed to my own lack of preparation. If I kept up with the readings I would have taken much more from the lectures. He wrote on the chalkboard for examples which were very hard to see. His lectures aren't sufficient to do well.

Dr Andres gets a hard time but he is a really smart prof and really helpful when you go to his lab to ask him stuff. Difficult course but smart guy. Prof Andres is a bit of geek and really into evolution so if you're into evolution theory and stuff then this is your course. Great and fun class to take. Never a dull moment with Professor Andres.

Dr. Andres is pretty great but the course itself needs some changing. You have to do a 2 hour presentation on a research paper (alone), every week you have to write a 700 word summary on the presentation that was presented the week prior by another student & you MUST participate in class for 10 points  those make a big difference in your grade.

He offers simultaneous Webex and uploads to his in-person classes, so you don't have to go to class. Immunology might be one of the hardest undergraduate classes and covers an insane amount of material (entire Kuby's immunology book) in 4 weeks. At the end of the class, you get to read actual papers, which was very cool. Good luck!

He will answer any question you have, no matter how dumb it is. His study guides are great; if you can answer every practice question on his study guide you will get an A in his class, but be prepared to dedicate about 5 - 7 hours a day (summer term). The book is very good (pdf is free), even though it's not required, it has very good explanations

I took him over the summer, and his class is definitely not something you can breeze through. His lectures aren't the most interactive, but they're super interesting. I learned so much in this class. If you genuinely take the time to study the material, you'll do fine! Also, his extra credit is insanely helpful, don't take it for granted!

Andres is a great professor. While he is monotone, youll learn a lot with him! Took him for immunology over summer and i loved it! Graded by 4 exams (final not cumulative) and some extra credit. Take him!! Youll learn a ton! Materials for exams can be found on lecture slides-- better to go to him with questions than the book... its useless. FUN!

Content was dense, but the questions on the exam were fair. He was also pretty lenient on free responses too. Use the slides and you should be fine (I didnt use the study guide or book). Averages for the exams were around 70-76% and there are some opportunities for E.C. via optional quizzes (was enough to bump up peoples grades by 2%). Take him!

This was a challenging but informative class. Despite what others say, the textbook is very, very helpful. Myself and my three friends who used the textbook received As. My friends that did not use it mostly did not do as well. Take your time when taking his exams, he will often give big hints like using the word ribosome in a transcription q.

Dr. Andres is the best! By far the best option for genetics. A tough class overall due to the material being so dense but he is a very fair instructor. The exams are lecture based so the textbook is not really necessary. Discussion is very beneficial in clarifying concepts and can help your grade a lot. Offers extra credit for attending class.

Andres is a wonderful professor. The content itself is difficult & dense, BUT it's manageable. I recommend recording lecture & going back to it later because the slides themselves sometimes dont make sense & his explanations from class do wonders. If you do that, you won't really need to look at the textbook. Attend class and get extra credit hehe

Andres is a great guy, he knows what he's talking about, and he's willing to answer any questions in his office, if you also have an idea of what you're talking about. His class is 3 multiple choice exams&1 cumulative final (MC &short answer), and the discussion class is 30% of your grade. He does not curve, but a ton of extra credit for attendance

andres knows genetics extremely well, but his tests are very hard. obviously you need to understand the material, but you basically need to memorize every bullet point in the powerpoints to do well. his test averages were very low and there's no curve. the material is very dry and can get confusing but the discussion book helps a lot

Dr. Andres is a great instructor. He made the class as clear and succinct as possible but the subject matter is dense especially if taken during the summer. Study the slides very well and use the textbook if extra explanation is needed but the powerpoints should be good enough. This class is difficult so be prepared to study a lot.

You have to truly understand Immunology to get a good grade in his class. The material is dense, although the tests mostly focus on the bigger picture. The 2nd half of class was fun - you get to read scientific articles & actually understand them thanks to his lectures.

There is a lot of material to grasp, but it is doable. It requires so much time to prepare yourself for his tests. He even told me that he creates the tests based off the PowerPoints without the need of a textbook. His tests are his PowerPoints so study that. Discussion helps greatly in clarifying concepts so don't skip and do well on quizzes.

Course covers an obscene amount of material. He knows his stuff, though he's not the most interesting character in lectures.  Slides are sufficient for learning the material; he's usually able to explain the concepts well enough that you shouldn't need to crack open your textbook.

Dr. Andres is a great professor. He's very knowledgeable about genetics and his tests are taken directly from his lectures so study those really well. Make use of discussion as it helps clarify concepts. Make sure you try to actively learn the material too since it could be a really dry subject sometimes. Also he gives extra credit so go to class!

Dr. Andres is actually a really good professor if you use the class to its full potential. To do well, pay attention in lecture and record them, and then go home and listen to the lectures over again and take notes. When tests roll around, make sure you know the concepts on the study guides, and you should be good to go.

His tests come literally word for word from the powerpoint. He also provides extremely detailed study guides. It's important to come to class because an attendance sheet is passed around. Genetics can be a bit of a dry subject but Andres tries his best to make it interesting. Tests are 50 questions long and very detailed, but completely doable.

Good professor, with that said do not choose straight letters when you get to vote. It's a lie that if you are borderline the prof. will bump you up. It holds true with other professors in Bio 304. Tip #2:  The exams are nationally standardized, so go out there and find test banks. Exams are worded to trick you (Ex. Which one is most FALSE?)

AMAZING professor. Very organized lectures, PowerPoints have everything you need (I didn't touch the book). Extra credit available, exams are medium/difficult, but fair. Go to discussion/do well on quizzes to solidify topics. If you study enough, you should have no problem getting a good grade. Ended up really enjoying this class!

Immunology is VERY DENSE but interesting. Dr. Andres explains the concepts really well. He gives out 3 exams and a non cumulative final (format is same for all exams -- MC, short responses, and matching). Go to his office hours because he's always willing to help. Record his lectures and study the ppts. Excited to take him for Genetics next sem!!!

professor andres was great. His tests are based on lectures, so no surprises there. The exams are dense. I learned a lot from this professor, I should've waited and taken 304 with him! He is awesome take him.

Dr. Andres is one of the best professors at UNLV.  For the graduate level class, we had to give a lecture on a chapter and paper of our choosing and take short response exams.  Altogether, this class is highly informative, intriguing, and beneficial to my future career in science.  I highly recommend taking immunology with him!

Dr. Andres is awesome! He gives out lengthy study guides for all of his tests which is extremely helpful because the material on the exams is DENSE. He wants everyone to pass. This became one of my favorite classes and learned a ton.

He's wonderful and brilliant! Do well on the discussions! They'll prepare you for the exam and help your grade! Also, go to class and do the iclicker questions for the EC. It helps so much when you're on the borderline! Final was really easy and the short answer was truly big picture. Class material is very interesting and he showed documentaries:)

This class is not difficult if you study correctly and take advantage of discussion. He's straightforward with what he wants you to know. DO THE STUDY GUIDES. They are the exams. Tests are beastly 50 short answer. I am glad he isn't teaching this again. I miss Nika.

The class material is extremely dry, but Dr. Andres always did his best at trying to make the material relevant. Had him for 304 and again for 453. For 453, his tests are LONG, since they consist of 50 short answer questions. He's a great lecturer for teaching immunology and the material is beyond fair and really quite interesting. It didn't come down to my mastery of the material rather than how fast can you write legibly

He is a great professor! I don't know why some people complained about him. He clarifies anything that is not understood. The study guides he provides are extremely helpful. The lab is worth a large chunk of your grade and is very easy. iClicker points also help. Study hard and you will do great!

This is my third class with Andres and I loved how different this one was. I was so interested in this class. The papers can be rough but after you go through them they are not so bad. This class gets you ready for graduate level learning whether it be med school, PhD, or whatever. The papers are very advanced and require you to independently dive in. The final paper was a beast so definitely plan ahead. Don't let subpar exam grades discourage you b/c he let's you make it up in other areas. Not an easy class but it's enjoyable.

Easily one of the best, most interesting classes I took at UNLV.  Prof. Andres puts a lot of time and research into the lectures. Do the reading and go to office hours if you need help.  Prof. Andres one of the best instructors at UNLV.

I wish all biology classes were structured like this. Here's the equation for success: go to class, use your iclicker, take notes from the powerpoint, study for discussion, and study for exams. One of the best professors i've had at UNLV. He is very helpful, exams are based off of the powerpoints, gives i-cklicker extra credit, the discussions help alot since you get to see the material more than once. Getting an A is very attainable if you put in a little effort. All in all really good professor i highly recommend him!

Great teacher. Very clear and organized. Some funny moments, but class was usually boring. Book is useless. I highly recommend this teacher. Study his powerpoints and you will ace the tests.  He drops 1 test and gives extra credit. This class is pretty simple, test every 6 lectures and he offers many opportunities for extra credit. Study the notes and an A is attainable.

everyone giving a bad rating to Dr. Andres did NOT study. if you STUDY his notes, it's so easy to get an A. Lazyness can't be tolerated if you want an A. you do need to refer to the book on pictures only, or for some clarity, but 95% of exam is straight from notes. i defnitely recommed him!

Though his lectures may be boring, he is clear and precise. He has a good sense of humor and is willing to help students out if they seek his help. Go to every class because clicker questions will help you out in the long run. Tests are a bit hard but not impossible. Study his powerpoint notes!

Go to class almost all of test questions on his power point and he puts out studdy guides which can be time consuming but very worth it. Very interesting yet very hard. Don't need book.

Dr. Andres is the best biology teacher at UNLV. He has extensive background in the field and deserves to teach at a much more revered institution - those who don't agree probably don't really enjoy biology!

Andres is great, his tests are right from his notes! He is super nice and helpful. The only downside is the iClicker, which is so stupid - everybody hates it and it is a waste of class time. Good teacher; he's helpful if you need him. i took it as an audit course... Tests are pretty hard, but doable... Lab is very important and will help you a lot. He's a pretty mellow guys, but sometimes shows humor in class...
its a tough class for sure but its do-able if you do all the reading and actually take the time to really study.  andres is a good teacher. explains things well.

German 101 was so much fun with Hommel!  She is incredibly helpful and encouraging.

Hommel is an amazing professor. I had her for an INQS, and it was honestly my favorite class of the semester. She is ALWAYS willing to help you out, and will go out of her way to make sure you understand the material. She also has a cheeky sense of humor, which makes class enjoyable.

Professor Hommel is an awesome professor. She is kind, always looking to make sure she can help us, and genuinely cares for us. She is my favorite professor at Linfield.

She is one of the best professors I have had at Linfield. Highly recommended.

She brings a lot to class, always willing to help people out and is great at catering to everyone on different levels. As with most language classes, it's hard to know where you stand throughout the course, but she's always willing to help.

Prof Frank was extremely knowledgeable on each subject in class. She was always willing to help, always had a smile on her face and it was obvious she cares about her students education. Professor Gudrun is one of the most helpful professors I have ever had. Something's wrong if you don't love Brisa. Sweetest professor at Cornell.

Amazing professor. SPAN 1120 was my first language class in college and I was very apprehensive going into it because my knowledge of Spanish was very rusty. Amazing teacher very clear grader one of the nicest profs I've ever had!
Great

Excellent!!! Truly cares about the student's improvement. Always offers helpful feedback and answers all questions. Clarifies any uncertainties about readings. Overall truly taught me so much amazing things and made Spanish so much fun!

Wow.... amazing woman.  I want to talk about her ability as a professor, but I can't help it--- I have such a crush on her!  Se encanto---       wonderful class, very serious about her work, very caring and encouraging.  Great TAs too in discussion groups--

She is awesome. She is funny and interesting, and her class was consistent and challenging in a good way. I learned a lot from her! She is young and relatable and is clearly on the side of the students. Loved this class!
Brisa is awesome, and the class is a lot of work but fun
really energetic, class was pretty easy. TAs were usually lenient.
Great teacher.
Great professor!

nice person and very energetic and tries to help. crazy about grammar. sometimes idk what she was taking points off for. is not forgiving if you don't have oral presentations perfect. make sure you participate a lot in class

this teacher has a very strong romanian Accent its very hard to understand what he says and he gets mad when you ask questions, i do not recommend this teacher if your the type that asks questions because he will put you in the spotlight if you do.

Great teacher make it an easy class!  Easy A.  This was a refresher course for me as I am a returning student.  He is very helpful and he explains everything three different ways.  Tests are easy and concise.  Take this class!

Mitch was a great professor! I took him during spring 2010! Because of his class and his help I got the basics of Biology and how to study! Now I got my degree and got into medical school!! Thank you Mitch

Really cool professor. Hard class but coming to class and paying attention is a must to pass. He also gives you the lecture power points. He also had pretty good jokes.Overall really pleasant person and willing to help when asked.

Prof. Osborne looks out for her students and ensures that they actually learn instead of worrying about grades all the time. A lot of homework is given, but it helps you pick up the language quickly. Make sure to study for tests and practice for presentations.

One of the best professors at Cornell, in comparison to other language classes and professors, she is amazing and cares about you. I would definitely recommend it. Do your homework on time, study for the tests and essays and you will be fine.

Ms Priya is a nice and interesting teacher. in the class, she speak the content with some joke.
