Dr. Foy is amazing! She is the sweetest person I have ever met! She is extremely smart and I learned a ton from her class. She is also really really helpful. Just talk to her and she will help you with anything, even if it doesn't relate to the class. Definitely take her class!

Dr.Foy is the smartest person I have ever met.  I  have taken three courses with her, and I learn more in fifteen minutes in her class than I do in any other class on campus.  She is not only knowledgeable and intuitive in her own area of research, but she knows all about ancient Greek literature a from the past to the present. Fantastic person too

Dr. Foy was definitely the best professor of my first semester! She is sweet, funny, entertaining, and a really great professor.  Her class isn't easy but she really wants everyone to do well and gives you lots of feedback on your papers. Show up to class, write your papers, and she will love you!

She's kind of crazy, but in a way that you can't help but love her. When she returns a paper, there will always be long comments and edits throughout - which is great! With Dr. Foy you know where you stand and she will improve your ability to write papers effectively. Not so much difficult, but it is time and work intensive. Try her class out!

While the subject is not particularly interesting, if you have to take this class, she is the best professor for it.  She is extremely energetic and excited about the subject.  She works very hard to get you excited and to help you if you are struggling in any way. Your writing, or at least your editing skills will improve because of her.
Rfoy 1 is the coolest person ever!Beware of the raisins!

Dr. Foy is great. VERY helpful and sincerely cares about her students. Great stories. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS, it helps a ton. She expects a lot, and a LOT of Progression in your writing. Hones your writing no matter how bad or good you think you may be. Take her class if possible.

Dr Foy is an awesome teacher with a great personality! We had ten 1-2 page papers (easy) and two 5 page papers and one 8 page paper (final). Attendance is mandatory, but you can miss up to 3 classes. She is always willing to help you and wants you to do well in her class.

Hands down the best professor ever.  She is smart, broadly educated, interesting, fair, helpful and fascinating in the classroom.  I'd recommend that everyone experience Dr. Foy at least once before leaving Tulane.  Knows her stuff and knows how to get it across. Love her and the class.

AMAZING!!  She is SO helpful and will go OUT of her way to help you.  Attendance is important, but due dates are Extremely flexible!!  She's very outgoing and made me want to go to class.  She kept me awake and interested during her 9:00 class!!  A definite must take professor!!
Hard grader and goes off an a tangent and talks waaaay to much.
My first and favorite class. I changed my major to English after having her. English is not my native language,but she helped me and I have kept a 4.0 since.
Dr. Foy is my favorite professor!

Dr. Foy is the greatest professor that I have ever had. I have never left her class without being amazed and ready to go back for more.  If you want to see the true greatness of academia, take one of her classes. She is also the most hilarious professor ever!

Dr. Foy is one of the best professors I have had at Tulane.  She was very challenging at times but believes in you. She sets a standard that she expects you to meet and she is willing to help ALL of her students meet that standard. Tough reading that you have to do at the same time you have to write other papers. This class helps for other classes.
Fascinating discussions, esp. for an 8 am class
Tough grader, but it will only help you become a better writer. She wants her students to do well. She likes to talk a lot and is overall a very good professor.

She is NOT a hard professor!!! A lot of people say she's a hard grader, but I got a high A on  everything without a problem. She DOES grade really difficultly on tests, but she spreads the grading out knowing some people don't do well on them... I would rec. her classes to anyone... interesting and energetic prof!

Hard grader but will help you if you go see her during office hours. She will help you rewrite parts. Allows 1 rewrite per sem. 3 5 page essays (one on the movie mystic river) and a 10 page resarch paper on a topic of your choice. Foy is not easy but will help you become a better writer.
she talks a lot about unimportant things and grades pretty hard on tests.  she was energetic though and kept class interesting for the most part.
she grades really hard
No Comments

She is an EXTREMELY tough grader, she looks for exactly what she wants, no less.  She will help you out if you get a bad grade and give you a chance to rewrite the paper.  Only take her class if you KNOW you are an extremely talented writer

Foy was a very involved professor.  I agree strongly that she is a picky grader, but gives you plenty of chances for rewrites, and most of the time will practically rewrite the mistakes for you. You will be a better writer after her class.
She spends most of the class talkin 500 miles and hour about some tangent topic that none of us care about.  Also, she grades soo hard, no one ever gets an A on their papers, don't take her class.

This woman is the most picky grader i have ever encountered.  I would not suggest that anyone take an english class from her.  She generally says one thing and does another; she didn't even attempt to follow the syllibus.
She was very funny, had really engaging lectures, and the quizzes werent too hard if you studied for them!

Faults: her lectures are word for word the same exact thing as the textbook. I loved this class, and everything about it. I did not like her quizes, took her from a great professor to an awful one. Quizzes were impossible and she was not willing to help students on them. I had a 97 average on exams and 65 on the quizzes. drop the quizzes chavda

Grading is way too difficult for an introductory class and expectations unrealistic.  I generally get all A's some B's and I am failing this class.  Never posts things online when she says she is going too, AVOID her classes at all costs.

Totally unreasonable professor. Very rude to students and interrupts constantly. Expects too much for an introductory class. Impossible quizzes. Will hear what you are saying but won't actually listen.
Unfair. terrible teacher, makes quizzes that everyone fails, has incredibly boring lectures.  Also demeans students in class.

awfulawfulawfulawful. Terrible teacher and basically human being when dealing with her students. She is not fair in any way for a class that has an easy topic.  Basically easy topic and interesting class but automatic fail for a grade. In a class of 80 people where the majority is failing.
I agree with the previous post. She is rude and demeaning to students and sucks as a teacher! Avoid this one if you can!

This professor is very unorganized.  She does not cover all items on the syllabus. She changes items on the syllabus for her convenience.  She is rude and demeaning to students.  I learned more from the textbook than this professor.  I got the feeling that this professor is more interested in performing research than teaching.

Great teacher. I don't know what some people are talking about but she was never rude and she really gives us the opportunity for class discussion. Her quizzes are easy if you even have a general knowledge of government. If not just read the chapters. Exams are writing intensive but easy.

Hard Professor. If you are looking for an easy gen ed. dont take thisss. ALOT of reading, and pop quizzes. Exams are writing intentive. usually 10 short answers and 2 long essays. She is always late and never organized. I got an A, but didnt enjoy the class or professor at all.

A rebuttle to the person who said that shes the worst professor ever: She was never rude, the exams are easy IF you read the chapter and take notes before each class. I dont think thats too much to ask for from a COLLEGE student. Also of the questions on the exam are given to us beforehand and the answers are EASILY found in the book. Great Teacher
She really encourages students to participate in class.  She is engaging and is willing to meet with her students after class.

She is the worst professor ever. Yes she tries to be funny sometimes but she soo rude.She talks down to her students and isnt very open to  others opinions. Her exams are EXTREMELY hard. writing intensive.she excepts wayyy to much for a 400 level class. I would NOT take a class with her if you have the choice.
She a wonderful person, however she needs a personal assistant.  Often, she was late for her own deadlines.  The amount of information that she expected the class to master was beyond reasonable.

Shes very enthusiastic about teaching american government, sometimes even funny. She engages the class in discussing and makes the class interesting. If you read the assigned chapter before every class, you will do fine. Exams are completely out of the book. Studying for them can be mildly time consuming but the info isn't difficult to understand.

Great professor with a clear knowledge of and passion for her subject.  Emphasis on current events and how they relate to the subject matter makes the class much more interesting, as long as you are aware of what's going on in the world.  She is also open to suggestions from students on ways to improve the class-if you have a problem just tell her!

Brad is the professor I recommend to anyone needing to take an FWS. He is an amazing storyteller and seems to know so much about everything! He was pretty flexible with deadlines especially if you have a lot going on. He is always available for office hours and will work around your schedule, so take advantage of that. Your grade will thank you!!

Brad always knows what's going on and allows rewrites for almost all the papers. Unlike other writing professors, he is not only good at writing but also knows physics and math, has easy grading, and is the best professor

One of the best prof at Cornell. Write whatever ideas that into your brain, Brad is always neutral and will be 100% respectful to them, and he likes us to come up with 'special ideas'. Great and deep lectures, great and deep feedback on the paper. You will have revision chances for each paper, and you can show him the draft for each paper.

If you just wanna gain a S grade in FWS , this course is your best choice. Pro. Brad put the whole grading and workload pretty little and the estimated time spending per week is 5 hrs or less. But he is willing to listen to your advice and if you want to dive in deep topics, you can still talk with him in person.

It was a really hard class for me, but Professor Ramshaw was very helpful and accommodating through the entire semester. I scored around the median for every assignment and exam and still somehow ended with an A? I would strongly recommend this Professor though, super chill guy.

What a caring man. Caters and accommodates to all your needs and then some. Responds well to pranks, has watched Friends, just an overall God. You can ask the same question thrice and he'll patiently answer it in clear, detailed prose. I have nothing but the highest level of respect for this man.
hes rude and arrogant, youll learn, but youll be dealing with a condescending guy with no tact or ability to see outside his own ego
His notes are very clear and organized. The homeworks tend to be very tedious and annoying, you must go to office hours to fish out how to do the problems from the TAs. Prelims were very challenging.
Amazing professor. Very organized, gives difficult problem sets and prelims but you actually feel like you learn. This guy is a genius.
Very well-organized and interested in his students.
He's pretty good at throwing darts...Can hit a bullseye without even looking...
very well organized. Above comments are false, never taught fluids. Commments apply to Prof. Archer.

Dr. Brown's Comparative Nutrition class has been my favorite at Cornell so far.  The lectures are entertaining and informative and the labs are fun in the typical Animal Science way.  There is no textbook but rather handouts to read.  Tests are mostly take-home.
He is nice and fair.  However, his lectures tend to get a little dry.  Also, don't buy the textbook.  You will never use it, and it does not relate to the course at all.

He is very easygoing, friendly, and helpful.  His class is pretty easy as long as you keep up with assignments and pay attention once in a while.  He can be rather boring, and his jokes aren't exactly hilarious, but he's extremely knowledgeable, passionate, and approchable.

The fact that he has the same name as the author of the Da Vinci Code is probably the only entertaining thing about his lectures...except when he attempts jokes. Then we don't laugh WITH him, but AT his sense of humor in general and the fact that he can keep a straight face when discussing camel sex.
No Comments
This guy really knows his stuff!  Great class!!
A fun, hands-on introduction to animal care, including lots at field trips.  Prof. Brown is a real sweetie!

Everything that would be done in the class was dictated in the syllabus. Quizzes were exactly what was described they would be leading up to them. The class itself was extremely engaging with a lot of guest speakers. Attendance is not mandatory, but it is highly recommended not to lose pace.

Scheduling office hours with her is basically impossible. She'll respond to your request, but never actually confirms the meeting. She also doesn't give any slides. Her TA office hours were always packed b/c we all knew we needed to be there to understand anything happening in the class.
one of the best professors ever. She expects you to care, as you should.

Professor LeClercq is incredible! Very committed to her students, willing to offer professional and academic help outside the classroom. The course itself is very practical. Be prepared to do all readings and watch videos to engage in the classes. Her grading is tough but fair. You stand to learn a lot from her and the course!

Clear and engaging lectures. Grading in the class was tough but fair. Her exams in labor law are demanding but open note. The class requires you invest a good amount of time, attend lecture or watch all the recorded lectures (attendance is not mandatory). Not easy but you learn a lot and she does curve. The class average is usually around a B/B+.

Generally, I would only recommend to take this if you already had some tennis experience beforehand (at least JV ish level). Pretty chill guy, actually found out that he knew some of the kids who played tennis back home. Class is a little bit of a workout (definitely kept me in shape haha). Overall, definitely recommend.
I actually got better at tennis during his class, but he did extend the class to like a week after the end was supposed to be rather than just canceling classes due to inclement weather.

Well all of the previous comments certainly scream sarcasm...  For an "advanced" class, this was pretty much a joke.  We stood around and hit down the line or cross-court nearly the whole time, before playing some useless game.  Arthur is...interesting...and knows his stuff, but his own strokes are sort of odd so his examples can be kind of off...

Arthur Arthur he's the man...if he can't get low, no one can. Arthur's brilliance in taking the sport of tennis and innovating it into exciting and fun minigames (including the one where he feeds you the ball and you play the point out from the baseline)...he should win the Nobel Prize for smart people... ehh where's my curry?!

This class, most simply put, is MONDO.  Arthur is great, and as Paris Hilton would say...That's Hot.  The intermediate tennis class was an experience of a lifetime.I am ready for the advanced class, and I can hardly wait ... loves it!  Take this course for a good time ... Have fun!!

Arthur is the MAN! As long as you love to play tennis, and you don't mind "GETTIN LOW" for shots you're going to have fun in this class. Must take...highly recommended.  You can do pretty much whatever you want, and you play this cool game all the time where he feeds you the ball, and you play doubles from the base line.  THIS GAME IS GREAT!!!
Probably the greatest person I ever met

Arthur Ovaska is one of the most thoughtful and dedicated design professors at Cornell. His enthusiasm for Architecture is contagious. Years later I can still hear his voice encouraging us to really LOOK at the world around us.
He's the greatest professor that ever lived.

He can sniff out chow-worthy Huevos Rancheros from 120 miles away. And if you are reading these reviews thinking you'll learn something about the profs, do the alumnus a favor and go enroll in another school. Cheers.
experienced, great listener, helfpful feedback, good studio professor overall.
Amazing professor. Best I've ever had.
He just sits there and scares students...
Very laid back and understanding. He was willing to work around our studio class and was very approachable.
Very easy going for drawing and allowed flexibility on work based on how much would be required for design. Easy to talk to and understanding. He made the class interesting.
No Comments

Very smart guy, but inconsistent--could be inspiring but seems distracted or remote some of the time, and other times is dead "on"...More of an artist than a teacher--not enough communication, you're not sure where you stand or what his stand is
So so. Talented but inconsistent prof. Doesn't communicate as well as he could. Creative ideas, but passive-agressive personality makes it hard to approach him

Professor D was great. The online part of the class was convenient and the lectures were very engaging. If you have any background in any physics this class will likely be way too intro level for you, but sometimes you're looking for that easy class. 5 tests felt like a lot but you end up dropping one. Material is a bit random at times but is easy.

Dr. D is a good professor all around. He is really kind and wants his students to succeed. If you need help, he will help, and his behavior will never dissuade you from going to lectures. My only issue is that the lectures were sometimes pretty confusing and required extra studying.
Oh, and there are 5 tests.  Luckily you can drop one.
Overall a manageable and comfortably paced course in thermodynamics. Course consists of quasi-weekly problem sets and two prelims which were fair.
can be disorganized on the lecture materials but otherwise cares about the class and the students.

Dr D had Interesting lectures and was knowledgeable about the subject but it was hard to go back and follow lectures without rewatching them as PowerPoint/class posted notes weren't stellar on their own. Homework and climate math (quantitative quizzes) were manageable, plus no exams during covid semester, only weekly multiple-choice quizzes w drops

My favorite professor so far! Lectures were super clear and he was very encouraging and helpful to everyone in the class. He didn't have specific office hours but was really easy to schedule a meeting with outside class. Definitely make sure to pay attention in class because he may call on you to answer a question & you'll do better on the homework

Taken online. The lecture slides are confusing but the prof does a good job explaining them. Grading was very lenient and based on weekly quizzes, take-home quizzes, and simple assignments. Not sure if he will go back to tests once online is over instead of the weekly quizzes. Take this class if you're interesting in scientific climate change stuff

A very animated and passionate lecturer - you can tell he cares about the subject. He also genuinely wants students to succeed and always answers questions. Prelims are pretty straightforward and similar to class examples, and he gives good study guides.

One of my favorite professors at Cornell. The course is challenging, but interesting. Professor DeGaetano will make you work for your grade. Great course, attendance is key; he says things in lecture that you will be tested on and they are not in the lecture notes/slides.

This was the worst class I have taken here and I did not learn anything at all the entire year. The class was boring and the prof unhelpful. Also none of the assignments were clear and the readings were dumb.

One of the best lecturers at Cornell. The class requires discipline since the homeworks aren't mandatory, they're just prep for the tests. Our final grade was fully determined by 3 exams, but they were fairly easy. The questions were almost all extremely similar to the problem sets.

Lecture is good but the tests are stupid since they test how well you can do hand simulation of network algorithms instead of your understanding of network architecture. Homework solutions sometimes riddled with mistakes. Overall the light workload compensates for most of its faults.

Really nice guy and definitely will make time and exert the effort to help you. But... in lecture, he came across kind of snarky. Curses a lot. But simultaneously demands a lot of respect. Explains things relatively well. Almost all homeworks are required to be done in groups (of 3+, I think?). Which is actually nice, in a way.
Loved him while taking OS. Really cared about students' learning and their experience.

I took this class and dropped it half way. The material is interesting but he's a nightmare to deal with. Every problem in the class was always someone else's fault, never his. Seems pretty full of himself. Won't be taking a class he teaches again.

Rachit was an amazing professor. He taught the course as one long story about how and why the internet came to be designed the way that it is. This class was not really about the specific implementations of protocols, but it focused much more on what problems the protocols try to address and how to design future ones. Take this class !!!

Prof Agarwal is by far the best CS lecturer I've had. He breaks down complicated concepts in an easily accessible way and makes it his personal mission to ensure his students are confident and happy with the material. I'm a pretty apathetic student overall but his lectures made me rly excited about networks. Def recommend, he goes above and beyond!

Amazing engaging lecturer. Really cares about the topic and makes it very interesting. Great low stress course. Optional Homeworks/Projects. Only graded items are exams, which are really fair. Cannot recommend this course enough.

Every good rating in 4450 was done during the pandemic where 50% of their grade was a course eval. In normal times, your entire grade is based on exams, which are horribly written. He gives you ZERO prep for exams and the psets he does give have no relevance to the exams. Everyone bombed the first prelim and he did not curve the class. DO NOT TAKE

Rachit is a nice guy, but actively misleads students about the difficulty of his tests. He will tell you that going to lecture is what it takes to succeed, but that is a lie. He gave us a prelim that was so hard that even the grad TAs said it was too difficult, and he still refused to curve the exam even though the median was a C.

Minimal effort required outside of class, but attention required during class. Concepts are simple but tests are made really hard. Pop quizzes are easy as long as you pay attention in class. The most accessible professor in Cornell, willing to stay really late for office hour. I really like him as a professor.

Prof. Agarwal is perhaps the best CS lecturer I've had here. He starts from the basics and then builds up to more complex topics, but always goes back to foundational ideas to bring everything full circle. He's also willing to help students anytime after class hours. Tests can be tricky, but go to class and a good chunk of the questions are gimmes

Computer networks class, wow! One of the best professors at Cornell CS. His lectures are amazingly well crafted. He starts with the most fundamental questions and builds the entire protocol around those questions. It is clear how much Prof. Agarwal cares about students and about teaching. One of the best classes in my four years at Cornell.

CS6455 was a new graduate class on advanced computer networks. We read a couple of papers every week with topics varying from classical papers in Internet design to recent papers in datacenter networks. We then discussed papers in the class. The class was very interactive and professor had great insights about past and future of computer networks.

I took his graduate class on big data systems in Spring 2017. I was one of the few undergrads in the class, so I had to catch up on the terminology. However, Prof. Agarwal was always available to help me catch up. He has truly interesting insights about the area and an in-depth knowledge about all the papers we discussed. I liked the class.

Prof. Agarwal is one of the most amazing lecturers at Cornell. He is engaging, funny and keeps the class interactive. He cares so much about the students. He often stayed in his office until late and came back early morning to help us with home works. I hope he improves the course organization ( and have better TAs and co-instructor in future).
New Professor. I find his enthusiasm and knowledge to be awesome. Was very unorganized, and this undermined the learning of this class by a lot. WIll hopefully get better soon!

It was his first time teaching, and he did a great job in the lectures (some mistakes, but the lectures were very engaging). The class was unorganized, but he was very approachable, always ready to help and really cared about us students. There are very few other professors who stay in office until 11PM to help students and come back at 8AM.

I learned OS in the 48 hours before the final exam, by studying from previous finals.  This professor provided support through unreasonable homeworks, vague expectations, and the assurance that "grades don't matter" right before he released low scores on 6 homeworks on the day the semester ended.  Enroll at your own risk.

The other responders are being a bit harsh; he's a nice/helpful guy and his lectures were pretty good, but the class was poorly organized by him to the point where it was extremely frustrating. Blowing other deadlines to get this class's work done on time, only to have him constantly shift the due dates back, was unfair to say the least.

I learned more about OS from other courses that I was taking than from this class. I just learned that instructor assignments can also have seg faults, HW grades are arbitrary, and remember kids, in a hard drive, the head spins. Clearly knows what he's doing

Worst class I've ever taken. Homeworks and projects were assigned randomly (we once had 2 Psets and 1 project due in one week). Repeatedly insisted the small details don't matter, just the underlying concepts, yet the homeworks and final exam both had really tedious questions that were never even touched on in lecture. Avoid at all costs.

I blindly stumbled through this course, consistently failing with minimal support or feedback. Professor often seemed frustrated with students being so lost and wanted to improve but didn't know how, while students were frustrated our time wasn't respected. He does have potential, and I hope he takes some feedback and becomes a great professor!

This was his first time teaching the class. I could fill a textbook with all the mistakes he made as a first time lecturer. But that won't matter because if this class has taught me anything, textbooks are worthless. Homeworks are largely just googling answers or begging TAs for help. Please take this class another semester if see this professor.

HAHAHA isn't it funny when you work all weekend to finish a project and then you get a month long extension because half the class didn't finish and you fail a prelim for another class  in the process. Good times. But in all seriousness, this class was pretty annoying. Being a guinea pig for a semester is not fun. Rachit said this would be fun :(.
Awesome!

I absolutely loved this class. She was by far one of the most knowledgeable history professors I've had at any school. She explained things very thoroughly, and had the ability to add depth and complexity to subjects other teachers might gloss over or simplify. IMO, a class with her is a must for history majors at CSUCI.
I loved this class! The professor explains things so well. I dont really care for history, but she made it fun. It was my favorite class last semester.

This class was great! A lot of reading, but its interesting, and she always explained them. The research paper was hard, but she gives you half the semester to work on it, and grades fairly. She gives a lot of comments for improving. I would recommend her class. Prof Reynoso is very passionate about the material and actually cares about students.
The class was okay, but the readings were too much, the essay prompts were vague, the expectations were too high, and the grading was way too harsh

This was a good class but felt that the professor didn't grade very fairly at all. She gave good feedback on all papers and taught well but when you the grades were not representative of the work or effort put in. Also participation weighed too heavily and she expects too much of students.

Verdie is great and loves to hear student feedback and participation. She can be a little tough at first but as long as you take her comments it will be just fine. Not the most approachable but definitely always willing to help. She is definitely passionate about her work in order to get students engaged
Verdie is passionate about the course material and excellent at engaging students. Her class taught me new ways of thinking and reading and provided a safe space to express my views.

Directionless, vague, poorly put-together. Verdie's True Stories is a disjointed mess of a class that bounces from book to book; books only related in the way that they serve to push her agenda. Not that I always disagreed with her agenda. For example, fighting racism and sexism are noble pursuits, but the class felt like well-trodden propaganda.

Sometimes the prompts for essays were confusing, but Verdie is generous with her time in office hours and her feedback is really thorough and helpful. The discussion and student-led sections were always great. She's tough at first but if you work hard and do all of the assignments it will pay off.

I had True Stories with her and it was a disjointed and disappointing haze of poorly-led discussions. She's very passive-aggressive so DO NOT get on her bad side; after I wrote something adverse to her agenda, papers were returned with vague criticisms and I couldn't do well. I ended up with a B-, while in my other FWS I got an A+. Don't take her!

One of the best GOVT professors at Cornell University. I personally think that her Political Institutions Under Autocrats class was difficult BUT it is one of the most interesting and useful classes I have taken at this school! I would gladly take another class with Prof. Rosenfeld.

This was my first time taking a GOVT class, and I really enjoyed it. Prof Rosenfeld's lectures were engaging and well-organized. She is very accessible outside of class and always willing to help with the essay. Class discussions are always very interesting, and we are encouraged to share our opinions even if we disagree. Great professor!

Professor Rosensaft is an incredibly storied orator. All students ended up with some type of A grade (per the professor), and 70% of the grade is based on one 5 minute presentation at the end of the semester. The other 30% is "participation," though this is not really monitored or tracked. Would take this class again.
Truly the most amazing person

Dr. Giroux is a kindhearted, passionate professor who wants to see her students succeed. If you communicate your needs to her, she will be very understanding and go above and beyond to help you feel confident and comfortable with the material. There are lots of readings and podcasts for class, but they aren't too difficult and are interesting.

Professor Giroux is so wonderful! Take a class with her if you have the opportunity. I feel like I have learned so much in this class without the stress of having an unmanageable amount of work. She really cares about her students, and even though its a big class, she loves to get to know people individually. One of the best professors at Cornell.

One of the nicest professors I had this term. Always available for help, even offering special office hours before projects were due. Online lectures got a little boring and there was little interaction (participation wasn't mandatory). Light workload until the end when there were two projects.
She's really nice, accessible outside of class, cognizant of the fact that there's a global pandemic!

She is an amazing person. She genuinely cares about students and likes to engage with them in and out of class. By far the nicest professor I've had. Also, the class was very interesting because she teaches it in such a clear and direct way. There isn't that much homework and exams are very fair.
Honestly the kindest professor at Cornell. Super willing to help and is always very supportive. The class is a little dry but she makes it very worth taking!

Sarah was such a great intro to my major. Shes super enthusiastic and charismatic. The class itself is interesting and not a large time commitment. Homework could be a bit confusing at times, but she is willing to work with you whenever you feel lost.
Dr. Giroux is really really nice and a good teacher. Her lectures are interesting and she's a very fair grader. Really approachable.

This guy talks a lot but it's because he's interested in his work. Great lecturer, but if you don't show up to class good luck surviving. Despite this, very accessible and understanding outside of class.

Louis does talk a lot, but he's a great guy. If you make an effort to learn you will surely enjoy this class. Very unique professor at Cornell where he genuinely enjoys and understands his field, hard not to learn here.
If you get Lou going, he won't stop talking. The guy clearly loves his field, but can be monotonous after 2hrs of lecture in lab. Great guy though.

One of the most frustrating classes I've taken. Complete lack of rubric for the 3 essays that comprise your grade. You can fix every mistake the TA cites and then get the exact same grade on the next essay. Professor is arrogant and condescending when you reach out for help.
The worst class taken. Horrible teaching style also.
Professor is arrogant and pretends as if he cares about students. Horrible grading criteria.

Taken online asynchronous. Whole grade is based on 3 papers so I never did class or readings. The papers are difficult, allow no outside sources, and are subject to arbitrary TA grades. Leave yourself a lot of time for them. Rlly hated doing the papers but the class may still be worth it if you don't have time for daily/weekly stuff.

The worst class ever taken at Cornell. The grade is completely determined by three papers, which have very broad and confusing topics. The TAs do not respond to emails and do not leave any comment for a low grade assigned. The professor is indifferent to students' concerns. Papers were also regraded and assigned a lower grade. Horrible class!

This class was awful. Graded only by three papers with very broad questions and unclear grading criteria. They care more about details then anything else, if you don't write the paper exactly how they want it your grade will plummet. My friends and I dreaded this class. Lowest grade I've gotten in three years at Cornell for no reason at all. Avoid!

I would not recommend this class to someone I hate. The essay prompts are very broad yet the TAs all have one set approach in mind. If you don't write to their standards, it will show. They don't allow outside sources and the readings are not interesting.

As the leading professor in his field, lectures/topics covered were great. Can get dry at times, but you will come out having learned many new things. On the flip side, he can be super witty and fun to watch lecture. He seems to care about students' learning outcomes and makes it clear what expects on prelims.

Professor Hyman is truly amazing. I had him for class this past fall and he has clear expectations/grading and as long you put in the effort, you will do well. Assigns a good amount of reading but doesn't expect you to read everything word for word. Definitely worth taking his classes: he is funny, kind, and genuinely cares about his students.

Um, what?  He lectures from his book.  Literally, his lectures are just him reading from his book most of the time, with side comments here and there.  The class in general is a little dry and boring.  At times, it does get interesting though.  He tries to push his political agenda too much and depending on which TA you have it's hit or miss.
Louis R. Hyman has 'It'  That's all you need to know.
Not at all helpful in office hours. Avoid!!!!

The course was interesting, but I found Professor Hyman to be a less than mediocre professor. He does none of his own grading, instead leaving you at the mercy of TA's. He doesn't even review it. If you want to contest the grade you may get worse. He's too full of himself to be an assistant professor. I'd pass on this class.
Wonderful Professor!  Very engaging and clear lectures.  Two Exams and a Paper.  Very clear expectations and not too difficult.  Makes class fun!

I'm truly going to miss his class. His lectures takes a very dry subject and makes the time captivating. 2 test and and a paper. Very clear on all aspects of the class. His knowledge of the subject is second to none. If you don't take a class with him while you're here, you're truly missing out. See ya at Wedgwood Hyman.

To date, he is my favorite professor at Cornell.  Straightforward, he tells you what he's expecting on examinations and on the paper.  A man whose vivid animation is arresting, he makes dynamic use of the lecture hall,  And if you're considering taking 2070, his teaching style is as good, if not better, than his lecture.  He's also brilliant.

Professor Hyman is amazing. Labor History seems like a dull subject but he never fails to find a way to make it interesting. His lectures can be dense but will keep you on your toes. He tells you want he wants on your exam and is really fair. Plus, he is a genius.

His lectures can be hard to understand because he moves quickly. The trick is to write down what he has on his opening slide and use it as an outline. Once you do this, the class should be easy, and he is a really nice guy. I def recommend anyone who has to take the class to take it with him.
Prof. Billera is very friendly and willing to help. Do come to his office hours and it is of great help for the tests.

If given a choice, DO NOT take the class with Billera.  He knows his stuff, but he doesn't teach it.  It was the difference of night and day when the other professor filled in for him.  If you do have him, read the book, it's pretty straightfoward.
Great teacher, very willing to help if you seek it out.  Clear, organized lectures, interesting material.

Heavily biased grading in History of Economic Analysis. The structure is that you essentially get 2 grades and they are weighted in some ambiguous way (not listed on syllabus) for your final grade. 8:40 class, provides useless feedback on papers, and is downright cold . Take anything else  Received a grade much lower than expected with no warning.

For History of Economic Analysis with Falkson you will enjoy the material if you have the time in your schedule to devote to the class. You can also put in a modest effort and spend a lot of time on the two assignments, and still manage a good grade. Very smart guy.

The professor is very nice and you can tell he truly loves teaching, so it's hard to complain because he definitely cares about his students. That said, this class was very disorganized. He would hop from one topic to the next and since he never used the textbook, I never knew how and where to study from. Good material, but all over the place.

The guy below me must be high. Falkson may at times ramble and be incomprehensible, but his office hours are so helpful! The course material I found, for the most part, to be pretty difficult, but he was patient enough to help me through the material.

I could not follow this guy at all during lecture. He didn't follow the book and he would change notation constantly. He also tended to ramble about macro theory. I really wish I had taken this course with Prof. Bar instead.

Prof Escalona Torres is amazing! Honestly he might be my favorite professor of all time. I took SPAN 1210 + 1220 with him. He's super caring, he was great at explaining the material, and he really made every class fun. Cannot praise this man enough. So sad that I can't take more classes with him, I think he's at a different university now :(

Absolutely loved this man. Funny, personable, approachable, not harsh, really helpful. Homework was pretty easy. Projects take up more time. Improved my Spanish in just one semester. Lots of oral practice in class so participate. Would recommend taking a class with him if possible.

Span 1230 was really disorganized and frustrating for me but I felt that he really did everything he could to make the course less confusing. He's a really nice guy and also very knowledgeable. He's harsh on pronunciation given his linguistics background but it was very helpful. Def would take a class with him again

Professor Escalona Torres is so charismatic and intellectual. I enjoyed the material he brought to class, which he tried to personalize and relate to real life and his own life as well. I think he tried to make Spanish practical for us, but the Spanish department at Cornell really limits what he can do.

Juan is super enthusiastic and made an effort to make class interesting and expand office hours. With that being said, SPAN 1230 is difficult and there is a lot of homework. If you have to take it I'd recommend Juan in a heartbeat, he made the material easier to understand and more interesting. But it is a lot of work -- not his fault but be ware.
Incoherent.  That pretty much says it all.

The most interesting instructor I have come across at Cornell. Put simply, if you are interested in "thinking," you will absolutely love this guy. If you just want to take a FWS and get it out of the way, you will not enjoy Sierra. He is very tough/critical, but it's an awesome class if you're willing to work and think critically about your writing

Horrible all-around teacher. He is more interested in bashing you than analyzing the readings. The first thing he told our class was that he wanted us all to drop so he wouldn't have to teach. He nit-picks over every word you say and will assume your writing level is BETTER than that of a politician's speech-writer.

I wasn't much of an English guy in high school but he totally changed that and for a while I was actually contemplating switching my major to comparative literature.  Besides leading interesting discussions and being a very smart guy, he was very helpful outside of class and he was very concerned with improving my writing.  Great class.

If you consider yourself an above average writer & enjoy reading, this might be a good teacher for you. If you just want to take his class because it sounds interesting, dont take it especially for FWS.  If you got serious doubts about your writing ability, DONT TAKE HIS CLASS, you're gonna get screwed over unless English is your favorite subject.

Prof Hinestroza is honestly amazing! He genuinely cares about his students and their learning and appreciates hard work. Sure, there is a lot of work in this course, but he specifies time and again that if you're not up for the work, the course isn't meant for you. Learnt a lot of new, cool things in the class.

Assigns an immense amount of work. A lot of FSAD Management students have opted for later years' tracks just to avoid this class. I'm not sure if it's even allowed to assign semi-finals, independent project, group project, and a final exam at the same time, but this Prof has the audacity to do it. Easy grader. There's only a few real lectures.

Not the most interesting subject matter, but I enjoyed this class. Discussions were straightforward, assignments were very clearly and returned promptly. Seemed relaxed about teaching a freshman writing seminar, and seemed to treat students with same relaxed approach. Would recommend.

LOVED Dr. Torres.  He was passionate about Witchcraft, which was amazing, even as an engineering student I really got into his class.  If you need an extension or have questions about a text he's super helpful and his personality is just wonderful.  10/10 would recommend.

Brant was an excellent teacher.  Very good in class.  He makes his subject very interesting and brings a lot of knowledge from his own research into class.  Very good looking and interesting to talk to.  Fair grader.

Brant is sooo great!! He's intelligent, approachable, and funny. I don't think I've ever left class without having laughed at least once. He is very accessible and will work with you closely on your writing until you have a clear focus. My interest and understanding of Shakespeare has skyrocketed after taking this FWS.

I've had two classes with her and she's wonderful! Can be tough at times but is seriously dedicated to helping you learn the material and is often quite funny. You obviously have to participate a lot since its a language class so I don't suggest taking it early in the morning or you'll be too tired to want to do the exercises

Flaminia is great; she keeps class lighthearted and fun, but also really helps to jumpstart your Italian.  She knows how to work with students at all levels and is a genuinely nice person.  She takes our work seriously but is always good for a laugh during class.  If you don't slack off, you'll really enjoy and get a lot out of this course
i love this professor!

I hear the intro (101) with her is difficult, but 109 was a blast.  Small class of 25 or so where I made some of my best friends.  Flaminia is a sweetheart and a wonderful woman who sometimes cooks at ZaZa's (it's nice to see her there).  I don't know about lower levels but she's amazing in 209!
Just because she's cute and from Italy doesn't mean that she's a good professor.  Picks favorites, pretty damn condescending, not much of an intellectual.
fantastica. if you can take a class with her, don't hesitate...if you're at least somewhat interested in italian, you'll love her and her class.

Flaminia is amazing, and I've had 3 classes with her...She is so patient, beyond helpful, and has no problem giving As if you pay attention and  keep up with the work. She also has a great sense of humor and seems to really care about her students.
Great professor, awesome classes...she makes Italian worth taking
Best professor at Cornell - brilliant and extremely fair...you have to do the work though....
Flaminia always seems bored in class.  She doesn't seem very smart, but that is probably because she hates her job. She can also take out this frustration by making fun of students in class.
awesome, smart, hilarious
No Comments
Fun, sassy, very intelligent, and good at getting discussions started. Willing to help out, fair grader. Can get testy when provoked.
She's so cute!! She can be tough, definitely hard-core for the Italian dept.
Amazing - best prof at Cornell.  If you do the work she is the greatest!

Professor Edreva does an amazing job at creating work that is insightful and relaxing. They do an excellent job at communicating what is expected in the class and they are easy to approach with any questions. It's easy to feel comfortable talking about work in-depth and it's a time to be creative!

I have never contacted Dr Rossi, as this is an online quest 1 class that is pretty easy. Lectures for everything, readings seem mandatory but lectures cover pretty much everything. Grading is awful, sometimes It would be almost 2 months before grades were uploaded. However, work is easy. Tests utilize honor lock, but you can have notes to use.

Dr. Rossi is completely unreachable. She does not respond to emails. She does not hold office hours. The TAs have expressed difficulty with getting a hold of her. The class is really easy, with video lectures (that aren't hers) but is assignment heavy, but not unmanageable. The class is a great experience, I just wish the professor was engaged.
Dr. Rossi is a great professor who cares about what she teaches. This class was easy to digest, interesting, and an easy A if you pay attention. 100% would take again!

Dr. Rossi is very kind and considerate! Tests are easy if you read the textbook--especially considering they are open-book! As long as you give the class an honest effort, you will do well! Classes can be a bit boring at times, however.

Amazing professor, her canvas modules are very well organized and she answers questions via email or canvas inbox. She does leave like 10 tasks per week but they are super easy and short. It is an easy course and you learn about culture and of course a different language.
she was really nice, gave great feedback on all assignments and was just a fun class overall :)
she is very sweet and flexible, her assigments are very easy even though there is around 10-12 a week, and sometimes you work in pairs. but shes amazing.

I took this all online. I needed an arts and humanities course so I went into this class already speaking italian but I appreciated her brief lectures in both English and Italian and the quizzes were based on her lectures so they were straightforward. You do have to work in pairs a lot so prepare for that.

This is an online class, and she made us do paired, recorded presentations EVERY WEEK! If you want flexibility and not have anyone relying on you, DO NOT take her. There's a heavy amount of small assignments and she sends out at least 2 announcements every day. She clearly cares for her job but honestly, it hurts the class and it wasn't enjoyable.

always did my work, my presentations, & whenever she picked me to participate in class activities i always went up and tried my best, 9/10 i was correct in my answer. A girl that sat behind me & mostly copied off me. This lady passes her, but failed me. I did not understand how I didnt try when I did everything i was asked. Deff grades unfairly
she is definetively an amazing professor, I have never learned a language so fast in my life, I really recomend her class

Professor Innis is a fantastic professor who has engaging lectures and activities. She is a very caring and enthusiastic teacher who gives everyone a chance to shine. She made French so easy for me to understand.  Please take her if you have the chance!
I took french 101 and italian 101.  She's really funny and she cares about her students.  She's the best teacher!!

Professoresa Innis is a very fun teacher! she loves to teach and especially since she is from italy her passion for teaching italian shows in her face!! very fun and i learned a lot, book is necessary!!

Professor Innis is really nice and her lectures are easy to understand. Her class relies a lot in the online textbook code and the textbook itself. She'll help you out a lot spelling things and assigns fun group activities for a better understanding. French is a tough language but she made it very fun and easy to learn.
Amazing teacher, She can really speak french! Her lectures are amazing, you must have the online book though. She's really nice and helpful
She's the best french teacher C:
Very good professor. I love French because of this class

Very fast paced class, though curriculum is more to blame than the prof.  She is a fluent native speaker and can answer pretty much any question on the topic.  Always in a good mood.  Homework is through one of those expensive online programs, but again, the department chose it, not the prof.  She's a sweet lady who cares for her students.

Professor Innis has complete command of the French language.  She is equipped to answer all questions regarding life and culture of France as well as its place in history.  She moves through grammar with ease so that students will leave the course being able to converse coherently in all tenses.  I would recommend her classes to all Francophiles.
Very sweet and helpful!!! Very easy if you like languages. Peace of cake for spanish and italian speakers.
Very sweet woman, who wants her students to succeed and cares. Always cracking jokes and very funny, never seen her in a bad mood. She is extremely helpful and grades easily. Take her!!
Cool Teacher but Goes way too fast and she assumes you know French not lots of HW
Great teacher, funny & nice. Always available for help and enjoys teaching. New to teaching at SW. Would recommend her class.

Professor Magomedova truly cares about all of her students and wants them to succeed. Russian is an extremely hard language, but her class makes it seem manageable and I found myself wanting to study. She is engaging and extremely knowledgeable. Take a class with her if you can!

Eleonora is one of the kindest people I have ever met. Had her for 101, 102, and 203. She really cares about her students and is willing to help them succeed.  You will have homework every day, but they are short and take between 10-20 minutes. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC.

I haven't had much contact with literature and was nervous to take this class, but I ended up loving it! Eleonora is extremely caring and accommodating, and I loved every piece we read over the semester. I'd take it again if I could.

Really good teacher. I rarely use RMP but Eleanora did a great job making a difficult language easy to understand. She is very popular for a reason and will do literally anything she can to help her students, including letting students call her cell phone for help and having flexible deadlines.

I love Eleanora! Seriously try to take RUSS 101 and/or 102 with her because she will make anyone fall in love with the language and the culture. She is incredibly kind and really cares about her students. As long as you consistently do homework and study, you should be fine (at least for RUSS 101).

I'm pretty sure I've rated her before, but I took another class from her this semester and I cannot stress enough how amazing she is. She's hilarious, fun to talk to, sweet, and a genuinely incredible instructor. Her class is consistently my highest grade in a semester, and she's so lovely. Not quite as good over zoom, but she's still amazing.

Eleonora was an amazing and caring prof. She really wants you to succeed. Definitely recommend if you're looking for an easy FL fulfillment. She gives your her number to call anytime. She is so funny and loves to make jokes and pick on you. Small classes so you get to interact. Wonderful professor and you'll learn a lot too. The textbook is free!

Eleonora assigns homework every night. She is an extremely fast grader and has literally left me voicemails to tell me when I do well on an exam. She teaches to teach, not to give grades. She will be flexible with you if you need it. Get to know her, spend time with her, and you'll get an A even if Russian isn't your strong point.
Russian is not a very easy language to learn but she makes it enjoyable and pleasant. This was probably my first positive experience in learning a language.

I love Eleonora! I look forward to her class every day because I can always count on her to make me laugh. Four hours a week with her doesn't feel like enough. I considered taking 102 just to have another semester with her, but I was just taking the class for fun. I also found the language to be quite easy under her instruction.

I love her so freaking much. I cannot tell you enough that you HAVE TO TAKE HER. She's the best. She's so understanding and really cares about students. She's also hilarious and makes going to class a real treat. I cannot recommend her too much. Just take her class. Take it. Go to connect carolina and register for it right now. I'm waiting.

Quite literally the best professor at Carolina. She will go out of her way to help you succeed. She's a lenient grader and also one of the funniest people I've ever met. Truly a gem. If you're considering taking Russian as your language, please do it. Seriously. Best decision I've made in college.

Eleonora is my favorite professor at UNC if you're thinking about taking this class, do it! She's extremely caring, there's a little homework every day but she won't penalize you for turning it in late. It's okay to miss class if you just email her and don't make a habit of it. She's really funny and her expectations are very clear. I'll miss her!

Eleonora is the best teacher I've ever had, hands down. She is so caring about her students and wants them to be successful. She regularly meets with students outside of class and gives individualized feedback so the student can improve on specific areas. If you want an amazing class and professor, this is it.

Eleonora is a great teacher and really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Russian is hard, but if you put in the time and effort and get help from Eleonora when needed it is easy to do well.
Eleonora is great! Cares about her students, teaching, and being inclusive! Makes class fun because she is so enthusiastic!

Absolutely amazing. This is my 6th year of college (and 3rd college), and I can honestly say she is one of my ultimate favs! SO caring, wants you to succeed, understanding and down right awesome. Russian is hard, you can't get past that, but I never thought I'd say I got an A in Russian until her! She really knows how to teach.
I can't say enough good things about her. She met multiple times off campus to help one on one. She is such a great teacher and kind soul.
She is the bee's knees. She will certainly pique your interest in the Russian language and culture. She cares for her students and is very passionate about teaching. Take Russian with her!!!

SHE IS SO GREAT!  SO funny and soooo nice! Willing to help you whenever you need it! Genuinely cares about all of her students! Study for the tests and they are not very hard. I'm terrible at any and all foreign languages and I did very well in RUSS 101. Take her class!
She is absolutely amazing, I lover her and wish I could have her for every class at UNC.  She makes the material fun to learn, and her personality can't be beat

Eleonora is the best professor at UNC! She is really funny and is a lenient grader. She understands if you are busy and will push back quizzes and tests for you. If you have a chance to take Russ 101 with her do it!
Excellent teacher who constantly makes you laugh. Not an easy class but definitely worth taking, she wants you to succeed.

Love Eleanora! Specifically signed up for her class cos I'd heard good things about her. She's funny & will help you if you struggle. She calls on students regularly, so you have to pay attention. HW is to be handed in every lesson, which got old fast lol. She grades very generously though. Found her class very worthwhile & made my semester shine.

Eleonora is highly entertaining and engaging. I absolutely love her! I really enjoy going to this class and she is very understanding about circumstances keeping you from class. She is very willing to help you with material outside of class. Genuinely excited about the material.
Absolutely loved her. One of the best professors I've had in any subject! Hilarious and extremely fun. Pretty easy class too.
She is a little crazy, but very entertaining. I've never had a professor who cares so much about her students!

Eleonora is the most amazing teacher!  She's hilarious and sweet and really cares about the material.  If you're having any trouble, she's more than willing to help you.  The best teacher and I highly highly recommend her!  She makes Russian so much fun!
Great professor, great class!  Highly recommend!
Very entertaining and funny in class.  Keeps you engaged.  Very helpful outside of class if you don't understand the material.  She's very sweet and just an interesting person in general.
Probably one of the most interesting characters in the Slavic Studies Department.  Anyone who has the chance to take a class with her should.

I took Professor Hicks Fall class and you definitely need the book as we had weekly discussion that were due every Thursday no exceptions. She does assign additional work however she has recommended deadlines and hard deadlines so that's very helpful. If you need help with any assignments she's very helpful and responds fast.

Had her for online and professor was a tough grader. Also unorganized I had so many assignments graded after several weeks so if you get anxious waiting for grades I'd suggest looking for a different professor. Quizzes and assignments aren't difficult, just keep checking the rubric

i actually took her summer class. there was no zoom meetings, but she had weekly videos which were a nice touch to the course. i was nervous going into this course because of some of her reviews, but she ended up being completely awesome. i really enjoyed her class, and the best way to succeed is to do your work and by reading the rubrics

Dedicate a lot of time to read the material and watch the videos! All the answers to quizzes are in the readings and videos so make sure to pay attention to that! She's a great and friendly professor, however, she does expect a lot of detailed information in your essays and discussions. She also provides plenty of time for you to turn in work.

The tests were hard. However, she is incredible. Professor Hicks makes weekly videos that bring a personal touch to online classes. She puts a lot of effort into a student's learning experience, but you must work for the grade. I recommend her, but be ready to learn. PS- the book is boring black-and-white and not interactive.

Very vague, would reject submissions and then nitpick how she wanted specific information. Mainly had this class online never in person most reviews are about classes in person but online shes a tough grader, teaches as it were a university class when its a community college course, adds extra activity sheets due the same week and says the work is counted late if you dont turn it in the next the day, especially on Holidays. Seems nice
Shes a good professor, and will check on you often. I liked her
She is a good professor! Tests are easy which makes passing her class easy. Lots of lecture notes, but at the end they do help.

Great professor. She genuinely cares about her students but she does require you to use some common sense. professor give a lot of material to study on that will be nothing like the test and is not very clear during class lectures. She is not a professor that understands student have jobs and other courses. She is very strict and will try to clutter as much material as she can through out the semester.

she's a very caring prof and doesn't take attendance for her online class. her classes are very boring tho... i don't think i paid much attention. group projs are easy but just annoying to deal with, esp online. no hw, just two short group presentations and then the final paper at the end of the semester. exams are easy too

Never had an easier A of a class. She's also the sweetest lady, never have I seen such a mellow teacher. Take her, also attendance isn't a problem and you can leave at any point in class since it's a big lecture.

If you don't get an A in this class, you should not be in Baruch.

Professor Curlo is a very nice lady. She doesnt go by a book so just focus on her powerpoints and you will be fine. Boring, very boring class she just talks the entire time in a monotone voice with accent. She's very sweet, it's an easy class to do well in, but you're not going to learn much. Do it for an easy grade and if it fits your schedule but if you're trying to get meaningful info this isn't the class.

Can't understand her accent. She basically speaks to herself. Hard multiple choice exams, 40% on lowest test & 60% on highest test.-2%. if you do not do 10 page group paper.  Doesnt curve grade. I rather listen to trumps speeches than sit through her class.

Professor Curlo is really caring and sweet, but she is soft spoken so sit in front. You can learn from the slides she posts and she also curves. Two midterm and a final. Professor Curlo is the nicer professor is Baruch. She knows how to involve the student into the marketing area. Excellent class!
