Literally only 30% of the people go to lectures, not because the class is easy, but because the lectures dont help at all and people would just give up. Overall the class is fine.

Vague, has high expectations but doesn't provide much instructions, gives hw on MPLab but doesn't show how to use features expected in hw, only covers basics, answers some questions if asked during lecture, enthusiasm varies, grading is quite harsh and he's a bit of a slow grader, can be understanding of student troubles, conflicted on taking again

Omar is amazing for Microcontrollers. He knows his stuff and his lectures are well organized. He answers every question without ridicule. Probably the best upper div professor in the department. Professor Omar is by far the best professor online. Pros: Give Good feedback Lectures are live. He actually teaches the content Exams based on Homework and average difficulty Fair Grader, gives Partial Credit Gives fat curves Has Industry Connections (Good networking) Cons: None

Omar is not a good professor, he is very confusing and if you go ask him about a question sometimes he will make you more confused. his way of grading is ridiculous, you don't even know where did you loss the points. a lot of times he pronounce the words wrong. unfair exams, quizzes. makes you get the book and the he don't use the book for anything

Very easy grader. We only had 2 quizzes (which make 20% of your grade). Weekly assignments had 3-4 parts. Lecture was 3 hours long and he does not make it fun. he was a joke of an instructor. just read directly off of handouts. the course he taught us was only a complementary course however he felt like he had to teach the entire chem. eng. course to us.  felt like he could go on power trips becuase he had the title of dr.

A very open professor. Please participate, her lectures were fun. You can talk any opinion during discussion, as long as your opinion is respectful. Discussions were very relaxing and joyful. One of my favorite teachers, definetely has great input in her lectures.
Great instructor. Real nice, with lots of talking. It gets you thinking.

This professor loves to talk for endless hours making the class very boring and hard to concentrate. Reading responses required, discussions occur along with these. There is a group project. She's good at steering people to be unbiased when doing their final research paper. Lots of rough drafts, but her feedback makes it worthwhile. There is a group project, but graded individually.

Has a tendency to ramble but is very nice. There will be a group project with pre-determined topics to choose from. Will fast-forward through films, which can be a bit frustrating. Reading responses are required and checked nearly every class. Group discussions happen with each reading.

She is a good professor and explains the material well. She is definitely interested in the material she is teaching and transmits that interest to her students. Extremely difficult class, lots of reading, and long papers to write. However, the teacher is helpful and really good at what she does. Take the class if you're sincerely interested in culture or anthropology.

sachiko is the best! you should definitely take her

SACHIKO IS AMAZING~~~she is one of those professors that you will want to SEE outside of class to like, have lunch with or something. Very good professor, cute funny and all slides are online.  Her midterm and final are intense but otherwise she's great!

Expected class to be about "treasures" of the world like someone else said because the title was "pyramids, tombs, & treasures" but it's an archeology class with labs.  Pretty easy class. For being a class that I HAD to take, she made it pretty interesting and not too bad.  The only complaint I would have would be her accent, but after the first few days, you get over it.  If I had to say whether or not to take her, go ahead, it wouldn't be in vain, shes fine..

Yes, she's pretty. She has an accent but she is not difficult to understand. She is very nice and enjoys archaeology. Never used book, but tests were harder  than the labs.

Sachiko is a great teacher, I'd take her again.  Sometimes its hard to understand because of her accent but shes more than happy to repeat herself.  The labs are easy, and she posts the notes from class online.  She's very accommodating and helpful.  She always has a good attitude too :)
Love Sensei, amazing teacher and understanding person. She talks a little fast but you catch on fairly quick but definitely study though.

I love sensei!! She's so sweet and helpful, the textbook is used every day in class and we're even given extra side notes outside of the book. SENSEI! I love her so much, despite the class being super difficult. This was my 3rd Japanese class so its understandable that its really hard but Sensei really does teach the material well. Professor Ota is a great teacher. I've learned more Japanese in one semester of her class than some people know after taking a few years in high school. She is a great teacher and will go over ANYTHING with you. may be difficult to hear in lecture. can seem condescending at times, but not intentionally. feedback is very confusing

She's an angel. She's not a super easy grader but her teaching style is really interesting and, honestly, the most helpful. She's like a sassy grandma, I love her.

Great teacher and advisor.  Had her for Years 1 and 2, but still talk to her even though mostly just for advising appointments.  Teaches all levels and is a great teacher.  Seems strict and tough at first, but she's one of the best.  Hang in there and she'll grow on you.  Quite funny at times.  :D

OMIGH, BEST ACT SENSEE EVER. This woman is so excellent. Though at times curt, she's hilarious, fun, and challenging. (And amazing and animated and super-mega-totally-excellent.) I was mostly bored because the teaching style was so frazzled. I feel like my time could've been spent doing other stuff.

Alessandra is amazing! She really knows what she is talking about when it comes to screenwriting and creates a classroom environment that made me feel confident and capable, even though I had never written a screenplay before. She gives great notes, is really humble given everything she has accomplished, and she's also friendly and funny.

She gives useful feedback, but her teaching style was all over the place. Class felt unbalanced/impromptu, and it eventually became very repetitive, leaving me bored. I'd recommend challenging yourself to write a script or taking the course with a different professor.

She teaches a lot of valuable information in a concise and easy way--overall, a great teacher. However, she is so frazzled and overworked that she sometimes will completely disregard the student's perspective. She made us watch and read "Big Lebowski" and the lecture was on "Juno" instead. Very nice person once you get to meet her, but it seems like she has a lot of things in her mind so she sometimes brain farts. She gives great advice on structure of screenplays. Gives great feedback on screenplays.

It's clear by her class that Mrs. Bautze has likely never taught online before. Every week there's some technical issue that the class has to catch for her. Alessandra is new, has a whole lot of potential and in a couple semesters will be positively wonderful. She highly values active participation. TALK. For heaven's sake.

Was an asynchronous class and there were no video lectures uploaded, was difficult to follow through the instructions. she is a very tough grader and does not accommodate. she replies promptly to emails but is very unorganized about a lot of things. There's no other homework if you do the in-class activity each week which only counts towards your participation grade. The material is light and Alessandra is a good teacher. I recommend the class.
Great class, all online, prof was good. You need to do the work and read the instructions carefully or you'll lose marks. As long as you put in some effort you will pass.

This is a tough class, but the prof is great. The labs are all recorded videos so you can do them at your own pace, and help is always available when needed. Make sure you read the instructions and the rubric carefully because she's a tough grader if you don't do what is asked of you. You will learn a lot, but be prepared to work.

FOR MRK260- This class is asynchronous and you don't get to interact with the prof much, but any time I emailed her she answered promptly. The course has a lot of work, but the exercises are interesting and the grading seemed fair to me. Not sure what all of the other comments are about, since I had a positive experience in this class.

This prof is amazing! one of the best ones I've had at Seneca thus far. This course is fully online but the labs are interesting and I learned a lot. She is always available via email and answers questions quickly.

Love this class! a great introduction to After Effects

for MRK 260 - Tough Grader, don't take her classes!

Very strict. Effort is not considered

MRK260: Always has issues on instruction / documents, Not until a student tells her it contains incorrect data or inaccessible file will she then correct it. Strict......
I will recommend future students to do their lab work on time. Prof Alessandra is a good professor but she is a strict grader. If you dont follow the rubric you are sure to lose marks.

SO much work worth very little grades. Very little guidance provided throughout the course. FOR MRK260--> Tons of work to do each week, videos, exercises, presentations, and LinkedIn or google certification. Professor is a tough grader, with even 1 mistake in an exercise or submission you will lose a lot of marks. You won't have a direct interaction with her, the course is completely asynchronous.

Professor Alessandra is amazing. No textbook is needed for this course. Course material is not heavy and entertaining (TedX videos). She is caring and always accessible (literally at any time:). She tries her best to serve her students and make their lives easier. Online session is taken on Zoom and attendance and participation matters. Recommend:)

Prof Lanzara is a great lecturer, who made the subject of e&m approachable to students. Derivations in class were sometimes complex, but not too complicated that they could not be followed. She is very passionate about physics and an engaging lecturer. Tests were reasonable with problems from past exams and textbook.

She's a good lecturer, fairly good at explaining things with her limited time. Know that Physics 7B goes through content quick though and it's very VERY easy to fall behind. Stay on top of the lectures and content, go to discussion sections and work and you're golden. Exams are very fair, not as challenging as the discussion problems and not hard.

This professor helped me understand physics. Physics 7A was bad, but with this professor I was able to get through 7B. Textbook heavy. Her exams will include textbook problems. Gives fair exams. Lectures are helpful.  Sometimes she explains material differently from the textbook. She gives hints for exams only for the people actually there.

Prof. Lanzara was very charismatic and fun during lectures. She tried to encourage students to learn the course content through fun demonstrations in class that would later appear on the exams. The only issue with this class is that the content is not accessible outside of the lectures.

She genuinely cares about her students succeeding in this course. Her lectures include the derivations of most formulas, and she usually hints to what types of problems will be on the exams. That said, homework is pretty hard (although the problems are mostly taken from the textbook) and the exams generally reflect the problems on the homework.

STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS!!! Lanzara did not care at all! She did not lecture, she only posted prerecorded lectures from 2020 and even stopped showing up to office hours as the semester progressed. She was unresponsive regarding questions and didn't even seem to remember what part of the course we were on. I highly recommend taking anyone else.

Professor Lanzara seemed really nice and caring, but her asynchronous lecture style left a lot of be desired, often running over time. Textbook is helpful for practice, but the homework and tests cover what is discussed in lecture. Tests were fair if you understood the concepts well. Wish I could have taken it in person.

get ready to teach yourself. her lectures are fine for homework but don't really prepare you for the midterms (as expected). online school with her wasn't awesome since she didn't do any live lectures and you couldn't ask questions unless you went to OH which isn't always easy to do depending on your schedule.
Fairly dry lectures, though she does demos sometimes. One of the nicer 7b professors. Youll understand what shes saying after the first lecture.

Lanzara writes extremely hard tests and grades them harshly, which is the hardest thing about the course. However, she is a pretty good lecturer with lots of examples and derivations which help you work through the homework and (somewhat) the exams.

Professor Lanzara's class covers very difficult topics, and she does a decent job covering them in lecture. That being said, a lot of the work for her class must be done on your own. You must take the initiative to seek help when you are struggling and use all of the resources available. When you do so though, she will be very kind and supportive.

She genuinely wants you to pass the class, she hints to what problems will be on exams. Spends a lot of the time doing dry derivations and math regarding important equations but usually that ends up being on the midterms anyway. Lectures are curved individually which is a plus if you do average on exams, you're pretty much guaranteed a B or higher

Overall a great Professor. The lectures are kinda dry tbh. She wants you to learn stuff for sure tho. Reportedly request to move from upper div to 7 series so she can reach more general students. questionable grading because her 2 lecs are curved separately while tests are the same excpect final.

Lanzara is kind of boring in class, but I like that she goes through the derivation of many important formulas. She tends to waste time in lectures by constantly repeating herself, but at least her midterms and final are rather straightforward compared to other professors. Plus her handwriting is neat, which is more than i can say for most..

A great professor. You get used to the accent in a week. Shes nice, super funny, and very clear with her lectures. She gives hard tests though but extremely fair. Do her old exams she uses a lot of similar examples.

She's so loving, but man were her tests hard. She really stepped it up this semester compared to her previous exams. Midterm material was difficult because of math and range of topics, always a question (out of 5) that you had to be in lecture to get. A good professor, but not easy.

Lanzara was descent at lecturing. She didn't get you excited for E&M, but she presented it in a clear way. No cheat sheets were allowed for the tests, but as a consequence she made the questions straightforward. She was a bit of a jerk though, often making people who asked questions in class feel dumb, don't be deceived by her nice italian accent.

Lanzara is an amazing professor. E&M is an extremely difficult part of physics, yet she makes it so much better. Her lectures are crystal clear (and her handwriting is immaculate). Tests are tough, but that's more due to it being physics rather than any failure on her part to teach. You'll still have to work for an A, but it's doable!
Great Professor for 7B! Very clear, comprehensive lectures. Tests were of average difficulty, though midterm 2 was difficult. Would definitely recommend.
Her accent is pretty thick, so it was hard for me to understand what she was saying a good portion of the time. Midterm and final averages were abysmal, but the curve helped.
Hard tests, but a really good professor. Clear lectures and helpful during office hours.

Very sweet lady, but her tests don't show that side of her. Her first midterm was pretty hard, but her second was not too bad. Her final was near impossible however. Nevertheless, tests aside, she's a sweet person and willing to help, even if her lectures may not be the best in the world.

SHE'S AWESOME! She's caring, sweet, and doesn't like to fail you or make life hard for you! Class isn't fun, and lectures are hard to listen to.  But on the plus side, exams are less murder than other professors' (not easy, just less murder).

If you were good at physics (i.e. participated high school physics contests, etc.) and do your homework, you don't need to go to lectures and don't have to study for exam. Exams are contest-like format (a little easier though) so can't really study for it anyway.

Teaching is good at beginning but then starts to go downhill as time goes on. Even though her accent takes getting used too, she has many demonstrations to complement her boring lectures. Was extremely difficult to understand her Italian accent.  Was probably the result for the lack of my interest in her class.

Great teacher...the accent may be a little hard at first...pay attention to examples she gives in class they are sometimes very similar to her test...She's the type of professor that if you treat them with respect they will in turn respect you.
tests are very fair as long as you do the homework and go to section, make sure you understand concepts. class wasn't too bad and Lanzara is very understanding.

Had physics background so never really went to lectures and did pretty good.  She writes terrible tests that are very difficult to understand and always have at least 3-4 errors on them.

Fairly good lecturer and seems to genuinely care. She's generally clear about material, but sometimes doesnt accurately portray exam level material during lectures w/ examples. I really didn't like her lectures at all, tests were middle of the road, and I just didn't like her demeanor.
Overall she's a good professor. She tries really hard to take students' opinions into account when making the midterms.

I didn't enjoy the material but she made lectures fairly painless. But she thinks everyone's as smart as she is, and that reflects on the tests. Says they're easy even when the average is a C or a D. physics is boring and dull, lanzara is a good professor, like all accents give it a week or two and it's totally clear.

Professor is good in Lectures but beware of her exams, they tend to be relatively hard. But overall she's a great professor, and really cares about her students.
I can't understand a single word this lady is saying.  I have to pay constant attention and put a lot of effort into clarifying what she is saying

very good lecturer, interesting homework.  challenging tests, but her teaching style is really clear and fun.  she had us do presentations on modern uses of solid state physics at the end of the course, which were interesting and easy.

She gives good notes during lectures.  Examples during lectures are simple and basic, while tests and homework are comparatively difficult.  It is usually a big excitement once she can get the demo to work.  Sometimes not enough time to finish problems or lecture.

She was really nice, but not helpful in lecture.  Spent too much time proving stuff, not enough time actually doing problems.  Lecture had nothing to do with tests or hw...stopped going.  Class difficulty wasn't too bad, just dont slack off too much.
She really cares about her students and won't refuse to take the time to explain all your questions if you visit her office hours. She's great, although the subject sucks!!

A good, nice lecturer, but like most other classes, she gave very basic examples in class, but had very challenging problems in both the homework and tests. Physics 7A is not easy no matter what teacher you have- only a certain amount of people will get A's, B's, etc. Tried hard, ended up with a B-.

The class was relatively easy up until the final although the MT's were a little tough. About the demos, those are more the fault of the department (lack of funding) and not the professor. The final was very interesting. Difficult questions both in doing and comprehending them. I hope it works out.

Definitely a very good professor.  She explains things clearly and is willing to go over any questions.  Occassionally, her demos will not work or there are errors in her example problems.  Overall, very good.  Her exams are somewhat hard, but the curve balances it out.

A very kind and caring teacher who knows how to teach. I don't find her Italian accent hard to understand. She's very approachable and gives very clear and organized lectures. She originally came from Stanford, so maybe that explains why she's a lot better than the average teacher here. :)

Hey, the accent is the only thing worth showing up for at 8 a.m!  Overall, she's a very non-threatening prof in a very threatening class. Her midterms weren't too easy, but what do you expect from Physics 7a?  Worth taking.
tough material, but she's really dedicated to the class, though many seem to have trouble w/ her accent
An organized, funny and good professor with an accent.  It's the course that is tough, but she helps explain things clearly.

I LOVE HER! She is amazing, helpful and a good teacher. She knows what she's doing and you can tell she loves teaching. This teacher will do anything for you to pass. I will take her again and again. Great teacher!

Professor Galassi is an amazing professor and truly cares for her students.  She makes it her obligation for students to pass and truly understand the language.  She is very relatable and a well-rounded professor.
He presents the material very clearly and lectures are organized and interesting.

Even though Kramnick is retiring, I have to leave a review because he's just that amazing. He's the epitome of a brilliant professor in need of a hair stylist. An incredible professor who is world renowned.  I absolutely loved Kramnick.

Amazing professor that managed to engage me with a subject I had little interest in. Clear, accessible, and not unnecessarily difficult I recommend everyone take a class with him.

Kramnick is the epitome of an old school, laid back, brilliant professor with wild gray hair. 1 assignment for our grad seminar (a paper) that doesn't have a due date. I am currently taking a online Winter session with Kramnick and must say he is a genius. If you are a Gov major you must take his Intro to Political Philosophy course.

Fascinating, old-school professor who is always on his game. Lecturers are interesting and detailed. Would have liked for him to let the class participate and ask questions, but overall, good professor.

Kramnick was a fantastic professor! Got me excited about American Political thought. Lectures could get a little boring by the end, but overall, they were great. I've never felt so connected with a professor in a large lecture class.

Kramnick lived up to the reputation. He is brilliant and it shows. He may be getting old, but he hasn't lost his touch (like Lowi has). I highly recommend anyone interested in government, philosophy, or history to take American Political Thought.
He's really helpful

Kramnick is an award winning professor who really knows his stuff. If you do the reading, you should have no problem.  I didn't and still managed a B+. TA's tend to be very knowledgeable also although they teach in completely different styles and are a little tough on papers

He was very clear in his lectures, but also painfully boring. Many people (myself included) found it extremely difficult to stay awake in class. He's very knowledgeable about what he teaches, but he tends to repeat himself over and over and lectures became monotonouse and uninteresting. Kramnick is very interesting and enthusiastic about his teaching subject. However there is a TON of reading and TA grading is pretty hard. There is a midterm and a final as well as a term paper so there isn't a ton of work but it also makes it easy to get behind on the reading.

The lectures make the class super easy. If you pay attention, the readings will only become supplements to your essay. The TA's grade harshly, but that is how it is with all Gov TA's at Cornell. Kramnicks passionate, and it really makes the lectures better. He would save a whole lot of time by not repeating the same point over and over again though

Has an incredible love for the material and is a great lecturer. Someone you'd want to be your grandfather! Not too difficult a workload, with 2 essays and a final exam, but the lack of assessment kind of encourages you not to read...and you don't exactly need to know the readings until the final.
Amazing class, as was expected having taken 161 with Prof. K.
Entertaining lectures, highly approachable and will review your essays favorably if you feel your TA didn't quite get it.
Excellent readings, but Kramnick refuses to go into any depth with them. It's a shame, seeing that this is his specialty...

Kramnik was an excellent lecturer, but if you are not a govt major, be wary.  There are only three graded items (midterm, papre, and final), and if you can not express your ideas well and have any understanding about your topic, you will do poorly.  The TA sections are kind of a waste of time, but unfortunately, those are mandatory.

You could probably not do a single reading and get by just on the lectures (although if you are interested in taking this class, these are readings you'll enjoy).  Prof. K is the man, but the TAs vary from exceptional to mediocre at best.  Try to get a good TA then get on her good side.

Although you won't learn anything incredibly profound, this is still a solid intro class. Kramnick is a class-act guy who is  to schmooze with students and help them out. The course itself was pretty straightforward, and is not difficult at all if you go to lecture and see what he emphasizes.
I actually took Prof. Kramnick's intro and upper level political philosophy classes. I loved both classes. I never wanted to miss a class because his lectures are amazing.

Two requirements for a great professor: infectious love of the material, and gets along well with students. Kramnick excels at both (and many more). Kramnick is the quintessential friendly grandfather figure with a side of academic know-how and rainbow sprinkles on top. Despite the large size of the lecture, he tries to get to know students personally, which I found really likable. As for the class, the real source of info is him. You can get away with skipping a few readings, and still learn.

Though he acts a little bit like Woody Allan, kramnick is my favorite teacher this semester. He is interesting, intelligent, and insightful. Sometimes the lectures can get a little boring, but I think its more the material than him. Very down to earth, try and have lunch with him and you'll see what I mean.

Amazing lecturer! His lectures always connect with the readings. There's no sections, but there is a lot of reading. Just remember one thing when you go to his class, "the race for life."  You'll know what I mean when you take the class :D. Grading for papers are subjective and varies by TAs.  Go to class b/c prelims require class notes!

Take it if you can, and you're not one of the idiots that thinks there's a war on Christmas.  It's not hard, it's straightforward, and it's better than most other classes.  Kramnick is funny and smart, and even if you disagree with him, you have to acknowledge that he's not making things up or distorting facts.

Kramnick's egotistical, but most celebrated profs are. The material is interesting, but a little boring. I loved this class.  I'm not a government major, but I though the lectures were intersting, (even if he does go off topic a lot) and there was practically no work involved.  Easy and fun.
amazing teacher, smart, very clear, brings up some really interesting issues

Great teacher, very engaging.  If you complete all of the reading and practice outlined in the syllabus, I'm sure you will get AT LEAST a C+. If you grasp the information well, an "A" is well within reach.  He also makes efforts to facilitate experiences outside of the classroom to engage you in using the language and observing Japanese Culture.

Shikimachi-sensei is wonderful! Does his best to help his students truly grasp the language and not just memorize enough to get by. One of the most genuine professors I've had, comes to class everyday with a vibe that makes learning this intense language fun!

Best professor I've had at ODU so far. Had him for JAPN111 and now have him for JAPN212. Tries to facilitate class interactions and really wants his students to pass. Funny man too. Had a bit of background in jap before taking 111 so it was easy to me, but its a hard language, so study. Often lets out class a bit early on fridays

Weekly quizzes were similar to the easiest optional HW problems so doing the HW will help a lot. Practice midterm very similar to the real one (if anything the real one was easier). Final was reasonably harder than the practice final. Would've liked more examples and fewer proofs in lectures. Good curve at the end considering a decent average (77).

Professor Saito was good in the beginning, you have a quiz every week, one midterm, and a final. So you have to be on top of your game. He says that the quizzes are based on specific chapters, but they are not. The co-class is an amazing help.

Weekly quizzes (40%), 1 Midterm (20%), Final (40%). Quizzes weren't too bad thanks to the TA, but assigned hw also helped a lot to prepare for it. Midterm and Final were VERY similar to the practices he released, so use it to study/prepare. Grading was pretty lenient as well as curve. Not the best, but definitely better than my old math professors.

Optional homework which is all textbook problems that he does not provide solutions for. Lecture recordings sometimes just went missing or didn't have audio and he never accommodated. Was completely out of reach for the past few weeks INCLUDING FOR THE FINAL. He knows his calc but avoid him if you can. If you try, you'll be able to get a good grade

He explains the concepts fine, however, his examples are always way too simple compared to the problems he gives on the quizzes. He would usually use simple polynomials for his examples during lectures, but the problems we were asked on the quizzes always include trig. functions.

Tough course, but a good professor. His lectures and homework are very helpful for quizes and tests. The main point I dislike his class is the quizes every week, which requires you to keep up with the class tightly.(But on the other hand it encourages you to work hard) As he said the grade system is flexible enough, nice curve and drop for quizes.
Tough class. Very generous curve. Practice midterm was similar to actual midterm. Practice final not so similar and decently hard.
Tough concepts that were made even more difficult, only graded by 3 things, a weekly quiz thats 40% of your grade, a midterm thats 20% and a final thats 40%

Thick accent makes and already difficult course unlearnable, joined with a tendency to over use proofs. Unnecessarily complicates  topic, and leaves foundations weak. No use of technology & uses blackboards, means that it is difficult to see his work, and thus makes this class even more difficult. I learnt more from the Youtube than lectures. 0/5

Professor was okay. Very proof-heavy and doesnt use a lot of examples in his lectures. This can make the lectures very confusing. Class was graded on weekly quizzes(40%), one midterm(25%)and one final(40%). If you keep up on the optional homework it shouldnt be too bad but definitely wasnt my favorite professor.
Lowkey this guy's lectures are so comprehensible and he's a little funny so I really enjoy his lectures. He spells things out and his lectures are very logical.

Professor Saito was wonderful, he always put lots of effort into his lectures and one could tell he cares a lot about helping people learn this material. He's the kind of professor that seems to have an extensive knowledge of a variety of subjects, but he didn't gloss over the basics. He's very sweet & passionate about teaching!

Saito presented the material in a clear and effective way during his lectures. Weekly homework was optional, and weekly quizzes given in discussion sections were fair. So far one of the better math professors I have had at this university.
Lecture is dense and homework is hard, but learned a lot. Nice curve.

I think professor Saito was a great professor! His lectures were straight forward and easy to understand... His grading scheme wasn't hard either, just do some of the optional homework + understand what he said in lecture and you'll likely get 10/10 for his quizzes (which weren't hard, and not to mention were 40% of your grade!) Highly recommend!
Awesome!

His class is based on exams and quizzes, where the weekly quizzes and the final are each worth 40% of the grade and the midterm is worth 20% of the grade. His weekly quizzes are similar to his optional homework, so study those if you want to ace them. He also drops the lowest two quiz scores. The midterm and final is similar to the practice exams.

Absolutely LOVED Dr. Saito. He deeply cares for his students and is very accessible during office hours. The quizzes arent too difficult, and homework is optional. I like that he uses chalkboard - its easier to take notes and allows you to look back at parts you might've missed. This does mean you need to attend lecture tho. Overall, a real gem!

He is a nice professor who, I believe, completely understands the topic and is very effective at explaining the hard sections. He even goes back and reviews 21A when we have to recall certain formulas, theorems, etc... I would definitely take him as a professor again if I could. Also, he tends to make subtle jokes that make you laugh. Great guy!
Weekly quizzes saved me. Doesn't give many practice exams for the midterm and final. His accent is thick but easy to get used to after a couple weeks.

The homework isn't due, but you should do it. Quizzes aren't hard if you do the homework or pay attention to the lecture. He has an accent, but it isn't bad. The only issue is that he writes on the chalkboard and in cursive, so you have to go to his class in able to get notes and understand the lecture. Also, the lectures are very informative.

Good lectures, does a good job explaining theory to students then actually does examples of what he's teaching to better explain what he's teaching. Weekly quizzes are strongly based on the homework, which is optional, and midterms and final are very similar to his practice exams. Straight forward grading and class.

I LOVED Saito. Took him after failing my first quarter. He wrote everything down on the chalkboard, his accent is a little thick but you get used to it. He uses a specific type of variable writing form, learn it quick because he grades tough on that aspect. Other than that, it was a very straight forward class. Would take any math class he offered.

Great lectures, great division of sections to really show you how everything works. Online mathworks hw plus textbook problems which help most. Quizzes every week  - CRAM BEFORE and just do it, learn it, because they matter.

Quizzes were tough but most people did reaaaally bad so just try to do better than most. The tests were almost the same as the practice ones thankfully. I didn't go to lecture but I understand he mainly just rambles about stuff, just learn everything online and you'll do fine lol.

Professor Saito has a good knowledge of the subject and really cares about his students. He does have an accent as mentioned below, but he writes out what he says on the board, so it wasn't a big deal for me. Class is set up like this: weekly quizzes, one midterm, one final, and online homework. Practice exams were pretty helpful.

Professor Saito's 21C class was one I would take again. He is very enthusiastic in lecture when teaching and it shows that he really cares about the subject matter he is teaching. He makes the material fairly understandable but you should still use online resources to thoroughly apply it. He makes you work for your grade but the class is rewarding.

Prof Saito is ok, he doesn't lecture with examples. Mostly proofs, which get confusing. Gotta learn the application yourself. Graded hmwk (20%) is easy, but weekly quizzes (35%) got tough. Midterm and final practice exams were similar to the real things. Good curve this quarter. His accent isn't bad, but the way he teaches isn't straightforward

Terrible. His accent is bad enough but he is also just a bad lecturer. He actually prints out the textbook pages and just writes it on the board with chalk and explains very little. He only did proofs for the most part with a few examples in class. Online homework was terribly hard and time consuming. Tests were kinda hard but he is a tough grader.
Knows the subject well, but grading was hard and no helpful comments were given, or any indication of which part of the problem was wrong

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. I decided to take him because I thought he couldn't be THAT bad... but little did I know. His accent is terrible, good luck understanding him. He legit ONLY  does proofs in lecture, he maybe did like 7 examples throughout the whole course. Quizzes every week that are BRUTAL and he is notorious for harsh grading and no curve.

I was forced to take 21C with him because I could not enroll into Marx's class. He is a good guy who helped me to remake homework but I cannot understand his lecture because of his accent. His quizzes were brutal.

I took him for 21C, I found that he put no effort into teaching and showed no passion for the subject. I was seriously injured prior to a quiz that required me to go to the emergency room and he didn't allow me to remake the quiz. His exams are brutal, if you make a tiny arithmetic mistake early on in a question you will loose 90% of the credit

I took him for 21C, there were weekly quizes which partial credit was rarely given for so they were brutal, they are also worth 30% of your grade. There was also 3 homeworks a week worth 20% of your grade. He's like the old guy from Mulan, you can't understand a single word this guy says and his lectures were mostly useless.

All he does  during class is reading his lecture notes. He doesn't go through any exercise problems with students. He explains to you how you should solve the little "examples" in his lecture notes instead of actually solving them. Homework for this quarter was mainly MATLAB problems, which he never lectured any!

Taking with him is a good choice for those who consider pursuing a degree or career related to math and engineering . If you ask for easiness , I would say he is not a tough grader although  it also depends on your math background and how much effort you want to put in.

Taking with him is really a good choice for those who consider pursuing a degree or career related to math and engineering . If you ask for easiness , I would say he is not a tough grader although  it also depends on your math background and how much effort you want to put in.
Saito is just a great guy. Taking classes with him will not be a walk in the park but I have nothing bad to say about him.
Great guy.  Gave practice midterm and final, curve very generous.  A little bit of an accent but still understandable.
So bad

Saito was a so-so professor - nothing to write home about. It helped that 20% of the grade for WebWork, and his lectures were easy to read later on if you take notes exactly as he writes them. That being said, lectures were very boring, and weekly quizzes (being 30% of the grade) were killer. The final also made our class cry internally. Curves.

Saito has a lot of trouble conveying new ideas to students because he spends all of lecture proving an equation rather than using it using one example. His tests are very difficult and the final was surprising bad, the average was a 54%. There is only one midterm and final though. Quizzes are worth 30% of your grade so don't skip discussion.

Saito is absolutely horrendous in trying to convey concepts to students, but you can't blame him due to the language barrier. Although his lectures frustrated me more than it helped me, his enthusiasm for math had me laughing for days and his humor is pretty on point. Honestly, take Saito if you have a background in math. His personality is great.
Terrible lecturer, terrible tests. A very bad experience.

His tests were way tougher than expected, I didn't do so hot on them but his grading scale was very generous so I ended up doing alright in the class overall. He did not curve for our class which I know angered a lot of kids, but since he drops your lowest quizhomework, it isn't too bad. He gets a little theoretical though so I preferred the book.
Honestly don't take him, he is terrible. No clarity, the test are nothing like the homework's or quizes. just avoid at all cost.

his lectures are very straight forward and explain well. if you copy everything on the board, you will have everything you need to help on the homework, which is 3 assignments per week and there are 4 problems per assignment. he also gave us a practice midterm which was almost exactly like the midterm.

He is a solid professor and a man with a passionate heart about teaching math.  He might not be very good at explaining conceptual ideas during lectures, however he is a very nice guy to talk to if you have questions. HW and Quizzes are part of your grade, which I liked. Very good blackboard writing and would recommend to take him!

He is a solid professor and a man with a passionate heart about teaching math.  He might not be very good at explaining conceptual ideas during lectures, however he is a very nice guy to talk to if you have questions. HW and Quizzes are part of your grade, which I liked. Very good blackboard writing and would recommend to take him.

He's doesn't explain concepts very well. The quizzes and WebWorks were OK, but they were annoying and some were kinda hard. Same with the midterm. You might think things are going well until you take the final which is 35% of your grade. The final is ridiculously hard and I dropped a letter grade after the final. THERE WAS NO CURVE FOR THE CLASS!

Not the best at explaining topics that involve visualization but pretty good with other topics. Nice guy and always willing to help. Extremely passionate about math. The only math prof I've had that asks questions involving proofs. Midterm this quarter was too easy (81% average). Quizzes can be tricky. Average was too high so barely a curve.
It is a horrible professor. His lecture is not helpful at all. The webwork sucks and meaningless. The worst professor I've ever seen.

Saito presents the material very well. He is a good lecturer and has a loud voice which makes up for the fact that he has a little bit of an accent. Weekly quizzes are fair, WebWork is slightly annoying but that goes with any professor. His exams are difficult but are also fair in my opinion. Study, keep up, and attend lectures. They're worth it.
Useful lectures. He has an accent but it's easy to understand what he's saying. Webwork problems are annoying though. His quizzes and tests are insanely hard but he grades very generously.

Fairly bland lectures from computer. Seems more focused on going through his notes.  Homework is 3-6 problems which may take a while to finish. MATLAB problems are fairly easy. Tests may include "good exercise" parts of lecture notes. Not enough topics on applied aspects of linear algebra. Wish there were more experiments for us to do with MATLAB

Didn't like his style of lecture. He has everything prewritten on his tablet and just stands in front of the class and reads/explains what's on his notes. Very fast. While he's lecturing, the material doesn't make much sense but he does post it online and it's a good resource when you reread them. His tests are easy and hw is somewhat applied.

Professor Saito is a fairly good professor-he progresses through the material at a good pace and does both example problems and proofs in class. HW is via WebWork. Tests are very similar to the practice exams and are pretty fair. A word of caution-previous raters noted a "generous curve", but this quarter there was essentially no curve at all.

Saito is a very good professor, I jst got a solid C for his class, but overall, the grading is fare, the lecture is sort of interesting, he sometimes shows pictures/research that related to the material he is teaching. fun class.

You know you have a good teacher when you can look back on your notes after not understanding in lecture, then read the notes more and understand. The notes he gave in class had WORDS with all the equations so you actually know what the theory is behind it. He's an awesome teacher, homework helps your grade, and I'd recommend Saito any day
very good professor. knowledgeable, and good lecturer. generous curve

A pretty good lecturer, I really liked him. All of the stuff he goes over during class is relevant to the course and is going to be on the test. There is weekly quizzes and online hw (20%) helps ur grade. There are some tricky questions on his test. I would recommend you to take him if u have to take 21c.
It was a really easy class (me being an engineer).  I reccomend him, a good 21 series prof.  Accent is a little challenging, but I overcame it.

Nothing applied about this class. Lectures completely theoretical and unhelpful. Tests are not representative of material. Boring as can be. unfair tests. This class is just memorizing solutions from the solutions manual. his notes are worthless, never does examples.

Saito rocks man. He is one of the most generous calculus professors. His midterm and final were challenging but the curve was so good that it didn't even matter. Take him if you can, he truely is one of the best.

He is the best teacher i had for math 21 series. He explains everything well and makes sure everyone understand. Make sure you study his practice midterm and understand it. because his midterms and finals are based on his practice tests. And you should be fine.

Saito does OWNS YOU!!! very good teacher that gives good examples for everything he teaches. Like every other math professor he tries to prove every theorem, which is tough to follow. Homework online is easy, but weekly quizes get annoying. Go to office hours because hardly anyone does and he and TA's are very helpful.

I have been blessed to take saito this quarter. The Curve was huge, and he is really a good teacher. The only thing that bothered me was the weekly quizzes. Final was pretty hard and midterm was tough, but again huge curve. Study practice exams. SAITO SENSEI!!!
He's the first mat teacher I've had who has really organized lectures.  Examples aren't stupidly easy so they actually help. What's really annoying is that we have a quiz in every discussion.
i think he is the best math professor i have after i came to davis...he explains things very well..and gives examples to help you to understand
Saito 0wns you! Great teacher and the exams are good.
He talks really fast and is sometimes hard to understand. His test arent that bad though.

Saito-sensei exudes mathematical genius. He taught MAT 167 Fall 2002 I believe with the intention of giving us more applications than theory, but we did mostly theory. Linear algebra isn't hard at all, thanks to him. [Pio]

So, there is NO curve in this class. Exams were difficult and all it is, is one final and one midterm and lab. A lot of students did horrible on the first exam and he did not curve. If you do bad on one exam, raising your grade is VERY hard. Beware of this.

Dr. Yamanaka is a great professor who is passionate about insect (fruit flies). Lectures are interesting and informative, he relates the class material to real world research. If you go to lectures, take notes, and study before the exams you will do great.

Professor Yamanaka is a great professor. He makes insect physiology easy to understand by comparing them to our own body. He's very easy to pay attention because of the amount of enthusiasm he has in his voice. You do not need to memorize the types of insects, just general idea of how their body works (stimuli, chemicals, organs, digestive system)

kanaboshi was honestly a good professor it was just the class was pretty hard. your grade consists mostly of the tests so if you dont do good on those you wont do good in the class. he also cold calls in class so you have to read the cases he gives you to read for class. the class was interesting overall just pretty hard

he's okay but he makes you watch every single lecture video, and he checks, or you will fail. his slideshows also have gaps in them that you need to fill in like a high school class. but also, half his course is pass/fail so you wont be able to see your grade until they're posted after the term ends and he calculates the percentage :/

Dr K is one of my favorite professors. He is super knowledgeable and will make sure you understand the material if you ask for another explanation. I took AP Gov in high school, so the class wasn't too hard, but if you are new to politics and law then it might be difficult. All tests are open note and if you do the study guide you'll do great.

Prof. Kanaboshi is both entertaining and engaging. When you first have him his accent is kind of tricky to understand, but you'll get it over time. He has a very good attitude and is personal with the students. His workload is pretty heavy; he had us read 1-5 court cases per week, so just be ready to dive into politics with him.

This Professor is very passionate about what he teaches. However he is one of those professors who thinks his class is the only class you are taking. He expects nothing less than perfection and he grades on that scale as well. I took the online course and it was very textbook and video heavy, and you must watch all the videos for credit, he checks!

Professor K is sometimes difficult to understand but overall wants to help you succeed as much as he can along with being very passionate about the subject. His class is very lecture heavy, but he is very enthusiastic and hilarious. UTILIZE HIS OFFICE HOURS THEY WILL HELP YOU A LOT! My main problem was that his expectations were always very unclear

Although it was a little hard to understand him at first, it got easier throughout the semester. He is very funny and caring and he makes sure you understand things before moving on. All of the tests were open note which was very nice.

Three exams (including final) makeup 60% of your grade BUT they are open note. You can use anything on the exams so long as it's printed out. He is very funny and very caring. Always asks if we understand the material and encourages questions. If you're okay with more reading and ready to put in work, he's an amazing professor.

I think that Prof. K is a great person; however, his HNR class is difficult. He added in fun videos to help us learn court cases which were nice but his exams are very difficult (though open note) and there is a lot of reading court cases in his class.

One of my favorite professors I have had! He is so caring towards his students, offering extensions for assignments when needed. For the essay we had he provided very detailed feedback which was very helpful. The tests were all open note and not too hard, he also curves if the class average is below 85%. He made lectures interesting too!

I have a love hate relationship with this professor. But the tests are open book open note, and he seems to really care about his students. If you're struggling in his class go to him for help and he will help you. Also do the readings before class he likes to randomly ask people about the readings.

So many lectures and so much reading. Luckily he breaks down the lectures and uses closed caption so note taking is a lot easier. DO NOT SKIM LECTURES. He knows and you will fail. Take notes on EVERYTHING in the lectures or you will fail. 3 exams, 6 quizzes, 6 discussion boards and replies. You have to study, there is NO way around it.

Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. You're graded based off of three tests, no other grades. He's extremely unorganized, very hard to understand, and his instructions are unclear. His test questions were very obscure and had nothing to do with what we learned. A nice guy out of the classroom and that's where he should stay. Good luck.

You have to watch all the online lectures in full or you will not recieve credit for that weeks assignment. The readings are hard and difficult to understand. Put in a lot of effort and youll pass. But miss a day and youre screwed.

Dr. Kanaboshi was OK. He grades somewhat harshly. Way to much work for an asynchronous online course. Requires you to watch long lecture videos. If you watch the videos and take notes you should do well. Very time consuming class.

He was the only professor who actually tried to make sure we could pay attention to his videos instead of just recording. He edited really well and gave us a chance to watch the videos on our own time.

A lot of people in my honors sequence didn't like him, but I really enjoyed his class! Since it was a completely online class, he recorded lectures and posted them. What I did was just type out word for word what he said and then used those notes on exams. Super easy to get a good grade that way! A lot of lectures but completely doable, no stress.

For your sake, avoid Professor Kanaboshi. He was the worst professor I had this semester. His grading makes very little sense and seems pretty random. The exams are worded really badly and the final consists of an exam, a research paper, and a presentation with no criteria to base it off of.

This class was supposed to be an introductory class but he taught it with an expectation that we should already know the content. He takes a long time to grade assignments and the exams and writing assignments are really tough. Avoid this class with him.

Despite this class being online, there was a lot of useful information which required a ton of reading. Personally, I crammed this class like no other and did half of the semesters work in about a week and the tests are usually pretty easy. He is a very tough grader on papers and written responses though. He won't grade or respond fast.

He is a nice guy but this class was extremely difficult. He posts videos instead of a live lecture but theyre usually not up until late at night with little time to watch before class. The exams are open note but really tough and he gives feedback for the final paper that doesnt make any sense. Funny professor but would not recommend him.

For this past semester, his course was basically asynchronous which was extremely helpful because you could read the court cases and watch the lecture videos at your own pace. He is always willing to explain something through email if you're confused or are just looking for extra help. The court cases can be VERY overwhelming and time consuming.

He was really good with his videos, that was the only way I actually studied, and he was funny as well. The fact that his section was often asynchronous helped, but we had deadlines. I'd definitely take his class again.

Dr. K is an incredible kind and caring prof. I took honors law with him and he made it very easy to understand and even shortened the cases for us. The only downside is that your grade is 3 exams with 16 questions each. If you miss even one or two questions, you fall below an A.

Prof. Kanaboshi is an amazing professor. I looked forward to attending his class because he makes the material fun. The book is mandatory and pretty expensive, although it is impossible to pass the class without it. Exams are open-book, partially multiple choice and short answer. This class was very time demanding but worth it.

Kanaboshi is funny, outgoing, and nice. I really enjoyed his class. He made the material interesting, and kept the lectures upbeat & fun. Exams are open note, and he guides you through the assignments.

Must pay attention during lecture. He moves fast, but he tries to make sense. Test are open note, but you need to know the material well. Takes attendance, and participation is rated. Overall not a hard class, just takes more effort than most.

Tells you exactly what you need to do, curves tests, assignments minimal and easy, attendance is mandatory because he randomly calls on students to discuss cases which is not as hard or scary as you think coming from a shy quiet student, tests are hard even tho open book open notes, you have to listen and take notes, read if you want to pass

Kanaboshi is one of the best profs I've had. I had him for both 302 and 305 and would highly recommend him. As long as you do the reading assignments and take good notes in class there is absolutely no way you should not do well in this class. He tells you exactly what to highlight and all exams are open note and open book. Plus he is hilarious

I took professor Kanaboshi for two classes 302 and 305. They were similar in structure having 3 exams and two assignments each. However the he graded completely different for the two. He is much more relaxed in CJ 305. I wouldn't necessarily recommend CJ 305 but I would certainly advise not taking CJ 302 with Kanaboshi way harder than his 305.

Professor Kanaboshi has an accent that is hard to understand at first but you get used it. He curves all the exams to 80% which is nice, and the test questions come from the lecture slides! If you get the chance take him!
Great professor! very funny and makes the class interesting. Knows his materials and explains it very well.. Very respectful and available outside of class. I would take him again for sure.

Dr. Kanaboshi was very funny, however the class was very dry despite his effort to make it fun. Attendance is a must because he will randomly call on students to discuss the reading, therefore the readings are almost a must. Be prepared to highlight A LOT! The exams are open note, open book but still very difficult. Be organized before the exam!

Must read to pass the class! Easy tests as long as you read bc they are open note and textbook. Going to class is graded and helps a lot. Nice and funny prof. Gives good examples and teaches very well. Just a heavy accent to get used to.

Great professor! He makes you read a lot of Supreme Court cases and goes over them in class. He teaches it law-school style, so he calls out students and has them explain the case and significant findings from the case. If you don't read, you lose points. Class is based off of participation (read and show up), 2 exams, and a 20 page paper.

My favorite prof I have had at GV! His accent becomes easy to understand after a couple classes. 3 tests and one one-page paper. He even raises grades to meet a specific class average. I found his class very easy, and he is a genuinely funny and guy. Makes jokes, gets grades back quick, and even gives out candy. Ended with over 100% in the class.

I was worried about the accent but it was super clear after just a week of getting used to it. He is hilarious and his voice kind of sounds like stitch from lilo and stitch. He likes to act things out and use profanity which kept the class upbeat. The tests were easy as well as the pop quizzes and one paper. Questions on tests come from lectures!

He was pretty good at explaining the material, his accent threw me off sometimes though but not a lot. He curves all of his tests to be at least 82% so if the class average on a test is 70% he will curve it by 12% which is really nice. No homework really, the reading is "required" but he never really talks about the book readings at all.

Has an accent which takes some getting used to the first few class sessions, but not terrible. Very knowledgeable and funny. Lectures are easy to follow. The tests are pretty tough, I study very hard and still do not do as well as I hope.
Really funny but he's asian so hard to understand at some points but if you don't understand he is not offended if you ask to repeat.

Really funny, but serious professor. Grading is straightforward, just three exams and a score for attendanceparticipation. He lets you miss two lectures without penalty. Tests are open bookopen noteopen anything, but are still challenging, so you still have to study. Just do the readings and study for the tests and you'll be fine.

I liked Professor Kanaboshi. He had a strong accent but you will get used to it. There will be a lot of reading! You have two writing assignments which are easy and are a page long. But the only draw back I have with him are his test. I struggled with his test. They were very detailed and difficult.

One of my favorite CJ professors. He is hilarious and his class is very fair. Do the reading and read the cases. Tests are graded on a curve. Not an easy A but a good class if you will put in a little work.
I love this guy! His personality makes the class interesting. He is always there if you need any help or have any questions.

I enjoyed this professor.  You get used to his accent after the first couple days.  (his accent and personality add to the class).  Class is based on the book since most of it is case based.  Does check attendance with note cards.   If you show up to class and do the reading, there is absolutely no reason you shouldn't do well.  He grows on you.
Make sure you practice.
Required course for non-keyboard music majors.

Took Hakutani for Piano for Non-Majors. As long as you have your practice book and practice a little outside of class, you will be fine. Hakutani always makes sure to give suitable feedback to always improve the phrasing of your music and works with you where you are. Tests are in-class participation, so a rather easy A.

I took Hakutani for Piano 1 and 2 without any prior knowledge of piano. He worked with me and didn't intimidate me out of learning the piano. Funny, friendly, and great teacher! He's a very easy grader if he sees you trying. He's super talented and smart! Sometimes the theory part goes over my head, but he understands that and worked with me.

Great professor! Really interesting lectures. Overall, a great class.

Professor Bronfenbrenner is very well respected in her field and she makes that very clear within her class. She's very knowledgeable but isn't the best at conveying that knowledge. She is tough but amazing. Her expertise is unparalleled. She really is one of the best at ILR.

Dr. Bronfenbrenner is knowledgeable and experienced. However, she does not communicate that knowledge well at all. Her grading is ambiguous, she changes her mind without telling you, she only speaks in mumbles or yelling. The class could have been great, but she shouldn't be teaching anymore.
Kate B is one of the best professors at ILR. She's tough but if you take her class you'll learn a lot and be well prepared to go into the labor movement.

Without a doubt the most important labor-focused professor in the ILR School. Professor Bronfenbrenner is a wonderful and kind professor who is extremely knowledgeable and well respected in her field. Very knowledgable, but not a great teacher. Assumes a lot of prior knowledge. Unclear on expectations. Kate is truly an inspirational professor who teaches extremely relevant courses for those who aspire to go into the labor movement/labor relations. Kate may not have explicit lessons plans but she is obviously a clever, passionate professor. Extremely Helpful Professor who teaches challenging classes. Attend class, ask questions, show interest, and you will do well.
You people don't get it. She's just as tough to those of us on the labor side. If you want to learn no one teaches it better but don't expect an easy A.

Professor Kate is amazing! She takes the time to engage with each student and is very accommodating. I have tremendously improved my writing skills because of her and would highly recommend to take her class.

I took FWS 1380 (the only course code choice was 1420, so I had to choose that) with Professor Navickas, and it was really amazing. The discussions were always super interesting, with not a lot of reading and a very doable workload. It was my favorite class of the semester.

pretty straightforward class and professor. do readings, understand readings, tested on readings. grading was a little vague but whatever

Such an amazing lecturer. She explains everything so well and clearly. Definitely recommend her for labor law!

Professor Griffith grades based on a prelim, legal writing assignment, and a final. She is very clear in class on how to approach the prelim and the TA is very helpful for questions about cases. Prof Griffith is a spectacular teacher. She clarified all of the course material and clearly explained the expectations for the course. 2 tests and 1 legal research assignment. Prof Griffith is amazing - always makes sure her students are clear and understand the material. 2 exams one paper. Make sure you take really good notes in class, study, and you'll do great. She is overrated on here because the other professors teaching labor law are unbearable. Her class is significantly more work than other labor law professors due to the in class tests. She is a fair and reasonable person and doesn't have the elitist superiority many other professors do. There are pros and cons to her course, weigh them and decide.

really boring before the 1st midterm but it gets better.  She takes specific notes about your exam so you really know what to improve/understand your grade.  very friendly and helpful and brings in amazing guest speakers. def reccommend for labor law

Great professor. I didn't have any interest in labor law but this class was one of best classes I've taken. A really awesome professor who knows her stuff, and knows how to get students to learn. Made the class clear and rewarding even though i previously had no interest in law.  The research paper is pretty straight forward, and shouldn't give you trouble unless you wait until the end. And the tests are really clear, she doesn't give trick questions.

Best ILR law professor. There's a ton to study and some of the stuff you think wont be on the exams will be on there. The 1st exam is tougher and the paper is tough, but i think her final curve is strong. she's a great teacher and really sweet. do yourself a favor and take her.
What a great gal, she will answer any and every question you have during class and will slow down and review certain cases if the class seems to have trouble with it.

Excellent. Highly recommend any of her courses. Not the easiest grader, but expectations are made clear and if you put in the work, you'll have no trouble getting a good grade. Best Teacher I have had in the ILR school,  Hands Down. She is very fair and interesting. Great job engaging the class. Tests are extremely fair. Awesome. Definitely take this class with this professor.

I've taken a number of Professor Griffith's classes.  She is always fair and engaging.  She is very willing to help anyone who goes to her office hours.  Definitely the best professor I have had in ILR; probably the best I have had at Cornell.

Professor Griffith was a great teacher. She was very helpful during office hours and always asked students if they had questions during class. She was always willing to further explain cases discussed in class or details went over about specific cases. I definitely reccommend her course!

Clear, accessible, and fair. Anyone who takes the time to see her in OHs knows that she genuinely cares for her students. Presents all sides of policy debates. IMO, the best labor law prof.  Griffith strikes the perfect balance between Gold and Lieberwitz--her classes are not overbearing, but still rewarding and educational.
She's very clear and precise. make sure you pay attention in class. The cases are pretty interesting, and I thought I would hate the class but I actually enjoyed it.

she does a great job at introducing students to law and learning how to apply it. she gives exams for which you can cram but you must have gone to class and have done the reading. you will leave her class with the ability to read and pull out legal principles from cases, but with gold you will know much more but suffer more.

She is so helpful if you go to office hours. You have to do the reading to even think about passing her class. The exam questions are fair. Fair grader, nice lady. She and the TA were willing to help if you needed it. Griffith knows what she is talking about. You learn a lot in the class. It is very straight forward. The tests and paper are very fair. Required reading every class (if you don't do it, the class is can difficult). She encourages everyone to speak.  Recommended.

Worse class ever!

Professor McCullough is awesome! She can be a tough grader, but if you go to her during office hours she'll work with you on your writing. Her class *is* work (it's not super easy,) but if you come to class and go to her office hours you should be able to get a good grade.
I've take McCoullough for FGSS 201 and several other courses - I'd take anything she taught.
best teacher ive had at cornell. no question about it.
One of the best.  She deserves more credit than she's getting.
Interesting discussions but awful selection of material.
too many papers and revisions, hard grader, boring books

Easy class! She is very nice despite what others say, as long as you show up and don't talk during class she will give you a good grade. Lectures are really boring, but for an easy grade I would say it was worth it.

Wicked easy, all the tests are stright out of the notes. Very nice and available for help if you need it. Kinda boring, but if you take the notes you should do well.

Genuinely one of the nicest professors. SO kind and understanding, very accommodating if you're going through something & communicate w/ her. Easy grader, but a lot of assignments, so this class could be time consuming

She is super sweet. I loved her class. I took her in the spring of 2021. Class was online async. I paper and a final project. weekly discussion boards and reading annotations. Overall, a good experience.

Professor Iwata is a fantastic professor and has an extremely clear grading criteria when it comes to weekly homework assignments as well as the midterm and final projects which are not very difficult. Loved her, such a great professor who cares about students/she wants you to pass. As long as you do the weekly reading annotation (it's very easy) and the discussion post (also easy) you will pass. Professor Iwata is genuinely one of the kindest profs I have ever had. Ridiculously easy class. Probably the most lenient grader I have ever had. As long as you submit something you're guaranteed to get a B on the assignment and it doesn't take much to get an A. Super sweet and her IH2 class was not overwhelming. You just annotate and write in discussion posts, a paper or two, and thats pretty much it. She is amazing! I took her for IH1. She really cares about her students if you communicate with her. There are no quizzes, tests, or papers. I really enjoyed Professor Iwata. Take her!!!

I loved having Prof Iwata for IH2. The class structure is simple. Read the texts and write a collection of thoughts after each text is done. Take Jessie
She is a nice person and teacher, and not a tough grader. Sometimes, I don't even know why she gave me a 90+ or even 100...

Professor Iwata is the sweetest human being alive, and will encourage you to be the best student you can be and teach you a lot if you apply yourself. Makes IH fun and manageable.

Professor Iwata is amazing. She made Intellectual heritage a smooth sailing experience. She doesn't give quizzes she just does note collections which are fairly easy if you keep up with the reading. She is an amazing teacher who really cares about her students! The class is completely participation based but she won't grind your gears about it - talking just makes it more fun! The journals she assigns are super easy: you only need to do a 1 page analysis and she grades very lightly. She is really such a kind person- I recommend her to everyone

She's hard not to like as both a professor and person! There are really no wrong answers in discussions and writing assignments as long you put thought into your contributions. Projects are not bad at all. The class can get boring if you don't participate simply because some people want to talk the whole time. Overall, awesome choice for Mosaics!

Professor Iwata is the sweetest and most thoughtful teacher I have had. She listens to what everyone has to say without criticism or judgement. This is the first class that I have had that I feel totally comfortable to participate. Some advice I would give is to participate often to form a good relationship her early on (you'll likely get As).

Such a nice person! As a teacher, she really knows her stuff and she values your own thoughts as opposed to just those of the authors and the critics. The journal assignments are a lot of work, but there are no wrong answers if you put quality thought into them. If you don't participate, class will be boring, so try to speak up when you can.

Jessie is the BEST: caring, knowledgeable, and so sweet. Rewards creativity and original thought. Always willing to help, very accessible outside of class. Fair grader: we even decided our own participation grades! Very passionate about subject matter and course texts. Best professor I've had so far at Temple, hands down. Take her!

Jessie rewards in-depth thought, in any direction, very well in her grading. She is very nice and open to differing viewpoints. Easy A if you use analysis instead of summary in your work.
She is amazing, kind and helpful. The grades will be fine as long as you show up every class and do the assignments. Take her!

Prof. Jessie is a sweet lady, she's always there for you. You have to do a lot of assignments but it's not that hard. You have to do blogs pretty much every week. Intense college level reading, reading notes due everyday of class along with weekly blogs on readings. She is a relatively easy grader, but there are so few grades if you do poorly on one you are probably not going to do well in the class. Personally, I didn't enjoy her class although I have to say she does force you to look at things differently.

She is awesome.She makes you look things differently.Her class was politics of power,money,disability,race,gender etc and how they affect individuals in the society.You will enjoy her class take it.She is tougher grader so make effort.This was ESL class but she made is very pleasant for everybody.Remember to blog.
She defiantly a great professor! She prefers a creative portfolio and grades fairly. Choose her class this semester too. She is one of my favorite professors at Temple!

weekly blog, no essays, some quizzes, involving discussions, very understanding. honestly, a fun class instead of a dreadful boring lecture.will try to incite debate b/w students.looks at all perspectives in a discussion. take her if possible.

Jessie is a very nice and energetic person!  Her class was great up until the last month, when a lot of previously non-discussed work was due, and our class was thrown into a frenzy. She is such a nice person I must say. She is always talking about the books and you don't need to read the books for this class. Great teacher. Little wacky and tries to be funny, but she is caring, nice, and easy to talk to. Makes the class easy and fun and I enjoy going to it every other day. Take her! She is great.
really helpful. wanted to reccomend her to other people. shes a very cheerful person. helps u whenever u need it. Easy class!
Ms. Iwata is a great person, always willing to help you whenever you want. However, the class was pointless. I had classmates who never read any of the books and still passed with an A.

I really don't like IH, but she's an okay professor. All I have to say is read the assigned readings, do most of the assigned blogs, participate, and come to class regularly and you'll pass with no less than a B. But the woman is a little on the wacky side. Most IH professors are.

As long as you pay attention you'll be fine.

If you have to take math 231, take Dr. Taalman. As long as you read the textbook and seek out help when you need it, you will do well; she sets the class up in a way where your grade will not be destroyed for not doing well on one quiz/test. The material is difficult, but its calculus, so what more can you expect. SHOW UP TO THE LECTURES!!!!!!!!

She's AWESOME. You can retake up to 6 quizzes during the entire semester, and every Friday she holds help sessions for anyone who wants to sign up for them. The only mandatory class is on Wednesdays, and her class is super flexible. Very caring woman as well.

I had her for my freshman year in math 231 it was a very casual class. You can definitely pass without reading much of the text and there are a four question quiz at the end of each week all being open note and based around the homework. She was a good professor but it does feel really self taught when you aren't paying attention.

She's not great, but she may be the best option for MATH 232. Unfortunately, a large portion of the class is spent on her showing us proofs while we will never need to use the proofs on the quizzes. Often the class gets lost and completely zones out. She does still explain some concepts clearly, and she is definitely better than my prof for 231.

I like Taalman as a person, she's pretty frustrating as a professor. With basically no lecture time during class, halfway through the semester she told the class we weren't doing the reading because almost none of us understood the material from just reading the book multiple times. I get this is a hard class, but she made it exponentially harder.

Dr. Taalman is one of the most friendly and caring math professors I've ever had! That being said, her class is quite difficult as you are expected to teach yourself the entirety of the material in this course. The grading is a bit strange, but allows you to focus on only the things that are difficult for you. Great professor, hard class.

Have fun teaching yourself calculus. If you can master(3 out of 3) 15 out of 18 quizzes you will get an A in the class. The only problem is she doesn't teach and don't even get me started on the pigtails.

If you don't like flipped classrooms don't take her as a professor. I really disliked the class and thought it was awful. She had all of her office hours online so meeting in person was hard. She is nice and all but I dreaded going to her class.

The flipped classroom worked well for me. Everything was explained very well in class and all questions were answered clearly. I skipped class a lot, so I ended with a B, but if i hasn't skipped I would have gotten an A. So don't skip and you'll do really well

She spends 1 class on a section and assigns way too much homework due by the next class as if it is your only class.
