Worked like crazy and still received a D-.

Laura is very nice and wants everyone to do well, but I found her class to be the most challenging math class I've ever taken. She teaches as a flipped classroom (aka you read the material and learn it and then come to class with questions/group work).  Two tests, a final, five homework quizzes, and daily reading quizzes. Notes allowed for quizzes.

Such a nice, considerate woman but she teaches a flipped class. You're expected to read the material and teach yourself while class is focused on problems. This works for some students but you have to be motivated to do work. There are 3 tests and 5 quizzes there are also daily HW quizzes based on reading. Fair grader & gives partial test credit.

At first, i wasn't crazy about the flipped classroom thing. It's really hard at first. But after a couple weeks, it gets a lot better. It actually helped me learn a lot and I think i did better because of it. However, Im not crazy about how she isn't available much outside of class. I wish office hours were better.

Nice woman, poor teacher. Doesn't break anything down &  basically substitutes the text as the teacher. She did write the book but it's difficult to learn from it. No office hours, instead she has "online office hours" basically a big group chat that's very unproductive. Group work every class so she doesn't have to teach. A quiz a day too.

First, Laura Taalman is a very nice person. That being said, she is the worst excuse for a professor I have ever had. The entire course is self taught, she explains nothing, answers no questions, and has quizzes every single day of class. She grades you based off of how she "feels" you did, there is no reasoning behind the grades you receive.

avoid taking her at all costs. Doesnt teach at all. Thinks that group work replaces a lecture, and when she asks if you have a question, she never answers it and ignores you and asks if there is another question if it was too hard. Textbook is written by her and has multiple equations and solutions wrong. Hard tests and does not posts grade.

She's nice and very knowledgeable in math, but we don't do much during class.  Yu teach yourself everything; take your own notes from the textbook, choose what homework to do.  Although there is no "assigned homework," you have to do it in order to pass.  I highly suggest that you have a previous background in math before taking this class.

3D Printing is a lot of fun already and Laura makes even more so. She uses a relaxed teaching style and relevant technology current events to get students excited about the technology. She also challenges students to expand their creative and technical skills throughout the semester. Great for graduating seniors who need the 1 credit lab.

TAKE HER!!!! Best professor at JMU! Laura really knows her stuff and does a fantastic job explaining the material. She expects her students to come to class having read the section a head of time and then goes over the material and answers questions in class. Take good notes! You can use your notebook on tests and quizzes!

Overall, I learned a lot in her MATH 131 class but I would not recommend for students who do not have a background in AP Calculus. You are required to know EVERYTHING in the textbook, but it is up to you if you read it or not. If you are having trouble she is always there to help if you approach her and tell her your situation.
Overall good teacher, very clear about want she expects and very friendly. Always willing to help and I really enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Very independent, you kinda have to teach yourself, if you don't learn that way take someone else.  Not easy but a very fair grader!!  Very helpful if you make an effort to see her after class!!  She wants to see you succeed and if you try she will

This class is very independent because you have to read/ do A LOT of (optional) homework problems yourself. It can be difficult to follow along in class because you pretty much teach yourself and she moves quickly. However, she is more than fair with her grading and she wants you to succeed! If you're a fast learner, I would recommend her.
Great teacher who knows everything about 3d printing. Fun and everything a professor should be, take her.
Laura is the best!!!!! Take her! She is so sweet and cares.
She's a wonderful teacher! She requires that the reading be done before class but she's really helpful when you get into class! A very funny person and extremely nice. :)
This was an independent study class, and it was amazing! Dr. Taalman is incredibly helpful with anything you need, and very very knowledgeable! Fantastic teacher! Much take if you get the chance!

Math 235 isn't that easy but Taalman definitely makes it passable. She uses her own curved grading scale and you get to use your notebook for 10 or 20 minutes at the end of every test and quiz. She's also super sweet and clearly very enthusiastic about calculus. Definitely worth taking the class!

The textbooks she writes are lamentable at best. They are extremely confusing and leave the reader to figure things on their own as if they are mathematicians themselves. I have spent hours looking over problems in her textbooks (calc 3) only to seek an alternate source and grasp the content within minutes. Not worth your money to buy her texts.

She is an awesome person who is very friendly and personable. She doesn't really lecture or teach the material. She has you read her textbook and outline each section to basically learn yourself. In order to do well you have to do all the homework problems for each section andy his is time consuming. Tests/quizes are very hard. Curves though.
Laura is awesome and really nice. But exams and quizzes are the only grades in this class and they are always HARD. If you're not interested in math, this might not be the course for you.

Take Dr. Taalman! She's absolutely amazing! She wrote the textbook and knows what she's talking about. No homework, grades are based on tests and quiz's and to do well you have to put in a lot of work and effort.

Laura is the ideal professor to take Calc 235 with! She was very clear with her explanations and regardless of how stupid the question may have seemed, she was very enthusiastic to explain it so that you would understand. But homework is extremely important. Exams reflect homework problems and attendance is mandatory so you don't miss anything.

Laura is one of my favorite professors at JMU. I generally HATE math, but I loved taking this class. At first, I hated the team-based learning but it ended up helping a lot. All I have to say is DO YOUR HOMEWORK and don't fall behind. I got an A- but I worked my butt off, but you can do the same. Definitely the best calc teacher you can get.

Laura is probably one of the best professors I've had so far. We used the textbook she wrote for this class so she obviously knows what she's talking about. She's very eager to help and do whatever it takes to make sure you pass the class. The material itself is not easy, but if you do the homework and study, there is no reason you shouldn't pass!

good teacher. not too difficult of a class. but not easy either. have to learn to use latex. use latex to type up milestone homework. reading quizzes every day. the final is weighed very heavily. she's very laid back and always has office hours. i'd recommend taking this class with her. very good professor.

Laura is a really chill professor. However, I don't really like her teaching style. You have to know which questions to ask in order to get the necessary info.

Laura is a very helpful, kind, and funny (at times) professor. The class is by no means easy (it is calculus after all), but she does her best to make sure everyone makes it through with at least a C-. She uses her own book, which is very straight forward and helpful. If you pay attention & do the work you'll do just fine in the course.
She is a really cool teacher.  Take her for 245.

Self- Directed learning class, students are teaching themselves and teaching eachother but Professor Taalman helps to guide everyone along.  I think this class was very helpful when it comes to teaching and it was a very easy A

Laura is a great teacher. She is very difficult, but I took her for discrete mathematics (intro to proofs). If you are a math person then take her take her do it! She will prepare you so well for upper level math.

She only taught the class one time.  The structure of the class consists of getting in groups and all starring at each other.  Everyone is confused and she just floats around the room.  She has a great grading scale thats one thing I will give her.

I actually hate this class. I really enjoyed math until this class! It is completely student run which makes it EXTREMELY confusing! I honestly felt like I didn't accomplish anything during class. It was pointless. If she likes you you will get a good grade, if not, then you won't. She has her own grading scale...which once again is likeness based.

Dr. Taalman is incredibly tough. The class is entirely run by the students. You work on problems from the book independently and then present in front of the whole class. Only 2 tests, each containing only one question - tough because if you don't know the answer to one question, you fail. Do not take if your shy.

Laura is awesome.  She really pushes you to do work, her tests are challenging and be prepared to work for a good grade.  She doesn't use a traditional grading scale, makes up her own.  Excellent at teaching and getting material across, DO THE HOMEWORK. Take her, but be prepared to study.  I love Laura!

Laura Taalman is a great professor,young and really funny. Fairly difficult class because on tests she really asks that you understand the concepts, not just shortcuts. Attendance is only mandatory on test days. You have homework but she doesn't check it. You can turn in your homework though to boost a bad test grade. She's a very good professor.

Her class seems POINTLESS to go to. She does random attendance quizzes. She is a nice person and friendly, but I don't like the way she wrote the book. Her grading, I have to say, is pretty fair though. If you get her don't be too disappointed, it's a good nap. DO NOT buy your book from JMU, I got mine for $7 off some random website BRAND NEW!
Really good teacher.

She's AMAZING! Such a great teacher and is funny, personable, and interesting. She'll answer any question and is completely fair in grading. Her lectures are not only entertaining but also very clear and helpful! A+ Teacher!

Laura is great teacher. Our class was Origami, so most of the time we spent folding paper, but as long as you do the work, it's easy to get an A.  She's way better than a lot of the other math professors at this school and she's really laid back and helpful.

Hardest class i ever took in my entire life. I am horrible at Math but had to take this. She tries to be helpful but expects everyone to already know half the stuff she presents. Assigns a ton of homework, tests and final are extremely hard. Do not recommend.
Very hard... great professor but expects everyone to be a math major. Do the work, study hard and ask questions
She is really nice person.. She always wears a black T shirts it looks friendly to me..^^ We don't have a class in every wendseday!!

HARD, but if you are willing to do the work its worth it, helps if there are smart girls in your class to help, you know who you are ladies, great prof, need more like her here, if you do the work and go to class, she will take care of you grade-wise, she understands you don't want to retake the cla

Laura is THE BEST CALC TEACHER! she is cool as hell,you can IM her if you have homework probz and she wrote the book so she knows what she is talkin about. Too bad she had to leave on maternity. Great teacher! Very interesting class. Helps you out a lot. Have to do the homework but not always collected. Interesting class. Makes you understand Calc a lot better
Both semesters were hard but Laura is probably the best professor to teach... anything
it u never took calc, don't take this class. she is so strict, duuh she wrote the book. she is very harddddd

Laura's by far the most incredible prof i've ever had.  She's very well organized, so you always know what to expect.  The book is easy to understand because she wrote it day for review before once a week quizzes, lessons 3 days a week.  If you stay on top of the work, you'll be fine.

Laura is a great professor. She is hilarious! She is always willing to help you during her office hours.  Tests are very hard, but she curves.  A lot of work is involved for the class, but as long as your keep up with it and go for help, you'll do fine.
I love Laura!  She's so funny and her notes are really well organized.  I had already taken calc in high school and still loved her class.  Take her!

I thought Laura was one of the absolute BEST professors I've ever had in my college career. She's fun to be around in and out of class and always willing to help a student in need. She's an awesome at teaching and actually caring about her students.
Really  good teacher...class requires a lot of work but nothing unbearable...material is somewhat difficult but she is willing to help everyone..take her if you can
The best math teacher i've ever had.  Alot of work but if you actually do the homework then its not so bad.

laura is by far THE best math teacher you could have...there is a LOT of work, but she is fun, very good at explaining things and cares about her students...def go to office hours if extra help is needed!!

i hate math, but laura has made it a little more bearable. the class's pace is a little fast for me, and there is a huge amount of homework every night...tests are hard, but not unfair. i'm sure she's better than most math teachers

Kick ass professor who cares A LOT about her students.  Will help in any way possible and explain things in a variety of ways until you understand that.  Must do the reading but she wrote the book so it is easy to read... you'll love her!!!:)
hard, but you will learn alot. i suggest taking this class if you want to brush up on your math skills or if you need it for your major.  make sure to go to her office hours.

verrrrry hard class. two-semesters long so she goes into way too much detail, needlessly. if you can, take the 235 class and get it over with in one semester. otherwise, laura is VERY nice and willing to help.
Hard material and lots of work, but GREAT teacher. VERY helpful!

massive amounts of homwork, randomly collects it so you have to do it to make a decent grade. tests are killer. showing up to class, taking notes, and about 2 hours of homework/studying each night should pass you.
shoot yourself now if you have to take 231. laura is great, but the class very time-consuming and difficult.  tests are hard but fair. tons of homework. too in depth unless you are a math major.
very good teacher, she is a genius yet somehow can teach things to you in a really simplified way. a lot of homework, if you do the hw you will be fine
hard work, but well worth it. very indepth, great job puttin it all together :)
Laura is the best... she is cares about her students and knows her stuff!
Best All around Prof. ever! do HW and get her help! don't just go to class
She is a really nice lady...I feel like I learned a lot.  Take her!
A great teacher, helps you when you don't understand.  Understanding and fair.
She's an awesome teacher!  very easy to talk to in class or out!  VERY fair!
You have to work in this class, lots of hw probs, but tests are fair
gives way too much hw.. but very nice and fair
greatest math teacher ever, easy to talk to, willing to answer questions
hard class but nicest prof ever...wears combat boots & has pink hair
Best math teacher ever, totally new approah to calc, wrote the textbook!

This professor appears to lack professionalism and adequate teaching skills. His lectures are constructed under the assumption that the student has the same expert level of understanding on the topic as him. With this, he offers no assistance with the course material whatsoever. Hardest course I've taken so far at OSU, be prepared to fail.

I really like Taal, but he could improve as an instructor. He goes a little too fast in lectures, and there isn't enough review material for exams. If he would find a way to slow down the lectures a little bit and add some review material for exams, he would be a definite 5/5.

Taal is an awesome professor. I enjoyed his sense of humor and appreciated the way he made himself available to answer questions. This is a tough class. There is a lot of derivation you must be prepared poor. I'd recommend reviewing material from your algebra and calculus classes before taking this course. You learn how to use EXCEL!! Great course

Taal is one of my favorite professors at OSU. This course is pretty challenging, a lot of staff to learn. Taal is really helpful and added extra office time. Just ask questions if you are confused about the lecture. Be sure to know how to do the problem sets. Midterm and final are like PS. Labs took a lot of time but teach us how to use R and excel

Majority of class is based around controversial wildlife debates: barred owl culling, hatcheries after dam removal, removal of failing wild population of red wolves in NC. Read papers, write problem precis, evidence statements, debate with group, and write paper. Data quizzes on papers from that week. Show up to class and participate. Great class!

I would take classes with Taal again just because he is so helpful and encouraging. I failed one of the midterms, and he actually came up to me and asked if I wanted his help to study before the finals. The way he runs his class makes it math-heavy, but it's also very do-able if you pay attention and ask questions when needed.

Taal is a great guy who will reach out to you if you are struggling and need help. You can definitely go to him with questions! His exams can be difficult if math is hard for you. He puts a lot of emphasis on mathematics in his classes. I find that his voice can put me to sleep, but he makes funny comments that make up for it!
Always willing to help out, answer questions, and get to know students. You can tell he truly cares about his students and their learning. Exams were a good reflection of homeworks/practice prelims

Amazing guy. Great lectures and very approachable in and out of class. For exams, as long as you do the homework and review materials you're already very well prepared. If you get a chance to take class with him, don't hesitate!

Taking a course with Marcelo Aguiar is truly a privilege. His lectures are well-structured and inspiring. In office hours and even after lecture he is super approachable and answers all questions clearly. His exams are on par with the review materials he provides.

His notes are immaculately organized + he always provides concrete examples of the abstract/convoluted theorems that we learn. Super accessible outside of class + always answers emails + stays up to over an HOUR after class helping students. Extremely clear when answering questions. Exams are SUPER reflective of stuff covered in class. 100/10.

Professor Aguiar is definitely one of the best professors in the math department. If you pay attention in class, you should not have any problems following him and do well in the course. He would always stay after class to answer questions. If you do ask him questions, he would give an answer appropriate for your level of mathematical maturity.
80% of your grade was based on exams. The exams were really difficult and did not match the level difficulty on homework and review material.
He is amazing!

Hands down a GOAT professor. Puts an incredible amount of efforts into preparing for class and helping students. Explains things clearly and concisely so try not to miss lectures. Truly cares about his students. Questions are always welcome and help is available almost whenever. Much-appreciated accommodations were made during covid19.

Aguiar was so lovely. He encourages students to ask questions and tries to link the class to real-world examples. He has a good grasp of how much students can viably absorb in one class and usually doesn't try to overstuff the class.

He is amazing. He explains math so carefully/simply that anyone who pays attention will understand everything eventually. This was the only class where I didn't miss a single lecture because if you do you'll miss his great explanations. Go to class, do your homework, and do the exam handouts before every exam. And you'll do great

By far, this was the most amazing math professor I have ever had. Sit in one lecture and you'll see why, every definition and example he works through is explained thoroughly and instead of just giving formulas, he derives them so you really understand. I felt prepared for exams because of him. My only complaint is review sheets don't have answers.

He is a really good teacher and offers clear explanations. Although assignments are not easy, if you do go to office hours he is more than willing to help you out. He is very approachable. Try to take as many classes with him as possible. One of the nicest and genuinely concerned teachers.

Marcelo is the best teacher I've had at Cornell. His explanations are impeccable and he makes every concept in the class easy to understand. The guy loves math. If we finish class early, he'll take a few minutes to explain how what we're learning relates to cool random things in nature, like astronomy, network connectivity, biology, etc. Great guy.

Professor Friedland's lectures were great and he is very knowledgeable about the French Revolution, which was the topic of the class.

Throughout the semester, he managed to draw a clear, logical line from the beginning of the Revolution to its end.

I would definitely strongly recommend this course.

French Rev is the coolest class i've taken at Cornell. Prof Friedland makes a dramatic period of time both interesting and fun. Be ready to read a lot. 2 essays, one final essay based. Prof makes sure to make his lectures as interesting as possible and knows so many little facts. Doesn't like Napoleon though.
An exemplary historian who is one of the nicest professors you will meet at Cornell. Class act.

Friedland's French Revolution class is amazing. He knows an insane amount about the subject, and his lectures are soooo interesting, and he's a really funny guy. You don't have to go, but you really won't want to miss any. He doesn't seem to be a tough grader and gives really great essay feedback. Definitely do the readings and participate.

Best professor I've had at Cornell so far. His lectures were always interesting and he added his sense of humor to them in small ways that kept it engaging. Honestly just a great guy and a great prof, take a class with him if you can.
beast mode

A wonderful class with an amazing professor!! The French Revolution course has by far been my favorite class at Cornell. He is incredibly engaging, provides insightful commentary, and his lectures are super fun and always interesting. Discussion is mandatory, but lecture is not (but you'll never want to miss it). The grading can be a more difficult

Professor Friedland's lectures are very clear for those with or without a background in history. Very funny guy who doesn't take himself too seriously, but still effectively communicates his course material. Two essays + an essay-only final. Doesn't post slides online.

BEST LECTURER AT CORNELL. Was able to make incredibly boring material extremely exciting. Very engaging. Weekly readings aren't that bad and the Prelims are straightforward. If there's one professor at Cornell you should absolutely take a class from it's Friedland.
The lectures are great. Prof. Friedland gives clear descriptions about the French Revolution.  You have to work hard and read each week though.
Easily one of the best professors I had at Cornell. I actually looked forward to his lectures.

Engaging lectures and interesting, manageable reading load. Discussions were sometimes difficult because he could be a bit reluctant to let you have your own ideas. Assignment and exam instructions were unclear. On exams, wanted long-winded summaries of readings, not argumentative essays. Overall an interesting but slightly frustrating class.

Friedland is brilliant and super knowledgeable, even about the most random stuff. He's really easy-going, friendly, and engaging, but he keeps the class challenging and thoughtful. Discussion flows well.
He's an awesome lecturer. He's also a really nice person and takes the time to give lots of feedback on papers. Don't miss a chance to take a class with him.
He was a great lecturer but was unclear in his paper assignments and never followed through with personally helping students.  He is new but already notorious for being somewhat of a tough grader.

I loved Professor Friedland. His lectures were always clear and focused, and he would often add little jokes into his lecture slides. I had him for discussion as well, and the section was always really helpful in understanding that week's material and he made sure it was never boring. I'm taking another class from him next semester!

Fantastic, and easily the best professor I've had. Lectures were always very clear and very funny--he really goes the extra mile in everything he does. Extensive and helpful grading feedback. He's not easy, but he's not unduly hard either. Take him!

Professor Friedland is one of the best professors at Cornell. He is so nice and so passionate about what he teaches and will help you whenever you need it. I do recommend that you show up to all the lectures since the majority of info from the course will be given there. Overall, an awesome professor.
He is incredible. Take a class with him! Amazing lectures, super clear and gives great feedback. He really wants everyone to do well.
Awesome lectures. Really nice prof. Entertaining and serious at the same time. I'll  definitely try to take another class with him.

Tamra is AMAZING. Such an entertaining person, genuinely cares about all of the students. The kind of instructor you would take your personal, not just academic, problems to. Highly recommend her for an FWS. Also a very fair grader, this class was easy.
If you are reading this and you do not ballot one of Tamra's classes, you are a fool.

Tamra was an amazing FWS teacher.  I really did not want to take an FWS, but she made it one of the most enjoyable classes. I grew a lot as a writer, and the class was extremely painless compared to other FWS's. Love her!
Professor Welker is very nice. Her lectures were very engaging. The readings provoked deep thought about global problems. The discussion sections were also very insightful.

Professor Welker always ensured that material was relevant to current issues and connected with students experiences in the real world. Class discussions always were lively and she allowed time for all students to voice their opinions throughout the class. Although some readings were on confusing topics, Professor Welker always was understanding.
Prof. Welker is such a knowledgeable, aware, and caring professor. She is very involved in her research and genuinely wants her students to learn as well. Talk to her about her time in Indonesia!
great class, bees are cool!
amazing class, professor and person. Vey clear and engaging presentations, slides, and grading criteria. As long as you show up to class, you'll do well on assignments

Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer and I really enjoying learning about the fascinating biology of honeybees. It was always interesting to be in lecture and very often fun. I wish her slide shows were a bit shorter so we can get to everything in class
I swear to god just show up and get your A

Taking this course right now and really loving what I am learning. the course is super intersting and well structured with pre and post lecture quizzes that keep me on my toes and engaged. The in class activities help with that too. Definitely a great course for non majors

TAKE THIS CLASS!! Mrs Calliaud is literally the sweetest little French professor and her energy lights up the room every time she speaks. The content is also super interesting! Best class I've taken at Cornell so far

Professor Caillaud is a great lecturer; she goes the extra step to ensure her students are engaged and interested in the topics she discusses.

She was the best and a fantastic lecturer, very understanding with regrads to needs of individual student, and very responsive. The active learning material during lecture was useful even though it slowed down the pace of the lectures. Great class! We need to save the bees!

A great class about bees, really interesting, and taught with care and thoughtfully. Weekly homework involves pre-lecture videos and readings, plus an online quiz. The final project is awesome and I had a lot of fun with my partners. Loved this class! And professor Caillaud too!

Without question, the greatest professor I've ever had the pleasure of studying under ever. You guys will learn so much being in her class and the commitments for the week are minimal at most. Would definitely take again, and no, this isn't a paid review. Prof. Caillaud is an 11/10.

She has great knowledge of the subject and she is very enthusiastic which kept me very engaged during lectures. Using polleverywhere also helped me stay motivated during class, the weekly online quizzes were super helpful but she never posted the key

Marina Caillaud was the best professor I had in my four years at Cornell. She is caring, kind, intelligent, and she is absolutely hilarious. just taking that course rn and loving it.

Dr. Najemy is the single worst lecturer in the hist. dept.  the italian renaissance should be a pretty interesting class, right?  Wrong.  The only things that save this class are the quality reading list and Bob, the TA.

She's a great professor. If you are taking LBST 1103 then you will have to do some work in her class but it is relatively easy and she's super sweet. I would definitely take her again if my major allowed.

Dean Gilger is the best professor I have had! She makes lectures on boring subjects interesting and has a voice that is easy to listen to. Get to know her! If she knows your name then you are doing something right. If you are nice and participate in class then she will help you with anything. I would take any class that Dean Gilger teaches!

She is hysterical, although I don't think she is trying to be.  She goes off on tangents, and has hilarious hand motions that keep me awake during the 9 am session.  Tests are pretty tough, but she offers very helpful review sessions the night before.  I would recommend her, it's a riot.

Loved this class.  Loved Prof. Ginger - she gives you the outlines of her lectures and if you keep your notes along with the outline it's very easy to prepare for tests.  Best L201 teacher, heard so many complaints about other prof's. Very knowledgeable and willing to meet with you and discuss things outside of class.  Would take her class again!

Never ever take her class! Her teaching is boring. The tests are extremely wired... The first test was on the section of basic of law system, and she spent 1/3 of the questions on how insanity people are judged. If you are looking for a challenge, go for it. If you want to learn something and get good grades, go with other profs.

I love her. She always comes to class with a lot of pep and motivation and she's willing to meet with you whenever you want outside of class. If you attend her classes and go through the examples - tests are easy. A perk to having her is you get a reader therefore never have to carry around the textbook. Easier than the other L201 professors!
This class was Hard as hell. The test are hard as hell and the extra credit quizzes are nothing compared to the test. Basically Get out of this class

I'll "Mug" hard as soon as I'm 90 and still teaching, then I'll write that on my own review.  Nice try Ginger.  She needs to retire, completely useless teacher, or learn to teach like the education students, not a legal secretary.  Avoid at all costs.

Prof. Ginger is horrible, she just lectures, and her tests are extremely confusing.  Get a different teacher if you can, I took her practice test, got a C, like i did in the class, took my friends practice test from his Prof, and got an A.  She never answers questions in class. Very unhelpful.

This class is tough, but it's not impossible.  There are 3 100 pt tests and 5 5pt extra credit quizzes.  You have to KNOW and APPLY the material on the test.  I got a D on my first exam, but then I got serious and managed to pull out an A in the class.
This class is hard as all get out

A very personable professor who is willing to help her students deal with understanding the course materials. She gives essays and bonus points quizzes. I wouldn't say this is an easy A class; but hey who says law is supposed to be walk in the park? Work and mug hard...and you'll come through with victory!

Possibly the worst teacher in Kelley.  Her grading is crazy, you can forget about getting an A, she has no class participation.  Her lectures are boring and repetitive.  Her questions are poorly written.  I do not know how she is teaching an Honors class.
She is the worst teacher ever.
The previous poster is spot on.  Pray to God you don't take this class.  I am a Kelley Scholar and a Honors student and know what I am talking about.

Absolutly horrid.  Unreasonable and unfair grading.  Lectures are boring and repetitive.  Will not hesitate to fail students.  Very odd person who while nice at times, does not know how to teach a class.  Avoid at all costs.
Loved the teacher. Had great experience with her. She was very personable. It is not an easy class, yet not that challenging. Reading is all it takes. Law is about rules and logic!
Very Difficult and only has early morning classes.  Very hard to talk to and inconsiderate.
Worst teacher I have ever had.  The topics discussed in class aren't detailed enough for the intensity of her exams.  You must read the book!
Her lesson is very hard to understand, and she gives her student a bunch of rules that we must follow, like we are a preliminary student!!

Ginger was one of the worst profs I've ever had. He started of intro freshmen chem with calculus integration of the wave function, and skipped things like LDS. He expected that since we took AP, he could teach us 300-level physical chem (no joke, our lab was borrowed from a 3 or 400 course). HE TAUGHT US CHEM 155! Apparently, it was intentional.
could tell he put extra effort into being more approachable but it did not work lol. lots of suck ups in the class made it annoying but overall not a cruel grader.

Obviously incredibly passionate about chemistry but entirely unapproachable. Uses chalkboards during lecture (sometimes hard to read), roughly 12 hw questions + Python practice & quiz/week, exams are super difficult. BUT the median is curved to a 3.5-3.7, the TAs are excellent, and the content is very very interestingjust a time commitment.

Smart scientist, clearly a genius. Not great at teaching the material itself; if you want an easy A, go to 142. If you want to learn the material in-depth and challenge yourself, this is the right choice. Exams are ridiculously hard: lab, FRQ, MCQ, Python-- but a 4.0 is doable and entirely possible. This class will force you to learn pchem fast!

The thing is, I did great in the class gpa wise. However, the class was an absolute nightmare. I spent hours a day reading the textbook, doing homework, and rewatching lectures. I felt like I was teaching myself a lot of stuff. Exam averages were around 50% and it was difficult to reason with him and I felt frustrated and lost a lot of the time.

I got a 4.0 and yet it was the worst class I have ever taken. Ginger was condescending, unhelpful, arrogant, and cruel to his students. No one ever knew their grade in the class. Exam averages were 40% and he would berate us for this despite being unwilling to help. Expect it to be 5 credits but 75% of your workload, and learn python quickly!

I spent so much time on this class. For a five credit class, I was routinely putting in 30+ hours of work. Ginger's lectures were all over the place, and while I will give him credit for knowing his stuff, when I went to office hours to ask him questions, he almost always went off on tangents, and he was bad at explaining the concepts simply

Prof Ginger is knowlegable and respected. He gives amazing lectures and demo. If you're interested in chem and challenging concepts, take his 155! Be prepared for the amazing ride: the exams are hard, with lab portions! You'll do fine by practicing all the psat exams extensively because there are predictable patterns. (taken Wi20)
The class was amazing, managed to make Quantum Mechanics concepts very easy to understand. Stops for questions very often in class and is accessible outside of lecture time for extra help.

The best chem professor I've ever had so far. Dr. Ginger is super smart and very passionate about his research and teaching. He really cares about his students and is very willing to help us out. His class is challenging and trains us to become rigorous STEM students. Exams are difficult and the averages are low, but the curve is very generous.

Dr. Ginger is probably one of the smartest people on campus. With his double degree in chemistry and physics, he makes sure to blow your mind with every lecture you attend. He moves fast, though. So, get ready to take advantage of outside resources to enhance your learning. Tests are very challenging but he does recycles questions.

I got a 3.3 in 142 and a 3.7 in 152 and this was ENTIRELY because Ginger was my prof. I am not particularly good at (or even fond of) chem, but I loved going to lecture because he's such a good prof. However, his tests are HARD: all mc, negative pts for wrong answers, none of the above as a choice for calculations. Bonus points for his funny shirts
Very tough class. He didn't give good explanations, and was condescending. Organized, clear but very difficult.

Lectures are pointless. He doesn't know how to teach chemistry to students who don't know anything at all. He thinks everything's "easy" when it's actually not to us. Expects us to understand everything after he says it. Doesn't want to answer questions after class. Grades SAT style (seriously?). Average was 30% first exam, 40% the second.

Hes so good lol I love him. Hes by far the best professor in the chemistry department. That ive had at least. His grading thoooo? Its like the SAT where you get docked off for guessing. Hes a good professor though.
Lectures really fasts and expects you to understand everything he has said 5 secs after he said it

BEFORE TAKING THIS CLASS JUST KNOW THAT EACH TEST QUESTION IS MULTIPLE CHOICE AND WORTH 4 POINTS, HOWEVER, IF YOU GUESS WRONG ON ONE QUESTION IT COUNTS AS -1. A GIRL I KNOW GOT -2/100 ON OUR FIRST MIDTERM AND THE AVERAGE WAS A 32/100. SUPER DIFFICULT CLASS.
Will force to push your thinking than just any other general chemistry class, which in turn helped me think about things from a completely different angle.

The hardest class I have taken yet but the best professor I have had. He can be arrogant at times but he pushes you to achieve your highest potential. I had to study very hard for this class and as a result have developed much better study skills. A class you should take if you are considering med or grad school to see if you have what it takes.

You need to read the book before hand. All CHEM 155 2019ers will know we covered an entire chapter in a day because he felt like it. His father has the same name, so his full name is David Stanton Ginger Jr, please tell him you found his last name here. He says the word "Measure" like the word "Seizure". And if you need to learn python, good luck!

He really trains us to be better scholars. He asks us to plow through all contents because he knows we need them for the future. He would purchase lab materials on his own for us to have a better experience. He got out of surgery two days later and refused to take pain killers just so he can teach properly. His class is hard, but very beneficial.

Amazing professor, cares a lot about the success of the students. That said, he does talk really fast during lectures, but if you read the textbook ahead of time, its usually not hard to follow. Doing the homeworks and understanding the labs will help on exams.

Ginger is really passionate about chemistry, though he's not the best at teaching it. He lectures like he expects you to already know content so read before class and keep up with the homework. Go to lectures, the weekly quizzes typically test something we talked about in class. The midterms are challenging but he recycles questions from past exams

A lot of people have downvoted Dr. Ginger but he's honestly one of the best chemistry professors I've ever had! He's super passionate about chem and indulges everyone's questions, and he makes you work for it. The homework, labs, and exams are hard but not impossible. And he genuinely wants his students to succeed! Definitely worth taking.

Took him about a year ago and I really liked him. His course material is interesting and his lectures are very organized. His TAs know what they're doing and you'll never doubt that he doesn't know what he's talking about. He gives you about ten years of tests to combat the test banks kept by Greek row and just people in general.

lots will downvote simply because I gave him a high rating HEAR ME OUT Ginger is one of the toughest classes I took. He may not be the most approachable, but he is very understanding and will help you during office hours/will answer questions during lecture. Old test bank is a godsend. read every word in the textbook. study buddy helps. dont cram.

His class is pretty hard but he provides tons of old tests that are incredibly useful. Working through old test material and reading the textbook will help supplement his lecture material and make the class more manageable. He's clearly extremely knowledgeable about the subject and is quite helpful during office hours.

Probably the most arrogant, unapproachable professor I've ever had. Lectures themselves only cover a very small portion of the class. Might as well have no class and just get tested on the textbook and save 30 hours of my life.

Hes one of those people that is making me hate chemsitry more and more even though i want to major in it. He is unenthusiastic and doesnt care to help us understand the material. Might as well have a robot teach the class regurgitating what he has on his personal notes. An arrogant robot, albeit

Useless professor that only has a job because of tenure and his research lab. Extremely arrogant in class and cold calls people to embarrass them. Not approachable at all, will give you a snarky comment. Pronounces measure "mazzure" like he's having a seizure. He literally brags that he has tenure and doesn't care about student feedback. STAY AWAY.

He's pretty darn hard. Graded my exams multiple choice and SAT style, so the average test grade was about 50%. Be ready to work hard if you take his class. He knows his stuff though, has a renowned research lab and flew around the country while he was teaching (which unfortunately meant we had a few substitute lecturers).

Definitely tried to shove in as much information into three minutes without any regards to actually trying to make the material decipherable to the students. His exams were ridiculously difficult and almost impossible to study for considering the amount of work he piled right before. He is also extremely arrogant and unapproachable after class.

Be prepared to work hard. He grades heavily on test performance, but on a curve. Most of the time, I took a test and felt like I knew nothing, but came out alright. He seems distant, but is a good and capable teacher if you buckle down and try to understand the concepts behind the material you teach. It is not a straightforward class, so beware.

Dr. Ginger falls in line with many traditional professors - those who force you to think on your own and who expect all work is done without objection. That, however, is not bad - taking this course made me think more than I have in any other subject and really opened my eyes to the types of courses I should pursue. Be ready for a difficult course!

I have to sign up to rate Dr. Ginger. He is the person to help you realize if you want to pursue your career in Chemistry or Physical Chemistry. I am one of people who fall this chem sequence and end up with Computer Science. His course is extremely rough no matter how smart you are. He can help you to test whether you have the intelligent  on PChe
Knows an amazing amount of Chem but no passion for teaching. Had to drop the class because he basically teaches for the ppl that know everything already

Literally made me lose my passion for chemistry in the course of 3 weeks. Prof Vaughan for 145 really made me want to pursue chemistry until I have to deal with Ginger. He's cynical about grades and very cocky. Do yourself a favor and take 152.

He's a fantastic teacher. You have to be willing to learn and work hard but if you are then you will succeed. This is a class where you have to push yourself and can't expect things to be spoon fed to you.

He has high expectations; his tests are tough and he'll assume that you read before attending lecture. Go to office hours when you can and read, read, read the book. Sometimes he's so sarcastic that he doesn't even realize it. It really makes class a little more bearable.  He'll be there for you but you'll have to work to see that.
Deducts points on the exams if you get it wrong. This class was a major struggle for me, and I was retaking it from high school. Discouraged me from finishing the chem series.
Very brilliant person, he definitely comes off as arrogant though. Challenging class, learned a lot from him both about chemistry and generally.

I've always loved chemistry (it's my intended major), but Ginger made it very difficult for even his students with a willingness to put in the time and desire to learn to do well in this class. The average grade for the first midterm was around 49%, and the second was about 51%. Made me feel like just a number; doesn't care about students success.

While the material isn't particularly difficult, the way the tests are done makes it more difficult. They are multiple choice graded SAT style. Prof. Ginger expects students to already know what he's teaching in lecture. I would recommend reading the book and most of all doing the suggested problems in the back. They were used on exams.

I liked Ginger overall. He was fairly clear when lecturing -- only focusing on the stuff that mattered. That said, you do have to put in the time and effort to make sure you do well in the class. The thing I appreciated most in his class was that his expectations were very clear and if you studied there were no curveballs on exams.

Loved his class. Make sure you go- some of the answers on the test are only mentioned in class.    The people that don't like Ginger are the ones that don't work hard. Expect to work, but if you do you will be fine. He is hilarious, passionate about his work, and a wonderful teacher.

Ginger goes through the information and his slides quickly, which is hard for some who want to take notes, but he does a lot of problems in class which are helpful (and sometimes even replicated on exams). Be aware that his exams are multiple choice and penalize you for guessing (.25 deduction for every missed problem).

Ginger is a very nice guy, but is rarely accessible for help. He only had one office hour per week and was always rushing off to meetings and told students to post their questions online. His lectures are fast and not very helpful, I mainly relied on the book and Aleks. Also, his tests are extremely difficult, much harder than the homework given.

He grades his tests SAT style (you get a quarter of a point subtracted from your total score for each wrong answer) and that's really all you need to know. His lectures weren't terrible but he talks really fast and goes through slides way faster than anybody can take notes.

Went into Chem142 with Ginger hearing he was one of the hardest professors. However, after having him as my first college professor I hope the rest of my professors are just as insightful and intelligent and helpful as he is. Reading the textbook helped a great deal with the material only to be solidified by the lectures. Not as hard as it sounds.

His tests are pretty unforgiving and points are deducted for any wrong answers, so if you never learned how to study for a test in high school, you'd better start picking up that habit. Personality-wise, Ginger is a pretty courteous guy; he's friendly, but not lenient. He will make you work for that grade.

His tests are tough and he does do point deductions if you get wrong answers, but he teaches you to be a better student. He is a great lecturer, didn't find his lectures dry at all or hard to understand. You really just need to do practice problems, come to lectures, and read the book and you should be fine.

His tests are really tough, but it makes you learn how to be a better student and work for your grade. Do the practice suggested problems in the book, because his tests come from those a lot. Also use the course discussion board as it is a really good resource. He does clicker questions but not on the regular so go to class to get credit for those.

Professor Ginger is one of the smartest teachers I have ever had. Yes his tests are hard but that responsibility is on the students, and if you get a bad grade, it is not his fault for your mistakes. His lectures do move fast but he does prepare you well for each content. Office hours are super helpful too! I have a ton of respect for this man.

Professor Ginger is a very intelligent man with the potential to be a great teacher. You will learn the material well if you pay attention. My primary concern is the way he structures exams, Professor Ginger is intent on having a very low average score, using tests with unrealistic time constraints that don't test how well you know the material.

He is a great teacher and I believe that most of the students that have trouble in his lectures are those who aren't used to the speed of college class. Be ready to do the ALEKS assignment as they help you keep up with class. The course to cover is too much and yes he does go fast. But only because he wants to give time where things get complicated

Coming into the University new and having to take Professor Ginger was the worst thing that has ever happened to me. He was harsh, and very hard. He had 14 point deduction for every wrong answer. He also strongly recommended that we do not do pre med. He was very unencouraging.

Professor Ginger is an incredibly intelligent man, which may come across as being unclear or scattered during lecture. However, he is the best teacher I've ever had. He's dedicated, understanding, and truly cares about his students. If you're willing to work hard you shouldn't have a problem.

Wouldn't recommend for freshman. It wasn't a great fall quarter to start off for me. Lectures just went by fast, tests had penalties, and it seems the quiz sections weren't prepared as much. Would recommend someone who's more freshman-friendly and welcoming. First day, a sub came in for him, saying that people will fail. That was just depressing...

I really liked Professor Ginger.  He was tough, but hey it's college, if you aren't willing to open up the expensive textbook you are paying for... you're gonna struggle.  I liked his grading system, it's more realistic for future exams that mean more.  Read the book, do lots of practice problems, watch office hour videos if you are hung up.

Not a great first choice Chemistry Professor. Retook course with a different professor, did way better. Tests have penalties for every wrong answer. Either get it right or lose the entire amount of points plus a deduction from penalty. I suggest avoiding unless you don't have a choice.

If I (ELL student, only one year of high school Chem, never took AP Chem) could receive a 4.0 in that class, everyone should be able to succeed if heshe puts in the efforts. The curve is ridicoulsly high; I got around 70% for the final, still a 4.0.

This class is mostly a review from the chemistry I learned at my high school.  If you took two years of chemistry in high school then this class should be really easy.  I even showed up 40min late to my final and ended up with a 4.0 .  Tests are multiple choice.  If you have a question he'll just tell you to post it to the discussion board.

Ginger does go fast through the material, but then the last 6 lectures are almost entirely review of harder stuff. Inevitable mistakes on multi-choice tests do cost you, but this wouldn't stop a hardworking dedicated student from getting a 3.7-4.0. If you want good exam grades, do LOTS of textbook problems as test questions are strikingly similar.

Professor Ginger is difficult. There really is no way around it. Prepare to study a lot (of the end of the chapter textbook problems because ALEKS won't help) and still maybe not do as well as you would hope. That being said its a curved class so if you are on the right side of the curve you will do fine.
This class was very very hard. His tests were a lot harder than other classes. He went through materials way too quick. However, the cheat sheet is helpful.

Good lord! I flew right through Chem in high school, but it didn't prepare me at all for anything like David Ginger, PhD. His midterms are truly something else, in the worst way possible. It's actually possible to get a negative score on them, which is just... aaagh. No. Bye. Definitely study the previous tests in preparing for the final!

Ginger should NOT be teaching 142. This is his first quarter in many years teaching gen chem so maybe it'll get better, but he moves ridiculously fast through material and assumes everyone has a very solid base in chemistry. His tests are extremely difficult and long; his grading system doesn't help anyone out. Knowledgable, just too hard.

It was a primarily freshman class and Professor Ginger acknowledged the transition from high school to college. He was very clear cut in lecture and very clear about how you needed to study and that you needed to come to lecture to learn. Nevertheless, the midterms and finals are very difficult and leave little room for error.

Took this class as a fig and MAN was that a mistake! Ginger seems to forget that this class is aimed at freshmen. He will not sugar coat or simplify anything. Want to know how you're doing? Good luck because the only way you can tell is by passing or failing a midterm, which by then is often too late. He is often available, and easily contacted.

I learn so many new things in this class even i took chemistry classes in high schoo He is a GREAT lecturer, and he doesn't make the test difficult to fail student. My class is graded on a curve, so he has a point when he made the questions difficult so people who get good grades really understand the content, instead of being "lucky" in the exam.

Professor Ginger's tests are hard and he goes through his lecture pretty fast. HOWEVER, I can tell he is very knowledegable and he is pretty clear on most of the materials. You definitely need to try hard in his class to get a good grade. But again, if you try hard you WILL get a good grade

It's a tough class even for someone who has taken a similar course in the past. His insistence to grade tests as they do with standardized tests will kill your gpa, even though that type of test grading seems to be on its way out in the actual standardized testing.
Most difficult class I have ever taken in my life. He flies through everything so fast you don't have time to wrap your head around any of the concepts.

Ginger should not be teaching CHEM 142. As an introductory class, we shouldn't have to rush through everything so quickly and have ridiculously hard tests. This is a hard class but shouldn't be this challenging. He is in fact a very knowledgable professor and is very smart. But almost too smart for CHEM 142. Just be ready for a low GPA.

He doesn't know how to lecture properly. He skipped the basics assuming that most people have previously taken a similar class in physics. And he doesn't remember what he tells the class. What He says won't be on the exams always show up. Also he only looks at the wrong answers for plagiarism (never got caught for correct answers).

Physical Chemistry is by no means an easy course. Prof. Ginger helped me to excel and pushed my thinking with guided questions and good alternative explanations. He definitely emphasizes the mathematical portion, but that was helpful for me. Tests are difficult, but if you go to lecture and keep up on the homework, you can succeed.

The tests are all MC and really hard. You have to stay on top of all the online assignments, textbook reading, and take good notes. Lectures are mediocre, sometimes he does cool demos, but he assumes the class already has a strong base in chemistry. Not very helpful since it is a 500+ person lecture.

I'm pretty sure Dr. Ginger wrote all the good reviews on this page. He was the worst professor I've had and I had to go to CHEM 152 to understand anything. He thinks CHEM 155 is Physical Chemistry. Also, all his examples are about Organic Chemistry, which is a class you can't take until you're done with the general series.

A very difficult class, but if you put in the work it will be worthwhile. It is possible to learn an incredible amount of chemistry. It is an honors class: the workload is substantial, lengthy, & extensive. Ginger is an unbelievably intelligent man: I have no question of his knowledge whatsoever, but at times his explanations can be quite complex.
He was pretty bad but he wasn't that bad. Maybe 3rd to the worst professor I've had at UW. He had so many errors during his lectures and that's what costed random points on my homework every time.

He's one of those professors who can show you examples but can't teach the concepts behind. Also he avoids students. He holds office hours when most chem students have lab and it's quite difficult to contact him. He makes at least 3 errors in each lecture so you can't even study from his lectures for the exams.

I am pretty sure that this professor does not know how to teach. The only reason why my grade is above average is because I learned all of these in physics before taking this class. So unless you already know quantum mechanics, do not take this professor.

Absolutely fantastic professor. The class might be hard, but he is enthusiastic and knowledgeable and makes the class pretty fun, despite the difficulty. Tests are killer but very repetitive, so doing practice exams is very helpful. MASSIVE time commitment, I spent over 20 hours on one of the labs. But overall you learn a ton.(:

The hardest course I have ever taken - in retrospect I was entirely unprepared for it. Dr. Ginger, however, was very clear and even funny during lecture. The way he calls on students in class is intimidating, but his passion for chemistry is clear so it's ok.
The hardest class I've taken, but well worth it if you're up for the challenge. You have to put in a lot of effort but Prof. Ginger does too and he keeps the class organized and easy to follow.

A truly brilliant man and a great teacher. The class is incredibly difficult and will stretch your chemistry abilities in many ways. Tests are hellish, labs are intense and require a great amount of time, and the homework is not simple either. However, it is all worth it. After completing the class you will appreciate how great it was.

This was one of the worst instructors I have ever taken from.  Homework was unclear, tests were insane, and the instructor randomly called on people.  Please do yourself a big favor and take pchem from Xiaosong Li, Lutz Maibaum, or anyone else.  You'll undertand more, trust me.

Professor Ginger is a very enthusiastic teacher who also takes interest in whether students understand him. His lectures are fast-paced and his tests extremely hard, but the curve helps a lot. You'll need time-managing skills as well as chem knowledge to do well on his tests. (PS: I hope my previous, incomplete review has been removed by now.)

This class was epic. So much work to do, most of it worth it. Lectures gripping, really expanded my learning of the topic. Ginger is fantastic when in comes to spewing information at you. Very difficult tests, but generous curve. Loved every minute.

Brilliant, blazes through the material, writes wickedly difficult tests.  He can be intimidating at first, but is really helpful in office hours.  I learned more in this class about how to study than in any other class I have taken at the UW.

Not sure what others are talking about; I didn't find his lectures anything spectacular. I would describe them as ambiguous and unsystematic. Anything I learned I taught MYSELF. Unhelpful during office hours: asked him a question and he responded with "Well what do you think?" Exams were super hard. I will admit the curve was generous.

Yes, the first two reviews sounds a lot like Ginger.  Very helpful during office hours.  However, the words "easy exam" are never muttered in class. Very hard exams but grades on a "nice" curve.  Work hard and it will pay off. It's not until the class is over that you realize how great the class was.  This class was challenging but very rewarding.

Absolutely ridiculous work load for a freshman class. The amount of material he expects you to already know is also ridiculous. Good luck taking this class without a solid background in calculus and physics. And (like other people have said) he is incredibly arrogant and will never fail to show you how much more intelligent he is than you.
This class was extremely challenging and had a ridiculous workload for an intro series. However he is a good lecturer and you will learn a lot. Very accessible for extra help.

None of your prior comments indicate that you know the meaning of "challenge".  Quantum chemistry is extremely demanding, but also the most rewarding class I've ever taken.  Good luck to the rest of you in the real world.

Had him for quantum. Very intense!!! But crystal clear expectations, no hand holding, really pushed me. Scared the crap out of my while I was in his class but the man can teach!!! I would recommend him 100 times over!
One of the most intense and involved professors you will have.  He writes hard tests, but grading is all relative.  This course involves a lot of work, but it's worth it!

Good lecturer in class.  Fast, but standard (for H Chem) homework/lecture pace.  Exams were very tough, but are designed to spread the curve.  Overall I'd say an very good class, especially as his first time teaching 155.

Wow, good going David on your self-written reviews. If you look closely at the other reviews you can clearly see the same person. My assessment: Davis is one of the most arrogant professors Ive ever had, and I dont think he has alot of gravitas to back it up.
Had him for physical chemistry, one of the most demanded courses and everything was so clear it blew my mind. My first perfect grade and it was in Quantum Mechanics! Office Hours wonderful!
Presents very difficult material in a fairly understandable manner. Very helpful; office hours were excellent.
She wasnt the easiest A ever, but she was pretty good. She gave 5 papers and let you redo them like the other raters said. Nice and kept class interesting with discussions and readings.

I do not know who the other raters are but I will say that I was greatly disappointed when I went to this class. There are ELEVEN papers (some are reading responses but are graded) 1 of which is a long research paper. I will say it is probably possible to do very well, she'll let you resubmit your work. This is the best class I've taken and recommend it often.

I'm an entom major and this class was a required course. It's not easy -- but it's doable if you put in the time to study and make a proper insect collection. For someone who is not remotely interested in insects, or science for that matter, I would highly recommend taking this course! The best, most interesting class I've taken at Cornell. Tests have information taken directly from the slides with essays you can prepare ahead of time. Other assignments are graded easily. He's also REALLY nice and pretty nerdy so he really likes to see enthusiasm for his subject. TAKE THIS CLASS. I wish I could take it again.

Very good lecturer and does a great job of explaining the material. The class isn't exceedingly difficult, but it's not a walk in the park, either. The exams are mostly multiple choice and require some more-than-basic knowledge to do well on them. Overall, not a hard class with some good studying and attention to detail.
Great Professor. Very accommodating and understanding of personal circumstances.

While lectures are not required, they are very fun and easy to follow. Would recommend reading textbook although not required. HW is not too frequent and pretty easy. Plenty of review offered for each exam. Reccomend participate in extra credit throughout semester. Very nice professor and hosts lots of OH

As others have said Prof. Sanders genuinely wants you to succeed. I highly recommend going to lecture as he is very good at explaining concepts in ways that are easy to understand, and his deadpan humor keeps it interesting. Discussions are optional. Very willing to meet outside of class for help. Exams are very fair and match the practice tests

My opinion of Sanders is mixed. He is definitely the easiest 1110 prof. He gave up to around 2% extra credit (depending on grading method). Unfortunately he mismanaged online exams, which led him to make a cheat sheet only final, despite 1110 not really being a course you could fit into a single sheet of paper. Sucked up tons of finals week for me.
Literally the best professor here. He is so kind and helpful. He also gives so many extra credit opportunities. If you put in the effort you will get a great grade.
No complaints, amazing professor

I was expecting to be bored out of my mind in my econ class. Professor Sanders ended up making the class much more interesting than I thought an econ class could be. He had fun interactive things. The class wasn't a walk in the park but he does want you to succeed in it.

Extremely energetic at 9:05 in the morning, cracks jokes that I thought were funny during lecture, responds pretty quickly on the discussion board (especially before an exam). Sometimes went a little too quickly in lecture. There's a textbook but it's not necessary. Exams were online and entirely multiple choice, and very fair.

Professor Sanders is SUPER nice. Really really like him. Just seems like a good guy. He doesn't want you to fail. He really works to make sure you can get the best grade possible in the class. Totally respect him and would be more than happy to take another class with him. Super helpful as well.
Great professor! Smart, good lectures, interesting class.
Such a good lecturer. He is exceptionally kind and helpful during office hours. Overall, a fantastic teacher!

Took his class a while ago but couldn't ask for a better intro micro teacher. Was pretty organized and always tried to make the class material relevant and interesting, which is hard for a 400+ person intro class. Class isn't hard if you at least pay attention, but even if you don't he's very approachable for help.

Such a great professor, he released every prior test he has ever given to study off of. His lectures were well organized and fun to listen to. He was very accommodating during the shooting and bomb scares that happened in fall 21. You can tell he wants the best for his students. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! They help so much!

Sanders was a good lecturer for an introductory econ class. His classes always started by briefing recent research related to topics being covered in class at the time. The homework is not a great representative of the exams, but the exams themselves are very easy and he provides plenty of past exams to review.

Dr. Sanders is an amazing lecturer. Hes charismatic, funny, and is soooo passionate about economics. Would definitely recommend him. He comes up with his own exam questions and they always have a whole theme to it; its so funny. Our final this year was Animal Crossing themed!
Very good prof. Extremely good lectures and helpful in office hours. Exams reflect content well.

lectures werent helpful in terms of calculations, didnt always best explain the material. He records his lectures though so you can go back and listen to them. Makes himself available , great explaining in office hours. If youre good at math you'll be okay. If math isn't your forte it's going to require alot of work. Do all the practice prelims!
Amazing. Incredible. Phenomenal. Best professor at Cornell. Give this guy tenure.

Professor Sanders is the best professor I have had at Cornell University. He is always extremely caring as well as being an excellent lecturer. Professor Sanders is quick responder on ed discussion and you never need to be scared to ask questions in class or online. I would take definitely take a class just because it was taught by him!

Professor Sanders is one of my favorite professors in Cornell, he is very caring and respects every students. He cares about student's mental health and try his best accommodating with students needs. Lectures are mandatory but I strongly recommend people to attend lecture because it's very useful and he is a great lecturer.

Amazing lecturer and is really great at explaining concepts. Puts in a ton of effort to help his students. Overall stand up guy. The class isn't too hard if you have at least a bit of background in Econ, but the tests and assessments are doable through doing the past practice exams and asking questions.

Easily the best lecturer I have ever had. You can watch the recorded lectures later so attendance isn't necessary but if you do not watch the lectures you will not pass the class. The tests are fairly simple and very straightforward and he provides plenty of practice prelims. The homework is easy but of no help on the tests. Textbook is useless.

ECON 1110 had a light workload. Only attended a couple of lectures all semester and still had a solid grasp of the course material. The exams were similar to previous years so you knew what to expect. The required homework was not helpful to prepare. Median was a B+ but if you have any background in economics it is a stress-free and easy class.

Such a passionate professor and really cares about his students. Lectures were really clear and he spends a lot of time explaining concepts and graphs. DO THE PRACTICE PRELIMS, though. The questions are extremely similar and the homework is often too easy to be that helpful. I honestly never read the textbook, just pay attention in class.

Professor Sanders is such a positive guy. He makes class stress free and truly cares more about your understanding of the material than just a grade. Lecture is very important, as long as you pay attention to the concepts he explains, you will do very well. I highly suggest taking any course you can with him, I definitely would take another!
Amazing class! Lectures are very engaging. I found the tests to be challenging but fair.

HW - multiple choice, 3 tries for every Q, easy 100% on HW. Lectures - quality slides, but sometimes skips calculation examples that could be helpful. Discussion - optional, not rly helpful. Exams - fair. Make you think, but easy Qs too. Grading - gives different % breakdown options and assigns the best one for u, this semester could drop a prelim
I loved Econ 111 with Sanders. He made lectures exciting and interesting. There was a fair amount of HW, but he gave us three tries on each question so it was easy. Highly recommend Sanders!!

The best professor and the best course I have ever had I have been crying for hours after taking his last lecture. Nick is really awesome! I even want to take ECON1110 again next semester. He is incredibly good at teaching and bring students warmth during such a crazy pandemic period. The homework is sometimes easy, but prelims are moderate.

I had Professor Sanders for intro Micro and Economics and Environmental Policy. It is obvious that he loves what he teaches. He backs up all his statements with engaging research papers. Also, he has a deep respect for the students that can be hard to come by in a professor. Econ3850 was easier than micro.

Prof Sanders is a really great guy! You can tell that he is passionate about economics and the well-being of his students. Piece of advice: make sure you study past prelims/finals in order to do well on that year's exam. Definitely loved having him as a professor because of how engaging he was and how concisely he was able to explain concepts.

Sanders is a great person to introduce you to econ but he does tend to run behind schedule so he gets a less thorough as the semesters go by. You don't really need to show up, the textbook is decent. My TA was terrible and so were a lot of others so don't bank on that. Do a couple of his past tests, his testing is quite different from the hw.

Moves quickly through lecture slides and doesn't always explain the quantitative/calculation parts, but is great for the most part. Posts the slides online so you can skip lecture if you want. Discussions were useless. HW is easy. Exams were straightforward and similar in structure to previous years' exams. Nice guy, makes jokes during lecture.
Great professor. As long as you go to class and pay attention even though not required, exams are easy. Use previous exams he provides to study. He keeps lectures interesting also
Great lecturer. Makes class very interesting. Very accessible outside of class, with tons of extra office hours before prelims and finals. Not an easy class, but if you do the work, you can do well.

Professor Sanders is a great professor that has interesting real-world examples that make me look forward to class. His tests are very fair and make you learn the material. If you do the previous prelims and read the book you'll be fine, but I suggest showing up to the lectures to learn about the world.

good professor. he tries to be really interesting so the material actually becomes more confusing (ik lol). He will provide examples for topics without providing a framework to apply that example onto. The textbook is a must if you have never taken econ. His tests are fair, but short, so you need to be very accurate to do well. Nice guy.

Sanders is a great professor everybody loves him. However go to his lectures and spend time actually learning the homework or you won't do well. The class is fairly easy if you put in the time. The office hours are great too. Discussions are pointless and very optional.

Super easy class. I went to 2 lectures (I should have gone to more as he is a good lecturer), did not study for any of the prelims and did not go to my section a single time. I think if you just go to lectures and section and pay attention an A is pretty much guaranteed. I had two other friends who actually did the work and they both got A+'s

Not a hard class, but not an easy A bc it is SUPER easy to underestimate it. HW takes 5 minutes & isn't helpful for studying. I got a C+ on Prelim 1 bc I thought it'd be like the HW and that messed up my final grade even tho I A+'s on Prelim 2 & the final. Focus on practice problems + lecture slides. Super nice guy, & willing to help.

Interesting and engaging lecturer who clearly is passionate about the material. Presents material in a clear, understandable way. First two thirds or so of the class the material was pretty easy; got difficult near the end. I especially appreciated that he had lots of extra office hours at convenient times prior to prelims and especially the final.

Sanders is unbelievably dedicated to his job. His lectures have everything you need to know conceptually. His love for econ is contagious and his office hours are fantastic. Don't bother reading the textbook--use it as a supplement if needed. The class is not a lot of work but also not an easy A. Do lots of practice problems to study for prelims.

Andrea was never there - always out of town! The course was taught by her TA, Chris. She's an extremely talented and imaginative artist and that was her focus during her time as a professor at the U of M, rather than teaching.
Andrea is a very easy-going and understanding professor. Definitely cares about art.

It felt more like a lecture class about other artists rather than working on projects. 80% of projects must be done outside of class. Overall, she's nice and considerate about other people's problems.
Really nice teacher. Clearly has a passion for sculpture.

He is one of the best profs I've had here at Ferris! He will do anything to help you pass! If you're ever confused in the class, just go to his office hours and he will explain anything you want, and you can stay until you understand!

Great! So helpful. He goes off sometimes in lecture, but go see him one on one in his office and he explains everything!. Super nice.I took his class a year, and he still says hi and talks to me when I see him.

He's a doll. Totally willing to do anything and everything to help you understand and pass the class. Also, he try to give every student 1 on 1 time so you don't feel like you're in a lecture hall with 90 other people. totally recommend:)
Professor genuinely enjoys teaching and is extremely supportive and helpful.

Nice professor, I would say. Although this is an online course, he replied in piazza really fast, even it is 11:00pm. The model prediction competition on kaggle is really funny and it is easy to earn full mark.

He's in the research stream, but he teaches better than all stats profs (except maybe Luai). He gives bonus marks if you do well in the kaggle competition. Super helpful and active on Piazza. He doesn't make you feel dumb. I never had to read the textbook. His tests are extremely fair, all of my friends 4.0'd his course. I wish he taught more! :D

He is passionate about material for sure though.
Opanasenko is a nice guy. Very thick accent and lectures were confusing. Struggled a lot with the class due to this. He also had very messy notes.
Fantastic professor!

The class is tough, with a lot of proofs, but he's really patient and explains things in a way that actually makes sense. Just be ready to work hard!
He's gives great lectures and is helpful in office hours too. Just make sure you start homework early and don't wait till the last minute. Prelim and final were fair.
One of the more challenging classes that I've taken at Cornell, but lectures are crystal clear. Also Bitar is very approachable and helpful outside of class.
Is very slow - takes too long to post things like homework solutions

Took in Spring 2016 - his first year teaching ECE 3100. I thought he was awesome, can be really blunt/quick at times, but will help you understand it esp 1-on-1. Good lectures.
