She is prepared, professional, expects students to act like adult college students, and creates a safe space for us to explore things. She came recommended, and I wasn't disappointed.

Gretchen is one of the best profs I've had. What I found really annoying were the number of RS students who complain about her and the work load. She was patient, but kept to her standards. Excellent course, well-designed, and would gladly take her again.

She doesn't put grades on Canvas which was really annoying. The workload was a lot; it took about 2-3 hours a night. She always talked about irrelevant things like her family life & politics. The class is really just papers, so you really don't learn anything. Class time was really boring, but sometimes she lets you out early.

Hated her! Even though the stuff you do in class was kind of manageable, she was just very rude & obnoxious about a lot. She liked certain students, but the ones she didn't like she would back-talk & be disrespectful to. Just do the work & if you have questions, be prepared for a long speech & no real answer. WOULDN'T RECOMMEND!!

Coulter seem very nice and likable, however she spends most the quarter pushing her personal views onto students (which she gets very mad if you don't agree with) instead of teaching about composition. Her grading criteria is very unclear for the final ethnography project and the many reading responses. She is also unwilling to put grades on Canvas

I liked Gretchen at the start of the term but after students pushed back against an idea she forced on the class, her dark side showed and it became clear to me she is more concerned with pushing her own ideology on students than teaching. I actually agree with most of what she said but I do not like when I have to accept any ideology to pass.

Such a great professor. Assigns good material and knows how to get students to engage in class. Definitely reading heavy. Attendance is important but if you have good reason and let her know ahead of time she will work with you. I had to miss a few days for surgery and she was very accommodating.

I don't know how anyone could give Gretchen a poor rating. She's extremely sweet and passionate about literature, which makes class more enjoyable. I will say there is A LOT of reading and writing in here though. 10 chapters of textbook, the entire book "Boy" by Roald Dahl, a young adult novel- all need to be read with reading logs to follow.

I'm SO glad I took this class. I've grown as a thinker and a writer, and I now know how to confidently ask questions about things I may not know. Gretchen is smart, caring, supportive, and creates relationships that last beyond her class. The coursework is relevant to the subject, but also to real life. Love her! English 201, WCC

She would say, "If this class is 5 credits, you'll get 5 credits worth of work." when almost every class is 5 creditss. She was very condescending if you missed class. Even after messaging her on Canvas. You could tell her that you were in the hospital and she would probably say, "Maybe you shouldn't have gotten hurt, then."

It's a good thing I didn't pay attention to the naysayers on this site. Gretchen is OUTSTANDING. The readings, assignments, class discussions, and 1 on 1 meetings, made this this class one of the top 3 I've taken at WCC. She is smart, clearly dedicated to students, and she's hilarious! She challenges opinions--not reasoned arguments. Love her!

I took this class as an elective credit. It was AMAZING. Gretchen helps you to read and connect literature to real life. She tries to make each class a safe place where you get to explore your ideas, and on the whole, students really bond in her classroom. I loved the reading selections, and the writing assignments were reasonable. Great prof

If you want an easy A dont take this class. Gretchen assigns homework every night and spends classtime with discussion about readings she assigned. She has helped me grow as a writer and I really like how she was very specific with her grading criteria. You can genuinely tell Gretchen cares for all her students and wants to help them succeed.

Overall I did not have that great of an experience with her.I have to to say that I find it interesting that most of the negative comments have a common theme and that is that she really does not like opinions differing from hers and I most defiantly experienced this. She also mandates a graphic R-rated for a family friendly English class

CL is amazing!  Gretchen sets it up so that students get to contribute to the course content.  We chose books for presentations.  I loved learning how CL is not just about touchy/feely stuff.  We learned about theories of literature and how CL has evolved over many decades. The discussions were amazing and G knows her stuff--and it was super fun!

Expect to spend most of the quarter reading and responding to texts. Homework can take a long time and there is an assignment every night. But if done according to the rubric and you talk to her, you will do great. She is inspiring and reinvigorated my love of writing and reading.

Gretchen  makes it clear that she doesn't accept late work and absences aren't excused because she wants her students to pass. She is clear on criteria and as long as you follow it, passing the class is not a problem. Lots of readings and responses. The class is discussion based as well, so there aren't any lectures. Would take again.

I read through many of these comments and I think that the nay-sayers must be whiny and lazy students.  This instructor is amazing.  She will go far and beyond what you ask of her, and the course content really connects with real life.  She also makes (and keeps) her commitment to write outstanding letters of recommendation.  Well worth the money.

While I've seen some reviews complaining about Gretchen, I really enjoyed her for my English 201 class. She was kind and very understanding of some special circumstances I had.  Keep in mind though- she gives a LOT of homework. There's stuff due every day. It's a brutal load for the first half of the quarter, but it eases up towards the end.

She is very biased against conservative thought so be careful of that, she also does not like opinions that do not match with hers. She gives a pretty hard assignment were you have to study some sort of a group and she is not super clear on the directions for that in the beginning.

Mrs Coulter is beyond rude,and is by far the worst teacher I have had. The issue with her is that she can challenge you on your thoughts,and ideas, and if you do the same to her she will become very aggressive. She also mandates attendance but she herself was gone the first week of class, and many other times through out the rest of the quarter.

Mrs. Coulter started out great but drastically changed throughout of the quarter. She was very opinionated and would push much of her own beliefs onto students, and do not even think about discussing something that is different from what she believes she will have none of it. She also makes the students read a very inappropriate book.

I liked her at first, then we had to observe people in a place like the hospital so i came up with somewhere & told her my idea. She said yes  then told me no.. after i observed that place! Also she wasn't helpful outside the classroom at all! she wouldn't help me with my essays & was just plain rude to me. I almost failed her class! Dont recommend
Gretchen is not a tough grader if the work you produce is fairly well done.  She does assign a lot of reading and along with the reading you have a page plus reading responses.
Management assignment outside class. Very good professor if one is planning a degree at Whatcom Community College. Had her in 2009.

Teaching style is different than other English/Lit courses you'll take. Enthusiastic, knows her stuff, and pretty open to new ideas. Expect to work hard with little guidance, but she's not as tough on grading as you'd think & you'll come away from the class a better writer.

Book is a must have as every night you are to read a chapter and do a "1 page" reading response, it's in quotes because there are always so many questions or it needs to be so detailed it's always over a page and a half. Expected to go to library or bring different kinds of children's books from home. She does try to keep it as cheap as possible .

Gretchen is definitely enthusiastic about teaching. She really enjoys her job which makes you enjoy the class. Be prepared to work this class is a lot of reading and writing. At least three papers per week single-spaced and a full page. Occasionally she seems annoyed when you ask her questions, but everyone has off days.

It was clear from the first day that Gretchen was meant to be a teacher. She's enthusiastic about what she teaches, and I personally found all of the material very relevant and thought-provoking. Gretchen was extremely lenient on late-work, as long as you would communicate and show an effort to catch up. Plus, she's super approachable, and funny

Expect: a ton of homework, weird opinions on about everything (empirical sciences aren't objective, folks! because people chose to be there which somehow makes the data skewed), a lot of confusion. Don't expect: Comments on your submissions, exciting classes, any sort of meaningful help with writing.

Gretchen is a passionate instructor.  She cares about her students and her subject material.  I learned to dig deeper and to stop skimming the surface of my reading and thinking.  She has a great sense of humor and is very open to ideas that stretch or expand or connect to things outside her curriuclum.  You have to back stuff up, but she is great.

Gretchen is the BEST. Not only is she sweet as can be, she is very knowledgeable and organized. There is a good amount of homework, but it's easy once you start. No tests. End of quarter research paper. Two presentations. My favorite class I've taken at WCC so far and wish I could take it again. Going to the ChildLit Conference was wonderful.

Gretchen is highly knowledgeable and a very enthusiastic teacher.  She purposefully strives to make her courses relevant to a student's perspective.  This class taught me that there is way more to Children's literature than whether you like it or not.  I'll never read that same again.

Gretchen has a sweet personality and she offers plenty of opportunities for asking questions. However, she is very vague in her instructions. She was not understanding towards ideas that did not jive with hers. And FYI a lot of the stories we read had R rated content. If you do not want to fill your mind with that junk that do not take her class.

I loved Gretchen's class. Her work was challenging but fun and easy to keep up with as long as you don't slack off and you take the class seriously. She will definitely work with you. Not tolerant with excuses for late work so don't bother. If you're a beginning English major I'd definitely recommend her.

English has always been my favorite subject and I have always received over a 3.0 in English related classes. Gretchen's class was by far my least favorite english class. if you miss a day plan on missing two assignments. she often doesn't show up to class and does not send an email to let students know. DO NOT TAKE WITH HER!

This teacher is amazing. She really opened my eyes to a topic I knew very little about prior to taking this course, and now I am absolutely in love with that subject. Very kind and understanding teacher with a world of knowledge! Highly recommended.

I loved Gretchen.  She has a great passion for English, and uses her own experiences as an English student to try and help students avoid common pitfalls.  Her class was very fun to go to, and the texts were all very interesting. There's a fair amount of writing, but honestly it really isn't that much for a 200-level writing course.

Gretchen is an AWESOME teacher.  I heard good reviews about her from other students and I was not disappointed.  You read and write a lot, but she is very supportive and cares about student success.  She also writes terrific letters of recommendation for her students.  The whiners need to take someone else.

Ms. Coulter is the most frustrating professor I have had the misfortune of studying under. All I can do is echo the previous negative comments about her unwillingness to acknowledge any views other than her own. This ruined the learning environment and made writing essays uncomfortable. Any ideas not in line with hers get ripped apart when graded.

This teacher intruded upon my personal life, kicked me out of the class when I reacted to her physical act of intrusion. When I went to turn in my final the next class, she would not allow me into the classroom, and said, "Go cry to your running start counselor, you are not in my class." I did my best in class, and she failed me. Horrible teacher.

This is an anyalitical writing class, and people who don't want to do that are going to hate her. Gretchen is a brilliant teacher though, she gives clear guidlines, interesting readings, and is always open to new ideas. More so than anything though she wants you to approach her. I haven't had an instructer yet who was as kind and helpful as she was

Gretchen is by far the BEST instructor I have ever had.  Yes, there is a lot of writing, but the material read is interesting and discussions are insightful!  She will ALWAYS make herself available to you and also makes it clear that she makes herself available to assist in letters of reference and university applications!  TAKE HER!!!!!!!

This class is really challenging.  The reading material is dense and the writing is nonstop.  But I have to say that in spite of it being alot of work, Gretchen ensures that you leave the class as a better student than when you began.  She cares about her subject matter and you.  A+

Gretchen really loves what she teaches and it shows. She was very clear about the assignments-the directions for the essays were pages long. The class was challenging and I am glad that it was. I grew in my writing abilities as well as analysis abilities and developed more of an appreciation of literature. I miss the discussions and the class.

I was told Gretchen Coulter was a really great teacher--but that you write A LOT.  This is true!  However, we read some of the most diverse readings I've experienced in college so far.  Plus, she is truly committed to her students.  She writes AWESOME letters of recommendation.  I would take her again in a minute.

I was really nervous about this class.  You don't get graded by your own teacher; it is by a panel of readers.  Gretchen got everyone of us through to 101.  She is tough, but she really cares about us.  And I learned things I will use in many of my future courses.

Gretchen is a great prof.  I was really worried about coming back to school but she has encouraged me a lot.  I don't get the comments about her being closeminded.  She is really open and really respectful of student input.  I'll bet it is folks who are really opinionated and not really open themselves.  Take her.  You won't regret it.

I'm in this class because my advisor recommended it.  I wasn't sure what it would be like.  But I'm really glad I took it and Gretchen's a enthusiastic teacher.  I don't really get the comments about her being opinionated.  My experience is that she is open and cares alot about her students.

Gretchen lights up a literature class!  Her enthusiasm and passion for her subject and her students is awesome!  I wish she taught more classes at WCC.  This course feels like a book club--but with writing.  Take it--you won't regret it.
Strong course in thinking, reading, and writing analytically and critically.  Valuable for my future coursework.  Gretchen really cares about the success of her students--and it shows.
Not a fan. Definitely dropped her class.  It's kind of... her way or the highway.

she is one of those teachers that thinks shes the best and is helping with everything but shes not she doesnt care at all about student oppinion if someone states something that she doesnt think is right or that she doesnt want to hear she will completly ignore it and move on to the next person i have nothing against her but wouldnt recomend her

I wish I could take a class from Gretchen every quarter till I graduate, because she is seriously the best English teacher I have ever had. She's insightful, fair, very patient and always willing to help you on ANYTHING. Remember to cite like you've never cited before on your final paper!

She expects a lot from her students in terms of homework. She stated straight up she believes writing a lot prevents writer's block. Which isn't a problem if you like writing - that's basically how you can summer Gretchen up. If you love composition, you'll love her class and it'll be easy. If you hate composition, you'll hate this class.

Gretchen is such a sweetheart! People say  her class is more like a 3rd grade class..would you call reading 10-20 (philosophy) pages every other day 3rd grade? She's just great. My only complaint is that when giving feedback, she is pretty repetitive. And it's not that she ignores what she disagrees with, she's just looking for something specific.

The mark of a good teacher is one who can keep a student coming to class even if said student hates the reading material. Gretchen accomplished this, making me see relevance in what was possibly the worst book ever. She is extremely personable on a one-on-one basis and her faith in my abilities was an inspiration. Take her! She knows her business.

Gretchen is a very nice lady and she  loves our class, but only because it is filled people who don't tend to disagree with her. If you have an opinion that is different than hers, be ready to back it up with evidence or she will basically ignore you. All of the reading for this class was so boring. Atonement? *snore*

Easily the best English teacher I've ever had. You have to read a lot and be prepared in class, but the class is fun and you get speak your mind. Don't worry about buying a book because she gives hand outs in class. Pretty easy grader, and very lenient on topics for essays. I would recommend this class to anyone

Gretchen can go on power trips but I found that if I said nothing at all during the class and just sat there and smiled, all was well. You get a lot of homework in this course but she grades very easily. Unless you're a complete idiot, you can pass this class. If you make an effort to meet up with her, she'll adore you.

She was by far the worst professor I have ever had! She was rude, contradictory, and blatantly ignored anyone that did not share her PERSONAL opinions. She plays the "favorites" card like its going out of style. She demands you show up for class and rarely shows up herself. If you are signing up for classes, DO NOT take one from Gretchen Coulter!

Should probably be teaching K-grade rather than college. Seems nice enough unless you come into class with intelligence of your own, then just be sure to keep your mouth shut or you'll have issues with her. Treats students she doesn't like as if they're in elementary school, and she doesn't explain assignments well to anybody. Very annoying.

Mrs. Coulter is the only college professor who teaches at a third-grade level. While she smiles and has a cheery disposition, she understands less about her topic than any other professor I've ever had. If you can spell your name, she'll give you an A. And if you disagree with her opinion in a class discussion, prepare to be ignored and avoided.
Gretchen is a new teacher who is still trying to get settled. She is a pretty easy grader.

Had this professor in Fall 2023. Overall a very good professor in a mundane class. The course itself was pretty long and boring in its content (not the fault of the professor), but she brought in guest speakers to make the class more interesting and shaped class assignments to be beneficial for the real world (i.e a mock scholarship application).

Prof. Kelly is a very easygoing professor. Although the class material was very broad, she often invited engaging guest speakers that made the class very interesting. She is very lenient with grades and due dates. Also, she's and airport manager at San Carlos so she is involved in the field and can help with networking. Great professor, easy A.

I emailed my adviser regarding a math class. I was struggling and was not sure whether to drop the class in order to make sure my GPA stayed high or to stay in the class. My adviser did not email me back. I went to her office hours and she was not there. She did not even help me with my schedule at all just gave me my pin. Terrible!

Very rude to say the least. The first time I met her she asked me if I had a problem with being still. She told me that I needed to get that taken care of and that the nurses in our office would be able to diagnose my problems and give me something to be more calm. She did not advise me at all and in fact she told me what to do. Didnt Help at all.
AWFUL.
easy teacher makes class fun probably couldnt pass english w/o her

i do not recommend taking her class. she is confusing and it is difficult to understand exactly what she wants. she gets easily confused when she is asked questions and rarely answers the questions adequately. she did however have a good exam review where the students did research on exam topics and readings and shared with the class. exam was easy
very good teacher and very helpful

Locoman is very dilligent. She is trying her best, but ... sometimes her accent is too heavy. Her classes are a little bit boring and it seems that she lacks a proper understanding of politics in America. Well, good luck to her!
She was really helpful and usually responded to emails quickly. She gave helpful feedback I'd definitely recommend taking her classes in the future.

I absolutely loved Katie's class. She is extremely knowledgable and shares her passion of kinesiology so effortlessly. Very little homework, and tests. The labs for her class are fun and engaging. I would recommend this class for everyone in kinesiology. She truly cares about her students and does a great job at explaining labs.
I LOVED taking Katie's class. She is so kind, passionate, and she really inspired me on my fitness and professional journey.

Katie truly exceeded my expectations. Not only her command over the subject matter evident in every lecture, but her passion for teaching and genuine concern for student understanding is showing. She always made herself available for questions, encouraging an environment of open discussion and intellectual curiosity. 

I learned a lot from her!

Amazing lecturer who comes off as very sincere and fair.  His grading is not harsh, but I came away from the class confident that I knew the material.  I'm glad I got the chance to have Dr. Angenent as a teacher.

Professor Angenent is the best professor I have had at UW Madison. This class is very difficult in general, but he makes it so much easier to understand. You can feel his passion through his teaching, and he genuinely cares about his students so much. If you have to take MATH341, definitely take him!

Professor Angenent wants you to succeed. He's very eager to answer questions, both in class and on Piazza, and he's fair about grading curves. All class lectures are accessible on Canvas. The homework assignments and other class resources prepare you for the two midterms and the final.

Sigurd is a very caring and inspirational professor for advanced math and research. His lectures are very concise and easy to follow. He always gives students an intuition how and why it works. I was in a research group on the curve shortening flow and the professor made the class very interesting. Highly recommended.
Angenent is very accessible outside of class, will answer literally any question you can think of in a digestible manner. Respected throughout the math department.
Really clear and intuitive explanation with good pictures. Doesn't assign homework until last three weeks of class. Hope for more consistent assignments.

Professor Angenent is a real gem at UW-Madison. He is well-known all over the world in mathematics. His lectures are clear and comprehensive. He is very kind and respectable towards students. His knowledge is beyond this world and I would say that he is one of the best mathematicians in the US. I would surely take another class. Great lectures!

One of the best professors I've had by far at UW. Turned a usually difficult class into something that was seemingly easy. Homework well-prepared you for the exams and was very fair in terms of grading and tests. Clearly wanted students to do well and cares a lot.

He's very kind, goes through enough examples and provide visuals so all the students understand. Really chose to focus on the basics of set theory and linear algebra, which is how 341 meant to be. Homework prepares you well for the exams.

Sigurd is the best math professor I had at this school. Actually he is definitely one of the best professors I have during my college career. He is very friendly, respectful and helpful. I would love to take his class again.

I took math 421 with Sigurd and I say he is the best math professor I ever had at this school. He is respectful and helpful. His lectures are very useful and we dont even need to buy textbooks. Id love to take his classes again.

Such a great professor. He explains the "why" behind difficult concepts, which makes it all make sense. Real Analysis can be a tough subject but his exams and homework are fair and you really learn so much. He cares about his students.

Professor Angenent was very clear in lectures and was careful to walk through difficult topics with lots of examples and intuitive reasoning. He is an extremely friendly person and is always helpful in his office hours. Practice exams are very indicative of the actual exams; there are no surprises. I would be glad to take another course with him.

Sigurd was hands down the best math professor I have had at UW. He made Stochastic Processes/Markov Chains clear and interesting while still expecting a lot out of students. Wish I had taken more of his classes!

Sigurd is a great professor. He is very enthusiastic and has the rare capability of being able to simplify difficult topics in multivariable calculus. He posts useful study guides before the exams. I would definitely recommend!

This class was very easy to pass because Professor Angenent would post a study guide before the tests with everything on it. This made the class very predictable. Lectures aren't that important as long as you kinda know what's going on. He is interesting and funny so that's a plus.
Prof Angenents lectures are clear and the tests are straightforward. There are not many extra resources for the class but overall it is easy enough material to do well.
Best math professor I've had. Wish I had taken another course with him before I graduated. He's really really clear, really nice, and his exams are extremely fair and easy.
Just six words: BEST PROFESSOR. TAKE 521 WITH HIM.

Overall, would recommend.  Homework is reasonable, but tests can be hard. Lectures are sometimes a bit dry, but they are always clear. Some thought that the textbook (Rudin), was dense, but I thought it was alright. No office hours, answered questions on piazza instead. Overall, a good professor
Take 521 with him. He is the best  math professor ever!!!!

Real analysis isn't a very easy subject by any means, and mathematical proofs in general can be hard to follow, but Professor Angenent knows how to make this stuff make sense. I've never felt lost in his class.

Sigurd is amazing. His lectures are very clear and inspiring. He comes up with proofs with diagrams and motivates students to think with his hints. Exams and grading are very fair. That being said, you will definitely learn more and get less pain from him than others. If you have a chance to take a course with him, register without hesitation!

The best professor I have ever had! He cares about intuitions and examples that can helps a lot for understanding (and also useful for future proof by contradictions!). He is a really nice guy, and his lectures are amazingly organized. We are using one of the worst textbook (super hard and dry), but his class is the most interesting and intuitive
Amazing lecture. He is one of the best lecturer in maths department to explain things.

Incredible. If have the good fortune to be able to take a class with this guy you should. Very clear explainations and really emphasizes what is important. Tests and homework are at just at the right level to be challenging but doable. Also, he is just an extremely nice guy.

Super easy lecturer; did not cover all of the topics, was very slow in terms of pace, exams were very easy. Take him if you want a very easy version of calc 3 where you won't learn as much as you would with a more rigorous professor. HW not required.

Best math teacher around. He does not grade homework, but if you are keeping up with the discussion quizes, you'll be fine. Very reasonable with students. More theory based than practical based. Very efficient with use of lectures and students' time in general.

Sigurd is a great professor. His lectures can get off topic sometimes but usually what he is talking about is still interesting. The best part of this class compared to other 234 classes I knew others were taking were that the test questions were very predictable and the test were SUPER easy for a multivariable calc course.

Sigurd was an incredible professor.  I had previously taken Calc 3 with Bing Wang and had to drop the class because he was such a bad professor.  SIgurd is infinitely better.  He is easy to understand and only teaches the necessary material that will be on a test.

Professor Angenent is the best professor I've had in the UW math department. His explanations are clear and he is very helpful in elaborating on class concepts in office hours. I felt the course was too slow in the beginning, but it did provide a thorough foundation for later concepts. I hope to take another class with him in the future.
Professor Angenent gives slow but clear lectures. Tests are very fair, especially because of the test expectations he gives.

Ange goes pretty slow compared to most calc professors. This has its advantages and its pitfalls. Given that calc 3 is only a 200-level course, however, I think he is a fantastic professor. His lectures are easy to follow and the exams are super reasonable.
Unclear explanation and sometimes goes out of topic. Never take his class. The discussion helped me through otherwise I'll never understand anything.

Lectures very well and truly has a passion for teaching students. He wrote all of the calculus packets, so he is all about teaching people. His tests are the easiest math exams I have ever had. Just wants to have everyone understand the concepts well and is willing to give the whole class and A. Very cool guy.

Professor Angenent was the author of the 234 course packet so he really knows his stuff. He uses lots of examples so you don't leave class feeling panicked and is an engaging lecturer. His exams are beyond easy the class average on the last one was 94%. If you do have any questions he is super approachable and genuinely want his students to do well

Sigurd is an amazing professor. His lectures are very clear and he doesn't waste time teaching pointless topics. There are no surprises on the exams he prepares you very well. I highly recommend this professor, he is one of my favorites.

Sigurd is awesome!  Extremely helpful professor who explains things in a clear, concise manor.  The text was written by him but is actually quite useless.  No curve for the class but tests were quite fair.

This is a really good teacher. He explains all of the concepts very clearly and the tests are very fair. The text can be misleading though, the homework is difficult compared to the tests and there are quite a few mistakes. The key to this class is going to lecture and asking for help.

Decent teacher with appropriate amounts of homework, quizzes, and tests. Has a lot of math-related jokes and is a generally jovial guy. Lecture did not relate to discussions, however. I would recommend him to people who are unsure which math class to take.

Highly recommend this guy.  Lectures can be a little confusing or not really applicable at times but his really dry humor will keep you interested.  Homework problems are usually pretty basic and they are very similar, or exactly the same, as test and quiz problems.  Overall low workload and straightforward testing, what more can you ask for.
Pretty cool guy he explains things very well and i didnt even mind going to lecture
He isn't a bad teacher but not the best either. The course is difficult by nature but there are some concepts that he assumes the class already knows.
Midterm 1&2 are easy but 3 is a little bit difficult. He's a good teacher with lecture notes online.
He is a very nice person and understanding but his book is horrible. His examples and proofs are either too easy to apply to harder problems or are too complicated to understand.

He doesn't teach you what you need to know, just what he likes to talk about. He does elaborate proofs/problems that aren't relevant to what's on the test. He leaves a lot up to the TAs, so it's important you have an amazing TA in order to do well in his course. The textbook he wrote is awful, it's very unclear and full of errors.
He is an awful professor. His book is basically useless, because it has mistakes consistently through the whole book. Don't take any of his classes, steer clear of him.

Sigurd is one of the best maths instructors that one could hope for.  His lectures are clear and precise--with a dash of dry humor.  Exams require you to understand the material in depth.  There is a reason I plan on taking his class a third semester in a row!

This guy, who's incredibly dry for a teacher, decided to make his own terrible textbook for both semesters of Calc. Not only are there mistakes everywhere, but there are no answers in his "book." Instead of making us buy this piece of crap book, I would rather have an actual book from a legitimate source, rather than not knowing answers to his q's.
Went into incredible detail about the proofs for the calc. The lectures are not the most exciting lectures in the world.

Only take this class if you absolutely need to. If you tested out of it, do not take this class to get a "basis in college calculus" because it is a class of proofs of calculus theories. Unfortunately, Angenent is the "best" prof to take 221 with, even though he rambled on and on about the simple topics but almost never got to the difficult ones.
He was a great teacher. Wrote the text so his examples were like ones in the book. Easy to understand. Exams aren't horrible. Class is curved at the end.
Sigurd is very nice and funny, but it IS Calculus. It's not a fun class. It's challenging and the lectures drag on. You should definitely only take it if you need it for your major.

Sigurd simply put is the epitome of awesome. I was very fortunate to have had him as a professor. More than anything else I really gained an excellent understanding about math. His class can be very easy if you take advantage of all the resources he offers you, which are many. He is remarkably witty and is amazingly clear. An amazing teacher!

Very helpful if you utilize his office hours. Gives clear examples in lecture, but sometimes the examples lack difficulty. He even has a sense of humor. Very dry humor. The first test for 221 was incredibly hard (average 66) but the second midterm balanced it out.

Professor yilmaz is actually very enthusiastic,as long as you email him with questions,he will answer you quickly and be very helpful at the same time.But his homeworks and tests are very difficult,and he is also not very good at teaching,of course,it may also be the reason of computer algorithm itself is very difficult,so it is very hard to teach.

Dr. Yilmaz is a great professor who challenges his students to think on their own. His lectures are a bit dry at times but he is super helpful outside of class if you get stuck. Terrible class and professor. Professor is here only for the money. The professor admits that he can't teach the subject. I question Auburn University at times. I took this class over summer and he made anthropology a very interesting class! I skimmed over the book for key terms, but he gives study guides for the exams. Straightforward, tells you exactly what will be on the test if you come to class. No surprises. You earn your grade. Lectures are interesting and hes funny and very understanding. Allows extra credit if you put in the work.
I would definitely take a class from Atici again! He truly cares about his students and is always available for help.

He's a great professor in all honesty. His accent is a bit hard to get used to at first, but he's always telling jokes. There is no homework, 2 exams, 1 group(or solo) project. Super cool guy. Really laid back and fun. His lectures were always great. He knows how to keep you interested and makes you laugh while doing it. His talks tend to wonder off but always go back to the topic.

Professor Atici is a very personable guy! I've taken two of his classes. He is very caring and helpful. He truly cares about his students succeeding. Professor Atici is friendly and personable, with a good sense of humor. For ANTH 102 he followed the lecutre slides (which he modified). He made sure to accentuate the most important information. Overall a nice guy, I felt obligated to write this rating because Prof. Atici seems like he will really do what he can to help as long as you put in effort. He takes suggestions well and has been overall very helpful.

Study the textbook and his slides and you'll do great. This class was very interesting and I learned a lot about different cultures!
Very helpful and very interested in the subject matter. He is a wonderful asset to the University and I think he will be a wonderful department head some day.

Just completed a computer apps course with Dr. Atici.  He strives to help students succeed- if you need any help, you can go to him. He's a great asset for UNLV! The professor was really great! He was helpful and responsive! He replied Piaaza questions very quickly.

Class was very difficult and lectures were little to no help for assignments and prelims. Final is optional which is good, but can hurt you if you choose to take it.  Prelim medians were very difficult making the median very low, but the way Gries curves the class is somewhat confusing. Hardest class I've ever taken.
The exams make up the majority of your grade. When doing the assignments, make sure you REALLY know what you're doing, and understand what's going on if you're working with a partner.

The prelims are what actually decide your grade in this class. Gries provides a lot of information to help you succeed on these tests though. He provides a list of concepts and a lot of practice exams. He also answers question on piazza very quickly. His answers are very direct, but not rude (even when the questions are pretty rude).

Bad lecturer, good 1-1 teacher. Do the assignments to learn, but they have little to no impact on your grade; only the prelims matter. Had Bs on the prelims, A+ on assignments (above the mean on most) but still got a B. Things change from semester to semester (i.e. assignments, pace etc) but all lectures content-wise are on videonote.
Sometimes comes across weird on Piazza, but a very good lecturer and makes great resources for students in CS 2110.
His tests are hard but the lectures are extremely useful, very well organised and cover important topics. One of the best professors for Computer Science anywhere in America.
Gries is honestly hilarious. He's a slightly boring lecturer but is very fair and keeps the topic interesting. I liked the guy a lot.

Very interesting, though non-mandatory lectures. Clearly a legend in CS. Deeply cares about every student's success. Amazing teacher. Optional final. Watch out, though: mandatory midterms are very hard and he doesn't believe in curves ("if you all do C work, you will all get Cs"). TAs are very mediocre, and recitation attendance is very important.

Lectures are kinda boring and once in awhile he gets lost in his own examples. Incredibly fast response time if you ask him questions online; his replies are usually brief and even a little cold but I think its unintentional. He writes obscure and not really topical questions on the tests but Foster has made the questions more reasonable recently.

Gries is a very nice and helpful professor. The material in his class gives us a very good foundation for our future study in Computer Science. He is very patient when you ask him questions . One of best professors in Cornell.
Lectures were not helpful at all. You're basically on your own to learn the material and for the projects.

He was okay - he clearly understood what he was doing, and was willing to help but his Piazza responses were often terse and bordered on rude.  The class was not very challenging overall - the later parts, which mattered more, were not tested much and not necessary for a good grade in the class.

Lectures are vague; he goes over material too quickly. He'll help you, but only if you ask intelligent questions. He gets angry easily, especially if you neglect something he's already said somewhere sometime. Curves are not really nice.

He is a pretty good lecturer. He is an interesting guy with a super nice personality. Definitely learned a lot in this class. Only complaint is that sometimes his Piazza answers are rushed and unclear.
He makes the material too hard. He has a genuine desire to help students but just doesn't succeed.

He's my undergrad adviser. He taught me way beyond just being a good CS nerd. He taught me how and why I should analyze everything, and not be afraid of being different, one of a kind.  As I went through grad school and med schools, his teaching was still guiding me every step of the way.  Now I own medical centers, his words are still teaching me.
Gries is a good teacher, he's just really old and sometimes you just get really bored. The assignments are fun and straightforward, prelims straightforward, and final optional. I enjoyed his class!
One of the best professors I had at Cornell.

I usually just read comments and never give my own, but I feel an urge to leave my comment for the first time. I couldn't believe that there are so many bad comments about Gries. He is one of the best professors I've ever had  at Cornell. Passionate, knowledgeable, and extremely willing to help students out. A sweet old guy.

He has dumbed down 2110 to the point where it is basically intro to java. The assignments are step by step guides to writing a useless program. What's supposed to be a course that introduces Object Oriented programming and prepares students to get an internship at a CS company, is now a complete joke.
He's a good professor, very knowledgeable about the subject, and clearly interested in teaching. In person, he's very sweet and helpful. (But online, sometimes he seems rude and impatient...?)
Gries is the most helpful and condescending professor I know. Will help you but be prepared to feel stupid if you have a question. Not too difficult overall and is a good lecturer as well.

Gries is one of my favorite professors at Cornell so far. You can tell he cares about students and teaching a lot. He is the kind of professor who tries to do everything himself to make sure students understand class materials, for example, monitoring piazza all the time and answering all questions almost. He doesn't leave teaching tasks to TA's.
He is very good!

Let alone his teaching skills, if theres one person who gave me a whole new vision of computer science, Professor Gries is that person. He's single handedly the happiest person and best professor I have met. Being a student of his has been an absolute pleasure, and Im truly grateful.
The man is an absolute boss. He literally helped invent software engineering, and is extremely knowledgable in practically all areas of CS. He clearly enjoys teaching!
Very helpful professor. Clear in teaching. Want students to learn.

He is never going to teach again at Cornell!!! :(( He is the reason I am going into computer science. Best professor ever. Prelims were really challenging and final was easy. Assignments are not bad if you have done all your reading. Labs are really useful!

Pretty funny at times and definitely passionate about the subject.  Class can be irritating for those who have prior experience.  Gries is very set in his ways and obsessed with his metaphors and invariants.

I didn't really learn much in lecture (hard to learn programming by staring at a powerpoint). Labs and assignments helped a lot more for understanding. Prelims and final are somewhat challenging, but gives us previous exams to study. I never programmed before and I thought the class was alright.  He's retiring so not teaching CS 1110 anymore.

I don't understand know why so many people don't like his teaching style; really, professor Gries is just trying to teach us the basic stuff of programming. For those jackasses who can't program at all and think they are smart, do not blame professor Gries

Literally treats you like a 1st grader. Doesn't care at all about actually writing functional code. Beginning of the class is more about drawing pictures than actually learning to program. Makes stuff unnecessarily confusing. I usually skip lectures. Assignments graded way to harshly and for the wrong reasons. Worst professor I've had at CU so far.

If you want to be taught programming like a kindergartener, take this course. If you want to reprimanded every time you make a typo in your syntax, take this course. If you want your grade to suffer because your variable names aren't the ones Gries wanted, take this course. If your believe that your program working doesnt matter, TAKE THIS COURSE.
His course, CS 1130 is the worst course I have ever taken at Cornell.  He is not helpful at all.
It's really hard. Go to class

Never taken a CS class before. He was excellent introductory CS teacher - keep an open mind and good attitude in his class and his way of teaching works extremely well to help you grasp the material. I don't understand all this Gries-hating that goes on. CS is not meant to be an easy subject, his class is as easy an introduction as it gets.
Very knowledgeable on the subject (he literally wrote the book), but is an awful teacher.

I don't know what everyone is talking about - I really liked Prof. Gries. He is a very nice guys and I found him to be a very effective lecturer. I had no experience whatsoever in CS and I felt that I understood class and he even piqued my interested in the field. Personally, I'd highly recommend him. Best teacher I've had at Cornell yet.

I absolutely loved CS before this class. In this class I absolutely understood nothing that he said. The only stuff I knew was what my high school teacher had taught me (he was much better). Gries really was extremely nice but I learned nothing at all. It made me hate CS... :(

Nice guy, but atrocious teacher. Supposedly the rest of the CS department is superb except him. I had no programming experience and did terribly in this class even after working hard on it. TAs didn't seem to care. Tests are graded harshly. Had to drop the class. It reflects poorly on Cornell to have him as an introductory prof.
Horrible professor - nice guy. Doesn't understand the purpose of a metaphor.

Lectures were boring and important material on prelims were never covered in lecture. I was lost in labs because he never taught anything relevant in class and expected us to be able to figure it out ourselves in lab. He is also overly picky on the style code. TA's were helpful though.
Terrible!  He seemed like a very nice man, but I had no programming experience, and after this class, I still don't have any.  This is absolutely the reason I switched out of Engineering.

Gries is pretty boring, and I could only pay attention to Lillian Lee's lectures. He can be pretty helpful though and is a nice grandpa-like guy. For a first-timer at compsci, the textbook and beginning of labs were very confusing for me. The best help is to see the consultants, not the busy TAs. Once you've got the basics, the rest is fine.

I had no programming experience before this. Gries is not that clear until about the 5th time he repeats a subject. YOU have to put in serious work to do well, it's not a freebie class. With that said, I think the grading is hard but fair. He is actually extremely helpful if you ask. Prof Lee was teaching this class with him, that helped a LOT

I dont even know where to begin with this man. The assignments are graded abnormally harshly, he doesn't explain anything, the book that he wrote and makes us use is an illegible joke. He is more obssessed with drawing folders than programming. Avoid this man at all costs, you will not do well in his class.

Confusing concepts with the folder stuff doesn't make sense. Assignments and labs are EXTREMELY difficult if you've never programmed. Have to constantly get help from TAs, Consultants, friends. Takes too much time.

By FAR the worst professor I have ever had. I had never taken programming and don't understand anything of whats going on. He expects you to know everything although it is an introductory course. Highly confusing, convoluted notes that do not make sense. He should not even call himself a professor. Avoid this class.

Absolutely horrible. As a student who has never take Java I am extremely confused. He does not take time to explain anything thoroughly and expects you to do very difficult labs. He is very rude, condescending and has no right to call himself a professor by the way he behaves. The book (which he wrote) is even worse than he is. Avoid this class!
Very helpful when asked questions, promptly responds to emails, exams closely follow previous years, cares about students

While Java is interesting, Gries is not a great writer or lecturer.  He has a very stilted way of speaking, and he over uses italics to make his writing just a stilted.  His analogies are extremely basic, to an infuriating degree - you could be a very accomplished Java programmer and fail his exams if you didn't understand his boxes. Silly!

The course is more about teaching you Gries' metaphors and methods (which usually involve drawing boxes) than teaching you the concepts behind his metaphors and methods. James Gosling (the dude who started java) would probably fail the prelims because they're all about Gries' boxes and not about java.

The only good thing to come of this class is that Gries gets to force even more undergrads to buy his book. Your assignments are graded by a computer, and you receive no help with regrade attempts. Consultants are not motivated to help you. He teaches his own personal analogies like they are a universal standard. Horrible class. Dropping out

Gries is awful at teaching CS so if you don't have a background in Java make sure you buy a different textbook as Gries over complicates things and makes ridiculous analogies. Part of the problem is Gries wrote the textbook so many explanations are word for word from the book. Luckily prelims are easy but Gries spoils intro to Java.
Okay class with some nice assignments. The tests weren't very difficult either. The downside is that his lectures are really, really boring. By the second half of the class I just stopped attending.
I made it through 4 weeks of this guy's lectures before I couldn't take it anymore. Gries, your textbook sucks and PUT ON SOME SHOES
Stupid analogies. Makes you buy the textbook he wrote himself, so if you try and avoid his terrible teaching methods by reading the book, you get another dose of useless.

WARNING: if you have programming experience, you will probably hate this class.  His analogies and overly complicated ways of explaining simple concepts will drive you crazy.  If you have no programming experience, by all means, go ahead and take it, you should be fine if you do the work and read the textbook.
Is an awful ComSci teacher. If you don't read the book (which he co-authored with his son, btw), you will fail. The lecture is pointless, and his analogies are stupid.

His class was good, but if you've never taken CS before you'd need office hours. His exams are exactly what he tells you they'll be. Try memorizing the terms in addition to understanding them and you should do well. Also, the programming assignments are key - if you do well on them you'll most likely do well in the course.
He writes his test in codes that no one understands! Has to follow his stupid invariant for writing loops or you get no credit. Everyone is failing and he cracks stupid jokes. DONT TAKE HIS CLASS.
Great teacher, nice guy, and funny. I just dont like how hooked he is on the file drawer thing, but other than that pretty good class.

The entire class is dumbed down. His file drawer/manilla folder analogy is useless (will never apply if you decide to go further in programming). Experienced programmers and intro programmers are confused. Book is inappropriate (HS level text). Assigns reading on the CD with the book. CD plays a random sound when you click. Avoid this class.

Absolutely horrible book and analogies for simple programming concepts!  If you already know how to program,  I pity you for having to learn his new analogies for the exams.  If you don't know how to program, know this:  No one else teaches programming with such dumbed-down analogies as he does.

This man is best teacher! He is so kind and makes lots of jokes. He knows his class is not totally easy, but if you but a little effort in, you will like this class very much becuase gries rocks! He was also voted best teacher many times at cornell...

I really wanted to learn programming...but he made it very boring.  The lectures were a waste..too morbid. People were scared to raise hands!  I go to lectures for the profs, learning material on your own is no good when you can't get insight from good people.  The beginning of his course is good, easy to follow.  Later it's all over the place.
One of the most boring profs I've had

He has a childish and annoying way of teaching programming. Besides that the material is easy if you work on it and memorize terms and boxes, etc. He has a very nasty attitude too. I asked him for help and he accused me of wasting his time! Very Upsetting but whatever - he's still easy.

Good lecturer, goes slow and makes things easy to understand. He has some interesting metaphors which may seem a little childish but they get the job done (you really understand the material). I really respect this man.

I haven't been here that long, but Gries is the worst professor I have had so far. He's obsessed with drawing boxes and folders to confuse you instead of teaching you how to program, and he loves testing on them.  Uses stupid metaphors to explain things.  Oh, he also uses a Mac and doesnt wear shoes

He has this very formulaic way of teaching programming. This might not be too bad if you don't have any programming experience. If you go to his lectures, read the textbook, and do assignments, you'll do well. Exams are not hard, you just have to know it the way he teaches you to.

From my experience, Gries is a great cs professor for those who are just starting to learn java. Granted you must put the effort into learning the material! If you don't, you can expect to do poorly, which is ultimately the studens' fault not Gries's.

he makes you confused about the simplest of things. he has these stupid analogies about CS programming, and to him its more important that you learn his stupid analogies and methods rather than the ability to code. worst. professor. ever. (for me)
He should do sth about his stupid analogy system, seriously! yes, he is a jerk, and he made me suffer through these 2 classes!

The hardest class I have taken at Cornell.  He is an okay teacher, assumes you know a lot about subject already.  Not great in lecture, but helpful when you go to office hours.  V. hard class, assignments, and tests.

His lectures seemed designed more so that he could listen to himself talk than so that he could teach anything. When he did attempt to actually inform you of something, it was generally done in a condescending tone using insipid metaphors.
Good professor, is overly paticular about knowing his analogies

Terrible.  He is malicious, doesn't prepare (slides and even STUDY GUIDES have typos), not in contact with TAs, doesn't care.  Makes fun of students.  Have to follow his conventions.  Probably the worst professor at Cornell.  Ruins otherwise great topics.
Horrible horrible class.  Stupid analogy system and you are tested more on that than on programming!  His lectures are unclear and he spent most of the time fixing his own mistakes.

Just a note, you are supposed to have programming experience to take CS 100J. Otherwise you're supposed to take CS 099. And, besides Gries is such a nice man. So what if his analogies are strange (what the hell is a remora?).
What a nice man. He is soooo helpful and enthusiastic. Some people don't like his metaphors, but they're good if you've never programmed before. Knows his stuff.

What an incredibly bad teacher.  The man has no idea how to present ideas for an audience, his folders/files analogy is the worst I've seen (and the TAs all think it's useless too) and his lectures show a total lack of respect for his students.  Someone s

Spent half of each lecture updating his typo-ridden powerpoint presentations. Add to that inconsistent grading, a $55 draft of a book, and the assumption that you already have programming experience, and you have a pretty horrible class.
hmmnn...very interesting prof...avoid CS courses if possible.Theyr tougher than u can imagine.cheers,ben.

Sorry to disagree, but I think Gries was an awesome prof.  Very approachable.  The class was pretty easy, as long as you did the readings and attended lecture.  The concepts that he emphasized in the course were really useful for CS211.

Difficult to attend class due to teacher.  Class seems pointless, programming is long and painful, it seems you have to program the way he would or you lose points (not much room to do you own programming), folders/file-drawers. Take only if you have to.

Avoid if possible.  Heavy emphasis on analogies involving file drawers, folders, and other office supplies.  Excessive focus on invariants when writing loops.  The textbook (his own) is riddled with typos, as are his assignments from time to time.

Prof. Gries is a horrible way to start your programming career. He teaches an extended metaphor of "manilla folders" as instances of classes, and we are tested in these horrible anolgies. However, Gries will give you the answers during prelims i
I have a problem with folders and file cabinets.  And why do they have to be specifically manila folders?
Tough but fair, if you put the work into his class you'll learn a lot.
Doesn't teach material in an understandable fashion. You will not learn how to program in Java by just showing up to class and labs. Tough grader.

Proff. Hairston is a genuinely good standard professor. He teaches exactly why you SHOULD know for the exam. It's probably not his fault that whoever writes the exams has issues with constructing a clear question. It seems like they give a group of grad students shots of tequila and then make them write the exam from memory, and then no one revises
One of the best professors I have ever come across while earning a degree. Friendly, honest, respectful, knowledgeable Great guy and made for a great experience in Limnology

Nelson is awesome- he really cares about his students and wants you to get excited about lakes! He studies zooplankton so he focuses his teaching on that but you'll learn a lot about limnology in general. Take the lab if you can- you'll learn applicable skills and Nelson teaches the labs himself- not just a TA. One of my favorite professors!
Very nice, clear instructor. Interesting and kind. I wish he had taught more of my class!
Great professor, one of my favorites at Cornell.  Nelson speaks very clearly and the way he taught the class allows you to follow the material very well and stay engaged.  Lakes are awesome!
Nelson is a great prof and a nice guy. He really really knows his stuff about lakes and makes the subject extremely interesting.

Dr. Darrell is a good knowledgable professor however she is a very tough grader and is quite sarcastic. She knows what she talking about but will often insert her sarcasm. She is not always clear on writing assignments which are very confusing. Her test was quite hard as well but it was open book. She often has epiphany assignments that she gives.
Great professor. Does give a lot of assignments that will be helpful in the long run.
Inspirational when she speaks about her achievements and accomplishments. Some lectures may be strictly about that!!

Dr. Darrell was very unorganized.  She was not clear in asking for what she wanted in our assignments.  The class did not seem like it was a priority because she would change things on a whim.  Also, she did not seem open when asking for help.  I had several classmates challenge their final grades because she has no clear grading system.  I would NOT take her again.

She was a very tough grader. If you don't get what she wants out of her papers, YOU BETTER SPEAK UP! If not, you will wish you would have. She does not require too many assignments but a LOT of reading from the DSM-IV (now DSM-V). The few assignments that you do have are (let's say) OVERWHELMING only if you don't understand. Her test are easy.

he never got to the point. You basically have to teach yourself. I somehow taught myself how to do the math, my friend struggled, he never really answered the questions you asked. He required a textbook, but never used it. take notes on equations he gives. other than that the mylabs examples helps me better than him.

Good math teacher, really cares about the students. Interesting to listen to the lectures, the guy is obviously extremely smart. Also encouraged a lot of extra credit by means of campus events which was nice. Overall one of the better professors at Columbia State.

I didn't appreciate him enough until I realized other statistics professors have you use complicated formulas while he teaches you to use statcrunch. He can ramble sometimes and class time can be slow, but he's very understanding and compassionate. Overall chill dude and good professor for intro stats.

Professor Darrell is hands down my favorite professor this semester. He always makes sure to apply the material to real-life data (which makes his lectures more intriguing in my opinion). He has always answered emails very quickly and seems to be very understanding when it comes to class absences. Overall, I wish I had more professors like him.

Professor Darrell was one of my favorite teachers this semester. Don't get me wrong, I hate statistics and I struggled with the class. However, he is extremely willing to help you succeed. He is very responsive to emails and willing to work with you if you need help. I would recommend him if statistics is a requirement for you to take.
Worst math class I've ever encountered. Had 8 exams in the last 2 weeks of class. I would not recommend it.

Very big ego, pretty much implies if you aren't basically a budding mathematician you won't pass his class. Will do lectures that barley correspond with the homework and expects you to spend all your free time doing math. Gets mad easily, and many other problems. I do not recommend this teacher at all.

Great teacher. Tries to make content relevant and extensively covers example sets. For lower level courses, there are practice exams and clearly presented material. In person classes are fun because he starts each class session off with group trivia for extra points.

Prof. Darrell is amazing. I absolutely loved his class. He is so caring about his students and just overall kind. He gives practice quizzes for every test so you have a chance to review and drops the lowest quiz and test grades at the end of the semester. He shows you exactly what you need to write down in your notes and explains everything well.

Best grade I've EVER gotten in a math class (coming from an English major). Professor Darrell is incredibly knowledgeable and willing to work with you no matter what. The homework is helpful and the quizzes and tests are near identical. He also drops your lowest test AND quiz grade. Seriously, if you need a math credit, take this professor!

Took his online course in March due to Covid. Genuinely enjoyed it. HOWEVER. He does assign alot of online homework and quizzes. In his lectures he tends to ramble a bit about off topic things and gets a bit boring. Lets just say youll End up teaching yourself math. If you take his class please be ready to work, its not an easy A at all.

I really enjoyed this professor, I'm not good in math and he explained thing really well in class. He listens and stops to make sure everyone understands. Everything homework, quizzes, and test are all online, which is nice. He does extra credit in class.
He was good I just wasnt good at math
Mr. Darrell is a great teacher, he really helps you to understand the material. I would highly recommend him for the summer course.

The very first day of class, he basically told us that if we didn't already know how to do everything in the class, we might as well leave. Somebody also gave an incorrect answer at one point, and he spoke to us in a pretty condescending way. He assigned homework due on a specific day and 4 days before the date, assigned 4 quizzes due on that day.

Loved this class and this professor. I'm kind of a natural in math--even AP Calc in HS--but statistics has always been a grey area for me. However, he really helped me to understand rather than just shoving terms and formulas down my throat. He's great at explaining things and making sure everyone is on the same page. Just prepare for a lot of hw.

I really enjoyed and followed his teaching methods. I thought he was an amazing teacher. He's great. Very clear, Very concise. Just take notes and don't be afraid to ask questions. I was struggling with a problem in class, and he just gently encouraged me to try it. Very understanding of students problems (whether in class or not).

Mr. Darrell was the best stats professor I could've asked for! He really took the time to explain every concept and would help when asked. He teaches you how to do everything on the calculator and how to do it mentally. Almost every assignment is online, including tests and homework. The tests and homework are identical so write everything down!!

If you're a natural at math then this class will be no problem. Everything is done online and it's a learn it yourself class. This instructor is not good at teaching but if you have free time and good study habits you will do fine.

If you can handle a professor that is rude, belittles you, and gives sarcastic answers to questions, then by all means, take Professor Darrell. I have not encountered a professor who seems to care so little about his students success before this class.

Mr. Darrell was ok. He gave so much homework and was very vague when answering questions. If you didn't know how to work something on a calculator, he would just recommend you learn that on your own instead of helping, like a teacher should. Very odd. Also, there were at least 3 times were we went over class time for more than 5 minutes.

I would not recommend this teacher. He doesn't manage class time well, he is rude, doesn't take the time to help he just expects you to understand the material. lots of homework. Test are difficult because it is stuff that he didn't go over in class.
I thought Professor Darrell was wonderful! He gave all the information we needed during lecture. If you take good notes you will pass.

Good teacher if math is your thing, all of the homework, quizzes and test are on MyMathLab. When it comes to deadlines/due dates he usually ends up moving them because people aren't finished unless its one or two people. Talks the full amount of time every class period. Must put in work outside of the class. If you like math take him.

Not a fan. Very standoffish, and is quick to point out if you're even wrong a little bit. Throws tons of work on you last minute. Gives you a lot of time to do a chapter of homework, but yells at you if it's not done before the due date. Not very helpful.

Didn't manage class time well. We spent the first 4 weeks of the semester crawling through stuff that should have been common sense, and then blitzed through the tough stuff at the end of the class.  If you are math minded it wont be that bad, just read the book and try to keep ahead, if you're not math minded, get a tutor.

I think he was fairly thorough with his explanations.  We got behind, so there was probably 40-50 hours of homework in the last 2 weeks.  That was rough.  He doesn't respond to everyone's emails or questions for help.  He cursed at us once out of anger.  I thought he was thorough, but I'm okay at math.  If you're not, you'll need a tutor.
I highly do not recommend him
I would never take a class of his. he isn't specific. moves entirely too fast. doesn't explain well. expects you to just get it and when you don't doesn't help you enough to get it.

Yes, the class was very hard; it was calculus, not finger-painting 101. What a lot of people don't seem to get is that he made it a lot easier than it could have been. He gave practice tests, extra credit, and online tests. If asked for help on a problem, he would do that as well. Maybe he was harder on others in previous classes, but not for me.

The man is absurd as a teacher. Incredibly melodramatic, always screaming about how if you don't know this or that you won't pass. He projects his learning style onto his students, "if I can do it you can", can't even do hw problems without help from other teachers, and obsesses over insignificant details. You don't take his class, you endure it.

Definitely a hard class, but I put a lot of time and work into the tests, homework and quizzes and passed with an A. The only thing that bothered me about Mr. Darrell was he did drone on a little bit sometimes, and he was not at all lenient about absences even when I had a valid excuse. Otherwise, I would take him again. Lots of extra credit!!!

The first couple of weeks were easy. the homework had examples so you could see how to work the problems. Well he took that off around week three, and you need that to pass because he is a awful teacher. Never had a problem with math till this class. I'm struggling to pass it. Test and quizes are hard. Don't take Darrell!!!!!!

He wastes too much time on unnecessary details. He is constantly working problems wrong and hardly gives enough examples of problems. This course was basically self taught and I did horrible. Do not take. He wasted 30 min of review before a test on a problem he couldn't work, then deleted it from the homework and said we'd never see it again anyway

He is a stickler for every sign. He constantly back tracks on his examples in class because he messed up the problem. then he doesn't take the time to start back over,  he just changes the part he messed up and tells you to fix it. He spends longer showing you how not to do problems, than he does actually teaching the right way. Worst teacher.

This course is one of the harder general education requirements during a regular semester and is even more intense during an accelerated summer course. R. Darrell is in-depth in his in class examples, however he does expect you to read the book and attempt extra problems. Not the type of professor one takes, if expecting an easy course load.

First of all if you don't to spend every waking hour doing calculus then dont take this class. His tests are confusing, summer class is near impossible. Quiz everyday, hours of homework each night. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

He is very rude. His tests are difficult. His quizzes are ridiculous. He expects you to give word for word definitions. If you define something with a correct definition, but not with HIS definition - then its wrong. I would recommend any other teacher than him. I am a 4.0 student and almost failing his class.
