Tough grader and LOTS of assignments, but I do really like Dr. Kieran. I've taken her for Careers and Abnormal. She is a good lecturer and cares about her students. I feel like I learned a lot from her. She's not easy by any means, but if you want to make a career in Pysch and you ENJOY Pysch, she's great!

Took this course during the spring. She docks points for EVERY little thing! It's almost like her life mission. Nothing is ever good enough for her. If you miss a period a question mark, or the smallest detail she will take off 10-12 points. Do yourself a favor and skip her.

I took her during the summer and I wouldn't take her ever again. She docks points for EVERY little thing. It seems like it's her life mission. Yes, there is extra credit but by the time she docks all your points off that's your extra credit.

class was super easy, but there is a lot to do. online activities, lots of discussions, quizzes, i think 4 exams, and 1 essay. the essay was super hard, but i made a C on it and still passed the class with an A. there is so much extra credit! there is a lot of assignments but it is all easy and there is extra credit for everything. i learned a lot!

I know it's only 5 weeks into the semester but, this professor is great. She has a very detailed rubric for each assignment which pretty much guarantees you at least an B or an A if you followed it precisely. She also drops your 3 lowest quiz grades. Tests are on lockdown and webcam, but the quizzes are not. Weekly discussions with bonus points.

I loved Dr. Kieran's careers in psychology course! The assignments were fun and useful. If you are an average student and you put in effort you will come out of this class with an A. Dr. Kieran is very descriptive with her teachings and straightforward with her expectations. She honestly cares for her students. Would def take again.

I enjoyed Dr. K's class. The course was well designed and easy to navigate, the assignments weren't too intense, and she's a pretty nice person who gives a fair bit of extra credit. My only real critique is that it would occasionally take her a long time to grade, especially discussion posts.

I took her online summer course. Online elements are straightforward and organized. Several quizzes, discussion boards, three tests, and four projects. Many extra credit opportunities. Lecture/reading heavy.  Not too difficult, but a bit of an excessive workload considering the class. The class is supposed to help you, not stress you out even more.

Dr. Kieran gives many opportunities to receive extra points. There are weekly quizzes and discussion posts, so be sure to pay attention to the weekly due dates. The discussion points can get extra points and she drops the 3 lowest quiz grades. Attendance is mandatory but class is only once a week and you can miss several before affecting your grade

I love her! She is so kind and caring, all the work given is very clear and easy to follow. The textbook and powerpoints will prepare you for tests, they never include anything she has not covered. Weekly discussion posts/quizzes. Take her if you can :)

She is a great professor. The only thing I didn't like was that she had a 'flipped classroom'. So basically we had to listen to her pre-recorded lectures on our own, and then we talked in class. Personally, I didn't like this bc got easily distracted. She does give plenty of extra credit and is nice. Wants us to succeed. STUDY for exams!!

I really loved professor Kieran. She really taught me so much about careers in psych and she was always ready to help students. The class is a bit over-average on the work load but it was all relevant and easy to navigate. There is a lot of extra credit, and her projects were mostly fun as well.
Online course was very straight forward. Quizzes were not on lockdown. Genuinely passionate about the material. Study for the tests and you'll get an A.

This is honestly the easiest class Ive ever taken. The prof is super sweet and gives a lot of extra credit. Quizzes are open book/note and she drops 3 of your lowest quiz scores. You can easily get over 100% in the class. If you fail this class you need to evaluate yourself.

Took her Online class. Weekly assignments but all very easy. No textbook required, PowerPoint and Lectures only. The test are easy because theyre strictly based from PowerPoint (lecture material isnt on test). If you can keep up with weekly assignments and do well on test you can certainly get an A but I wouldnt call it an easy A.

Take her! She is very clear in lectures and if you attend and pay attention you basically have everything you need for the exams. She is very friendly and even helped me with a project for an entirely different class two semesters after I had taken her class. She even remembered me when I emailed. And Im not a memorable student, in my opinion.

Dr. K was the absolute best professor I've ever had. As this was an online class (due to covid), all lectures were prerecorded and students were expected to complete discussion posts. Tons of opportunity to gain extra points is given and Dr. K will absolutely work with you if needed. Fantastic lectures and a fantastic teacher. Absolutely love Dr. K

There were never any papers in this class - had 3 (or 4) tests and that's it. Lecture-based but incredibly easy class to pass. Teaching-wise, she's hilarious and amazing. Her lectures are never boring, and she's very respectful of others if you're respectful of her time as well.

I loved Dr K. She does make you work and you do need to read the chapters, but she is a wonderful teacher. I loved her power point lectures, studying those really helped me do well in her class. There are several extra credit opportunities. She is a great choice!

I took online spring semester Dr. Kieran's Abnromal Psychology and it was pretty good. Even though it was online, the TA Lindsay was really helpful and I recommend getting to know the TA of future classes. She's a bit strict on her one essay so make sure you dive heavily into her rubric very carefully. Study the slide shows & book for the test.

Dr. K is a great professor. She is super sweet and genuine. You can tell that she truly cares about the well-being of her students. Lots of class discussion, 3 exams, 3 projects, and a couple of extra credit opportunities. I learned a lot in this class & it made me love psychology even more. Pay attention during lecture. PP slides alone won't help.

I've taken her twice & both were VERY difference experiences. I will not be taking her again. For this class you have 3 exams & 3, detailed projects. Exams are multiple choice and SA, & her study guides are bogus. She graded assignments HARSHLY, with majority of the class failing the second project & she did nothing about it. Attendance is graded

I had Dr K for my Careers in Psych class and she was amazing! Very sweet and cares about her students. The textbook is required and she compresses it into slides for her lectures, which makes her tests easy. You can tell she cares about her students and she is very generous with grading projects, etc. Get into her class her if you can!!!

lots of extra credit opportunities. she gives a lot of pop quizzes, but they're quite easy if you did the reading. it's a very helpful class, and she cares a lot about her students. make sure to follow all directions for assignments. the syllabus is crucial to the way she teaches.

Dr. Kieran is one of the most caring professors I've ever had at KSU. There were 2 tests and 2 projects in her class. Projects were easy, but time consuming. Her tests were more difficult because she never tells you what's going to be on it. Just says that the powerpoints should be our study guide. Overall, sweet lady. Easy class. Just study.

Shes a great professor, understands what shes teaching and loves doing it. Her exams are application based and there is no study guide, so going in without having studied at least a little is not an option. One 5 page paper but its SUPER EASY and actually fun to do. A good bit of homework to do. Love the class and I love the professor.

Dr. Kieran is one of the best professors Ive taken at kennesaw. Her tests are straight from the power points, she even bolds the terms so we know which ones to learn. Her hw is through learning curve so you have to buy an access code for the textbook, or you can do all the assignments in the 2 week free trial.

Come to class. Engage. The rest is easy. 2 exams and a final. Article critique, one independent project, and a self examination paper. Easy A if you just do the minimum. I didn't use the textbook and got an A

I took her hybrid class and it was laid out really well. I highly recommend taking her for any of her classes if possible. She is passionate about her subject. If you study and put in effort, you will get the grade you want. Review sessions with UTA is highly advised, if times work with you, because they are super useful. She has great humor too!!
took the hybrid. shes funny and smart, wants to help, easy tests, not too much work. one big essay but not too bad. completely recommend and will take again!

Man I loved Dr. Kieran! Her tests and assignments are not too difficult, but are still a good assessment if you're actually learning. The discussions in this course are so great. Dr. Kieran really cares about her students succeeding, but also their self care. Take her!!!
Unclear lectures on an already confusing subject, students give up trying to learn material, examples are poor and unclear, just random ideas she comes up with on the spot
She's my favorite professor. You will learn and laugh in a very tough class. Accessible, seriously cares for her students-- Love Dr. Kieran, take her whenever you can

Dr. Kieran is an awesome professor! She is funny and very approachable. She does grade pretty tough, but she also gives detailed feedback. There is a project/presentation for this class. Be sure to get started early if you can. Looking over the quizzes at the end of the book chapters will help with the exams and quizzes she gives.

Dr. K is so sweet and funny. One of my favorite profs at KSU. Attendance isn't required, but go to class because the lectures are great. She also genuinely cares for her students and will help you out with any questions. She knew the material and was passionate about psychology, which made the class fun and interesting. Literally inspired me

This is one of the hardest classes, but only because the material is very dense. Dr. K gives you everything you need to make an A and is very willing to help you out. Her lectures are hilarious and very intriguing. I definitely recommend every psych student taking this class because you learn a lot of valuable information.
Great Professor. She is tough but she makes the material so interesting.

After the first exam she decided to have open discussion instead of lecturing over material. She also made attendance 10% of the grade, so you had to waste your time and attend. She also grades personally. So, if she feels like you deserve a C even though you earned a B, you're getting a C. Not accessible after class. Find someone else.

Dr. Kieran is the best Psychology professor I've had at KSU. She constantly works to make sure that we have to most up-to-date information on the subject. She has short answer portions on her tests, and those can be tricky, but if you study, it's fine. Four tests including final, which is cumulative. 4 online quizzes. & 1 (fun) paper. Take her!!

Super interesting, super helpful, funny, blunt, goes out of her way to help students understand, has built in extra credit assignments. I took her for abnormal and physio, both classes are hard because they're upper level classes, the material is hard. Dr. Kieran goes out of her way to make lectures interesting and her lecture slides are beautiful.

Dr. Kieran was an amazing professor for Physio. Lectures are long, but she makes it fun and easy. Her test aren't very hard if you study, they do cover a lot of information though. I got an A on the paper and I wrote it the night before it was due, it's not hard at all. Take her, you won't regret it. She also gives extra credit.

Dr. Kieran is a wonderful person and she's brilliant! She's there for you when you need it. There are only 3 tests including the final, one paper, an annotated bibliography that's an easy A, and a group project that wasn't too bad. I'm taking her again for Abnormal Psych next semester :)

Paper worth 200 points, no direction given, example paper is riddled with errors, and is unwilling to help us out. Exam average was close to 73's for all exams, and the average for the paper was 72. Information overload compared to what will be on the exams. Exams are difficult. I worked my butt off and I barely have a B.

The class material is fascinating. The professor, however,  is not. We received virtually no instruction for a term paper worth 200 points of our grade. Expectations were not clear whatsoever. she's a nice person, but an awful teacher. often times unclear about what she wants and what we need to know about the exam and for the papers. goes off topic a lot. doesn't go over the exam. SHE'S A HARD GRADER. you think you got an A on the paper? nope you got a C.  two papers, three exams (including the final)

Great professor, but her lectures sometimes get off topic because other students chip in on their stories. Her tests are hard, but you have to study the powerpoints precisely. Overall, great teacher, but just needs to be more clear on what's on tests.

I made an A, but worked hard. There's one paper and it was an easy A. The tests are what is kind of hard. Pay attention to boldunderlinedcapitalized words on her power points. There are some short answer and fill in the blank questions but if you study you're good. You don't need the book, I didn't look at it once all semester. Great professor!!

Cross Cultural Psych. Posted previously saying might get an A but got a B. Most people got Bs who wanted As. Some thought were getting Bs got Cs. Must study everything on slides beyond study guides. Read articles and book to ensure an A. Not an easy A. But great teacher.

Study slides well for tests, not book. The book just helps to understand more and she tells us to read it before class so can discuss better but slides are most important. Didn't study slides well on first test and got a c on it. But think can get an A by the end.

AWESOME professor! She puts the slides online, and the tests come primarily from those. One big project due in the semester, but it isn't too bad. I would definitely take her. She makes everything perfectly clear and is always willing to answer any questions.

I would try to take any other professor over her. She isn't terrible but never let us go over our tests/quizzes, or never see them for that matter, so we never knew what we got wrong and right. Interesting material, but if I could go back, I'd take Wolfe.

Professor Kieran is absolutely wonderful and I highly recommend her. The class is really interesting and the textbook is actually a good read. There's a project but it's easy and fun.

Nice guy, seems like he wants to be helpful. But he's so terrible with his organizational skills that he is not able to effectively teach. You read so much and talk about maybe 20% of it. He's constantly changing due dates and expectations. Not cool.

He is without a doubt one of the best professors at Franklin and Marshall. Professor Kieran really cares about his students. He makes you work, but if you put the effort forth, it will pay off in the end.

I took his 9/11 war on terror fys. Tons and tons of reading. Insane amount actually. He's a tough grader and can definitely come off as arrogant  in his lectures but all in all I have never learned more. Great guy. Go to office hours. participate in class.
He is helpful considerate professor. He really enhance me to think critically. He will give you a good grade if you do work hard. I learned a lot!

He's really a great professor. He cares a lot about his students and takes his job seriously. He isn't easy, but he will definitely help you become a better writer and a more engaged student. Definitely take his class!

Great guy but not an easy professor.  He gives you a ton of reading and expects you to do all of it.  Also grades very hard.  However, he is helpful if you show him you care.. see him in office hours!

Great professor. Definitely cares about his students, and he tries to incorporate interesting popular movies and such into the class. He's a bit tough, but he gives constructive feedback and makes sure students understand how to get a better grade. Take his classes while he's still here!

I love Kieran!  Aside from being really attractive :), he's a great guy who cares about his students and will really push you to do your best in his class. 911 Course - To the previous comment - I felt the same at the beginning but it got really much more clear towards the end. aside from knowing he has a phd I haven't learned much else.  you read a lot but talk about the same stuff over and over. not really sure where this class is going...i'll check back in at the end of the semester.

Professor Kieran is passionate about Public Funding and very knowledgeable in the subject. Her video lectures on youtube are personable and easy to follow. Get ready to work for your grade. Hes tough. Get ready to read. Very very political. 3/5. I like him but others do not.

I took his 20th Century America, I love him if I did history I would make him my advisor. Overall hes decent. Dont disagree with his opinions thought. He has to be right and if hes not he will belittle you. Socialist who lets you know about it but doesnt let political ideas affect his grading. Dont challenge him though. He thinks hes better than you.
Super tough professor but if you do the reading and participate he is fair. Great guy to converse with in and out of class. Take him!
Show up to lecture it's helpful
This professor made my class easy and smooth! They give really good feedback and the assignments are light and simple. I would 100% take this class again if I could or have this professor again :)

The nicest PE teacher I've met, she just wants you to have fun and show up to class. She accepts makeup if you cannot make it to class, Definitely recommend. Not only is it an easy class but fun! I took her volleyball course.

I took her class online and it was very easy. Few things to turn it. Normally easy. Sometimes I forgot it was even due because of how easy it would be and fast to complete. Definitely take this professor.

Super nice professor, obviously a PE teacher who got stuck with an academic class. It was simple and straightforward. Nothing crazy. Teacher is very nice. It is nice learning about kinesiology professions as a kin major. Don't take this if you're trying to get PE credit and not a kin major- will not be valuable for you at all. Take it (:

Take Coach Roblee for volleyball. She plays music and is very easy-going. You don't have to be the best, just show up to class and participate. Had a great time in her class
Brilliant professor, great guy. Highly recommended. An absolute expert on negotiations and conflict resolution.  Incredibly clear, very willing to help, you will leave having learned TONS.
great class.  tons of reading but the only thing thats important is Fisher and Ury's Getting to Yes.
He is a brilliant professor and an even better human being. I loved everything about his class and would highly recommend it to anyone who wants to learn about negotiations and conflict resolution.
Makes a very dry subject somewhat interesting.  Very easy exams.

Professor Lipsky made my Cornell and my ILR experience.  I took three classes with him and did my honors thesis with him.  He's one of the world's foremost experts in the field of dispute resolution and yet is one of the most kind, generous, and personable people I have had the pleasure of knowing.  A great professor and a better friend.
I ma an old timer ('85 grad). Prof Lipsky is a gentleman and a fine teacher

One of Cornell's very best and most experienced profs who had also been a Dean of ILR.  Focusing on negotiation skills and bargaining power, the course is really interactive and practical and will remain so even if the concepts of unionism and CB in the US continue to evolve in the same direction.
Interesting material, funny anecdotes, overall a really great and caring (albeit busy) professor & inspiring mentor. He enjoys teaching and it shows.
Very interesting prof, lectures are great. Very busy so not always availible to help, try Seeber instead. Very knowledgable and clear.  Lectures actually keep me awake!

A very interesting professor who is very involved in negotiations like the NYPD.  His experience in his many facets of his career allow him to make the connections between the course and his experience.  He pretty much told us during his lectures what could be on the final exam which was helpful.
I love professor Lipsky. So interesting.
best professor i've had at Cornell, makes the material interesting, tests are fair and gives a lot of choice, take 601 with him too
One of the best profs I have ever had - he's really amazing.
Cool guy.  Tells interesting stories in class which give rather bland material life.  Definatey should dtake multiple classes with him.
Looks like Dr. Evil, but  is cool and interesting

Rudest professor in my college experience. The material is confusing.

Very awful. Assignment is very unclear. The professor is very inconsiderate. Thought it would be fun class but ended up being my least favorite class for the semester. Hate this class.

Great class and great professor. It sounds like he was really tough on the psych 1102 class. I guess he must have learned a lesson, because he was great in this class. He's a very engaging professor, clearly very interested in teaching. I strongly recommend seeing him in office hours, especially if you are interested in the subject.

He gives interesting lectures and is very funny, although sometimes he tries a little too hard to get a laugh. He's awesomely nerdy and passionate about linguistics. Sometimes funny and interesting, but boring and slow at other times. He's not rude to students, at least not in this semester. Readings are boring, and tests have vague multiple choice answers sometimes. And this is cognitive SCIENCE. Expect some technical stuff. Okay professor.

One of the rudest professors in my entire college experience. He insults students for asking questions (its an intro class)and is a terrible teacher. HORRIBLE! NEVER EVER EVER think of taking cog sci with him. It will ruin your gpa and your life!

He could sometimes be funny and occassionally sparked my interest in lecture. However, most of the time I found both the lectures and the readings boring, hard to get through, and hard to stay awake in. He's also very unaccomodating with make-ups. Overall, avoid this class if you can.
HORRIBLE. he destroyed an easy into class. Lectures made no sense, reading were long and pointless. Exams hardly made sense

Hale is a great professor, he makes you work and think.  Other people just dislike him because it's not "an easy do-nothing  A".  That shouldn't mean he's a bad professor though.  He's also very fair and very clear in what he wants you to know.

HATED this class.  Easily my least favorite class at Cornell.  He seemed to get angry at questions (even of the students were being smart-alecs).  Tests were confusing, lectures unclear, and I felt like he focused too much on the computer science aspect of the subject.  I wish I had never taken it.
This is the worst class. The material is confusing and innapplicable for an intro class. I dropped it after 3 weeks because it was very uninteresting and confusing.

This was absolutely the worst class I have taken at Cornell. Not only is he unable to teach the material at an introduction level, he is rude to students with questions. This class is not as hard as others described. As an ILR major, I took this class for my distribution req. and actually enjoyed it. I'm not the kind of person that is extremely good at sciences, but I feel like the class is of proper difficulty. To assure you, as for now I have a 90% in this class. Hale is very enthusiastic and a good lecturer.
i don't know anyone that has above a 75% in this class and he hasn't said the word "curve" all semester. this class is awful.

This class is impossible. There is no text book and Hale is pompous. I was intimidated the whole semester and never felt comfortable going to him for help. The readings are dense and the lectures are confusing and unclear. Unless you really love the subject, don't take this class. I thought it would be a fun/interesting elective. I was wrong.

THIS CLASS IS HARD. there is no textbook and the online readings are very dense and dull. lectures are a must, because without them its really hard to put the readings together. if you aren't VERY interested in artificial intelligence, this is not the class for you. this class DESTROYED my interest in cognitive science (i was planning a minor)

Hale is a good professor and is helpful and fairly clear, but linguistics is a difficult subject. Hale is cool, he's funny but he seems to forget it's an intro class sometimes especially with the vocab he uses. Try flipping through the book before adding this course!

An amazing professor with extreme enthusiasm about his subject and his students.  He is willing to help students however much they need, so long as they show an interest in learning and working at the material. Not a class or a professor for slackers though, Hale will make you WORK for your grade.

One of my best class experiences at CSU. Dr. Jimenez Chacon very obviously cares and encourages all of his students, and you basically get out what you put in. There is a lot of reading material, but as long as you read and do the assignments and participate in discussions, this class is amazing

Dr. Jimenez Chacon was honestly the BEST professor I have had at CSU. He is incredibly knowledgeable and extremely respectful. No matter what level you are at, he still manages to make every student feel comfortable. Participation is key- DO NOT let this scare you because the course is amazing and you will learn so much! Please take this class!

One of the smartest people I've had the pleasure to be taught by. You can tell that he loves to teach and share his ideas, but that means you should be open to sharing yours too. He is always SO kind about whatever you decide to contribute in class
Genuinely the best spanish professor I've ever had. He is so encouraging, so kind, and motivates students to learn

Incredibly understanding and kind. Best Spanish professor I've had in the US. Encourages participation in class discussions, but gives you time to prepare and time to discuss in smaller groups first. Welcomes all kinds and levels of spanish, obviously has a huge passion for what he teaches. Great guy.

Very passionate instructor who clearly loves what he teaches. Be patient with him as he is a new professor at CSU and seems to be writing his own lesson plans from scratch. He makes you think critically.
Very good professor. Super smart. Although sometimes he is a little bit wordy.

Professor Del Rio is super sweet and has a great sense of humor. Do the readings and go to class!

MAJOR sweetheart. I went into this class after 2 years of no Spanish courses and very little conversation and I was scared out of my mind. She totally understood and helped me feel comfortable speaking Spanish again. Such a positive atmosphere and I ALWAYS left in a better mood after every class.
She is a wonderful professor and a beautiful person. Love her. Would take any class that she teaches.
One of the best teachers I've ever had.

I love Angela (Maria Rubin)! So sweet. If you are a good student, she lets you get away with turning in compositions late and making-up quizzes. Gives clear outlines for tests and quizzes. The Best

She has a big heart! She is my favorite instructor at UNLV so far. It was fun and very challenge at the same time. Very worth it!

Professor Angela is a wonderful professor! Although Span 213 was very difficult for me, she made this class feel less like hell by providing good feedback. He was the TA for a lasers course I took. His accent was a bit hard to understand. The course was really tough and he seemed willing to help. But it was difficult to understand him. He showed care and good command of subject though.

I was able to coast a little bit having taken AP Calc but even without that it wouldn't have been overwhelming.

Prof. Holm is by far the best math professor I had in my life. Her passion for math and teaching makes the lecture interesting and inspires others to transform their attitudes towards math. From her I could totally see myself taking another math class after Calc 1. I'm lucky to have her. Highly recommended.
Very helpful and brilliant math professor. But you do need to study for the tests and put efforts to homeworks. You will learn a lot and will not regret taking it.

Lectures were very clear and organized. Homework and exams were challenging but not impossible, and even interesting! Prof. Holm could get flustered sometimes but is really nice, helpful, and brilliant.
Great Dame; sweet/cute, intelligent, and helpful. She sometimes confused me, but at other times, she lit the lightbulb for math. Definitely recommend this class and professor.

I admit that math simply did not play in my favor at Cornell, but Professor Holm is extremely awkward & frequently difficult to follow during class. She goes off on random tangents for half an hour at a time and leaves everyone falling asleep. She does try to be helpful if you're lost, but if you don't understand it her way, you may never.
Very good professer!  Really knows her materials, though the class moves really fast.  She is extremely willing to help you at any point to make sure no one is confused.
He does not cover enough material correlated with the textbook. Very unresponsive to emails. Tests are inconsistent with lecture material.
The hws and exams were not bad. The exams had medians of like 50s, which is awful but knowing that if you know half of the material and youll get a B was fine with me. Attend lectures for credit.
His class was not great, but it wasn't terrible either. Certainly was mainly learning from the homework though, as his lectures were not that comprehensive nor super well done

I would have done better in the class if I had just skipped lectures and only read the textbook and reviewed past exams. His existence discouraged me so much I literally lost all motivation to study for the class. He doesn't care about students, his class is extremely disorganized, and he arrived to every class late (even though they were online!)

Not so great teacher, lectures are not very useful for doing well on exams. However, lecture attendance is mandatory because of random recorded polls he does during class (and even after class ends). Learned mostly by doing homework on Sapling Learning, honestly pretty helpful. Would not take again, but not much choice.

I don't know anyone in his class went to lecture after the first three weeks. He seems to emphasize minuscule ideas while passing over big concepts. I did okay in the class by just reading the textbook and doing the homework. Biggest piece of advice is DO HIS EXAMS from previous years to study for your exams. This saved my grade.

Marohn is very passionate about chemistry. TOO passionate. He'll go off on spiels and tangents like nobody's business. I can think of only one class where he ended the lecture on time. What are his lectures so long for? I have no idea, because the practice problems in the homeworks taught me more than his lectures ever did

Very, very passionate about chem, however the teaching is not great. Nice guy, funny at times, but confusing. If you have a very strong background and great interest in chem, some of his lectures will be very interesting. If not, they are confusing, boring, and not helpful for exams. The homework and textbook are necessary to get the material.

His lectures can be interesting to those of you who already took AP Chem and plan to become a Chemical or Biomedical engineer. Otherwise, they are not at all helpful. He does not teach what is tested on prelims. If you want to get an A in this class then you should really hit up the textbook when prelims come around. His demos are A++ though.

Very passionate and sort of funny, but lectures aren't very helpful if all you care about is getting the grade and fulfilling your requirement (although there is an attendance grade); instead of teaching the material you'll be tested on, he mostly talks about history, proofs, experiments, etc. I didn't use the textbook at all.
Enthusiasm teacher! Nice person!!

Lectures are useless. Much of what is covered in class is unnecessary. However, random online questions for credit are posted often throughout the lectures so attendance is mandatory to get credit. If you are fine learning on your own by using the textbook/youtube, you will be fine. But having to go to lectures that do not help is annoying.

He's obviously very passionate about chemistry, but he's horrible at teaching it to students. His lectures are not helpful at all. They only confuse students more. The proofs he does are pointless and don't actually convey the material you need to know to do well on the prelims. Would recommend signing up for an AEW, you'll learn way more.

It's gen chem. You will not enjoy it unless you have prior experience, and he doesn't make it easier. Just read the textbook do the Sapling and practice exams and hope for the best. Learning proofs is useless unless you're THAT passionate about chem bruh.

He's very smart and enthusiastic about chemistry, but he gives his lectures under the assumption that you already understand the material. Instead of explaining any concepts, he just does proofs or works examples without explaining the general principles behind them. I stopped going to lecture and ended up learning everything through the textbook.

He's actually the worst teacher I've ever had. Showed up to lectures, took notes, and payed close attention to what Marohn was teaching. I ended up doing poorly on Prelim 1. Then, I stopped going to lecture/self-studied the course for the 50 minutes during lecture and ended up above the mean on Prelim 2. If you get him as a professor I am SO sorry.

To start, he's a nice guy but a terrible teacher. He teaches new stuff in a too complex manor such that you walk out of lecture learning nothing. He always says he'll assign a "very short" problem set, yet every time he says "very short" it ends up being the longest one we've done thus far, and keeps getting longer. The tests are impossible too.
BAD

Great person with amazing enthusiasm and dedication. Unfortunately this does not translate into good lectures. If you read ahead of the lectures, you'll find them much more useful, but even then attendance likely won't help you solve many problems.
Lectures were the most useless thing.  He just derives equations which has nothing to do with the tests and doesn't really help you learn chemistry.

Marohn makes concepts cryptic, whether it be in lecture or OHs. Labs are graded too harshly and take too much time. Passing the tests are manageable if you read the text; lectures are not necessary at all--they can confuse you more. I was considered ChemE, but after this class I (and about 75% of the class) changed their minds.

Marohn is a great guy and he obviously knows the material well, but he does not do a good job conveying this in lectures. The lectures were very sloppy and confusing, and the expectations for the course were extremely unclear. I pretty much learned the course material through the textbook.

Marohn is a very nice, friendly person. His enthusiasm for the subject is astounding. However, that enthusiasm doesn't translate well into lecturing and teaching an intro honors chem course. Spent way too much time deriving formulas in lecture. Lectures are hard to follow. If you want to pass DO THE HOMEWORK and really study it. Go to office hours

Marohn has good intentions, and some of his lectures are interesting. However, he spends far too much lecture time deriving formulas and ideas and nowhere near enough actually discussing the material. As such, to pass the class, I know many people that did not show up to lecture that did better than those that did. Do the homework and study it hard

Marohn is obviously really interested in what he is teaching. He's very entertaining and fairly approachable. The problem is that he doesn't convey the material very well. His lectures could be very confusing and didn't reflect what appeared on the exams. Almost everything had to be learned from the textbook, which was pretty bad. A+ demos, though.

Professor Marohn holds office hours once almost every week but he takes forever and goes out of topic while solving a problem and there are tons of students asking him questions. Labs really are annoying (some of them will be like 8-9 pages). However, tests are curved really generously so if you do +1 SD the mean you will likely get A+ in the cours

Although he's enthusiastic about chemistry Prof. Marohn's lectures are completely useless as he unnecessarily derives formulas and lectures about topics that have nothing to do with what we need to know or what will be on the prelim. Everything I "learned" from this class was from the textbook. Overall, this class was a very bad experience.

Did not give enough time to read the textbook pages before assignments were due, even though they were pretty essential to completing the problem sets. Lectured on lots of material which were not covered on prelims or the final. From observation, if you could understand his lectures, you would enjoy them. Otherwise, you would absolutely hate them

This was Marohn's first semester teaching 2150, so maybe thats why it sucked so much, but YEAH it sucked a lot. His lectures were confusing and didn't cover what we needed to know for the exams. Lots of unnecessary derivations. So, the book was basically how we learned. Problem sets were a good guideline for the exams.

His lectures are entertaining, but it's not really clear how the lecture relates to the book, prelims, etc. He spent a lot of time deriving formulas, which was interesting, but he never really told you how to useapply the formulas and concepts, and since he deviated from the book a lot it got really confusing. Also, the 1st prelim was just hell.
He is a very entertaining lecturer, but his lectures are very confusing. He moves too fast, and doesn't explain concepts well at all.
Good content, but  worst professor ever. The class covers materials that way exceed the capability of Freshman engineers.
Throws in interesting concepts and ideas during class. Easy to understand. Comes well prepared.
Go to TA office hours if you want to understand anything in this class. Lectures are unclear and pretty useless. Class is disorganized and way more work than a 2 credit class should be.
Probably the most worthless class.  Did not learn anything and took way too much time for 2 credits.  Unorganized and just troublesome.

Too much work for 2 cred. class. Lab reports (~1 every 2 wks.)took 15 hrs+, and sometimes textbook prob. the other wks. Lecture was Prof. M. deriving eqtns; mumbling and writing illegibly. Went every time, didn't learn a thing. TA had to teach me. Final proj. deadline violated univ. rules, when called on this, changed it, but we were still screwed.

This professor has no clue what is going on in his class. Lab reports are LITERALLY given one day before they are due. His lectures are confusing, and ultimately not necessary to perform well in the class. Smart man, but terrible teacher, and terribly structured course. Assignments not returned for weeks.
Did not cover material from book and was incomprehensible most of the time. His lectures were incoherent and jumped all over the place. The final was hard too.

You can tell he tries hard, but he still has a lot of improving to do. Not very clear in lecture, and tends to mumble a lot. Class is not curved very friendly, either, but I can't blame him for that. Overall, not that bad, but not the best either. Be sure to go to class when he gives demonstrations, they're worth it

Dr.Marohn mumbles sometimes, and he does mathematical proofs that are sometimes too in depth for an intro. chem class.  However, proofs make the topics less dry, because you learn why things work the way they do.  Also, he has a passion for chem and is always willing to help those who need it.  If you focus in lecture, you'll get a lot out of it.

Marohn is not a bad teacher. He knows how to keep the attention of a room full of 200 students and is very clear as to what students need to know for the class. The more in depth examination of material can be very helpful in understanding the material, even if they are not neccesary for the course. His passion/excitement is always apparent.

Awful.  I don't even bother going to most of the lectures since they don't help me at all-he goes way more in depth than needed in an intro class, and I just end up confused.  His handwriting is hard to read too.  Enroll in 007, it is really helpful if you want to get a good grade.

His is one of the worst teachers i have ever had, excluding the junior high level (where they were all jokes). His lectures are the epitome of unclarity. He is utterly unable to connect the ideas being taught and tries to teach concepts in terms of the rules used to solve problems within those concepts.
Marohn is not a good professor.  Sure, he's funny and tries to make chem fun, but he cannot teach.  He doesn't make any sense when he lectures and is not a good public speaker.

Worst professor possibly imaginable for a freshman chemistry course. Boring, teaches irrelevant material, disorganized, rambles, and basically makes the class seem this arbitrary collection of material. (Teaching semiconductor physics to freshman engineers for no reason? WHY?)
What can I say... He is a nice guy and has nice handwriting...

He gets into complex derivations that you'll never need to know, the class was very unorganized, lecture notes did not help at all (i never even looked at them while studying), he didn't really care much about the students, made a lot of false promises (ex-he posted a study guide the day of the prel

I really think John Marohn's a good guy.  I just HATED his lectures.  I could rarely stay awake through his rambling and, when I did, ended up with pages and pages of useless notes.  The only incentives to EVER going to lecture are his goofy jokes and ocassional volatile experiments.
I personally used his lecture as a lunch break. His lectures don't cover the exams well so you'll be hitting the textbook up. He also makes you memorize equations instead of learning concepts.

i took this class purely becoz i'm interested in the material covered. However, Prof. Marohn disappointed me with his ill teaching: he speaks fast often without looking at the students, covers lots of topics each week and most prelims are virtually the duplicates of the past prelims. sigh

Teaches over the students' heads a lot of the time, but he knows his stuff.  Lectures were confusing and often boring, but the demonstrations were fun.  Nice guy with good intentions; he's just not as clear as he could be.
He's a fun guy and makes the class fun, but his lectures are not very well tied to the book and are too complex many times.
lectures were extremely unhelpful work was tough and  so were the prelims. fair curve though
He needs to speak more to the student body instead of talking out loud to himself.
No Comments
Cool prof-  very helpful, blows stuff up in class
Sometimes goes off on derivations and stuff you don't need to know in class, but class is pretty good overall.  Very helpful during office hours and does cool demos.
lots of work but a very good prof. great demos. go to his office hours very helpful will try to answer any of your questions. nvery nice guy fair prelims - not to bad if you study well good curve too
No Comments
Definitely need to sit up front so it's easier to understand him but otherwise great prof.  Very fair prelims.
No Comments
Good teacher; hard to hear sometimes due to room acoustics; great in-class expirements and exams were both reasonable and comprehensive.
Although it is traditionally seen as a tough class, it is not that tough actually. He gave final grade pretty leniently!
sometimes can't understand what he's talking about but really cool demos
Mostly teaches well, sometimes difficult to understand. Helpful if doing poorly: large curves on prelims. Go to AEWs if having trouble. Tests of average difficulty: study!

Professor Hammer is one of my favorite professors at Cornell. She cares about the students and is committed to helping everyone understand the material. The course was not too hard; there were a nice amount of readings but you can get away with skimming. 10/10 professor.
don't take for ilr advanced writing seminar.  it isn't as easy as it sounds because she is a very tough grader and there are SOOOO many papers assigned

Means well but the lectures are just not engaging. Tone is hard to follow. Questions are nonstarters. Attempts at starting a discussion just leave everyone confused. Relevance of material unclear. No progression in classes, material is disjointed. A nice lady but would never take her class again.
Often rude and inconsiderate of students
Hard to do well in her class if she doesn't like you.
Amazing lady full of knowledge; take organizational behavior with her and with her only.
No Comments

Professor Barbasch was incredibly available, staying after lectures to help students (constantly), and treating all with respect. The course gets a bad rap because it is difficult, but that is not something in his hands. The support system in this class is strong, just make friends in class and ask him questions or email him/your TA. Good luck!

Lectures were chaotic and poorly controlled. I stopped going to lectures because nothing made sense and went to a different lecture with a different professor. I did much better after that. Dr. Barbasch is an amazing mathematician, however, teaching is not his strength. Exams were just as chaotic.
His teaching was horrible and I could not understand through his accent.

Professor Barbasch inspired me to pursue a major in Mathematics, and was the best math professor I had. I recommend his class to all freshmen. His proof-based approach to teaching math captivates me each time I sit in lecture, and makes me want to learn more content. He is a very fair grader, and I can do all of his exams with minimal effort.

I have never had math explained to me in a more confusing way. He doesn't speak in complete sentences, which I understand given that English is not his first language, but what he says just doesn't make sense. You don't need to go to lectures, office hours are mildly helpful, just go to the other professor's lecture and read the textbook.

He's a better in office hours than in actual lecture. He cares about his students, but hes not good when it comes to explaining to 60+ kids. I'd advise watching youtube before you come to his lectures.

This is the worst math class I have taken. Barbasch is a nice person, but his lectures are so confusing. He does a terrible job explaining and I started struggling with concepts I have been using for 2 years.

He's a nice guy and he clearly knows his stuff, but he's terrible at teaching it. Its worth going to an 8am with a different prof instead of taking a class with him. His approach to topics isn't organized, and his explanations are not well thought out. The classes leave you very confused (even if you've done that topic before).
Nice guy, not a good lecturer, unfortunately. I ended up watching another professor's recorded lectures for at least half the semester.
I would not take a class with him if you have the chance. He was really nice, but was not a good lecturer.

He's a nice guy, and very knowledgeable, but his teaching is not great. The pace of the class is extremely fast, and he expects you to know a lot already. Lectures are hard to follow, dull, and not very helpful for the exam. Be prepared to do a lot of textbook studying for exams. If you need to take 1910, I would recommend a different professor.

I have no doubt that professor Barbasch is a nice guy, he really tries hard not to let his student fail. But the man can't teach, lectures aren't helpful at all so you basically have to self-study everything. Exams are tough. Really my worst experience at Cornell...

I would say if you got Calc BC credit in high school to just skip this class. No point in trying to "solidify" your math foundation. I took this class thinking it'd help me ease into college but it was really tough and not worth it. If taking the class I highly recommend using/reading the textbook.

My lowest and worst grade ever at Cornell. For the love of God, I beg you do not take this class. He presents more theory than considered necessary. His ability to be considered a Professor academic makes me look down upon academia as a whole. Impossible exams w/ bonus points, if you didnt take calc2 in high school, you better start studying now
I would have given him the lowest score if it weren't for his generous office hours.

Professor Barbasch has a thick accent and expects you to know a lot of difficult material. He speeds through his lectures and it's very tough to do well in his course. However, he's there for you if you go to his office hours. He admitted that he has to speed through the course because he has to cover a lot of material. Overall, not bad if you try.
He decided to randomly not curve the class at the end and let me know my grade wasn't based on averages, after giving me a C+. I had always been above the mean and median.
Disorganized and very difficult
Painfully dull lectures and a thick accent.  The tests weren't horrible, though.

Made my life miserable. He may know his subject material, but he cannot teach it well. Office hours are somewhat helpful, but I advise all non-math majors to take this class as S/U. He is also very absent-minded.
Often sets up review sessions outside of class, very fair in grading. Decent professor, slightly boring and difficult to understand. Has a good sense of humor.

He's not a bad guy at all. His lectures are interesting and he can even be funny sometimes. The best thing is that he never assumes you know anything about the subject beforehand; he's very systematic and methodical. If you're struggling, he'll help you out. A great experience for me.
SOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO EASY

Very clear and concise. The lecture is not "dry" but precise, something that is essential to mathematics. He is always happy to answer questions, especially if he sees that you are making an effort to understand the problem (which may not always be evident in lecture).
He doesn't seem to be interested nor to know how to lecture calculus. Nice guy, but the class gets kind of dry sometimes

He basically presents the material at an extremely fast rate.  The sense i got was that he was incredibly bored while teaching and thus his lectures were very uninspired.  Seemed to assume that the class would immediately understand and absorb anything he wrote on the board.  He is helpful if you se
terrible... cant teach

He's a nice guy, and will try to help you out if you have any questions or problems.  But he can't teach- nobody seems to understand him.  The good thing is that the textbook covers everything you need to know, but that's no substitute for a good teacher.

Seems to lecture to himself; but crack a joke, and he'll be a jolly guy. Be sure to ask him questions, or else he'll ramble for a while and leave u way behind. He's obviously more interested in his own work than teaching intro calc; weird fashion sense.

This class was easy to do well in, but hard to get an A if that's what you're shooting for. The prelims are a bit knit-picky and the online textbook can be a bit boring but I would otherwise totally recommend this Intro. to Bio course for non-majors. The lectures were the most dynamic ones I've seen considering the size of the class.
I liked this class a lot, and Professor Agrawal was such a great professor! While it isn't too hard to catch up if you skip, there are in-class "Poll Everywhere" questions for attendance.
Super great lecturer, and very chill class. Not too difficult and would recommend

Excellent lecturer in an intro bio course. Found lectures on monarch butterfly ecology (his area of expertise) fascinating. I thoroughly enjoyed the course, although I wish practice prelims or any sort of exam questions were given. Wish he lectured more than the other professors.
Class was interesting in terms of material, with weekly homeworks that weren't too difficult. Professor was genuinely interested in teaching.
Great lecturer,  nice guy

Great professor. Clear and concise, and absolutely love to teach. Clearly wants his students to learn instead of just stuffing random bio information down your throat and expecting you to regurgitate. He is very approachable and engaging in lecture. I really wished 3690 was taught only by him instead of a group of professors.
cool

Anurag's very appearance and his wonderful mien inspire me to galvanize myself into action, grow a magnificent neckbeard, and go out into the world to explore the uncharted wilderness. He also wears entrancing t-shirts.
Chill class

Not the most useful course but easy and extremely interesting (read: senior course). Teaches by telling awesome stories about chemical ecology phenomena in nature. Good humored, fun, really smart, approachable. Great prof.

Great lecturer, makes the material easy to learn through powerpointsin-depth lectures. Easy to get at least an A- if you have a tough semester, easy A if you have more time. Dont get the textbook its only used for a few problem sets. Oh and if you want to learn how to become a ForEx trader from a crazy Armenian then this is the course for you.

A good professor to take if you're not really interested in macroeconomics. If you go to lecture and actually do the homework, it's pretty hard not to get at least an A-. Personally, I was kind of disappointed at the lack of quantitative work we did in his class, but it might just be that macroeconomics doesn't use that much math to begin with.

Barseghyan is hilarious. His lectures are full of jokes and references to Armenia. He is truly passionate about economics and tries to instil an interest in the students. However, he's not the strongest lecturer. He often just kinda paraphrases right through what you have to learn and ignores the syllabus. Never used the textbook except for hw.

Someone with real talent at jokes and supplement materials, sometimes they will last through the whole lecture. His exams are straight forward but it does require you to do a lot of self studies, especially when he vanishes right after class. Overall a good experience.

Funny/entertaining lecturer but not the best teacher ever. Never uses the textbook. Don't really have to know the calculus because he doesn't ask questions that require it/you only have to regurgitate the information. I believe he curves to a B or B+. Interactive class atmosphere in which he often calls people out.

Levon is the man. Intermediate Macro is very much intuitive, and there are only a couple models that really just require a basic feel for intermediate-level math. He uses bimmers and armenia in his examples, no work required outside of class, his lectures were hilarious to sit through, take his class.

He's not a bad teacher and tries his best to help his students. On the flip side, he's also not the clearest lecturer and writes some annoying exams. The textbook is pretty much used for only homework and helps only a little with the tests. If one doesn't like wildcards, I would suggest taking intermediate macro with another teacher.

Really funny guy, who teaches not from some ordained syllabus, but from the heart. He'll want you to learn the underlying theory of economics and arbitrage -- not just cram information in your head for a test. He's a little too infatuated with himself and it can come across during office hours or lecture. However, he teaches to median of the class.

Good lecturer with a sense of humor. His lectures, though informative, usually have nothing to do with the actual textbook readings, so sometimes I wasn't quite sure of the points that he was trying to make. Manageable workload.
Go Armenia!!
Great class.  Levon is hilarious and he teaches you real world stuff which always keeps you interested.

This guy is hilarious! His tests were only on a relatively small part of what was taught in class. What he did do in class was talk a lot about arbitraging opportunities, and how to make money, and when to buy or sell our bananas or Beemers. Very good class, but he does have a tendency to move quickly through slides.

Barseghyan is funny, energetic, and insightful. He says explicitly that he doesn't try to trick you, and he doesn't. It's one of those easy classes that you get a lot out of, take macro with levon if you can.
Funny teacher who makes class time interesting. But he does go over materials really quickly. You have to try hard to understand on the spot.

TAKE IT!  Lecture's are worthwhile for but materials are posted online.  The "esteemed professor" is hilarious and his prelims/finals are easy enough.  Practice prelims/finals are provided and are very helpful, as are the review sessions before them.  Prof's commentary is particularly interesting on the $-making and social side.  Awesome class.
Funny guy and easy class, but he does not do a good job of explaining the material. Very interesting to listen to, but you wont understand the material from listening to him.
great professor, so funny in lecture. doesn't try to trick students on prelims - he tells you exactly what will be on it. if you have to take 314, take it with him!

He is hilarious! Need to study to do well, but the tests are just like practice prelims and have almost no numerical problems, so the class isn't too hard. He has an accent but isn't hard to understand. Lecture notes are decent, but I liked the textbook better. Wouldn't be unheard of for him to use cans of beer or bananas as money in examples.
Great lectures but seems somewhat... impatient at times. But still hilarious. Don't underestimate the tests just because they look short. I made the mistake of overconfidence and I paid.

Prof. Barseghyan makes the economic idea really stick in the students' heads. 10 years down the road, I might forget everything else I've learned in college, but I am sure stuff I learned in 314 will stay in my head.
good sense of humor about economics.

Funniest professor at Cornell, hands down.  The concepts are sometimes difficult, but if you take the time t figure them out, you will do fine.  I can't get over how funny this man is.  Take this class over anything not taught by him!

who knows why he has class at 840?  pretty straight forward class and lecture, but his tests are pretty difficult and he uses them as a "learning tool", meaning there are hard questions on them (hard meaning 1/3 of the test is brand new).

He is halarious and if you HAVE to go through econ 314, take it with him.  His notes are so clear you dont have to go to class.  Yet, classes are very funny and you learn a lot.  I found the course hard, but anyone with a nack for econ wouldnt.  I love when he says "just chill"

Take 314 with this Professor! I was hesitant to take an 8:40 class, but its worth every curse at your alarm clock. You don't need to kill yourself to get an A in this class, just be diligent and you'll get a great grade. The TA was also the best one I've had at Cornell...GO TO THE EXAM REVIEW SESSIONS. Take 314 with Levon or you'll regret it...

If you want to take Econ 314, choose his. He is by far the most interesting and helpful Econ prof. in Cornell. The course might require some work but, as long as you do the problem sets, you will be fine.
All I have to say is, when you use Paris Hilton videos as an example good it makes economics so much more enjoyable.
Fantastic professor. His class is so captivating. I never thought I'd participate in an 8:40 class but his class wakes you up!
This man is the best professor I have ever had at Cornell. Take his class. Done.

Levon is the man, simply put.  Brilliant professor with a great sense of humor.  Teaches economics from a practical and applied viewpoint - concepts first, models later.  Rational, unbiased views on politics and economic policy, which is a rare find.  Not afraid to speak his mind and tell it how it is.  Take the class, it's worth it.
His jokes make lecture more entertaining, but he isn't as clear in his explanations as he could be.  Arrogant.
great guy, dont take 314 with anyone else, theres no way you can do bad in this class!

awesome guy! he is a very intelligent and a good, entertaining lecturer; he keeps student attention with his jokes while stimulating them to think deeply about econ issues by asking questions.  one of the best profs at cornell

Yes, he is the man. The class was a lot of fun and the homework wasn't too bad either. Just be aware not to wear anything (such as a hat) that will make you stick out in the lecture hall, because he'll call on you.

One of the best professors at the Econ department. He focus on understanding the concepts rather than just pure math like all other Professors. Many real life examples to help you understand true economics. Exams are bit tricky, study for it. TA is really awsome too. "Ding Ding"!

I love you Levon and I'll never forget you.  He is the best Econ professor I've ever had.  The other professor teaching this class was Zhu.   What a difference.  Levon is precise and exacting--he is at all times clear and original.  I'll never forget lecture 1 when he shocked the class.
Levon rocks.  This is a class where you learn something about the real world.  I would strongly recommend to non-econ majors (like me) who want to learn a lot about econ without working too much.

He's cool. But I've got to add sth bad about him. cuz he has so many praise already.  He's so mean!!He uses the same exams all the time. And I wish his exam could be more reasonable. ummm, he loves banana, bimmer, dudes... He should be less arrogant though, and plz, respect textbooks more.

After taking 314, Levon is probably my favorite professor at Cornell.  He makes the class interesting and I have actually recommended others to take the class SPECIFICALLY so they have him.  His discussions in lecture have been profound enough to influence my day-to-day consumption.

Fun class and good lecturer.  Has right-wing bias (for me bad).  Fairly easy tests and grading.  You can skip class and read the online notes, but then you miss out on Levon's jokes.  Speaks English well.  Would recommend.
beemers, bulletproof clear, and "the guy in the red hat", great times
Fun lecturer - generally clear. Tries to make course as easy as possible. He loooooves to fight with liberals. Would take again.

"Levon"'s class often turns into a conversation between himself and "the guy in the hat." The powerpoints consist of graphs copied from the textbook (which he admitted is crap). Lectures essentially useless, but he is an  (unintentiona
Loves Beemers. Reasonable prof, teaches from PowerPoint so i really don't consider it teaching, likes to go off on useless tangents, but best english out of the other 314 profs

The class is easy, but really boring. I fell asleep in every class even though I tried to stay awake. Take notes (tested on things not on the PowerPoints because the other professor is there taking notes on what he says.) The tests are hard-- need to know too many specific details to do well. Don't take it unless you need to.
Really awesome teacher! He's so approachable and crazy knowledgeable about food science.

Great lecturer, very nice, great class--easy & interesting.  Super nice; only time I saw him slightly "testy" was during the mass exodus after the quiz at the beginning of class!  Ridiculous.  The class is really easy, but you do have to study a little bit.
No Comments
Tests are way too hard.  Someone needs to remind him this is only a 2 credit class.  Very testy in class.  Don't take it if you really don't have to.

I did not think Professor Carvell was a good professor. His lectures weren't informative and he did not give a lot of opportunities to practice. The exams were heavy on open-ended questions that were not practiced beforehand. His TAs were awful and could not answer questions that were asked, and seemed just as confused as the students.

I took the class in Summer 2020 (it went online because of COVID). Hes super chilled and very accommodating. He gave very clear explanations in the videos and in lectures. The class is easy. Even though the prerequisite is Financial Accounting theres barely any accounting in the course and its just basic Math.
Textbook not necessary. Online course can be frustrating but also useful. Exams are very easy, almost no homework
best teacher ever. soooooo deeeeep

Professor Carvell is funny - he is always going on tangents but that's good when the class is just numbers. If you're a math person, this class is a joke. He's also really helpful outside of class for questions about anything.
Carvell rocks
No Comments

Professor Hostetler genuinely cares about his students, and it comes through in every facet of the course.  I have genuinely grown as a person and scholar through his instruction, and I would highly recommend his course to anyone who aspires to see leadership in a new light.

Very random, drones on and on cartoonishly with juvenile humor, then feigns professional decorum. Isn't an inspiring leader; condones low levels of behavior from students during activities- either egocentric or sheepish. Expectations are as strange as the structure of the course and his presentations were not effective. Wouldn't recommend.
His teaching skills are excellent but he isn't very helpful in person.

I really fell in love with anthropology through Prof. Ramberg. Courses are reading-heavy, but nothing more than would be expected for someone dedicated to the humanities. Her class discussions were rewarding when you did participate. One of the few classes as well where I felt I got a fantastic variety of readings, some of which I would read again.

Professor Ramberg gives wonderful lectures that provide a lot of clarity on reading material. Lecture attendance is very important. Her essay prompts are vague but this never hurts your grade; she offers a lot of freedom in terms of what you write about. I loved her class so much that I'm taking another class by her this semester!

Clearly very knowledgeable, though didn't explain confusing concepts well. A lot of readings - some interesting, some not so much. I was scared to participate in class after witnessing the verbal attack of a classmate voicing an unpopular opinion, with little defense from Professor Ramberg. Nonetheless, the class made me a more thoughtful person.

Material was not what you would expect of an introduction to gender studies class.  Grading was super vague/slightly arbitrary. Did not post grades for large group project because "we would have the best idea of how well we did" as if that makes any sense. Okay class, some interesting topics but discussion always centered around her own opinion
SHE IS THE BEST! Very helpful. Readings are long but super interesting, and she has been such an inspiration in my life.

Professor Ramberg is a wonderful professor. She assigns a little too much reading but discussions and insights in class are for the most part worth it. A bit difficult with grading, expects you to put in an unnecessarily large amount of time when working on papers and projects. Overall a pretty good professor though.
Favorite professor

Prof. Pizzaro was a very engaging lecturer. The grading scheme of the class was very generous and the class was topically interesting. Always great to start the day listening to the Psych 1101 playlist at Bailey!
Professor Pizarro's lectures are very enjoyable and his personality shines through in-person.

Only open book weekly quizzes and a final. Lots of memorization, but it's overall an easy A, or A+ if u put in effort. First few quizzes will be tough as you get used to the format but 2 lowest quizzes get dropped. There is also five percent extra credit for participating in experiments. The content itself is super engaging and interesting.

Dave is an amazing professor. He's very funny and cares a lot about the students even though it is large lecture. It is very easy to get a good grade if you keep up with the quizzes (some questions may be confusing, but very doable) and study for the final based on the review. It definitely is a must take class :)

Professor Pizarro made this class so enjoyable. He's really funny, cares about his students, and is just a nice guy to be around. The class itself is very interesting and engaging. Some quizzes may be hard to do well on, but most are straightforward. The final was pretty light. This is probably my favorite class so far at Cornell, and I loved it.

Literally my favorite professor that I have had so far at Cornell. Lectures are easy to follow, content is interesting and on top of that he's hilarious and really cares about students doing well. It's a big lecture so you don't get to know him one-on-one but he is more than willing to help students if you reach out. 10/10 would recommend

Before I came to Cornell Pizarro's class was recommended to me, so I decided to take it for fun. Didn't change my life or anything but it was interesting enough. Even though I fell asleep in lecture a lot, whenever I woke up Pizarro was saying something funny. Classwork is very minimal, just read textbook/slides before tests. Great fun facts class.

Professor Pizarro is an amazing lecturer! His lectures are hilarious and passionate, and he always has a bunch of personal examples to illustrate the concepts he discusses. The material itself is very reasonable and pretty simple to learn. He has weekly quizzes, which are usually straight forward. He also has extra credit in his class.

Prof. Pizarro is extremely engaging and personable. His lectures were captivating and he always had interesting stories to tell which aligned with the lecture. The textbook was free and your grade mostly relies on weekly quizzes (which are very fair, in my opinion). Learned so much and he undoubtedly sparked my interest for psychology!

Professor Pizarro is a great lecturer and makes his class super interesting. While lectures are not mandatory, they were fun to go to because of him. He is very understanding of his students and cares about them. He's one of the best professors I have had at Cornell.

Dr. Pizarro is a great lecturer and is very clear-cut with his expectations. He acknowledges that it is an easy class and even states that there is no reason anyone shouldn't be able to get an A. His lectures were an engaging introduction to many basic concepts in psychology and the assignments he gave were always straightforward.

This prof is really amazing and the class is super easy. His lectures were not only hilarious but well-organized and informative too. The workload is minimal, consisting of reading and a quiz every week. He just seems like a great guy overall. When there was a shooter on campus and a bomb threat a few days before, he was very accommodating.

Caring, amazing Professor, not hard to get an A as long as you do your readings. Would definitely recommend Professor David, his interest for Psychology makes the students enjoy learning from him. He is also funny so you don't get super bored in lecture.
Amazing, funny and invested professor.

Lectures are very interesting, as is the textbook (the textbook even throws in jokes and funny things a lot). Easy to do well in the class (if you read), and you learn some interesting stuff. Highly recommend!

Easily the best run online course I have had at Cornell. Lectures were done with movie level production value and were extremely entertaining. Very generous extra credit makes it hard not to succeed. Highly recommend.

Ive had a really rough semester as a freshman, and things have been more confusing due to COVID. His lectures have gotten me through it all. He is very accommodating to students and reduces our load when were busy with other classes. Weekly quizzes instead of prelims have been a great format for online learning
Prof cares about students. Psych 1101 is a huge class but well-managed. Very easy.
Prof Pizarro is amazing - his lectures online were so high quality and hes super funny and very very kind.

Prof Pizarro is awesome. His lectures are so well produced and really engaging. He is so funny and really cares about us getting something out of the class. The online format is tough bc of the weekly quizzes but Im pretty sure thats all run by TAs. Professor Pizarro himself is amazing. Would 1000% take another of his classes.

Favorite professor by far at Cornell. His lectures are like stand-up comedy. You probably don't need to go to lecture to pass, but he's so funny you'll want to go. I wish I could retake his class - it's unlike any other. You do need to study, but take advantage of the summary pages and quizlet for vocab. Extra credit can also boost your grade lots

Pizarro is an engaging lecturer. He makes class interesting. Although lectures are great, they are far from necessary as tests are largely based on lecture slides and the textbook. Cram the night before for tests and you're good.
Awesome guy! Very interestingpeople should definitely also check out his podcast
The chillest professor I've ever had. Lectures are amazing. Just take notes and read the textbook. Prelims are multiple choice.
Pizarro is the coolest :)
Really entertaining and interesting!
Engaging, funny, hot. What more could you ask for?
Daves a great guy  lectures may not be mandatory, but its worth going just for the professor.
Really knowledgeable, interesting and engaging. Learned a lot. Perfect level of difficulty for an intro course!

Take this class if you want an easy A, minimal in-class learning, and negligible workload. If you want to comprehensively learn and appreciate psychology as a subject, I wouldn't recommend it. Lectures are useless and contain very little substance. 80% of the material is exclusively found in the textbook, so the class is basically auto-tutorial.

Pizarro is a really good professor. He's funny and if you wait long enough after class you can even talk to him. The class is not very demanding, show up if you want (or don't) the only thing you'll miss are the potential EC questions and hearing his jokes. You don't really need to keep up with the reading, but make sure to do extra credit!

A lot of reading but as long as you do it, which you will, cause you'll have no other choice, you're likely to get an A. Extra credit really helps with that too. I think you need a 94 to make an A but believe me, the work is worth it. Also, lectures are fun because Pizzaro adds all these videos and experiments which make it interesting.

Best class at Cornell! This is a must-take class and you're ensured an A as long as you read the material covered well. Lectures are amazing and Prof. Pizzaro is hilarious. The exams are all multiple choice questions and the material is very interesting. If I could, I would definitely take this class again. Also, you get extra credit very easily.

If you show up to class, take notes, and read the textbook you will do fine in this class. If you don't read, prepare for the exams because they will wreck you. Besides that, Pizarro is an amazing lecturer that makes sure you always feel engaged and aren't bored in class.
One of the best lecturers I've had. His lectures are really interesting and all you really have to do is read the textbook and study his slides. Super chill

Pizarro's lectures are funny and interesting, but he is very difficult to get a hold of outside class. However, there are a huge number of TA's who hold office hours and review sessions and are generally really helpful. The tests aren't as easy as people claim, but they're pretty fair and if you study you'll do well. Plus there's extra credit.

Great class if you are looking for something not stressful. Lectures were interesting and contained a lot of information on the test. Professor was always energetic and engaging. One of the best lecturers I've had at Cornell.
LOVE PIZARRO!!!!! Take this class, you won't regret it.

Easiest class ever. Graded on two prelims and a final. All multiple choice. Read the textbook and you'll be fine, honestly. I can count on one hand the amount of times I actually showed up to lecture, and I still got an A+. EXTREMELY generous extra credit5% on your overall grade just for participating in a few experiments. Kinda hot too, ngl.

My favorite class at Cornell so far. Super easy. TED-talk style lecturesattendance isn't required. I stopped going to class after the second week of the semester and I got a 99.7%. Just make sure you learn the vocabulary from the lectures and the textbook. 5% extra credit for participating in experiments. No assignments. Pizarro's the man.

Psychology is a VERY interesting subject, but Prof. Pizarro is not that much... I counted much more on the textbook than on the lectures bc they seemed so forcefully artificial and boring, in general. It's an easy class, though.
Lectures aren't super useful but they are interesting.

I love this man with my entire being. Lectures are interesting, but you don't have to go. Entire grade is made up of two prelims & a final (all multiple choice; prelims were 45 questions each, final was 60). I stopped going to class after a month and ended up with a 99%. Can get up to 5% extra credit by signing up for experiments (0.5-1 hrs each).

Pizarro is the BEST! I was excited to go to lectures; they're fun, interesting, and engaging. Pizarro is hilarious and super smart and he definitely makes it easy to succeed in the class, This class was easily my favorite and has inspired me to take more Psych courses in the future.

Lecture was more like a Ted talk - very engaging and funny, but lecture attendance wasn't really necessary. Get the notes from a classmate and read the textbook if you have to, but I recommend going to lecture just because it's fun and interesting. Covers a very broad range of material in little detail but lots of cool case studies.
Such a great teacher, I loved going to class three times a week with this guy. He keeps things interesting and relatable and he is outwardly passionate about his field of study.

Solid intro class. Grade is composed solely of 2 prelims and 1 final. Tests are heavily based on the textbook but often had lecture-based questions too, including guest lectures. As long as you study thoroughly, you'll be fine. If you do all the extra credit, you'll get a 5% bump on your overall grade which is huge. Great class, great professor.
